children.translated_text: = <s>Kauṭilīya Arthaśāstra</s> =

children.text:
(Book.1: Concerning the topic of training)
(Chap..1: Enumeration of sections and books)
oṃ.namaḥ.śukra.bṛhaspatibhyāṃ --
KAZ01.1.01/.pṛthivyā lābhe pālane ca yāvanty artha.śāstrāṇi pūrva.ācāryaiḥ prasthāpitāni prāyaśas tāni saṃhṛtya^ekam idam artha.śāstraṃ kṛtam //
children.translated_text:
(Book 1: Concerning the topic of training)
(Chapter 1: Enumeration of sections and books)
Om. Homage to <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
KAZ01.1.01/ Of nearly all the treatises on political science (<s>arthaśāstras</s>) set forth by previous teachers concerning the acquisition and protection of the earth, having drawn them together, this single treatise on political science has been composed.

children.text: KAZ01.1.02/ tasya^ayaṃ prakaraṇa.adhikaraṇa.samuddeśaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.02/ This is the enumeration of its topics and books.

children.text:
KAZ01.1.03a/ vidyā.samuddeśaḥ, vṛddha.samuddeśaḥ, indriya.jayaḥ, amātya.utpattiḥ, mantri.purohita.utpattiḥ, upadhābhiḥ śauca.aśauca.jñānam amātyānām, - -
KAZ01.1.03b/ gūḍha.puruṣa.praṇidhiḥ, sva.viṣaye kṛtya.akṛtya.pakṣa.rakṣaṇam, para.viṣaye kṛtya.akṛtya.pakṣa.upagrahaḥ, -
KAZ01.1.03c/ mantra.adhikāraḥ, dūta.praṇidhiḥ, rāja.putra.rakṣaṇam, aparuddha.vṛttam, aparuddhe vṛttiḥ, rāja.praṇidhiḥ, niśānta.praṇidhiḥ, ātma.rakṣitakam, --, iti vinaya.adhikārikaṃ prathamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.03a/ Enumeration of the sciences, enumeration of the elders, conquest of the senses, appointment of ministers, appointment of the chaplain and counselors, ascertaining the integrity and corruption of ministers through secret tests,
KAZ01.1.03b/ deployment of secret agents, protection of parties loyal and disloyal within one's own territory, winning over parties loyal and disloyal in the enemy's territory,
KAZ01.1.03c/ the business of counsel, deployment of envoys, protection of princes, the conduct of a restrained [prince], conduct toward a restrained [prince], surveillance of the king, surveillance of the royal household, protection of one's own person — thus the first book, on the topic of training (<s>vinayādhikārika</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.04a/ janapada.niveśaḥ, bhūmic.chidra.apidhānam, durga.vidhānam, durga.niveśaḥ, samnidhātṛ.nicaya.karma, samāhartṛ.samudaya.prasthāpanam, akṣa.paṭale gāṇanikya.adhikāraḥ, -
KAZ01.1.04b/ samudayasya yukta.apahṛtasya pratyānayanam, upayukta.parīkṣā, śāsana.adhikāraḥ, kośa.praveśya.ratna.parīkṣā, ākara.karma.anta.pravartanam, akṣa.śālāyāṃ suvarṇa.adhyakṣaḥ -
KAZ01.1.04c/ viśikhāyāṃ sauvarṇika.pracāraḥ, koṣṭha.āgāra.adhyakṣaḥ, paṇya.adhyakṣaḥ, kupya.adhyakṣaḥ, āyudha.adhyakṣaḥ, tulā.māna.pautavam, -
KAZ01.1.04d/ deśa.kāla.mānam, śulka.adhyakṣaḥ, sūtra.adhyakṣaḥ, sīta.adhyakṣaḥ, surā.adhyakṣaḥ, sūna.adhyakṣaḥ, gaṇikā.adhyakṣaḥ, -
KAZ01.1.04e/ nāv.adhyakṣaḥ, go.adhyakṣaḥ, aśva.adhyakṣaḥ, hasty.adhyakṣaḥ, ratha.adhyakṣaḥ, patty.adhyakṣaḥ, senā.pati.pracāraḥ, mudrā.adhyakṣaḥ, vivīta.adhyakṣaḥ, samāhartṛ.pracāraḥ, -
KAZ01.1.04f/ gṛha.patika.vaidehaka.tāpasa.vyañjanāḥ praṇidhayaḥ, nāgarika.praṇidhiḥ -- ity adhyakṣa.pracāro dvitīyam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.04a/ Settlement of the countryside, filling up of uncultivated land, construction of forts, settlement within forts, the duties of the treasurer and the collector, the superintendent's office at the accounting bureau,
KAZ01.1.04b/ recovery of revenue that has been embezzled by officials, examination of those employed, the business of edicts, examination of gems to be deposited in the treasury, inauguration of mining and manufacturing operations, the superintendent of gold at the assay office,
KAZ01.1.04c/ operations of the goldsmith in the market street, the superintendent of the storehouse, the superintendent of commerce, the superintendent of forest products, the superintendent of the armory, weights and measures and their standardization,
KAZ01.1.04d/ measurement of space and time, the superintendent of tolls, the superintendent of weaving, the superintendent of agriculture, the superintendent of liquor, the superintendent of the slaughterhouse, the superintendent of courtesans,
KAZ01.1.04e/ the superintendent of ships, the superintendent of cattle, the superintendent of horses, the superintendent of elephants, the superintendent of chariots, the superintendent of infantry, operations of the commander-in-chief, the superintendent of passports, the superintendent of pasture lands, operations of the collector,
KAZ01.1.04f/ secret agents disguised as householders, traders, and ascetics, surveillance of the city — thus the second book, on the operations of superintendents (<s>adhyakṣapracāra</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.05a/ vyavahāra.sthāpanā, vivāda.pada.nibandhaḥ, vivāha.samyuktam, dāya.vibhāgaḥ, vāstukam, samayasya anapākarma, ṛṇa.adānam, aupanidhikam, dāsa.karma.kara.kalpaḥ, -
KAZ01.1.05b/ sambhūya samutthānam, vikrīta.krīta.anuśayaḥ, dattasya anapākarma, asvāmi.vikrayaḥ, sva.svāmi.sambandhaḥ, sāhasam, vāk.pāruṣyam, daṇḍa.pāruṣyam, dyūta.samāhvayam, prakīrṇakaṃ - iti, dharma.sthīyaṃ tṛtīyam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.05a/ Establishment of legal procedures, basis of litigation, matters connected with marriage, partition of inheritance, buildings, non-performance of agreements, non-payment of debts, deposits, the rules concerning slaves and laborers,
KAZ01.1.05b/ cooperative undertakings, rescission of purchase and sale, non-rescission of gifts, sale by a non-owner, relationship between owner and property, violence (<s>sāhasa</s>), verbal assault, physical assault, gambling and betting, miscellaneous — thus the third book, on [the administration of] justice (<s>dharmasthīya</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.06a/ kāru.kara.kṣaṇam, vaidehaka.rakṣaṇam, upanipāta.pratīkāraḥ, gūḍha.ājīvināṃ rakṣā, siddha.vyañjanair māṇava.prakāśanam, śaṅkā.rūpa.karma.abhigrahaḥ, -
KAZ01.1.06b/ āśu.mṛtaka.parīkṣā, vākya.karma.anuyogaḥ, sarva.adhikaraṇa.rakṣaṇaṃ -
KAZ01.1.06c/ eka.aṅga.vadha.niṣkrayaḥ, śuddhaś citraś ca daṇḍa kalpaḥ, kanyā.prakarma, aticāra.daṇḍāḥ - iti kaṇṭaka.śodhanaṃ caturtham adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.06a/ Protection of artisans and laborers, protection of merchants, counteracting calamities, protection against those who subsist by secret means, detection of youths [employed as spies] by agents with ascertained credentials, apprehension based on suspicious appearance and behavior,
KAZ01.1.06b/ examination of sudden death, interrogation by words and acts, protection of all departments,
KAZ01.1.06c/ the ransom for the loss of a limb, pure and varied forms of punishments, duties regarding virgins, penalties for transgressions — thus the fourth book, on the removal of thorns (<s>kaṇṭakaśodhana</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.07/ dāṇḍakarmikam, kośa.abhisaṃharaṇam, bhṛtya.bharaṇīyam, anujīvi.vṛttam, samaya.ācārikam, rājya.pratisaṃdhānam, eka.aiśvaryaṃ - iti yoga.vṛttaṃ pañcamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.07/ Administration of punishments, raising of the treasury, maintenance of servants, conduct toward dependents, observance of customary law, restoration of the kingdom, sole sovereignty — thus the fifth book, on conduct through effort (<s>yogavṛtta</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.08/ prakṛti.sampadaḥ, śama.vyāyāmikaṃ - iti maṇḍala.yoniḥ ṣaṣṭham adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.08/ Excellences of the constituent elements, [policy of] peace and exertion — thus the sixth book, the basis of the circle [of kings] (<s>maṇḍalayoni</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.09a/ ṣāḍguṇya.samuddeśaḥ, kṣaya.sthāna.vṛddhi.niścayaḥ, saṃśraya.vṛttiḥ, samahīna.jyāyasāṃ guṇa.abhiniveśaḥ, hīna.saṃdhayaḥ, vigṛhya āsanam, saṃdhāya āsanam, vigṛhya yānam, saṃdhāya yānam, -
KAZ01.1.09b/ sambhūya prayāṇam, yātavya.amitrayor abhigraha.cintā, kṣaya.lobha.virāga.hetavaḥ prakṛtīnām, sāmavāyika.viparimarśaḥ, -
KAZ01.1.09c/ saṃhita prayāṇikam, paripaṇita.aparipaṇita.apasṛtāḥ saṃdhayaḥ, dvaidhī.bhāvikāḥ saṃdhi.vikramāḥ, yātavya.vṛttiḥ, anugrāhya.mitra.viśeṣāḥ, -
KAZ01.1.09d/ mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.karma.saṃdhayaḥ, pārṣṇi.grāha.cintā, hīna.śakti.pūraṇam, balavatā vigṛhya uparodha.hetavaḥ, daṇḍa.upanata.vṛttam, -
KAZ01.1.09e/ daṇḍa.upanāyi.vṛttam, saṃdhi.karma, samādhi.mokṣaḥ, madhyama.caritam, udāsīna.caritam, maṇḍala.caritaṃ - iti ṣāḍguṇyaṃ saptamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.09a/ Enumeration of the sixfold policy, determination of decline, stability, and growth, conduct of the one seeking refuge, engagement of qualities among equals, inferiors, and superiors, peace treaties with the weaker, sitting quiet after hostility, sitting quiet after peace, marching after hostility, marching after peace,
KAZ01.1.09b/ joint military expedition, deliberation regarding the two to be attacked — the enemy and the ally, causes for the revolt, avarice, and disaffection of the constituent elements, review of confederacies,
KAZ01.1.09c/ marching in concert with peace, peace treaties — settled, unsettled, and withdrawn, strategies of dual policy combining peace and aggression, conduct toward the enemy to be attacked, special kinds of allies to be supported,
KAZ01.1.09d/ peace treaties involving allies, money, land, and labor, deliberation regarding the one who strikes in the rear, strengthening a weak force, reasons for besieging after hostility with a stronger [king], conduct of one brought under by force,
KAZ01.1.09e/ conduct of one who brings under by force, the action of peace, release from bondage, conduct of the middle [king], conduct of the neutral [king], conduct in the circle [of kings] — thus the seventh book, on the sixfold policy (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.10/ prakṛti.vyasana.vargaḥ, rāja.rājyayor vyasana.cintā, puruṣa.vyasana.vargaḥ, pīḍana.vargaḥ, stambha.vargaḥ, kośa.saṅga.vargaḥ, mitra.vyasana.vargaḥ - iti vyasana.ādhikārikam aṣṭamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.10/ The category of calamities of the constituent elements, deliberation on calamities of the king and the kingdom, the category of personal calamities, the category of afflictions, the category of obstruction, the category of treasury losses, the category of calamities of allies — thus the eighth book, on the topic of calamities (<s>vyasanādhikārika</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.11a/ śakti.deśa.kāla.bala.abala.jñānam, yātrā.kālāḥ, bala.upādāna.kālāḥ, samnāha.guṇāḥ, pratibala.karma, paścāt kopa.cintā, bāhya.ābhyantara.prakṛti.kopa.pratīkārāḥ -
KAZ01.1.11b/ kṣaya.vyaya.lābha.viparimarśaḥ, bāhya.ābhyantarāś ca^āpadaḥ, duṣya.śatru.samyuktāḥ, artha.anartha.saṃśaya.yuktāḥ, tāsām upāya.vikalpajāḥ siddhayaḥ - ity abhiyāsyat karma navamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.11a/ Knowledge of power, place, time, strength, and weakness, times for military campaigns, times for raising forces, qualities of an army, deployment against an equal force, deliberation on the one who attacks in the rear, counteracting revolts of external and internal constituent elements,
KAZ01.1.11b/ review of loss, expenditure, and gain, external and internal calamities, those connected with a treacherous enemy, those connected with advantage, disadvantage, and uncertainty, the successes arising from the varieties of expedients — thus the ninth book, on the activity of one about to march (<s>abhiyāsyatkarmā</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.1.12/ skandha.āvāra.niveśaḥ, skandha.āvāra.prayāṇam, bala.vyasana.avaskanda.kāla.rakṣaṇam, kūṭa.yuddha.vikalpāḥ, sva.sainya.utsāhanam, sva.bala.anya.bala.vyāyogaḥ, yuddha.bhūmayaḥ, patty.aśva.ratha.hasti.karmāṇi, pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānāṃ bala.agrato vyūha.vibhāgaḥ, sāra.phalgu.bala.vibhāgaḥ, patty.aśva.ratha.hasti.yuddhāni,
daṇḍa.bhoga.maṇḍala.asaṃhata.vyūha.vyūhanam, tasya prativyūha.sthāpanaṃ - iti sāṃgrāmikaṃ daśamam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.12/ Setting up the military camp, marching from the camp, protecting against calamities and attacks on the army, varieties of stratagems in warfare, inspiring one's own army, coordination of one's own forces and allied forces, battlegrounds, operations of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants, division of the army into flanks, sides, and front with deployment of forces, division of elite and inferior forces, battles of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants,
arranging dispersed and compact formations in the shape of a staff, snake, circle, and detached body, and establishing counter-formations — thus the tenth book, on the topic of war (<s>sāṃgrāmika</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.13/ bheda.upādānāni, upāṃśu.daṇḍāḥ - iti saṃgha.vṛttam ekādaśam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.13/ Means of sowing dissension, covert punishments — thus the eleventh book, on the conduct toward corporations (<s>saṃghavṛtta</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.14/ dūta.karma, mantra.yuddham, senā.mukhya.vadhaḥ, maṇḍala.protsāhanam, śastra.agni.rasa.praṇidhayaḥ, vīvadha.āsāra.prasāra.vadhaḥ, yoga.atisaṃdhānam, daṇḍa.atisaṃdhānam, eka.vijayaḥ - ity ābalīyasaṃ dvādaśam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.14/ The work of envoys, war through counsel, assassination of army chiefs, inciting the circle [of kings], deployment of weapons, fire, and poison, destruction in the form of raids and sudden attacks, outwitting through stratagem, outwitting through force, single victory — thus the twelfth book, on [the conduct of] the weaker [king] (<s>ābalīyasa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.15/ upajāpaḥ, yoga.vāmanam, apasarpa.praṇidhiḥ, paryupāsana.karma, avamardaḥ, labdha.praśamanaṃ - iti durga.lambha.upāyas trayodaśam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.15/ Instigation [of enemy's subjects], creating obstacles through stratagem, deployment of agents, the operations of a siege, assault, pacification of a conquered [territory] — thus the thirteenth book, on the means of capturing a fort (<s>durgalambhopāya</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.16/ para.bala.ghāta.prayogaḥ, pralambhanam, sva.bala.upaghāta.pratīkāraḥ - ity aupaniṣadikaṃ caturdaśam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.16/ Means of destroying an enemy army, enticement, counteracting damage to one's own army — thus the fourteenth book, on esoteric practices (<s>aupaniṣadika</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.17/ tantra.yuktayaḥ - iti tantra.yuktiḥ pañcadaśam adhikaraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.17/ Methodological devices — thus the fifteenth book, on the plan of the treatise (<s>tantrayukti</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.1.18/ śāstra.samuddeśaḥ pañcadaśa.adhikaraṇāni sa-aśīti.prakaraṇa.śataṃ sa-pañcāśad.adhyāya.śataṃ ṣaṭ.śloka.sahasrāṇi^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.1.18/ The enumeration of the treatise: fifteen books, one hundred and fifty topics, one hundred and fifty chapters, six thousand verses.

children.text:
KAZ01.1.19ab/ sukha.grahaṇa.vijñeyaṃ tattva.artha.pada.niścitam /
KAZ01.1.19cd/ kauṭilyena kṛtaṃ śāstraṃ vimukta.grantha.vistaram //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.1.19ab/ Easy to grasp and to understand, with the meaning of principles and words firmly established —
KAZ01.1.19cd/ this treatise was composed by <s>Kauṭilya</s>, free from the prolixity of texts.

children.text:
(Chap.2, ṣection.1: Enumeration of the sciences)
((i) Establishing (the necessity of) philosophy)
KAZ01.2.01/ ānvīkṣikī trayī vārttā daṇḍa.nītiś ca^iti vidyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Chapter 2, Section 1: Enumeration of the sciences)
((i) Establishing (the necessity of) philosophy)
KAZ01.2.01/ Philosophy (<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>), the three Vedas (<s>trayī</s>), economics (<s>vārttā</s>), and the science of government (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>) — these are the sciences.

children.text: KAZ01.2.02/ trayī vārttā daṇḍa nītiś ca^iti mānavāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.02/ The three Vedas, economics, and the science of government — [say] the followers of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.2.03/ trayī viśeṣo hy ānvīkṣikī^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.03/ For philosophy is merely a special branch of the three Vedas.

children.text: KAZ01.2.04/ vārttā daṇḍa.nītiś ca^iti bārhaspatyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.04/ Economics and the science of government — [say] the followers of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.2.05/ saṃvaraṇa.mātraṃ hi trayī loka.yātrā.vida iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.05/ For the three Vedas are merely a cloak for one who knows the ways of the world.

children.text: KAZ01.2.06/ daṇḍa.nītir ekā vidyā^ity auśanasāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.06/ The science of government alone is the [true] science — [say] the followers of <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.2.07/ tasyāṃ hi sarva.vidyā.ārambhāḥ pratibaddhā iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.07/ For in it are grounded the undertakings of all the sciences.

children.text: KAZ01.2.08/ catasra eva vidyā iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.08/ There are indeed four sciences — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.2.09/ tābhir dharma.arthau yad vidyāt tad vidyānāṃ vidyātvam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.09/ The fact that through them one learns <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>artha</s> (wealth) — that is what makes the sciences sciences.

children.text: KAZ01.2.10/ sāṃkhyaṃ yogo lokāyataṃ ca^ity ānvīkṣikī //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.10/ <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and <s>Lokāyata</s> — these constitute philosophy (<s>ānvīkṣikī</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.2.11/ dharma.adharmau trayyām artha.anarthau vārttāyāṃ naya.anayau daṇḍa.nītyāṃ bala.abale ca etāsāṃ hetubhir anvīkṣamāṇā lokasya upakaroti vyasane^abhyudaye ca buddhim avasthāpayati prajñā.vākya.kriyā.vaiśāradyaṃ ca karoti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.2.11/ Examining, by means of reasoning, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> in the Vedic lore, material gain and loss in economics, sound policy and unsound policy in the science of government, and the relative strengths and weaknesses of these — [philosophy] benefits the world, keeps the mind steady in adversity and prosperity, and produces excellence of understanding, speech, and action.

children.text:
KAZ01.2.12ab/ pradīpaḥ sarva.vidyānām upāyaḥ sarva.karmaṇām /
KAZ01.2.12cd/ āśrayaḥ sarva.dharmāṇāṃ śaśvad ānvīkṣikī matā //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.2.12ab/ A lamp for all the sciences, a means for all activities,
KAZ01.2.12cd/ a foundation for all <s>dharmas</s> — philosophy is ever held to be.

children.text:
(Chap.3, ṣection.1, (ī) Establishing (the necessity of) the Vedic ḷore)
KAZ01.3.01/ sāma.ṛg.yajur.vedās trayas trayī //
children.translated_text:
(Chapter 3, Section 1, (i) Establishing (the necessity of) the Vedic lore)
KAZ01.3.01/ The <s>Sāma</s>, <s>Ṛg</s>, and <s>Yajur Vedas</s> — these three constitute the Vedic triad (<s>trayī</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.3.02/ atharva.veda.itihāsa.vedau ca vedāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.02/ The <s>Atharva Veda</s> and the <s>Itihāsa Veda</s> are also Vedas.

children.text: KAZ01.3.03/ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando.vicitir jyotiṣam iti ca^aṅgāni //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.03/ Phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>), ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>), grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), etymology (<s>nirukta</s>), metrics (<s>chandoviciti</s>), and astronomy (<s>jyotiṣa</s>) — these are the auxiliary sciences (<s>aṅgas</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.3.04/ eṣa trayī.dharmaś caturṇāṃ varṇānām āśramāṇāṃ ca sva.dharma.sthāpanād aupakārikaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.04/ This <s>dharma</s> of the Vedic triad is beneficial through establishing the proper duties (<s>svadharma</s>) of the four social classes (<s>varṇas</s>) and the life-stages (<s>āśramas</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.3.05/ svadharmo brāhmaṇasya adhyayanam adhyāpanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ dānaṃ pratigrahaś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.05/ The proper duty of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is: study, teaching, performing sacrifices, officiating at sacrifices, giving, and receiving [gifts].

children.text: KAZ01.3.06/ kṣatriyasya^adhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ dānaṃ śastra.ājīvo bhūta.rakṣaṇaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.06/ Of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>: study, performing sacrifices, giving, living by arms, and protection of beings.

children.text: KAZ01.3.07/ vaiśyasya^adhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ dānaṃ kṛṣi.pāśupālye vaṇijyā ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.07/ Of a <s>Vaiśya</s>: study, performing sacrifices, giving, agriculture, animal husbandry, and trade.

children.text: KAZ01.3.08/ śūdrasya dvijāti.śuśrūṣā vārttā kāru.kuśīlava.karma ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.08/ Of a <s>Śūdra</s>: service to the twice-born, economic activity (<s>vārttā</s>), and the work of artisans and performers.

children.text: KAZ01.3.09/ gṛhasthasya svadharma.ājīvas tulyair asamāna.ṛṣibhir vaivāhyam ṛtu.gāmitvaṃ deva.pitr.atithi.pūjā bhṛtyeṣu tyāgaḥ śeṣa.bhojanaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.09/ For a householder: livelihood through one's own proper duty, marriage with equals not sharing the same lineage of sages, conjugal relations in the proper season, worship of gods, ancestors, and guests, generosity toward dependents, and eating what remains [after serving others].

children.text: KAZ01.3.10/ brahma.cāriṇaḥ svādhyāyo agni.kārya.abhiṣekau bhaikṣa.vratitvam ācārye prāṇa.antikī vṛttis tad.abhāve guru.putre sa-brahma.cāriṇi vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.10/ For a celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>): Vedic study, fire ritual and ablutions, living by begging and vows, lifelong service to the teacher, and in the absence of the teacher, [service] to his son or a fellow student.

children.text: KAZ01.3.11/ vānaprasthasya brahmacaryaṃ bhūmau śayyā jaṭā.ajina.dhāraṇam agni.hotra.abhiṣekau devatā.pitr.atithi.pūjā vanyaś ca^āhāraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.3.11/ For a forest hermit (<s>vānaprastha</s>): celibacy, sleeping on the ground, wearing matted hair and animal skin, fire offerings and ablutions, worship of deities, ancestors, and guests, and forest produce as food.

children.text: KAZ01.3.12/ parivrājakasya jita.indriyatvam anārambho niṣkiṃcanatvaṃ saṅga.tyāgo bhaikṣavratam anekatra^araṇye ca vāso bāhya.ābhyantaraṃ ca śaucam //
children.translated_text: For an ascetic (parivrājaka): mastery over the senses, non-engagement [in worldly affairs], possessionlessness, renunciation of attachments, the vow of begging, dwelling in the wilderness and not in one place, and both external and internal purity.

children.text: KAZ01.3.13/ sarveṣām ahiṃsā satyaṃ śaucam anasūya ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā ca //
children.translated_text: For all: non-violence (ahiṃsā), truthfulness, purity, freedom from envy, compassion, and forbearance.

children.text: KAZ01.3.14/ svadharmaḥ svargāya^ānantyāya ca //
children.translated_text: One's own proper duty (svadharma) leads to heaven and to eternity.

children.text: KAZ01.3.15/ tasya^atikrame lokaḥ saṃkarād ucchidyeta //
children.translated_text: In the transgression of that [duty], the world, through the confusion of classes, would perish.

children.text:
KAZ01.3.16ab/ tasmāt svadharmaṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā na vyabhicārayet /
KAZ01.3.16cd/ svadharmaṃ saṃdadhāno hi pretya ca^iha ca nandati //
children.translated_text:
Therefore, the king should not allow the proper duties of beings to be violated;
for one who upholds proper duty rejoices both in the hereafter and in this world.

children.text:
KAZ01.3.17ab/ vyavasthita.ārya.maryādaḥ kṛta.varṇa.āśrama.sthitiḥ /
KAZ01.3.17cd/ trayyā^abhirakṣito lokaḥ prasīdati na sīdati //E
children.translated_text:
The world, with the boundaries of the noble ones well-established, with the system of social classes and life-stages firmly set,
protected by the Vedic triad (<s>trayī</s>), prospers and does not decline.

children.text:
((īi) Establishing (the necessity of) Economics, and (iv) the ṣcience of Politics)
KAZ01.4.01/ kṛṣi.pāśupālye vaṇijyā ca vārtā, dhānya.paśu.hiraṇya.kupya.viṣṭi.pradānād aupakārikī //
children.translated_text:
((ii) Establishing (the necessity of) Economics, and (iv) the Science of Politics)
Agriculture, animal husbandry, and trade constitute economics (<s>vārttā</s>); it is beneficial through providing grain, cattle, gold, raw materials, and labor.

children.text: KAZ01.4.02/ tayā sva.pakṣaṃ para.pakṣaṃ ca vaśī.karoti kośa.daṇḍābhyām //
children.translated_text: Through it, [the king] brings under his control his own faction and the enemy's faction, by means of the treasury and the army.

children.text: KAZ01.4.03/ ānvīkṣikī trayī vārttānāṃ yoga.kṣema.sādhano daṇḍaḥ, tasya nītir daṇḍa nītiḥ, alabdha.lābha.arthā labdha.parirakṣaṇī rakṣita.vivardhanī vṛddhasya tīrthe pratipādanī ca //
children.translated_text: The rod of force (<s>daṇḍa</s>), which secures the well-being and livelihood of philosophy, the Vedic triad, and economics — its administration is the science of government (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>); its purpose is the acquisition of what has not been obtained, the preservation of what has been obtained, the augmentation of what has been preserved, and the bestowal of the augmented upon worthy recipients.

children.text: KAZ01.4.04/ tasyām āyattā loka.yātrā //
children.translated_text: On it depends the orderly functioning of the world.

children.text: KAZ01.4.05/ "tasmāl loka.yātrā.arthī nityam udyata.daṇḍaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who desires the orderly functioning of the world should always be with the rod of force upraised.

children.text: KAZ01.4.06/ na hy evaṃvidhaṃ vaśa.upanayanam asti bhūtānāṃ yathā daṇḍaḥ /" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: For there is no means of subjugating beings equal to the rod of force — thus say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ01.4.07/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.4.08/ tīkṣṇa.daṇḍo hi bhūtānām udvejanīyo bhavati //
children.translated_text: For one who is harsh in punishment becomes a source of terror to beings.

children.text: KAZ01.4.09/ mṛdu.daṇḍaḥ paribhūyate //
children.translated_text: One who is mild in punishment is treated with contempt.

children.text: KAZ01.4.10/ yathā.arha.daṇḍaḥ pūjyate //
children.translated_text: One who punishes justly is honored.

children.text: KAZ01.4.11/ suvijñāta.praṇīto hi daṇḍaḥ prajā dharma.artha.kāmair yojayati //
children.translated_text: For punishment, when well-considered and properly administered, endows the subjects with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (material gain), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure).

children.text: KAZ01.4.12/ duṣpraṇītaḥ kāma.krodhābhyām avajñānād vā vānaprastha.parivrājakān api kopayati, kiṃ.aṅga punar gṛhasthān //
children.translated_text: When poorly administered — whether through desire, anger, or negligence — it enrages even forest hermits and wandering ascetics, how much more so householders.

children.text: KAZ01.4.13/ apraṇītas tu mātsya.nyāyam udbhāvayati //
children.translated_text: When not administered at all, it gives rise to the law of the fish (<s>mātsyanyāya</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.4.14/ balīyān abalaṃ hi grasate daṇḍa.dhara.abhāve //
children.translated_text: For the strong devours the weak in the absence of one who wields the rod of force.

children.text: KAZ01.4.15/ sa tena guptaḥ prabhavati iti //
children.translated_text: The [world], protected by him [who wields the rod], prevails — thus [it is said].

children.text:
KAZ01.4.16ab/ catur.varṇa.āśramo loko rājñā daṇḍena pālitaḥ /
KAZ01.4.16cd/ svadharma.karma.abhirato vartate sveṣu vartmasu //E
children.translated_text:
The world, consisting of the four social classes and life-stages, when governed by the king through the rod of force,
devoted to its own proper duties and occupations, walks in its appointed paths.

children.text:
(ṣection.2: Association with elders)
KAZ01.5.01/ tasmād daṇḍa.mūlās tisro vidyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Section 2: Association with elders)
Therefore, the three sciences have the rod of force as their foundation.

children.text: KAZ01.5.02/ vinaya.mūlo daṇḍaḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ yoga.kṣema.āvahaḥ //
children.translated_text: The rod of force, rooted in discipline (<s>vinaya</s>), brings welfare and security to living beings.

children.text: KAZ01.5.03/ kṛtakaḥ svābhāvikaś ca vinayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Discipline is of two kinds: acquired and innate.

children.text: KAZ01.5.04/ kriyā hi dravyaṃ vinayati na^adravyam //
children.translated_text: For training disciplines [only] one who has the material [capacity], not one who lacks it.

children.text: KAZ01.5.05/ śuśrūṣā śravaṇa.grahaṇa.dhāraṇa.vijñāna.ūha.apoha.tattva.abhiniviṣṭa.buddhiṃ vidyā vinayati na^itaram //
children.translated_text: Learning disciplines one whose intellect is devoted to obedient listening, hearing, grasping, retaining, discerning, reasoning, and refuting to arrive at truth — not another.

children.text: KAZ01.5.06/ vidyānāṃ tu yathāsvam ācārya.prāmāṇyād vinayo niyamaś ca //
children.translated_text: And discipline and restraint in the sciences come from the authority of the respective teachers.

children.text: KAZ01.5.07/ vṛtta.caula.karmā lipiṃ saṃkhyānaṃ ca^upayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: After the completion of the tonsure ceremony, [the prince] should take up writing and arithmetic.

children.text: KAZ01.5.08/ vṛtta.upanayanas trayīm ānvīkṣikīṃ ca śiṣṭebhyo vārttām adhyakṣebhyo daṇḍa.nītiṃ vaktṛ.prayoktṛbhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: After the initiation ceremony (<s>upanayana</s>), [he should learn] the Vedic triad and philosophy from learned scholars, economics from superintendents, and the science of government from theoreticians and practitioners.

children.text: KAZ01.5.09/ brahmacaryaṃ ca ṣoḍaśād varṣāt //
children.translated_text: And celibate studentship (<s>brahmacarya</s>) from the sixteenth year.

children.text: KAZ01.5.10/ ato go.dānaṃ dāra.karma ca^asya //
children.translated_text: After that, the gift of cattle and the marriage ceremony are [performed] for him.

children.text: KAZ01.5.11/ nityaś ca vidyā.vṛddha.samyogo vinaya.vṛddhy.artham, tan.mūlatvād vinayasya //
children.translated_text: And constant association with learned elders for the growth of discipline, since discipline is rooted in that.

children.text:
KAZ01.5.12/ pūrvam ahar.bhāgaṃ hasty.aśva.ratha.praharaṇa.vidyāsu vinayaṃ gacchet /
KAZ01.5.13/ paścimam itihāsa.śravaṇe //
children.translated_text:
In the first half of the day, [the prince] should receive training in the sciences of elephants, horses, chariots, and weapons;
in the latter half, [he should devote himself to] listening to historical narratives (<s>itihāsa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.5.14/ purāṇam itivṛttam ākhyāyika.udāharaṇaṃ dharma.śāstram artha.śāstraṃ ca^iti^itihāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Purāṇas</s>, historical accounts, tales, illustrative examples, <s>dharmaśāstra</s>, and <s>arthaśāstra</s> — these constitute <s>itihāsa</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.5.15/ śeṣam ahorātra.bhāgam apūrva.grahaṇaṃ gṛhīta.paricayaṃ ca kuryāt, agṛhītānām ābhīkṣṇya.śravaṇaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: In the remaining part of the day and night, he should undertake the study of new material and the revision of what has been learned, and the repeated hearing of what has not been grasped.

children.text: KAZ01.5.16/ śrutādd hi prajñā^upajāyate prajñāyā yogo yogād ātmavattā^iti vidyānāṃ sāmarthyam //
children.translated_text: For from learning arises wisdom, from wisdom [arises] practical application, from practical application [arises] self-possession — this is the efficacy of the sciences.

children.text:
KAZ01.5.17ab/ vidyā.vinīto rājā hi prajānāṃ vinaye rataḥ /
KAZ01.5.17cd/ ananyāṃ pṛthivīṃ bhuṅkte sarva.bhūta.hite rataḥ //E
children.translated_text:
A king disciplined by learning, devoted to the discipline of his subjects,
enjoys the undivided earth, delighting in the welfare of all beings.

children.text:
(ṣection.3: Control over the senses, (i) Casting out the group of six enemies)
KAZ01.6.01/ vidyā vinaya.hetur indriya.jayaḥ kāma.krodha.lobha.māna.mada.harṣa.tyāgāt kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Section 3: Control over the senses, (i) Casting out the group of six enemies)
Learning is the cause of discipline; mastery over the senses must be achieved by abandoning the group of six [enemies]: desire, anger, greed, pride, arrogance, and overjoy.

children.text: KAZ01.6.02/ karṇa.tvag.akṣi.jihvā.ghrāṇa.indriyāṇāṃ śabda.sparśa.rūpa.rasa.gandheṣv avipratipattir indriya.jayaḥ, śāstra.anuṣṭhānaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: The non-deviation of the senses — ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose — with respect to sound, touch, form, taste, and smell is mastery over the senses; or else it is adherence to the teachings of the <s>śāstras</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.6.03/ kṛtsnaṃ hi śāstram idam indriya.jayaḥ //
children.translated_text: For this entire treatise is [essentially about] mastery over the senses.

children.text: KAZ01.6.04/ tad viruddha.vṛttir avaśya.indriyaś cāturanto api rājā sadyo vinaśyati //
children.translated_text: A king whose conduct is contrary to that, who is uncontrolled in his senses, perishes instantly even if he rules over the four quarters of the earth.

children.text: KAZ01.6.05/ yathā dāṇḍakyo nāma bhojaḥ kāmād brāhmaṇa.kanyām abhimanyamānaḥ sa-bandhu.rāṣṭro vinanāśa, karālaś ca vaidehaḥ //
children.translated_text: As, for example, <s>Dāṇḍakya</s>, the lord of the <s>Bhojas</s>, lusting after a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s daughter, perished along with his kinsmen and kingdom, and so did <s>Karāla</s> of <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.6.06/ kopāj janamejayo brāhmaṇeṣu vikrāntaḥ, tāla.jaṅghaś ca bhṛguṣu //
children.translated_text: Through anger, <s>Janamejaya</s>, who committed violence against <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, [was destroyed], and <s>Tālajaṅgha</s> against the <s>Bhṛgus</s>.

children.text:
KAZ01.6.07/ lobhād ailaś cāturvarṇyam atyāhārayamāṇaḥ, sauvīraś ca^ajabinduḥ /
KAZ01.6.08/ mānād rāvaṇaḥ para.dārān aprayacchan, duryodhano rājyād aṃśaṃ ca //
children.translated_text:
Through greed, <s>Aila</s>, who excessively exploited all four social classes, [was destroyed], and <s>Ajabindu</s> of <s>Sauvīra</s>;
through pride, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who refused to return another's wife, and <s>Duryodhana</s>, [who refused] a share of the kingdom.

children.text: KAZ01.6.09/ madād dambhodbhavo bhūta.avamānī, haihayaś ca^arjunaḥ //
children.translated_text: Through arrogance, <s>Dambhodbhava</s>, who showed contempt for all beings, [was destroyed], and <s>Arjuna</s> of the <s>Haihayas</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.6.10/ harṣād vātāpir agastyam atyāsādayan, vṛṣṇi.saṃghaś ca dvaipāyanam iti //
children.translated_text: Through overjoy, <s>Vātāpi</s>, who provoked <s>Agastya</s> [was destroyed], and the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan [who provoked] <s>Dvaipāyana</s> — thus [it is said].

children.text:
KAZ01.6.11ab/ ete ca^anye ca bahavaḥ śatru.ṣaḍ.vargam āśritāḥ /
KAZ01.6.11cd/ sa-bandhu.rāṣṭrā rājāno vineśur ajita.indriyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
These and many other kings, resorting to the group of six enemies,
perished with their kinsmen and kingdoms, being uncontrolled in their senses.

children.text:
KAZ01.6.12ab/ śatru.ṣaḍ.vargam utsṛjya jāmadagnyo jita.indriyaḥ /
KAZ01.6.12cd/ ambarīṣaś ca nābhāgo bubhujāte ciraṃ mahīm //E
children.translated_text:
<s>Jāmadagnya</s>, having cast off the group of six enemies, with senses mastered,
and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and <s>Nābhāga</s>, enjoyed the earth for a long time.

children.text:
((ī) ṭhe life of a sage-like king)
KAZ01.7.01/ tasmād ari.ṣaḍ.varga.tyāgena^indriya.jayaṃ kurvīta, vṛddha.samyogena prajñām, cāreṇa cakṣuḥ, utthānena yoga.kṣema.sādhanam, kārya.anuśāsanena svadharma.sthāpanam, vinayaṃ vidyā.upadeśena, loka.priyatvam artha.samyogena vṛttim //
children.translated_text:
((ii) The life of a sage-like king)
Therefore, [the king] should achieve mastery over the senses by abandoning the group of six enemies, wisdom through association with elders, sight through [the use of] spies, the securing of welfare and livelihood through enterprise, the establishment of proper duty through administration of affairs, discipline through instruction in learning, and popularity through conferring material benefit upon [the people].

children.text: KAZ01.7.02/ evaṃ vaśya.indriyaḥ para.strī.dravya.hiṃsāś ca varjayet, svapnaṃ laulyam anṛtam uddhata.veṣatvam anarthya.samyogam adharma.samyuktam anartha.samyuktaṃ ca vyavahāram //
children.translated_text: Thus, with senses controlled, he should avoid [the property of] other men's wives and goods, and violence; he should avoid [excessive] sleep, fickleness, falsehood, ostentatious dress, association with the harmful, and conduct connected with <s>adharma</s> and with what is unprofitable.

children.text: KAZ01.7.03/ dharma.artha.avirodhena kāmaṃ seveta, na nihsukhaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: He should pursue pleasure (<s>kāma</s>) without conflicting with <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>; he should not be devoid of happiness.

children.text: KAZ01.7.04/ samaṃ vā trivargam anyonya.anubaddham //
children.translated_text: Or, he should pursue the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>) equally, as they are mutually connected.

children.text: KAZ01.7.05/ eko hy atyāsevito dharma.artha.kāmānām ātmānam itarau ca pīḍayati //
children.translated_text: For any one of the three — <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> — when excessively pursued, harms itself and the other two.

children.text: KAZ01.7.06/ artha^eva pradhāna^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Artha</s> (material gain) alone is paramount — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.7.07/ artha.mūlau hi dharma.kāmāv iti //
children.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> are both rooted in <s>artha</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.7.08/ maryādāṃ sthāpayed ācāryān amātyān vā, ya^enam apāya sthānebhyo vārayeyuḥ, chāyā.nālikā.pratodena vā rahasi pramādyantam abhitudeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: He should appoint teachers or ministers who would restrain him from [falling into] dangerous situations, or who would privately admonish him when he errs, as if by [the use of] a shadow-clock and goad.

children.text:
KAZ01.7.09ab/ sahāya.sādhyaṃ rājatvaṃ cakram ekaṃ na vartate /
KAZ01.7.09cd/ kurvīta sacivāṃs tasmāt teṣāṃ ca śṛṇuyān matam //E
children.translated_text:
Kingship can only be achieved with helpers; a single wheel does not turn.
Therefore, he should appoint counselors and listen to their counsel.

children.text:
(Appointment of ministers)
KAZ01.8.01/ "saha.adhyāyino amātyān kurvīta, dṛṣṭa.śauca.sāmarthyatvāt" iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Appointment of ministers)
"He should appoint as ministers those who were his fellow students, since their integrity and capability have been observed" — says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.02/ "te hy asya viśvāsyā bhavanti" iti //
children.translated_text: "For they become trustworthy to him" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.03/ na^iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.04/ "saha.krīḍitatvāt paribhavanty enam //
children.translated_text: "Having been his playmates, they treat him with disrespect.

children.text: KAZ01.8.05/ ye hy asya guhya.sadharmāṇas tān amātyān kurvīta, samāna.śīla.vyasanatvāt //
children.translated_text: Those who share his secret practices — he should appoint them as ministers, since they share the same dispositions and weaknesses.

children.text: KAZ01.8.06/ te hy asya marmajña.bhayān na^aparādhyanti" iti //
children.translated_text: For they, out of fear that he knows their secrets, do not act against him" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.07/ "sādhāraṇa^eṣa doṣaḥ" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is a defect common [to both sides]" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.08/ "teṣām api marmajña.bhayāt kṛta.akṛtāny anuvarteta //
children.translated_text: "He too, out of fear that they know his secrets, would have to go along with their doings, whether right or wrong.

children.text:
KAZ01.8.09ab/ yāvadbhyo guhyam ācaṣṭe janebhyaḥ puruṣa.adhipaḥ /
KAZ01.8.09cd/ avaśaḥ karmaṇā tena vaśyo bhavati tāvatām //
children.translated_text:
To as many people as a lord of men reveals his secrets,
to that many does he become subservient, being helpless through that act.

children.text: KAZ01.8.10/ ya^enam āpatsu prāṇa.ābādha.yuktāsv anugṛhṇīyus tān amātyān kurvīta, dṛṣṭa.anurāgatvāt" iti //
children.translated_text: Those who have supported him in calamities involving danger to life — he should appoint them as ministers, since their devotion has been observed" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.11/ na^iti piśunaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Piśuna</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.12/ "bhaktir eṣā na buddhi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is mere loyalty, not a quality of intellect.

children.text: KAZ01.8.13/ saṃkhyāta.artheṣu karmasu niyuktā ye yathā.ādiṣṭam arthaṃ saviśeṣaṃ vā kuryus tān amātyān kurvīta, dṛṣṭa.guṇatvāt" iti //
children.translated_text: Those who, when appointed to tasks with calculated objectives, accomplish the assigned objective with added value — he should appoint them as ministers, since their ability has been observed" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.14/ na^iti kauṇapadantaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṇapadanta</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.15/ "anyair amātya.guṇair ayuktā hy ete //
children.translated_text: "For these are lacking in other ministerial qualities.

children.text: KAZ01.8.16/ pitṛ.paitāmahān amātyān kurvīta, dṛṣṭa.avadānatvāt //
children.translated_text: He should appoint as ministers those who served his father and grandfather, since their record of service has been observed.

children.text: KAZ01.8.17/ te hy enam apacarantam api na tyajanti, sagandhatvāt //
children.translated_text: For they do not abandon him even when he errs, because of their bond [with the family].

children.text: KAZ01.8.18/ amānuṣeṣv api ca^etad dṛśyate //
children.translated_text: And this is seen even among non-human [creatures].

children.text: KAZ01.8.19/ gāvo hy asagandhaṃ go.gaṇam atikramya sagandheṣv eva^avatiṣṭhante" iti //
children.translated_text: For cows, passing over an unfamiliar herd of cows, settle only among those of the same scent" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.20/ na^iti vātavyādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Vātavyādhi</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.21/ "te hy asya sarvam avagṛhya svāmivat pracaranti //
children.translated_text: "For they, having grasped everything of his, conduct themselves as if they were the master.

children.text: KAZ01.8.22/ tasmān nītivido navān amātyān kurvīta //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he should appoint new ministers who are versed in statecraft.

children.text: KAZ01.8.23/ navās tu yama.sthāne daṇḍa.dharaṃ manyamānā na^aparādhyanti" iti //
children.translated_text: For new [ministers], regarding the wielder of the rod of force as [equivalent to] the god of death, do not act against him" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.24/ na^iti bāhu.dantī putraḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says the son of <s>Bāhudantī</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.25/ "śāstravid adṛṣṭa.karmā karmasu viṣādaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: "One who knows the texts but has not witnessed [practical] affairs falls into despondency in [actual] tasks.

children.text: KAZ01.8.26/ tasmād abhijana.prajñā.śauca.śaurya.anurāga.yuktān amātyān kurvīta, guṇa.prādhānyāt" iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he should appoint as ministers those endowed with noble birth, wisdom, integrity, courage, and loyalty, since the primacy of qualities [is paramount]" — [he says].

children.text: KAZ01.8.27/ sarvam upapannam iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: All [views] are well-founded — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.8.28/ kārya.sāmarthyādd hi puruṣa.sāmarthyaṃ kalpyate //
children.translated_text: For the capability of a person is assessed from the capability [shown] in the task.

children.text:
KAZ01.8.29ab/ sāmarthyaś ca -- vibhajya^amātya.vibhavaṃ deśa.kālau ca karma ca /
KAZ01.8.29cd/ amātyāḥ sarva eva^ete kāryāḥ syur na tu mantriṇaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
And with capability — having assessed the means of ministers, the place, time, and task,
all of these should be made ministers, but not [all of them] counselors.

children.text:
(Appointment of counsellors and chaplain)
KAZ01.9.01/ jānapado abhijātaḥ svavagrahaḥ kṛta.śilpaś cakṣuṣmān prājño dhārayiṣṇur dakṣo vāgmī pragalbhaḥ pratipattimān utsāha.prabhāva.yuktaḥ kleśa.sahaḥ śucir maitro dṛḍha.bhaktiḥ śīla.bala.ārogya.sattva.yuktaḥ stambha.cāpala.hīnaḥ sampriyo vairāṇām akartā^ity amātya.sampat //
children.translated_text:
(Appointment of counsellors and chaplain)
Born in the country, of noble birth, self-reliant, trained in the arts, far-sighted, wise, retentive, dexterous, eloquent, resolute, possessed of initiative and power of judgment, capable of enduring hardship, honest, friendly, of firm loyalty, endowed with character, strength, health, and courage, free from stubbornness and fickleness, amiable, and one who does not create enmities — this is the ideal qualification of a minister (<s>amātyasampad</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.9.02/ ataḥ pāda.argha.guṇa.hīnau madhyama.avarau //
children.translated_text: Those lacking a quarter or a half of these qualities are of middling and inferior [rank respectively].

children.text: KAZ01.9.03/ teṣāṃ janapad.abhijanam avagrahaṃ ca^āptataḥ parīkṣeta, samāna.vidyebhyaḥ śilpaṃ śāstra.cakṣuṣmattāṃ ca, karma.ārambheṣu prajñāṃ dhārayiṣṇutāṃ dākṣyaṃ ca, kathā.yogeṣu vāgmitvaṃ prāgalbhyaṃ pratibhānavattvaṃ ca, saṃvāsibhyaḥ śīla.bala.ārogya.sattva.yogam astambham acāpalaṃ ca, pratyakṣataḥ sampriyatvam avairatvaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.03/ He should ascertain their country of origin and family background through trusted persons; their skill and insight into the treatises (<s>śāstra</s>) from those sharing the same training; their wisdom, perseverance, and dexterity in undertaking tasks; their eloquence, boldness, and ready wit in discussions; their character, strength, health, fortitude, and composure — free from arrogance and fickleness — from those living with them; and their agreeableness and absence of hostility through direct observation.

children.text: KAZ01.9.04/ pratyakṣa.parokṣa.anumeyā hi rāja.vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.04/ For the conduct of a king is to be judged by what is directly perceived, what is reported by others, and what is inferred.

children.text: KAZ01.9.05/ svayaṃ drṣṭaṃ pratyakṣam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.05/ What is seen by oneself is direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.9.06/ para.upadiṣṭaṃ parokṣam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.06/ What is reported by others is indirect knowledge (<s>parokṣa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.9.07/ karmasu kṛtena^akṛta.avekṣaṇam anumeyam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.07/ Evaluating what has been done and what has not been done in tasks is inference (<s>anumeya</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.9.08/ yaugapadyāt tu karmaṇām anekatvād anekasthatvāc ca deśa.kāla.atyayo mā bhūd iti parokṣam amātyaiḥ kārayet // ity amātya.karma /
KAZ01.9.09/ purohitam udita.udita.kula.śīlaṃ sa-aṅge vede daive nimitte daṇḍa.nītyāṃ ca^abhivinītam āpadāṃ daiva.mānuṣīṇām atharvabhir upāyaiś ca pratikartāraṃ kurvīta //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.9.08/ But because tasks are simultaneous, manifold, and distributed across many places, lest there be a lapse of place and time, he should have them carried out indirectly through ministers. Thus ends [the chapter on] the work of ministers.
KAZ01.9.09/ He should appoint as chaplain (<s>purohita</s>) one of distinguished family lineage and character, learned in the <s>Veda</s> together with its auxiliary sciences (<s>aṅgas</s>), in divination, in reading omens, and in the science of government (<s>daṇḍanīti</s>), one who is able to counteract calamities both divine and human through <s>Atharva Veda</s> rites and other means.

children.text: KAZ01.9.10/ tam ācāryaṃ śiṣyaḥ pitaraṃ putro bhṛtyaḥ svāminam iva ca^anuvarteta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.9.10/ Him a student should follow as a teacher, a son his father, and a servant his master.

children.text:
KAZ01.9.11ab/ brāhmaṇena^edhitaṃ kṣatraṃ mantri.mantra.abhimantritam /
KAZ01.9.11cd/ jayaty ajitam atyantaṃ śāstra.anugama.śastritam //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.9.11ab/ Royal power (<s>kṣatra</s>) nurtured by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, consecrated by the counsel of ministers,
KAZ01.9.11cd/ conquers what has never been conquered, being armed with the weapons of the treatises (<s>śāstra</s>).

children.text:
(Ascertainment of the integrity or the absence of integrity of minister by means of secret tests)
KAZ01.10.01/ mantri.purohita.sakhaḥ sāmānyeṣv adhikaraṇeṣu sthāpayitvā^amātyān upadhābhiḥ śodhayet //
children.translated_text:
(Ascertainment of the integrity or the absence of integrity of ministers by means of secret tests)
KAZ01.10.01/ Together with the chaplain and a trusted companion, having placed ministers in common offices, he should test them through secret probes (<s>upadhā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.02/ purohitam ayājya.yājana.adhyāpane niyuktam amṛṣyamāṇaṃ rājā^avakṣipet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.02/ The king should dismiss the chaplain who has been appointed to perform sacrifices and teach for unworthy persons and who shows indignation [at his dismissal].

children.text: KAZ01.10.03/ sa sattribhiḥ śapatha.pūrvam ekaikam amātyam upajāpayet - "adhārmiko ayaṃ rājā, sādhu dhārmikam anyam asya tat.kulīnam aparuddhaṃ kulyam eka.pragrahaṃ sāmantam āṭavikam aupapādikaṃ vā pratipādayāmaḥ, sarveṣām etad rocate, kathaṃ vā tava" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.03/ He [the chaplain], together with agents, should approach each minister individually with an oath-bound proposal: 'This king is unrighteous. Come, let us install another righteous one — someone of his own lineage, or an unimpeded kinsman, or a sole sovereign, or a neighboring king, or a frontier chief, or one who has risen by his own merit. All approve of this — what say you?'

children.text: KAZ01.10.04/ pratyākhyāne śuciḥ / iti dharma.upadhā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.04/ One who refuses is proven pure. This is the test of righteousness (<s>dharma-upadhā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.05/ senā.patir asat.pragraheṇa^avakṣiptaḥ sattribhir ekaikam amātyam upajāpayet lobhanīyena^arthena rāja.vināśāya, "sarveṣām etad rocate, kathaṃ vā tava" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.05/ The commander-in-chief, dismissed under a false pretext, should through agents approach each minister individually with an enticing offer of wealth for the destruction of the king: 'All approve of this — what say you?'

children.text: KAZ01.10.06/ pratyākhyāne śuciḥ / ity artha.upadhā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.06/ One who refuses is proven pure. This is the test of material gain (<s>artha-upadhā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.07/ parivrājikā labdha.viśvāsā^antaḥpure kṛta.satkārā mahā.mātram ekaikam upajapet - "rāja.mahiṣī tvāṃ kāmayate kṛta.samāgama.upāyā, mahān arthaś ca te bhaviṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.07/ A female wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājikā</s>), having gained trust within the royal harem and being honored there, should approach each high officer individually: 'The chief queen desires you; she has arranged a means of meeting. A great fortune will also come to you.'

children.text: KAZ01.10.08/ pratyākhyāne śuciḥ / iti kāma.upadhā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.08/ One who refuses is proven pure. This is the test of pleasure (<s>kāma-upadhā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.09/ prahavaṇa.nimittam eko amātyaḥ sarvān amātyān āvāhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.09/ On the pretext of a festival, one minister should convene all the ministers.

children.text: KAZ01.10.10/ tena^udvegena rājā tān avarundhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.10/ Alarmed by this [gathering], the king should imprison them.

children.text: KAZ01.10.11/ kāpaṭikaś ca^atra pūrva.avaruddhas teṣām artha.māna.avakṣiptam ekaikam amātyam upajapet - "asat pravṛtto ayaṃ rājā, sādhv enaṃ hatvā^anyaṃ pratipādayāmaḥ, sarveṣām etad rocate, kathaṃ vā tava" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.11/ And there, an undercover agent (<s>kāpaṭika</s>), previously imprisoned, should approach each minister individually — one whose wealth and honor have been taken away — saying: 'This king acts wrongly. Come, let us kill him and install another. All approve of this — what say you?'

children.text: KAZ01.10.12/ pratyākhyāne śuciḥ / iti bhaya.upadhā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.12/ One who refuses is proven pure. This is the test of fear (<s>bhaya-upadhā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.13/ tatra dharma.upadhā.śuddhān dharma.sthīya.kaṇṭaka.śodhaneṣu karmasu sthāpayet, artha.upadhā.śuddhān samāhartṛ.samnidhātṛ.nicaya.karmasu, kāma.upadhā śuddhān bāhya.ābhyantara.vihāra.rakṣāsu, bhaya.upadhā.śuddhān āsanna.kāryeṣu rājñaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.13/ Among these, those proven pure through the test of righteousness should be appointed in legal administration (<s>dharmasthīya</s>) and tasks of eliminating thorns [anti-criminal operations]; those proven pure through the test of wealth, in the offices of the collector (<s>samāhartṛ</s>), the treasurer (<s>saṃnidhātṛ</s>), and revenue operations; those proven pure through the test of pleasure, in guarding the outer and inner recreation grounds; those proven pure through the test of fear, in tasks close to the king's person.

children.text: KAZ01.10.14/ sarva.upadhā.śuddhān mantriṇaḥ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.14/ Those proven pure through all tests should be made counselors (<s>mantriṇas</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.10.15/ sarvatra^aśucīn khani.dravya.hasti.vana.karma.anteṣu upayojayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.10.15/ Those impure in all tests should be employed at mines, timber operations, and elephant forests.

children.text:
KAZ01.10.16ab/ trivarga.bhaya.saṃśuddhān amātyān sveṣu karmasu /
KAZ01.10.16cd/ adhikuryād yathā śaucam ity ācāryā vyavasthitāḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.10.16ab/ Ministers proven pure through the three tests of the triple goals (<s>trivarga</s>) and fear,
KAZ01.10.16cd/ should be appointed in their respective offices according to their purity — so the teachers have determined.

children.text:
KAZ01.10.17ab/ na tv eva kuryād ātmānaṃ devīṃ vā lakṣyam īśvaraḥ /
KAZ01.10.17cd/ śauca.hetor amātyānām etat kauṭilya.darśanam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.10.17ab/ But the sovereign should never make himself or the queen a target
KAZ01.10.17cd/ for the sake of testing the ministers' purity — this is the view of <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text:
KAZ01.10.18ab/ na dūṣaṇam aduṣṭasya viṣeṇa^iva^ambhasaś caret /
KAZ01.10.18cd/ kadācidd hi praduṣṭasya na^adhigamyeta bheṣajam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.10.18ab/ One should not corrupt the uncorrupted, as if poisoning water;
KAZ01.10.18cd/ for perhaps, once corrupted, no remedy might be found.

children.text:
KAZ01.10.19ab/ kṛtā ca kaluṣā.buddhir upadhābhiś caturvidhā /
KAZ01.10.19cd/ na^agatvā^antaṃ nivarteta sthitā sattvavatāṃ dhṛtau //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.10.19ab/ An intellect once made impure through the fourfold tests
KAZ01.10.19cd/ would not turn back without going to the end, [only] being held steady by the resolve of the strong-willed.

children.text:
KAZ01.10.20ab/ tasmād bāhyam adhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā kārye caturvidhe /
KAZ01.10.20cd/ śauca.aśaucam amātyānāṃ rājā mārgeta sattribhiḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.10.20ab/ Therefore, having established an external basis for the fourfold operation,
KAZ01.10.20cd/ the king should ascertain the purity and impurity of ministers through agents.

children.text:
(Appointment of persons in secret service)
KAZ01.11.01/ upadhābhiḥ śuddha.amātya.vargo gūḍha.puruṣān utpādayet kāpaṭika.udāsthita.gṛha.patika.vaidehaka.tāpasa.vyañjanān sattri.tīṣkṇa.rasada.bhikṣukīś ca //
children.translated_text:
(Appointment of persons in secret service)
KAZ01.11.01/ The group of ministers proven pure through the tests should create secret agents (<s>gūḍha-puruṣas</s>) in the guise of fraudulent students (<s>kāpaṭika</s>), recluses (<s>udāsthita</s>), householders (<s>gṛhapatika</s>), traders (<s>vaidehaka</s>), and ascetics (<s>tāpasa</s>), as well as classmate-spies (<s>sattri</s>), firebrand agents (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), poison-givers (<s>rasada</s>), and mendicant women (<s>bhikṣukī</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.02/ para.marmajñaḥ pragalbhaś chātraḥ kāpaṭikaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.02/ A student who knows the enemy's vulnerabilities and is bold — he is the fraudulent student (<s>kāpaṭika</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.03/ tam artha.mānābhyāṃ protsāhya mantrī brūyāt - "rājānaṃ māṃ ca pramāṇaṃ kṛtvā yasya yad akuśalaṃ paśyasi tat tadānīm eva pratyādiśa" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.03/ Him the minister should encourage with wealth and honor and say: 'Taking the king and me as your authority, whatever misconduct you see in anyone, report it immediately.'

children.text: KAZ01.11.04/ pravrajyā pratyavasitaḥ prajñā.śauca.yukta udāsthitaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.04/ One who has renounced the monastic life and is endowed with wisdom and integrity — he is the recluse (<s>udāsthita</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.05/ sa vārttā.karma.pradiṣṭāyāṃ bhūmau prabhūta.hiraṇya.antevāsī karma kārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.05/ He, on land designated for agricultural work, should carry on operations with a large following and ample gold.

children.text: KAZ01.11.06/ karma.phalāc ca sarva.pravrajitānāṃ grāsa.ācchādana.āvasathān pratividadhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.06/ And from the profits of the work, he should provide food, clothing, and shelter for all the renunciants.

children.text: KAZ01.11.07/ vṛtti.kāmāṃś ca^upajapet - "etena^eva veṣeṇa rāja.arthaś caritavyo bhakta.vetana.kāle ca^upasthātavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.07/ And those seeking a livelihood should be recruited: 'In this very guise, the king's business must be carried out, and at the time of rations and pay, you must present yourselves.'

children.text: KAZ01.11.08/ sarva.pravrajitāś ca svaṃ svaṃ vargam evam upajapeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.08/ And all the renunciants should similarly recruit their own respective groups.

children.text: KAZ01.11.09/ karṣako vṛtti.kṣīṇaḥ prajñā.śauca.yukto gṛha.patika.vyañjanaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.09/ A farmer who has lost his livelihood, endowed with wisdom and integrity — he has the appearance of a householder agent (<s>gṛhapatika</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.10/ sa kṛṣi.karma.pradiṣṭāyāṃ bhūmau - iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.10/ He, on land designated for farming — the rest is the same as before.

children.text: KAZ01.11.11/ vāṇijako vṛtti.kṣīṇaḥ prajñā.śauca.yukto vaidehaka.vyañjanaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.11/ A trader who has lost his livelihood, endowed with wisdom and integrity — he has the appearance of a merchant agent (<s>vaidehaka</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.12/ sa vaṇik.karma.pradiṣṭāyāṃ bhūmau - iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.12/ He, on land designated for trade — the rest is the same as before.

children.text: KAZ01.11.13/ muṇḍo jaṭilo vā vṛtti.kāmas tāpasa.vyañjanaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.13/ A shaven-headed or matted-hair [person] seeking a livelihood — he has the appearance of an ascetic agent (<s>tāpasa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.11.14/ sa nagara.abhyāśe prabhūta.muṇḍa.jaṭila.antevāsī śākaṃ yava.muṣṭiṃ vā māsa.dvimāsa.antaraṃ prakāśam aśnīyāt, gūḍham iṣṭam āhāram //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.14/ He, near a city, with a large following of shaven-headed and matted-hair disciples, should eat publicly only vegetables or a handful of barley at intervals of one or two months, but secretly [consume] whatever food he desires.

children.text: KAZ01.11.15/ vaidehaka.antevāsinaś ca^enaṃ samiddha.yogair arcayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.15/ And the followers of the merchant agent should honor him with displays of successful results.

children.text: KAZ01.11.16/ śiṣyāś ca^asya^āvedayeyuḥ - "asau siddhaḥ sāmedhikaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.16/ And his disciples should announce: 'This one is accomplished, possessed of supernatural powers (<s>siddhi</s>).'

children.text: KAZ01.11.17/ samedha.āśāstibhiś ca^abhigatānām aṅga.vidyayā śiṣya.saṃjñābhiś ca karmāṇy abhijane avasitāny ādiśet - alpa.lābham agni.dāhaṃ cora.bhayaṃ dūṣya.vadhaṃ tuṣṭi.dānaṃ videśa.pravṛtti.jñānam, "idam adya śvo vā bhaviṣyati, idaṃ vā rājā kariṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.17/ And to those who approach seeking prognostication of success, he should predict, using the science of physiognomy (<s>aṅga-vidyā</s>) and signals from disciples, events already concluded in their lives — small gains, losses by fire, dangers from thieves, punishment of the guilty, gifts of favor, knowledge of events in foreign lands — [saying:] 'This will happen today or tomorrow' or 'This the king will do.'

children.text: KAZ01.11.18/ tad asya gūḍhāḥ sattriṇaś ca sampādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.18/ And his hidden agents and classmate-spies should bring these predictions to fulfillment.

children.text: KAZ01.11.19/ sattva.prajñā.vākya.śakti.sampannānāṃ rāja.bhāgyam anuvyāharet, mantri.samyogaṃ ca brūyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.19/ For those endowed with courage, wisdom, and eloquence, he should foretell royal fortune and arrange a meeting with the minister.

children.text: KAZ01.11.20/ mantrī ca^eṣāṃ vṛtti.karmabhyāṃ viyateta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.20/ And the minister should support them with livelihood and work.

children.text: KAZ01.11.21/ ye ca kāraṇād abhikruddhās tān artha.mānābhyāṃ śamayet, akāraṇa.kruddhāṃs tūṣṇīṃ daṇḍena, rāja.dviṣṭa.kāriṇaś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.11.21/ Those who are angered with just cause should be pacified with wealth and honor; those who are angry without cause should be silently punished, as should those who act against the king.

children.text:
KAZ01.11.22ab/ pūjitāś ca^artha.mānābhyāṃ rājñā rāja.upajīvinām /
KAZ01.11.22cd/ jānīyuḥ śaucam ity etāḥ pañca.saṃsthāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.11.22ab/ And those honored by the king with wealth and status among the royal dependents
KAZ01.11.22cd/ should ascertain their purity — these five establishments (<s>saṃsthās</s>) have been declared.

children.text:
(Appointment of roving spies^ ṛules for secret servants)
KAZ01.12.01/ ye ca^apy asmabandhino avaśya.bhartavyās te lakṣaṇam aṅga.vidyāṃ jambhaka.vidyāṃ māyā.gatam āśrama.dharmaṃ nimittam antara.cakram ity adhīyānāḥ sattriṇaḥ, saṃsarga.vidyāṃ ca //
children.translated_text:
(Appointment of roving spies; rules for secret servants)
KAZ01.12.01/ And those who have no family ties and must inevitably be maintained — they become classmate-spies (<s>sattri</s>), studying the science of physiognomy (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), body-language reading (<s>aṅga-vidyā</s>), sorcery (<s>jambhaka-vidyā</s>), illusory arts (<s>māyā</s>), the duties of the life-stages (<s>āśrama-dharma</s>), divination (<s>nimitta</s>), and secret communication (<s>antara-cakra</s>), as well as the science of association (<s>saṃsarga-vidyā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.12.02/ ye janapade śūrās tyakta.ātmāno hastinaṃ vyālaṃ vā dravya.hetoḥ pratiyodhayeyus te tīkṣṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.02/ Those in the countryside who are courageous, who have renounced their lives, and who would fight an elephant or a wild beast for the sake of reward — they are the firebrand agents (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.12.03/ ye bandhuṣu nihsnehāḥ krūrā alasāś ca te rasadāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.03/ Those who are devoid of affection for their relatives, cruel, and idle — they are the poison-givers (<s>rasada</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.12.04/ parivrājikā vṛtti.kāmā daridrā vidhavā pragalbhā brāhmaṇy antaḥpure kṛta.satkārā mahā.mātra.kulāny abhigacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.04/ A female wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājikā</s>) seeking a livelihood, destitute, widowed, and bold — a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> [of this type] should, having been honored within the royal harem, visit the households of high officers.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.05/ etayā muṇḍā vṛṣalyo vyākhyātāḥ // iti saṃcārāḥ /
KAZ01.12.06/ tān rājā sva.viṣaye mantri.purohita.senā.pati.yuva.rāja.dauvārika.antarvaṃśika.praśāstṛ.samāhartṛ.samnidhātṛ.pradeṣṭṛ.nāyaka.paura.vyāvahārika.kārmāntika.mantri.pariṣad.adhyakṣa.daṇḍa.durga.antapāla.āṭavikeṣu śraddheya.deśa.veṣa.śilpa.bhāṣā.abhijana.apadeśān bhaktitaḥ sāmarthya.yogāc ca^apasarpayet //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.12.05/ By analogy with her, shaven-headed <s>Śūdra</s> women are also explained. Thus ends [the section on] roving spies.
KAZ01.12.06/ The king should deploy them in his own realm — among the minister, chaplain, commander-in-chief, crown prince, chief of the palace guard, chief of the inner apartments, the chief justice, the collector, the treasurer, the magistrate, the <s>nāyaka</s>, the city overseer, the law officer, the superintendent of manufactures, the council of ministers, the superintendent of military departments, the commandant of the fort, and the frontier commanders and forest chiefs — agents with credible cover of region, dress, craft, language, and birth, according to loyalty and fitness for employment.

children.text: KAZ01.12.07/ teṣāṃ bāhyaṃ cāraṃ chatra.bhṛṅgāra.vyajana.pāduka.āsana.yāna.vāhana.upagrāhiṇas tīkṣṇā vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.07/ The firebrand agents (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) should know their external intelligence — [carried by] those who attend them bearing the umbrella, water vessel, fan, sandals, seat, conveyance, and mount.

children.text: KAZ01.12.08/ taṃ sattriṇaḥ saṃsthāsv arpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.08/ The classmate-spies (<s>sattri</s>) should channel that [intelligence] through the establishments.

children.text: KAZ01.12.09/ sūda.ārālika.snāpaka.saṃvāhaka.āstaraka.kalpaka.prasādhaka.udaka.paricārakā rasadāḥ kubja.vāmana.kirāta.mūka.badhira.jaḍa.andhac.chadmāno naṭa.nartaka.gāyana.vādaka.vāg.jīvana.kuśīlavāḥ striyaś ca^ābhyantaraṃ cāraṃ vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.09/ Cooks, kitchen attendants, bath attendants, masseurs, bed-makers, barbers, dressers, water-servers — the poison-givers (<s>rasada</s>) — and dwarfs, hunchbacks, <s>Kirātas</s>, the mute, deaf, dull, and blind in disguise, as well as actors, dancers, singers, musicians, storytellers, and buffoons, and women — these should know the internal intelligence.

children.text: KAZ01.12.10/ taṃ bhikṣkyaḥ saṃsthāsv aprayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.10/ The mendicant women (<s>bhikṣukī</s>) should channel that [intelligence] through the establishments.

children.text: KAZ01.12.11/ saṃsthānām antevāsinaḥ saṃjñā.lipibhiś cāra.saṃcāraṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.11/ The disciples of the establishments should conduct the exchange of intelligence through coded signs and secret writing.

children.text: KAZ01.12.12/ na ca^anyonyaṃ saṃsthās te vā vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.12/ Neither the establishments nor they [the agents] should know one another.

children.text: KAZ01.12.13/ bhikṣukī.pratiṣedhe dvāhstha.paramparā mātā.pitṛ.vyañjanāḥ śilpa.kārikāḥ kuśīlavā dāsyo vā gīta.pāṭhya.vādya.bhāṇḍa.gūḍha.lekhya.saṃjñābhir vā cāraṃ nirhareyuḥ.//
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.13/ When mendicant women are denied access, intelligence should be extracted through a chain of doorkeepers, or through those disguised as mother and father, female artisans, actresses, female slaves — or through songs, recitations, musical instruments, and vessels containing concealed written messages.

children.text: KAZ01.12.14/ dīrgha.roga.unmāda.agni.rasa.visargeṇa vā gūḍha.nirgamanam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.14/ Or secret exit [of intelligence] may be effected by simulating a prolonged illness, madness, fire, poisoning, or an evacuation.

children.text: KAZ01.12.15/ trayāṇām eka.vākye sampratyayaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.15/ Confidence [in a report] is established when three [agents] agree in one statement.

children.text: KAZ01.12.16/ teṣām abhīkṣṇa.vinipāte tūṣṇīṃ.daṇḍaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.16/ For those who repeatedly fail, the punishment is silent [i.e., secret] sanction or removal.

children.text: KAZ01.12.17/ kaṇṭaka.śodhana.uktāś ca^apasarpāḥ pareṣu kṛta.vetanā vaseyur asampātinaś cāra.artham //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.17/ And the roving agents mentioned in connection with the removal of thorns [anti-criminal operations] should reside in the enemy's territory as paid [double] agents, without meeting one another, for the purpose of espionage.

children.text: KAZ01.12.18/ ta ubhaya.vetanāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.12.18/ They receive wages from both sides.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.19ab/ gṛhīta.putra.dārāṃś ca kuryād ubhaya.vetanān /
KAZ01.12.19cd/ tāṃś ca^ari.prahitān vidyāt teṣāṃ śaucaṃ ca tadvidhaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.12.19ab/ Those whose wives and children have been seized should be made into double agents;
KAZ01.12.19cd/ and those sent by the enemy should be recognized, and their purity [tested] by similar methods.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.20ab/ evaṃ śatrau ca mitre ca madhyame ca^āvapec carān /
KAZ01.12.20cd/ udāsīne ca teṣāṃ ca tīrtheṣv aṣṭādaśasv api //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.12.20ab/ Thus, he should deploy spies among the enemy, the ally, the middle [king],
KAZ01.12.20cd/ the neutral [king], and in the eighteen types of high officers (<s>tīrthas</s>) of each.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.21ab/ antar.gṛha.carās teṣāṃ kubja.vāmana.paṇḍakāḥ /
KAZ01.12.21cd/ śilpavatyaḥ striyo mūkāś citrāś ca mleccha.jātayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Their inner-household operatives are hunchbacks, dwarfs, and eunuchs, women skilled in crafts, mute persons, and those of various <s>Mleccha</s> (barbarian) castes.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.22ab/ durgeṣu vaṇijaḥ saṃsthā durga.ante siddha.tāpasāḥ /
KAZ01.12.22cd/ karṣaka.udāsthitā rāṣṭre rāṣṭra.ante vraja.vāsinaḥ //
children.translated_text: In forts, merchants [serve as] stationary agents; at the outskirts of forts, accomplished ascetics; in the countryside, those posing as cultivators; at the borders of the countryside, those dwelling in cattle camps.

children.text:
KAZ01.12.23ab/ vane vana.carāḥ kāryāḥ śramaṇa.āṭavika.ādayaḥ /
KAZ01.12.23cd/ para.pravṛtti.jñāna.arthāḥ śīghrāś.cāra.paramparāḥ //
children.translated_text: In the forest, forest-dwellers such as wandering ascetics and forest tribals should be employed. For knowledge of the enemy's activities, swift chains of spies [should be established].

children.text:
KAZ01.12.24ab/ parasya ca^ete boddhavyās tādṛśair eva tādṛśāḥ /
KAZ01.12.24cd/ cāra.saṃcāriṇaḥ saṃsthā gūḍhāś ca^agūḍha.saṃjñitāḥ //
children.translated_text: And those [spies] of the enemy should be detected by similar [agents] of similar kind. The mobile agents of spies, both the covert and those called overt —

children.text:
KAZ01.12.25ab/ akṛtyān kṛtya.pakṣīyair darśitān kārya.hetubhiḥ /
KAZ01.12.25cd/ para.apasarpa.jñāna.arthaṃ mukhyān anteṣu vāsayet //E
children.translated_text: those who are not [truly] loyal, shown [to be so] by those on the side of the loyal through manufactured pretexts — for the purpose of knowing the enemy's infiltrators, he should settle prominent persons at the borders.

children.text: (Keeping a watch over the seducible and non-seducible parties in one's own territory)
children.translated_text: (Keeping a watch over the seducible and non-seducible parties in one's own territory)

children.text: KAZ01.13.01/ kṛta.mahā.mātra.apasarpaḥ paura.jānapadān apasarpayet //
children.translated_text: Having deployed spies against the high officials, he should spy upon the townspeople and rural folk.

children.text: KAZ01.13.02/ sattriṇo dvandvinas tīrtha.sabhā.pūga.jana.samavāyeṣu vivādaṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Secret agents working in pairs should stir up disputes in assemblies of pilgrimage sites, halls, guilds, and popular gatherings.

children.text: KAZ01.13.03/ "sarva.guṇa.sampannaś ca^ayaṃ rājā śrūyate, na ca^asya kaścid guṇo dṛśyate yaḥ paura.jānapadān daṇḍa.karābhyāṃ pīḍayati" iti //
children.translated_text: "This king is reputed to possess all virtues, yet none of his virtues are visible — he who oppresses the townspeople and rural folk with punishments and taxes" — thus [they should say].

children.text: KAZ01.13.04/ tatra ye^anupraśaṃseyus tān itaras taṃ ca pratiṣedhayet //
children.translated_text: Thereupon, those who express approval [of such talk], the other [agent] should note them and restrain that [speaker].

children.text: KAZ01.13.05/ "mātsya.nyāya.abhibhūtāḥ prajā manuṃ vaivasvataṃ rājānaṃ cakrire //
children.translated_text: "The people, oppressed by the law of the fish (<s>mātsyanyāya</s>), made <s>Manu Vaivasvata</s> their king.

children.text: KAZ01.13.06/ dhānya.ṣaḍ.bhāgaṃ paṇya.daśa.bhāgaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca^asya bhāga.dheyaṃ prakalpayām-āsuḥ //
children.translated_text: They allocated to him as his share one-sixth of the grain, one-tenth of the merchandise, and gold.

children.text: KAZ01.13.07/ tena bhṛtā rājānaḥ prajānāṃ yoga.kṣema.āvahāḥ //
children.translated_text: Sustained by that [share], kings ensure the welfare and security (<s>yoga-kṣema</s>) of the people.

children.text: KAZ01.13.08/ teṣāṃ kilbiṣam adaṇḍa.karā haranty ayoga.kṣema.āvahāś ca prajānām //
children.translated_text: Those who do not impose punishment and taxes take away [the people's] well-being, and [those who are] not providers of welfare and security to the people —

children.text: KAZ01.13.09/ tasmād uñcha.ṣaḍ.bhāgam āraṇyakā^api nirvapanti - "tasya^etad bhāga.dheyaṃ yo^asmān gopāyati" iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even forest-dwellers offer one-sixth of their gleanings — 'This is his due share, [the one] who protects us,' thus.

children.text: KAZ01.13.10/ indra.yama.sthānam etad rājānaḥ pratyakṣa.heḍa.prasādāḥ //
children.translated_text: Kings occupy the position of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Yama</s>, dispensing visible displeasure and favor.

children.text: KAZ01.13.11/ tān avamanyamānān daivo^api daṇḍaḥ spṛśati //
children.translated_text: Even divine punishment touches those who show contempt for them.

children.text: KAZ01.13.12/ tasmād rājāno na^avamantavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, kings should not be treated with disrespect."

children.text: KAZ01.13.13/ ity evaṃ kṣudrakān pratiṣedhayet //
children.translated_text: Thus he should restrain the petty [agitators].

children.text: KAZ01.13.14/ kiṃ.vadantīṃ ca vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And they should ascertain what people are saying (<s>kiṃvadantī</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.13.15/ ye ca^asya dhānya.paśu.hiraṇyāny ājīvanti, tair upakurvanti vyasane^abhyudaye vā, kupitaṃ bandhuṃ rāṣṭraṃ vā vyāvartayanti, amitram āṭavikaṃ vā pratiṣedhayanti, teṣāṃ muṇḍa.jaṭila.vyañjanās tuṣṭa.atuṣṭatvaṃ vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who earn their livelihood through his grain, cattle, and gold, who assist him in adversity or prosperity, who turn back a rebellious kinsman or territory, or who repel an enemy or forest chieftain — agents disguised as mendicants and ascetics should ascertain the satisfaction or dissatisfaction of these [persons].

children.text: KAZ01.13.16/ tuṣṭān bhūyo^artha.mānābhyāṃ pūjayet //
children.translated_text: The satisfied should be honored further with wealth and respect.

children.text: KAZ01.13.17/ atuṣṭāṃs tuṣṭi.hetos tyāgena sāmnā ca prasādayet //
children.translated_text: The dissatisfied should be appeased through gifts and conciliation as a means of gaining their satisfaction.

children.text: KAZ01.13.18/ parasparād vā bhedayed enān, sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhebhyaś ca //
children.translated_text: Or he should create division among them by setting them against one another, and [also set them] against neighboring kings, forest chieftains, kinsmen of the ruling house, and those who are confined.

children.text: KAZ01.13.19/ tathā^apy atuṣyato daṇḍa.kara.sādhana.adhikāreṇa janapada.vidveṣaṃ grāhayet //
children.translated_text: If still dissatisfied, he should make them incur the hatred of the people by entrusting them with the authority to collect punishments and taxes.

children.text: KAZ01.13.20/ viviṣṭān upāṃśu.daṇḍena janapada.kopena vā sādhayet //
children.translated_text: The most dangerous ones he should neutralize through secret punishment or by inciting the people's wrath.

children.text: KAZ01.13.21/ gupta.putra.dārān ākara.karma.anteṣu vā vāsayet pareṣām āspada.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: He should settle them, with their sons and wives guarded, in mines and frontier posts, out of fear that they might become a base for enemies.

children.text: KAZ01.13.22/ kruddha.lubdha.bhīta.māninas tu pareṣāṃ kṛtyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who are angry, greedy, frightened, or proud — these are susceptible to the enemy's schemes.

children.text: KAZ01.13.23/ teṣāṃ kārtāntika.naimittika.mauhūrtika.vyañjanāḥ paraspara.abhisambandham amitra.āṭavika.sambandhaṃ vā vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Agents disguised as astrologers, interpreters of omens, and horoscope-readers should ascertain their mutual connections or their connections with enemy [kings] and forest chieftains.

children.text:
KAZ01.13.24/ tuṣṭān artha.mānābhyāṃ pūjayet /
KAZ01.13.25/ atuṣṭān sāma.dāna.bheda.daṇḍaiḥ sādhayet //
children.translated_text: The satisfied should be honored with wealth and respect. The dissatisfied should be dealt with through conciliation, gifts, dissension, and force.

children.text:
KAZ01.13.26ab/ evaṃ sva.viṣaye kṛtyān akṛtyāṃś ca vicakṣaṇaḥ /
KAZ01.13.26cd/ para.upajāpāt samrakṣet pradhānān kṣudrakān api //E
children.translated_text: Thus, the wise one should protect from the enemy's subversion both the prominent and the petty persons in his own territory, both the seducible and the non-seducible.

children.text: (Winning over the seducible and non-seducible parties in the enemy"s territory)
children.translated_text: (Winning over the seducible and non-seducible parties in the enemy's territory)

children.text: KAZ01.14.01/ kṛtya.akṛtya.pakṣa.upagrahaḥ sva.viṣaye vyākhyātaḥ, para.viṣaye vācyaḥ //
children.translated_text: The winning over of the seducible and non-seducible factions has been explained for one's own territory; [now] it shall be stated for the enemy's territory.

children.text:
KAZ01.14.02/ saṃśrutya^arthān vipralabdhaḥ, tulya.kāriṇoḥ śilpe vā^upakāre vā vimānitaḥ, vallabha.avaruddhaḥ, samāhūya parājitaḥ, pravāsa.upataptaḥ, kṛtvā vyayam alabdha.kāryaḥ, svadharmād dāyādyād vā^uparuddhaḥ, māna.adhikārābhyāṃ bhraṣṭaḥ, kulyair antarhitaḥ, prasabha.abhimṛṣṭa.strīkaḥ, kāra.abhinyastaḥ, para.ukta.daṇḍitaḥ, mithyā.ācāra.vāritaḥ, sarva.svam
āhāritaḥ, bandhana.parikliṣṭaḥ, pravāsita.bandhuḥ - iti kruddha.vargaḥ //
