children.translated_text: One who has been cheated after being promised benefits; one who has been slighted despite equal service in a craft or favor; one obstructed by a royal favorite; one who was summoned and then defeated; one afflicted by exile; one who incurred expenditure but failed to accomplish his objective; one blocked from his rightful inheritance or patrimony; one fallen from honor and office; one suppressed by his own kinsmen; one whose wife was forcibly violated; one subjected to imprisonment with hard labor; one punished at another's instigation; one whose misconduct was publicly exposed; one whose entire property was confiscated; one distressed by imprisonment; one whose relatives were banished — this is the angry group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.03/ svayam upahataḥ, viprakṛtaḥ, pāpa.karma.abhikhyātaḥ, tulya.doṣa.daṇḍena^udvignaḥ, paryātta.bhūmiḥ, daṇḍena^upanataḥ, sarva.adhikaraṇasthaḥ, sahasā.upacita.arthaḥ, tat.kulīna.upāśaṃsuḥ, pradviṣṭo rājñā, rāja.dveṣī ca - iti bhīta.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who has personally suffered injury; one who has been mistreated; one notorious for evil deeds; one alarmed by punishment of those with similar offenses; one whose land has been seized; one subdued by punishment; one who is a party in every tribunal; one who has suddenly accumulated wealth; one whose clan members cherish expectations; one hated by the king; and one who hates the king — this is the frightened group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.04/ parikṣīṇaḥ, anya.ātta.svaḥ, kadaryaḥ, vyasanī, atyāhita.vyavahāraś ca - iti lubdha.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who is impoverished; one whose property has been seized by another; a miser; one addicted to vices; and one engaged in ruinous transactions — this is the greedy group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.05/ ātma.sambhāvitaḥ, māna.kāmaḥ, śatru.pūjā.amarṣitaḥ, nīcair upahitaḥ, tīkṣṇaḥ, sāhasikaḥ, bhogena^asaṃtuṣṭaḥ - iti māni.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who overestimates himself; one who craves honor; one who resents the enemy receiving honor; one slighted by those of lower rank; one who is sharp-tempered; one who is reckless; one who is not satisfied with [his current] enjoyments — this is the proud group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.06/ teṣāṃ muṇḍa.jaṭila.vyañjanair yo yad.bhaktiḥ kṛtya.pakṣīyas taṃ tena^upajāpayet //
children.translated_text: Through agents disguised as mendicants and ascetics, whichever [person] is inclined toward which [faction] among the seducible, him he should subvert through that [means].

children.text: KAZ01.14.07/ "yathā mada.andho hastī mattena^adhiṣṭhito yad yad āsādayati tat sarvaṃ pramṛdnāti, evam ayam aśāstra.cakṣur andho rājā paura.jānapada.vadhāya^abhyutthitaḥ, śakyam asya pratihasti.protsāhanena^apakartum, amarṣaḥ kriyatām" iti kruddha.vargam upajāpayet //
children.translated_text: "Just as a rutting elephant ridden by a maddened [driver] crushes everything it encounters, so has this king, blinded and lacking the eye of [political] science, risen up for the destruction of townspeople and rural folk. It is possible to harm him by encouraging [an opposing] counter-elephant. Let resentment be aroused!" — thus he should subvert the angry group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.08/ "yathā līnaḥ sarpo yasmād bhayaṃ paśyati tatra viṣam utsṛjati, evam ayaṃ rājā jāta.doṣa.āśaṅkas tvayi purā krodha.viṣam utsṛjati, anyatra gamyatām" iti bhīta.vargaṃ.upajāpayet //
children.translated_text: "Just as a hidden serpent releases its venom where it perceives danger, so this king, suspecting that a fault has arisen in you, will first release the poison of his wrath [upon you]. Go elsewhere!" — thus he should subvert the frightened group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.09/ "yathā śva.gaṇināṃ dhenuḥ śvabhyo duhyate na brāhmaṇebhyaḥ, evam ayaṃ rājā sattva.prajñā.vākya.śakti.hīnebhyo duhyate na^ātma.guṇa.sampannebhyaḥ, asau rājā puruṣa.viśeṣajñaḥ, tatra gamyatām" iti lubdha.vargaṃ.upajāpayet //
children.translated_text: "Just as the cow of dog-keepers is milked for the dogs and not for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, so this king is milked by those devoid of strength, intelligence, eloquence, and ability, and not by those endowed with personal virtues. That [other] king is a judge of men's merits — go to him!" — thus he should subvert the greedy group.

children.text: KAZ01.14.10/ "yathā caṇḍāla.uda.pānaś caṇḍālānām eva^upabhogyo na^anyeṣām, evam ayaṃ rājā nīco nīcānām eva^upabhogyo na tvadvidhānām āryāṇām, asau rājā puruṣa.viśeṣajñaḥ, tatra gamyatām" iti māni.vargam upajāpayet //
children.translated_text: "Just as the well of an outcaste is for the use of outcastes alone and not of others, so this base king is for the enjoyment of base persons only and not for noble persons (<s>āryas</s>) like yourself. That [other] king is a judge of men's merits — go to him!" — thus he should subvert the proud group.

children.text:
KAZ01.14.11ab/ tathā^iti pratipannāṃs tān saṃhitān paṇa.karmaṇā /
KAZ01.14.11cd/ yojayeta yathā.śakti sa-apasarpān sva.karmasu //
children.translated_text: Those who have agreed with 'so be it,' bound by a pledge of allegiance, he should employ, together with his secret agents, in their respective tasks, to the extent possible.

children.text:
KAZ01.14.12ab/ labheta sāma.dānābhyāṃ kṛtyāṃś ca para.bhūmiṣu /
KAZ01.14.12cd/ akṛtyān bheda.daṇḍābhyāṃ para.doṣāṃś ca darśayan //E
children.translated_text: He should win over the seducible parties in the enemy's territory through conciliation and gifts, and the non-seducible through dissension and force, while also exposing the enemy's faults.

children.text:
(ṭhe topic of counsel)
KAZ01.15.01/ kṛta.sva.pakṣa.para.pakṣa.upagrahaḥ kārya.ārambhāṃś cintayet //
children.translated_text:
(The topic of counsel)
Having secured the allegiance of [parties in] his own and the enemy's faction, he should deliberate upon the undertaking of enterprises.

children.text: KAZ01.15.02/ mantra.pūrvāḥ sarva.ārambhāḥ //
children.translated_text: All undertakings are preceded by counsel.

children.text:
KAZ01.15.03/ tad.uddeśaḥ saṃvṛtaḥ kathānām anihśrāvī pakṣibhir apy anālokyaḥ syāt /
KAZ01.15.04/ śrūyate hi śuka.sārikābhir mantro bhinnaḥ, śvabhir apy anyaiś ca tiryag.yonibhir iti //
children.translated_text: The place designated for that [counsel] should be enclosed, impervious to the overhearing of conversations, and unobservable even by birds. For it is heard that counsel has been betrayed by parrots and <s>sārikā</s> birds, by dogs, and by other animals.

children.text: KAZ01.15.05/ tasmān mantra.uddeśam anāyukto na^upagacchet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, no unauthorized person should approach the place of counsel.

children.text: KAZ01.15.06/ ucchidyeta mantra.bhedī //
children.translated_text: One who betrays counsel should be destroyed.

children.text: KAZ01.15.07/ mantra.bhedo hi dūta.amātya.svāminām iṅgita.ākārābhyām //
children.translated_text: For the betrayal of counsel [is detected] from the gestures and expressions of envoys, ministers, and the sovereign.

children.text: KAZ01.15.08/ iṅgitam anyathā.vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: A gesture (<s>iṅgita</s>) is an alteration in normal behavior.

children.text: KAZ01.15.09/ ākṛti.grahaṇam ākāraḥ //
children.translated_text: An expression (<s>ākāra</s>) is the apprehension of facial appearance.

children.text: KAZ01.15.10/ tasya saṃvaraṇam āyukta.puruṣa.rakṣaṇam ā.kārya.kālād iti //
children.translated_text: The concealment thereof, and the guarding of authorized personnel, [should be maintained] until the time for action.

children.text: KAZ01.15.11/ teṣāṃ hi pramāda.mada.supta.pralāpāḥ, kāma.ādir utsekaḥ, pracchanno^avamato vā mantraṃ bhinatti //
children.translated_text: For the careless talk arising from negligence, intoxication, or sleep, and the excitement caused by desire and the like, or a [person who is] overlooked or despised, betrays the counsel.

children.text: KAZ01.15.12/ tasmād ādrakṣen mantram //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should guard the counsel.

children.text: KAZ01.15.13/ "mantra.bhedo hy ayoga.kṣema.karo rājñas tad.āyukta.puruṣāṇāṃ ca //
children.translated_text: "For the betrayal of counsel causes harm to the welfare and security of the king and those persons appointed by him.

children.text: KAZ01.15.14/ tasmād guhyam eko mantrayeta" iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should deliberate in secret alone" — says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.15/ "mantriṇām api hi mantriṇo bhavanti, teṣām apy anye //
children.translated_text: "For even counselors have [their own] counselors, and they in turn have others.

children.text: KAZ01.15.16/ sā^eṣā mantri.paramparā mantraṃ bhinatti //
children.translated_text: This chain of counselors betrays the counsel.

children.text:
KAZ01.15.17ab/ "tasmān na^asya pare vidyuḥ karma kiṃcic cikīrṣitam /
KAZ01.15.17cd/ ārabdhāras tu jānīyur ārabdhaṃ kṛtam eva vā //
children.translated_text: "Therefore, let no others know any of his intended actions; let those charged with their execution know only what has been undertaken or already accomplished."

children.text: KAZ01.15.18/ "na^ekasya mantra.siddhir asti" iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Counsel cannot succeed with one [person] alone" — says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.19/ "pratyakṣa.parokṣa.anumeyā hi rāja.vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: "For the conduct of a king involves what is directly observed, what is unobserved, and what is to be inferred.

children.text: KAZ01.15.20/ anupalabdhasya jñānam upalabdhasya niścita.bala.ādhānam artha.dvaidhasya saṃśayac.chedanam eka.deśa.dṛṣṭasya śeṣa.upalabdhir iti mantri.sādhyam etat //
children.translated_text: Knowledge of what is not perceived, firm determination regarding what has been perceived, resolution of doubt in ambiguous matters, and discovery of the remainder from what is partially seen — this is what is to be accomplished through counselors.

children.text: KAZ01.15.21/ tasmād buddhi.vṛddhaiḥ sārdham adhyāsīta mantram //
children.translated_text: Therefore, he should sit in counsel with those who are advanced in wisdom.

children.text:
KAZ01.15.22ab/ "na kaṃcid avamanyeta sarvasya śṛṇuyān matam /
KAZ01.15.22cd/ bālasya^apy arthavad.vākyam upayuñjīta paṇḍitaḥ //"
KAZ01.15.23/ "etan mantra.jñānam, na^etan mantra.rakṣaṇam" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "One should not despise anyone; one should listen to the opinion of all. A wise man should make use of even a child's speech if it has substance." "This pertains to the knowledge of counsel, not to its protection" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.24/ "yad asya kāryam abhipretaṃ tat.pratirūpakaṃ mantriṇaḥ pṛcchet - "kāryam idam evam āsīt, evaṃ vā yadi bhavet, tat kathaṃ kartavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: "Regarding whatever enterprise he has in mind, he should ask the counselors about something resembling it — 'Such a matter existed thus, or what if it were thus — how should it be done?'

children.text: KAZ01.15.25/ te yathā brūyus tat kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Whatever they advise, that he should do.

children.text: KAZ01.15.26/ evaṃ mantra.upalabdhiḥ saṃvṛtiś ca bhavati" iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, the acquisition of counsel and concealment are both achieved" — thus [they say].

children.text: KAZ01.15.27/ na^iti piśunaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Piśuna</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.28/ "mantriṇo hi vyavahitam arthaṃ vṛttam avṛttaṃ vā pṛṣṭā anādareṇa bruvanti prakāśayanti vā //
children.translated_text: "For counselors, when asked about a matter that is remote, whether it has occurred or not, speak with indifference or reveal [the secret].

children.text: KAZ01.15.29/ sa doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: That is the defect.

children.text: KAZ01.15.30/ tasmāt karmasu ye yeṣv abhipretās taiḥ saha mantrayeta //
children.translated_text: Therefore, regarding particular tasks, he should deliberate with those who are intended for those [tasks].

children.text: KAZ01.15.31/ tair mantrayamāṇo hi mantra.siddhiṃ guptiṃ ca labhate" iti //
children.translated_text: For by deliberating with them, he obtains both the success of counsel and its protection."

children.text: KAZ01.15.32/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.33/ anavasthā hy eṣā //
children.translated_text: For this leads to an infinite regress.

children.text: KAZ01.15.34/ mantribhis tribhiś caturbhir vā saha mantrayeta //
children.translated_text: He should deliberate with three or four counselors.

children.text: KAZ01.15.35/ mantrayamāṇo hy ekena^artha.kṛcchreṣu niścayaṃ na^adhigacchet //
children.translated_text: For one deliberating with a single [counselor] does not arrive at a decision in difficult matters.

children.text: KAZ01.15.36/ ekaś ca mantrī yathā.iṣṭam anavagrahaś carati //
children.translated_text: And a single counselor acts as he pleases, without restraint.

children.text: KAZ01.15.37/ dvābhyāṃ mantrayamāṇo dvābhyāṃ saṃhatābhyām avagṛhyate, vigṛhītābhyāṃ vināśyate //
children.translated_text: One deliberating with two [counselors] is overpowered when they are united, and ruined when they are in conflict.

children.text: KAZ01.15.38/ tat triṣu catuṣu vā kṛcchreṇa^upapadyate //
children.translated_text: That [problem] arises only with difficulty when there are three or four [counselors].

children.text: KAZ01.15.39/ mahā.doṣam upapannaṃ tu bhavati //
children.translated_text: But it becomes one attended with a great fault.

children.text: KAZ01.15.40/ tataḥ pareṣu kṛcchreṇa^artha.niścayo gamyate, mantro vā rakṣyate //
children.translated_text: After that, in [the remaining] matters, the determination of policy is arrived at with difficulty, or the counsel is kept secret.

children.text:
KAZ01.15.41/ deśa.kāla.kārya.vaśena tv ekena saha dvābhyām eko vā yathā.sāmarthyaṃ mantrayeta //(alterṇative views approved)
KAZ01.15.42/ karmaṇām ārambha.upāyaḥ puruṣa.dravya.sampad deśa.kāla.vibhāgo vinipāta.pratīkāraḥ kārya.siddhir iti pañca.aṅgo mantraḥ //
children.translated_text:
However, according to the demands of place, time, and task, one should deliberate with one or with two as ability permits. (Alternative views approved)
The method of undertaking actions, the equipment of men and materials, the apportionment of place and time, the counteracting of mishaps, and the accomplishment of the task — these are the five components of counsel.

children.text: KAZ01.15.43/ tān ekaikaśaḥ pṛcchet samastāṃś ca //
children.translated_text: He should consult them one by one and collectively.

children.text: KAZ01.15.44/ hetubhiś ca^eṣāṃ mati.pravivekān vidyāt //
children.translated_text: And by [examining their] arguments, he should discern the differences in their opinions.

children.text: KAZ01.15.45/ avāpta.arthaḥ kālaṃ na^atikrāmayet //
children.translated_text: Having obtained his objective, he should not let the [proper] time pass.

children.text: KAZ01.15.46/ na dīrgha.kālaṃ mantrayeta, na teṣāṃ pakṣīyair yeṣām apakuryāt //
children.translated_text: He should not deliberate for a long time, nor [should he deliberate] with partisans of those whom he intends to harm.

children.text: KAZ01.15.47/ "mantri.pariṣadaṃ dvādaśa.amātyān kurvīta" iti mānavāḥ //
children.translated_text: "He should appoint a council of ministers (<s>mantripariṣad</s>) of twelve ministers" — say the followers of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.48/ "ṣoḍaśa" iti bārhaspatyāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Sixteen" — say the followers of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.49/ "viṃśatim" ity auśanasāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Twenty" — say the followers of <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.50/ yathā.sāmarthyam iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "As many as ability permits" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.15.51/ te hy asya sva.pakṣaṃ para.pakṣaṃ ca cintayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: For they should consider for him both his own side and the enemy's side.

children.text: KAZ01.15.52/ akṛta.ārambham ārabdha.anuṣṭhānam anuṣṭhita.viśeṣaṃ niyoga.sampadaṃ ca karmaṇāṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should attend to the initiation of works not yet begun, the continuation of works already undertaken, the improvement of works already carried out, and the proper execution of assigned duties.

children.text: KAZ01.15.53/ āsannaiḥ saha karmāṇi paśyet //
children.translated_text: He should review affairs together with those who are near.

children.text: KAZ01.15.54/ anāsannaiḥ saha pattra.sampreṣaṇena mantrayeta //
children.translated_text: With those who are not near, he should deliberate through the dispatch of letters.

children.text: KAZ01.15.55/ indrasya hi mantri.pariṣad.ṛṣīṇāṃ sahasram //
children.translated_text: For <s>Indra</s>'s council of ministers is a thousand sages.

children.text: KAZ01.15.56/ sa tac cakṣuḥ //
children.translated_text: That is his eye.

children.text: KAZ01.15.57/ tasmād imaṃ dvy.akṣaṃ sahasra.akṣam āhuḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore they call this two-eyed one 'thousand-eyed.'

children.text: KAZ01.15.58/ ātyayike kārye mantriṇo mantri.pariṣadaṃ ca^āhūya brūyāt //
children.translated_text: In an urgent matter, having summoned the ministers and the council of ministers, he should speak.

children.text: KAZ01.15.59/ tatra yad.bhūyiṣṭhā brūyuḥ kārya.siddhi.karaṃ vā tat kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Thereupon, what the majority says, or what would bring about the accomplishment of the task — that he should do.

children.text:
KAZ01.15.60/ kurvataś ca --
KAZ01.15.60ab/ na^asya guhyaṃ pare vidyuś chidraṃ vidyāt parasya ca /
KAZ01.15.60cd/ gūhet kūrma^iva^aṅgāni yat syād vivṛtam ātmanaḥ //

KAZ01.15.61ab/ yathā hy aśrotriyaḥ śrāddhaṃ na satāṃ bhoktum arhati /
KAZ01.15.61cd/ evam aśruta.śāstra.artho na mantraṃ śrotum arhati //E
children.translated_text:
Just as a non-Vedic scholar does not deserve to partake of a <s>śrāddha</s> [funeral feast] among the virtuous,
so one who has not learned the meaning of the treatises does not deserve to hear the counsel.

children.text:
(ṛules for the envoy)
KAZ01.16.01/ udvṛtta.mantro dūta.praṇidhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Rules for the envoy)
After the conclusion of the council's deliberation comes the deployment of envoys.

children.text: KAZ01.16.02/ amātya.sampadā^upeto nisṛṣṭa.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: One endowed with the qualifications of a minister and with full authority [is an envoy] with plenipotentiary powers (<s>nisṛṣṭārtha</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.16.03/ pāda.guṇa.hīnaḥ parimita.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: One deficient by a quarter in qualifications [is an envoy] with limited authority (<s>parimitārtha</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.16.04/ ardha.guṇa.hīnaḥ śāsana.haraḥ //
children.translated_text: One deficient by half in qualifications is a mere bearer of the message (<s>śāsanahara</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.16.05/ suprativihita.yāna.vāhana.puruṣa.parivāpaḥ pratiṣṭheta //
children.translated_text: He should set out well-provided with conveyance, vehicle, attendants, and provisions.

children.text: KAZ01.16.06/ śāsanam evaṃ vācyaḥ paraḥ, sa vakṣyaty evam, tasya^idaṃ prativākyam, evam atisaṃdhātavyam, ity adhīyāno gacchet //
children.translated_text: Having studied [the briefing] — 'the message is thus; the other is to be addressed thus; he will say this; to that, this is the reply; thus he is to be outmaneuvered' — he should depart.

children.text: KAZ01.16.07/ aṭavy.anta.pāla.pura.rāṣṭra.mukhyaiś ca pratisaṃsargaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: And he should establish contact with the chiefs of forests, frontier guards, cities, and provinces.

children.text: KAZ01.16.08/ anīka.sthāna.yuddha.pratigraha.apasāra.bhūmīr ātmanaḥ parasya ca^avekṣeta //
children.translated_text: He should observe the positions of troops, battle formations, means of capturing [the enemy], and routes of retreat — both his own and the enemy's.

children.text: KAZ01.16.09/ durga.rāṣṭra.pramāṇaṃ sāra.vṛtti.guptic.chidrāṇi ca^upalabheta //
children.translated_text: He should ascertain the extent of the fort and the countryside, their resources, means of livelihood, defense, and vulnerabilities.

children.text: KAZ01.16.10/ para.adhiṣṭhānam anujñātaḥ praviśet //
children.translated_text: He should enter the enemy's capital only when permitted.

children.text: KAZ01.16.11/ śāsanaṃ ca yathā.uktaṃ brūyāt, prāṇa.ābādhe^api dṛṣṭe //
children.translated_text: And he should deliver the message exactly as instructed, even when danger to life is perceived.

children.text: KAZ01.16.12/ parasya vāci vaktre dṛṣṭyāṃ ca prasādaṃ vākya.pūjanam iṣṭa.paripraśnaṃ guṇa.kathā.saṅgam āsannam āsanaṃ satkāram iṣṭeṣu smaraṇaṃ viśvāsa.gamanaṃ ca lakṣayet tuṣṭasya, viparītam atuṣṭasya //
children.translated_text: In the other's speech, face, and gaze, he should observe [signs of] satisfaction — favorable words, respectful reception, welcome inquiry, discussion of [the envoy's] merits, a nearby seat, hospitable treatment, remembrance of [mutual] interests, and demonstration of trust — as [signs] of the pleased [king]; the opposite, of the displeased.

children.text: KAZ01.16.13/ taṃ brūyāt - "dūta.mukhā hi rājānaḥ, tvaṃ ca^anye ca //
children.translated_text: He should say to him: 'Kings speak through the mouths of envoys — you and others alike.

children.text: KAZ01.16.14/ tasmād udyateṣv api śastreṣu yathā.uktaṃ vaktāro dūtāḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when weapons are raised, envoys speak as instructed.

children.text: KAZ01.16.15/ teṣām anta.avasāyino^apy avadhyāḥ, kim aṅga punar brāhmaṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Even those among them who speak to the point of termination [of negotiations] are not to be killed — how much less <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>?

children.text: KAZ01.16.16/ parasya^etad vākyam //
children.translated_text: This is the other's message.

children.text: KAZ01.16.17/ eṣa dūta.dharmaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Such is the duty of an envoy.'

children.text: KAZ01.16.18/ vased avisṛṣṭaḥ pūjayā na^utsiktaḥ //
children.translated_text: He should remain [at the foreign court] if not dismissed, and not be elated by honors.

children.text: KAZ01.16.19/ pareṣu balitvaṃ na manyeta //
children.translated_text: He should not consider the other [king's forces] to be powerful.

children.text: KAZ01.16.20/ vākyam aniṣṭaṃ saheta //
children.translated_text: He should endure an unpleasant message.

children.text: KAZ01.16.21/ striyaḥ pānaṃ ca varjayet //
children.translated_text: He should avoid women and drink.

children.text: KAZ01.16.22/ ekaḥ śayīta //
children.translated_text: He should sleep alone.

children.text: KAZ01.16.23/ supta.mattayor hi bhāva.jñānaṃ dṛṣṭam //
children.translated_text: For the inner thoughts of those asleep or intoxicated are observed [by others].

children.text: KAZ01.16.24/ kṛtya.pakṣa.upajāpam akṛtya.pakṣe gūḍha.praṇidhānaṃ rāga.aparāgau bhartari randhraṃ ca prakṛtīnāṃ tāpasa.vaidehaka.vyañjanābhyām upalabheta, tayor antevāsibhiś cikitsaka.pāṣaṇḍa.vyañjana.ubhaya.vetanair vā //
children.translated_text: He should ascertain the instigation of the [enemy's] faction amenable to persuasion, the secret deployment [of agents] among the hostile faction, attachment and disaffection toward [their] lord, and vulnerabilities of the constituent elements — through [agents] disguised as ascetics and traders, or through their disciples, or through those disguised as physicians, heretical mendicants, or double agents.

children.text: KAZ01.16.25/ teṣām asambhāṣāyāṃ yācaka.matta.unmatta.supta.pralāpaiḥ puṇya.sthāna.deva.gṛha.citra.lekhya.saṃjñābhir vā cāram upalabheta //
children.translated_text: When direct conversation with them is not possible, he should gather intelligence through the prattle of beggars, the drunk, the mad, or the sleeping, or through signals at holy places, temples, paintings, and writings.

children.text: KAZ01.16.26/ upalabdhasya^upajāpam upeyāt //
children.translated_text: He should undertake the instigation of those [whose disposition has been] ascertained.

children.text: KAZ01.16.27/ pareṇa ca^uktaḥ svāsāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ pramāṇaṃ na^ācakṣīta //
children.translated_text: And when asked by the enemy [king], he should not reveal the true strength of his own constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ01.16.28/ "sarvaṃ veda bhavān" iti brūyāt, kārya.siddhi.karaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: He should say, 'Your honor knows everything,' or [say] whatever would accomplish the objective.

children.text:
KAZ01.16.29/ kāryasya^asiddhāv uparudhyamānas tarkayet - "kiṃ bhartur me vyasanam āsannaṃ paśyan, svaṃ vā vyasanaṃ pratikartu.kāmaḥ, pārṣṇi.grāham āsāram antaḥ.kopam āṭavikaṃ vā samutthāpayitu.kāmaḥ, mitram ākrandaṃ vā vyāghātayitu.kāmaḥ, svaṃ vā parato vigraham antaḥ.kopam āṭavikaṃ vā pratikartu.kāmaḥ, saṃsiddhaṃ vā me bhartur yātrā.kālam abhihantu.kāmaḥ,
sasya.paṇya.kupya.saṃgrahaṃ durga.karma bala.samuddānaṃ vā kartu.kāmaḥ, sva.sainyānāṃ vā vyāyāmasya deśa.kālāv ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ, paribhava.pramādābhyāṃ vā, saṃsarga.anubandha.arthī vā, mām uparuṇaddhi" iti //
children.translated_text:
If, when the objective is not accomplished, he is detained, he should consider: 'Is it because [the enemy] sees my master's calamity approaching? Or because he wishes to counter his own calamity? Or because he wishes to instigate an attack from the rear, a tribal chief, internal revolt, or a forest people? Or because he wishes to obstruct an ally or a [potential] supporter? Or because he wishes to counter a war, internal revolt, or forest uprising against himself? Or because he wishes to strike at a successful campaign of my master when the time is ripe?
Or because he wishes to gather grain, merchandise, and raw materials, undertake fortification work, or raise an army? Or because he is waiting for the right place and time for the training of his own forces? Or out of contempt or carelessness? Or because he seeks a lasting alliance? — [for these reasons] he detains me.'

children.text: KAZ01.16.30/ jñātvā vased apasared vā //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained [the reason], he should remain or depart.

children.text: KAZ01.16.31/ prayojanam iṣṭam avekṣeta vā //
children.translated_text: Or he should pursue a desired objective [that may present itself].

children.text: KAZ01.16.32/ śāsanam aniṣṭam uktvā bandha.vadha.bhayād avisṛṣṭo^apy apagacchet, anyathā niyamyeta //
children.translated_text: Having delivered an unpleasant message, even if not dismissed, he should leave out of fear of imprisonment or execution; otherwise he would be restrained.

children.text:
KAZ01.16.33ab/ preṣaṇaṃ saṃdhi.pālatvaṃ pratāpo mitra.saṃgrahaḥ /
KAZ01.16.33cd/ upajāpaḥ suhṛd.bhedo gūḍha.daṇḍa.atisāraṇam //
children.translated_text:
Carrying messages, maintaining treaties, display of power, winning allies,
instigation, breaking of enemy alliances, covert deployment of force,

children.text:
KAZ01.16.34ab/ bandhu.ratna.apaharaṇaṃ cāra.jñānaṃ parākramaḥ /
KAZ01.16.34cd/ samādhi.mokṣo dūtasya karma yogasya ca^āśrayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
Seizing [the enemy's] kinsmen and gems, gathering intelligence, heroic action,
reconciliation and release — these are the functions of an envoy, and they rest upon statecraft (<s>yoga</s>).

children.text:
KAZ01.16.35ab/ sva.dūtaiḥ kārayed etat para.dūtāṃś ca rakṣayet /
KAZ01.16.35cd/ pratidūta.apasarpābhyāṃ dṛśya.adṛśyaiś ca rakṣibhiḥ //E
children.translated_text:
He should have these carried out through his own envoys and should guard against the enemy's envoys,
through counter-envoys and secret agents, both visible and invisible guards.

children.text:
(ṅuarding against princes)
KAZ01.17.01/ rakṣito rājā rājyaṃ rakṣaty āsannebhyaḥ parebhyaś ca, pūrvaṃ dārebhyaḥ putrebhyaś ca //
children.translated_text:
(Guarding against princes)
A king who is well-guarded guards his kingdom from those near and from enemies, and first of all from his wives and sons.

children.text: KAZ01.17.02/ dāra.rakṣaṇaṃ niśānta.praṇidhau vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: The guarding of wives we shall discuss in the section on the surveillance of the royal household (<s>niśāntapraṇidhi</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.17.03/ "putra.rakṣaṇaṃ tu //
children.translated_text: As for the guarding of sons —

children.text: KAZ01.17.04/ "janma.prabhṛti rāja.putrān rakṣet //
children.translated_text: "One should guard princes from birth.

children.text: KAZ01.17.05/ karkaṭaka.sadharmāṇo hi janaka.bhakṣā rāja.putrāḥ //
children.translated_text: For princes are like crabs in nature — they devour their progenitor.

children.text: KAZ01.17.06/ teṣām ajāta.snehe pitary upāṃśu.daṇḍaḥ śreyān" iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the father has not yet developed affection for them, secret punishment is preferable" — says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.07/ "nṛśaṃsam aduṣṭa.vadhaḥ kṣatra.bīja.vināśaś ca" iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: "It is cruel to kill the innocent, and it destroys the royal lineage" — says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.08/ "tasmād eka.sthāna.avarodhaḥ śreyān" iti //
children.translated_text: "Therefore, confinement in a single place is preferable" — says he.

children.text: KAZ01.17.09/ ahi.bhayam etad" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is the danger of [confinement like that of] a snake" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.10/ "kumāro hi "vikrama.bhayān māṃ pitā^avaruṇaddhi" iti jñātvā tam eva^aṅke kuryāt //
children.translated_text: "For the prince, knowing 'my father confines me out of fear of [my] valor,' would turn against him.

children.text: KAZ01.17.11/ tasmād anta.pāla.durge vāsaḥ śreyān" iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, residence in a frontier fort is preferable" — say they.

children.text: KAZ01.17.12/ "aurabhraṃ bhayam etad" iti piśunaḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is the danger of [being kept like] a lamb" — says <s>Piśuna</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.13/ "pratyāpatter hi tad eva kāraṇaṃ jñātvā^anta.pāla.sakhaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: "For, knowing that very [confinement] to be the reason for his rebellion, he would become allied with the frontier chief.

children.text: KAZ01.17.14/ tasmāt sva.viṣayād apakṛṣṭe sāmanta.durge vāsaḥ śreyān" iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, residence in a border fort of a feudatory removed from one's own territory is preferable" — says he.

children.text: KAZ01.17.15/ "vatsa.sthānam etad" iti kauṇapadantaḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is [making him] a hostage (<s>vatsasthāna</s>)" — says <s>Kauṇapadanta</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.16/ "vatsena^iva hi dhenuṃ pitaram asya sāmanto duhyāt //
children.translated_text: "For the feudatory would milk his father through him, just as [one milks] a cow through a calf.

children.text: KAZ01.17.17/ tasmān mātṛ.bandhuṣu vāsaḥ śreyān" iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, residence among the maternal relatives is preferable" — says he.

children.text: KAZ01.17.18/ "dhvaja.sthānam etad" iti vāta.vyādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is [making him] a rallying standard" — says <s>Vātavyādhi</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.19/ "tena hi dhvajena^aditi.kauśikavad asya mātṛ.bāndhavā bhikṣeran //
children.translated_text: "For under that banner, like <s>Aditi</s> and [the mother of] <s>Kauśika</s>, his maternal relatives would solicit [the kingdom] from him.

children.text: KAZ01.17.20/ tasmād grāmya sukheṣv enam avasṛjet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should let him loose in rural pleasures.

children.text: KAZ01.17.21/ sukha.uparuddhā hi putrāḥ pitaraṃ na^abhidruhyanti" iti //
children.translated_text: For sons immersed in pleasures do not turn against their father" — says he.

children.text: KAZ01.17.22/ jīvan.maraṇam etad iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "This is a living death" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.23/ kāṣṭham iva ghuṇa.jagdhaṃ rāja.kulam avinīta.putram abhiyukta.mātraṃ bhajyeta //
children.translated_text: A royal family with an undisciplined son, like timber eaten by wood-worms, would break at the first assault.

children.text: KAZ01.17.24/ tasmād ṛtumatyāṃ mahiṣyām ṛtvijaś carum aindrābārhaspatyaṃ nirvapeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the chief queen is in her fertile season, the priests should offer the sacrificial cake (<s>caru</s>) dedicated to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.25/ āpanna.sattvāyāḥ kaumāra.bhṛtyo garbha.bharmaṇi prasave ca viyateta //
children.translated_text: When she has conceived, an expert in the care of the young (<s>kumārabhṛtya</s>) should attend to the nurturing of the embryo and the delivery.

children.text: KAZ01.17.26/ prajātāyāḥ putra.saṃskāraṃ purohitaḥ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: After she has given birth, the family priest (<s>purohita</s>) should perform the sacraments for the son.

children.text: KAZ01.17.27/ samarthaṃ tadvido vinayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When capable, experts in their respective fields should educate him.

children.text: KAZ01.17.28/ "sattriṇām ekaś ca^enaṃ mṛgayā.dyūta.madya.strībhiḥ pralobhayet "pitari vikramya rājyaṃ gṛhāṇa" iti //
children.translated_text: "And one of the secret agents should tempt him with hunting, gambling, liquor, and women [saying], 'Seize the kingdom by overthrowing your father!'

children.text: KAZ01.17.29/ tam anyaḥ sattrī pratiṣedhayet" ity āmbhīyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Another secret agent should dissuade him" — say the followers of <s>Āmbhīya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.30/ mahā.doṣam abuddha.bodhanam it kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "It is a great fault to awaken the unawakened [to evil]" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.17.31/ navaṃ hi dravyaṃ yena yena^artha.jātena^upadihyate tat tad ācūṣati //
children.translated_text: For a new vessel absorbs whatever substance is smeared upon it.

children.text: KAZ01.17.32/ evam ayaṃ nava.buddhir yad yad ucyate tat tat.śāstra.upadeśam iva^abhijānāti //
children.translated_text: Likewise, this [prince] of unformed intellect accepts whatever is told to him as if it were the teaching of a treatise.

children.text: KAZ01.17.33/ tasmād dharmyam arthyaṃ ca^asya^upadiśen na^adharmyam anarthyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should instruct him in what is righteous and profitable, not in what is unrighteous and unprofitable.

children.text: KAZ01.17.34/ sattriṇas tv enaṃ "tava smaḥ" iti vadantaḥ pālayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: The secret agents, however, declaring 'We are yours,' should protect him.

children.text: KAZ01.17.35/ yauvana.utsekāt para.strīṣu manaḥ kurvāṇam āryā.vyañjanābhiḥ strībhir amedhyābhiḥ śūnya.āgāreṣu rātrāv udvejayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If, out of the exuberance of youth, he turns his mind toward other men's wives, women disguised as noblewomen — [actually being] impure [outcaste] women — should frighten him in empty houses at night.

children.text: KAZ01.17.36/ madya.kāmaṃ yoga.pānena^udvejayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If addicted to liquor, they should frighten him with a drugged drink.

children.text: KAZ01.17.37/ dyūta.kāmaṃ kāpaṭikair udvejayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If addicted to gambling, they should frighten him through cheats.

children.text: KAZ01.17.38/ mṛgayā.kāmaṃ pratirodhaka.vyañjanais trāsayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If addicted to hunting, they should terrify him through [agents] disguised as highway robbers.

children.text: KAZ01.17.39/ pitari vikrama.buddhiṃ "tathā" ity anupraviśya bhedayeyuḥ - "aprārthanīyo rājā, vipanne ghātaḥ, sampanne naraka.pātaḥ, saṃkrośaḥ, prajābhir eka.loṣṭa.vadhaś ca" iti //
children.translated_text: If he harbors thoughts of violence against his father, they should enter [his confidence] saying 'Yes, indeed,' and then dissuade him — [saying]: 'The king is not to be assailed; if the attempt fails, death [awaits]; if it succeeds, descent into hell, universal condemnation, and destruction by the people as if by a single clod.'

children.text: KAZ01.17.40/ virāgaṃ vedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should report [the prince's] disaffection [to the king].

children.text: KAZ01.17.41/ priyam eka.putraṃ badhnīyāt //
children.translated_text: A beloved only son he should keep confined.

children.text: KAZ01.17.42/ bahu.putraḥ pratyantam anya.viṣayaṃ vā preṣayed yatra garbhaḥ paṇyaṃ ḍimbo vā na bhavet //
children.translated_text: One with many sons should send [the troublesome ones] to the frontier or to foreign territory, where there would be no intrigue, insurrection, or revolt.

children.text: KAZ01.17.43/ ātma.sampannaṃ saināpatye yauvarājye vā sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: One who has attained excellence he should install in the generalship or in the position of heir-apparent (<s>yauvarājya</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.17.44/ buddhimān.āhārya.buddhir durbuddhir iti putra.viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: Intelligent, corrigible, and unintelligent — these are the types of sons.

children.text: KAZ01.17.45/ śiṣyamāṇo dharma.arthāv upalabhate ca^anutiṣṭhati ca buddhimān //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.45/ One who, while being instructed, grasps both <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>artha</s> (wealth) and also puts them into practice — he is of intelligent disposition.

children.text: KAZ01.17.46/ upalabhamāno na^anutiṣṭhaty āhārya.buddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.46/ One who grasps but does not put into practice — he is of corruptible intellect.

children.text: KAZ01.17.47/ apāya.nityo dharma.artha.dveṣī ca^iti durbuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.47/ One who is prone to ruin and hostile to <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> — he is of wicked intellect.

children.text: KAZ01.17.48/ sa yady eka.putraḥ putra.utpattāv asya prayateta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.48/ If such a one is the only son, the king should endeavor to have [another] son begotten for him.

children.text: KAZ01.17.49/ putrikā.putrān utpādayed vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.49/ Or he should have sons begotten through an appointed daughter (<s>putrikā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.17.50/ vṛddhas tu vyādhito vā rājā mātṛ.bandhu.kulya.guṇavat.sāmantānām anyatamena kṣetre bījam utpādayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.50/ An aged or ailing king should have a son begotten in his wife through one among [those who are] maternal kinsmen, clansmen, or virtuous vassals.

children.text: KAZ01.17.51/ na ca^eka.putram avinītaṃ rājye sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.17.51/ And he should not install an undisciplined only son in the kingdom.

children.text:
KAZ01.17.52ab/ bahūnām eka.samrodhaḥ pitā putra.hito bhavet /
KAZ01.17.52cd/ anyatra^āpada aiśvaryaṃ jyeṣṭha.bhāgi tu pūjyate //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.17.52ab/ A father should confine many [sons] together, and be devoted to the welfare of his sons;
KAZ01.17.52cd/ except in times of calamity, sovereignty is honored as the share of the eldest.

children.text:
KAZ01.17.53ab/ kulasya vā bhaved rājyaṃ kula.saṃgho hi durjayaḥ /
KAZ01.17.53cd/ arāja.vyasana.ābādhaḥ śaśvad āvasati kṣitim //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.17.53ab/ Or the kingdom may belong to the clan, for a united clan is unconquerable;
KAZ01.17.53cd/ free from the affliction of kinglessness, it dwells upon the earth forever.

children.text:
(ṭhe conduct of a prince in disfavour)
(Behaviour towards a prince in disfavour)
KAZ01.18.01/ vinīto rāja.putraḥ kṛcchra.vṛttir asadṛśe karmaṇi niyuktaḥ pitaram anuvarteta, anyatra prāṇa.ābādhaka.prakṛti.kopaka.pātakebhyaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(The conduct of a prince in disfavor)
(Behavior toward a prince in disfavor)
KAZ01.18.01/ A disciplined prince, living under hardship and assigned to an unworthy task, should follow his father, except in matters that endanger life, provoke the subjects, or involve mortal sin.

children.text: KAZ01.18.02/ puṇye karmaṇi niyuktaḥ puruṣam adhiṣṭhātāraṃ yācet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.02/ When assigned to a meritorious task, he should request a superintendent to oversee.

children.text: KAZ01.18.03/ puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitaś ca saviśeṣam ādeśam anutiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.03/ And when placed under a superintendent, he should carry out the order with exceptional [diligence].

children.text: KAZ01.18.04/ abhirūpaṃ ca karma.phalam aupāyanikaṃ ca lābhaṃ pitur upanāyayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.04/ He should present to his father the proper fruit of the work and any profit gained through strategic means.

children.text: KAZ01.18.05/ tathā^apy atuṣyantam anyasmin putre dāreṣu vā snihyantam araṇyāya^āpṛccheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.05/ If even so the father remains displeased and shows affection toward another son or wives, he should take leave for the forest.

children.text: KAZ01.18.06/ bandha.vadha.bhayād vā yaḥ sāmanto nyāya.vṛttir dhārmikaḥ satya.vāg.avisaṃvādakaḥ pratigrahītā mānayitā ca^abhipannānāṃ tam āśrayeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.06/ Or, fearing imprisonment and execution, he should seek refuge with a vassal who is righteous in conduct, virtuous, truthful, not treacherous, and one who receives and honors those who come to him for protection.

children.text: KAZ01.18.07/ tatrasthaḥ kośa.daṇḍa.sampannaḥ pravīra.puruṣa.kanyā.sambandham aṭavī.sambandhaṃ kṛtya.pakṣa.upagrahaṃ ca kuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.07/ Stationed there, endowed with treasury and army, he should establish marriage alliances with families of brave men, alliances with forest tribes, and win over disaffected factions.

children.text: KAZ01.18.08/ eka.caraḥ suvarṇa.pāka.maṇi.rāga.hema.rūpya.paṇya.ākara.karma.antān ājīvet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.08/ Moving alone, he should earn a livelihood through the trades of gold-smelting, gem-dyeing, and working with gold, silver, and merchandise from mines.

children.text: KAZ01.18.09/ pāṣaṇḍa.saṃgha.dravyam aśrotriya.upabhogyaṃ vā deva.dravyam āḍhya.vidhavā.dravyaṃ vā gūḍham anupraviśya sārtha.yāna.pātrāṇi ca madana.rasa.yogena^atisaṃdhāya^apaharet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.09/ Or, secretly entering into the wealth of heretical communities, the property of temples not used by learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, or the wealth of rich widows, and deceiving caravans, ships, and vessels with a preparation of the intoxicating drug, he should steal [them].

children.text: KAZ01.18.10/ pāragrāmikaṃ vā yogam ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.10/ Or he should practice a stratagem involving [agents] from another village.

children.text: KAZ01.18.11/ mātuḥ parijana.upagraheṇa vā ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.11/ Or he should operate through winning over his mother's attendants.

children.text:
KAZ01.18.12/ kāru.śilpi.kuśīlava.cikitsaka.vāg.jīvana.pāṣaṇḍac.chadmabhir vā naṣṭa.rūpas tad.vyañjana.sakhaś.chidreṣu praviśya rājñaḥ śastra.rasābhyāṃ prahṛtya brūyāt - "aham asau kumāraḥ, saha.bhogyam idaṃ rājyam, eko na^arhati bhoktum, ye kāmayante māṃ bhartuṃ tān ahaṃ dviguṇena bhakta.vetanena^upasthāsyāmi" iti // ity aparuddha.vṛttam /
KAZ01.18.13/ aparuddhaṃ tu mukhya.putra.apasarpāḥ pratipādya^ānayeyuḥ, mātā vā pratigṛhītā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.18.12/ Or, disguised as artisans, craftsmen, entertainers, physicians, orators, or heretics, with altered appearance and accompanied by friends bearing such marks, entering through vulnerabilities, and striking the king with weapon or poison, he should declare: "I am that prince; this kingdom is to be enjoyed jointly — one person alone does not deserve to enjoy it; those who wish to serve me, I shall support with double wages and provisions." Thus is the conduct of a restrained [prince].
KAZ01.18.13/ A restrained [prince], however, should be won over and brought back by agents posing as chief sons, or by his mother who has been won over.

children.text: KAZ01.18.14/ tyaktaṃ gūḍha.puruṣāḥ śastra.rasābhyāṃ hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.14/ One who has been abandoned, secret agents should kill with weapons or poison.

children.text: KAZ01.18.15/ atyaktaṃ tulya.śīlābhiḥ strībhiḥ pānena mṛgayayā vā prasañjayitvā rātrāv upagṛhya^ānayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.18.15/ One who has not been abandoned, they should entice through women of similar disposition with drink or hunting, and seize him at night and bring him back.

children.text:
KAZ01.18.16ab/ upasthitaṃ ca rājyena mad.ūrdhvam iti sāntvayet /
KAZ01.18.16cd/ ekastham atha samrundhyāt putravāṃs tu pravāsayet //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.18.16ab/ When [the prince] has presented himself, the king should pacify him with sovereignty [promised] after his own [death];
KAZ01.18.16cd/ then when isolated, he should confine him; but one who has sons should be banished.

children.text:
(ṛules for the king)
KAZ01.19.01/ rājānam utthitam anūttiṣṭhante bhṛtyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Rules for the king)
KAZ01.19.01/ When the king is active, his servants follow in activity.

children.text: KAZ01.19.02/ pramādyantam anupramādyanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.02/ When he is negligent, they follow in negligence.

children.text: KAZ01.19.03/ karmāṇi ca^asya bhakṣayanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.03/ And they consume his works.

children.text:
KAZ01.19.04/ dviṣadbhiś ca^atisaṃdhīyate /
KAZ01.19.05/ tasmād utthānam ātmanaḥ kurvīta //
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.19.04/ And he is outwitted by his enemies.
KAZ01.19.05/ Therefore, he should apply himself to personal exertion.

children.text: KAZ01.19.06/ nālikābhir ahar aṣṭadhā rātriṃ ca vibhajet, chāyā.pramāṇena vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.06/ He should divide the day into eight parts and the night likewise, by means of water-clocks or by the measure of shadows.

children.text: KAZ01.19.07/ tripauruṣī pauruṣī catur.aṅgulā naṣṭac.chāyo madhya.ahna^iti catvāraḥ pūrve divasasya^aṣṭa.bhāgāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.07/ [A shadow of] three man-lengths, one man-length, four finger-breadths, and no shadow at midday — these are the first four eighth-parts of the day.

children.text: KAZ01.19.08/ taiḥ paścimā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.08/ The latter [four parts] are explained by these in reverse.

children.text: KAZ01.19.09/ tatra pūrve divasasya^aṣṭa.bhāge rakṣā.vidhānam āya.vyayau ca śṛṇuyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.09/ During the first eighth of the day, he should hear reports on protective measures and on income and expenditure.

children.text: KAZ01.19.10/ dvitīye paura.jānapadānāṃ kāryāṇi paśyet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.10/ In the second, he should attend to the affairs of townspeople and countryfolk.

children.text: KAZ01.19.11/ tṛtīye snāna.bhojanaṃ seveta, svādhyāyaṃ ca kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.11/ In the third, he should attend to bathing and meals, and engage in personal study (<s>svādhyāya</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.19.12/ caturthe hiraṇya.pratigraham adhyakṣāṃś ca kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.12/ In the fourth, he should receive gold and appoint superintendents.

children.text: KAZ01.19.13/ pañcame mantri.pariṣadā pattra.sampreṣaṇena mantrayeta, cāra.guhya.bodhanīyāni ca budhyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.13/ In the fifth, he should hold counsel with the council of ministers by dispatching letters, and learn of the intelligence gathered by secret agents.

children.text: KAZ01.19.14/ ṣaṣṭhe svaira.vihāraṃ mantraṃ vā seveta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.14/ In the sixth, he should attend to free recreation or to counsel.

children.text: KAZ01.19.15/ saptame hasty.aśva.ratha.āyudhīyān paśyet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.15/ In the seventh, he should inspect elephants, horses, chariots, and the military.

children.text: KAZ01.19.16/ aṣṭame senā.pati.sakho vikramaṃ cintayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.16/ In the eighth, together with the commander-in-chief, he should deliberate on military strategy.

children.text: KAZ01.19.17/ pratiṣṭhite^ahani saṃdhyām upāsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.17/ At the end of the day, he should perform the twilight worship (<s>sandhyā</s>).

children.text: KAZ01.19.18/ prathame rātri.bhāge gūḍha.puruṣān paśyet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.18/ In the first part of the night, he should receive secret agents.

children.text: KAZ01.19.19/ dvitīye snāna.bhojanaṃ kurvīta, svādhyāyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.19/ In the second, he should attend to bathing and meals, and to personal study.

children.text: KAZ01.19.20/ tṛtīye tūrya.ghoṣeṇa saṃviṣṭaś caturtha.pañcamau śayīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.20/ In the third, he should retire to the sound of trumpets and sleep during the fourth and fifth [parts].

children.text: KAZ01.19.21/ ṣaṣṭhe tūrya.ghoṣeṇa pratibuddhaḥ śāstram itikartavyatāṃ ca cintayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.21/ In the sixth, awakened by the sound of trumpets, he should reflect on the treatise and the tasks to be done.

children.text: KAZ01.19.22/ saptame mantram adhyāsīta, gūḍha.puruṣāṃś ca preṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.22/ In the seventh, he should sit in council and dispatch secret agents.

children.text: KAZ01.19.23/ aṣṭame ṛtvig.ācārya.purohita.svastyayanāni pratigṛhṇīyāt, cikitsaka.māhānasika.mauhūrtikāṃś ca paśyet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.23/ In the eighth, he should receive benedictions from priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>), the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), and the chaplain (<s>purohita</s>), and see the physician, the cook, and the astrologer.

children.text: KAZ01.19.24/ savastāṃ dhenuṃ vṛṣabhaṃ ca pradakṣiṇī.kṛtya^upasthānaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.24/ Having circumambulated a cow with calf and a bull, he should proceed to the assembly hall.

children.text: KAZ01.19.25/ ātma.bala.ānukūlyena vā niśā.ahar.bhāgān pravibhajya kāryāṇi seveta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.25/ Or, in accordance with his own strength and capacity, he should divide the parts of night and day and attend to his duties.

children.text: KAZ01.19.26/ upasthāna.gataḥ kārya.arthinām advāra.āsaṅgaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.26/ Having gone to the assembly hall, he should ensure that petitioners have unobstructed access.

children.text: KAZ01.19.27/ durdarśo hi rājā kārya.akārya.viparyāsam āsannaiḥ kāryate //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.27/ For a king who is difficult to see is caused by those near him to confuse what should and should not be done.

children.text: KAZ01.19.28/ tena prakṛti.kopam ari.vaśaṃ vā gacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.28/ Thereby he incurs the wrath of the subjects or falls into the power of the enemy.

children.text: KAZ01.19.29/ tasmād devatā.āśrama.pāṣaṇḍa.śrotriya.paśu.puṇya.sthānānāṃ bāla.vṛddha.vyādhita.vyasany.anāthānāṃ strīṇāṃ ca krameṇa kāryāṇi paśyet, kārya.gauravād ātyayika.vaśena vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.19.29/ Therefore, he should attend to the affairs, in order, of [those connected with] deities, hermitages, heretical orders, learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cattle, and holy places; of children, the aged, the sick, the distressed, and the helpless; and of women — according to the gravity of the matter or in accordance with the urgency of the case.

children.text:
KAZ01.19.30ab/ sarvam ātyayikaṃ kāryaṃ śṛṇuyān na^atipātayet /[ś]
KAZ01.19.30cd/ kṛcchra.sādhyam atikrāntam asādhyaṃ vā^api jāyate //[ś]
KAZ01.19.31ab/ agny.agāra.gataḥ kāryaṃ paśyed vaidya.tapasvinām /[ś]
KAZ01.19.31cd/ purohita.ācārya.sakhaḥ pratyutthāya^abhivādya ca //[ś]
KAZ01.19.32ab/ tapasvināṃ tu kāryāṇi traividyaiḥ saha kārayet /[ś]
KAZ01.19.32cd/ māyā.yogavidāṃ caiva na svayaṃ kopa.kāraṇāt //[ś]
KAZ01.19.33ab/ rājño hi vratam utthānaṃ yajñaḥ kārya.anuśāsanam /[ś]
KAZ01.19.33cd/ dakṣiṇā vṛtti.sāmyaṃ tu dīkṣā tasya^abhiṣecanam //[ś]
KAZ01.19.34ab/ prajā.sukhe sukhaṃ rājñaḥ prajānāṃ ca hite hitam /[ś]
KAZ01.19.34cd/ na^ātma.priyaṃ hitaṃ rājñaḥ prajānāṃ tu priyaṃ hitam //[ś]
KAZ01.19.35ab/ tasmān nitya.utthito rājā kuryād artha.anuśāsanam /
KAZ01.19.35cd/ arthasya mūlam utthānam anarthasya viparyayaḥ //[ś]
KAZ01.19.36ab/ anutthāne dhruvo nāśaḥ prāptasya^anāgatasya ca /[ś]
KAZ01.19.36cd/ prāpyate phalam utthānāl labhate ca^arthasampadam //[ś]
children.translated_text:
KAZ01.19.30ab/ He should hear every urgent matter and never set it aside;
KAZ01.19.30cd/ for when neglected, it becomes difficult to accomplish or even impossible.
KAZ01.19.31ab/ Having gone to the fire-hall, he should attend to the affairs of the learned and the ascetics,
KAZ01.19.31cd/ rising and greeting them, together with the chaplain, the teacher, and his counselors.
KAZ01.19.32ab/ The affairs of ascetics, however, he should have handled together with those versed in the three Vedas,
KAZ01.19.32cd/ as well as those of practitioners of magical arts — not by himself, lest it give cause for anger.
KAZ01.19.33ab/ For the vow of a king is exertion; his sacrifice is the administration of affairs;
KAZ01.19.33cd/ the sacrificial fee is equitable distribution of livelihood; and his consecration is his coronation.
KAZ01.19.34ab/ In the happiness of the subjects lies the happiness of the king; in the welfare of the subjects, his welfare.
KAZ01.19.34cd/ What is pleasing to the king himself is not beneficial; what is pleasing to the subjects is beneficial.
KAZ01.19.35ab/ Therefore, a king who is ever active should attend to the administration of wealth;
KAZ01.19.35cd/ the root of wealth is exertion; the opposite is the root of ruin.
KAZ01.19.36ab/ In the absence of exertion, there is certain destruction of what has been acquired and what is yet to come;
KAZ01.19.36cd/ through exertion one gains the fruit and obtains the fullness of wealth.

children.text:
ṛegulations for the royal resideñce
KAZ01.20.01/ vāstuka.praśaste deśe saprākāra.parikhā.dvāram aneka.kakṣyā.parigatam antaḥpuraṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text:
(Regulations for the royal residence)
KAZ01.20.01/ In a site approved by experts in architecture, he should have the inner palace (<s>antaḥpura</s>) constructed with ramparts, moats, and gates, surrounded by multiple enclosures.

children.text: KA01.20.02/ kośagṛha.vidhānena madhye vāsa.gṛham, gūḍha.bhitti.saṃcāraṃ mohana.gṛhaṃ tan.madhye vā vāsa.gṛham, bhūmi.gṛhaṃ vā^āsanna.caitya.kāṣṭha.devatā.apidhāna.dvāram aneka.suruṅgā.saṃcāraṃ tasya^upari prāsādaṃ gūḍha.bhitti.sopānaṃ suṣira.stambha.praveśa.apasāraṃ vā vāsa.gṛhaṃ yantra.baddha.tala.avapātaṃ kārayet, āpat.pratīkāra.artham āpadi vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.02/ In the middle, a dwelling modeled on a treasury building, with passages concealed in the walls and a chamber of illusion; or in the center of that, a dwelling; or an underground chamber with its door concealed behind a shrine, timber, or deity [image], with passages through multiple tunnels, and above it, a palace with staircases hidden in the walls, or a dwelling with entrance and exit through hollow pillars, with a mechanically operated trap-floor — this should be built as a counter-measure against danger, or [only] in times of danger.

children.text: KAZ01.20.03/ ato^anyathā vā vikalpayet, saha.adhyāyi.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.03/ Or he may devise otherwise, for fear of a fellow student [knowing the design].

children.text: KAZ01.20.04/ mānuṣeṇa^agninā trir apasavyaṃ parigatam antaḥpuram agnir anyo na dahati, na ca^atra^anyo^agnir jvalati, vaidyutena bhasmanā mṛt.samyuktena karaka.vāriṇā^avaliptaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.04/ The inner palace, circumambulated three times counterclockwise with fire produced by human agency, cannot be burned by any other fire, nor does any other fire blaze therein — [especially when] smeared with ashes from lightning-struck [wood] mixed with earth and water from a pot.

children.text: KAZ01.20.05/ jīvantī.śvetā.muṣkaka.puṣpa.vandākābhir akṣīve jātasya^aśvatthasya pratānena guptaṃ sarpā viṣāṇi vā na prabhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.05/ [A place] protected by <s>jīvantī</s>, <s>śvetā</s>, <s>muṣkaka</s> flowers, <s>vandāka</s>, <s>akṣīva</s>, and the aerial roots of a naturally-grown <s>aśvattha</s> tree — serpents and poisons cannot prevail [there].

children.text: KAZ01.20.06/ mayūra.nakula.pṛṣata.utsargaḥ sarpān bhakṣayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.06/ Releasing peacocks, mongooses, and spotted deer destroys serpents.

children.text: KAZ01.20.07/ śukaḥ sārikā bhṛṅga.rājo vā sarpa.viṣa.śaṅkāyāṃ krośati //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.07/ A parrot, a <s>sārikā</s> (myna), or a <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (shrike) cries out at the suspicion of snake venom.

children.text: KAZ01.20.08/ krauñco viṣa.abhyāśe mādyati, glāyati jīvaṃ.jīvakaḥ, mriyate matta.kokilaḥ, cakorasya^akṣiṇī virajyete //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.08/ A <s>krauñca</s> (heron) becomes intoxicated near poison, a <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> (pheasant) becomes listless, a <s>mattakokila</s> (cuckoo) dies, and the eyes of a <s>cakora</s> (partridge) become discolored.

children.text: KAZ01.20.09/ ity evam agni.viṣa.sarpebhyaḥ pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.09/ Thus should he take countermeasures against fire, poison, and serpents.

children.text: KAZ01.20.10/ pṛṣṭhataḥ kakṣyā.vibhāge strī.niveśo garbha.vyādhi.saṃsthā vṛkṣa.udaka.sthānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.10/ Behind, in the division of enclosures, [should be] the women's quarters, the maternity and infirmary wing, and a grove with water.

children.text: KAZ01.20.11/ bahiḥ kanyā.kumāra.puram //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.11/ Outside, [should be] the quarters for princesses and young princes.

children.text: KAZ01.20.12/ purastād alaṅkāra.bhūmir mantra.bhūmir upasthānaṃ kumāra.adhyakṣa.sthānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.12/ In front, [should be] the ornamentation ground, the council chamber, the audience hall, and the quarters for the prince and the superintendents.

children.text: KAZ01.20.13/ kakṣya.antareṣv antarvaṃśika.sainyaṃ tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.13/ In the spaces between enclosures, the palace guard should be stationed.

children.text: KAZ01.20.14/ antar.gṛha.gataḥ sthavira.strī.pariśuddhāṃ devīṃ paśyet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.14/ Having entered the inner chambers, he should see the queen only after she has been verified by elderly women.

children.text: KAZ01.20.15/ devī.gṛhe līno hi bhrātā bhadrasenaṃ jaghāna, mātuḥ śayyā.antargataś ca putraḥ kārūṣam //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.15/ For concealed in the queen's chamber, a brother slew <s>Bhadrasena</s>, and hidden within the mother's bed, a son [slew] <s>Kāruṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.20.16/ lājān madhunā^iti viṣeṇa paryasya devī kāśi.rājam, viṣa.digdhena nūpreṇa vairantyam, mekhalā.maṇinā sauvīram, jālūtham ādarśena, veṇyāṃ gūḍhaṃ śastraṃ kṛtvā devī vidūrathaṃ jaghāna //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.16/ A queen killed the king of <s>Kāśī</s> by offering him parched grain laced with poison instead of honey; [another killed] <s>Vairantya</s> with a poisoned anklet; [another killed the king of] <s>Sauvīra</s> with a gem set in the girdle; and [another] queen, having concealed a weapon in her braid, slew <s>Vidūratha</s>.

children.text: KAZ01.20.17/ tasmād etāny āspadāni pariharet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.17/ Therefore, he should avoid these objects [as potential instruments of assassination].

children.text: KAZ01.20.18/ muṇḍa.jaṭila.kuhaka.pratisaṃsargaṃ bāhyābhiś ca dāsībhiḥ pratiṣedhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.18/ He should prohibit the women's association with shaven-headed [nuns], those wearing matted hair, and female charlatans, and also with outside maidservants.

children.text: KAZ01.20.19/ na ca^enāḥ kulyāḥ paśyeyuḥ, anyatra garbha.vyādhi.saṃsthābhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.19/ Nor should kinsmen see them, except [those in] the maternity and infirmary wing.

children.text: KAZ01.20.20/ rūpa.ājīvāḥ snāna.pragharṣa.śuddha.śarīrāḥ parivartita.vastra.alaṃkārāḥ paśyeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.20/ Courtesans, with bodies cleansed through bathing and massage, wearing exchanged garments and ornaments, should attend [the king].

children.text: KAZ01.20.21/ aśītikāḥ puruṣāḥ pañcāśatkāḥ striyo vā mātā.pitṛ.vyañjanāḥ sthavira.varṣadhara.abhyāgārikāś ca^avarodhānāṃ śauca.āśaucaṃ vidyuḥ, sthāpayeyuś ca svāmi.hite, //
children.translated_text: KAZ01.20.21/ Men of eighty years or women of fifty, bearing the marks of mother and father, elderly rain-observers, and stewards should know the purity and impurity of the women of the harem, and should keep them engaged in their master's welfare.

children.text:
KAZ01.20.22ab/ sva.bhūmau ca vaset sarvaḥ para.bhūmau na saṃcaret /[ś]
KAZ01.20.22cd/ na ca bāhyena saṃsargaṃ kaścid ābhyantaro vrajet //[ś]
KAZ01.20.23ab/ sarvaṃ ca^avekṣitaṃ dravyaṃ nibaddha.āgama.nirgamam /[ś]
KAZ01.20.23cd/ nirgacched abhigacched vā mudrā.saṃkrānta.bhūmikam //[ś] E
children.translated_text: Everyone should stay in his own area and not wander into another's area. No one from the inner [quarters] should have contact with an outsider. All goods, with entries and exits recorded, should go out or come in only through areas [marked with] sealed passes.

children.text:
(Concerning the protection of (the king"s) own person)
KAZ01.21.01/ śayanād utthitaḥ strī.gaṇair dhanvibhiḥ parigṛhyate, dvitīyasyāṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kañcuka.uṣṇīṣibhir varṣa.dhara.abhyāgārikaiḥ, tṛtīyasyāṃ kubja.vāmana.kirātaiḥ, caturthyāṃ mantribhiḥ sambandhibhir dauvārikaiś ca prāsa.pāṇibhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Concerning the protection of the king's own person)
Having risen from bed, [the king] is surrounded by groups of women archers; in the second enclosure, by attendants wearing jackets and turbans — bodyguards and household servants; in the third, by hunchbacks, dwarfs, and <s>Kirātas</s>; in the fourth, by counselors, relatives, and door-keepers armed with spears.

children.text: KAZ01.21.02/ pitṛ.paitāmahaṃ sambandha.anubaddhaṃ śikṣitam anuraktaṃ kṛta.karmāṇaṃ ca janam āsannaṃ kurvīta, na^anyato.deśīyam akṛta.artha.mānaṃ sva.deśīyaṃ vā^apy apakṛtya^upagṛhītam //
children.translated_text: He should keep near himself persons who are hereditary [servants from] father and grandfather, bound by kinship, trained, devoted, and proven in service — not foreigners, nor even those of his own country who have not been honored with wealth and status, or who have been taken in after being wronged.

children.text: KAZ01.21.03/ antar.vaṃśika.sainyaṃ rājānam antaḥpuraṃ ca rakṣet //
children.translated_text: The palace guard (<s>antarvaṃśika</s>) army should protect the king and the inner quarters.

children.text: KAZ01.21.04/ gupte deśe māhānasikaḥ sarvam āsvāda.bāhulyena karma kārayet //
children.translated_text: The chief cook should have all food prepared in a secure place with abundant tasting.

children.text: KAZ01.21.05/ tad rajā tathaiva pratibhuñjīta pūrvam agnaye vayobhyaś ca baliṃ kṛtvā //
children.translated_text: The king should partake of that [food] in the same manner, having first made an offering to the fire and to the birds.

children.text: KAZ01.21.06/ agner jvālā.dhūma.nīlatā śabda.sphoṭanaṃ ca viṣa.yuktasya, vayasāṃ vipattiś ca //
children.translated_text: Blue coloring of the flame and smoke of the fire and crackling sounds [indicate] the presence of poison; as does the death of the birds.

children.text:
KAZ01.21.07a/ annasya ūṣmā mayūra.grīva.ābhaḥ śaityam āśu kliṣṭasya^iva vaivarṇyaṃ sa-udakatvam aklinnatvaṃ ca -
KAZ01.21.07b/ vyañjanānām āśu śuṣkatvaṃ ca kvātha.dhyāma.phena.paṭala.vicchinna.bhāvo gandha.sparśa.rasa.vadhaś ca -
KAZ01.21.07c/ draveṣu hīna.atiriktac.chāyā.darśanaṃ phena.paṭala.sīmanta.ūrdhva.rājī.darśanaṃ ca -
KAZ01.21.07d/ rasasya madhye nīlā rājī, payasas tāmrā, madya.toyayoḥ kālī, dadhnaḥ śyāmā, madhunaḥ śvetā, dravyāṇām ārdrāṇām āśu pramlānatvam utpakva.bhāvaḥ kvātha.nīla.śyāvatā ca -
KAZ01.21.07e/ śuṣkāṇām āśu śātanaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ ca, -
KAZ01.21.07f/ kaṭhinānāṃ mṛdutvaṃ mṛdūnāṃ ca kaṭhinatvam, tad.abhyāśe kṣudra.sattva.vadhaś ca, -
KAZ01.21.07g/ āstaraṇa.pravaraṇānāṃ dhyāma.maṇḍalatā tanturoma.pakṣma.śātanaṃ ca, -
KAZ01.21.07h/ loha.maṇimayānāṃ paṅkama.lopadehatā sneha.rāga.gaurava.prabhāva.varṇa.sparśavadhaś ca - iti viṣayuktasya liṅgāni //
children.translated_text: Signs of poisoned [food]: steam resembling the hue of a peacock's neck; rapid discoloration as if spoiled; moistness and non-stickiness of the food; rapid drying of side dishes, and the appearance of broken layers of froth with a dark tinge, and destruction of smell, touch, and taste; in liquids, the appearance of shadows either diminished or exaggerated, and the appearance of layers of froth, parting lines, and upward streaks; in juices, a blue streak in the middle; in milk, a coppery one; in wine and water, a dark one; in curds, a dark-blue one; in honey, a white one; rapid wilting, over-ripened appearance, and dark-blue or dark discoloration of moist substances; rapid crumbling and discoloration of dry substances; softening of hard substances and hardening of soft ones, and the death of small creatures nearby; dark circular patches on spreads and coverings, and the falling off of threads, hair, and fringes; muddiness and peeling of objects made of metal or gems, and destruction of their oiliness, color, weight, potency, hue, and touch — these are the signs of poisoning.

children.text: KAZ01.21.08/ viṣa.pradasya tu śuṣka.śyāva.vaktratā vāk.saṅgaḥ svedo vijṛmbhaṇaṃ ca^atimātraṃ vepathuḥ praskhalanaṃ vākya.viprekṣaṇam āvegaḥ karmaṇi sva.bhūmau ca^anavasthānam iti //
children.translated_text: Signs of a poison-giver: a dry, dark face; stammering speech; excessive sweating, yawning, trembling, stumbling; looking about while speaking; agitation; and inability to remain in one's place or task.

children.text: KAZ01.21.09/ tasmād asya jāṅgulīvido bhiṣajaś ca^āsannāḥ syuḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, experts in antidotes (<s>jāṅgulīvida</s>) and physicians should be near him.

children.text: KAZ01.21.10/ bhiṣag.bhaiṣajya.agārād āsvāda.viśuddham auṣadhaṃ gṛhītvā pācaka.peṣakābhyām ātmanā ca pratisvādya rājñe prayacchet //
children.translated_text: The physician, having taken medicine from the physician's pharmacy, verified by tasting to be pure, and having had the cook and the compounder taste it, and having tasted it himself, should give it to the king.

children.text: KAZ01.21.11/ pānaṃ pānīyaṃ ca^auṣadhena vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: Beverages and drinking water are explained [in the same way] as medicines.

children.text: KAZ01.21.12/ kalpaka.prasādhakāḥ snāna.śuddha.vastra.hastāḥ samudram upakaraṇam antarvaṃśika.hastād ādāya paricareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: The barber and attendants, with bathed and clean-clothed hands, should receive their implements from the hands of the palace guard and serve [the king].

children.text: KAZ01.21.13/ snāpaka.saṃvāhaka.āstaraka.rajaka.mālā.kāra.karma dāsyaḥ prasiddha.śaucāḥ kuryuḥ, tābhir adhiṣṭhitā vā śilpinaḥ //
children.translated_text: The women servants, known for their cleanliness, should perform the duties of bathing, massaging, bed-making, laundering, and garland-making; or artisans supervised by them.

children.text: KAZ01.21.14/ ātma.cakṣuṣi niveśya vastra.mālyaṃ dadyuḥ, snāna.anulepana.pragharṣa.cūrṇa.vāsa.snānīyāni ca sva.vakṣo.bāhuṣu ca //
children.translated_text: They should hand over garments and garlands after placing them before their own eyes, and [apply] bathing oils, unguents, rubbing powders, fragrant powders, and bath preparations upon their own chests and arms [first].

children.text: KAZ01.21.15/ etena parasmād āgatakaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: By this, [the treatment of] anything received from outside is [also] explained.

children.text: KAZ01.21.16/ kuśīlavāḥ śastra.agni.rasa.krīḍā.varjaṃ narmayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Entertainers should amuse [the king] without weapons, fire, or poison in their performances.

children.text: KAZ01.21.17/ ātodyāni ca^eṣām antas tiṣṭheyuḥ, aśva.ratha.dvipa.alaṃkārāś ca //
children.translated_text: Their musical instruments should remain inside, as well as the ornaments of horses, chariots, and elephants.

children.text: KAZ01.21.18/ āpta.puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitaṃ yāna.vāhanam ārohet, nāvaṃ ca^āpta.nāvika.adhiṣṭhitam //
children.translated_text: He should mount a conveyance supervised by trusted men, and a boat manned by trusted sailors.

children.text: KAZ01.21.19/ anya.nau.pratibaddhāṃ vāta.vega.vaśāṃ ca na^upeyāt //
children.translated_text: He should not board a boat tied to another vessel or one at the mercy of the wind's force.

children.text: KAZ01.21.20/ udaka.ante sainyam āsīta //
children.translated_text: The army should be stationed at the water's edge.

children.text: KAZ01.21.21/ matsya.grāha.viśuddham udakam avagāheta //
children.translated_text: He should enter water cleared of fish and crocodiles.

children.text: KAZ01.21.22/ vyāla.grāha.viśuddham udyānaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: He should visit a garden cleared of snakes and crocodiles.

children.text: KAZ01.21.23/ lubdhaka.śva.gaṇibhir apāsta.stena.vyāla.para.ābādha.bhayaṃ cala.lakṣya.paricaya.arthaṃ mṛga.araṇyaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: He should go to the hunting forest, cleared of the danger of thieves, wild animals, and enemy attacks by hunters and dog-keepers, for the purpose of practicing [archery on] moving targets.

children.text: KAZ01.21.24/ āpta.śastra.grāha.adhiṣṭhitaḥ siddha.tāpasaṃ paśyet, mantri.pariṣadā saha sāmanta.dūtam //
children.translated_text: Attended by trusted weapon-bearers, he should meet accomplished ascetics; and with his council of ministers, [he should meet] envoys of neighboring kings.

children.text: KAZ01.21.25/ samnaddho^aśvaṃ hastinaṃ vā^ārūḍhaḥ samnaddham anīkaṃ paśyet //
children.translated_text: Clad in armor and mounted on a horse or elephant, he should review the armed forces in battle array.

children.text: KAZ01.21.26/ niryāṇe^abhiyāne ca rāja.mārgam ubhayataḥ kṛta.ārakṣaṃ śastribhir daṇḍibhiś ca^apāsta.śastra.hasta.pravrajita.vyaṅgaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: When going out or marching forth, he should proceed along the royal road, guarded on both sides by men with swords and staffs, cleared of armed persons, wandering ascetics, and the disabled.

children.text: KAZ01.21.27/ na puruṣa.sambādham avagāheta //
children.translated_text: He should not enter a dense crowd of people.

children.text: KAZ01.21.28/ yātrā.samāja.utsava.prahavaṇāni ca daśa.vargika.adhiṣṭhitāni gacchet //
children.translated_text: He should attend festivals, fairs, celebrations, and processions [only when] supervised by [agents organized in] groups of ten.

children.text:
KAZ01.21.29ab/ yathā ca yoga.puruṣair anyān rājā^adhitiṣṭhati /[ś]
KAZ01.21.30cd/ tathā^ayam anya.ābādhebhyo rakṣed ātmānam ātmavān //[ś] E
children.translated_text: Just as the king oversees others through secret agents, so should the self-controlled [king] protect himself from the attacks of others.

children.text:
(Book ṭwo: ṭhe activity of the heads of departments)
(Chap, 1, ṣec, 19: ṣettlement of the countryside)
KAZ02.01.01/ bhūta.pūrvam abhūta.pūrvaṃ vā jana.padaṃ para.deśa.apavāhanena sva.deśa.abhiṣyanda.vamanena vā niveśayet //
children.translated_text:
(Book Two: The activity of the heads of departments)
(Chapter 1, Section 19: Settlement of the countryside)
He should settle the countryside — whether previously inhabited or uninhabited — by drawing off population from the enemy's territory or by draining off the excess from his own.

children.text: KAZ02.01.02/ śūdra.karṣaka.prāyaṃ kula.śata.avaraṃ pañca.kula.śata.paraṃ grāmaṃ krośad.vikrośa.sīmānam anyonya.ārakṣaṃ niveśayet //
children.translated_text: He should settle a village, predominantly of <s>Śūdra</s> cultivators, with no fewer than a hundred families and no more than five hundred, with boundaries of one to two <s>krośas</s>, providing mutual protection [among villages].

children.text: KAZ02.01.03/ nalī.śaila.vana.bhṛṣṭi.darī.setu.bandha.śamī.śālmalī.kṣīra.vṛkṣān anteṣu sīmnāṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should establish at the boundaries reedy marshes, rocky outcrops, forests, thickets, caves, embankments, and <s>śamī</s>, <s>śālmalī</s>, and milk-yielding trees.

children.text: KAZ02.01.04/ aṣṭaśata.grāmyā madhye sthānīyam, catuhśata.grāmyā droṇa.mukham, dviśata.grāmyāḥ kārvaṭikam, daśa.grāmī.saṃgraheṇa saṃgrahaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should establish a <s>sthānīya</s> (provincial capital) at the center of eight hundred villages, a <s>droṇamukha</s> (district seat) for four hundred villages, a <s>kārvaṭika</s> (market town) for two hundred villages, and a <s>saṃgraha</s> (collection point) for every ten villages.

children.text: KAZ02.01.05/ anteṣv anta.pāla.durgāṇi jana.pada.dvārāṇy anta.pāla.adhiṣṭhitāni sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: At the borders, he should establish frontier forts as gateways of the countryside, supervised by border-guards.

children.text: KAZ02.01.06/ teṣām antarāṇi vāgurika.śabara.pulinda.caṇḍāla.araṇya.carā rakṣeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: The intervening areas should be guarded by trappers, <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, and forest-dwellers.

children.text:
KAZ02.01.07a/ ṛtvig.ācārya.purohita.śrotriyebhyo brahma.deyāny adaṇḍa.karāṇy abhirūpa.dāyādakāni prayacchet -
KAZ02.01.07b/ adhyakṣa.saṃkhyāyaka.ādibhyo gopa.sthānika.anīkastha.cikitsaka.aśva.damaka.jaṅghākārikebhyaś ca vikraya.ādhāna.varjāni //
children.translated_text: He should grant <s>brahmadeya</s> (Brahmin land grants), exempt from fines and taxes, with proper inheritance provisions, to sacrificial priests, teachers, chaplains, and learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; and [grants] exempt from sale or mortgage to superintendents, accountants, and others such as village headmen, district officers, army commanders, physicians, horse-trainers, and couriers.

children.text: KAZ02.01.08/ karadebhyaḥ kṛta.kṣetrāṇy aikapuruṣikāṇi prayacchet //
children.translated_text: He should grant cultivated fields to tax-payers as individual holdings.

children.text: KAZ02.01.09/ akṛtāni kartṛbhyo na^ādeyāni //
children.translated_text: Uncultivated [fields] should not be taken away from those who would cultivate them.

children.text: KAZ02.01.10/ akṛṣatām āchidya^anyebhyaḥ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: He should confiscate [land] from those not cultivating and give it to others.

children.text: KAZ02.01.11/ grāma.bhṛtaka.vaidehakā vā kṛṣeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or village laborers and merchants should cultivate [the land].

children.text: KAZ02.01.12/ akṛṣanto vā^avahīnaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or those not cultivating should pay compensation for the shortfall.

children.text: KAZ02.01.13/ dhānya.paśu.hiraṇyaiś ca^etān anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: He should support them with grain, cattle, and gold.

children.text: KAZ02.01.14/ tāny anu sukhena dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should repay those [advances] at their convenience.

children.text: KAZ02.01.15/ anugraha.parihārau ca^etebbhyaḥ kośa.vṛddhi.karau dadyāt, kośa.upaghātakau varjayet //
children.translated_text: He should grant favors and exemptions to these [settlers] that increase the treasury, and avoid those that deplete it.

children.text: KAZ02.01.16/ alpa.kośo hi rājā paura.jānapadān eva grasate //
children.translated_text: For a king with a depleted treasury devours the townspeople and rural folk themselves.

children.text: KAZ02.01.17/ niveśa.sama.kālaṃ yathā.āgatakaṃ vā parihāraṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: He should grant exemptions at the time of settlement or as they arrive.

children.text: KAZ02.01.18/ nivṛtta.parihārān pitā^iva^anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Those whose exemptions have expired, he should support like a father.

children.text: KAZ02.01.19/ ākara.karma.anta.dravya.hasti.vana.vraja.vaṇik.patha.pracārān vāri.sthala.patha.paṇya.pattanāni ca niveśayet //
children.translated_text: He should establish mines, manufacturing operations, timber and elephant forests, cattle camps, trade routes and caravan paths, waterways, land routes, market towns, and ports.

children.text: KAZ02.01.20/ saha.udakam āhārya^udakaṃ vā setuṃ bandhayet //
children.translated_text: He should construct a reservoir [for irrigation] using natural water or channeled water.

children.text: KAZ02.01.21/ anyeṣāṃ vā badhnatāṃ bhūmi.mārga.vṛkṣa.upakaraṇa.anugrahaṃ kuryāt, puṇya.sthāna.ārāmāṇāṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Or he should assist others building [reservoirs] with land, roads, timber, and implements, as well as [for] sacred sites and public gardens.

children.text: KAZ02.01.22/ sambhūya.setu.bandhād apakrāmataḥ karmakara.balīvardāḥ karma kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: From a cooperative irrigation project, those who withdraw should have their work done by laborers and oxen.

children.text: KAZ02.01.23/ vyayakarmaṇi ca bhāgī syāt, na ca^aṃśaṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: And he should bear his share of the expenditure but not receive a share [of the produce].

children.text: KAZ02.01.24/ matsya.plava.hari.tapaṇyānāṃ setuṣu rājā svāmyaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: The king should assume ownership over fisheries, ferries, and green and gold [products] in the reservoirs.

children.text: KAZ02.01.25/ dāsa.āhitaka.bandhūn aśṛṇvato rājā vinayaṃ grāhayet //
children.translated_text: The king should impose discipline on those who do not heed their slaves, bonded servants, and kinsmen.

children.text: KAZ02.01.26/ bāla.vṛddha.vyasany.anāthāṃś ca rājā bibhṛyāt, striyam aprajātāṃ prajātāyaś ca putrān //
children.translated_text: The king should maintain the young, the aged, the afflicted, the destitute, and also childless women and the sons of women who have given birth [but cannot support them].

children.text: KAZ02.01.27/ bāla.dravyaṃ grāma.vṛddhā vardhayeyur ā vyavahāra.prāpaṇāt, deva.dravyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: The village elders should manage the property of minors until they come of age, as well as the property of deities.

children.text: KAZ02.01.28/ apatya.dāraṃ mātā.pitarau bhrātṛṛn aprāpta.vyavahārān bhaginīḥ kanyā vidhavāś ca^abibhrataḥ śaktimato dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, anyatra patitebhyaḥ, anyatra mātuḥ //
children.translated_text: A fine of twelve <s>paṇas</s> [is imposed] on one who, having the means, fails to maintain his offspring, wife, parents, minor brothers, unmarried sisters, or widows — except for those who have fallen [from caste], and except for the mother.

children.text: KAZ02.01.29/ putra.dāram apratividhāya pravrajataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, striyaṃ ca pravrājayataḥ //
children.translated_text: The lowest <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) penalty [is imposed] on one who renounces [the world] without making provision for his sons and wife, and [also] on one who causes a woman to renounce.

children.text: KAZ02.01.30/ lupta.vyāyāmaḥ pravrajed āpṛcchya dharmasthān //
children.translated_text: One who has retired from active life may renounce, after taking leave of the judges (<s>dharmasthānas</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.01.31/ anyathā niyamyeta //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, he should be restrained.

children.text: KAZ02.01.32/ vānaprasthād anyaḥ pravrajita.bhāvaḥ, sajātād anyaḥ saṃghaḥ, sāmutthāyikād anyaḥ samaya.anubandho vā na^asya jana.padam upaniviśeta //
children.translated_text: No other form of renunciation than that of the forest hermit (<s>vānaprastha</s>), no congregation other than one of the same caste, and no association other than that arising from common purpose should settle in his countryside.

children.text: KAZ02.01.33/ na ca tatra^ārāmā vihāra.arthā vā śālāḥ syuḥ //
