children.translated_text: Nor should there be parks or halls for recreational purposes there.

children.text: KAZ02.01.34/ naṭa.nartaka.gāyana.vādaka.vāg.jīvana.kuśīlavā na karma.vighnaṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Actors, dancers, singers, musicians, professional reciters, and entertainers should not cause obstruction to work.

children.text: KAZ02.01.35/ nirāśrayatvād grāmāṇāṃ kṣetra.abhiratatvāc ca puruṣāṇāṃ kośa.viṣṭi.dravya.dhānya.rasa.vṛddhir bhavati //
children.translated_text: Because villages are without [idle] dependents and men are devoted to their fields, there is an increase in the treasury's [revenues from] forced labor, goods, grain, and liquids.

children.text:
KAZ02.01.36ab/ para.cakra.aṭavī.grastaṃ vyādhi.durbhikṣa.pīḍitam /[ś]
KAZ02.01.36cd/ deśaṃ parihared rājā vyaya.krīḍāś ca vārayet //[ś]
KAZ02.01.37ab/ daṇḍa.viṣṭi.kara.ābādhai rakṣed upahatāṃ kṛṣim /[ś]
KAZ02.01.37cd/ stena.vyāla.viṣa.grāhair vyādhibhiś ca paśu.vrajān //[ś]
KAZ02.01.38ab/ vallabhaiḥ kārmikaiḥ stenair anta.pālaiś ca pīḍitam /[ś]
KAZ02.01.38cd/ śodhayet paśu.saṃghaiś ca kṣīyamāṇaṃ vaṇik.patham //[ś]
KAZ02.01.39ab/ evaṃ dravya.dvi.pavanaṃ setu.bandham atha^ākarān /[ś]
KAZ02.01.39cd/ rakṣet pūrva.kṛtān rājā navāṃś ca^abhipravartayet //[ś] E
children.translated_text: The king should protect a territory seized by enemy forces or forest tribes, or afflicted by disease and famine, and should prohibit wasteful expenditures and amusements. He should protect agriculture from harm caused by punishments, forced labor, and taxes, and cattle herds from thieves, wild animals, poisons, crocodiles, and diseases. He should cleanse trade routes that are declining due to [oppression by] royal favorites, officials, thieves, or border-guards, as well as [from obstructions by] herds of cattle. Thus the king should protect existing dams, reservoirs, and mines, like a breeze twice [refreshing] wealth, and also inaugurate new ones.

children.text:
(ḍisposal of non-agricultural land)
KAZ02.2.01/ akṛṣyāyāṃ bhūmau paśubhyo vivītāni prayacchet //
children.translated_text:
(Disposal of non-agricultural land)
On non-agricultural land, he should grant pasture grounds for cattle.

children.text: KAZ02.2.02/ pradiṣṭa.abhaya.sthāvara.jaṅgamāni ca brahma.soma.araṇyāni tapasvibhyo go.ruta.parāṇi prayacchet //
children.translated_text: He should grant <s>Brahma</s>-forests and <s>Soma</s>-forests — with declared safety for stationary and moving beings — to ascetics, extending up to one <s>goruta</s> [in size].

children.text: KAZ02.2.03/ tāvan.mātram eka.dvāraṃ khāta.guptaṃ svādu.phala.gulma.guccham akaṇṭaki.drumam uttāna.toya.āśayaṃ dānta.mṛga.catuṣpadaṃ bhagna.nakha.daṃṣṭra.vyālaṃ mārgayuka.hasti.hastinīka.labhaṃ mṛga.vanaṃ vihāra.arthaṃ rājñaḥ kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should have a game forest made for the king's recreation, of corresponding size, with a single entrance, protected by a moat, with sweet-fruited shrubs and clusters [of trees], free from thorny trees, with open water reservoirs, with tamed deer and quadrupeds, with wild animals whose claws and fangs have been broken, and stocked with herds of elephants, males and females.

children.text: KAZ02.2.04/ sarva.atithi.mṛgaṃ pratyante ca^anyan.mṛga.vanaṃ bhūmi.vaśena vā niveśayet //
children.translated_text: On the frontier, he should establish another game forest open to all visitors, or [arrange it] according to the terrain.

children.text: KAZ02.2.05/ kupya.pradiṣṭānāṃ ca dravyāṇām eka.ekaśo vanāni niveśayet, dravya.vana.karma.antān aṭavīś ca dravya.vana.apāśrayāḥ //
children.translated_text: He should establish separate forests for each of the raw materials listed [earlier], and workshops at the edges of the timber forests and wildernesses dependent on the material forests.

children.text: KAZ02.2.06/ pratyante hasti.vanam aṭavy.ārakṣaṃ niveśayet //
children.translated_text: On the frontier, he should establish an elephant forest under the protection of the forest guards.

children.text: KAZ02.2.07/ nāga.vana.adhyakṣaḥ pārvataṃ na^ādeyaṃ sāra.sama.anūpaṃ ca nāga.vanaṃ vidita.paryanta.praveśa.niṣkāsaṃ nāga.vana.pālaiḥ pālayet //
children.translated_text: The superintendent of elephant forests (<s>nāgavanādhyakṣa</s>) should have the elephant forest — whether mountainous, riverine, or consisting of level marshland — guarded by elephant-forest keepers, with its boundaries, entrances, and exits well-known.

children.text: KAZ02.2.08/ hasti.ghātinaṃ hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should kill one who slays an elephant.

children.text: KAZ02.2.09/ danta.yugaṃ svayaṃ.mṛtasya^āharataḥ sapāda.catuṣpaṇo lābhaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who brings a pair of tusks from a naturally dead [elephant] receives a reward of four and a quarter <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.2.10/ nāga.vana.pālā hastipaka.pāda.pāśika.saimika.vana.caraka.pārikarmika.sakhā hasti.mūtra.purīṣac.channa.gandhā bhallātakī.śākhā.pracchannāḥ pañcabhiḥ saptabhir vā hasti.bandhakībhiḥ saha carantaḥ śayyā.sthāna.padyā.leṇḍa.kūla.ghāta.uddeśena hasti.kula.paryagraṃ vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: The elephant-forest keepers, accompanied by elephant trainers, foot-rope men, chain-rope men, trackers, forest rangers, and attendants, concealing their scent with elephant urine, dung, and hidden [under] branches of the <s>bhallātakī</s> tree, roaming with five or seven female decoy elephants, should ascertain the herds of elephants by their resting places, standing grounds, footprints, dung, bank-damage, and rubbing marks.

children.text: KAZ02.2.11/ yūtha.caram eka.caraṃ niryūthaṃ yūtha.patiṃ hastinaṃ vyālaṃ mattaṃ potaṃ bandha.muktaṃ ca nibandhena vidyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should identify by their distinctive marks: the herd-roaming [elephant], the solitary roamer, the one expelled from the herd, the herd leader, the [ordinary] elephant, the rogue, the one in rut, the young one, and the one released from captivity.

children.text: KAZ02.2.12/ anīkastha.pramāṇaiḥ praśasta.vyañjana.ācārān hastino gṛhṇīyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should capture elephants of praiseworthy marks and conduct, of the standard sizes prescribed for military ranks.

children.text: KAZ02.2.13/ hasti.pradhānaṃ vijayo rājñaḥ //
children.translated_text: Victory for the king depends primarily on elephants.

children.text: KAZ02.2.14/ para.anīka.vyūha.durga.skandha.āvāra.pramardanā hy atipramāṇa.śarīrāḥ prāṇa.hara.karmāṇo hastinaḥ //
children.translated_text: For elephants, with their enormous bodies and life-destroying power, crush the enemy's battle formations, forts, and encampments.

children.text:
KAZ02.2.15ab/ kāliṅga.aṅgarajāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prācyāś cedi.karūṣajāḥ /[ś]
KAZ02.2.15cd/ dāśārṇāś ca^apara.antāś ca dvipānāṃ madhyamā matāḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.2.16ab/ saurāṣṭrikāḥ pāñcanadās teṣāṃ pratyavarāḥ smṛtāḥ /[ś]
KAZ02.2.16cd/ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇā vīryaṃ javas tejaś ca vardhate //[ś] E

(Construction of forts)
KAZ02.3.01/ caturdiśaṃ jana.pada.ante sāmparāyikaṃ daiva.kṛtaṃ durgaṃ kārayet, antar.dvīpaṃ sthalaṃ vā nimna.avaruddham audakam, prāstaraṃ guhāṃ vā pārvatam, nirudaka.stambam iriṇaṃ vā dhānvanam, khañjana.udakaṃ stamba.gahanaṃ vā vana.durgam //
children.translated_text:
(Construction of forts)
In the four directions, at the borders of the settled countryside, he should have strategic forts constructed, either natural or man-made: an island or dry ground enclosed by low-lying [water] for a water-fort; a rocky [plateau] or cave for a mountain-fort; a waterless, bushy salt-flat for a desert-fort; or a [place with] knee-deep water and dense thickets for a forest-fort.

children.text: KAZ02.3.02/ teṣāṃ nadī.parvata.durgaṃ jana.pada.ārakṣa.sthānam, dhānvana.vana.durgam aṭavī.sthānam āpady apasāro vā //
children.translated_text: Of these, the river-and-mountain fort serves as a defensive position for the settled countryside, while the desert and forest forts serve as a refuge for the forest-dwellers or as a place of retreat in calamity.

children.text: KAZ02.3.03/ jana.pada.madhye samudaya.sthānaṃ sthānīyaṃ niveśayet, vāstuka.praśaste deśe nadī.saṅgame hradasya^aviśoṣasya^aṅke sarasas taṭākasya vā, vṛttaṃ dīrghaṃ catur.aśraṃ vā vāstu.vaśena vā pradakṣiṇa.udakaṃ paṇya.puṭa.bhedanam aṃsapatha.vāri.pathābhyām upetam //
children.translated_text: In the center of the settled countryside, he should establish a capital city (<s>sthānīya</s>) as a center of collection [of revenue], in a place approved by the architects, at the confluence of rivers, on the bend of an unfailing lake, or by the side of a reservoir or tank — circular, oblong, or square, or shaped according to the terrain, with water flowing clockwise, divided into commercial quarters, and provided with side-roads and waterways.

children.text: KAZ02.3.04/ tasya parikhās tisro daṇḍa.antarāḥ kārayet caturdaśa dvādaśa daśa^iti daṇḍān vistīrṇāḥ, vistārād avagāḍhāḥ pāda.ūnam ardhaṃ vā, tribhāga.mūlāḥ, mūla.catur.aśrā vā, pāṣāṇa.upahitāḥ pāṣāṇa.iṣṭakā.baddha.pārśvā vā, toya.antikīr āgantu.toya.pūrṇā vā saparivāhāḥ padma.grāhavatīś ca //
children.translated_text: He should have three moats constructed around it at intervals of one <s>daṇḍa</s>, fourteen, twelve, and ten <s>daṇḍas</s> wide respectively, as deep as their width less a quarter or half, with a base one-third [of the width], or square at the base, lined with stone or with sides bound by stone and brick, filled with water up to the brim — either natural or brought in — with outlets, and stocked with lotuses and crocodiles.

children.text: KAZ02.3.05/ caturdaṇḍa.apakṛṣṭaṃ parikhāyāḥ ṣaḍdaṇḍa.ucchritam avaruddhaṃ tad.dviguṇa.viṣkambhaṃ khātād vapraṃ kārayed ūrdhva.cayaṃ mañca.pṛṣṭhaṃ kumbha.kukṣikaṃ vā hastibhir gobhiś ca kṣuṇṇaṃ kaṇṭaki.gulma.viṣa.vallī.pratānavantam //
children.translated_text: At a distance of four <s>daṇḍas</s> from the moat, he should have a rampart (<s>vapra</s>) raised six <s>daṇḍas</s> high, narrowing [toward the top], twice as wide [at the base] as [its height], from the excavated earth, with its layers built upward, topped with platforms, with a belly-shaped [profile], trampled firm by elephants and cattle, and covered with thorny bushes, poisonous creepers, and trailing plants.

children.text: KAZ02.3.06/ pāṃsu.śeṣeṇa vāstuc.chidraṃ rāja.bhavanaṃ vā pūrayet //
children.translated_text: With the remaining earth, he should fill up gaps in the settlement or [build] the royal residence.

children.text:
KAZ02.3.07a/ vaprasya^upari prākāraṃ viṣkambha.dviguṇa.utsedham aiṣṭakaṃ dvādaśa.hastād ūrdhvam ojaṃ yugmaṃ vā ā caturviṃśati.hastād iti kārayet -
KAZ02.3.07b/ ratha.caryā.saṃcāraṃ tāla.mūlaṃ murajakaiḥ kapi.śīrṣakaiś ca^ācita.agram //
children.translated_text:
On top of the rampart, he should construct a wall of brick, rising to twice the width in height, from twelve <s>hastas</s> upward in odd or even [measure] up to twenty-four <s>hastas</s>,
with passage-ways for chariots at the base, its top studded with turrets (<s>murajakas</s>) and parapets (<s>kapiśīrṣakas</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.3.08/ pṛthu.śilā.saṃhataṃ vā śailaṃ kārayet, na tv eva kāṣṭamayam //
children.translated_text: Or he should construct it of broad stone slabs cemented together — but never of wood.

children.text: KAZ02.3.09/ agnir avahito hi tasmin vasati //
children.translated_text: For fire, once ignited, dwells in that [wood].

children.text: KAZ02.3.10/ viṣkambha.catur.aśram aṭṭālakam utsedha.sama.avakṣepa.sopānaṃ kārayet triṃśad.daṇḍa.antaraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: He should construct watch-towers, square in width, with staircases descending as deep as [the tower is] high, at intervals of thirty <s>daṇḍas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.3.11/ dvayor aṭṭālakayor madhye saharmya.dvi.talām adhyardhāya.āyāmāṃ pratolīṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Between two watch-towers, he should construct a covered way (<s>pratolī</s>) with an upper story of two floors and one and a half times [a daṇḍa] in length.

children.text: KAZ02.3.12/ aṭṭālaka.pratolī.madhye tri.dhānuṣka.adhiṣṭhānaṃ sa-apidhānac.chidra.phalaka.saṃhatam indra.kośaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Between the watch-tower and the covered way, he should construct a covered turret (<s>indrakośa</s>) — a platform for three archers, fitted with planks having openings and lids.

children.text: KAZ02.3.13/ antareṣu dvihasta.viṣkambhaṃ pārśve catur.guṇa.āyāmaṃ deva.pathaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: In the intervals, he should construct a parapet walk (<s>devapatha</s>) two <s>hastas</s> wide and four times as long on each side.

children.text: KAZ02.3.14/ daṇḍa.antarā dvi.daṇḍa.antarā vā caryāḥ kārayet, agrāhye deśe pradhāvanikāṃ niṣkira.dvāraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: He should construct pathways at intervals of one or two <s>daṇḍas</s>, and in impassable terrain, a sally port and an exit gate.

children.text: KAZ02.3.15/ bahir.jānu.bhañjanī.śūla.prakara.kūpa.kūṭa.avapāta.kaṇṭaka.pratisara.ahi.pṛṣṭha.tāla.pattra.śṛṅga.aṭaka.śva.daṃṣṭra.argala.upaskandana.pāduka.ambarīṣa.uda.pānakaiḥ praticchannaṃ channa.pathaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should construct a concealed pathway outside [the wall], equipped with knee-breakers, spike-fences, pits, trap-falls, thorn-hedges, serpent-backed [obstacles], palm-leaf [blades], horn-shaped [stakes], dog-tooth [spikes], bolt-barriers, stepping-traps, fire-pans, and wells.

children.text: KAZ02.3.16/ prākāram ubhayato meṇḍhakam adhyardha.daṇḍaṃ kṛtvā pratolī.ṣaṭ.tulā.antaraṃ dvāraṃ niveśayet pañca.daṇḍād eka.uttaram ā.aṣṭa.daṇḍād iti catur.aśraṃ ṣaḍ.bhāgam āyāmād.adhikam aṣṭa.bhāgaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Having made the wall on both sides with ram-shaped [buttresses] of one and a half <s>daṇḍas</s>, he should install a gate at intervals of six <s>tulās</s> in the covered way — square, from five <s>daṇḍas</s> plus one up to eight <s>daṇḍas</s>, with a width exceeding the length by one-sixth or one-eighth.

children.text: KAZ02.3.17/ pañca.daśa.hastād eka.uttaram ā.aṣṭādaśa.hastād iti tala.utsedhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The height of the floor is from fifteen <s>hastas</s> plus one up to eighteen <s>hastas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.3.18/ stambhasya parikṣepaḥ ṣaḍ.āyāmo, dviguṇo nikhātaḥ, cūlikāyāś catur.bhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: The circumference of the pillar is six times its width, twice [that] is the depth of embedding, and the pinnacle is one-fourth [of the circumference].

children.text: KAZ02.3.19/ ādi.talasya pañca.bhāgāḥ śālā vāpī sīmā.gṛhaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: The ground floor has five sections: the hall, the step-well, the boundary-room, and [others].

children.text: KAZ02.3.20/ daśa.bhāgikau dvau pratimañcau, antaram āṇī.harmyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Two side-platforms of one-tenth [size each], and in between, the turret-chamber.

children.text: KAZ02.3.21/ samucchrayād ardha.tale sthūṇā.bandhaś ca //
children.translated_text: At half the total height, [there is] a beam-frame.

children.text: KAZ02.3.22/ ardha.vāstukam uttama.agāram, tribhāga.antaraṃ vā, iṣṭakā.avabaddha.pārśvam, vāmataḥ pradakṣiṇa.sopānaṃ gūḍha.bhitti.sopānam itarataḥ //
children.translated_text: The upper chamber is half the floor-area, or one-third the interval, with sides bound by bricks, with a clockwise stairway on the left and a stairway within the wall on the other side.

children.text: KAZ02.3.23/ dvi.hastaṃ toraṇa.śiraḥ //
children.translated_text: The top of the gateway arch is two <s>hastas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.3.24/ tri.pañca.bhāgikau dvau kapāṭa.yogau //
children.translated_text: The two door-joints are in the proportion of three-fifths.

children.text: KAZ02.3.25/ dvau parighau //
children.translated_text: There are two cross-bars.

children.text: KAZ02.3.26/ aratnir indra.kīlaḥ //
children.translated_text: The bolt (<s>indrakīla</s>) is one <s>aratni</s> [long].

children.text: KAZ02.3.27/ pañca.hastam āṇi.dvāram //
children.translated_text: The wicket gate is five <s>hastas</s> [high].

children.text: KAZ02.3.28/ catvāro hasti.parighāḥ //
children.translated_text: There are four elephant-bars.

children.text: KAZ02.3.29/ niveśa.ardhaṃ hasti.nakham //
children.translated_text: The elephant's claw [projection] is half the entrance [width].

children.text: KAZ02.3.30/ mukha.samaḥ saṃkramaḥ saṃhāryo bhūmimayo vā nirudake //
children.translated_text: The drawbridge is level with the entrance, retractable, or made of earth [when the moat is] waterless.

children.text: KAZ02.3.31/ prākāra.samaṃ mukham avasthāpya tri.bhāga.godhā.mukhaṃ gopuraṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Having set the entrance level with the wall, he should construct the gate-tower (<s>gopura</s>) with a monitor-lizard-shaped front one-third [of the total].

children.text: KAZ02.3.32/ prākāra.madhye vāpīṃ kṛtvā puṣkariṇī.dvāram, catuḥ.śālam adhyardha.antaraṃ sāṇikaṃ kumārī.puram, muṇḍa.harmya.dvi.talaṃ muṇḍaka.dvāram, bhūmi.dravya.vaśena vā niveśayet //
children.translated_text: In the middle of the wall, having made a step-well, [he should construct] a lotus-pool gate, a four-hall [structure] with one-and-a-half intervals fitted with turrets as a maiden's quarter (<s>kumārīpura</s>), a flat-topped two-storied building with a flat-roofed entrance — or [lay it out] according to the terrain and materials [available].

children.text: KAZ02.3.33/ tri.bhāga.adhika.āyāmā bhāṇḍa.vāhinīḥ kulyāḥ kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should construct supply channels one-third longer [than the regular canals] for transporting goods.

children.text:
KAZ02.3.34ab/ tāsu pāṣāṇa.kuddālāḥ kuṭhārī.kāṇḍa.kalpanāḥ /[ś]
KAZ02.3.34cd/ muṣuṇḍhī.mudgarā daṇḍāś cakra.yantra.śataghnayaḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.3.35ab/ kāryāḥ kārmārikāḥ śūlā vedhana.agrāś ca veṇavaḥ /[ś]
KAZ02.3.35cd/ uṣṭra.grīvyo^agni.samyogāḥ kupya.kalpe ca yo vidhiḥ //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
In those [channels and forts, there should be]: stone [projectiles], spades, axes, shafts and cut timber,
clubs, maces, staffs, wheel-devices, and <s>śataghnīs</s> (hundred-killers);
iron-tipped [implements], tridents, pointed bamboo [lances],
camel-neck [catapults], fire-devices, and whatever is prescribed in the section on raw materials.

children.text:
(ḷay-out of the fortified city)
KAZ02.4.01/ trayaḥ prācīnā rāja.mārgās traya udīcīnā iti vāstu.vibhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Layout of the fortified city)
Three royal highways running east-west and three running north-south — this is the division of the city plan.

children.text: KAZ02.4.02/ sa dvādaśa.dvāro yukta.udaka.bhramac.channa.pathaḥ //
children.translated_text: It has twelve gates, with properly channeled water and concealed pathways.

children.text: KAZ02.4.03/ catur.daṇḍa.antarā rathyāḥ //
children.translated_text: The streets are at intervals of four <s>daṇḍas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.4.04/ rāja.mārga.droṇa.mukha.sthānīya.rāṣṭra.vivīta.pathāḥ samyānīya.vyūha.śmaśāna.grāma.pathāś ca^aṣṭa.daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: The royal highways, main intersections, provincial roads, country paths, and open pasture roads, as well as the processional avenues, military parade grounds, and cremation-ground roads — [all are] eight <s>daṇḍas</s> [wide].

children.text: KAZ02.4.05/ catur.daṇḍaḥ setu.vana.pathaḥ, dvi.daṇḍo hasti.kṣetra.pathaḥ, pañca.aratnayo ratha.pathaḥ, catvāraḥ paśu.pathaḥ, dvau kṣudra.paśu.manuṣya.pathaḥ //
children.translated_text: The embankment and forest road is four <s>daṇḍas</s>; the elephant-ground road is two <s>daṇḍas</s>; the chariot road is five <s>aratnis</s>; the cattle path is four [aratnis]; the path for small animals and humans is two [aratnis].

children.text: KAZ02.4.06/ pravīre vāstuni rāja.niveśaś cāturvarṇya.samājīve //
children.translated_text: In the best part of the city, the royal residence is situated, [designed to] accommodate all four social classes.

children.text: KAZ02.4.07/ vāstu.hṛdayād uttare nava.bhāge yathā.ukta.vidhānam antaḥpuraṃ prān.mukham udan.mukhaṃ vā kārayet //
children.translated_text: In the ninth division north of the city center, he should construct the inner apartments (<s>antaḥpura</s>) facing east or north, arranged as prescribed.

children.text: KAZ02.4.08/ tasya pūrva.uttaraṃ bhāgam ācārya.purohita.ijyā.toya.sthānaṃ mantriṇaś ca^āvaseyuḥ, pūrva.dakṣiṇaṃ bhāgm mahānasaṃ hasti.śālā koṣṭha.agāraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: In its northeastern section, the residences of the teachers, the chaplain, the sacrificial ground, and the water facilities should be placed, along with the counselors; in the southeastern section, the kitchen, the elephant stables, and the storehouses.

children.text: KAZ02.4.09/ tataḥ paraṃ gandha.mālya.rasa.paṇyāḥ prasādhana.kāravaḥ kṣatriyāś ca pūrvāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Beyond that, dealers in perfumes, garlands, and beverages, personal attendants, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> [of the royal guard], should inhabit the eastern quarter.

children.text: KAZ02.4.10/ dakṣiṇa.pūrvaṃ bhāgaṃ bhāṇḍa.agāram akṣa.paṭalaṃ karma.niṣadyāś ca, dakṣiṇa.paścimaṃ bhāgaṃ kupya.gṛham āyudha.agāraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: In the southeastern section — the merchandise warehouse, the accounting office, and the workshops; in the southwestern section — the raw materials storehouse and the armory.

children.text: KAZ02.4.11/ tataḥ paraṃ nagara.dhānya.vyāvahārika.kārmāntika.bala.adhyakṣāḥ pakva.anna.surā.māṃsa.paṇyā rūpājīvās tālāvacarā vaiśyāś ca dakṣiṇāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Beyond that, the superintendents of the city grain supply, commerce, manufacturing, and the army, dealers in cooked food, liquor, and meat, courtesans, acrobats, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> should inhabit the southern quarter.

children.text: KAZ02.4.12/ paścima.dakṣiṇaṃ bhāgaṃ khara.uṣṭra.gupti.sthānaṃ karma.gṛhaṃ ca, paścima.uttaraṃ bhāgaṃ yāna.ratha.śālāḥ //
children.translated_text: In the southwestern section — the station for donkeys and camels, and the workshops; in the northwestern section — the sheds for vehicles and chariots.

children.text: KAZ02.4.13/ tataḥ param ūrṇā.sūtra.veṇu.carma.varma.śastra.āvaraṇa.kāravaḥ śūdrāś ca paścimāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Beyond that, workers in wool, thread, bamboo, leather, armor, and weapons, and <s>Śūdras</s> should inhabit the western quarter.

children.text: KAZ02.4.14/ uttara.paścimaṃ bhāgaṃ paṇya.bhaiṣajya.gṛham, uttara.pūrvaṃ bhāgaṃ kośo gava.aśvaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: In the northwestern section — the shops for merchandise and medicines; in the northeastern section — the treasury and the cow and horse [stables].

children.text: KAZ02.4.15/ tataḥ paraṃ nagara.rāja.devatā.loha.maṇi.kāravo brāhmaṇāś ca^uttarāṃ diśam adhivaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Beyond that, workers in silver, gold, and gems for the city and the king, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should inhabit the northern quarter.

children.text: KAZ02.4.16/ vāstuc.chidra.anuśāleṣu śreṇī.prapaṇi.nikāyā āvaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: In the gaps of the city plan and along the side-halls, guilds (<s>śreṇī</s>), merchant associations, and communities should reside.

children.text: KAZ02.4.17/ apara.ajita.apratihata.jayanta.vaijayanta.koṣṭhān śiva.vaiśravaṇa.aśvi.śrī.madirā.gṛhāṇi ca pura.madhye kārayet //
children.translated_text: In the center of the city, he should construct the storehouses [named] <s>Apara</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Apratihata</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Vaijayanta</s>, as well as the temples of <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, and the liquor-house.

children.text: KAZ02.4.18/ yathā.uddeśaṃ vāstu.devatāḥ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should install the tutelary deities of the site in their designated places.

children.text: KAZ02.4.19/ brāhma.aindra.yāmya.saināpatyāni dvārāṇi //
children.translated_text: The gates [are named after]: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and the Generalissimo (<s>Senāpati</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.4.20/ bahiḥ parikhāyā dhanuḥ.śata.apakṛṣṭāś caitya.puṇya.sthāna.vana.setu.bandhāḥ kāryāḥ, yathā.diśaṃ ca dig.devatāḥ //
children.translated_text: Outside the moat, at a distance of a hundred bow-lengths, sacred groves, sanctuaries, forest-gardens, and embankments should be constructed, and the directional deities [installed] according to the [appropriate] directions.

children.text: KAZ02.4.21/ uttaraḥ pūrvo vā śmaśāna.bhāgo varṇa.uttamānām, dakṣiṇena śmaśānaṃ varṇa.avarāṇām //
children.translated_text: The cremation ground for the upper classes is in the northern or eastern section; the cremation ground for the lower classes is to the south.

children.text: KAZ02.4.22/ tasya^atikrame pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For transgression of this [rule], the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> fine [is imposed].

children.text: KAZ02.4.23/ pāṣaṇḍa.caṇḍālānāṃ śmaśāna.ante vāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Heretics (<s>pāṣaṇḍas</s>) and <s>Caṇḍālas</s> shall reside at the edge of the cremation ground.

children.text: KAZ02.4.24/ karma.anta.kṣetra.vaśena kuṭumbināṃ sīmānaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should establish the boundaries of householders according to the work-fields and cultivated areas.

children.text: KAZ02.4.25/ teṣu puṣpa.phala.vāṭān dhānya.paṇya.nicayāṃś ca^anujñātāḥ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: In those [areas], they should, with permission, establish flower and fruit gardens and stores of grain and merchandise.

children.text: KAZ02.4.26/ daśa.kulī.vāṭaṃ kūpa.sthānam //
children.translated_text: A group of ten families (<s>daśakulīvāṭa</s>) [should have] a well.

children.text: KAZ02.4.27/ sarva.sneha.dhānya.kṣāra.lavaṇa.gandha.bhaiṣajya.śuṣka.śāka.yavasa.vallūra.tṛṇa.kāṣṭha.loha.carma.aṅgāra.snāyu.viṣa.viṣāṇa.veṇu.valkala.sāra.dāru.praharaṇa.āvaraṇa.aśma.nicayān aneka.varṣa.upabhoga.sahān kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should have stored up — capable of lasting many years — stocks of all oils, grains, alkalis, salts, perfumes, medicines, dried vegetables, fodder, dried meat, grass, firewood, metals, hides, charcoal, sinews, poisons, horns, bamboo, bark, hardwood, weapons, shields, and stones.

children.text: KAZ02.4.28/ navena^anavaṃ śodhayet //
children.translated_text: He should replenish old [stores] with new.

children.text: KAZ02.4.29/ hasti.aśva.ratha.pādātam aneka.mukhyam avasthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should station [forces of] elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry with multiple chiefs.

children.text: KAZ02.4.30/ aneka.mukhyaṃ hi paraspara.bhayāt para.upajāpaṃ na^upaiti //
children.translated_text: For [forces] with multiple chiefs do not, out of mutual fear, submit to the enemy's instigation.

children.text: KAZ02.4.31/ etena^anta.pāla.durga.saṃskārā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the construction and maintenance of frontier forts has been explained.

children.text:
KAZ02.4.32ab/ na ca bāhirikān kuryāt pure rāṣṭra.upaghātakān /[ś]
KAZ02.4.32cd/ kṣipej jana.pade ca^etān sarvān vā dāpayet karān //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
He should not allow within the city those outsiders who are destructive to the countryside;
he should expel them into the countryside, or make all of them pay taxes.

children.text:
(ṭhe work of store-keeping by the director of stories)
KAZ02.5.01/ samnidhātā kośa.gṛhaṃ paṇya.gṛhaṃ koṣṭha.agāraṃ kupya.gṛham āyudha.agāraṃ bandhana.agāraṃ ca kārayet //
children.translated_text:
(The work of storekeeping by the director of stores)
The superintendent of stores (<s>saṃnidhātā</s>) should have constructed a treasury building, a commodities building, a granary, a raw materials building, an armory, and a prison.

children.text: KAZ02.5.02/ catur.aśrāṃ vāpīm an-udaka.upasnehāṃ khānayitvā pṛthu.śilābhir ubhayataḥ pārśvaṃ mūlaṃ ca pracitya sāra.dāru.pañjaraṃ bhūmi.samaṃ tri.talam aneka.vidhānaṃ kuṭṭima.deśa.sthāna.talam eka.dvāraṃ yantra.yukta.sopānaṃ bhūmi.gṛhaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Having had a square reservoir dug, not subject to seepage, and having lined both sides and the bottom with broad stones, he should have an underground chamber constructed — with a framework of hardwood, level with the ground, three stories deep, with multiple compartments, a paved floor, a single entrance, and a mechanically operated staircase.

children.text: KAZ02.5.03/ tasya^upari^ubhayato.niṣedhaṃ sa-pragrīvam aiṣṭakaṃ bhāṇḍa.vāhinī.parikṣiptaṃ kośa.gṛhaṃ kārayet, prāsādaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Above it, he should have the treasury building constructed — of brick, with barriers on both sides, a raised parapet, surrounded by a goods-transport passage; or a multi-storied building.

children.text: KAZ02.5.04/ jana.pada.ante dhruva.nidhim āpad.artham abhityaktaiḥ kārayet //
children.translated_text: At the edge of the countryside, he should have a permanent reserve fund stored for emergencies, [funded] by those who have renounced [their surplus].

children.text:
KAZ02.5.05a/ pakva.iṣṭakā.stambhaṃ catuḥ.śālam eka.dvāram aneka.sthāna.talaṃ vivṛta.stambha.apasāram ubhayataḥ paṇya.gṛhaṃ koṣṭha.agāraṃ ca -
KAZ02.5.05b/ dīrgha.bahu.śālaṃ kakṣya.āvṛta.kuḍyam antaḥ kupya.gṛham, tad eva bhūmi.gṛha.yuktam āyudha.agāraṃ -
KAZ02.5.05c/ pṛthag.dharma.sthīyaṃ mahā.mātrīyaṃ vibhakta.strī.puruṣa.sthānam apasārataḥ sugupta.kakṣyaṃ bandhana.agāraṃ kārayet //
KAZ02.5.06/ sarveṣāṃ śālāḥ khāta.uda.pāna.varca.snāna.gṛha.agni.viṣa.trāṇa.mārjāra.nakula.ārakṣā.sva.daivata.pūjana.yuktāḥ kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should have all the halls equipped with trenches, wells, latrines, bathing rooms, fire protection, poison antidotes, facilities for cats and mongooses [against vermin], and [space for] worship of the presiding deity.

children.text: KAZ02.5.07/ koṣṭha.agāre varṣamānam aratni.mukhaṃ kuṇḍaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: In the granary, he should install a rain gauge — a bowl with the mouth one <s>aratni</s> [wide].

children.text: KAZ02.5.08/ tat.jāta.karaṇa.adhiṣṭhitaḥ purāṇaṃ navaṃ ca ratnaṃ sāraṃ phalgu kupyaṃ vā pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Superintended by officials appointed for that purpose, he should receive old and new jewels, valuable [items], inferior goods, and raw materials.

children.text: KAZ02.5.09/ tatra ratna.upadhāv uttamo daṇḍaḥ kartuḥ kārayituś ca sāra.upadhau madhyamaḥ, phalgu.kupya.upadhau tat^ ca tāvat^ ca daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein, for fraud involving jewels, the highest penalty [applies] to both the doer and the instigator; for [fraud involving] valuable goods, the middle penalty; for inferior goods and raw materials, such and such a penalty.

children.text: KAZ02.5.10/ rūpa.darśaka.viśuddhaṃ hiraṇyaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: He should accept gold [only when] certified as pure by the assayer.

children.text: KAZ02.5.11/ aśuddhaṃ chedayet //
children.translated_text: Impure [gold] he should have cut [confiscated].

children.text: KAZ02.5.12/ āhartuḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For the one who brings [impure gold], the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) penalty [applies].

children.text: KAZ02.5.13/ śuddhaṃ pūrṇam abhinavaṃ ca dhānyaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: He should accept grain [only when it is] clean, full, and fresh.

children.text: KAZ02.5.14/ viparyaye mūlya.dviguṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the opposite case, the penalty is double the value.

children.text: KAZ02.5.15/ tena paṇyaṃ kupyam āyudhaṃ ca vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: By this, [the rules for] commodities, raw materials, and weapons are [also] explained.

children.text: KAZ02.5.16/ sarva.adhikaraṇeṣu yukta.upayukta.tatpuruṣāṇāṃ paṇa.ādi.catuṣ.paṇa.parama.apahāreṣu pūrva.madhyama.uttama.vadhā daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: In all departments, for the appointed officials, their subordinates, and their servants, for misappropriations starting from one <s>paṇa</s> up to a maximum of four <s>paṇas</s>, the penalties are the first, middle, and highest level of corporal punishment.

children.text: KAZ02.5.17/ kośa.adhiṣṭhitasya kośa.avacchede ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text: For the one superintending the treasury, if the treasury is breached — death.

children.text: KAZ02.5.18/ tad.vaiyāvṛtya.karāṇām ardha.daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: For those who serve under him — half the penalty.

children.text: KAZ02.5.19/ paribhāṣaṇam avijñāte //
children.translated_text: A reprimand for the uninformed [officials].

children.text: KAZ02.5.20/ corāṇām abhipradharṣaṇe citro ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text: For thieves who commit robbery — varied forms of capital punishment.

children.text:
KAZ02.5.21/ tasmād āpta.puruWa.adhiṣṭhitaḥ samnidhātā nicayān anutiṣṭhet //KAZ02.5.22a/ bāhyam abhyantaraṃ cāyaṃ vidyād varṣa.śatād api / [ś]
KAZ02.5.22b/ yathā pṛṣṭo na sajjeta vyaye śeṣe ca saṃcaye // [ś] E
children.translated_text:
Therefore, the superintendent of stores, assisted by trustworthy men, should maintain the stocks.
He should know both the external and internal [accounts], even from a hundred years ago,
so that when questioned, he may not falter regarding expenditure, balance, and accumulation.

children.text:
Chapter 6 section24 ṭhe settiṅg up of revenue by the administration
KAZ02.6.01/ samāhartā durgaṃ rāṣṭraṃ khaniṃ setuṃ vanaṃ vrajaṃ vaṇik.pathaṃ ca^avekṣeta //
children.translated_text:
(The setting up of revenue by the administration)
The collector (<s>samāhartā</s>) should oversee the fort, the countryside, mines, irrigated lands, forests, herds, and trade routes.

children.text: KAZ02.6.02/ śulkaṃ daṇḍaḥ pautavaṃ nāgariko lakṣaṇa.adhyakṣo mudrā.adhyakṣaḥ surā sūnā sūtraṃ tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ kṣāraḥ sauvarṇikaḥ paṇya.saṃsthā veśyā dyūtaṃ vāstukaṃ kāru.śilpi.gaṇo devatā.adhyakṣo dvāra.bahirikā.ādeyaṃ ca durgam //
children.translated_text: Customs duties, fines, standardized weights, the city superintendent, the superintendent of marks, the superintendent of seals, liquor, slaughter, textiles, oil, ghee, alkalis, the superintendent of gold, the trading guild, courtesans, gambling, the building superintendent, the guild of artisans and craftsmen, the superintendent of temples, and the revenue from gates and external [tolls] — these constitute [the revenue of] the fort.

children.text: KAZ02.6.03/ sītā bhāgo baliḥ karo vaṇik nadī.pālas taro nāvaḥ pattanaṃ vivicitaṃ vartanī rajjuś cora.rajjuś ca rāṣṭram //
children.translated_text: Crown lands (<s>sītā</s>), share [of produce], tribute (<s>bali</s>), tax (<s>kara</s>), merchants, river-guards, ferry [tolls], boats, ports, fines for offenses, road-cesses, rope-taxes, and fines for theft — these constitute [the revenue of] the countryside.

children.text: KAZ02.6.04/ suvarṇa.rajata.vajra.maṇi.muktā.pravāla.śaṅkha.loha.lavaṇa.bhūmi.prastara.rasa.dhātavaḥ khaniḥ //
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, diamonds, gems, pearls, corals, conch shells, metals, salt, earths, and mineral ores — these constitute mines.

children.text: KAZ02.6.05/ puṣpa.phala.vāṭa.ṣaṇḍa.kedāra.mūla.vāpāḥ setuḥ //
children.translated_text: Flower gardens, fruit orchards, groves, irrigated rice fields, and root and seed plots — these constitute irrigated lands (<s>setu</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.6.06/ paśu.mṛga.dravya.hasti.vana.parigraho vanam //
children.translated_text: The reservation of livestock, wild animals, materials, and elephant forests — this constitutes forests.

children.text: KAZ02.6.07/ go.mahiṣam aja.avikaṃ khara.uṣtram aśva.aśvataraṃ ca vrajaḥ //
children.translated_text: Cattle and buffaloes, goats and sheep, donkeys and camels, horses and mules — these constitute herds.

children.text: KAZ02.6.08/ sthala.patho vāri.pathaś ca vaṇik.pathaḥ //
children.translated_text: Land routes and water routes — these constitute trade routes.

children.text: KAZ02.6.09/ ity āya.śarīram //
children.translated_text: This is the body of revenue.

children.text: KAZ02.6.10/ mūlyaṃ bhāgo vyājī parighaḥ klptam(klṛptam) rūpikam atyayaś ca^āya.mukham //
children.translated_text: Price [of goods sold], share, commission, surcharge, fixed revenue, coined money, and fines — these are the heads of revenue.

children.text: KAZ02.6.11/ deva.pitṛ.pūjā.dāna.artham, svasti.vācanam, antaḥpuram, mahānasam, dūta.prāvartimam, koṣṭha.agāram, āyudha.agāram, paṇya.gṛham, kupya.gṛham, karma.anto, viṣṭiḥ, patti.aśva.ratha.dvipa.parigraho, go.maṇḍalam, paśu.mṛga.pakṣi.vyāla.vāṭāḥ, kāṣṭha.tṛṇa.vāṭāś ca^iti vyaya.śarīram //
children.translated_text: Worship of gods and ancestors, gifts, benedictions, the inner palace, the kitchen, envoys and dispatches, the granary, the armory, the commodities building, the raw materials building, manufacturing operations, forced labor, the maintenance of infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants, the cattle establishment, enclosures for domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and serpents, and stores of firewood and grass — this is the body of expenditure.

children.text: KAZ02.6.12/ rāja.varṣaṃ māsaḥ pakṣo divasaś ca vyuṣṭam, varṣā.hemanta.grīṣmāṇāṃ tṛtīya.saptamā divasa.ūnāḥ pakṣāḥ śeṣāḥ pūrṇāḥ, pṛthag.adhimāsakaḥ, iti kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: The royal year, the month, the fortnight, and the day are the elapsed [periods]; the fortnights of the rainy, winter, and summer seasons, diminished by the third and seventh days, with the remainder being full; each having a separate intercalary month — this is [the reckoning of] time.

children.text: KAZ02.6.13/ karaṇīyaṃ siddhaṃ śeṣam āya.vyayau nīvī ca //
children.translated_text: What is to be done, what has been accomplished, the balance, revenue and expenditure, and the capital fund (<s>nīvī</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.6.14/ saṃsthānaṃ pracāraḥ śarīra.avasthāpanam ādānaṃ sarva.samudaya.piṇḍaḥ saṃjātaṃ - etat karaṇīyam //
children.translated_text: The establishment, operation, form of the organization, collection, and the total of all accumulations and what has accrued — this is what is 'to be done.'

children.text: KAZ02.6.15/ kośa.arpitaṃ rāja.hāraḥ pura.vyayaś ca praviṣṭaṃ parama.saṃvatsara.anuvṛttaṃ śāsana.muktaṃ mukha.ājñaptaṃ ca^apātanīyaṃ - etat siddham //
children.translated_text: What has been deposited in the treasury, the king's share, and the city expenditure that has been entered [in the accounts], that which follows the precedent of the previous year, that which is exempt by royal order, and that which is directed verbally and is not to be contested — this is what is 'accomplished.'

children.text: KAZ02.6.16/ siddhi.karma.yogaḥ daṇḍa.śeṣam āharaṇīyaṃ balāt.kṛta.pratiṣṭabdham avamṛṣṭaṃ ca praśodhyaṃ - etat^śeṣam, asāram alpa.sāraṃ ca //
children.translated_text: The remainder of completed work obligations, the balance of fines, what is to be collected, what has been forcibly withheld or obstructed, and what has been overlooked and requires settlement — this is the 'balance,' both valueless and of little value.

children.text: KAZ02.6.17/ vartamānaḥ paryuṣito^anya.jātaś ca^āyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Current, carried over, and miscellaneous — these are [the types of] revenue.

children.text: KAZ02.6.18/ divasa.anuvṛtto vartamānaḥ //
children.translated_text: That which follows daily is 'current.'

children.text: KAZ02.6.19/ parama.sāṃvatsarikaḥ para.pracāra.saṃkrānto vā paryuṣitaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Carried over' is from the previous year or transferred from another jurisdiction.

children.text: KAZ02.6.20/ naṣṭa.prasmṛtam āyukta.daṇḍaḥ pārśvaṃ pārihīṇikam aupāyanikaṃ ḍamara.gataka.svam aputrakaṃ nidhiś ca^anya.jātaḥ //
children.translated_text: Lost and forgotten [property], fines [levied by] superintendents, collateral, [property of] those who have abandoned [their claims], profits from stratagems, [property from] disturbances and confiscations, escheated property of those who die without heirs, and treasure trove — these are 'miscellaneous.'

children.text: KAZ02.6.21/ vikṣepa.vyādhita.antara.ārambha.śeṣaṃ ca vyaya.pratyāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: And [savings from] deferred, interrupted, or suspended operations and the remainder from within [projects already begun] are revenue offsets against expenditure.

children.text: KAZ02.6.22/ vikriye paṇyānām argha.vṛddhir upajā, māna.unmāna.viśeṣo vyājī, kraya.saṃgharṣe vārdha.vṛddhiḥ - ity āyaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the sale of commodities, the increase in price is profit (<s>upajā</s>); the difference in weight and measure is commission (<s>vyājī</s>); in a bidding competition, the increase is [profit from] competitive pricing — these are [forms of] revenue.

children.text: KAZ02.6.23/ nityo nitya.utpādiko lābho lābha.utpādika iti vyayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Regular [expenditure], that which generates regular [returns], profit, and that which generates profit — these are [the types of] expenditure.

children.text: KAZ02.6.24/ divasa.anuvṛtto nityaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Regular' is that which follows daily.

children.text: KAZ02.6.25/ pakṣa.māsa.saṃvatsara.lābho lābhaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Profit' is the gain [accruing] over a fortnight, month, or year.

children.text: KAZ02.6.26/ tayor utpanno nitya.utpādiko lābha.utpādika iti vyayaḥ //
children.translated_text: What arises from those two — 'that which generates regular [returns]' and 'that which generates profit' — these are [types of] expenditure.

children.text: KAZ02.6.27/ saṃjātād āya.vyaya.viśuddhā nīvī, prāptā ca^anuvṛttā ca //
children.translated_text: The capital fund (<s>nīvī</s>) is the balance after deducting revenue and expenditure from the total accruals, both received and ongoing.

children.text:
KAZ02.6.28ab/ evaṃ kuryāt samudayaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca^āyasya darśayet /[ś]
KAZ02.6.28cd/ hrāsaṃ vyayasya ca prājñaḥ sādhayec ca viparyayam //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
Thus should the wise one consolidate the total, show an increase in revenue,
a decrease in expenditure, and enforce the reverse [if needed].

children.text:
(ṭhe topic of accounts in the records and audit office)
KAZ02.7.01/ akṣa.paṭalam adhyakṣaḥ prān.mukham udan.mukhaṃ vā vibhakta.upasthānaṃ nibandha.pustaka.sthānaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text:
(The topic of accounts in the records and audit office)
The superintendent of accounts should have the records office (<s>akṣapaṭala</s>) constructed facing east or north, with separate sections, and [a place for] the record books.

children.text:
KAZ02.7.02/ tatra^adhikaraṇānāṃ saṃkhyā.pracāra.saṃjāta.agram, karma.antānāṃ dravya.prayoga.vṛddhi.kṣaya.vyaya.prayāma.vyājī.yoga.sthāna.vetana.viṣṭi.pramāṇam, ratna.sāra.phalgu.kupyānām argha.prativarṇaka.māna.pratimāna.unmāna.avamāna.bhāṇḍam, deśa.grāma.jāti.kula.saṃghānāṃ dharma.vyavahāra.caritra.saṃsthānam, rāja.upajīvināṃ
pragraha.pradeśa.bhoga.parihāra.bhakta.vetana.lābham, rājñaś ca patnī.putrāṇāṃ ratna.bhūmi.lābhaṃ nirdeśa.utpātika.pratīkāra.lābham, mitra.amitrāṇāṃ ca saṃdhi.vigraha.pradāna.ādānaṃ nibandha.pustakasthaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text:
Therein he should have entered in the record books: the numerical summaries, operations, and net results of all departments; the outlay of materials, growth, depreciation, expenditure, extension, commission, allocation, wages, and forced labor for manufacturing operations; the prices, quality grades, weights, counterweights, excess measures, and deficit measures for jewels, valuable goods, inferior goods, and raw materials; the customs, legal procedures, practices, and institutional arrangements of regions, villages, castes, families, and corporations; the allowances, grants, enjoyments, exemptions, food provisions, wages, and profits
of those maintained by the king; the gains of the king's wives and sons in jewels and land, and the gains from mandated restitutions and remedies for calamities; and the treaties, hostilities, gifts, and receipts of allies and enemies.

children.text: KAZ02.7.03/ tataḥ sarva.adhikaraṇānāṃ karaṇīyaṃ siddhaṃ śeṣam āya.vyayau nīvīm upasthānaṃ pracāraṃ caritraṃ saṃsthānaṃ ca nibandhena prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Then, for all departments, he should furnish — by written record — what is to be done, what has been accomplished, the balance, revenue and expenditure, the capital fund, the established procedure, the operations, the practices, and the institutional arrangements.

children.text: KAZ02.7.04/ uttama.madhyama.avareṣu ca karmasu taj.jātikam adhyakṣaṃ kuryāt, sāmudayikeṣv avaklṛptikam(avakḷptikam) yam upahatya rājā na^anutapyeta //
children.translated_text: For superior, middling, and inferior tasks, he should appoint a superintendent of the corresponding rank; for comprehensive [tasks], one who is expendable — one whose destruction the king would not regret.

children.text: KAZ02.7.05/ sahagrāhiṇaḥ pratibhuvaḥ karma.upajīvinaḥ putrā bhrātaro bhāryā duhitaro bhṛtyāś ca^asya karmac.chedaṃ vaheyuḥ //
children.translated_text: His co-receivers, guarantors, those who live by the work, his sons, brothers, wife, daughters, and servants should bear [the liability for] any breach of duty.

children.text: KAZ02.7.06/ tri.śataṃ catuḥ.pañcāśat^ ca^ahorātrāṇāṃ karma.saṃvatsaraḥ //
children.translated_text: Three hundred and fifty-four day-and-night periods constitute the work-year.

children.text: KAZ02.7.07/ tam āṣāḍhī.paryavasānam ūnaṃ pūrṇaṃ vā dadyāt //
children.translated_text: He should submit the [annual accounts] — whether deficient or complete — by the end of [the month of] <s>Āṣāḍha</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.08/ karaṇa.adhiṣṭhitam adhimāsakaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: An intercalary month should be made with officials in charge of accounts.

children.text: KAZ02.7.09/ apasarpa.adhiṣṭhitaṃca pracāram //
children.translated_text: And the operations [should be verified] with secret agents in charge.

children.text:
KAZ02.7.10/ pracāra.caritra.saṃsthānāny anupalabhamāno hi prakṛtaḥ samudayam ajñānena parihāpayati, utthāna.kleśa.asahatvād ālasyena, śabdādiṣv indriya.artheṣu prasaktaḥ pramādena, saṃkrośa.adharma.anartha.bhīru.bhāyena, kārya.arthiṣv anugraha.buddhiḥ kāmena, hiṃsā.buddhiḥ kopena, vidyā.dravya.vallabha.apāśrayād darpeṇa, tulā.māna.tarka.gaṇita.antara.upadhānāt^
lobhena //
children.translated_text: For an official who, not ascertaining the operations, practices, and institutional arrangements, causes loss to revenue — through ignorance, because he is of ordinary nature; through laziness, because he cannot bear the effort of exertion; through negligence, because he is attached to sensory pleasures of sound and the like; through fear, because he dreads public outcry, unrighteousness, and calamity; through desire, because he is disposed to favor those who seek his help; through anger, because he is disposed to harm; through arrogance, because he relies on the support of learning, wealth, or favorites; through greed, because he manipulates balances, measures, calculations, and accounting —

children.text: KAZ02.7.11/ "teṣām ānupūrvyā yāvān artha.upaghātas tāvān eka.uttaro daṇḍaḥ" iti mānavāḥ //
children.translated_text: "For these, in ascending order, the penalty should exceed [the preceding] by one [unit], corresponding to the extent of the financial damage" — say the followers of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.12/ "sarvatra^aṣṭa.guṇaḥ" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "In all cases, eightfold [the damage]" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.13/ "daśa.guṇaḥ" iti bārhaspatyāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Tenfold" — say the followers of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.14/ "viṃśati.guṇaḥ" ity auśanasāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Twentyfold" — say the followers of <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.15/ yathā.aparādham iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "According to the offense" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.16/ gāṇanikyāni āṣāḍhīm āgaccheyuḥ //
children.translated_text: The accountants should come [to submit their reports] by [the month of] <s>Āṣāḍha</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.17/ āgatānāṃ samudra.pustaka.bhāṇḍa.nīvīkānām ekatra.asambhāṣā.avarodhaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.17/ He should arrange that those who have arrived — the maritime, record-keeping, merchandise, and balance-sheet officers — be detained without being allowed to confer with one another.

children.text: KAZ02.7.18/ āya.vyaya.nīvīnām agrāṇi śrutvā nīvīm avahārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.18/ Having heard the opening entries of income, expenditure, and balance, he should take up the balance.

children.text: KAZ02.7.19/ yac ca^agrād āyasya^antara.parṇe nīvyāṃ vardheta vyayasya vā yat parihāpayet, tad aṣṭa.guṇam adhyakṣaṃ dāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.19/ Whatever, from the opening figure of income, increases in the balance on the subsidiary ledger, or whatever of expenditure it causes to be reduced — for that he should make the superintendent pay eightfold.

children.text: KAZ02.7.20/ viparyaye tam eva prati syāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.20/ In the reverse case, the same [penalty] should apply to him [the accuser].

children.text: KAZ02.7.21/ yathā.kālam anāgatānām apustaka.bhāṇḍa.nīvīkānāṃ vā deya.daśa.bandho daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.21/ For those who do not arrive on time, or who come without record-books, merchandise, or balance-sheets — the fine is one-tenth of the amount due.

children.text: KAZ02.7.22/ kārmike ca^upasthite kāraṇikasya^apratibadhnataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.22/ When the operative [officer] presents himself but the accounting officer does not respond, [the latter receives] the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> (violent offense) fine.

children.text: KAZ02.7.23/ viparyaye kārmikasya dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.23/ In the reverse case, the operative [officer receives] double.

children.text: KAZ02.7.24/ pracāra.samaṃ mahā.mātrāḥ samagrāḥ śrāvayeyur aviṣama.mantrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.24/ The high officials, assembled together in accordance with procedure, should make declarations without secret deliberation.

children.text: KAZ02.7.25/ pṛthag.bhūto mithyā.vādī ca^eṣām uttamaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.25/ One who separates himself or speaks falsely among them should pay the highest fine.

children.text: KAZ02.7.26/ akṛta.aho.rūpa.haraṃ māsam ākāṅkṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.26/ One who has not produced the daily account should be given a month's grace.

children.text: KAZ02.7.27/ māsād ūrdhvaṃ māsa.dviśata.uttaraṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.27/ After a month, he should pay a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>] per month.

children.text: KAZ02.7.28/ alpa.śeṣa.lekhya.nīvīkaṃ pañca.rātram ākāṅkṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.28/ One who has only a small remainder of written records and balance-sheets should be given five days' grace.

children.text: KAZ02.7.29/ tataḥ paraṃ kośa.pūrvam aho.rūpa.haraṃ dharma.vyavahāra.caritra.saṃsthāna.saṃkalana.nirvartana.anumāna.cāra.prayogair avekṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.29/ After that, the daily account-holder, beginning with the treasury, should be examined by means of <s>dharma</s> (moral persuasion), <s>vyavahāra</s> (legal procedure), <s>caritra</s> (customary practice), <s>saṃsthāna</s> (documentary evidence), <s>saṃkalana</s> (reckoning), <s>nirvartana</s> (verification of output), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>cāra</s> (secret investigation) tests.

children.text: KAZ02.7.30/ divasa.pañca.rātra.pakṣa.māsa.cāturmāsya.saṃvatsaraiś ca pratisamānayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.30/ And he should reconcile [the accounts] by day, five-day period, fortnight, month, four-month period, and year.

children.text: KAZ02.7.31/ vyuṣṭa.deśa.kāla.mukha.utpatti.anuvṛtti.pramāṇa.dāyaka.dāpaka.nibandhaka.pratigrāhakaiś ca^ayaṃ samānayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.31/ He should reconcile the income by means of the past record, locality, time, origin, continuity, quantity, the payer, the collector, the recorder, and the receiver.

children.text: KAZ02.7.32/ vyuṣṭa.deśa.kāla.mukha.lābha.kāraṇa.deya.yoga.pramāṇa.ājñāpaka.uddhāraka.vidhātṛka.pratigrāhakaiś ca vyayaṃ samānayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.32/ He should reconcile the expenditure by means of the past record, locality, time, origin, profit, cause, amount due, authorization, quantity, the one who orders, the one who disburses, the one who administers, and the receiver.

children.text: KAZ02.7.33/ vyuṣṭa.deśa.kāla.mukha.anuvartana.rūpa.lakṣaṇa.pramāṇa.nikṣepa.bhājana.gopāyakaiś ca nīvīṃ samānayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.33/ He should reconcile the balance by means of the past record, locality, time, origin, continuity, form, distinguishing marks, quantity, the deposit, the container, and the custodian.

children.text: KAZ02.7.34/ rāja.arthe kāraṇikasya^apratibadhnataḥ pratiṣedhayato vā^ājñāṃ nibandhād āya.vyayam anyathā nīvīm avalikhato dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.34/ When the accounting officer does not respond to a matter concerning the king's interest, or obstructs [it], or records income or expenditure contrary to the register, or [records] the balance [differently] — double [the penalty].

children.text: KAZ02.7.35/ krama.avahīnam utkramam avijñātaṃ punar.uktaṃ vā vastukam avalikhato dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.35/ For recording an item out of sequence, out of order, unidentified, or duplicated — the fine is twelve <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.7.36/ nīvīm avalikhato dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.36/ For [so] recording a balance — double.

children.text: KAZ02.7.37/ bhakṣayato^aṣṭa.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.37/ For embezzling — eightfold.

children.text: KAZ02.7.38/ nāśayataḥ pañca.bandhaḥ pratidānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.38/ For destroying [records] — five times [the amount], plus restitution.

children.text: KAZ02.7.39/ mithyā.vāde steya.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.39/ For making a false statement — the penalty for theft.

children.text: KAZ02.7.40/ paścāt.pratijñāte dvi.guṇaḥ, prasmṛta.utpanne ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.7.40/ For retracting a confession afterwards — double; and also for [a claim] arising from forgetfulness.

children.text:
KAZ02.7.41ab/ aparādhaṃ saheta^alpaṃ tuṣyed alpe^api ca^udaye / [ś]
KAZ02.7.41cd/ mahā.upakāraṃ ca^adhyakṣaṃ pragraheṇa^abhipūjayet //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.7.41ab/ He should tolerate a small offense and be content even with a small increase;
KAZ02.7.41cd/ and a superintendent of great service he should honor with favors.

children.text:
(ṛecovery of revenue misappropriated by state employees)
KAZ02.8.01/ kośa.pūrvāḥ sarva.ārambhāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Recovery of revenue misappropriated by state employees)
KAZ02.8.01/ All undertakings begin with the treasury.

children.text: KAZ02.8.02/ tasmāt pūrvaṃ kośam avekṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.02/ Therefore, he should first examine the treasury.

children.text: KAZ02.8.03/ pracāra.samṛddhiś caritra.anugrahaś cora.nigraho yukta.pratiṣedhaḥ sasya.sampat paṇya.bāhulyam upasarga.pramokṣaḥ parihāra.kṣayo hiraṇya.upāyanam iti kośa.vṛddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.03/ Prosperity of operations, benefits through good conduct, suppression of thieves, restraint of officials, abundance of crops, plenty of merchandise, freedom from calamities, reduction of exemptions, and revenue in gold — these constitute the growth of the treasury.

children.text: KAZ02.8.04/ pratibandhaḥ prayogo vyavahāro^avastāraḥ parihāpaṇam upabhogaḥ parivartanam apahāraś ca^iti kośa.kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.04/ Obstruction, misapplication, commercial loss, postponement, causing diminution, personal enjoyment, substitution, and embezzlement — these constitute the decline of the treasury.

children.text: KAZ02.8.05/ siddhīnām asādhanam anavatāraṇam apraveśanaṃ vā pratibandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.05/ Obstruction is the non-collection of accomplished revenues, their non-deposit, or their non-entry [into the treasury].

children.text: KAZ02.8.06/ tatra daśa.bandho daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.06/ The fine for that is one-tenth [of the amount].

children.text: KAZ02.8.07/ kośa.dravyāṇāṃ vṛddhi.prayogāḥ prayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.07/ Misapplication is the lending at interest of treasury property.

children.text: KAZ02.8.08/ paṇya.vyavahāro vyavahāraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.08/ Commercial loss is [loss through] trade in merchandise.

children.text: KAZ02.8.09/ tatra phala.dvi.guṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.09/ The fine for that is double the profit [lost].

children.text: KAZ02.8.10/ siddhaṃ kālam aprāptaṃ karoti^ aprāptaṃ prāptaṃ vā^ity avastāraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.10/ Postponement is when one makes what is accomplished [appear] not to have arrived on time, or what has not arrived [appear to have] arrived.

children.text: KAZ02.8.11/ tatra pañca.bandho daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.11/ The fine for that is five times [the amount].

children.text: KAZ02.8.12/ klṛptam(kḷptam) āyaṃ parihāpayati vyayaṃ vā vivardhayati^iti parihāpaṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.12/ Causing diminution is when one reduces the established income or increases the expenditure.

children.text: KAZ02.8.13/ tatra hīna.catur.guṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.13/ The fine for that is four times the deficiency.

children.text: KAZ02.8.14/ svayam anyair vā rāja.dravyāṇām upabhojanam upabhogaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.14/ Personal enjoyment is the use of royal property by oneself or by others.

children.text: KAZ02.8.15/ tatra ratna.upabhoge ghātaḥ, sāra.upabhoge madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, phalgu.kupya.upabhoge tac ca tāvat^ ca daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.15/ For enjoying precious goods — death; for enjoying valuable commodities — the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for enjoying worthless raw materials — a fine equal to the [value of the] item itself plus the same amount.

children.text: KAZ02.8.16/ rāja.dravyāṇām anya.dravyena^ādānaṃ parivartanam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.16/ Substitution is the exchange of royal property for other goods.

children.text: KAZ02.8.17/ tad upabhogena vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.17/ That is explained by [the rules for] personal enjoyment.

children.text: KAZ02.8.18/ siddham āyaṃ na praveśayati, nibaddhaṃ vyayaṃ na prayacchati, prāptāṃ nīvīṃ vipratijānīta ity apahāraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.18/ Embezzlement is when one does not deposit accomplished income, does not disburse committed expenditure, or denies a received balance.

children.text: KAZ02.8.19/ tatra dvādaśa.guṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.19/ The fine for that is twelve times [the amount].

children.text: KAZ02.8.20/ teṣāṃ haraṇa.upāyāś catvāriṃśat //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.20/ The methods of misappropriation by them are forty.

children.text:
KAZ02.8.21a/ pūrvaṃ siddhaṃ paścād avatāritam, paścāt siddhaṃ pūrvam avatāritam, sādhyaṃ na siddham, asādhyaṃ siddham, siddham asiddhaṃ kṛtam, asiddhaṃ siddhaṃ kṛtam, alpa.siddhaṃ bahu kṛtam, bahu.siddham alpaṃ kṛtam, anyat siddham anyat kṛtam, anyataḥ siddham anyataḥ kṛtam,-
KAZ02.8.21b/ deyaṃ na dattam, adeyaṃ dattam, kāle na dattam, akāle dattam, alpaṃ dattaṃ bahu kṛtam, bahu dattam alpaṃ kṛtam, anyad dattam anyat kṛtam, anyato dattam anyataḥ kṛtam,-
KAZ02.8.21c/ praviṣṭam apraviṣṭaṃ kṛtam, apraviṣṭaṃ praviṣṭaṃ kṛtam, kupyam adatta.mūlyaṃ praviṣṭam, datta.mūlyaṃ na praviṣṭaṃ -
KAZ02.8.21d/ saṃkṣepo vikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ, vikṣepaḥ saṃkṣepo vā, mahā.argham alpa.argheṇa parivartitam, alpa.arghaṃ mahā.argheṇa vā -
KAZ02.8.21e/ samāropito^arghaḥ, pratyavaropito vā, saṃvatsaro māsa.viṣamaḥ kṛtaḥ, māso divasa.viṣamo vā, samāgama.viṣamaḥ, mukha.viṣamaḥ, kārmika.viṣamaḥ -
KAZ02.8.21f/ nirvartana.viṣamaḥ, piṇḍa.viṣamaḥ, varṇa.viṣamaḥ, argha.viṣamaḥ, māna.viṣamaḥ, māpana.viṣamaḥ, bhājana.viṣamaḥ - iti haraṇa.upāyāḥ // -
KAZ02.8.22/ tatra^upayukta.nidhāyaka.nibandhaka.pratigrāhaka.dāyaka.dāpaka.mantri.vaiyāvṛtya.karān eka.ekaśo^anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.8.21a/ [Recording] what was accomplished first as deposited later; what was accomplished later as deposited first; what is collectible as not collected; what is not collectible as collected; what was collected as not collected; what was not collected as collected; what was little collected as much; what was much collected as little; what was collected as one thing recorded as another; what was collected from one source recorded as from another —
KAZ02.8.21b/ what was due not given; what was not due given; what was not given at the proper time; what was given at an improper time; what was given as little recorded as much; what was given as much recorded as little; what was given as one thing recorded as another; what was given from one source recorded as from another —
KAZ02.8.21c/ what entered recorded as not entered; what did not enter recorded as entered; raw material entered without payment of price; price paid but not entered —
KAZ02.8.21d/ a consolidated [amount] recorded as dispersed; a dispersed [amount] recorded as consolidated; what is of great value exchanged for something of little value, or vice versa —
KAZ02.8.21e/ the price raised or lowered; the year made to disagree with months; the month with days; disagreement at assembly; disagreement at the opening entry; disagreement with the operative [officer] —
KAZ02.8.21f/ disagreement in output; disagreement in totals; disagreement in classification; disagreement in price; disagreement in measure; disagreement in weighing; disagreement in containers — these are the methods of misappropriation.
KAZ02.8.22/ Among these, the user, the storer, the recorder, the receiver, the payer, the collector, the minister-supervisor, and the attendants should be questioned one by one.

children.text: KAZ02.8.23/ mithyā.vāde ca^eṣāṃ yukta.samo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.23/ For making a false statement, their fine is equal to that of the [accused] official.

children.text: KAZ02.8.24/ pracāre ca^avaghoṣayet "amunā prakṛtena^upahatāḥ prajñāpayantu" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.24/ And during the investigation, he should proclaim: "Those who have been harmed by such-and-such an official, let them report."

children.text: KAZ02.8.25/ prajñāpayato yathā.upaghātaṃ dāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.25/ To the one who reports, he should make [the official] pay according to the damage.

children.text: KAZ02.8.26/ anekeṣu ca^abhiyogeṣv apavyayamānaḥ sakṛd eva para.uktaḥ sarvaṃ bhajeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.26/ And when facing multiple charges and being confronted, one who, when once challenged by another, confesses everything, should bear [the full penalty].

children.text: KAZ02.8.27/ vaiṣamye sarvatra^anuyogaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.27/ In case of irregularity, he should institute an inquiry everywhere.

children.text: KAZ02.8.28/ mahaty artha.apahāre ca^alpena^api siddhaḥ sarvaṃ bhajeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.28/ And in a major misappropriation, even if convicted of a minor offense, he should bear [the penalty for] all.

children.text: KAZ02.8.29/ kṛta.pratighāta.avasthaḥ sūcako niṣpanna.arthaḥ ṣaṣṭham aṃśaṃ labheta, dvādaśam aṃśaṃ bhṛtakaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.29/ An informer who is in a position where counter-measures have been taken and who has accomplished [the recovery] should receive one-sixth of the share; a hired [informer], one-twelfth.

children.text: KAZ02.8.30/ prabhūta.abhiyogād alpa.niṣpattau niṣpannasya^aṃśaṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.30/ When there is little recovery despite many charges, he should receive a share of what has been recovered.

children.text: KAZ02.8.31/ aniṣpanne śārīraṃ hairaṇyaṃ vā daṇḍaṃ labheta, na ca^anugrāhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.8.31/ When there is no recovery, he should receive a corporal or monetary punishment, and should not be shown mercy.

children.text:
KAZ02.8.32ab/ niṣpattau nikṣiped vādam ātmānaṃ vā^apavāhayet /[ś]
KAZ02.8.32cd/ abhiyukta.upajāpāt tu sūcako vadham āpnuyāt //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.8.32ab/ On recovery, he should withdraw the accusation or have [the accused] removed;
KAZ02.8.32cd/ but an informer who incites the accused should receive death.

children.text:
(Inspection of the ṛork of officers)
KAZ02.9.01/ amātya.sampadā^upetāḥ sarva.adhyakṣāḥ śaktitaḥ karmasu niyojyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Inspection of the work of officers)
KAZ02.9.01/ All superintendents, endowed with the qualifications of a minister, should be appointed to their tasks according to ability.

children.text: KAZ02.9.02/ karmasu ca^eṣāṃ nityaṃ parīkṣāṃ kārayet, citta.anityatvāt^ manuṣyānām //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.02/ And their work should be constantly examined, for human minds are inconstant.

children.text: KAZ02.9.03/ aśva.sadharmāṇo hi manuṣyā niyuktāḥ karmasu vikurvate //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.03/ For men, like horses by nature, when yoked to tasks, behave perversely.

children.text: KAZ02.9.04/ tasmāt kartāraṃ karaṇaṃ deśaṃ kālaṃ kāryaṃ prakṣepam udayaṃ ca^eṣu vidyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.04/ Therefore, he should ascertain [for each of] them the agent, the instrument, the locality, the time, the task, the outlay, and the return.

children.text: KAZ02.9.05/ te yathā.saṃdeśam asaṃhatā avigṛhītāḥ karmāṇi kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.05/ They should carry out their tasks as instructed, without conspiring together and without quarreling.

children.text: KAZ02.9.06/ saṃhatā bhakṣayeyuḥ, vigṛhītā vināśayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.06/ If conspiring, they would embezzle; if quarreling, they would destroy.

children.text: KAZ02.9.07/ na ca^anivedya bhartuḥ kaṃcid ārambhaṃ kuryuḥ, anyatra^āpat.pratīkārebhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.07/ And they should not undertake any venture without reporting to the master, except countermeasures against calamity.

children.text: KAZ02.9.08/ pramāda.sthāneṣu ca^eṣām atyayaṃ sthāpayed divasa.vetana.vyaya.dvi.guṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.08/ And at the places of their negligence, he should impose a penalty double the expenditure of the daily wages.

children.text: KAZ02.9.09/ yaś ca^eṣāṃ yathā.ādiṣṭam arthaṃ saviśeṣaṃ vā karoti sa sthāna.mānau labheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.09/ And whoever among them accomplishes the assigned objective, or more — he should receive [promotion in] position and honors.

children.text: KAZ02.9.10/ "alpa.āyatiś cet^ mahā.vyayo bhakṣayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.10/ "One of small income but great expenditure is embezzling.

children.text: KAZ02.9.11/ viparyaye yathā.āyati.vyayaś ca na bhakṣayati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.11/ In the reverse case, one whose expenditure matches income is not embezzling" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ02.9.12/ apasarpeṇa^eva^upalabhyeta^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.12/ He should be detected only through secret agents — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ02.9.13/ yaḥ samudayaṃ parihāpayati sa rāja.arthaṃ bhakṣayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.13/ One who diminishes the revenue is consuming royal property.

children.text: KAZ02.9.14/ sa ced ajñāna.ādibhiḥ parihāpayati tad enaṃ yathā.guṇaṃ dāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.14/ If he diminishes it out of ignorance and such [causes], he should be made to pay according to the degree.

children.text: KAZ02.9.15/ yaḥ samudayaṃ dvi.guṇam udbhāvayati sa jana.padaṃ bhakṣayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.15/ One who inflates the revenue twofold is consuming the countryside.

children.text: KAZ02.9.16/ sa ced rāja.artham upanayaty alpa.aparādhe vārayitavyaḥ, mahati yathā.aparādhaṃ daṇḍayitavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.16/ If he brings it to the royal treasury, for a small offense he should be warned; for a great one, punished according to the offense.

children.text: KAZ02.9.17/ yaḥ samudayaṃ vyayam upanayati sa puruṣa.karmāṇi bhakṣayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.17/ One who brings revenue [only] to expenditure is consuming the labor of the workers.

children.text: KAZ02.9.18/ sa karma.divasa.dravya.mūlya.puruṣa.vetana.apahāreṣu yathā.aparādhaṃ daṇḍayitavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.18/ He should be punished according to the offense, in cases of misappropriating work-days, materials, prices, or wages of workers.

children.text: KAZ02.9.19/ tasmād asya yo yasminn adhikaraṇe śāsanasthaḥ sa tasya karmaṇo yāthātathyam āya.vyayau ca vyāsa.samāsābhyām ācakṣīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.19/ Therefore, whoever is established by decree in whatever department, he should report the true state of that department's operations and its income and expenditure, both in detail and in summary.

children.text: KAZ02.9.20/ mūla.hara.tādātvika.kadaryāṃś ca pratiṣedhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.20/ And he should restrain those who are root-destroyers, those who seize the present, and misers.

children.text: KAZ02.9.21/ yaḥ pitṛ.paitāmaham artham anyāyena bhakṣayati sa mūla.haraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.21/ One who consumes ancestral and patrimonial wealth unjustly is a root-destroyer.

children.text: KAZ02.9.22/ yo yad yad utpadyate tat tad bhakṣayati sa tādātvikaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.22/ One who consumes whatever arises as it arises is a seizer of the present.

children.text: KAZ02.9.23/ yo bhṛtya.ātma.pīḍābhyām upacinoty arthaṃ sa kadaryaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.23/ One who accumulates wealth by oppressing servants and himself is a miser.

children.text: KAZ02.9.24/ sa pakṣavāṃś ced anādeyaḥ, viparyaye paryādātavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.24/ If such a one has a faction [supporting him], he is not to be seized; in the opposite case, he should be dispossessed.

children.text: KAZ02.9.25/ yo mahaty artha.samudaye sthitaḥ kadaryaḥ samnidhatte^avanidhatte^avasrāvayati vā - samnidhatte sva.veśmani, avanidhatte paura.jānapadeṣu, avasrāvayati para.viṣaye - tasya sattrī mantri.mitra.bhṛtya.bandhu.pakṣam āgatiṃ gatiṃ ca dravyāṇām upalabheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.25/ One who, established in a great revenue collection, is a miser and hoards, conceals, or lets slip [wealth] — hoards in his own house, conceals among townspeople and countryfolk, lets slip to enemy territory — his agent should discover the faction of ministers, friends, servants, and kinsmen, and the flow of goods in and out.

children.text: KAZ02.9.26/ yaś ca^asya para.viṣaye saṃcāraṃ kuryāt tam anupraviśya mantraṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.26/ And whoever facilitates his traffic in enemy territory — entering [the network] through him, one should learn the [treasonous] counsel.

children.text: KAZ02.9.27/ suvidite śatru.śāsana.apadeśena^enaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.27/ When fully ascertained, he should have him killed under the pretext of an enemy's decree.

children.text: KAZ02.9.28/ tasmād asya^adhyakṣāḥ saṃkhyāyaka.lekhaka.rūpa.darśaka.nīvī.grāhaka.uttara.adhyakṣa.sakhāḥ karmaṇi kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.28/ Therefore, his superintendents should carry out their work accompanied by accountants, scribes, inspectors, balance-keepers, and overseeing superintendents.

children.text: KAZ02.9.29/ uttara.adhyakṣā hasti.aśva.ratha.ārohāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.29/ The overseeing superintendents should be riders of elephants, horses, and chariots.

children.text: KAZ02.9.30/ teṣām antevāsinaḥ śilpa.śauca.yuktāḥ saṃkhyāyaka.ādīnām apasarpāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.30/ Their disciples, skilled in the crafts and of proven integrity, should serve as secret agents among the accountants and others.

children.text: KAZ02.9.31/ bahu.mukhyam anityaṃ ca^adhikaraṇaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.9.31/ He should establish an office with many heads and rotating [appointments].

children.text:
KAZ02.9.32ab/ yathā hy anāsvādayituṃ na śakyaṃ jihvā.talasthaṃ madhu7 vā viṣaṃ vā / [ś]
KAZ02.9.32cd/ arthas tathā hy artha.careṇa rājñaḥ svalpo^apy anāsvādayituṃ na śakyaḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.9.33ab/ matsyā yathā^antaḥ salile caranto jñātuṃ na śakyāḥ salilaṃ pibantaḥ /[ś]
KAZ02.9.33cd/ yuktās tathā kārya.vidhau niyuktā jñātuṃ na śakyā dhanam ādadānāḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.9.34ab/ api śakyā gatir jñātuṃ patatāṃ khe patatriṇām /[ś]
KAZ02.9.34cd/ na tu pracchanna.bhāvānāṃ yuktānāṃ caratāṃ gatiḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.9.35ab/ āsrāvayec ca^upacitān viparyasyec ca karmasu /[ś]
KAZ02.9.35cd/ yathā na bhakṣayanty arthaṃ bhakṣitaṃ nirvamanti vā //[ś]
KAZ02.9.36ab/ na bhakṣayanti ye tv arthān nyāyato vardhayanti ca /[ś]
KAZ02.9.36cd/ nitya.adhikārāḥ kāryās te rājñaḥ priya.hite ratāḥ //[ś] E
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.9.32ab/ For just as honey or poison placed on the tip of the tongue cannot remain untasted,
KAZ02.9.32cd/ so too, even a small amount of the king's wealth cannot remain untasted by one who handles it.
KAZ02.9.33ab/ Just as fish moving within the water cannot be detected while drinking the water,
KAZ02.9.33cd/ so too, officials appointed to their duties cannot be detected while taking wealth.
KAZ02.9.34ab/ It is possible to know the course of birds flying in the sky,
KAZ02.9.34cd/ but not the course of officials moving with concealed intentions.
KAZ02.9.35ab/ He should expose those who have grown [rich on embezzlement] and rotate them in their duties,
KAZ02.9.35cd/ so that they neither consume the wealth nor disgorge what has been consumed.
KAZ02.9.36ab/ Those who do not consume the wealth but increase it lawfully —
KAZ02.9.36cd/ they should be given permanent positions, being devoted to the king's welfare and benefit.

children.text:
(On edicts)
#KAZ02.10.01/ śāsane śāsanam ity ācakṣate //
children.translated_text:
(On edicts)
KAZ02.10.01/ The edict (<s>śāsana</s>) — so they call it — is [the instrument of] governance.

children.text: KAZ02.10.02/ śāsana.pradhānā hi rājānaḥ, tan.mūlatvāt saṃdhi.vigrahayoḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.02/ For kings are dependent on edicts, since treaties and wars are rooted in them.

children.text: KAZ02.10.03/ tasmād amātya.sampadā^upetaḥ sarva.samayavid āśu.granthaś cāru.akṣaro lekhana.vācana.samartho lekhakaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.03/ Therefore, the scribe should be endowed with the qualities of a minister, know all conventions, compose swiftly, write in a beautiful hand, and be capable of both writing and reading [aloud].

children.text: KAZ02.10.04/ so^avyagra.manā rājñaḥ saṃdeśaṃ śrutvā niścita.arthaṃ lekhaṃ vidadhyāt deśa.aiśvarya.vaṃśa.nāmadheya.upacāram īśvarasya, deśa.nāmadheya.upacāram anīśvarasya //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.04/ He, with an undistracted mind, having heard the king's message, should draft a document with definite meaning — using the honorifics of territory, sovereignty, lineage, and name for a sovereign, and those of territory, name, and title for a non-sovereign.

children.text:
KAZ02.10.05ab/ jātiṃ kulaṃ sthāna.vayaḥ.śrutāni karma.ṛddhi.śīlāny atha deśa.kālau /[ś]
KAZ02.10.05cd/ yauna.anubandhaṃ ca samīkṣya kārye lekhaṃ vidadhyāt puruṣa.anurūpam //[ś]
KAZ02.10.06/ artha.kramaḥ sambandhaḥ paripūrṇatā mādhuryam audāryaṃ spaṣṭatvam iti lekha.sampat //
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.10.05ab/ Having considered caste, family, position, age, learning,
KAZ02.10.05cd/ occupation, wealth, character, and also place and time, kinship ties, and the task at hand, he should draft a document suited to the person.
KAZ02.10.06/ Orderly arrangement of subject matter, coherence, completeness, sweetness, dignity, and clarity — these are the excellences of a document.

children.text: KAZ02.10.07/ tatra yathāvad anupūrva.kriyā pradhānasya^arthasya pūrvam abhiniveśa ity artha.kramaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.07/ Therein, proper sequential treatment and placing the principal subject matter first — that is orderly arrangement of subject matter.

children.text: KAZ02.10.08/ prastutasya^arthasya^anuparodhād uttarasya vidhānam ā.samāpter iti sambandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.08/ Arranging what follows without disrupting the subject at hand, through to its conclusion — that is coherence.

children.text: KAZ02.10.09/ artha.pada.akṣarāṇām anyūna.atiriktatā hetu.udāharaṇa.dṛṣṭāntair artha.upavarṇanā^aśrānta.padatā^iti paripūrṇatā //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.09/ Neither deficiency nor excess in subject matter, words, and syllables; elucidation of meaning through reasons, illustrations, and examples; and unbroken phrasing — that is completeness.

children.text: KAZ02.10.10/ sukha.upanīta.cāru.artha.śabda.abhidhānaṃ mādhuryam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.10/ Expression of pleasing meaning in elegant words, easily conveyed — that is sweetness.

children.text: KAZ02.10.11/ agrāmya.śabda.abhidhānam audāryam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.11/ Expression in words that are not vulgar — that is dignity.

children.text: KAZ02.10.12/ pratīta.śabda.prayogaḥ spaṣṭatvam iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.12/ Use of well-known words — that is clarity.

children.text: KAZ02.10.13/ a.kāra.ādayo varṇās triṣaṣṭiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.13/ The letters beginning with 'a' are sixty-three.

children.text: KAZ02.10.14/ varṇa.saṃghātaḥ padam //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.14/ A combination of letters is a word (<s>pada</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.10.15/ tac caturvidhaṃ nāma.ākhyāta.upasarga.nipātāś ca^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.15/ That is of four kinds: nouns (<s>nāma</s>), verbs (<s>ākhyāta</s>), prefixes (<s>upasarga</s>), and particles (<s>nipāta</s>).

children.text: KAZ02.10.16/ tatra nāma sattva.abhidhāyi //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.16/ Among these, a noun denotes a substance.

children.text: KAZ02.10.17/ aviśiṣṭa.liṅgam ākhyātaṃ kriyā.vāci //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.17/ A verb, without specific gender marking, expresses action.

children.text: KAZ02.10.18/ kriyā.viśeṣakāḥ pra.ādaya upasargāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.18/ Prefixes beginning with 'pra-' and others modify the action.

children.text: KAZ02.10.19/ avyayāś ca.ādayo nipātāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.19/ Indeclinables beginning with 'ca' and others are particles.

children.text: KAZ02.10.20/ pada.samūho vākyam artha.parisamāptau //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.20/ A group of words constitutes a sentence (<s>vākya</s>) when the meaning is complete.

children.text: KAZ02.10.21/ eka.pada.avaras tri.pada.paraḥ para.pada.artha.anuparodhena vargaḥ kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.21/ A clause should be formed with a minimum of one word and a maximum of three, without disrupting the meaning of the following word.

children.text: KAZ02.10.22/ lekha.parisaṃharaṇa.artha iti.śabdo vācikam asya^iti ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ02.10.22/ The word 'iti' serves to conclude a document, and 'this is his verbal [message]' [marks an oral communication].

children.text:
KAZ02.10.23ab/ nindā praśaṃsā pṛcchā ca tathā^ākhyānam atha^arthanā /[ś]
KAZ02.10.23cd/ pratyākhyānam upālambhaḥ pratiṣedho^atha codanā //[ś]
KAZ02.10.24ab/ sāntvam abhyupapattiś ca bhartsana.anunayau tathā /[ś]
KAZ02.10.24cd/ eteṣv arthāḥ pravartante trayodaśasu lekhajāḥ //[ś]
KAZ02.10.25/ tatra^abhijana.śarīra.karmaṇāṃ doṣa.vacanaṃ nindā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ02.10.23ab/ Censure, praise, inquiry, narration, and entreaty,
KAZ02.10.23cd/ refusal, reproof, prohibition, and command,
KAZ02.10.24ab/ conciliation, promise of assistance, and likewise threatening and appeasing —
KAZ02.10.24cd/ in these thirteen categories do the subjects of documents arise.
