children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.04/ They should know the integrity and corruption of village headmen and superintendents.

children.text: KAZ04.4.05/ yaṃ ca^atra gūḍha.ājīvinaṃ śaṅketa taṃ sattriṇā^apasarpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.05/ And whoever he suspects of being a person with secret income, he should have investigated by a classmate-spy.

children.text: KAZ04.4.06/ dharmasthaṃ viśvāsa.upagataṃ sattrī brūyāt - "asau me bandhur abhiyuktaḥ, tasya^ayam anarthaḥ pratikriyatām, ayaṃ ca^arthaḥ pratigṛhyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.06/ The classmate-spy should say to a judge he has befriended: 'A certain kinsman of mine has been unjustly accused; let his grievance be redressed, and accept this payment.'

children.text: KAZ04.4.07/ sa cet tathā kuryād upadā.grāhaka iti pravāsyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.07/ If he [the judge] does so, he should be banished as a bribe-taker.

children.text: KAZ04.4.08/ tena pradeṣṭāro vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.08/ By this, the [testing of] inspectors is explained.

children.text: KAZ04.4.09/ grāma.kūṭam adhyakṣaṃ vā sattrī brūyāt - "asau jālmaḥ prabhūta.dravyaḥ, tasya^ayam anarthaḥ, tena^enam āhārayasva" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.09/ The classmate-spy should say to a village headman or superintendent: 'A certain fool has much wealth; this [is] his vulnerability. Use it to extract [his wealth].'

children.text: KAZ04.4.10/ sa cet tathā kuryād utkocaka iti pravāsyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.10/ If he does so, he should be banished as an extortioner.

children.text: KAZ04.4.11/ kṛtaka.abhiyukto vā kūṭa.sākṣiṇo^abhijñāta.anartha.vaipulyena^ārabheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.11/ Or one falsely accused should employ false witnesses, beginning with an established record of many [prior] accusations.

children.text: KAZ04.4.12/ te cet tathā kuryuḥ kūṭa.sākṣiṇa iti pravāsyeran //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.12/ If they do so, they should be banished as false witnesses.

children.text: KAZ04.4.13/ tena kūṭa.śrāvaṇa.kārakā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.13/ By this, fabricators of false claims are explained.

children.text: KAZ04.4.14/ yaṃ vā mantra.yoga.mūla.karmabhiḥ śmāśānikair vā saṃvadana.karakaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī brūyāt - "amuṣya bhāryāṃ snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ vā kāmaye, sā māṃ pratikāmayatām, ayaṃ ca^arthaḥ pratigṛhyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.14/ And whoever he suspects of being a practitioner of charms, love-spells, root-magic, or cremation-ground [sorcery] for seduction — the classmate-spy should say to him: 'I desire the wife, daughter-in-law, or daughter of such-and-such a person; let her be made to desire me, and accept this payment.'

children.text: KAZ04.4.15/ sa cet tathā kuryāt saṃvadana.kāraka iti pravāsyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.15/ If he does so, he should be banished as a seduction-sorcerer.

children.text: KAZ04.4.16/ tena kṛtya.abhicāra.śīlau vyākhyātau //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.16/ By this, practitioners of harmful magic and sorcery are explained.

children.text: KAZ04.4.17/ yaṃ vā rasasya kartāraṃ kretāraṃ vikretāraṃ bhaiṣajya.āhāra.vyavahāriṇaṃ vā rasadaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī brūyāt - "asau me śatruḥ, tasya^upaghātaḥ kriyatām, ayaṃ ca^arthaḥ pratigṛhyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.17/ And whoever he suspects of being a maker, buyer, or seller of poison, or a dealer in medicinal poisons — the classmate-spy should say to him: 'Such-and-such is my enemy; let him be harmed, and accept this payment.'

children.text: KAZ04.4.18/ sa cet tathā kuryād rasada iti pravāsyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.18/ If he does so, he should be banished as a poisoner.

children.text: KAZ04.4.19/ tena madana.yoga.vyavahārī vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.19/ By this, a dealer in intoxicating substances is explained.

children.text: KAZ04.4.20/ yaṃ vā nānā.loha.kṣārāṇām aṅgāra.bhasma.asaṃdaṃśa.muṣṭika.adhikaraṇī.bimba.ṭaṅka.mūṣāṇām abhīkṣṇa.kretāraṃ maṣī.bhasma.dhūma.digdha.hasta.vastra.liṅgaṃ karmāra.upakaraṇa.saṃsargaṃ kūṭa.rūpa.kārakaṃ manyeta taṃ sattrī śiṣyatvena saṃvyavahāreṇa ca^anupraviśya prajñāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.20/ And whoever he suspects of being a counterfeiter — [recognizable by] frequently buying various metals and alkalis, charcoal, ash, tongs, gloves, crucibles, moulds, chisels, and melting pots; bearing marks of ink, ash, and smoke on his hands, clothes, and person; and associating with blacksmith's tools — the classmate-spy should enter [his confidence] as a pupil and through business dealings, and then expose him.

children.text: KAZ04.4.21/ prajñātaḥ kūṭa.rūpa.kāraka iti pravāsyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.21/ Once exposed, he should be banished as a counterfeiter.

children.text: KAZ04.4.22/ tena rāgasya^apahartā kūṭa.suvarṇa.vyavahārī ca vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.22/ By this, a thief of precious metals and a dealer in counterfeit gold are explained.

children.text:
KAZ04.4.23ab/ ārabdhāras tu hiṃsāyāṃ gūḍha.ājīvās trayodaśa /
KAZ04.4.23cd/ pravāsyā niṣkraya.arthaṃ vā dadyur doṣa.viśeṣataḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ04.4.23ab/ Thus, thirteen types of persons with secret criminal livelihoods who have begun acts of harm
KAZ04.4.23cd/ should be banished, or made to pay a ransom [proportionate to] the gravity of their offense.

children.text:
(ḍetection of criminals through secret agents in the disguise of holy men)
KAZ04.5.01/ sattri.prayogād ūrdhvaṃ siddha.vyañjanā māṇavān māṇava.vidyābhiḥ pralobhayeyuḥ, prasvāpana.antar.dhāna.dvāra.apoha.mantreṇa pratirodhakān, saṃvadana.mantreṇa pāratalpikān //
children.translated_text:
(Detection of criminals through secret agents in the disguise of holy men)
KAZ04.5.01/ After the deployment of classmate-spies, those in the guise of accomplished [ascetics] should entice young men with [promises of] magical powers: would-be burglars with the spell for inducing sleep, invisibility, and opening doors; would-be adulterers with the love-charm.

children.text: KAZ04.5.02/ teṣāṃ kṛta.utsāhānāṃ mahāntaṃ saṃgham ādāya rātrāv anyaṃ grāmam uddiśya^anyaṃ grāmaṃ kṛtaka.strī.puruṣaṃ gatvā brūyuḥ - "iha^eva vidyā.prabhāvo dṛśyatāṃ, kṛcchraḥ para.grāmo gantum" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.02/ When they have become eager, [the agents] should take a large group and, by night, setting out ostensibly for one village, go to another village [equipped with] fake men and women, and say: 'Let the power of the magical art be demonstrated right here; it is difficult to go to the other village.'

children.text: KAZ04.5.03/ tato dvāra.apoha.mantreṇa dvārāṇy apohya "praviśyatām" iti brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.03/ Then, with the door-opening spell, they should open the doors and say: 'Enter.'

children.text: KAZ04.5.04/ antar.dhāna.mantreṇa jāgratām ārakṣiṇāṃ madhyena māṇavān atikrāmayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.04/ With the invisibility spell, they should lead the young men through the midst of [seemingly] awake guards.

children.text: KAZ04.5.05/ prasvāpana.mantreṇa prasvāpayitvā rakṣiṇaḥ śayābhir māṇavaiḥ saṃcārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.05/ With the sleep-inducing spell, having [seemingly] put the guards to sleep, they should have the young men move about in their beds.

children.text: KAZ04.5.06/ saṃvadana.mantreṇa bhāryā.vyañjanāḥ pareṣāṃ māṇavaiḥ sammodayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.06/ With the love-charm, [women agents] disguised as wives should cause the young men to become intimate with the women of others.

children.text: KAZ04.5.07/ upalabdha.vidyā.prabhāvāṇāṃ puraścaraṇā.ādy ādiśeyur abhijñāna.artham //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.07/ For those who have become convinced of the power of the magical arts, they should prescribe preliminary rituals (<s>puraścaraṇā</s>) and such, as an identifying mark.

children.text: KAZ04.5.08/ kṛta.lakṣaṇa.dravyeṣu vā veśmasu karma kārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.08/ Or they should have them perform the act in houses [stocked] with marked property.

children.text: KAZ04.5.09/ anupraviṣṭā vā^ekatra grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.09/ Or, having accompanied [them], they should have them arrested at a single location.

children.text: KAZ04.5.10/ kṛta.lakṣaṇa.dravya.kraya.vikraya.ādhāneṣu yoga.surā.mattān vā grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.10/ Or they should have them arrested while intoxicated with drugged liquor, at [locations with] marked goods — buying, selling, or pledging [them].

children.text: KAZ04.5.11/ gṛhītān pūrva.apadāna.sahāyān anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.11/ Once arrested, they should be interrogated about their previous crimes and accomplices.

children.text: KAZ04.5.12/ purāṇa.cora.vyañjanā vā corān anupraviṣṭās tathā^eva karma kārayeyur grāhayeyuś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.12/ Or those in the guise of reformed thieves should infiltrate [actual] thieves, have them perform [criminal] acts likewise, and then have them arrested.

children.text: KAZ04.5.13/ gṛhītān samāhartā paura.jānapadānāṃ darśayet - "cora.grahaṇīṃ vidyām adhīte rājā, tasya^upadeśād ime corā gṛhītāḥ, bhūyaś ca grahīṣyāmi, vārayitavyo vaḥ sva.janaḥ pāpa.ācārah^" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.13/ The collector should display the arrested persons to the townspeople and countryfolk: 'The king is studying the art of thief-catching; by his instruction these thieves have been caught, and more will be caught. Restrain your own people from criminal conduct.'

children.text: KAZ04.5.14/ yaṃ ca^atra^apasarpa.upadeśena śamyā.pratoda.ādīnām apahartāraṃ jānīyāt tam eṣāṃ pratyādiśet "eṣa rājñaḥ prabhāvaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.14/ And whoever is known through the intelligence of the roving agents to be a thief of goads, whips, and the like — he should be pointed out to them: 'This is the king's power.'

children.text: KAZ04.5.15/ purāṇa.cora.go.pālaka.vyādha.śva.gaṇinaś ca vana.cora.āṭavikān anupraviṣṭāḥ prabhūta.kūṭa.hiraṇya.kupya.bhāṇḍeṣu sārtha.vraja.grāmeṣv enān abhiyojayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.15/ And those in the guise of reformed thieves, cowherds, hunters, and dog-keepers should infiltrate forest robbers and tribal bandits, and draw them into [attacking] caravans, cattle camps, and villages that are richly stocked with marked counterfeit gold, raw materials, and goods.

children.text: KAZ04.5.16/ abhiyoge gūḍha.balair ghātayeyuḥ, madana.rasa.yuktena vā pathy.adanena //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.16/ When they attack, [the agents] should have them killed by concealed forces, or by poisoned food placed on the road.

children.text: KAZ04.5.17/ gṛhīta.loptra.bhārān āyata.gata.pariśrāntān prasvapataḥ prahavaṇeṣu yoga.surā.mattān vā grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.5.17/ Or they should have arrested those who have fallen asleep, exhausted from carrying heavy loads of plunder after a long journey, or who are intoxicated with drugged liquor at festivals.

children.text:
KAZ04.5.18ab/ pūrvavac ca gṛhītvā^enān samāhartā prarūpayet /
KAZ04.5.18cd/ sarvajña.khyāpanaṃ rājñaḥ kārayan rāṣṭra.vāsiṣu //E
children.translated_text: And having arrested them as before, the collector (<s>samāhartā</s>) should display [the criminals publicly], demonstrating the king's omniscience among the inhabitants of the countryside.

children.text:
(Arrest on suspicion, with the stolen article and by indications of the act)
KAZ04.6.01/ siddha.prayogād ūrdhvaṃ śaṅkā.rūpa.karma.abhigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Arrest on suspicion, with the stolen article and by indications of the act)
Beyond [the detection of] established [criminal] operations, [there is] arrest based on suspicion, [recovery of] the article, and [evidence of] the act.

children.text:
KAZ04.6.02a/ kṣīṇa.dāya.kuṭumbam, alpa.nirveśaṃ, viparīta.deśa.jāti.gotra.nāma.karma.apadeśaṃ, pracchanna.vṛtti.karmāṇaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02b/ māṃsa.surā.bhakṣya.bhojana.gandha.mālya.vastra.vibhūṣaṇeṣu prasaktam, ativyaya.kartāraṃ, puṃścalī.dyūta.śauṇḍikeṣu prasaktam,-
KAZ04.6.02c/ abhīkṣṇa.pravāsinam, avijñāta.sthāna.gamanam, ekānta.araṇya.niṣkuṭa.vikāla.cāriṇaṃ, pracchanne sa.āmiṣe vā deśe bahu.mantra.saṃnipātaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02d/ sadyaḥ.kṣata.vraṇānāṃ gūḍha.pratīkāra.kārayitāram, antar.gṛha.nityam, abhyadhigantāraṃ, kāntā.paraṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02e/ para.parigrahāṇāṃ para.strī.dravya.veśmanām abhīkṣṇa.praṣṭāraṃ, kutsita.karma.śāstra.upakaraṇa.saṃsargaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02f/ virātre channa.kuḍyac.chāyā.saṃcāriṇaṃ, virūpa.dravyāṇām adeśa.kāla.vikretāraṃ, jāta.vairaśayaṃ, hīna.karma.jātiṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02g/ vigūhamāna.rūpaṃ, liṅgena^āliṅginaṃ, liṅginaṃ vā bhinna.ācāraṃ, pūrva.kṛta.apadānaṃ, sva.karmabhir apadiṣṭaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02h/ nāgarika.mahā.mātra.darśane guhamānam apasarantam anucchvāsa.upaveśinam āvignaṃ śuṣka.bhinna.svara.mukha.varṇaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.02i/ śastra.hasta.manuṣya.sampāta.trāsinaṃ, hiṃsra.stena.nidhi.nikṣepa.apahāra.para.prayoga.gūḍha.ājīvinām anyatamaṃ śaṅketa // iti śaṅkā.abhigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: One whose inheritance and household are depleted; who has meager resources; who falsely represents his place, caste, lineage, name, or occupation; who conceals his livelihood or activities; who is addicted to meat, liquor, delicacies, food, perfumes, garlands, clothes, and ornaments; who spends extravagantly; who is addicted to courtesans, gambling, and taverns; who travels frequently; who goes to unknown places; who frequents lonely spots, forests, or gardens at untimely hours; who holds many secret meetings in concealed or [otherwise] suspicious places; who secretly arranges treatment for fresh wounds and injuries; who is constantly indoors; who has unexplained acquisitions; who is excessively devoted to women; who frequently inquires about others' possessions — their women, wealth, and houses; who associates with wicked crafts, instruments, and treatises; who moves about at dead of night in the shadows of walls and coverings; who sells unfamiliar goods at improper places and times; who harbors a grudge; who is of low occupation and birth; who conceals his appearance; who wears a disguise or is disguised by [religious] marks; or who, though wearing [religious] marks, deviates in conduct; who has a prior criminal record; who is denounced by his own associates; who hides or retreats upon seeing the city-superintendent or high officials; who sits restlessly without breathing [easily]; who is agitated; whose voice, face, and complexion are dry and distressed; who is fearful at the sight of armed men or large assemblies — he should be suspected as one among those who live by violence, theft, treasure-hunting, misappropriating deposits, acting on behalf of enemies, or secret occupations. This is arrest on suspicion.

children.text: KAZ04.6.03/ rūpa.abhigrahas tu - naṣṭa.apahṛtam avidyamānaṃ taj.jāta.vyavahāriṣu nivedayet //
children.translated_text: Arrest based on [recovery of] the article: one should report lost or stolen [property that is] unaccounted for among those dealing in similar goods.

children.text: KAZ04.6.04/ tac cen niveditam āsādya pracchādayeyuḥ sācivya.kara.doṣam āpnuyuḥ //04.6.05/ ajānanto^asya dravyasya^atisargeṇa mucyeran //
children.translated_text: If, upon finding the reported [item], they conceal it, they incur the guilt of being an accessory. But if they do not recognize the item, they should be freed upon surrendering it.

children.text: KAZ04.6.06/ na ca^anivedya saṃsthā.adhyakṣasya purāṇa.bhāṇḍānām ādhānaṃ vikrayaṃ vā kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: And they should not, without reporting to the superintendent of the market, pledge or sell old goods.

children.text: KAZ04.6.07/ tac cen niveditam āsādyeta, rūpa.abhigṛhītam āgamaṃ pṛcchet "kutas te labdham" iti //
children.translated_text: If, upon finding a reported [item], one is arrested with the article, he should be asked about its provenance: 'How did you obtain this?'

children.text: KAZ04.6.08/ sa cet brūyāt "dāyādyād avāptam, amuṣmāl labdhaṃ krītaṃ kāritam ādhi.pracchannam, ayam asya deśaḥ kālaś ca^upasamprāpteḥ, ayam asya^arghaḥ pramāṇaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ mūlyaṃ ca" iti, tasya^āgama.samādhau mucyeta //
children.translated_text: If he says: 'It was inherited, obtained from so-and-so, purchased, commissioned, pledged in trust — this is the place and time of its acquisition, this is its price, measure, mark, and value' — and if the provenance is verified, he should be released.

children.text: KAZ04.6.09/ nāṣṭikaś cet tad eva pratisaṃdadhyāt, yasyā pūrvo dīrghaś ca paribhogaḥ śucir vā deśas tasya dravyam iti vidyāt //
children.translated_text: If [both parties are] claimants, that very [article] should be restored [to the rightful owner]; one whose use of it is prior and longstanding, or whose claim is well-established — to him the property should be known [to belong].

children.text: KAZ04.6.10/ catuṣpada.dvipadānām api hi rūpa.liṅga.sāmānyaṃ bhavati, kim aṅga punar eka.yoni.dravya.kartṛ.prasūtānāṃ kupya.ābharaṇa.bhāṇḍānām iti //
children.translated_text: For even quadrupeds and bipeds may have similarities in appearance and marks — how much more so manufactured goods, ornaments, and vessels, which are produced from a single source by a single maker.

children.text: KAZ04.6.11/ sa ced brūyāt "yācitakam avakrītakam āhitakaṃ nikṣepam upanidhiṃ vaiyāvṛtya.karma vā^amuṣya" iti, tasya^apasāra.pratisaṃdhānena mucyeta //
children.translated_text: If he says: 'It was borrowed, taken on approval, pledged, a deposit, a sealed deposit, or commission work of so-and-so' — he should be freed upon verification of his denial [of ownership] by cross-checking.

children.text: KAZ04.6.12/ "na^evam" ity apasāro vā brūyāt, rūpa.abhigṛhītaḥ parasya dāna.kāraṇam ātmanaḥ pratigraha.kāraṇam upaliṅganaṃ vā dāyaka.dāpaka.nibandhaka.pratigrāhaka.upadraṣṭṛbhir upaśrotṛbhir vā pratisamānayet //
children.translated_text: If the denial says 'not so,' the one arrested with the article should establish the reason for the other's gift, the reason for his own receipt, or the circumstances — through the giver, the one who caused it to be given, the documenter, the receiver, the eyewitnesses, or the earwitnesses.

children.text: KAZ04.6.13/ ujjhita.pranaṣṭa.niṣpatita.upalabdhasya deśa.kāla.lābha.upaliṅganena śuddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: For something found that was abandoned, lost, or dropped — purification [is achieved] by establishing the circumstances of the place, time, and acquisition.

children.text: KAZ04.6.14/ aśuddhas tac ca tāvac ca daṇḍaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: One not purified [of suspicion] should pay a fine equal to that [value] plus an equivalent amount.

children.text:
KAZ04.6.15/ anyathā steya.daṇḍaṃ bhajeta // iti rūpa.abhigrahaḥ /
KAZ04.6.16/ karma.abhigrahas tu - muṣita.veśmanaḥ praveśa.niṣkasanam advāreṇa, dvārasya saṃdhinā bījena vā vedham, uttama.agārasya jāla.vāta.ayana.nīpra.vedham, ārohaṇa.avataraṇe ca kuḍyasya vedham, upakhananaṃ vā gūḍha.dravya.nikṣepaṇa.grahaṇa.upāyam, upadeśa.upalabhyam abhyantarac.cheda.utkara.parimarda.upakaraṇam abhyantara.kṛtaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text:
Otherwise, he incurs the theft penalty. This is arrest based on [recovery of] the article.
As for arrest based on [evidence of] the act: entry into and exit from a burgled house without [going through] the door; piercing the door through its joints or with a key; piercing the roof through its lattice, ventilation opening, or gutter; marks of climbing up and descending the wall; piercing or undermining [the wall]; methods for concealing, depositing, or seizing hidden goods; and tools for cutting, breaking, scraping, or opening found inside, detectable by their traces — this should be known as done from the inside.

children.text: KAZ04.6.17/ viparyaye bāhya.kṛtam, ubhayata ubhaya.kṛtam //
children.translated_text: In the reverse case, [it is known as] done from the outside; in both cases, done by both.

children.text:
KAZ04.6.18a/ abhyantara.kṛte puruṣam āsannaṃ vyasaninaṃ krūra.sahāyaṃ taskara.upakaraṇa.saṃsargaṃ, striyaṃ vā daridra.kulām anya.prasaktāṃ vā,-
KAZ04.6.18b/ paricāraka.janaṃ vā tad.vidha.ācāram, atisvapnaṃ, nidrā.klāntam, āvignaṃ. śuṣka.bhinna.svara.mukha.varṇam, anavasthitam,-
KAZ04.6.18c/ atipralāpinam, ucca.ārohaṇa.saṃrabdha.gātraṃ, vilūna.nighṛṣṭa.bhinna.pāṭita.śarīra.vastraṃ, jāta.kiṇa.saṃrabdha.hasta.pādaṃ,-
KAZ04.6.18d/ pāṃsu.pūrṇa.keśa.nakhaṃ vilūna.bhugna.keśa.nakhaṃ vā, samyak.snāta.anuliptaṃ taila.pramṛṣṭa.gātraṃ sadyo.dauta.hasta.pādaṃ vā,-
KAZ04.6.18e/ pāṃsu.picchileṣu tulya.pāda.pada.nikṣepaṃ, praveśa.niṣkasanayor vā tulya.mālya.madya.gandha.vastrac.cheda.vilepana.svedaṃ parīkṣeta //
children.translated_text: When done from the inside, one should [investigate]: a man who is near [the victim], addicted to vices, with cruel companions, and associated with thieves' tools; or a woman from a poor family or one attached to another [man]; or attendants of similar conduct — excessively sleepy, fatigued from sleep, agitated, with dry and distressed voice, face, and complexion, restless, excessively talkative, with limbs strained from climbing, with body or clothes torn, rubbed, cut, or ripped, with hands and feet calloused or strained; with hair and nails full of dust, or with hair and nails trimmed or broken; or one properly bathed and anointed, body wiped with oil, hands and feet freshly washed; matching footprints in dusty or slippery [surfaces]; or, at [the points of] entry and exit, matching garlands, liquor-smell, perfume, cloth-fragments, ointment, or sweat — these should be examined.

children.text: KAZ04.6.19/ coraṃ pāradārikaṃ vā vidyāt //
children.translated_text: He should be identified as a thief or an adulterer.

children.text:
KAZ04.6.20ab/ sagopa.sthāniko bāhyaṃ pradeṣṭā cora.mārgaṇam /
KAZ04.6.20cd/ kuryān nāgarikaś ca^antar.durge nirdiṣṭa.hetubhiḥ //E
children.translated_text: The informer, together with the village headman and district officer, should conduct the external search for the thief; and the city-superintendent [should conduct the search] inside the fort, using the indicators described.

children.text:
(Inquest of sudden deaths)
KAZ04.7.01/ taila.abhyaktam āśu.mṛtakaṃ parīkṣeta //
children.translated_text:
(Inquest of sudden deaths)
He should examine a body that has been oiled [i.e., treated for preservation] and that died suddenly.

children.text: KAZ04.7.02/ niṣkīrṇa.mūtra.purīṣaṃ vāta.pūrṇa.koṣṭha.tvakkaṃ śūna.pāda.pāṇimān mīlita.akṣaṃ savyañjana.kaṇṭhaṃ pīṭana.niruddha.ucchvāsa.hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One whose urine and excrement have been voided, whose abdomen and skin are inflated with air, whose feet and hands are swollen, whose eyes are shut, and whose throat shows [strangulation] marks — [this one] should be known as killed by strangulation, with breathing obstructed by pressing.

children.text: KAZ04.7.03/ tam eva saṃkucita.bāhu.sakthim udbandha.hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: The same, with arms and thighs contracted, should be known as killed by hanging.

children.text: KAZ04.7.04/ śūna.pāṇi.pāda.udaram apagata.akṣam udvṛtta.nābhim avaropitaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One whose hands, feet, and abdomen are swollen, whose eyes are protruding, and whose navel is distended — [this one] should be known as [someone who was hanged and then] taken down.

children.text: KAZ04.7.05/ nistabdha.guda.akṣaṃ saṃdaṣṭa.jihvam ādhmāta.udaram udaka.hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One whose anus and eyes are rigid, whose tongue is bitten, and whose abdomen is bloated should be known as killed by drowning.

children.text: KAZ04.7.06/ śoṇita.anusiktaṃ bhagna.bhinna.gātraṃ kāṣṭhair aśmabhir vā hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One drenched in blood with limbs broken or pierced should be known as killed by wooden clubs or stones.

children.text: KAZ04.7.07/ sambhagna.sphuṭita.gātram avakṣiptaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One with limbs crushed and shattered should be known as [killed by being] thrown [from a height].

children.text: KAZ04.7.08/ śyāva.pāṇi.pāda.danta.nakhaṃ śithila.māṃsa.roma.carmāṇaṃ phena.upadigdha.mukhaṃ viṣa.hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One whose hands, feet, teeth, and nails are dark-blue, whose flesh, hair, and skin are loose, and whose mouth is smeared with foam should be known as killed by poison.

children.text:
KAZ04.7.09/ tam eva sa-śoṇita.daṃśaṃ sarpa.kīṭa.hataṃ vidyāt /
KAZ04.7.10/ vikṣipta.vastra.gātram ativanta.viriktaṃ madana.yoga.hataṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text:
The same, with bloody bite-marks, should be known as killed by a snake or insect.
One with clothes and body in disarray, excessively purged through vomiting and diarrhea, should be known as killed by an intoxicating preparation.

children.text: KAZ04.7.11/ ato^anyatamena kāraṇena hataṃ hatvā vā daṇḍa.bhayād udbaddha.nikṛtta.kaṇṭhaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: One killed by any of these means, or having been killed [by some other means and then disguised] — out of fear of punishment, [found] with a noose tied or throat cut — should be identified [as such].

children.text: KAZ04.7.12/ viṣa.hatasya bhojana.śeṣaṃ vayobhiḥ parīkṣeta //
children.translated_text: The leftover food of one killed by poison should be tested on birds.

children.text: KAZ04.7.13/ hṛdayād uddhṛtya^agnau prakṣiptaṃ ciṭiciṭāyad.indra.dhanur.varṇaṃ vā viṣa.yuktaṃ vidyāt, dagdhasya hṛdayam adagdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vā //
children.translated_text: Or, having extracted [a sample] from the heart and thrown it into fire, if it crackles and shows rainbow colors, it should be known as poisoned; or upon seeing that the heart of the cremated [body] remains unburned.

children.text: KAZ04.7.14/ tasya paricāraka.janaṃ vāg.daṇḍa.pāruṣya.atilabdhaṃ mārgeta, duḥkha.upahatam anya.prasaktaṃ vā strī.janaṃ, dāya.vṛtti.strī.jana.abhimantāraṃ vā bandhum //
children.translated_text: One should search [among] the attendants — those who have suffered verbal abuse, physical punishment, or excessive exaction; women who are distressed or attached to another [man]; or a kinsman who covets the inheritance, livelihood, or women [of the deceased].

children.text: KAZ04.7.15/ tad eva hata.udbaddhasya parīkṣeta //
children.translated_text: The same [investigation] should be conducted for one who was killed and then hanged [to simulate suicide].

children.text: KAZ04.7.16/ svayam udbaddhasya vā viprakāram ayuktaṃ mārgeta //
children.translated_text: Or, for one who truly hanged himself, one should search for the provocation and the [underlying] cause.

children.text: KAZ04.7.17/ sarveṣāṃ vā strī.dāyādya.doṣaḥ karma.spardhā pratipakṣa.dveṣaḥ paṇya.saṃsthā.samavāyo vā vivāda.padānām anyatamad vā roṣa.sthānam //
children.translated_text: For all [cases], the motive may involve disputes over women, inheritance, faults, competition in work, hostility toward an adversary, or commercial or guild or partnership disputes — or any other ground for resentment.

children.text: KAZ04.7.18/ roṣa.nimitto ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text: Murder is motivated by resentment.

children.text: KAZ04.7.19/ svayaṃ.ādiṣṭa.puruṣair vā, corair artha.nimittaṃ, sādṛśyād anya.vairibhir vā hatasya ghātam āsannebhyaḥ parīkṣeta //
children.translated_text: Whether [the victim was killed] by his own [agents], by commissioned persons, by thieves for the sake of wealth, or by the enemies of another person on account of resemblance — [the investigators] should examine the murder through those nearby.

children.text: KAZ04.7.20/ yena^āhūtaḥ saha sthitaḥ prasthito hata.bhūmim ānīto vā tam anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text: The person who invited [the victim], who stood with him, who set out with him, or who brought him to the place of death — him they should interrogate.

children.text: KAZ04.7.21/ ye ca^asya hata.bhūmāv āsanna.carās tān eka.ekaśaḥ pṛcchet "kena^ayam iha^ānīto hato vā, kaḥ sa.śastraḥ saṃgūhamāna udvigno vā yuṣmābhir dṛṣṭaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And those who were moving about near the place of death — they should be questioned one by one: 'By whom was he brought here or killed? Who was seen by you with weapons, hiding, or agitated?'

children.text: KAZ04.7.22/ te yathā brūyus tathā^anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text: As they say, so should the [investigation] proceed.

children.text:
KAZ04.7.23ab/ anāthasya śarīra.stham upabhogaṃ paricchadam /
KAZ04.7.23cd/ vastraṃ veṣaṃ vibhūṣāṃ vā dṛṣṭvā tad.vyavahāriṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: Of an unknown [victim], [they should examine] the possessions on his body, his personal effects, his clothing, his attire, and his ornaments, and [question] those who deal in such [items].

children.text:
KAZ04.7.24ab/ anuyuñjīta saṃyogaṃ nivāsaṃ vāsa.kāraṇam /
KAZ04.7.24cd/ karma ca vyavahāraṃ ca tato mārgaṇam ācaret //
children.translated_text: They should investigate his connections, his residence, the reason for [his] stay, his occupation, and his transactions, and then conduct the search.

children.text:
KAZ04.7.25ab/ rajju.śastra.viṣair vā^api kāma.krodha.vaśena yaḥ /
KAZ04.7.25cd/ ghātayet svayam ātmānaṃ strī vā pāpena mohitā //
children.translated_text: One who kills himself — whether by rope, weapon, or poison, whether out of passion or anger, whether a man or a woman deluded by sin —

children.text:
KAZ04.7.26ab/ rajjunā rāja.mārge tāṃś caṇḍālena^apakarṣayet /
KAZ04.7.26cd/ na śmaśāna.vidhis teṣāṃ na sambandhi.kriyās tathā //
children.translated_text: them a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> should drag along the royal road with a rope. There is no cremation-ground rite for them, nor the customary rites of kinship.

children.text:
KAZ04.7.27ab/ bandhus teṣāṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt preta.kārya.kriyā.vidhim /
KAZ04.7.27cd/ tad.gatiṃ sa caret paścāt sva.janād vā pramucyate //
children.translated_text: But a kinsman who performs the funeral rites for them shall afterward follow their fate, or be cast out from his own people.

children.text:
KAZ04.7.28ab/ saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena samācaran /
KAZ04.7.28cd/ yājana.adhyāpanād yaunāt taiś ca^anyo^api samācaran //E
children.translated_text: By [the lapse of] one year, [the kinsman who performed the rites] falls [from caste]; one who associates with a fallen [person also] falls; [this applies to those who associate] through officiating, teaching, or marriage — and through them, yet another who associates [also falls].

children.text:
(Investigation through interrogation and through torture)
KAZ04.8.01/ muṣita.saṃnidhau bāhyānām abhyantarāṇāṃ ca sākṣiṇām abhiśastasya deśa.jāti.gotra.nāma.karma.sāra.sahāya.nivāsān anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text:
(Investigation through interrogation and through torture)
In the presence of the stolen [article], [the investigators] should interrogate the accused regarding the place, caste, lineage, name, occupation, resources, companions, and residence — [doing so] before both external and internal witnesses.

children.text: KAZ04.8.02/ tāṃś ca^apadeśaiḥ pratisamānayet //
children.translated_text: And they should verify these by cross-checking with [other] evidence.

children.text: KAZ04.8.03/ tataḥ pūrvasya^ahnaḥ pracāraṃ rātrau nivāsaṃ ca<cā> grahaṇād ity anuyuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Then they should interrogate [him regarding] his movements on the previous day and his lodging at night, up to [the time of] arrest.

children.text: KAZ04.8.04/ tasya^apasāra.pratisaṃdhāne śuddhaḥ syāt, anyathā karma.prāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: If his denial is verified by cross-checking, he is cleared; otherwise, he is implicated by the act.

children.text: KAZ04.8.05/ tri.rātrād ūrdhvam agrāhyaḥ śaṅkitakaḥ pṛcchā.abhāvād anyatra^upakaraṇa.darśanāt //
children.translated_text: After three nights, a suspect should not be held without grounds for questioning, unless implements [of the crime] are found.

children.text: KAZ04.8.06/ acoraṃ cora ity abhivyāharataś cora.samo daṇḍaḥ, coraṃ pracchādayataś ca //
children.translated_text: For one who calls a non-thief a thief, the punishment is equal to that for a thief; likewise for one who shelters a thief.

children.text: KAZ04.8.07/ coreṇa^abhiśasto vaira.dveṣābhyām apadiṣṭakaḥ śuddhaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: One accused by a thief but shown [to be accused] out of enmity or hatred is cleared.

children.text: KAZ04.8.08/ śuddhaṃ parivāsayataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who detains an innocent person, the lowest <s>sāhasa</s> penalty [applies].

children.text: KAZ04.8.09/ śaṅkā.niṣpannam upakaraṇa.mantri.sahāya.rūpa.vaiyāvṛtya.karān niṣpādayet //
children.translated_text: For one [whose guilt] is established by suspicion, he should bring forth the accomplices in tools, counsel, companions, [matching] appearance, and commissioned work.

children.text: KAZ04.8.10/ karmaṇaś ca pradeśa.dravya.ādāna.aṃśa.vibhāgaiḥ pratisamānayet //
children.translated_text: And regarding the act, he should verify [the accused's account] through [evidence of] the location, the goods taken, the shares, and the division [of spoils].

children.text: KAZ04.8.11/ eteṣāṃ kāraṇānām anabhisaṃdhāne vipralapantam acoraṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: When these elements cannot be corroborated, one who babbles should be known as a non-thief.

children.text: KAZ04.8.12/ dṛśyate hy acoro^api cora.mārge yadṛcchayā saṃnipāte cora.veṣa.śastra.bhāṇḍa.sāmānyena gṛhyamāṇaś cora.bhāṇḍasya^upavāsena vā, yathā^aṇi.māṇḍavyaḥ karma.kleśa.bhayād acoraḥ "coro^asmi" iti bruvāṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: For even an innocent person may be found on a thief's path by chance, caught at a gathering by similarity of thief's attire, weapons, and goods, or by proximity to stolen goods — just as <s>Aṇi-Māṇḍavya</s>, an innocent man, said 'I am a thief' out of fear of the ordeal of torture.

children.text: KAZ04.8.13/ tasmāt samāpta.karaṇaṃ niyamayet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should convict only when the case is complete.

children.text: KAZ04.8.14/ manda.aparādhaṃ bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ vyādhitaṃ mattam unmattaṃ kṣut.pipāsā.adhva.klāntam atyāśitam āmaka.aśitaṃ durbalaṃ vā na karma kārayet //
children.translated_text: One of minor offense, a child, an old person, one who is sick, intoxicated, insane, exhausted by hunger, thirst, or travel, one who has overeaten, eaten raw food, or is weak — should not be subjected to torture.

children.text: KAZ04.8.15/ tulya śīla.puṃścalī.prāpāvika.kathā.avakāśa.bhojana.dātṛbhir apasarpayet //
children.translated_text: He should deploy [agents] of similar character, [or] through prostitutes, those who prepare food, storytellers, those who provide space, or those who provide meals.

children.text: KAZ04.8.16/ evam atisaṃdadhyāt, yathā vā nikṣepa.apahāre vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: Thus he should entrap [the suspect], or as explained in [the section on] theft of deposits.

children.text: KAZ04.8.17/ āpta.doṣaṃ karma kārayet, na tv eva striyaṃ garbhiṇīṃ sūtikāṃ vā māsa.avara.prajātām //
children.translated_text: One whose guilt has been established should be subjected to torture — but never a pregnant woman or a woman who has recently given birth within [the last] month.

children.text: KAZ04.8.18/ striyās tv ardha.karma, vākya.anuyogo vā //
children.translated_text: For a woman — half the [degree of] torture, or questioning by words [alone].

children.text: KAZ04.8.19/ brāhmaṇasya sattri.parigrahaḥ śrutavatas tapasvinaś ca //
children.translated_text: For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [there should be] the custody of a secret agent — [likewise for one] who is learned and an ascetic.

children.text: KAZ04.8.20/ tasya^atikrama uttamo daṇḍaḥ kartuḥ kārayituś ca, karmaṇā vyāpādanena ca //
children.translated_text: For transgressing that — the highest fine for both the one who does it and the one who orders it, and [likewise] for [causing] death through torture.

children.text: KAZ04.8.21/ vyāvahārikaṃ karma.catuṣkaṃ - ṣaḍ daṇḍāḥ, sapta kaśāḥ, dvāv upari.nibandhau, udaka.nālikā ca //
children.translated_text: The standard set of judicial tortures is four: six blows with a stick, seven lashes with a whip, two suspensions by the arms, and one water-tube [treatment].

children.text: KAZ04.8.22/ paraṃ pāpa.karmaṇāṃ nava vetra.latāḥ, dvādaśa kaśāḥ, dvāv ūru.veṣṭau, viṃśatir nakta.māla.latāḥ, dvātriṃśat.talāḥ, dvau vṛścika.bandhau, ullaṃbane ca dve, sūcī hastasya, yavāgū.pītasya eka.parva.dahanam aṅgulyāḥ, sneha.pītasya pratāpanam ekam ahaḥ, śiśira.rātrau balbaja.agra.śayyā ca //
children.translated_text: Beyond that, for heinous criminals: nine strikes with a cane, twelve lashes, two thigh-bindings, twenty strikes with a <s>naktamāla</s> vine, thirty-two slaps, two scorpion-bindings, two hangings [upside-down], a needle [inserted into] the hand, and for one who has drunk gruel — burning of one joint of a finger; for one who has drunk oil — one day of exposure to heat; and on a cold night — a bed on the tips of <s>balbaja</s> grass.

children.text: KAZ04.8.23/ ity aṣṭādaśakaṃ karma //
children.translated_text: This is the set of eighteen [tortures].

children.text: KAZ04.8.24/ tasya.upakaraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ praharaṇaṃ pradharaṇam avadhāraṇaṃ ca khara.paṭṭād āgamayet //
children.translated_text: The equipment, the measure, the [mode of] striking, the [mode of] holding, and the [method of] ascertaining — he should learn from the donkey-tablet [register of regulations].

children.text: KAZ04.8.25/ divasa.antaram eka.ekaṃ ca karma kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should administer one torture at a time on alternate days.

children.text: KAZ04.8.26/ pūrva.kṛta.apadānaṃ pratijñāya^apaharantam eka.deśa.dṛṣṭa.dravyaṃ karmaṇā rūpeṇa vā gṛhītaṃ rāja.kośam avastṛṇantaṃ karma.vadhyaṃ vā rāja.vacanāt samastaṃ vyastam abhyastaṃ vā karma kārayet //
children.translated_text: For one who confesses to previously committed crimes and then steals again, for one found with some of the stolen goods, for one caught in the act or by description, for one who squanders the royal treasury, or one condemned to death by labor — by the king's order, the [full] set of tortures should be administered all together, separately, or repeatedly.

children.text: KAZ04.8.27/ sarva.aparādheṣv apīḍanīyo brāhmaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: In all offenses, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is not to be subjected to physical [torture].

children.text: KAZ04.8.28/ tasya^abhiśasta.aṅko lalāṭe syād vyavahāra.patanāya, steyo śvā, manuṣya.vadhe kabandhaḥ, guru.talpe bhagam, surā.pāne madya.dhvajaḥ //
children.translated_text: His punishment-brand on the forehead should indicate the offense for [the purpose of] social exclusion: for theft, [the mark of] a dog; for killing a human, a headless torso; for violating the teacher's bed, a female organ; for drinking liquor, a tavern sign.

children.text:
KAZ04.8.29ab/ brāhmaṇaṃ pāpa.karmāṇam udghuṣya^aṅka.kṛta.vraṇam /
KAZ04.8.29cd/ kuryān nirviṣayaṃ rājā vāsayed ākareṣu vā //E
children.translated_text:
Having publicly denounced a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of evil conduct and branded him with a scar,
the king should banish him from the kingdom, or settle him in the mines.

children.text:
(Keeping a watch over officers of all departments)
KAZ04.9.01/ samāhartṛ.pradeṣṭāraḥ pūrvam adhyakṣāṇām adhyakṣa.puruṣāṇāṃ ca niyamanaṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Keeping a watch over officers of all departments)
The collector and the judges should first regulate the superintendents and the officials of the superintendents.

children.text: KAZ04.9.02/ khani.sāra.karma.antebhyaḥ sāraṃ ratnaṃ vā^apaharataḥ śuddha.vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who steals valuable goods or precious stones from mining and manufacturing operations — execution by purification [i.e., capital punishment].

children.text: KAZ04.9.03/ phalgu.dravya.karma.antebhyaḥ phalgu dravyam upaskaraṃ vā pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For [one who steals] inferior goods or equipment from operations involving inferior commodities — the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text:
KAZ04.9.04/ paṇya.bhūmibhyo vā rāja.paṇyaṃ māṣa.mūlyād ūrdhvam āpāda.mūlyād ity apaharato dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, ā.dvi.pāda.mūlyād iti catur.viṃśati.paṇaḥ, ā.tri.pāda.mūlyād iti ṣaṭ.triṃśat.paṇaḥ, ā.paṇa.mūlyād ity aṣṭa.catvāriṃśat.paṇaḥ, ā.dvi.paṇa.mūlyād iti pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, ā.catuṣpaṇa.mūlyād iti madhyamaḥ, ā.aṣṭa.paṇa.mūlyād ity uttamaḥ, ā.daśa.paṇa.mūlyād
iti vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text:
Or from commodity depots — for stealing royal merchandise worth from one <s>māṣa</s> up to one-quarter <s>paṇa</s>, a fine of twelve <s>paṇas</s>; up to half a <s>paṇa</s>, twenty-four <s>paṇas</s>; up to three-quarters of a <s>paṇa</s>, thirty-six <s>paṇas</s>; up to one <s>paṇa</s>, forty-eight <s>paṇas</s>; up to two <s>paṇas</s>, the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine; up to four <s>paṇas</s>, the middle; up to eight <s>paṇas</s>, the highest;
up to ten <s>paṇas</s>, death.

children.text: KAZ04.9.05/ koṣṭha.paṇya.kupya.āyudha.agārebhyaḥ kupya.bhāṇḍa.upaskara.apahāreṣv ardha.mūlyeṣu eta eva daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: From granaries, commodity stores, raw material stores, and armories — for thefts of raw materials, goods, or equipment at half the [above] values, these same fines [apply].

children.text: KAZ04.9.06/ kośa.bhāṇḍa.agāra.akṣa.śālābhyaś catur.bhāga.mūlyeṣu eta eva dvi.guṇā daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: From the treasury, the vessel-stores, and the assay office — at one-quarter the [above] values, these same fines doubled.

children.text: KAZ04.9.07/ corāṇām abhipradharṣaṇe citro ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text: For thieves who commit armed robbery — varied forms of capital punishment.

children.text: KAZ04.9.08/ iti rāja.parigraheṣu vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: Thus is explained [the procedure] for royal property.

children.text:
KAZ04.9.09/ bāhyeṣu tu - pracchannam ahani kṣetra.khala.veśma.āpaṇebhyaḥ kupya.bhāṇḍam upaskaraṃ vā māṣa.mūlyād ūrdhvam ā.pāda.mūlyād ity apaharatas tri.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, gomaya.pradehena vā pralipya^avaghoṣaṇam^ ā.dvi.pāda.mūlyād iti ṣaṭ.paṇaḥ, gomaya.bhasmanā vā pralipya^avaghoṣaṇam, ā.tri.pāda.mūlyād iti nava.paṇaḥ, gomaya.bhasmanā vā pralipya^avaghoṣaṇam,
śarāva.mekhalayā vā^ ā.paṇa.mūlyād iti dvādaśa.paṇaḥ, muṇḍanaṃ pravrājanaṃ vā^ ā.dvi.paṇa.mūlyād iti catur.viṃśati.paṇaḥ, muṇḍasya^iṣṭakā.śakalena pravrājanaṃ vā^ ā.catuṣ.paṇa.mūlyād iti ṣaṭ.triṃśat.paṇah^ ā.pañca.paṇa.mūlyād
ity aṣṭa.catvāriṃśat.paṇaḥ, ā.daśa.paṇa.mūlyād iti pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍah^ ā.viṃśati.paṇa.mūlyād it dviśatah^ ā.triṃśat.paṇa.mūlyād iti pañca.śatah^ ā.catvāriṃśat.paṇa.mūlyād iti sāhasrah^ ā.pañcāśat.paṇa.mūlyād iti vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text:
For private [property], however: for one who secretly steals by day from fields, threshing floors, houses, or shops — raw materials, goods, or equipment worth from one <s>māṣa</s> up to one-quarter <s>paṇa</s>, a fine of three <s>paṇas</s>; or smearing with cow-dung and public denunciation; up to half a <s>paṇa</s>, six <s>paṇas</s>; or smearing with cow-dung ash and public denunciation; up to three-quarters of a <s>paṇa</s>, nine <s>paṇas</s>; or smearing with cow-dung ash and public denunciation,
or wearing a shard-girdle; up to one <s>paṇa</s>, twelve <s>paṇas</s>; or head-shaving or banishment; up to two <s>paṇas</s>, twenty-four <s>paṇas</s>; or for one already shaven, banishment carrying a potsherd; up to four <s>paṇas</s>, thirty-six <s>paṇas</s>; up to five <s>paṇas</s>,
forty-eight <s>paṇas</s>; up to ten <s>paṇas</s>, the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine; up to twenty <s>paṇas</s>, two hundred; up to thirty <s>paṇas</s>, five hundred; up to forty <s>paṇas</s>, one thousand; up to fifty <s>paṇas</s>, death.

children.text: KAZ04.9.10/ prasahya divā rātrau vā^āntaryāmikam apaharato^ardha.mūlyeṣu eta eva daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who steals by force, day or night, from inside [a dwelling] — at half the [above] values, these same fines [apply].

children.text: KAZ04.9.11/ prasahya divā rātrau vā sa-śastrasya^apaharataś catur.bhāga.mūlyeṣu eta eva dvi.guṇā daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who steals by force, day or night, while armed — at one-quarter the [above] values, these same fines doubled.

children.text: KAZ04.9.12/ kuṭuṃbika.adhyakṣa.mukhya.svāmināṃ kūṭa.śāsana.mudrā.karmasu pūrva.madhya.uttama.vadhā daṇḍāḥ, yathā.aparādhaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: For householders, superintendents, chiefs, and masters [who engage in] forgery of edicts or seals — the first, middle, highest, and capital punishments, or according to the offense.

children.text: KAZ04.9.13/ dharmasthaś ced vivadamānaṃ puruṣaṃ tarjayati bhartsayaty apasārayaty abhigrasate vā pūrvam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt, vāk.pāruṣye dvi.guṇam //
children.translated_text: If a judicial officer threatens, reviles, dismisses, or overcharges a person in litigation — he should impose the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine on him; for verbal abuse, double.

children.text: KAZ04.9.14/ pṛcchyaṃ na pṛcchati, apṛcchyaṃ pṛcchati, pṛṣṭvā vā visṛjati, śikṣayati, smārayati, pūrvaṃ dadāti vā, iti madhyamam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: If he does not question what should be questioned, questions what should not be questioned, or having questioned then dismisses, coaches, reminds, or gives [the answer] first — he should impose the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine on him.

children.text: KAZ04.9.15/ deyaṃ deśaṃ na pṛcchati, adeyaṃ deśaṃ pṛcchati, kāryam adeśena^ativāhayati, chalena^atiharati, kāla.haraṇena śrāntam apavāhayati, mārga.āpannaṃ vākyam utkramayati, mati.sāhāyyaṃ sākṣibhyo dadāti, tārita.anuśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ punar api gṛhṇāti, uttamam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: If he does not inquire into what should be decided, inquires into what need not be decided, delays a case without reason, dismisses it by trickery, wears down a litigant by prolonging the time, diverts a case already on track from its proper course, provides intellectual assistance to witnesses, or re-opens a case already decided and closed — he should impose the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine on him.

children.text: KAZ04.9.16/ punar.aparādhe dvi.guṇaṃ sthānād vyavaropaṇaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: For a repeated offense, double [the fine] and removal from office.

children.text: KAZ04.9.17/ lekhakaś ced uktaṃ na likhati, anuktaṃ likhati, duruktam upalikhati, sūktam ullikhati, artha.utpattiṃ vā vikalpayati, iti pūrvam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryād, yathā.aparādhaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: If a scribe does not write what is stated, writes what is not stated, corrects what is incorrectly stated, erases what is correctly stated, or distorts the import of the matter — he should impose the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine on him, or [a penalty] according to the offense.

children.text: KAZ04.9.18/ dharmasthaḥ pradeṣṭā vā hairaṇya.daṇḍam adaṇḍye kṣipati kṣepa.dvi.guṇam asmai daṇḍaṃ kuryāt, hīna.atirikta.aṣṭa.guṇaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: If a judicial officer or judge imposes a monetary penalty on one who is not to be penalized — he should impose on him a fine double the [wrongful] imposition; or eightfold [the difference] for a deficient or excessive [penalty].

children.text: KAZ04.9.19/ śarīra.daṇḍaṃ kṣipati śārīram eva daṇḍaṃ bhajeta, niṣkraya.dvi.guṇaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: If he imposes corporal punishment — he himself should receive the same corporal punishment, or pay double the ransom.

children.text: KAZ04.9.20/ yaṃ vā bhūtam arthaṃ nāśayati abhūtam arthaṃ karoti tad.aṣṭa.guṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Or if he destroys an existing case or fabricates a non-existent case — he should pay a fine of eight times that [amount].

children.text: KAZ04.9.21/ dharmasthīye cārake bandhana.agāre vā śayyā.āsana.bhojana.uccāra.saṃcāra.rodha.bandhaneṣu tri.paṇa.uttarā daṇḍāḥ kartuḥ kārayituś ca //
children.translated_text: In a judicial tribunal, an investigation cell, or a prison, for obstructing sleeping, sitting, eating, defecation, movement, release, or imprisonment — fines increasing by three <s>paṇas</s> for each [violation], for both the doer and the one who orders it.

children.text: KAZ04.9.22/ cārakād abhiyuktaṃ muñcato niṣpātayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, abhiyoga.dānaṃ ca, bandhana.agārāt sarva.svaṃ vadhaś ca //
children.translated_text: For one who releases or lets escape a person charged with an offense from the investigation cell — the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine and [liability for] the charge; from the prison — [confiscation of] all property and death.

children.text: KAZ04.9.23/ bandhana.agāra.adhyakṣasya saṃruddhakam anākhyāya cārayataś catur.viṃśati.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, karma kārayato dvi.guṇaḥ, sthāna.anyatvaṃ gamayato^anna.pānaṃ vā rundhataḥ ṣaṇ.ṇavatir daṇḍaḥ, parikleśayata utkoṭayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, ghnataḥ sāhasraḥ //
children.translated_text: For the prison superintendent who, without reporting a prisoner, makes him work — a fine of twenty-four <s>paṇas</s>; for making him do labor, double; for transferring him to another place or withholding food and drink — a fine of ninety-six; for tormenting or extorting him — the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for killing [a prisoner] — one thousand.

children.text: KAZ04.9.24/ parigṛhītāṃ dāsīm āhitikāṃ vā saṃruddhikām adhicarataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, cora.ḍāmarika.bhāryāṃ madhyamaḥ, saṃruddhikām āryām uttamaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who sexually violates a captured slave-woman or a bonded female prisoner — the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine; [for violating] the wife of a thief or a rebel — the middle; [for violating] a respectable imprisoned woman — the highest.

children.text: KAZ04.9.25/ saṃruddhasya vā tatra^eva ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, for [the violation of] a prisoner's [wife] in the same [prison] — death.

children.text: KAZ04.9.26/ tad eva^akṣaṇa.gṛhītāyām āryāyāṃ vidyāt, dāsyāṃ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: The same should be understood for a respectable woman not in custody; for a slave-woman — the first level of <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: KAZ04.9.27/ cārakam abhittvā niṣpātayato madhyamaḥ, bhittvā vadhaḥ, bandhana.agārāt sarva.svaṃ vadhaś ca //
children.translated_text: For one who lets escape [a prisoner] from the investigation cell without breaking [it open] — the middle [fine]; for breaking [it open] — death; from the prison — [confiscation of] all property and death.

children.text:
KAZ04.9.28ab/ evam artha.carān pūrvaṃ rājā daṇḍena śodhayet /
KAZ04.9.28cd/ śodhayeyuś ca śuddhās te paura.jānapadān damaiḥ //E
children.translated_text:
Thus should the king first purify with punishment those who handle his affairs;
and they, once purified, should restrain the townspeople and countryfolk with punishments.

children.text:
(ṛedemption from the cutting of individual limbs)
KAZ04.10.01/ tīrtha.ghāta.granthi.bheda.ūrdhva.karāṇāṃ prathame^aparādhe saṃdeśac.chedanaṃ catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo vā daṇḍaḥ, dvitīye chedanaṃ paṇasya śatyo vā daṇḍaḥ, tṛtīye dakṣiṇa.hasta.vadhaś catuḥ.śato vā daṇḍaḥ, caturthe yathā.kāmī vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Redemption from the cutting of individual limbs)
For pickpockets, those who cut purse-strings, and those who snatch with raised hands — on the first offense, cutting off [the tips of] the fingers or a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>; on the second, cutting off [the fingers] or a fine of one hundred; on the third, cutting off the right hand or a fine of four hundred; on the fourth, death at [the king's] discretion.

children.text: KAZ04.10.02/ pañca.viṃśati.paṇa.avareṣu kukkuṭa.nakula.mārjāra.śva.sūkara.steyeṣu hiṃsāyāṃ vā catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, nāsa.agrac.chedanaṃ vā^ caṇḍāla.araṇya.carāṇām ardha.daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: For the theft of [items] worth up to twenty-five <s>paṇas</s> — chickens, mongooses, cats, dogs, or pigs — or for harming [them], a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>, or cutting off the tip of the nose; for <s>Caṇḍālas</s> and forest-dwellers, half the fine.

children.text: KAZ04.10.03/ pāśa.jāla.kūṭa.avapāteṣu baddhānāṃ mṛga.paśu.pakṣi.vyāla.matsyānām ādāne tac ca tāvac ca daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For taking animals or birds, wild beasts, serpents, and fish caught in snares, nets, traps, or pitfalls — a fine equal to [the value of the catch] and the same again.

children.text: KAZ04.10.04/ mṛga.dravya.vanān mṛga.dravya.apahāre śātyo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For stealing wild animals or forest products from a game and product reserve — a fine of one hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.05/ biṃba.vihāra.mṛga.pakṣi.steye hiṃsāyāṃ vā dvi.guṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For stealing or harming images, pleasure animals, birds — double the fine.

children.text: KAZ04.10.06/ kāru.śilpi.kuśīlava.tapasvināṃ kṣudraka.dravya.apahāre śatyo daṇḍaḥ, sthūlaka.dravya.apahāre dvi.śataḥ, kṛṣi.dravya.apahāre ca //
children.translated_text: For stealing small articles from artisans, craftsmen, entertainers, and ascetics — a fine of one hundred; for stealing large articles — two hundred; and for stealing agricultural implements.

children.text: KAZ04.10.07/ durgam akṛta.praveśasya praviśataḥ prākārac.chidrād vā nikṣepaṃ gṛhītvā^apasarataḥ kāṇḍarā.vadho, dvi.śāto vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who enters a fort without an entry-permit, or who escapes through a breach in the rampart carrying stolen goods — execution by impalement (<s>kāṇḍaravadha</s>), or a fine of two hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.08/ cakra.yuktaṃ nāvaṃ kṣudra.paśuṃ vā^apaharata eka.pāda.vadhaḥ, tri.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who steals a wheeled [vehicle], a boat, or a small animal — cutting off one foot, or a fine of three hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.09/ kūṭa.kākaṇy.akṣa.arālā.śalākā.hasta.viṣama.kāriṇa eka.hasta.vadhaḥ, catuḥ.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For those who practice fraud with false <s>kākaṇī</s> [coins], dice, counters, gaming sticks, or cheating at hand — cutting off one hand, or a fine of four hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.10/ stena.pāradārikayoḥ sācivya.karmaṇi striyāḥ saṃgṛhītāyāś ca karṇa.nāsāc.chedanam, pañca.śato vā daṇḍaḥ, puṃṣo dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a woman who assists in theft or adultery, and for a woman who has been seized [in the act] — cutting off the ears and nose, or a fine of five hundred; for a man, double.

children.text: KAZ04.10.11/ mahā.paśum ekaṃ dāsaṃ dāsīṃ vā^apaharataḥ preta.bhāṇḍaṃ vā vikrīṇānasya dvi.pāda.vadhaḥ, ṣaṭ.chato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who steals a single large animal, a male or female slave, or sells funeral goods — cutting off both feet, or a fine of six hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.12/ varṇa.uttamānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca hasta.pāda.laṅghane rāja.yāna.vāhana.ādy.ārohaṇe ca^eka.hasta.pāda.vadhaḥ, sapta.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For stepping over the hands or feet of persons of the highest caste or of elders, or for mounting the king's conveyance, vehicle, or the like — cutting off one hand and one foot, or a fine of seven hundred.

children.text: KAZ04.10.13/ śūdrasya brāhmaṇa.vādino deva.dravyam avastṛṇato rāja.dviṣṭam ādiśato dvi.netra.bhedinaś ca yoga.añjanena^andhatvam, aṣṭa.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdra</s> who claims to be a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, who lies on a deity's property, who points out [those disliked by] the king, or who blinds both eyes [of another] with a magical ointment — blinding; or a fine of eight hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.10.14/ coraṃ pāradārikaṃ vā mokṣayato rāja.śāsanam ūnam atiriktaṃ vā likhataḥ kanyāṃ dāsīṃ vā sa-hiraṇyam aparahataḥ kūṭa.vyavahāriṇo vimāṃsa.vikrayiṇaś ca vāma.hasta.dvi.pāda.vadho, nava.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who releases a thief or an adulterer; who writes a royal edict with less or more [than what was authorized]; who deflowers a maiden or a slave-girl without paying gold; for a fraudulent trader; and for one who sells boneless meat — amputation of the left hand and both feet; or a fine of nine hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.10.15/ mānuṣa.māṃsa.vikraye vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For selling human flesh — death.

children.text: KAZ04.10.16/ deva.paśu.pratimā.manuṣya.kṣetra.gṛha.hiraṇya.suvarṇa.ratna.sasya.apahāriṇa uttamo daṇḍaḥ, śuddha.vadho vā //
children.translated_text: For one who steals the property of a deity, cattle, an image, a human, a field, a house, silver, gold, gems, or crops — the highest fine, or outright execution.

children.text:
KAZ04.10.17ab/ puruṣaṃ ca^aparādhaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ guru.lāghavam /
KAZ04.10.17cd/ anubandhaṃ tadātvaṃ ca deśa.kālau samīkṣya ca //
children.translated_text:
Considering the person, the offense, the cause, the gravity,
the consequences, the circumstances, the place, and the time —

children.text:
KAZ04.10.18ab/ uttama.avara.madhyatvaṃ pradeṣṭā daṇḍa.karmaṇi /
KAZ04.10.18cd/ rājñaś ca prakṛtīnāṃ ca kalpayed antarā sthitaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
the judge in criminal proceedings should determine the highest, lowest, or middle [penalty],
positioned between [the interests of] the king and the subjects.

children.text:
(ḷaw of capital punishment, simple and with torture)
KAZ04.11.01/ kalahe ghnataḥ puruṣaṃ citro ghātaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Law of capital punishment, simple and with torture)
For one who kills a person in a quarrel — execution with torture (<s>citraghāta</s>).

children.text: KAZ04.11.02/ sapta.rātrasya^antar.mṛte śuddha.vadhaḥ, pakṣasya^antar uttamaḥ, māsasya^antaḥ pañca.śataḥ samutthāna.vyayaś ca //
children.translated_text: If [the victim] dies within seven days — outright execution; within a fortnight — the highest [fine]; within a month — five hundred [<s>paṇas</s>], plus the cost of treatment.

children.text: KAZ04.11.03/ śastreṇa praharata uttamo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who strikes with a weapon — the highest fine.

children.text: KAZ04.11.04/ madena hasta.vadhaḥ, mohena dvi.śataḥ //
children.translated_text: [If the act was done] in intoxication — amputation of the hand; in confusion — a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.11.05/ vadhe vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For [actually causing] death — death.

children.text: KAZ04.11.06/ prahāreṇa garbhaṃ pātayata uttamo daṇḍaḥ, bhaiṣajyena madhyamaḥ, parikleśena pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who causes a miscarriage by a blow — the highest fine; by medicine — the middle [<s>sāhasa</s> fine]; by harassment — the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: KAZ04.11.07/ prasabha.strī.puruṣa.ghātaka.abhisāraka.nigrāhaka.avaghoṣaka.avaskandaka.upavedhakān pathi.veśma.pratirodhakān rāja.hasty.aśva.rathānāṃ hiṃsakān stenān vā śūlān ārohayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who forcibly kill, abduct, restrain, rob, plunder, or waylay men or women, or who obstruct highways or dwellings, or who harm royal elephants, horses, or chariots, or thieves — should be impaled on stakes.

children.text: KAZ04.11.08/ yaś ca^enān dahed apanayed vā sa tam eva daṇḍaṃ labheta, sāhasam uttamaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: And whoever burns [the body of an impaled criminal] or removes it — he receives the same punishment, or the highest <s>sāhasa</s> [fine].

children.text: KAZ04.11.09/ hiṃsra.stenānāṃ bhakta.vāsa.upakaraṇa.agni.mantra.dāna.vaiyāvṛtya.karmasu^uttamo daṇḍaḥ, paribhāṣaṇam avijñāte //
children.translated_text: For providing food, lodging, equipment, fire, incantations, gifts, or personal service to violent criminals and thieves — the highest fine; for [merely] talking to them when they are unrecognized.

children.text: KAZ04.11.10/ hiṃsra.stenānāṃ putra.dāram asamantraṃ visṛjet, samantram ādadīta //
children.translated_text: The wives and children of violent criminals and thieves should be released if uninvolved; if involved, they should be seized.

children.text: KAZ04.11.11/ rājya.kāmukam antaḥpura.pradharṣakam aṭavy.amitra.utsāhakaṃ durga.rāṣṭra.daṇḍa.kopakaṃ vā śiro.hasta.pradīpikaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: One who aspires to the kingdom, one who violates the inner apartments, one who incites forest-dwellers or enemies, or one who instigates revolt in the fort, countryside, or army — should be executed by burning with head and hands set ablaze.

children.text: KAZ04.11.12/ brāhmaṇaṃ tamaḥ praveśayet //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [guilty of such offenses] should be blinded (<s>tamaḥ praveśayet</s>, 'sent into darkness').

children.text: KAZ04.11.13/ mātṛ.pitṛ.putra.bhrātr.ācārya.tapasvi.ghātakaṃ vā^a.tvak.śiraḥ.prādīpikaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: For the killer of a mother, father, son, brother, teacher, or ascetic — execution by burning with the whole body (without skin) and head set ablaze.

children.text: KAZ04.11.14/ teṣām ākrośe jihvāc.chedaḥ, aṅga.abhiradane tad.aṅgān mocyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For reviling [them] — cutting of the tongue; for biting their limbs — amputation of the corresponding limb.

children.text: KAZ04.11.15/ yadṛcchā.ghāte puṃsaḥ paśu.yūtha.steye ca śuddha.vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For accidental killing of a person or theft of a herd of cattle — outright execution.

children.text: KAZ04.11.16/ daśa.avaraṃ ca yūthaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: A herd should be known as consisting of not less than ten.

children.text: KAZ04.11.17/ udaka.dhāraṇaṃ setuṃ bhindatas tatra^eva^apsu nimajjanam, anudakam uttamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, bhagna.utsṛṣṭakaṃ madhyamaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who breaks a water-retaining dam — drowning in that very water; if [the dam retains] no water — the highest <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for [a dam that is] broken and abandoned — the middle [level].

children.text: KAZ04.11.18/ viṣa.dāyakaṃ puruṣaṃ striyaṃ ca puruṣaghnīm apaḥ praveśayed agarbhiṇīm, garbhiṇīṃ māsa.avara.prajātām //
children.translated_text: A man who administers poison, and a woman who kills her husband, should be drowned — [the woman] if she is not pregnant; if pregnant, [execution is] after one month of giving birth.

children.text: KAZ04.11.19/ pati.guru.prajā.ghātikām agni.viṣadāṃ saṃdhic.chedikāṃ vā gobhiḥ pāṭayet //
children.translated_text: A woman who kills her husband, teacher, or offspring, who administers fire or poison, or who breaks through a [peace] treaty — should be torn apart by bulls.

children.text: KAZ04.11.20/ vivīta.kṣetra.khala.veśma.dravya.hasti.vana.ādīpikam agninā dāhayet //
children.translated_text: For one who sets fire to a pasture, field, threshing floor, dwelling, goods, elephant forest, etc. — death by burning.

children.text: KAZ04.11.21/ rāja.ākrośaka.mantra.bhedakayor aniṣṭa.pravṛttikasya brāhmaṇa.mahānasa.avalehinaś ca jihvām utpāṭayet //
children.translated_text: For one who reviles the king, one who betrays [the king's] counsel, one whose conduct is contrary, and for one who defiles a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s kitchen — the tongue should be torn out.

children.text: KAZ04.11.22/ praharaṇa.āvaraṇa.stenam anāyudhīyam iṣubhir ghātayet //
children.translated_text: For one who steals weapons or armor but is not a soldier — death by arrows.

children.text: KAZ04.11.23/ āyudhīyasya^uttamaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a soldier [who does the same] — the highest [fine].

children.text: KAZ04.11.24/ meḍhra.phala.upaghātinas tad evac^chedayet //
children.translated_text: For one who injures [another's] penis or testicles — the same [organ] should be cut off.

children.text: KAZ04.11.25/ jihvā.nāsa.upaghāte saṃdaṃśa.vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For injuring the tongue or nose — death by the pincers.

children.text:
KAZ04.11.26ab/ ete śāstreṣv anugatāḥ kleśa.daṇḍā mahātmanām /
KAZ04.11.26cd/ akliṣṭānāṃ tu pāpānāṃ dharmyaḥ śuddha.vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
These are the torturous penalties prescribed in the treatises for great offenders;
but for wicked [persons] who have not [previously] been punished, outright execution is considered righteous.

children.text:
(Violation of maidens)
KAZ04.12.01/ savarṇām aprāpta.phalāṃ prakurvato hasta.vadhaḥ, catuḥ.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Violation of maidens)
For one who deflowers a maiden of the same class who has not reached puberty — amputation of the hand, or a fine of four hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.12.02/ mṛtāyāṃ vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: If she dies — death [for the offender].

children.text: KAZ04.12.03/ prāpta.phalāṃ prakurvato madhyamā.pradeśinī.vadho, dvi.śato vā daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For deflowering one who has reached puberty — amputation of the middle and index fingers, or a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.12.04/ pituś ca^avahīnaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: And he should pay to the father the diminished [bride-price].

children.text: KAZ04.12.05/ na ca prākāmyam akāmāyāṃ labbheta //
children.translated_text: Nor should he gain the right [to marry] an unwilling [maiden].

children.text: KAZ04.12.06/ sakāmāyāṃ catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, striyās tv ardha.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: If she is willing — a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>; for the woman — half the fine.

children.text: KAZ04.12.07/ para.śulka.avaruddhāyāṃ hasta.vadhaḥ, catuḥ.śato vā daṇḍaḥ, śulka.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: For [deflowering] a maiden reserved by another's bride-price — amputation of the hand, or a fine of four hundred [<s>paṇas</s>], plus payment of the bride-price.

children.text: KAZ04.12.08/ sapta.ārtava.prajātāṃ varaṇād ūrdhvam alabhamānaḥ prakṛtya prākāmī syāt, na ca pitur avahīnaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: After seven menstrual periods beyond the [agreed] age [for marriage], if [the father] has not given [her in marriage], [the man who deflowers her] may do so and gain the right [to marry her]; nor should he pay the diminished [bride-price] to the father.

children.text: KAZ04.12.09/ ṛtu.pratirodhibhiḥ svāmyād apakrāmati //
children.translated_text: If those who obstruct her menstrual [rights, i.e., delay marriage], she may leave the guardianship.

children.text: KAZ04.12.10/ tri.varṣa.prajāta.ārtavāyās tulyo gantum adoṣaḥ, tataḥ param atulyo^apy analaṃkṛtāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: For a maiden who has had menstrual periods for three years — it is no offense for an equal [suitor] to approach her; after that, even an unequal [suitor may approach] one who is unadorned.

children.text: KAZ04.12.11/ pitṛ.dravya.ādāne steyaṃ bhajeta //
children.translated_text: For taking the father's property [while eloping] — she should bear the penalty for theft.

children.text: KAZ04.12.12/ param uddiśya^anyasya vindato dvi.śato daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who, [having been designated to marry] another, marries a different [person] — a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ04.12.13/ na ca prākāṃyam akāmāyāṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: Nor should he gain the right [to marry] an unwilling [maiden].

children.text: KAZ04.12.14/ kanyām anyāṃ darśayitvā^anyāṃ prayacchataḥ śatyo daṇḍas tulyāyām, hīnāyāṃ dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who shows one maiden and gives another — a fine of one hundred [<s>paṇas</s>] if [the substituted maiden is] of equal [quality]; double if inferior.

children.text: KAZ04.12.15/ prakarmaṇy akumāryāś catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, śulka.vyaya.karmaṇī ca pratidadyāt //
children.translated_text: For deflowering a non-virgin [represented as virgin] — a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>; and [the giver] should return the bride-price and wedding expenses.

children.text: KAZ04.12.16/ avasthāya taj.jātaṃ paścāt.kṛtā dvi.guṇaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: For one who, having stayed [with her], later discovers [the fraud] — he should pay double.

children.text: KAZ04.12.17/ anya.śoṇita.upadhāne dviśato daṇḍaḥ, mithyā.abhiśaṃsinaś ca puṃsaḥ //
children.translated_text: For fraudulent use of another's blood [to simulate virginity] — a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>]; and the same for the man who falsely accuses [her].

children.text: KAZ04.12.18/ śulka.vyaya.karmaṇī ca jīyeta //
children.translated_text: And [the man] should forfeit the bride-price and wedding expenses.

children.text: KAZ04.12.19/ na ca prākāṃyam akāmāyāṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: Nor should he gain the right [to marry] an unwilling [maiden].

children.text: KAZ04.12.20/ strī.prakṛtā sakāmā samānā dvādaśa.paṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt, prakartrī dvi.guṇam //
children.translated_text: A woman of the same class who willingly initiates [intercourse] — a fine of twelve <s>paṇas</s>; for the [female] initiator — double.

children.text: KAZ04.12.21/ akāmāyāḥ śatyo daṇḍa ātma.rāga.artham, śulka.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: For [initiating intercourse with] an unwilling [woman] — a fine of one hundred [<s>paṇas</s>], for the sake of self-gratification, plus payment of the bride-price.

children.text: KAZ04.12.22/ svayaṃ prakṛtā rāja.dāsyaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: One who herself initiates [intercourse and becomes unchaste] should become a royal slave-woman.

children.text: KAZ04.12.23/ bahir.grāmasya prakṛtāyāṃ mithyā.abhiśaṃsane ca dvi.guṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For [deflowering] a woman outside the village, and for false accusation [in such cases] — double the fine.

children.text: KAZ04.12.24/ prasahya kanyām apaharato dvi.śataḥ, sa-suvarṇām uttamaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who forcibly abducts a maiden — a fine of two hundred [<s>paṇas</s>]; if she has gold [dowry] — the highest [fine].

children.text: KAZ04.12.25/ bahūnāṃ kanyā.apahāriṇāṃ pṛthag yathā.uktā daṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: When many abduct a maiden — the prescribed fines apply separately to each.

children.text: KAZ04.12.26/ gaṇikā.duhitaraṃ prakurvataś catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, śulkaṃ mātur bhogaḥ ṣoḍaśa.guṇaḥ //04.12.27/ dāsasya dāsyā vā duhitaram adāsīṃ prakurvataś catur.viṃśati.paṇo daṇḍaḥ śulka.ābandhya.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text:
For deflowering a courtesan's daughter — a fine of fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>, [plus] the bride-price to the mother and a fee of sixteen times [the regular fee].
For deflowering the daughter — not a slave-woman — of a male or female slave — a fine of twenty-four <s>paṇas</s>, plus payment of the bride-price and maintenance.

children.text: KAZ04.12.28/ niṣkraya.anurūpāṃ dāsīṃ prakurvato dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍo vastra.ābandhya.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: For deflowering a slave-woman [whose redemption price] is proportionate — a fine of twelve <s>paṇas</s>, plus the gift of clothing and maintenance.

children.text: KAZ04.12.29/ sācivya.avakāśa.dāne kartṛ.samo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For providing assistance or opportunity [for the offense], the penalty is equal to that of the perpetrator.

children.text: KAZ04.12.30/ proṣita.patikām apacarantīṃ pati.bandhus tat.puruṣo vā saṃgṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: A wife who is unfaithful while her husband is away should be restrained by the husband's kinsmen or his [appointed] agent.

children.text: KAZ04.12.31/ saṃgṛhītā patim ākāṅkṣeta //
children.translated_text: Once restrained, she should await her husband.

children.text: KAZ04.12.32/ patiś cet kṣameta visṛjyeta^ubhayam //
children.translated_text: If the husband pardons [her], both should be released.

children.text: KAZ04.12.33/ akṣamāyāṃ striyāḥ karṇa.nāsa.ācchedanam, vadhaṃ jāraś ca prāpnuyāt //
children.translated_text: If [the wife] does not submit — cutting of her ears and nose for the woman, and the adulterer should receive death.

children.text: KAZ04.12.34/ jāraṃ cora ity abhiharataḥ pañca.śato daṇḍaḥ, hiraṇyena muñcatas tad.aṣṭa.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who brings an adulterer [to the husband] calling him 'a thief' — a fine of five hundred [<s>paṇas</s>]; for one who releases him for gold — eight times that amount.

children.text: KAZ04.12.35/ keśākeśikaṃ saṃgrahaṇam, upaliṅganād vā śarīra.upabhogānām, taj.jātebhyaḥ(taj.jñātebhyaḥ? cf.ṇ12.60)), strī.vacanād vā //
children.translated_text: Solicitation [is determined from]: mutual hair-pulling; or from evidence of bodily contact; from those who have knowledge [of the affair]; or from the woman's own statement.

children.text: KAZ04.12.36/ para.cakra.aṭavī.hṛtām ogha.pravyūḍhām araṇyeṣu durbhikṣe vā tyaktāṃ preta.bhāva.utsṛṣṭāṃ vā para.striyaṃ nistārayitvā yathā.saṃbhāṣitaṃ samupabhuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Another's wife who has been carried off by enemy forces or forest-dwellers, swept away by a flood, abandoned in the wilderness or during famine, or abandoned as dead — having rescued her, [the rescuer] may enjoy her as agreed.

children.text: KAZ04.12.37/ jāti.viśiṣṭām akāmām apatyavatīṃ niṣkrayeṇa dadyāt //
children.translated_text: One of superior class, unwilling, and having children — he should return [her] upon payment of the ransom.

children.text:
KAZ04.12.38ab/ cora.hastān nadī.vegād durbhikṣād deśa.vibhramāt /
KAZ04.12.38cd/ nistārayitvā kāntārān naṣṭāṃ tyaktāṃ mṛtā^iti vā //
children.translated_text:
From the hands of thieves, from the rush of a river, from famine, from foreign lands,
having rescued [a woman] from the wilderness, or one who was lost, abandoned, or [declared] dead —

children.text:
KAZ04.12.39ab/ bhuñjīta striyam anyeṣāṃ yathā.saṃbhāṣitaṃ naraḥ /
KAZ04.12.39cd/ na tu rāja.pratāpena pramuktāṃ svajanena vā //
children.translated_text:
a man may enjoy the wife of another as mutually agreed;
but not one released by the king's power or by her own kinsmen.

children.text:
KAZ04.12.40ab/ na ca^uttamāṃ na ca^akāmāṃ pūrva.apatyavatīṃ na ca /
KAZ04.12.40cd/ īdṛśīṃ tv anurūpeṇa niṣkrayeṇa^apavāhayet //E
children.translated_text:
Nor one of superior class, nor an unwilling one, nor one with prior offspring;
but one of such [eligible] description, he should release upon [payment of] a proper ransom.

children.text:
(Punishments for transgressions)
KAZ04.13.01/ brāhmaṇam apeyam abhakṣyaṃ vā grāsayata uttamo daṇḍaḥ, kṣatriyaṃ madhyamaḥ, vaiśyaṃ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, śūdraṃ catuṣ.pañcāśat.paṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Punishments for transgressions)
For forcing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> to consume what is undrinkable or inedible — the highest fine; for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> — the middle; for a <s>Vaiśya</s> — the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> fine; for a <s>Śūdra</s> — fifty-four <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: KAZ04.13.02/ svayaṃ grasitāro nirviṣayāḥ kāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who themselves consume [such things] should be exiled.

children.text: KAZ04.13.03/ para.gṛha.abhigamane divā pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, rātrau madhyamaḥ //
children.translated_text: For entering another's house during the day — the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> fine; at night — the middle [level].

children.text: KAZ04.13.04/ divā rātrau vā saśastrasya praviśata uttamo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For entering by day or night while armed — the highest fine.

children.text: KAZ04.13.05/ bhikṣuka.vaidehakau matta.unmattau balād āpadi ca^atisaṃnikṛṣṭāḥ pravṛtta.praveśāś ca^adaṇḍyāḥ, anyatra pratiṣedhāt //
children.translated_text: Beggars, traders, the intoxicated and the insane, those [entering] by force in times of distress, those who are very close [neighbors], and those who have already entered — are not punishable, except when prohibited.

children.text: KAZ04.13.06/ sva.veśmano virātrād ūrdhvaṃ parivāram ārohataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, para.veśmano madhyamaḥ, grāma.ārāma.vāṭa.bhedinaś ca //
children.translated_text: For one who climbs the upper story of his own house after curfew — the first level of the <s>sāhasa</s> fine; of another's house — the middle [level]; also for one who breaks into a village, garden, or enclosure.

children.text: KAZ04.13.07/ grāmeṣv antaḥ sārthikā jñāta.sārā vaseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Within villages, caravan-travelers of known goods should reside.

children.text: KAZ04.13.08/ muṣitaṃ pravāsitaṃ ca^eṣām anirgataṃ rātrau grāma.svāmī dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Whatever is stolen from or lost by them [while] they have not departed at night — the village headman should pay.

children.text: KAZ04.13.09/ grāma.antareṣu vā muṣitaṃ pravāsitaṃ vivīta.adhyakṣo dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, for goods stolen or lost in the spaces between villages, the superintendent of pasture-lands should pay.

children.text: KAZ04.13.10/ avivītānāṃ cora.rajjukaḥ //
children.translated_text: For [areas] without pasture-lands, the thief-police (<s>corarajjuka</s>) [is responsible].

children.text: KAZ04.13.11/ tathā^apy aguptānāṃ sīma.avarodhena vicayaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Even so, for unprotected [goods], they should provide restitution through a border-search.

children.text: KAZ04.13.12/ asīma.avarodhe pañca.grāmī daśa.grāmī vā //
children.translated_text: In the absence of a border-search — a group of five or ten villages [is responsible].

children.text: KAZ04.13.13/ durbalaṃ veśma śakaṭam anuttabdham ūrdha.staṃbhaṃ śastram anapāśrayam apraticchannaṃ śvabhraṃ kūpaṃ kūṭa.avapātaṃ vā kṛtvā hiṃsāyāṃ daṇḍa.pāruṣyaṃ vidyāt //
children.translated_text: For constructing a weak house, an unsupported cart, a pillar facing upward, leaving an unshielded weapon exposed, or leaving an uncovered pit, well, or trap — and [if someone] is harmed, [the penalties for] physical assault apply.

children.text: KAZ04.13.14/ vṛkṣac.chedane daṃya.raśmi.haraṇe catuṣpadānām adānta.sevane vāhane vā kāṣṭha.loṣṭa.pāṣāṇa.daṇḍa.bāṇa.bāhu.vikṣepaṇeṣu yāne hastinā ca smaghaṭṭane "apehi" iti prakośann adaṇḍyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For felling a tree, for seizing the reins or whip of an animal-drawn [vehicle], for driving untrained quadrupeds, for throwing wood, clods, stones, sticks, or arrows, for flinging the arm from a vehicle, or for colliding with an elephant — one is not punishable if [he shouted] 'Get out of the way!'

children.text: KAZ04.13.15/ hastinā roṣitena hato droṇa.annaṃ madya.kuṃbhaṃ mālya.anulepanaṃ danta.pramārjanaṃ ca paṭaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: One killed by an enraged elephant — [the king] should give a <s>droṇa</s> of food, a jar of liquor, garlands, unguents, and a cloth for the teeth-cleaning [rite of the deceased].

children.text: KAZ04.13.16/ aśva.medha.avabhṛtha.snānena tulyo hastinā vadha iti pāda.prakṣālanam //
children.translated_text: Death by elephant is equal to the purificatory bath at the conclusion of the horse-sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>) — therefore, foot-washing [of the elephant keeper is performed].

children.text: KAZ04.13.17/ udāsīna.vadhe yātur uttamo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: For the death of an innocent bystander — the highest fine for the rider.

children.text: KAZ04.13.18/ śṛṅgiṇā daṃṣṭriṇā vā hiṃsyamānam amokṣayataḥ svāminaḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, pratikruṣṭasya dvi.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.18/ For the owner who does not rescue [a person] being injured by a horned or fanged [animal] — the first level <s>sāhasa</s> fine; if [the victim] had called out [for help] — double.

children.text: KAZ04.13.19/ śṛṅgi.daṃṣṭribhyām anyonyaṃ ghātayatas tac ca tāvac ca daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.19/ For one who causes horned or fanged animals to fight each other — a fine equal to the [value of the] animal plus the same amount.

children.text: KAZ04.13.20/ deva.paśum ṛṣabham ukṣāṇaṃ go.kumārīṃ vā vāhayataḥ pañca.śato daṇḍaḥ, pravāsayata uttamaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.20/ For one who yokes a consecrated animal, a bull, a stud-bull, or a heifer — the fine is five hundred [<s>paṇas</s>]; for one who banishes [such an animal] — the highest [fine].

children.text: KAZ04.13.21/ loma.doha.vāhana.prajanana.upakāriṇāṃ kṣudra.paśūnām adāne tac ca tāvac ca daṇḍaḥ, pravāsane ca, anyatra deva.pitṛ.kāryebhyaḥ //
