children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.21/ For not surrendering small animals useful for wool, milking, draught, and breeding — a fine equal to the [value of the] animal plus the same amount; likewise for banishing [them] — except for purposes of worship of gods and ancestors.

children.text: KAZ04.13.22/ chinna.nasyaṃ bhagna.yugaṃ tiryak.pratimukha.āgataṃ pratyāsarad vā cakra.yuktaṃ yātā paśu.manuṣya.saṃbādhe vā hiṃsāyām adaṇḍyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.22/ When [a vehicle] has a broken nose-rope, a broken yoke, approaches from the opposite direction or head-on, or has a defective wheel — in case of injury in a crowd of animals and humans, the driver is not punishable.

children.text: KAZ04.13.23/ anyathā yathā.uktaṃ mānuṣa.prāṇi.hiṃsāyāṃ daṇḍam abhyāvahet //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.23/ Otherwise, he should incur the fine as stated for injury to human life.

children.text: KAZ04.13.24/ amānuṣa.prāṇi.vadhe prāṇi.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.24/ For killing a non-human creature — replacement of the creature [as well].

children.text: KAZ04.13.25/ bāle yātari yānasthaḥ svāmī daṇḍyaḥ, asvāmini yānasthaḥ, prāpta.vyavahāro vā yātā //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.25/ When a child is the driver, the owner [seated] in the vehicle is punishable; if the owner is not [in the vehicle], the one seated in it [is punishable]; or the driver who has reached the age of legal responsibility.

children.text: KAZ04.13.26/ bāla.adhiṣṭhitam apuruṣaṃ vā yānaṃ rājā haret //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.26/ A vehicle driven by a child or without an attendant — the king should confiscate.

children.text: KAZ04.13.27/ kṛtya.abhicārābhyāṃ yat.param āpādayet tad.āpādayitavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.27/ Whatever harm one inflicts on another through sorcery or black magic — the same should be inflicted on him.

children.text: KAZ04.13.28/ kāmaṃ bhāryāyām anicchantyāṃ kanyāyāṃ vā dāra.arthino bhartari bhāryāyā vā saṃvadana.karaṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.28/ The use of love-magic on an unwilling wife or maiden [by] one desiring marriage, or on a husband by a wife — this constitutes the act of enticement.

children.text: KAZ04.13.29/ anyathā.hiṃsāyāṃ madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.29/ For other kinds of harm [through magic] — the middle <s>sāhasa</s> fine.

children.text: KAZ04.13.30/ mātā.pitror bhaginīṃ mātulānīm ācāryāṇīṃ snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ bhaginīṃ vā^adhicaratas tri.liṅgac.chedanaṃ vadhaś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.30/ For one who commits sexual assault upon a mother, father's sister, maternal aunt, teacher's wife, daughter-in-law, daughter, or sister — cutting of the three organs and death.

children.text: KAZ04.13.31/ sakāmā tad eva labheta, dāsa.paricāraka.āhitaka.bhuktā ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.31/ If she was willing, she should receive the same [punishment]; likewise one enjoyed by a slave, a servant, or a bonded laborer.

children.text: KAZ04.13.32/ brāhmaṇyām aguptāyāṃ kṣatriyasya^uttamaḥ, sarva.svaṃ vaiśyasya, śūdraḥ kaṭa.agninā dahyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.32/ For a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [who violates] an unprotected <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman — the highest [fine]; for a <s>Vaiśya</s> — confiscation of all property; a <s>Śūdra</s> should be burned with fire of straw.

children.text: KAZ04.13.33/ sarvatra rāja.bhāryā.gamane kuṃbhī.pākaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.33/ Everywhere, for sexual intercourse with a king's wife — [death by] being boiled in a cauldron.

children.text: KAZ04.13.34/ śva.pākī.gamane kṛta.kabandha.aṅkaḥ para.viṣayaṃ gacchet, śva.pākatvaṃ vā śūdraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.34/ For sexual intercourse with a <s>Śvapākī</s> (outcaste woman) — [the offender] should be branded with the mark of a headless corpse and banished to enemy territory; or a <s>Śūdra</s> [becomes] a <s>Śvapāka</s>.

children.text: KAZ04.13.35/ śva.pākasya^āryā.gamane vadhaḥ, striyāḥ karṇa.nāsa.ācchedanam //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.35/ For a <s>Śvapāka</s> who has intercourse with an <s>Ārya</s> woman — death; for the woman — cutting off of ears and nose.

children.text: KAZ04.13.36/ pravrajitā.gamane catur.viṃśati.paṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.36/ For sexual intercourse with a female renunciant — the fine is twenty-four <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: KAZ04.13.37/ sakāmā tad eva labheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.37/ If she was willing, she should receive the same [punishment].

children.text: KAZ04.13.38/ rūpa.ājīvāyāḥ prasahya.upabhoge dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.38/ For forcible enjoyment of a courtesan — the fine is twelve <s>paṇas</s>.

children.text: KAZ04.13.39/ bahūnām ekām adhicaratāṃ pṛthak catur.viṃśati.paṇo daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.39/ For many who violate one [woman] — twenty-four <s>paṇas</s> each, separately.

children.text: KAZ04.13.40/ striyam ayonau gacchataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, puruṣam adhimehataś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.13.40/ For one who has unnatural intercourse with a woman — the first level <s>sāhasa</s> fine; likewise for one who urinates upon a man.

children.text:
KAZ04.13.41ab/ maithune dvādaśa.paṇas tiryag.yoniṣv anātmanaḥ /
KAZ04.13.41cd/ daivata.pratimānāṃ ca gamane dvi.guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ04.13.41ab/ For intercourse with animals, the [fine is] twelve <s>paṇas</s> for one not in control of himself;
KAZ04.13.41cd/ for intercourse with images of deities — double, it is declared.

children.text:
KAZ04.13.42ab/ adaṇḍya.daṇḍane rājño daṇḍas triṃśad.guṇo^aṃbhasi /
KAZ04.13.42cd/ varuṇāya pradātavyo brāhmaṇebhyas tataḥ param //
children.translated_text:
KAZ04.13.42ab/ For the king who punishes the unpunishable — the fine is thirty times [the standard], to be cast into the waters
KAZ04.13.42cd/ as an offering to <s>Varuṇa</s>, and thereafter to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text:
KAZ04.13.43ab/ tena tat pūyate pāpaṃ rājño daṇḍa.apacārajam /
KAZ04.13.43cd/ śāstā hi varuṇo rājñāṃ mithyā vyācaratāṃ nṛṣu //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ04.13.43ab/ Thereby is the sin arising from the king's misuse of punishment purified;
KAZ04.13.43cd/ for <s>Varuṇa</s> is the chastiser of kings who act unjustly toward men.

children.text:
(Infliction of secret punishment)
KAZ05.1.01/ durga.rāṣṭrayoḥ kaṇṭaka.śodhanam uktam //
children.translated_text:
(Infliction of secret punishment)
KAZ05.1.01/ The removal of thorns in the fort and the countryside has been stated.

children.text: KAZ05.1.02/ rāja.rājyayor vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.02/ We shall [now] speak of [the removal of thorns concerning] the king and the kingdom.

children.text: KAZ05.1.03/ rājānam avagṛhya^upajīvinaḥ śatru.sādhāraṇā vā ye mukhyās teṣu gūḍha.puruṣa.praṇidhiḥ kṛtya.pakṣa.upagraho vā siddhiḥ yathā.uktaṃ purastād, upajāpo^apasarpo vā yathā pāragrāmike vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.03/ Against chiefs who live at the king's expense and are shared with the enemy — the deployment of secret agents, or winning over their disaffected factions, is effective as previously stated; instigation or infiltration, as we shall describe regarding agents from another village.

children.text: KAZ05.1.04/ rājya.upaghātinas tu vallabhāḥ saṃhatā vā ye mukhyāḥ prakāśam aśakyāḥ pratiṣeddhuṃ dūṣyāḥ teṣu dharma.rucir upāṃśu.daṇḍaṃ prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.04/ But against favorites who harm the kingdom, or chiefs in combination who cannot be openly restrained — [the king], fond of righteousness, should apply secret punishment.

children.text: KAZ05.1.05/ dūṣya.mahā.mātra.bhrātaram asat.kṛtaṃ sattrī protsāhya rājānaṃ darśayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.05/ An undercover agent should incite a disaffected and dishonored brother of the target high official and show [him to] the king.

children.text: KAZ05.1.06/ taṃ rājā dūṣya.dravya.upabhoga.atisargeṇa dūṣye vikramayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.06/ The king should embolden him against the target by granting him access to the target's property and enjoyments.

children.text: KAZ05.1.07/ śastreṇa rasena vā vikrāntaṃ tatra^eva ghātayed "bhrātṛ.ghātako^ayam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.07/ When he strikes [the target] with weapon or poison, he should be killed right there — "This one is a fratricide."

children.text: KAZ05.1.08/ tena pāraśavaḥ paricārikā.putraś ca vyākhyātau //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.08/ By this are explained [the cases of] an illegitimate son and a maidservant's son.

children.text: KAZ05.1.09/ dūṣyaṃ.mahāmātraṃ vā sattri.protsāhito bhrātā dāyaṃ yāceta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.09/ Or, a brother incited by the undercover agent should demand his share of inheritance from the target high official.

children.text: KAZ05.1.10/ taṃ dūṣya.gṛha.pratidvāri rātrāv upaśayānam anyatra vā vasantaṃ tīkṣṇo hantā brūyād "hato^ayaṃ dāya.kāmukaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.10/ When he sleeps at night at the opposite door of the target's house or stays elsewhere — a sharp agent should kill him and declare: "This one has been killed, desirous of the inheritance."

children.text: KAZ05.1.11/ tato hata.pakṣam upagṛhya^itaraṃ nigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.11/ Then, taking up the cause of the slain party, [the king] should suppress the other.

children.text: KAZ05.1.12/ dūṣya.samīpasthā vā sattriṇo bhrātaraṃ dāyaṃ yācamānaṃ ghātena paribhartsayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.12/ Or, undercover agents near the target should threaten the brother who demands the inheritance with death.

children.text: KAZ05.1.13/ taṃ rātrau iti samānam //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.13/ At night — the same [procedure as before applies].

children.text: KAZ05.1.14/ dūṣya.mahā.mātrayor vā yaḥ putraḥ pituḥ pitā vā putrasya dārān adhicarati, bhrātā vā bhrātuḥ, tayoḥ kāpaṭika.mukhaḥ kalahaḥ pūrveṇa vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.14/ Or, when the son of one of the two — the target or the high official — commits adultery with the wife of his father, or a father with his son's wife, or a brother with a brother's — a treacherous quarrel [should be instigated], as explained above.

children.text: KAZ05.1.15/ dūṣya.mahā.mātra.putram ātma.saṃbhāvitaṃ vā sattrī "rāja.putras tvam, śatru.bhayād iha nyasto^asi" ity upajapet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.15/ An undercover agent should whisper to the son of the target or high official, or to one who is self-important: "You are a prince, deposited here out of fear of enemies."

children.text: KAZ05.1.16/ pratipannaṃ rājā rahasi pūjayet "prāpta.yauvarājya.kālaṃ tvāṃ mahā.mātra.bhayān na^abhiṣiñcāmi" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.16/ When he accepts, the king should honor him privately [saying]: "The time has come for your appointment as heir apparent, but I dare not consecrate you for fear of the high officials."

children.text: KAZ05.1.17/ taṃ sattrī mahā.mātra.vadhe yojayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.17/ The undercover agent should then engage him in the killing of the high official.

children.text: KAZ05.1.18/ vikrāntaṃ tatra^eva ghātayet "pitṛ.ghātako^ayam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.18/ When he strikes, he should be killed right there — "This one is a parricide."

children.text: KAZ05.1.19/ bhikṣukī vā dūṣya.bhāryāṃ sāṃvadanikībhir auṣadhībhiḥ saṃvāsya rasena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.19/ Or, a female mendicant, having gained the confidence of the target's wife through love-inducing drugs, should deceive her with poison.

children.text: KAZ05.1.20/ ity āpya.prayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.20/ This is the method [using] close associates.

children.text: KAZ05.1.21/ dūṣya.mahā.mātram aṭavīṃ para.grāmaṃ vā hantuṃ kāntāra.vyavahite vā deśe rāṣṭra.pālam anta.pālaṃ vā sthāpayituṃ nāgara.sthānaṃ vā kupitam avagrāhituṃ sārtha.ativāhyaṃ pratyante vā sa-pratyādeyam ādātuṃ phalgu.balaṃ tīkṣṇa.yuktaṃ preṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.21/ The target high official should be sent with a weak force accompanied by sharp agents — to subdue a forest [tribe] or a foreign village, or to establish a district governor or frontier guard in a region separated by wilderness, or to seize an angry town-governor, or to collect revenue with counter-payment in a border region.

children.text: KAZ05.1.22/ rātrau divā vā yuddhe pravṛtte tīkṣṇāḥ pratirodhaka.vyañjanā vā hanyuḥ "abhiyoge hataḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.22/ During a battle at night or by day, the sharp agents, or those disguised as interceptors, should kill [him] — "He was killed in the attack."

children.text: KAZ05.1.23/ yātrā.vihāra.gato vā dūṣya.mahā.mātrān darśanāya^āhvayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.23/ Or, while on a tour or excursion, [the king] should summon the target high officials for an audience.

children.text: KAZ05.1.24/ te gūḍha.śastrais tīkṣṇaiḥ saha praviṣṭā madhyama.kakṣyāyām ātma.vicayam antaḥ.praveśana.arthaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.24/ They, having entered with sharp agents carrying concealed weapons, should surrender their [weapons for] personal inspection in the middle enclosure for the purpose of entering the inner [chamber].

children.text: KAZ05.1.25/ tato dauvārika.abhigṛhītās tīkṣṇāḥ "dūṣya.prayuktāḥ sma" iti brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.25/ Then the sharp agents, seized by the doorkeeper, should declare: "We were sent by the targets."

children.text: KAZ05.1.26/ te tad.abhivikhyāpya dūṣyān hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.26/ Having publicized this, they should kill the targets.

children.text: KAZ05.1.27/ tīkṣṇa.sthāne ca^anye vadhyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.27/ And others should be executed in the place of the sharp agents [as accomplices].

children.text: KAZ05.1.28/ bahir.vihāra.gato vā dūṣyān āsanna.āvāsān pūjayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.28/ Or, while on an excursion outside, [the king] should honor the targets who are encamped nearby.

children.text: KAZ05.1.29/ teṣāṃ devī.vyañjanā vā duḥstrī rātrāv āvāseṣu gṛhyeta^iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.29/ A loose woman disguised as the queen should be apprehended at night in their camps — the same [procedure] as before.

children.text: KAZ05.1.30/ dūṣya.mahā.mātraṃ vā "sūdo bhakṣa.kāro vā te śobhanaḥ" iti stavena bhakṣya.bhojyaṃ yāceta, bahir vā kvacid adhva.gataḥ pānīyam //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.30/ Or [the king] should praise the target high official — "Your cook or confectioner is excellent" — and request food and drink; or, while traveling somewhere outside, [request] water.

children.text: KAZ05.1.31/ tad.ubhayaṃ rasena yojayitvā pratisvādane tāv eva^upayojayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.31/ Having laced both with poison, at the tasting they should serve them to those very [targets].

children.text: KAZ05.1.32/ tad.abhivikhyāpya "rasadau" iti ghātayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.32/ Having publicized this, [the king] should have them killed — "These are poison-givers."

children.text: KAZ05.1.33/ abhicāra.śīlaṃ vā siddha.vyañjano "godhā.kūrma.karkaṭaka.kūṭānāṃ lakṣaṇyānām anyatama.prāśanena manorathān avāpsyasi" iti grāhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.33/ Or, one disguised as an adept, [displaying signs of] magical powers, should entice [the target], who is inclined toward sorcery: "By eating one of these specially prepared lizards, tortoises, or crabs, you will attain your desires."

children.text: KAZ05.1.34/ pratipannaṃ karmaṇi rasena loha.musalair vā ghātayet "karma.vyāpadā hataḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.34/ When he accepts, [the agent] should kill him during the ritual with poison or iron pestles — "He died from a mishap in the ritual."

children.text: KAZ05.1.35/ cikitsaka.vyañjano vā daurātmikam asādhyaṃ vā vyādhiṃ dūṣyasya sthāpayitvā bhaiṣajya.āhāra.yogeṣu rasena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.35/ Or, one disguised as a physician, having established that the target has an incurable or dangerous disease, should deceive him with poison in his medicines and food.

children.text: KAZ05.1.36/ sūda.ārālika.vyañjanā vā praṇihitā dūṣyaṃ rasena^atisaṃdadhyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.36/ Or, agents disguised as cooks and chefs, having been placed [in the household], should deceive the target with poison.

children.text: KAZ05.1.37/ ity upaniṣat.pratiṣedhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.37/ This is the prevention of esoteric [enemies].

children.text: KAZ05.1.38/ ubhaya.dūṣya.pratiṣedhas tu //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.38/ But the prevention of both [types of] targets [is as follows]:

children.text:
KAZ05.1.39/ yatra dūṣyaḥ pratiṣeddhavyas tatra dūṣyam eva phalgu.bala.tīkṣṇa.yuktaṃ preṣayet, gaccha, amuṣmin durge rāṣṭre vā sainyam utthāpaya hiraṇyaṃ vā, vallabhād vā hiraṇyam āhāraya, vallabha.kanyāṃ vā prasahya^ānaya, durga.setu.vaṇik.patha.śūnya.niveśa.khani.dravya.hasti.vana.karmaṇām anyatamad vā kāraya rāṣṭra.pālyam anta.pālyaṃ vā^ yaś ca tvā pratiṣedhayen
na vā te sāhāyyaṃ dadyāt sa bandhavyaḥ syāt" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.39/ Where the target is to be eliminated, send the target himself with a weak force and sharp agents [saying]: "Go, raise an army or collect gold in such-and-such a fort or district; or seize gold from a favorite; or forcibly bring back a favorite's daughter; or carry out one of the works of fort, embankment, trade-route, colonization of wastelands, mine, forest-produce, or elephant forest; or [serve as] a district governor or frontier guard. And whoever obstructs you or does not render you assistance — he should be arrested."

children.text: KAZ05.1.40/ tathaiva^itareṣāṃ preṣayed "amuṣya^avinayaḥ pratiṣeddhavyaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.40/ And likewise he should dispatch the others [saying]: "His insubordination is to be restrained."

children.text: KAZ05.1.41/ tam eteṣu kalaha.sthāneṣu karma.pratighāteṣu vā vivadamānaṃ tīkṣṇāḥ śastraṃ pātayitvā pracchannaṃ hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.41/ When he quarrels with these at the points of conflict or over obstruction of work — the sharp agents, having drawn weapons, should kill him secretly.

children.text: KAZ05.1.42/ tena doṣeṇa^itare niyantavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.42/ By that offense, the others should be brought under control.

children.text: KAZ05.1.43/ purāṇāṃ grāmāṇāṃ kulānāṃ vā dūṣyāṇāṃ sīmā.kṣetra.khala.veśma.maryādāsu dravya.upakaraṇa.sasya.vāhana.hiṃsāsu prekṣā.kṛtya^utsaveṣu vā samutpanne kalahe tīkṣṇair utpādite vā tīkṣṇāḥ śastraṃ pātayitvā brūyuḥ "evaṃ kriyante ye^amunā kalahāyante: iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.43/ Among the cities, villages, or families of the targets — at boundaries, fields, threshing-floors, or dwelling-borders, or in disputes over property, equipment, crops, or vehicles, or at spectacles, religious ceremonies, or festivals — when a quarrel arises [naturally] or is instigated by sharp agents, the sharp agents, having drawn weapons, should declare: "Thus are treated those who quarrel with him."

children.text: KAZ05.1.44/ tena doṣeṇa^itare niyantavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.44/ By that offense, the others should be brought under control.

children.text: KAZ05.1.45/ yeṣāṃ vā dūṣyāṇāṃ jāta.mūlāḥ kalahās teṣāṃ kṣetra.khala.veśmāny ādīpayitvā bandhu.saṃbandhiṣu vāhaneṣu vā tīkṣṇāḥ śastraṃ pātayitvā tathaiva brūyuḥ "amunā prayuktāḥ smaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.45/ Or, among those targets whose quarrels have taken root, having set fire to their fields, threshing-floors, and dwellings, the sharp agents, having drawn weapons against their kinsmen, relatives, or vehicles, should likewise declare: "We were sent by him."

children.text: KAZ04.4.46/ tena doṣeṇa^itare niyantavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ04.4.46/ By that offense, the others should be brought under control.

children.text: KAZ05.1.47/ durga.rāṣṭra.dūṣyān vā sattriṇaḥ parasparasya^āveśanikān kārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.47/ Or, undercover agents should make the targets of the fort and the countryside guests of one another.

children.text: KAZ05.1.48/ tatra rasadā rasaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.48/ There, the poison-givers should administer poison.

children.text: KAZ05.1.49/ tena doṣeṇa^itare niyantavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.49/ By that offense, the others should be brought under control.

children.text: KAZ05.1.50/ bhikṣukī vā dūṣya.rāṣṭra.mukhyaṃ "dūṣya.rāṣṭra.mukhyasya bhāryā snuṣā duhitā vā kāmayate" ity upajapet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.50/ Or, a female mendicant should whisper to a target district-chief: "The wife, daughter-in-law, or daughter of [another] target district-chief desires you."

children.text: KAZ05.1.51/ pratipannasya^ābharaṇam ādāya svāmine darśayet "asau te mukhyo yauvana.utsikto bhāryāṃ snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ vā^abhimanyate" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.51/ When he accepts, [the mendicant] should take an ornament [from the woman] and show it to the [other] master [saying]: "That chief of yours, arrogant with youth, has designs on your wife, daughter-in-law, or daughter."

children.text: KAZ05.1.52/ tayoḥ kalaho rātrau iti samānam //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.52/ Their quarrel at night — the same [procedure] as before.

children.text: KAZ05.1.53/ dūṣya.daṇḍa.upanateṣu tu - yuva.rājaḥ senā.patir vā kiṃcid apakṛtya^apakrānto vikrameta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.53/ Against those who submit to the target's army — the crown prince or the commander-in-chief should commit some offense and then withdraw and make a show of force.

children.text: KAZ05.1.54/ tato rājā dūṣya.daṇḍa.upanatān eva preṣayet phalgu.bala.tīkṣṇa.yuktān iti samānāḥ sarva eva yogāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.54/ Then the king should dispatch those very ones who submitted to the target's army, with a weak force and sharp agents — the same methods apply throughout.

children.text: KAZ05.1.55/ teṣāṃ ca putreṣv anukṣiyatsu yo nirvikāraḥ sa pitṛ.dāyaṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.55/ And as their sons die out in succession, whoever remains blameless should receive the paternal inheritance.

children.text: KAZ05.1.56/ evam asya putra.pautrān anuvartate rājyam apāsta.puruṣa.doṣam //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.1.56/ Thus the kingdom follows his sons and grandsons, purged of the taint of [dangerous] men.

children.text:
KAZ05.1.57ab/ sva.pakṣe para.pakṣe vā tūṣṇīṃ daṇḍaṃ prayojayet /
KAZ05.1.57cd/ āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca kṣamāvān aviśaṅkitaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ05.1.57ab/ Whether in his own faction or the enemy's, he should apply punishment silently,
KAZ05.1.57cd/ patient and unsuspecting, both for the present and for the future.

children.text:
(ṛeplenishment of the treasury)
KAZ05.2.01/ kośam akośaḥ pratyutpanna.artha.kṛcchraḥ saṃgṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Replenishment of the treasury)
KAZ05.2.01/ One who lacks a treasury, being in financial difficulty, should replenish it from available resources.

children.text: KAZ05.2.02/ jana.padaṃ mahāntam alpa.pramāṇaṃ vā^adeva.mātṛkaṃ prabhūta.dhānyaṃ dhānyasya^aṃśaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturthaṃ vā yāceta, yathā.sāraṃ madhyam avaraṃ vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.02/ From the countryside — whether large or small, not rain-dependent, and rich in grain — he should request a third or fourth share of the grain, [varying as] the best, middling, or lowest according to [the region's] capacity.

children.text: KAZ05.2.03/ durga.setu.karma.vaṇik.patha.śūnya.niveśa.khani.dravya.hasti.vana.karma.upakāriṇaṃ pratyantam alpa.pramāṇaṃ vā na yāceta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.03/ He should not request [this] from a frontier [region] that supports fort and embankment construction, trade routes, settlements in uninhabited areas, mining operations, and elephant forests — nor from a small one.

children.text: KAZ05.2.04/ dhānya.paśu.hiraṇya.ādi niviśamānāya dadyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.04/ To one who is settling [new land], he should give grain, cattle, gold, and the like.

children.text: KAZ05.2.05/ caturtham aṃśaṃ dhānyānāṃ bīja.bhakta.śuddhaṃ ca hiraṇyena krīṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.05/ He should purchase with gold a fourth share of grain, net of seed and provisions.

children.text: KAZ05.2.06/ araṇya.jātaṃ śrotriya.svaṃ ca pariharet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.06/ He should exempt forest-produced [grain] and that belonging to Vedic scholars.

children.text: KAZ05.2.07/ tad apy anugraheṇa krīṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.07/ Even that he should purchase with favorable [terms].

children.text: KAZ05.2.08/ tasya^akaraṇe vā samāhartṛ.puruṣā grīṣme karṣakāṇām udvāpaṃ kārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.08/ Or, failing that, the collector's men should have the farmers thresh [early] in summer.

children.text: KAZ05.2.09/ pramāda.avaskannasya^atyayaṃ dvi.guṇam udāharanto bīja.kāle bīja.lekhyaṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.09/ Citing a double penalty for negligent defaulters, they should make a seed-loan at sowing time.

children.text: KAZ05.2.10/ niṣpanne harita.pakva.ādānaṃ vārayeyuḥ, anyatra śāka.kaṭa.bhaṅga.muṣṭibhyāṃ deva.pitṛ.pūjā.dāna.arthaṃ gava.arthaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.10/ They should prohibit the taking of green and ripe [produce before assessment], except for handfuls of vegetables, broken stalks, and [quantities needed] for worship of gods and ancestors, or for cattle.

children.text: KAZ05.2.11/ bhikṣuka.grāma.bhṛtaka.arthaṃ ca rāśi.mūlaṃ parihareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.11/ And they should exempt the base of the heap [set aside] for beggars and village employees.

children.text: KAZ05.2.12/ sva.sasya.apahāriṇaḥ pratipāto^aṣṭa.guṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.12/ For one who steals his own crop, the penalty is eightfold restitution.

children.text: KAZ05.2.13/ para.sasya.apahāriṇaḥ pañcāśad.guṇaḥ sītā.atyayaḥ, sva.vargasya, bāhyasya tu vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.13/ For one who steals another's crop, the crown-land penalty is fiftyfold — [that is, for] one of his own group; for an outsider, death.

children.text: KAZ05.2.14/ caturtham aṃśaṃ dhānyānāṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vanyānāṃ tūla.lākṣā.kṣauma.valka.kārpāsa.rauma.kauśeya.kauṣadha.gandha.puṣpa.phala.śāka.paṇyānāṃ kāṣṭha.veṇu.māṃsa.vallūrāṇāṃ ca gṛhṇīyuḥ, danta.ajinasya^ardham //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.14/ They should take: a fourth of grain; a sixth of forest products, cotton, lac, linen, bark-fiber, cotton [cloth], hemp, silk, medicinal herbs, perfumes, flowers, fruits, vegetables, firewood, bamboo, meat, and dried meat; and half of ivory and hides.

children.text: KAZ05.2.15/ tad anisṛṣṭaṃ vikrīṇānasya pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.15/ For one who sells [these] without authorization, the first <s>sāhasa</s> penalty [applies].

children.text: KAZ05.2.16/ iti karṣakeṣu praṇayaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.16/ Thus [the emergency levy] on farmers.

children.text: KAZ05.2.17/ suvarṇa.rajata.vajra.maṇi.muktā.pravāla.aśva.hasti.paṇyāḥ pañcāśat.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.17/ Dealers in gold, silver, diamonds, gems, pearls, coral, horses, and elephants — [pay] fifty percent tax.

children.text: KAZ05.2.18/ sūtra.vastra.tāmra.vṛtta.kaṃsa.gandha.bhaiṣajya.śīdhu.paṇyāś catvāriṃśat.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.18/ Dealers in thread, cloth, copper, brass, bell-metal, perfumes, medicines, and spirits — forty percent.

children.text: KAZ05.2.19/ dhānya.rasa.loha.paṇyāḥ śakaṭa.vyavahāriṇaś ca triṃśat.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.19/ Dealers in grain, liquids, and metals, and those using carts — thirty percent.

children.text: KAZ05.2.20/ kāca.vyavahāriṇo mahā.kāravaś ca viṃśati.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.20/ Dealers in glassware and large-scale traders — twenty percent.

children.text: KAZ05.2.21/ kṣudra.kāravo bandhakī.poṣakāś ca daśa.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.21/ Small-scale traders and brothel-keepers — ten percent.

children.text: KAZ05.2.22/ kāṣṭha.veṇu.pāṣāṇa.mṛd.bhāṇḍa.pakva.anna.harita.paṇyāḥ pañca.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.22/ Dealers in wood, bamboo, stone, earthen pots, cooked food, and vegetables — five percent.

children.text: KAZ05.2.23/ kuśīlavā rūpa.ājīvāś ca vetana.ardhaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.23/ Entertainers and courtesans should pay half their wages.

children.text: KAZ05.2.24/ hiraṇya.karaṃ karmaṇyān āhārayeyuḥ, na ca^eṣāṃ kaṃcid aparādhaṃ parihareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.24/ They should collect the gold tax from those capable of working, and should not excuse any of their offenses.

children.text: KAZ05.2.25/ te hy aparigṛhītam abhinīya vikrīṇīran //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.25/ For they would bring in and sell what has not been taxed.

children.text: KAZ05.2.26/ iti vyavahāriṣu praṇayaḥ //05.2.27/ kukkuṭa.sūkaram ardhaṃ dadyāt, kṣudra.paśavaḥ ṣaḍ.bhāgam, go.mahiṣa.aśvatara.khara.uṣṭrāś ca daśa.bhāgam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ05.2.26/ Thus [the emergency levy] on traders.
KAZ05.2.27/ [Owners of] poultry and pigs should give half; [owners of] small animals, a sixth; [owners of] cattle, buffaloes, mules, donkeys, and camels, a tenth.

children.text: KAZ05.2.28/ bandhakī.poṣakā rāja.preṣyābhiḥ parama.rūpa.yauvanābhiḥ kośaṃ saṃhareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.28/ Brothel-keepers, using royal female servants of supreme beauty and youth, should gather [wealth] for the treasury.

children.text: KAZ05.2.29/ iti yoni.poṣakeṣu praṇayaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.29/ Thus [the emergency levy] on brothel-keepers.

children.text: KAZ05.2.30/ sakṛd eva na dviḥ prayojyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.30/ [The emergency levy] should be imposed only once, not twice.

children.text: KAZ05.2.31/ tasya^akaraṇe vā samāhartā kāryam apadiśya paura.jānapadān bhikṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.31/ Or, failing that, the collector, citing an [emergency] cause, should solicit [contributions] from townspeople and countryfolk.

children.text: KAZ05.2.32/ yoga.puruṣāś ca^atra pūrvam atimātraṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.32/ And planted agents should be the first to give excessively [to set an example].

children.text: KAZ05.2.33/ etena pradeśena rājā paura.jānapadān bhikṣeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.33/ By this method, the king should solicit [contributions] from townspeople and countryfolk.

children.text: KAZ05.2.34/ kāpaṭikāś ca^enān alpaṃ prayacchataḥ kutsayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.34/ And undercover agents should publicly criticize those who give little.

children.text: KAZ05.2.35/ sārato vā hiraṇyam āḍhyān yāceta, yathā.upakāraṃ vā, sva.vaśā vā yad upahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.35/ Or he should request gold from the wealthy according to their capacity, or according to their [promised] contribution, or whatever they might voluntarily offer.

children.text: KAZ05.2.36/ sthānac.chatra.veṣṭana.vibhūṣāś ca^eṣāṃ hiraṇyena prayacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.36/ And their positions, titles, turbans, and decorations he should confer for gold.

children.text: KAZ05.2.37/ pāṣaṇḍa.saṃgha.dravyam aśrotriya.upabhogyaṃ deva.dravyaṃ vā kṛtya.karāḥ pretasya dagdha.gṛhasya vā haste nyastam ity upahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.37/ Or [agents should] bring in the property of sectarian communities — [saying it is] not to be enjoyed by non-Vedic scholars — or temple property, claiming it was entrusted to the hands of a deceased person or to a burned-down house.

children.text: KAZ05.2.38/ devatā.adhyakṣo durga.rāṣṭra.devatānāṃ yathā.svam ekasthaṃ kośaṃ kuryāt, tathaiva ca^upaharet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.38/ The superintendent of temples should consolidate the treasuries of the deities of the fort and countryside into a single fund, and should deposit [it] in the same way.

children.text: KAZ05.2.39/ daivata.caityaṃ siddha.puṇya.sthānam aupapādikaṃ vā rātrāv utthāpya yātrā.samājābhyām ājīvet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.39/ Or, by night, he should raise up [an image at] a divine shrine, an accomplished holy site, or a miraculous [site], and profit from processions and festivals.

children.text: KAZ05.2.40/ caitya.upavana.vṛkṣeṇa vā devatā.abhigamanam anārtava.puṣpa.phala.yuktena khyāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.40/ Or he should publicize a divine visitation at a sacred grove tree — [exhibiting it as] bearing flowers and fruits out of season.

children.text: KAZ05.2.41/ manuṣya.karaṃ vā vṛkṣe rakṣo.bhayaṃ prarūpayitvā siddha.vyañjanāḥ paura.jānapadānāṃ hiraṇyena pratikuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.41/ Or, proclaiming a spirit-danger at a tree with human tribute, agents in the guise of accomplished [ascetics] should collect gold from the townspeople and countryfolk as a countermeasure.

children.text: KAZ05.2.42/ suruṅgā.yukte vā kūpe nāgam aniyata.śiraskaṃ hiraṇya.upahāreṇa darśayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.42/ Or in a well connected to a tunnel, he should display a multi-headed serpent, [soliciting] offerings of gold.

children.text: KAZ05.2.43/ nāga.pratimāyām antaś.channāyāṃ caityac.chidre valmīkac.chidre vā sarpa.darśanam āhāreṇa pratibaddha.saṃjñaṃ kṛtvā śraddadhānānāṃ darśayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.43/ Or he should display to the faithful a serpent-sighting — at a hidden serpent-image, a shrine cavity, or an anthill opening — conditioned by [the serpent's] feeding signal; and make it visible.

children.text: KAZ05.2.44/ aśraddadhānānām ācamana.prokṣaṇeṣu rasam upacārya devatā.abhiśāpaṃ brūyāt, abhityaktaṃ vā daṃśayitvā //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.44/ To the skeptical, he should administer poison in their rinsing and sprinkling water and declare it a divine curse; or, having bitten one who is expendable [with a real snake].

children.text: KAZ05.2.45/ yoga.darśana.pratīkāreṇa vā kośa.abhisaṃharaṇaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.45/ Or through displays of magical demonstrations and countermeasures, he should collect [funds] for the treasury.

children.text: KAZ05.2.46/ vaidehaka.vyañjano vā prabhūta.paṇya.antevāsī vyavahareta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.46/ Or an agent in the guise of a merchant, with a large following and much merchandise, should conduct trade.

children.text: KAZ05.2.47/ sa yadā paṇya.mūlye nikṣepa.prayogair upacitaḥ syāt tadā^enaṃ rātrau moṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.47/ When he has accumulated [wealth] through the price of goods, deposits, and loans — then, by night, he should have him robbed.

children.text: KAZ05.2.48/ etena rūpa.darśakaḥ suvarṇa.kāraś ca vyākhyātau //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.48/ By this, the money-changer and the goldsmith are explained.

children.text: KAZ05.2.49/ vaidehaka.vyañjano vā prakhyāta.vyavahāraḥ prahavaṇa.nimittaṃ yācitakam avakrītakaṃ vā rūpya.suvarṇa.bhāṇḍam anekaṃ gṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.49/ Or an agent in the guise of a merchant, of established reputation, should collect much silver and gold vessels — either borrowed or under-priced — on the pretext of a festival.

children.text: KAZ05.2.50/ samāje vā sarva.paṇya.saṃdohena prabhūtaṃ hiraṇya.suvarṇam ṛṇaṃ gṛhṇīyāt, pratibhāṇḍa.mūlyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.50/ Or at a fair, he should borrow large amounts of gold and silver through the pooling of all merchandise, along with the value of counter-goods.

children.text: KAZ05.2.51/ tad ubhayaṃ rātrau moṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.51/ Both [the goods and the borrowed money] should be stolen by night.

children.text: KAZ05.2.52/ sādhvī.vyañjanābhiḥ strībhir dūṣyān unmādayitvā tāsām eva veśmasv abhigṛhya sarva.svāny āhareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.52/ Women in the guise of virtuous wives should infatuate those marked [for confiscation], and having seized [them] at their own houses, should carry off all their property.

children.text: KAZ05.2.53/ dūṣya.kulyānāṃ vā vivāde pratyutpanne rasadāḥ praṇihitā rasaṃ dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.53/ Or when a dispute arises among the kinsmen of the marked [person], planted poison-agents should administer poison.

children.text: KAZ05.2.54/ tena doṣeṇa^itare paryādātavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.54/ On account of that offense, the others should be made to pay.

children.text: KAZ05.2.55/ dūṣyam abhityakto vā śraddheya.apadeśaṃ paṇyaṃ hiraṇya.nikṣepam ṛṇa.prayogaṃ dāyaṃ vā yāceta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.55/ Or an [agent], having approached the marked [person] under an expendable pretext, should demand goods on a credible claim — as merchandise, gold deposit, loan, or inheritance.

children.text: KAZ05.2.56/ dāsa.śabdena vā dūṣyam ālambeta, bhāryām asya snuṣāṃ duhitaraṃ vā dāsī.śabdena bhāryā.śabdena vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.56/ Or he should seize the marked [person] on the pretext [that he is] a slave, or his wife, daughter-in-law, or daughter on the pretext [that she is] a slave-woman or [his] wife.

children.text: KAZ05.2.57/ taṃ dūṣya.gṛha.pratidvāri rātrāv upaśayānam anyatra vā vasantaṃ tīkṣṇo hatvā brūyāt "hato^ayam artha.kāmukaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.57/ That [marked person], sleeping at night at the doorstep of the marked [person's] house or lodging elsewhere — a firebrand agent should kill him and say: 'This fortune-seeker has been slain.'

children.text: KAZ05.2.58/ tena doṣeṇa^itare paryādātavyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.58/ On account of that offense, the others should be made to pay.

children.text: KAZ05.2.59/ siddha.vyañjano vā dūṣyaṃ jambhaka.vidyābhiḥ pralobhayitvā brūyāt "akṣaya.hiraṇyaṃ rāja.dvārikaṃ strī.hṛdayam ari.vyādhi.karam āyuṣyaṃ putrīyaṃ vā karma jānāmi" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.59/ Or an agent in the guise of an accomplished [ascetic] should entice the marked [person] with conjuring arts and say: 'I know the art of inexhaustible gold, of royal access, of winning women's hearts, of inflicting disease on enemies, of longevity, or of [obtaining] sons.'

children.text: KAZ05.2.60/ pratipannaṃ caitya.sthāne rātrau prabhūta.surā.māṃsa.gandham upahāraṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.60/ When [the target] has accepted, he should have him make at night, at a sacred site, an offering with abundant liquor, meat, and perfume.

children.text: KAZ05.2.61/ eka.rūpaṃ ca^atra hiraṇyaṃ pūrva.nikhātaṃ preta.aṅgaṃ preta.śiśur vā yatra nihitaḥ syāt, tato hiraṇyam asya darśayed "atyalpam" iti ca brūyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.61/ And there, at [the site where] identical gold has been previously buried, along with a corpse's limb or a dead infant, he should show the gold to him and say: 'Too little.'

children.text: KAZ05.2.62/ "prabhūta.hiraṇya.hetoḥ punar upahāraḥ kartavya iti svayam eva^etena hiraṇyena śvo.bhūte prabhūtam aupahārikaṃ krīṇīhi" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.62/ 'For the sake of more gold, another offering must be made; with this very gold, buy the offering materials by tomorrow yourself.'

children.text: KAZ05.2.63/ sa tena hiraṇyena^aupahārika.kraye gṛhyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.63/ He should be arrested while purchasing the offering materials with that gold.

children.text: KAZ05.2.64/ mātṛ.vyañjanayā vā "putro me tvayā hataḥ" ity avakupitā syāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.64/ Or a woman in the guise of a mother should rage at him: 'My son has been killed by you.'

children.text: KAZ05.2.65/ saṃsiddham eva^asya rātri.yāge vana.yāge vana.krīḍāyāṃ vā pravṛttāyāṃ tīkṣṇā viśasya^abhityaktam atinayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.65/ Or at the very completion [of the ritual], when the night-sacrifice, forest-sacrifice, or forest-amusement has begun, firebrand agents should kill the expendable [agent] and lead away [the target].

children.text: KAZ05.2.66/ dūṣyasya vā bhṛtaka.vyañjano vetana.hiraṇye kūṭa.rūpaṃ prakṣipya prarūpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.66/ Or an agent in the guise of a servant of the marked [person] should plant counterfeit coins among the wage-money and then expose them.

children.text: KAZ05.2.67/ karma.kara.vyañjano vā gṛhe karma kurvāṇaḥ stena.kūṭa.rūpa.kāraka.upakaraṇam upanidadhyāt, cikitsaka.vyañjano vā garam agada.apadeśena //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.67/ Or an agent in the guise of a laborer, working in the house, should deposit tools for theft and counterfeiting; or one in the guise of a physician [should deposit] poison under the pretext of an antidote.

children.text: KAZ05.2.68/ pratyāsanno vā dūṣyasya sattrī praṇihitam abhiṣeka.bhāṇḍam amitra.śāsanaṃ ca kāpaṭika.mukhena^ācakṣīta, kāraṇaṃ ca brūyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.68/ Or a classmate-spy near the marked [person] should, through an undercover agent, reveal hidden anointing vessels and an enemy's dispatch, and explain the [incriminating] reason.

children.text: KAZ05.2.69/ evaṃ dūṣyeṣv adhārmikeṣu ca varteta, na^itareṣu //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.2.69/ Thus [the king] should act against the marked [for confiscation] and the unrighteous, but not against others.

children.text:
KAZ05.2.70ab/ pakvaṃ pakvam iva^ārāmāt phalaṃ rājyād avāpnuyāt /
KAZ05.2.70cd/ ātmac.cheda.bhayād āmaṃ varjayet kopa.kārakam //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ05.2.70ab/ He should pluck from the kingdom only ripe fruit, as from an orchard;
KAZ05.2.70cd/ he should avoid the unripe that breeds anger, for fear of cutting [the tree] itself.

children.text:
(ṣalaries of state servants)
KAZ05.3.01/ durga.jana.pada.śaktyā bhṛtya.karma samudaya.pādena sthāpayet, kārya.sādhana.sahena vā bhṛtya.lābhena //
children.translated_text:
(Salaries of state servants)
KAZ05.3.01/ According to the capacity of the fort and countryside, he should fix the maintenance of servants at one-quarter of the total revenue, or at whatever proportion of servant-expenditure is [needed for] accomplishing the task.

children.text: KAZ05.3.02/ śarīram avekṣeta, na dharma.arthau pīḍayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.02/ He should consider the body [of the state]; he should not oppress <s>dharma</s> or <s>artha</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.3.03/ ṛtvig.ācārya.mantri.purohita.senā.pati.yuva.rāja.rāja.mātṛ.rāja.mahiṣyo^aṣṭa.catvāriṃśat.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.03/ The sacrificial priest, the teacher, the minister, the chaplain, the commander-in-chief, the crown prince, the queen-mother, and the chief queen — [each receives] forty-eight thousand [<s>paṇas</s>].

children.text: KAZ05.3.04/ etāvatā bharaṇena^anāspadyatvam akopakaṃ ca^eṣāṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.04/ With this level of maintenance, they have no ground [for dissatisfaction] and no cause for rebellion.

children.text: KAZ05.3.05/ dauvārika.antar.vaṃśika.praśāstṛ.samāhartṛ.saṃnidhātāraś catur.viṃśati.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.05/ The chief of the palace guard, the chief of the inner apartments, the chief justice, the collector, and the treasurer — twenty-four thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.06/ etāvatā karmaṇyā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.06/ With this [amount], they become effective workers.

children.text: KAZ05.3.07/ kumāra.kumāra.mātṛ.nāyaka.paura.vyāvahārika.kārmāntika.mantri.pariṣad.rāṣṭra.anta.pālāś ca dvādaśa.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.07/ Princes, mothers of princes, the <s>nāyaka</s>, the city superintendent, the law officer, the superintendent of manufactures, the council of ministers, and the frontier commanders — twelve thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.08/ svāmi.paribandha.bala.sahāyā hy etāvatā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.08/ For with this [amount], they have the strength and support [tied to] the master.

children.text: KAZ05.3.09/ śreṇī.mukhyā hasty.aśva.ratha.mukhyāḥ pradeṣṭāraś ca^aṣṭa.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.09/ Guild-chiefs, heads of elephant, horse, and chariot [divisions], and inspectors — eight thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.10/ sva.varga.anukarṣiṇo hy etāvatā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.10/ For with this [amount], they attract their own groups [to the king's service].

children.text: KAZ05.3.11/ patty.aśva.ratha.hasty.adhyakṣā dravya.hasti.vana.pālāś ca catuḥ.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.11/ Superintendents of infantry, horses, chariots, and elephants, and guardians of forests, mines, and elephant forests — four thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.12/ rathika.anīkastha.cikitsaka.aśva.damaka.vardhakayo yoni.poṣakāś ca dvi.sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.12/ Charioteers, formation-keepers, physicians, horse-trainers, carpenters, and brothel-keepers — two thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.13/ kārtāntika.naimittika.mauhūrtika.paurāṇika.sūta.māgadhāḥ purohita.puruṣāḥ sarva.adhyakṣāś ca sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.13/ Fortune-tellers, diviners, astrologers, reciters of <s>Purāṇas</s>, bards, panegyrists, chaplain's assistants, and all superintendents — one thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.14/ śilpavantaḥ pādātāḥ saṃkhyāyaka.lekhaka.ādi.vargaś ca pañca.śatāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.14/ Skilled foot-soldiers, and the group of accountants, scribes, and the like — five hundred.

children.text: KAZ05.3.15/ kuśīlavās tv ardha.tṛtīya.śatāḥ, dvi.guṇa.vetanāś ca^eṣāṃ tūrya.karāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.15/ Entertainers, however — two hundred and fifty; and those among them who play musical instruments, double wages.

children.text: KAZ05.3.16/ kāru.śilpino viṃśati.śatikāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.16/ Artisans and craftsmen — one hundred and twenty.

children.text: KAZ05.3.17/ catuṣpada.dvipada.paricāraka.pārikarmika.aupasthāyika.pālaka.viṣṭi.bandhakāḥ ṣaṣṭi.vetanāḥ, ārya.yukta.ārohaka.māṇavaka.śaila.khanakāḥ sarva.upasthāyinaś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ05.3.17/ Attendants of quadrupeds and bipeds, personal servants, domestic workers, and keepers, those on forced labor, and bonded workers — sixty in wages; and also noble-born riders, young trainees, rock-cutters, and all general attendants.

children.text: KAZ05.3.18/ ācāryā vidyāvantaś ca pūjā.vetanāni yathā.arhaṃ labheran pañca.śata.avaraṃ sahasra.param //
children.translated_text: Teachers and learned persons should receive honoraria and wages according to merit, ranging from a minimum of five hundred to a maximum of one thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.19/ daśa.paṇiko yojane dūto madhyamaḥ, daśa.uttare dvi.guṇa.vetana ā.yojana.śatād iti //
children.translated_text: A middle-level messenger receives ten <s>paṇas</s> per <s>yojana</s>; with increases of ten [<s>paṇas</s>], the wages double, up to one hundred <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.3.20/ samāna.vidyebhyas tri.guṇa.vetano rājā rāja.sūya.ādiṣu kratuṣu //
children.translated_text: The king [receives] triple the wages [of those with] equal learning, at <s>Rājasūya</s> and other sacrifices.

children.text: KAZ05.3.21/ rājñaḥ sārathiḥ sāhasraḥ //
children.translated_text: The king's charioteer [receives] one thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.22/ kāpaṭika.udāsthita.gṛha.patika.vaidehaka.tāpasa.vyañjanāḥ sāhasrāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those disguised as fraudulent ascetics, spies posing as householders, traders, and ascetics [receive] one thousand.

children.text: KAZ05.3.23/ grāma.bhṛtaka.sattri.tīkṣṇa.rasada.bhikṣukyaḥ pañca.śatāḥ //
children.translated_text: Village agents, stationary spies, firebrand agents, poison-agents, and mendicant female spies [receive] five hundred.

children.text: KAZ05.3.24/ cāra.saṃcāriṇo^ardha.tṛtīya.śatāḥ, prayāsa.vṛddha.vetanā vā //
children.translated_text: Roving spies [receive] two hundred and fifty, or wages increasing with effort.

children.text: KAZ05.3.25/ śata.varga.sahasra.vargāṇām adhyakṣā bhakta.vetana.lābham ādeśaṃ vikṣepaṃ ca kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Superintendents of groups of a hundred and groups of a thousand should arrange the allocation, assignment, and disbursement of food-rations and wages.

children.text: KAZ05.3.26/ avikṣepo rāja.parigraha.durga.rāṣṭra.rakṣa.avekṣaṇeṣu ca //
children.translated_text: There should be no disbursement-delay in [matters concerning] the royal household, the fort, the countryside's defense, and surveillance.

children.text: KAZ05.3.27/ nitya.mukhyāḥ syur aneka.mukhyāś ca //
children.translated_text: There should be permanent heads and also multiple [rotating] heads.

children.text: KAZ05.3.28/ karmasu mṛtānāṃ putra.dārā bhakta.vetanaṃ labheran //
children.translated_text: For those who die in service, their sons and wives should receive the food-rations and wages.

children.text: KAZ05.3.29/ bāla.vṛddha.vyādhitāś ca^eṣām anugrāhyāḥ //
children.translated_text: The young, the aged, and the sick among them should be supported.

children.text: KAZ05.3.30/ preta.vyādhita.sūtikā.kṛtyeṣu ca^eṣām artha.māna.karma kuryāt //
children.translated_text: For funerary, sickness, and childbirth rites, he should perform acts of monetary honor for them.

children.text: KAZ05.3.31/ alpa.kośaḥ kupya.paśu.kṣetrāṇi dadyāt, alpaṃ ca hiraṇyam //
children.translated_text: A king with a small treasury should give commodities, cattle, and fields, and [only] a small amount of gold.

children.text: KAZ05.3.32/ śūnyaṃ vā niveśayitum abhyutthito hiraṇyam eva dadyāt, na grāmaṃ grāma.saṃjāta.vyavahāra.sthāpana.artham //
children.translated_text: Or, one who has set out to settle an uninhabited [area] should give only gold, not a village — [this is] for the purpose of establishing [proper] administration of village-generated transactions.

children.text: KAZ05.3.33/ etena bhṛtānām abhṛtānāṃ ca vidyā.karmabhyāṃ bhakta.vetana.viśeṣaṃ ca kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Thus he should establish differentials in food-rations and wages based on knowledge and skill for both the salaried and the unsalaried.

children.text: KAZ05.3.34/ ṣaṣṭi.vetanasya^āḍhakaṃ kṛtvā hiraṇya.anurūpaṃ bhaktaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Making one <s>āḍhaka</s> [of grain] the basis for a salary of sixty [<s>paṇas</s>], he should set the food-ration proportionate to the monetary [salary].

children.text: KAZ05.3.35/ patty.aśva.ratha.dvipāḥ sūrya.udaye bahiḥ saṃdhi.divasa.varjaṃ śilpa.yogyāḥ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Infantry, cavalry, charioteers, and elephant-riders should practice their military skills [exercises] outside at sunrise, excluding conjunction-days.

children.text: KAZ05.3.36/ teṣu rājā nitya.yuktaḥ syāt, abhīkṣṇaṃ ca^eṣāṃ śilpa.darśanaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: The king should be constantly attentive to them, and should frequently inspect their military skills.

children.text: KAZ05.3.37/ kṛta.nara.indra.aṅkaṃ śastra.āvaraṇam āyudha.agāraṃ praveśayet //
children.translated_text: Weapons and armor bearing the royal stamp should be deposited in the armory.

children.text: KAZ05.3.38/ aśastrāś careyuḥ, anyatra mudrā.anujñātāt //
children.translated_text: People should go about without weapons, except those authorized by [official] seal.

children.text: KAZ05.3.39/ naṣṭaṃ.vinaṣṭaṃ vā dvi.guṇaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: For [weapons] lost or destroyed, one should pay double [the value].

children.text: KAZ05.3.40/ vidhvasta.gaṇanāṃ ca kuryāt //
children.translated_text: And he should maintain a register of [military] losses.

children.text: KAZ05.3.41/ sārthikānāṃ śastra.āvaraṇam anta.pālā gṛhṇīyuḥ, samudram avacārayeyur vā //
children.translated_text: The border-guards should collect the weapons and armor of merchants, or have them deposited at the gate.

children.text: KAZ05.3.42/ yātrām abhyutthito vā senām udyojayet //
children.translated_text: Or, when about to set out on a military expedition, he should mobilize the army.

children.text: KAZ05.3.43/ tato vaidehaka.vyañjanāḥ sarva.paṇyāny āyudhīyebhyo yātrā.kāle dvi.guṇa.pratyādeyāni dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then agents disguised as traders should give all kinds of merchandise to military personnel during the campaign period, to be repaid at double [the price].

children.text: KAZ05.3.44/ evaṃ rāja.paṇya.yoga.vikrayo vetana.pratyādānaṃ ca bhavati //
children.translated_text: Thus occurs the sale of royal merchandise through [military] employment and the recovery of wages.

children.text: KAZ05.3.45/ evam avekṣita.āya.vyayaḥ kośa.daṇḍa.vyasanaṃ na^avāpnoti //
children.translated_text: Thus, one who monitors income and expenditure does not fall into the calamity of [depleting] the treasury and the army.

children.text: KAZ05.3.46/ iti bhakta.vetana.vikalpaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the system of differentials in food-rations and wages.

children.text:
KAZ05.3.47ab/ sattriṇaś ca^āyudhīyānāṃ veśyāḥ kāru.kuśīlavāḥ /
KAZ05.3.47cd/ daṇḍa.vṛddhāś ca jānīyuḥ śauca.aśaucam atandritāḥ //E
children.translated_text: Stationary spies, military personnel, courtesans, artisans, entertainers, and veterans of the penal system should diligently ascertain [people's] integrity and corruption.

children.text:
(Proper conduct for a dependant)
KAZ05.4.01/ loka.yātrāvid rājānam ātma.dravya.prakṛti.saṃpannaṃ priya.hita.dvāreṇa^āśrayeta //
children.translated_text:
(Proper conduct for a dependant)
One who understands the ways of the world should take shelter with a king who is endowed with personal qualities, wealth, and [good] subjects, through the gateway of what is dear and beneficial.

children.text: KAZ05.4.02/ yaṃ vā manyeta "yathā^aham āśraya.īpsur evam asau vinaya.īpsur ābhigāmika.guṇa.yuktaḥ" iti, dravya.prakṛti.hīnam apy enam āśrayeta, na tv eva^anātma.saṃpannam //
children.translated_text: Or, if one thinks: 'Just as I desire a patron, so does he desire a disciplined [servant] possessed of qualities that inspire confidence' — he should serve even one lacking in wealth and subjects, but never one lacking in self-control.

children.text: KAZ05.4.03/ anātmavā hi nīti.śāstra.dveṣād anarthya.saṃyogād vā prāpya^api mahad aiśvaryaṃ na bhavati //
children.translated_text: For one without self-control, either from hatred of political science or from association with the unworthy, does not endure even after attaining great sovereignty.

children.text: KAZ05.4.04/ ātmavati labdha.avakāśaḥ śāstra.anuyogaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Having found an opening with a self-controlled [king], he should offer advice according to [political] science.

children.text: KAZ05.4.05/ avisaṃvādādd hi sthāna.sthairyam avāpnoti //
children.translated_text: For through non-deception, one attains security of position.

children.text: KAZ05.4.06/ mati.karmasu pṛṣṭhas tadātve ca^āyatyāṃ ca dharma.artha.saṃyuktaṃ samarthaṃ pravīṇavad apariṣad.bhīruḥ kathayet //
children.translated_text: When consulted on matters of policy and action — both for the present and for the future — he should speak what is connected with <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>, competently and expertly, without fear of the assembly.

children.text: KAZ05.4.07/ īpsitaḥ paṇeta "dharma.artha.anuyogam aviśiṣṭeṣu balavat.saṃyukteṣu daṇḍa.dhāraṇaṃ mat.saṃyoge tadātve ca daṇḍa.dhāraṇam iti na kuryāḥ, pakṣaṃ vṛttiṃ guhyaṃ ca me na^upahanyāḥ, saṃjñayā ca tvāṃ kāma.krodha.daṇḍaneṣu vārayeyam" iti //
children.translated_text: If favored, he should stipulate: 'Do not [impose] punishment in [matters of] <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> inquiry upon those not distinguished [in rank] who are allied with the powerful; [and do not impose] punishment in association with me in the present. Do not undermine my faction, my livelihood, or my secrets; and by a signal, I shall restrain you in [matters of] desire, anger, and punishment.'

children.text: KAZ05.4.08/ ādiṣṭaḥ pradiṣṭāyāṃ bhūmāv anujñātaḥ praviśet, upaviśec ca pārśvataḥ saṃnikṛṣṭa.viprakṛṣṭaḥ para.āsanam //
children.translated_text: When commanded, he should enter the designated place with permission, and sit beside [the king], at a near or far [distance], on a separate seat.

children.text: KAZ05.4.09/ vigṛhya kathanam asabhyam apratyakṣam aśraddheyam anṛtaṃ ca vākyam uccair anarmaṇi hāsaṃ vāta.ṣṭhīvane ca śabdavatī na kuryāt //
children.translated_text: He should not make disputatious, impolite, indirect, unbelievable, or false statements, nor laugh loudly except in jest, nor make noise while expelling wind or spitting.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.10/ mithaḥ kathanam anyena, jana.vāde dvandva.kathanam, rājño veṣam uddhata.kuhakānāṃ ca, ratna.atiśaya.prakāśa.abhyarthanam, eka.akṣy.oṣṭha.nirbhogaṃ bhrukuṭī.karma vākya.avakṣepaṇaṃ ca bruvati, balavat saṃyukta.virodham, strībhiḥ strī.darśibhiḥ sāmanta.dūtair dveṣya.pakṣa.avakṣiptān arthyaiś ca pratisaṃsargam eka.artha.caryāṃ saṃghātaṃ ca varjayet
//
children.translated_text: He should avoid: private conversation with another [in the king's presence]; speaking in pairs during public discourse; [mimicking] the king's attire or [the behavior of] the arrogant and deceitful; requesting the display of extraordinary gems; winking with one eye, pursing the lips, frowning, or interrupting while [the king] speaks; opposition to the powerful or those allied [with them]; association with women, those who display women, envoys of neighboring kings, members of a hostile faction, or petitioners; pursuing the same objective [as another courtier]; and forming factions.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.11ab/ ahīna.kālaṃ rāja.arthaṃ sva.arthaṃ priya.hitaiḥ saha /
KAZ05.4.11cd/ para.arthaṃ deśa.kāle ca brūyād dharma.artha.saṃhitam //
children.translated_text: He should speak of the king's business at the proper time, his own business with those who are dear and helpful, and others' business at the [appropriate] place and time — [all] connected with <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.12ab/ pṛṣṭaḥ priya.hitaṃ brūyān na brūyād ahitaṃ priyam /
KAZ05.4.12cd/ apriyaṃ vā hitaṃ brūyāt^śṛṇvato^anumato mithaḥ //
children.translated_text: When asked, he should speak what is dear and beneficial; he should not say what is pleasant but harmful. Or he should say what is unpleasant but beneficial, privately and with the other's consent.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.13ab/ tūṣṇīṃ vā prativākye syād veṣya.ādīṃś ca na varṇayet /
KAZ05.4.13cd/ apriyā api dakṣāḥ syus tad.bhāvād ye bahiṣ.kṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: Or he should remain silent rather than give a [harmful] reply. And he should not describe courtesans and the like. Even those who are competent but disagreeable may be dismissed because of their nature.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.14ab/ anarthyāś ca priyā dṛṣṭāś citta.jñāna.anuvartinaḥ /
KAZ05.4.14cd/ abhihāsyeṣv abhihased ghora.hāsāṃś ca varjayet //E
KAZ05.4.15ab/ parāt saṃkrāmayed ghoraṃ na ca ghoraṃ pare vadet /
KAZ05.4.15cd/ titikṣeta^ātmanaś caiva kṣamāvān pṛthivī.samaḥ //
children.translated_text:
And those who are worthless but pleasant are seen [to succeed] by following [the king's] moods.
One should laugh at what is meant to be laughed at, and avoid harsh laughter. One should deflect harshness from others [onto oneself] and not speak harshly of others. One should endure [affronts] to oneself, forbearing and earth-like.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.16ab/ ātma.rakṣā hi satataṃ pūrvaṃ kāryā vijānatā /
KAZ05.4.16cd/ agnāv iva hi saṃproktā vṛttī rājā^upajīvinām //
children.translated_text: For a wise person should always first ensure his own safety. For the livelihood of those who depend on a king is described as being like [depending on] fire.

children.text:
KAZ05.4.17ab/ eka.deśaṃ dahed agniḥ śarīraṃ vā paraṃ gataḥ /
KAZ05.4.17cd/ sa-putra.dāraṃ rājā tu ghātayed ardhayeta vā //E
children.translated_text: Fire might burn one part [of the body] or, going further, the [whole] body; but a king can destroy or ruin [one] together with sons and wife.

children.text:
(Proper behaviour for a courtier)
KAZ05.5.01/ niyuktaḥ karmasu vyaya.viśuddham udayaṃ darśayet //
children.translated_text:
(Proper behaviour for a courtier)
When appointed to duties, he should show a net profit after deducting expenses.

children.text: KAZ05.5.02/ ābhyantaraṃ bāhyaṃ guhyaṃ prakāśyam ātyayikam upekṣitavyaṃ vā kāryaṃ "idam evam" iti viśeṣayec ca //
children.translated_text: Whether the task is internal, external, secret, public, urgent, or to be overlooked — he should distinguish [each by saying]: 'This is thus.'

children.text: KAZ05.5.03/ mṛgayā.dyūta.madya.strīṣu prasaktaṃ na^enam anuvarteta praśaṃsābhiḥ //
children.translated_text: If [the king] is addicted to hunting, gambling, drinking, or women, he should not follow him with praises.

children.text: KAZ05.5.04/ āsannaś ca^asya vyasana.upaghāte prayateta, para.upajāpa.atisaṃdhāna.upadhibhyaś ca rakṣet //
children.translated_text: And being close [to the king], he should strive to mitigate [the king's] vices, and protect him from the enemy's subversion, fraud, and trickery.

children.text: KAZ05.5.05/ iṅgita.ākārau ca^asya lakṣayet //
children.translated_text: And he should observe [the king's] gestures and expressions.

children.text: KAZ05.5.06/ kāma.dveṣa.harṣa.dainya.vyavasāya.bhaya.dvandva.viparyāsam iṅgita.ākārābhyāṃ hi mantra.saṃvaraṇa.artham ācarati prājñaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a wise person reads [the king's] desire, hatred, joy, despondency, resolve, fear, and their reversals through gestures and expressions, in order to conceal [his awareness of] the [king's] counsel.

children.text:
KAZ05.5.07/ darśane prasīdati, vākyaṃ pratigṛhṇāti, āsanaṃ dadāti, vivikto darśayate, śaṅkā.sthāne na^atiśaṅkate, kathāyāṃ ramate, parijñāpyeṣv avekṣate, pathyam uktaṃ sahate, smayamāno niyuṅkte, hastena spṛśati, ślāghye na^upahasati, parokṣaṃ guṇaṃ bravīti, bhakṣyeṣu smarati, saha vihāraṃ yāti, vyasane^abhyupapadyate, tad.bhaktīn pūjayati, guhyam ācaṣṭe,
mānaṃ vardhayati, arthaṃ karoti, anarthaṃ pratihanti - iti tuṣṭa.jñānam //
children.translated_text: He is pleased upon seeing [you]; he accepts your words; he offers a seat; he shows [you the matter] in private; he does not over-suspect in suspicious situations; he takes pleasure in conversation; he takes notice in matters to be communicated; he tolerates wholesome [but unpleasant] advice; he assigns [tasks] with a smile; he touches [you] with his hand; he does not mock what is praiseworthy; he speaks of your merits behind your back; he remembers [you] at meals; he goes together on recreational outings; he comes to your aid in adversity; he honors those devoted to you; he confides secrets; he increases [your] honor; he promotes [your] interests; he thwarts [your] misfortunes — this is the knowledge of [the king's] satisfaction.

children.text: KAZ05.5.08/ etad eva viparītam atuṣṭasya, bhūyaś ca vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: The opposite of all this [indicates] dissatisfaction, and more we shall state.

children.text:
KAZ05.5.09/ saṃdarśane kopaḥ, vākyasya^aśravaṇa.pratiṣedhau, āsana.cakṣuṣor adānam, varṇa.svara.bhedaḥ, eka.akṣi.bhrukuṭy.oṣṭha.nirbhogaḥ, sveda.śvāsa.smitānām asthāna.utpattiḥ, para.mantraṇam, akasmād.vrajanam, vardhanam anyasya, bhūmi.gātra.vilekhanam, anyasya^upatodanam, vidyā.varṇa.deśa.kutsā, sama.doṣa.nindā, pratidoṣa.nindā, pratiloma.stavaḥ,
sukṛta.anavekṣaṇam, duṣkṛta.anukīrtanam, pṛṣṭha.avadhānam, atityāgaḥ, mithyā.abhibhāṣaṇam, rāja.darśināṃ ca tad.vṛtta.anyatvam //
children.translated_text: Anger upon seeing [you]; refusal to listen to or prohibition of [your] speech; not offering a seat or [meeting your] gaze; change of complexion and voice; winking with one eye, frowning, or pursing the lips; sweating, sighing, or smiling at inappropriate moments; conversing with others; suddenly departing; promoting another; scratching the ground or [his own] body; poking at another; disparaging [your] learning, character, or homeland; condemning for a common fault; condemning for every fault; praising in a contrary manner; not acknowledging good deeds; recounting misdeeds; listening from behind [a screen]; excessive generosity [to others, not you]; speaking falsely; and those who attend the king [reporting that] his behavior [toward you] has changed.

children.text: KAZ05.5.10/ vṛtti.vikāraṃ ca^avekṣeta^apy amānuṣāṇām //
children.translated_text: And one should observe behavioral changes even in non-human [beings, as omens].

children.text: KAZ05.5.11/ "ayam uccaiḥ siñcati" iti kātyāyanaḥ pravavrāja, "krauñco^apasavyam" iti kaṇiṅko bhāradvājaḥ, "tṛṇam" iti dīrghaś cārāyaṇaḥ, "śītā śāṭī" iti ghoṭa.mukhaḥ, "hastī pratyaukṣīt" iti kiñjalkaḥ, "ratha.aśvaṃ prāśaṃsīt" iti piśunaḥ, prati.ravaṇe śunaḥ piśuna.putraḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This one urinates high' — thus <s>Kātyāyana</s> went into exile. 'The <s>krauñca</s> [bird passed] to the left' — thus <s>Kaṇiṅka Bhāradvāja</s>. '[He pointed to] a blade of grass' — thus <s>Dīrgha Cārāyaṇa</s>. 'The garment is cold' — thus <s>Ghoṭamukha</s>. 'The elephant sprinkled counter-wise' — thus <s>Kiñjalka</s>. '[The king] praised the chariot-horse' — thus <s>Piśuna</s>. [And another understood] from the echo of dogs — <s>Piśunaputra</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.5.12/ artha.māna.avakṣepe ca parityāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: And upon diminution of wealth or honor, [one should consider] departure.

children.text: KAZ05.5.13/ svāmi.śīlam ātmanaś ca kilbiṣam upalabhya vā pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: Or, recognizing the master's disposition and one's own fault, one should make amends.

children.text: KAZ05.5.14/ mitram upakṛṣṭaṃ vā^asya gacchet //
children.translated_text: Or one should go to a friend of [the king's] who has been promoted.

children.text:
KAZ05.5.15ab/ tatrastho doṣa.nirghātaṃ mitrair bhartari ca^ācaret /
KAZ05.5.15cd/ tato bhartari jīve vā mṛte vā punar āvrajet //E
children.translated_text: Stationed there, he should work to eliminate [his] faults through friends and with the master. Then, whether the master lives or dies, he should return.

children.text:
(Continuance of the kingdom)
(Continuous sovereignty)
KAZ05.6.01/ rāja.vyasanam evam amātyaḥ pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text:
(Continuance of the kingdom)
(Continuous sovereignty)
Thus should a minister counteract the king's distress.

children.text: KAZ05.6.02/ prāg eva maraṇa.ābādha.bhayād rājñaḥ priya.hita.upagraheṇa māsa.dvi.māsa.antaraṃ darśanaṃ sthāpayed "deśa.pīḍā.apaham amitra.apaham āyuṣyaṃ putrīyaṃ vā karma rājā sādhayati" ity apadeśena //
children.translated_text: Well in advance, out of fear of the king's illness or death, through solicitation of what is dear and beneficial, he should arrange audiences at intervals of one or two months, using the pretext: 'The king is conducting a rite to avert a regional calamity, to repel an enemy, to promote longevity, or for the sake of a son.'

children.text: KAZ05.6.03/ rāja.vyañjanam arūpa.velāyāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ darśayet, mitra.amitra.dūtānāṃ ca //
children.translated_text: He should display the royal insignia [to the public] at an unrecognizable time [i.e., when the king's [true condition] cannot be observed], and to envoys of friends and enemies.

children.text: KAZ05.6.04/ taiś ca yathā.ucitāṃ saṃbhāṣām amātya.mukho gacchet //
children.translated_text: And through those [insignia], the minister should conduct conversations as customary, speaking on behalf of the king.

children.text: KAZ05.6.05/ dauvārika.antar.vaṃśika.mukhaś ca yathā.uktaṃ rāja.praṇidhim anuvartayet //
children.translated_text: And through the door-keeper and the palace-guard as intermediaries, he should continue the royal administration as established.

children.text: KAZ05.6.06/ apakāriṣu ca heḍaṃ prasādaṃ vā prakṛti.kāntaṃ darśayet, prasādam eva^upakāriṣu //
children.translated_text: Toward those who have done harm, he should show displeasure or favor in a manner pleasing to the subjects; toward those who have done service, only favor.

children.text: KAZ05.6.07/ āpta.puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitau durga.pratyantasthau vā kośa.daṇḍāv ekasthau kārayet, kulya.kumāra.mukhyāṃś ca^anya.apadeśena //
children.translated_text: He should keep the treasury and the army united and in one place, supervised by trusted men, stationed in the fort or at the frontier; and [he should do the same with] princes and clan-chiefs under some other pretext.

children.text: KAZ05.6.08/ yaś ca mukhyaḥ pakṣavān durga.aṭavīstho vā vaiguṇyaṃ bhajeta tam upagrāhayet //
children.translated_text: Any prominent person who has a faction and is stationed in a fort or forest region, and who might turn disloyal — him he should win over.

children.text: KAZ05.6.09/ bahv.ābādhaṃ vā yātrāṃ preṣayet, mitra.kulaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Or he should send him on a dangerous military campaign, or to the house of an ally.

children.text: KAZ05.6.10/ yasmāc ca sāmantād ābādhaṃ paśyet tam utsava.vivāha.hasti.bandhana.aśva.paṇya.bhūmi.pradāna.apadeśena^avagrāhayet, sva.mitreṇa vā //
children.translated_text: And whichever neighboring king he perceives as a threat — him he should detain under the pretext of a festival, wedding, elephant-capture, horse-trading, or land-grant, or through [the intervention of] his own ally.

children.text: KAZ05.6.11/ tataḥ saṃdhim adūṣyaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Then he should establish a [peace] treaty that is not prejudicial.

children.text: KAZ05.6.12/ āṭavika.amitrair vā vairaṃ grāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or he should create enmity between [the prince] and forest-dwelling enemies.

children.text: KAZ05.6.13/ tat.kulīnam aparuddhaṃ vā bhūṃy.eka.deśena^upagrāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or he should win over a member of the [royal] family or one not shut out [from succession] with a portion of territory.

children.text: KAZ05.6.14/ kulya.kumāra.mukhya.upagrahaṃ kṛtvā vā kumāram abhiṣiktam eva darśayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having gained the support of a family prince, a chief, he should present the prince already consecrated.

children.text: KAZ05.6.15/ dāṇḍa.karmikavad vā rājya.kaṇṭakān uddhṛtya rājyaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Or, like a staff-wielding enforcer, having removed the thorns of the kingdom, he should administer the realm.

children.text: KAZ05.6.16/ yadi vā kaścin mukhyaḥ sāmanta.ādīnām anyatamaḥ kopaṃ bhajeta taṃ "ehi, rājānaṃ tvā kariṣyāmi" ity āvāhayitvā ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or, if some chief — any one of the feudatories and the like — should become hostile, having invited him with 'Come, I will make you king,' he should have him killed.

children.text: KAZ05.6.17/ āpat.pratīkāreṇa vā sādhayet //
children.translated_text: Or he should accomplish [his aim] by counteracting the emergency.

children.text: KAZ05.6.18/ yuva.rāje vā krameṇa rājya.bhāram āropya rāja.vyasanaṃ khyāpayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having gradually transferred the burden of the kingdom to the crown prince, he should announce the king's death.

children.text: KAZ05.6.19/ para.bhūmau rāja.vyasane mitreṇa^amitra.vyañjanena śatroḥ saṃdhim avasthāpya^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: If the king falls [in battle] on foreign soil, [the minister], having established a treaty with the enemy through a friend disguised as an enemy's [envoy], should depart.

children.text: KAZ05.6.20/ sāmanta.ādīnām anyatamaṃ vā^asya durge sthāpayitvā^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, having placed any one of the feudatories and the like in the [enemy's] fort, he should depart.

children.text: KAZ05.6.21/ kumāram abhiṣicya vā prativyūheta //
children.translated_text: Or, having consecrated [a new] prince, he should make a counter-deployment.

children.text: KAZ05.6.22/ pareṇa^abhiyukto vā yathā.uktam āpat.pratīkāraṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Or, when attacked by the enemy, he should undertake the countermeasures against emergencies as described.

children.text: KAZ05.6.23/ evam eka.aiśvaryam amātyaḥ kārayed iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the minister should bring about sole sovereignty — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.6.24/ "na^evam" iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Not so' — says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.6.25/ "pramriyamāṇe vā rājany amātyaḥ kulya.kumāra.mukhyān parasparaṃ mukhyeṣu vā vikramayet //
children.translated_text: 'Or, when the king is dying, the minister should set the princes and family chiefs against one another, or against other chiefs.

children.text: KAZ05.6.26/ vikrāntaṃ prakṛti.kopena ghātayet //
children.translated_text: He should kill the one who has attacked by [stirring up] the anger of the subjects.

children.text: KAZ05.6.27/ kulya.kumāra.mukhyān upāṃśu.daṇḍena vā sādhayitvā svayaṃ rājyaṃ gṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having subdued the princes and family chiefs by secret punishment, he should seize the kingdom himself.

children.text: KAZ05.6.28/ rājya.kāraṇādd hi pitā putrān putrāś ca pitaram abhidruhyanti, kim aṅga punar amātya.prakṛtir hy eka.pragraho rājyasya //
children.translated_text: For the sake of the kingdom, fathers have turned against sons and sons against fathers — how much more so one of a minister's nature? For the minister is the sole controller of the kingdom.

children.text: KAZ05.6.29/ tat svayam upasthitaṃ na^avamanyeta //
children.translated_text: Therefore, what has come [to him] of its own accord, he should not disregard.

children.text: KAZ05.6.30/ "svayam ārūḍhā hi strī tyajyamānā^abhiśapati" iti loka.pravādaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'For a woman who has mounted [a man] of her own will curses [him] when rejected' — so goes the popular saying.

children.text:
KAZ05.6.31ab/ kālaś ca sakṛd abhyeti yaṃ naraṃ kāla.kāṅkṣiṇam /
KAZ05.6.31cd/ durlabhaḥ sa punas tasya kālaḥ karma cikīrṣataḥ //
children.translated_text:
Opportunity approaches a man waiting for the [right] moment only once;
for one who [then] wishes to act, that moment is difficult to find again.

children.text: KAZ05.6.32/ prakṛti.kopakam adharmiṣṭham anaikāntikaṃ ca^etad iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This [course] provokes the anger of the subjects, is unrighteous, and is uncertain' — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ05.6.33/ rāja.putram ātma.saṃpannaṃ rājye sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should install on the throne a prince of the royal family who possesses excellence.

children.text: KAZ05.6.34/ saṃpanna.abhāve^avyasaninaṃ kumāraṃ rāja.kanyāṃ garbhiṇīṃ devīṃ vā puras.kṛtya mahā.mātrān saṃnipātya brūyāt "ayaṃ vo nikṣepaḥ, pitaram asya^avekṣadhvaṃ sattva.abhijanam ātmanaś ca, dhvaja.mātro^ayaṃ bhavanta eva svāminaḥ, kathaṃ vā kriyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: In the absence of one possessing excellence, placing before [the assembly] a prince free from vices, a royal princess, or the pregnant queen, and having assembled the great ministers, he should say: 'This is your trust; look upon his father's [lineage], his own courage and birth, and your own [interests]; this one is but a standard-bearer — you yourselves are the masters; or, what do you wish to be done?'

children.text: KAZ05.6.35/ tathā bruvāṇaṃ yoga.puruṣā brūyuḥ "ko^anyo bhavat.purogād asmād rājñaś cāturvarṇyam arhati pālayitum" iti //
children.translated_text: As he speaks thus, agents should say: 'Who else but one led by Your Honor is fit to protect the four-fold social order as king?'

children.text: KAZ05.6.36/ "tathā" ity amātyaḥ kumāraṃ rāja.kanyāṃ garbhiṇīṃ devīṃ vā^adhikurvīta, bandhu.saṃbandhināṃ mitra.amitra.dūtānāṃ ca darśayet //
children.translated_text: 'So be it' — the minister should then install the prince, the royal princess, or the pregnant queen [as regent], and present [them] to the kinsmen, allies, envoys of allies and enemies.

children.text: KAZ05.6.37/ bhakta.vetana.viśeṣam amātyānām āyudhīyānāṃ ca kārayet, "bhūyaś ca^ayaṃ vṛddhaḥ kariṣyati" iti brūyāt //
children.translated_text: He should increase the food allowances and special wages of the ministers and the military, and should say: 'When he grows up, he will do even more.'

children.text: KAZ05.6.38/ evaṃ durga.rāṣṭra.mukhyān ābhāṣeta, yathā.arhaṃ ca mitra.amitra.pakṣam //
children.translated_text: Thus he should address the chiefs of the forts and the countryside, and the party of allies and enemies as befits.

children.text: KAZ05.6.39/ vinaya.karmaṇi ca kumārasya prayateta //
children.translated_text: And he should strive for the education and training of the prince.

children.text: KAZ05.6.40/ kanyāyāṃ samāna.jātīyād apatyam utpādya vā^abhiṣiñcet //
children.translated_text: Or, having produced an offspring from the princess by a man of equal caste, he should consecrate [that offspring].

children.text: KAZ05.6.41/ mātuś citta.kṣobha.bhayāt kulyam alpa.sattvaṃ chātraṃ ca lakṣaṇyam upanidadhyāt //
children.translated_text: For fear of disturbing the mother's mind, he should secretly keep ready a family [member] of modest ability and a pupil of [suitable] marks.

children.text: KAZ05.6.42/ ṛtau ca^enāṃ rakṣet //
children.translated_text: And he should guard her during her fertile season.

children.text: KAZ05.6.43/ na ca^ātma.arthaṃ kaṃcid utkṛṣṭam upabhogaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: And he should not procure any exalted enjoyment for himself.

children.text: KAZ05.6.44/ rāja.arthaṃ tu yāna.vāhana.ābharaṇa.vastra.strī.veśma.parivāpān kārayet //
children.translated_text: But for the king's sake, he should procure conveyances, vehicles, ornaments, garments, women, and household provisions.

children.text:
KAZ05.6.45ab/ yauvanasthaṃ ca yāceta viśramaṃ citta.kāraṇāt /
KAZ05.6.45cd/ parityajed atuṣyantaṃ tuṣyantaṃ ca^anupālayet //
children.translated_text:
And when [the prince] has reached youth, he should request release on the pretext of [needing] rest;
he should abandon [the position if] the [prince is] dissatisfied, and serve [him] if satisfied.

children.text:
KAZ05.6.46ab/ nivedya putra.rakṣā.arthaṃ gūḍha.sāra.parigrahān /
KAZ05.6.46cd/ araṇyaṃ dīrgha.sattraṃ vā seveta^ārucyatāṃ gataḥ //
children.translated_text:
Having entrusted [others with] the protection of the prince and having hidden away the treasury reserves,
if he has come to be disliked, he should retire to the forest or to a long sacrificial session.

children.text:
KAZ05.6.47ab/ mukhyair avagṛhītaṃ vā rājānaṃ tat.priya.āśritaḥ /
KAZ05.6.47cd/ itihāsa.purāṇābhyāṃ bodhayed artha.śāstravit //
children.translated_text:
Or, when the king is seized by the chiefs, one who has taken refuge in [the king's own] favorites
should awaken him through [the recitation of] <s>Itihāsa</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, being versed in the science of politics.

children.text:
KAZ05.6.48ab/ siddha.vyañjana.rūpo vā yogam āsthāya pārthivam /
KAZ05.6.48cd/ labheta labdhvā dūṣyeṣu dāṇḍakarmikam ācaret //E
children.translated_text:
Or, assuming the guise of a perfected adept, having gained access to the king through yoga,
he should obtain [influence]; and having obtained it, he should proceed to punish the guilty as a staff-wielding enforcer.

children.text:
((maṇḍala.yoniḥ ṣaṣṭham adhikaraṇam))
 (ṣaṇ.ṇavatitamaṃ prakaraṇaṃ - prakṛti.sampadah)
KAZ06.1.01/ svāmy.amātya.jana.pada.durga.kośa.daṇḍa.mitrāṇi prakṛtayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
((The basis of the circle [of kings]: the sixth book))
(Ninety-sixth topic: Excellences of the constituent elements)
The lord (<s>svāmin</s>), the minister (<s>amātya</s>), the countryside (<s>janapada</s>), the fort (<s>durga</s>), the treasury (<s>kośa</s>), the army (<s>daṇḍa</s>), and the ally (<s>mitra</s>) — these are the constituent elements (<s>prakṛtis</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.1.02/ tatra svāmi.sampat //
children.translated_text: Therein, the excellences of the lord —
