children.text: KAZ06.1.03/ mahā.kulīno daiva.buddhi.sattva.sampanno vṛddha.darśī dhārmikaḥ satya.vāg avisaṃvādakaḥ kṛtajñaḥ sthūla.lakṣo mahā.utsāho^adīrgha.sūtraḥ śakya.sāmanto dṛḍha.buddhir akṣudra.pariṣatko vinaya.kāma ity ābhigāmikā guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Of noble lineage, endowed with divine fortune, intellect, and valor, one who heeds the elders, righteous, truthful, not breaking his word, grateful, with great aims, highly enthusiastic, not procrastinating, whose feudatories are amenable, of firm resolve, not of a petty council, and desirous of discipline — these are the qualities that inspire allegiance.

children.text: KAZ06.1.04/ śuśrūṣā.śravaṇa.grahaṇa.dhāraṇa.vijñāna.ūha.apoha.tattva.abhiniveśāḥ prajñā.guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Desire to listen, listening, grasping, retaining, discriminating, inferring, rejecting, and commitment to the truth of things — these are the qualities of wisdom.

children.text: KAZ06.1.05/ śauryam amarṣaḥ śīghratā dākṣyaṃ ca^utsāha.guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Valor, impatience [with injustice], swiftness, and dexterity — these are the qualities of enterprise.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.06/ vāgmī pragalbhaḥ smṛti.mati.balavān udagraḥ sv.avagrahaḥ kṛta.śilpo^avyasano daṇḍa.nāyy upakāra.apakārayor dṛṣṭa.pratīkārī hrīmān āpat.prakṛtyor viniyoktā dīrgha.dūra.darśī deśa.kāla.puruṣa.kāra.kārya.pradhānaḥ saṃdhi.vikrama.tyāga.samyama.paṇa.parac.chidra.vibhāgī saṃvṛto^adīna.abhihāsya.jihma.bhrukuṭī.kṣaṇaḥ
kāma.krodha.lobha.stambha.cāpala.upatāpa.paiśunya.hīnaḥ śaklaḥ smita.udagra.abhibhāṣī vṛddha.upadeśa.ācāra ity ātma.sampat //
children.translated_text:
Eloquent, bold, possessing strong memory and intellect, high-spirited, self-restrained, skilled in the arts, free from vices, capable of wielding punishment, one who has seen the remedy for both favor and disfavor, modest, capable of employing [men] in emergencies and in normal times, one whose chief concern is place, time, human effort, and the task at hand, one who can distinguish between treaties, forceful action, liberality, and restraint and [who can exploit] the enemy's vulnerabilities, self-concealing, not dejected, not given to laughing, crooked [dealings], or frowning,
free from lust, anger, greed, obstinacy, fickleness, irritability, and slander, pleasant, with a cheerful and dignified demeanor, and following the counsel and conduct of the elders — these constitute the personal excellences [of the king].

children.text: KAZ06.1.07/ amātya.sampad uktā purastāt //
children.translated_text: The excellences of the minister have been stated earlier.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.08/ madhye ca^ante ca sthānavān ātma.dhāraṇaḥ para.dhāraṇaś ca^āpadi sva.ārakṣaḥ sva.ājīvaḥ śatru.dveṣī śakya.sāmantaḥ paṅka.pāṣāṇa.uṣara.viṣama.kaṇṭaka.śreṇī.vyāla.mṛga.aṭavī.hīnaḥ kāntaḥ sītā.khani.dravya.hasti.vanavān gavyaḥ pauruṣeyo gupta.gocaraḥ paśumān adeva.mātṛko vāri.sthala.pathābhyām upetaḥ sāra.citra.bahu.paṇyo daṇḍa.kara.sahaḥ
karma.śīla.karṣako^abāliśa.svāmy.avara.varṇa.prāyo bhakta.śuci.manuṣya iti jana.pada.sampat //
children.translated_text:
Possessing strategic value both at the center and at the borders, self-sustaining and capable of sustaining others, in emergencies self-defending, self-supporting, hostile toward the enemy, with amenable feudatories, free from swamps, rocky terrain, saline tracts, rough ground, thorny thickets, snakes, and wild beasts, beautiful, endowed with crown lands, mines, timber, elephants, and forests, with pasture for cattle, productive of men, with protected grazing grounds, rich in livestock, not dependent on rain, provided with water-routes and land-routes, rich in diverse and abundant merchandise, capable of bearing the army and taxes,
with an industrious and virtuous farming [population], not having a majority of foolish [subjects], low-caste people, or people whose masters are inferior, and with loyal and pure-hearted men — these are the excellences of the countryside.

children.text: KAZ06.1.09/ durga.sampad uktā purastāt //
children.translated_text: The excellences of the fort have been stated earlier.

children.text: KAZ06.1.10/ dharma.adhigataḥ pūrvaiḥ svayaṃ vā hema.rūpya.prāyaś citra.sthūla.ratna.hiraṇyo dīrghām apy āpadam anāyatiṃ saheta^iti kośa.sampat //
children.translated_text: Acquired through <s>dharma</s> by ancestors or by oneself, consisting chiefly of gold and silver, with diverse and ample jewels and money — [a treasury that] could endure even a prolonged emergency without future [income] — these are the excellences of the treasury.

children.text: KAZ06.1.11/ pitṛ.paitāmaho nityo vaśyas tuṣṭa.bhṛta.putra.dāraḥ pravāseṣv avisaṃvāditaḥ sarvatra^apratihato duḥkha.saho bahu.yuddhaḥ sarva.yuddha.praharaṇa.vidyā.viśāradaḥ saha.vṛddhi.kṣayikatvād advaidhyaḥ kṣatra.prāya iti daṇḍa.sampat //
children.translated_text: Inherited from father and grandfather, constant, obedient, with contented and well-maintained sons and wives, not betrayed on campaigns abroad, unstoppable everywhere, enduring of hardship, experienced in many battles, proficient in all weapons and all forms of warfare, sharing in growth and decline [with the king] and hence not disloyal, consisting chiefly of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — these are the excellences of the army.

children.text: KAZ06.1.12/ pitṛ.paitāmahaṃ nityaṃ vaśyam advaidhyaṃ mahal.laghu.samuttham iti mitra.sampat //
children.translated_text: Inherited from father and grandfather, constant, obedient, not disloyal, capable of mobilizing on a large or small scale — these are the excellences of an ally.

children.text: KAZ06.1.13/ arāja.bījī lubdhaḥ kṣudra.pariṣatko virakta.prakṛtir anyāya.vṛttir ayukto vyasanī nirutsāho daiva.pramāṇo yat.kiṃcana.kārya.gatir ananubandhaḥ klībo nitya.apakārī ca^ity amitra.sampat //
children.translated_text: Not of royal lineage, greedy, of a petty council, with alienated subjects, conducting unjust affairs, negligent, addicted to vices, without enterprise, dependent on fate, concerned with trivial matters, without follow-through, cowardly, and constantly causing harm — these are the [desirable] qualities of an enemy.

children.text: KAZ06.1.14/ evaṃ.bhūto hi śatruḥ sukhaḥ samucchettuṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: For an enemy of such qualities is easy to uproot.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.15ab/ ari.varjāḥ prakṛtayaḥ sapta^etāḥ sva.guṇa.udayāḥ /
KAZ06.1.15cd/ uktāḥ pratyaṅga.bhūtās tāḥ prakṛtā rāja.sampadaḥ //
children.translated_text:
These seven constituent elements — excluding the enemy — each endowed with its own excellences,
are described as limbs of the natural royal endowments.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.16ab/ sampādayaty asampannāḥ prakṛtīr ātmavān nṛpaḥ /
KAZ06.1.16cd/ vivṛddhāś ca^anuraktāś ca prakṛtīr hanty anātmavān //
children.translated_text:
A self-possessed king develops the constituent elements that are undeveloped;
but a king who lacks self-control destroys constituent elements that are flourishing and devoted.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.17ab/ tataḥ sa duṣṭa.prakṛtiś cāturanto^apy anātmavān /
KAZ06.1.17cd/ hanyate vā prakṛtibhir yāti vā dviṣatāṃ vaśam //
children.translated_text:
Therefore, such a king with corrupted constituent elements, though ruling to the four quarters, lacking self-control,
is either killed by his own constituent elements or falls into the power of his enemies.

children.text:
KAZ06.1.18ab/ ātmavāṃs tv alpa.deśo^api yuktaḥ prakṛti.sampadā /
KAZ06.1.18cd/nayajñaḥ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jayaty eva na hīyate //E
children.translated_text:
But a self-possessed king, even of a small territory, endowed with the excellences of the constituent elements,
versed in statecraft, conquers the entire earth and is never overcome.

children.text:
(śama.vyāyāmikam)
KAZ06.2.01/ śama.vyāyāmau yoga.kṣemayor yoniḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Peace and exertion)
Peace (<s>śama</s>) and exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>) are the source of security (<s>kṣema</s>) and acquisition (<s>yoga</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.2.02/ karma.ārambhāṇāṃ yoga.ārādhano vyāyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: Exertion is the means of accomplishing undertakings — [the channel of] acquisition.

children.text: KAZ06.2.03/ karma.phala.upabhogānāṃ kṣema.ārādhanaḥ śamaḥ //
children.translated_text: Peace is the means of enjoying the fruits of action — [the channel of] security.

children.text: KAZ06.2.04/ śama.vyāyāmayor yoniḥ ṣāḍguṇyam //
children.translated_text: The source of peace and exertion is the sixfold policy (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.2.05/ kṣayaḥ sthānaṃ vṛddhir ity udayās tasya //
children.translated_text: Its [possible] outcomes are: decline, stability, and growth.

children.text: KAZ06.2.06/ mānuṣaṃ naya.apanayau, daivam aya.anayau //
children.translated_text: Good counsel and bad counsel are the human [factors]; good fortune and ill fortune are the divine [factors].

children.text: KAZ06.2.07/ daiva.mānuṣaṃ hi karma lokaṃ yāpayati //
children.translated_text: For divine and human action together sustain the world.

children.text: KAZ06.2.08/ adṛṣṭa.kāritaṃ daivam //
children.translated_text: What is caused by the unseen is divine.

children.text: KAZ06.2.09/ tasminn iṣṭena phalena yogo^ayaḥ, aniṣṭena^anayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein, conjunction with a desired result is good fortune; with an undesired result, ill fortune.

children.text: KAZ06.2.10/ dṛṣṭa.kāritaṃ mānuṣam //
children.translated_text: What is caused by the visible is human.

children.text: KAZ06.2.11/ tasmin yoga.kṣema.niṣpattir nayaḥ, vipattir apanayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therein, the achievement of acquisition and security is good counsel; their failure is bad counsel.

children.text: KAZ06.2.12/ tac cintyam, acintyaṃ daivam //
children.translated_text: That [human factor] can be deliberated upon; the divine is beyond deliberation.

children.text: KAZ06.2.13/ rājā ātma.dravya.prakṛti.sampanno nayasya^adhiṣṭhānaṃ vijigīṣuḥ //
children.translated_text: A king endowed with personal excellence and the excellence of his resources and constituent elements — the one who seeks to conquer (<s>vijigīṣu</s>) — is the foundation of [good] counsel.

children.text: KAZ06.2.14/ tasya samantato maṇḍalī.bhūtā bhūmy.anantarā ari.prakṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: Surrounding him in a circle, with territories contiguous to his, are the enemy constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ06.2.15/ tathā^eva bhūmy.eka.antarā mitra.prakṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: Likewise, with one territory intervening, are the ally constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ06.2.16/ ari.sampad.yuktaḥ sāmantaḥ śatruḥ, vyasanī yātavyaḥ, anapāśrayo durbala.āśrayo vā^ucchedanīyaḥ, viparyaye pīḍanīyaḥ karśanīyo vā //
children.translated_text: A feudatory endowed with the qualities of an enemy is a foe; one beset with calamities is one to be marched against; one without support or with a weak support is to be exterminated; in the opposite case, he is to be harassed or worn down.

children.text: KAZ06.2.17/ ity ari.viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the distinctions among enemies.

children.text: KAZ06.2.18/ tasmān mitram ari.mitraṃ mitra.mitram ari.mitra.mitraṃ ca^ānantaryeṇa bhūmīnāṃ prasajyante purastāt, paścāt pārṣṇi.grāha ākrandaḥ pārṣṇi.grāha.āsāra ākranda.āsāraḥ //
children.translated_text: From [the <s>vijigīṣu</s>], in front — the ally, the enemy's ally, the ally's ally, and the enemy's ally's ally — are connected in sequence by [contiguity of] territories; behind — the one who strikes in the rear, the one to whom one cries for help, the ally of the rear-striker, and the ally of the one to whom one cries for help.

children.text: KAZ06.2.19/ bhūmy.anantaraḥ prakṛti.mitraḥ, tulya.abhijanaḥ sahajaḥ, viruddho virodhayitā vā kṛtrimaḥ //
children.translated_text: One contiguous in territory is a natural ally; one of equal lineage is an innate ally; one who is hostile or made hostile [by circumstances] is an artificial ally.

children.text: KAZ06.2.20/ bhūmy.eka.antaraṃ prakṛti.mitram, mātā.pitṛ.sambaddhaṃ sahajam, dhana.jīvita.hetor āśritaṃ kṛtrimam //
children.translated_text: One with one territory intervening is a natural friend; one related through mother or father is an innate friend; one who takes refuge for the sake of wealth or life is an artificial friend.

children.text: KAZ06.2.21/ ari.vijigīṣvor bhūmy.anantaraḥ saṃhata.asaṃhatayor anugraha.samartho nigrahe ca^asaṃhatayor madhyamaḥ //
children.translated_text: One contiguous in territory to both the enemy and the conqueror, capable of helping both when they are united and of overpowering each when they are separate — is the middle king (<s>madhyama</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.2.22/ ari.vijigīṣu.madhyānāṃ bahiḥ prakṛtibhyo balavattaraḥ saṃhata.asaṃhatānām ari.vijigīṣu.madhyamānām anugraha.samartho nigrahe ca^asaṃhatānām udāsīnaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who is beyond the constituent elements of the enemy, the conqueror, and the middle king, more powerful than all, capable of helping both the united and separate [parties] and of overpowering each when separate — is the neutral king (<s>udāsīna</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.2.23/ iti prakṛtayaḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the constituent elements [of the circle of kings].

children.text: KAZ06.2.24/ vijigīṣur mitraṃ mitra.mitraṃ vā^asya prakṛtayas tisraḥ //
children.translated_text: The conqueror, his ally, and the ally's ally — these are his three constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ06.2.25/ tāḥ pañcabhir amātya.jana.pada.durga.kośa.daṇḍa.prakṛtibhir eka.ekaśaḥ samyuktā maṇḍalam aṣṭādaśakaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: These [twelve kings], each combined with the five constituent elements — ministers, countryside, fortifications, treasury, and army — make up the circle of eighteen.

children.text: KAZ06.2.26/ anena maṇḍala.pṛthaktvaṃ vyākhyātam ari.madhyama.udāsīnānām //
children.translated_text: By this, the distinctness of the circles of the enemy, the middle [king], and the neutral [king] is explained.

children.text: KAZ06.2.27/ evaṃ catur.maṇḍala.saṃkṣepaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the summary of the four circles.

children.text: KAZ06.2.28/ dvādaśa rāja.prakṛtayaḥ ṣaṣṭir dravya.prakṛtayaḥ, saṃkṣepeṇa dvi.saptatiḥ //
children.translated_text: Twelve royal constituent elements and sixty material constituent elements — in total, seventy-two.

children.text: KAZ06.2.29/ tāsāṃ yathā.svaṃ sampadaḥ //
children.translated_text: Their respective excellences [are as follows].

children.text: KAZ06.2.30/ śaktiḥ siddhiś ca //
children.translated_text: Power and achievement.

children.text: KAZ06.2.31/ balaṃ śaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: Strength is power.

children.text: KAZ06.2.32/ sukhaṃ siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Prosperity is achievement.

children.text: KAZ06.2.33/ śaktis trividhā - jñāna.balaṃ mantra.śaktiḥ, kośa.daṇḍa.balaṃ prabhu.śaktiḥ, vikrama.balam utsāha.śaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: Power is threefold: the power of knowledge is the power of counsel (<s>mantraśakti</s>); the power of treasury and army is the power of sovereignty (<s>prabhuśakti</s>); the power of valor is the power of enterprise (<s>utsāhaśakti</s>).

children.text: KAZ06.2.34/ evaṃ siddhis trividhā^eva - mantra.śakti.sādhyā mantra.siddhiḥ, prabhu.śakti.sādhyā prabhu.siddhiḥ, utsāha.śakti.sādhyā utsāha.siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Likewise, achievement is threefold: that accomplished by the power of counsel is the achievement of counsel; that accomplished by the power of sovereignty is the achievement of sovereignty; that accomplished by the power of enterprise is the achievement of enterprise.

children.text: KAZ06.2.35/ tābhir abhyuccito jyāyān bhavati, apacito hīnaḥ, tulya.śaktiḥ samaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who is enhanced by these is superior; one who is diminished is inferior; one of equal power is [simply] equal.

children.text: KAZ06.2.36/ tasmāt^śaktiṃ siddhiṃ ca ghaṭeta^ātmany āveśayitum, sādhāraṇo vā dravya.prakṛtiṣv ānantaryeṇa śauca.vaśena vā //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should strive to establish power and achievement in oneself — either shared among the material constituent elements by proximity or by purity [of intent].

children.text: KAZ06.2.37/ dūṣya.amitrābhyāṃ vā^apakraṣṭuṃ yateta //
children.translated_text: Or, one should strive to diminish [the power and achievement] of the corruptible [elements] and of the enemy.

children.text:
KAZ06.2.38/ yadi vā paśyet "amitro me śakti.yukto vāg.daṇḍa.pāruṣya.artha.dūṣaṇaiḥ prakṛtīr upahaniṣyati, siddhi.yukto vā mṛgayā.dyūta.madya.strībhiḥ pramādaṃ gamiṣyati, sa virakta.prakṛtir upakṣīṇaḥ pramatto vā sādhyo me bhaviṣyati, vigraha.abhiyukto vā sarva.saṃdohena^ekastho^adurgastho vā sthāsyati, sa saṃhata.sainyo mitra.durga.viyuktaḥ sādhyo me bhaviṣyati,
"balavān vā rājā parataḥ śatrum ucchettu.kāmaḥ tam ucchidya mām ucchindyād" iti balavatā prārthitasya me vipanna.karma.ārambhasya vā sāhāyyaṃ dāsyati", madhyama.lipsāyāṃ ca, ity evaṃ.ādiṣu kāraṇeṣv amitrasya^api śaktiṃ
siddhiṃ ca^icchet //
children.translated_text:
Or, if one should perceive: 'My enemy, endowed with power, will damage the constituent elements through harshness of speech, punishment, and squandering of wealth; or, endowed with achievement, will fall into negligence through hunting, gambling, drinking, and women; and he, with alienated constituents, weakened, or negligent, will become conquerable by me; or, engaged in hostility, he will stand concentrated in one place with all his forces, without fortification, and he, with his army massed [in one place] but cut off from allies and forts, will become conquerable by me;
or a powerful king from the other side, wishing to destroy [my] enemy, having destroyed him, may then destroy me' — then he would give assistance, and in [seeking the] acquisition of the middle [king's alliance], and in such and similar situations — one may even desire that the enemy have power and achievement.

children.text:
KAZ06.2.39ab/ nemim eka.antarān rājñaḥ kṛtvā ca^anantarān arān /
KAZ06.2.39cd/ nābhim ātmānam āyacchen netā prakṛti.maṇḍale //
children.translated_text:
Making the alternate kings the rim and the adjacent ones the spokes,
the leader should seek to make himself the hub in the circle of constituent elements.

children.text:
KAZ06.2.40ab/ madhye hy upahitaḥ śatrur netur mitrasya ca^ubhayoḥ /
KAZ06.2.40cd/ ucchedyaḥ pīḍanīyo vā balavān api jāyate //E
children.translated_text:
For the enemy, placed in the middle [between] the leader and his ally — both [pressing from two sides] —
becomes one to be destroyed or crushed, even if powerful.

children.text:
(ṣāḍguṇya.samuddeśaḥ - kṣaya.sthāna.vṛddhi.niścayah)
KAZ07.1.01/ ṣāḍguṇyasya prakṛti.maṇḍalaṃ yoniḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Enumeration of the sixfold policy — Determination of decline, stability, and growth)
The circle of constituent elements is the basis of the sixfold policy.

children.text: KAZ07.1.02/ "saṃdhi.vigraha.āsana.yāna.saṃśraya.dvaidhī.bhāvāḥ ṣāḍguṇyam" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Treaty, hostility, sitting quiet, marching, seeking shelter, and the dual policy — these constitute the sixfold policy" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.1.03/ "dvaiguṇyam" iti vāta.vyādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: "It is [only] twofold" — says <s>Vātavyādhi</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.1.04/ "saṃdhi.vigrahābhyāṃ hi ṣāḍguṇyaṃ sampadyate" iti //
children.translated_text: "For the sixfold policy is accomplished through [just] treaty and hostility" — he says.

children.text: KAZ07.1.05/ ṣāḍguṇyam eva^etad avasthā.bhedād iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: It is indeed this [same] sixfold policy, differing only in [its] modes of application — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.1.06/ tatra paṇa.bandhaḥ saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Of these: the making of a compact is treaty (<s>saṃdhi</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.07/ apakāro vigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: Causing harm is hostility (<s>vigraha</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.08/ upekṣaṇam āsanam //
children.translated_text: Remaining indifferent is sitting quiet (<s>āsana</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.09/ abhyuccayo yānam //
children.translated_text: Augmentation [of forces for attack] is marching (<s>yāna</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.10/ para.arpaṇaṃ saṃśrayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Submitting oneself to another is seeking shelter (<s>saṃśraya</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.11/ saṃdhi.vigraha.upādānaṃ dvaidhī.bhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Adopting [both] treaty and hostility [simultaneously] is the dual policy (<s>dvaidhībhāva</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.1.12/ iti ṣaḍ.guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the six policies.

children.text: KAZ07.1.13/ parasmādd hīyamānaḥ saṃdadhīta //
children.translated_text: When declining relative to the other, one should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.1.14/ abhyuccīyamāno vigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: When thriving, one should engage in hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.1.15/ "na māṃ paro na^ahaṃ param upahantuṃ śaktaḥ" ity āsīta //
children.translated_text: When [one thinks]: 'Neither can the other harm me, nor I him' — one should sit quiet.

children.text: KAZ07.1.16/ guṇa.atiśaya.yukto yāyāt //
children.translated_text: When possessing a surplus of advantageous factors, one should march.

children.text: KAZ07.1.17/ śakti.hīnaḥ saṃśrayeta //
children.translated_text: When lacking in power, one should seek shelter.

children.text: KAZ07.1.18/ sahāya.sādhye kārye dvaidhībhāvaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: When an objective requires an ally, one should adopt the dual policy.

children.text: KAZ07.1.19/ iti guṇa.avasthāpanam //
children.translated_text: This is the assignment of the [six] policies [to their situations].

children.text: KAZ07.1.20/ teṣāṃ yasmin vā guṇe sthitaḥ paśyet "iha.sthaḥ śakṣyāmi durga.setu.karma.vaṇik.patha.śūnya.niveśa.khani.dravya.hasti.vana.karmāṇy ātmanaḥ pravartayitum, parasya ca^etāni karmāṇy upahantum" iti tam ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: When established in whichever policy, if [the king] perceives: 'Remaining in this position, I shall be able to advance the works of fortifications, embankments, trade routes, colonization of wastelands, mining, timber forests, elephant forests, and my own [other] enterprises, and to damage the enemy's [corresponding] enterprises' — he should adhere to that [policy].

children.text: KAZ07.1.21/ sā vṛddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: That is growth.

children.text: KAZ07.1.22/ "āśutarā me vṛddhir bhūyastarā vṛddhy.udayatarā vā bhaviṣyati, viparītā parasya" iti jñātvā para.vṛddhim upekṣeta //
children.translated_text: 'My growth will be swifter, greater, or more productive than my enemy's, and the reverse [will be true] for the enemy' — knowing this, one may disregard the enemy's growth.

children.text: KAZ07.1.23/ tulya.kāla.phala.udayāyāṃ vā vṛddhau saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, when growth is equal in time, outcome, and productivity, one should enter into a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.1.24/ yasmin vā guṇe sthitaḥ sva.karmaṇām upaghātaṃ paśyen na^itarasya tasmin na tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: When established in whichever policy, if one perceives damage to one's own enterprises but not to the other's — one should not remain in that [policy].

children.text: KAZ07.1.25/ eṣa kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: That is decline.

children.text: KAZ07.1.26/ "ciratareṇa^alpataraṃ vṛddhy.udayataraṃ vā kṣeṣye, viparītaṃ paraḥ" iti jñātvā kṣayam upekṣeta //
children.translated_text: 'In a longer time, with less [loss] and greater productive recovery I shall decline, and the reverse [will be true] for the enemy' — knowing this, one may disregard the decline.

children.text: KAZ07.1.27/ tulya.kāla.phala.udaye vā kṣaye saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, when decline is equal in time, outcome, and recovery, one should enter into a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.1.28/ yasmin vā guṇe sthitaḥ sva.karma.vṛddhiṃ kṣayaṃ vā na^abhipaśyed etat.sthānam //
children.translated_text: When established in whichever policy, if one perceives neither growth nor decline in one's own enterprises — that is stability.

children.text: KAZ07.1.29/ "hrasvataraṃ vṛddhy.udayataraṃ vā sthāsyāmi, viparītaṃ paraḥ" iti jñātvā sthānam upekṣeta //
children.translated_text: 'For a shorter time, with greater productive recovery I shall remain stable, and the reverse [will be true] for the enemy' — knowing this, one may disregard the stability.

children.text: KAZ07.1.30/ "tulya.kāla.phala.udaye vā sthāne saṃdhim upeyād" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Or, when stability is equal in time, outcome, and recovery, one should enter into a treaty' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.1.31/ na^etad vibhāṣitam iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is not a fixed rule — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.1.32a/ yadi vā paśyet "sandhau sthito mahā.phalaiḥ sva.karmabhiḥ para.karmāṇy upahaniṣyāmi, mahā.phalāni vā sva.karmāṇy upabhokṣye, para.karmāṇi vā, saṃdhi.viśvāsena vā yoga.upaniṣat.praṇidhibhiḥ para.karmāṇy upahaniṣyāmi, sukhaṃ vā sa.anugraha.parihāra.saukaryaṃ phala.lābha.bhūyastvena sva.karmaṇāṃ para.karma.yoga.āvahaṃ janam āsrāvayiṣyāmi - //
children.translated_text: Or, if one perceives: 'Established in a treaty, through my own great enterprises I shall damage the enemy's enterprises; or I shall enjoy my own great enterprises; or, through the confidence of the treaty, I shall damage the enemy's enterprises by means of secret agents employing occult methods and espionage; or with ease, through concessions and exemptions and the abundance of rewards, I shall attract to myself the people who support the enemy's enterprises —

children.text: KAZ07.1.32b/ balinā^atimātreṇa vā saṃhitaḥ paraḥ sva.karma.upaghātaṃ prāpsyati, yena vā vigṛhīto mayā.saṃdhatte tena^asya vigrahaṃ dīrghaṃ kariṣyāmi, mayā vā saṃhitasya mad.dveṣiṇo jana.padaṃ pīḍayiṣyati - //
children.translated_text: or the enemy, allied with one who is excessively powerful, will suffer damage to his own enterprises; or with whomever [the enemy] has a quarrel, by not making peace with me, I shall make his conflict prolonged; or, being my ally, [such a powerful king] will harass the countryside of one who is my enemy —

children.text: KAZ07.1.32c/ para.upahato vā^asya jana.pado mām āgamiṣyati, tataḥ karmasu vṛddhiṃ prāpsyāmi, vipanna.karma.ārambho vā viṣamasthaḥ paraḥ karmasu na me vikrameta - //
children.translated_text: or the enemy's countryside, damaged by another, will come over to me, and thereby I shall gain growth in [my] enterprises; or the enemy, with his enterprises ruined and in a difficult position, will not be able to act against me in [my] enterprises —

children.text: KAZ07.1.32d/ parataḥ pravṛtta.karma.ārambho vā tābhyāṃ saṃhitaḥ karmasu vṛddhiṃ prāpsyāmi, śatru.pratibaddhaṃ vā śatruṇā saṃdhiṃ kṛtvā maṇḍalaṃ bhetsyāmi - //
children.translated_text: or the enemy, having begun enterprises on the other [front], being allied with both [neighbors], I shall gain growth in [my] enterprises; or, being constrained by [his] enemy, having made a treaty with [that] enemy, I shall break through [his] circle —

children.text: KAZ07.1.32e/ bhinnam avāpsyāmi, daṇḍa.anugraheṇa vā śatrum upagṛhya maṇḍala.lipsāyāṃ vidveṣaṃ grāhayiṣyāmi, vidviṣṭaṃ tena^eva ghātayiṣyāmi" iti saṃdhinā vṛddhim ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: having broken through, I shall obtain [what I seek]; or, having brought the enemy under control through the rod of force and conciliation, in [my] aspiration for [controlling] the circle, I shall sow enmity; having created enmity, I shall have him killed by that very [ally]' — thus, one should pursue growth through treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.1.33a/ yadi vā paśyet "āyudhīya.prāyaḥ śreṇī.prāyo vā me jana.padaḥ śaila.vana.nadī.durga.eka.dvāra.ārakṣo vā śakṣyati para.abhiyogaṃ pratihantum, viṣaya.ante durgam aviṣahyam apāśrito vā śakṣyāmi para.karmāṇy upahantuṃ - //
children.translated_text: Or, if one perceives: 'My countryside, being predominantly military or guild-based, or protected by mountain, forest, river, and fortress [requiring only] a single gate to defend, will be able to repel the enemy's attack; or, having taken refuge in an impregnable fortress at the boundary of my territory, I shall be able to damage the enemy's enterprises —

children.text: KAZ07.1.33b/ vyasana.pīḍa.upahata.utsāho vā paraḥ samprāpta.karma.upaghāta.kālaḥ, vigṛhītasya^anyato vā śakṣyāmi jana.padam apavāhayitum" iti vigrahe sthito vṛddhim ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: or the enemy, with his energy impaired by calamities and afflictions, has reached the time for having his enterprises damaged; or, being engaged in hostility with another, I shall be able to draw away [the enemy's] people' — thus, established in hostility, one should pursue growth.

children.text: KAZ07.1.34/ yadi vā manyeta "na me śaktaḥ paraḥ karmāṇy upahantuṃ na^ahaṃ tasya karma.upaghātī vā, vyasanam asya, śva.varāhayor iva kalahe vā, sva.karma.anuṣṭhāna.paro vā vardhiṣye" ity āsanena vṛddhim ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, if one thinks: 'The enemy is not capable of damaging my enterprises, nor am I one who damages his; or, there is a vulnerability on his part; or, as in a quarrel between a dog and a boar, [both would suffer]; or, being devoted to the conduct of my own enterprises, I shall prosper' — thus, by sitting quiet, one should pursue growth.

children.text: KAZ07.1.35/ yadi vā manyeta "yāna.sādhyaḥ karma.upaghātaḥ śatroḥ, prativihita.sva.karma.ārakṣaś ca^asmi" iti yānena vṛddhim ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, if one thinks: 'The damage of the enemy's enterprises is achievable by marching, and I have secured the protection of my own enterprises' — thus, by marching, one should pursue growth.

children.text: KAZ07.1.36/ yadi vā manyeta "na^asmi śaktaḥ para.karmāṇy upahantum, sva.karma.upaghātaṃ vā trātum" iti, balavantam āśritaḥ sva.karma.anuṣṭhānena kṣayāt sthānaṃ sthānād vṛddhiṃ ca^ākāṅkṣeta //
children.translated_text: Or, if one thinks: 'I am not capable of damaging the enemy's enterprises or of protecting my own from damage' — then, having taken refuge with a powerful [king], by conducting one's own enterprises, one should hope for stability after decline, and growth after stability.

children.text: KAZ07.1.37/ yadi vā manyeta "saṃdhinā^ekataḥ sva.karmāṇi pravartayiṣyāmi, vigraheṇa^ekataḥ para.karmāṇy upahaniṣyāmi" iti dvaidhī.bhāvena vṛddhim ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, if one thinks: 'By treaty on one side, I shall advance my own enterprises; by hostility on the other, I shall damage the enemy's enterprises' — thus, by the dual policy, one should pursue growth.

children.text:
KAZ07.1.38ab/ evaṃ ṣaḍbhir guṇair etaiḥ sthitaḥ prakṛti.maṇḍale /
KAZ07.1.38cd/ paryeṣeta kṣayāt sthānaṃ sthānād vṛddhiṃ ca karmasu //E
children.translated_text:
Thus, established in the circle of constituent elements through these six policies,
one should seek stability after decline and growth after stability in [one's] enterprises.

children.text:
(saṃśraya.vṛtti)
KAZ07.2.01/ saṃdhi.vigrahayos tulyāyāṃ vṛddhau saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Conduct of one seeking shelter)
When growth is equal in treaty and hostility, one should enter into a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.2.02/ vigrahe hi kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.pratyavāyā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: For in hostility, there are the disadvantages of loss, expenditure, absence [from home], and [other] adversities.

children.text: KAZ07.2.03/ tena^āsana.yānayor āsanaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: By this, between sitting quiet and marching, sitting quiet is explained [as preferable].

children.text: KAZ07.2.04/ dvaidhī.bhāva.saṃśrayayor dvaidhī.bhāvaṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: Between the dual policy and seeking shelter, one should adopt the dual policy.

children.text: KAZ07.2.05/ dvaidhī.bhūto hi sva.karma.pradhāna ātmana eva^upakaroti, saṃśritas tu parasya^upakaroti, na^ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who has adopted the dual policy, being focused on his own enterprises, benefits himself; but one who has sought shelter benefits another, not himself.

children.text: KAZ07.2.06/ yad.balaḥ sāmantas tad.viśiṣṭa.balam āśrayet //
children.translated_text: One should seek shelter with [a king] whose strength is superior to that of [one's own] neighboring [enemy].

children.text: KAZ07.2.07/ tad.viśiṣṭa.bala.abhāve tam eva^āśritaḥ kośa.daṇḍa.bhūmīnām anyatamena^asya^upakartum adṛṣṭaḥ prayateta //
children.translated_text: In the absence of one with superior strength, having sought shelter with that very [neighboring enemy], one should strive unseen to assist him with any one of treasury, army, or territory.

children.text: KAZ07.2.08/ mahā.doṣo hi viśiṣṭa.bala.samāgamo rājñām, anyatra^ari.vigṛhītāt //
children.translated_text: For the coming together of kings with a superior [in strength] is greatly dangerous — except when one is engaged in hostility with [one's own] enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.2.09/ aśakye daṇḍa.upanatavad varteta //
children.translated_text: When incapable [of resistance], one should conduct oneself as one brought under the rod [of force].

children.text: KAZ07.2.10/ yadā ca^asya prāṇa.haraṃ vyādhim antaḥ.kopaṃ śatru.vṛddhiṃ mitra.vyasanam upasthitaṃ vā tan.nimittām ātmanaś ca vṛddhiṃ paśyet tadā sambhāvya.vyādhi.dharma.kārya.apadeśena^apayāyāt //
children.translated_text: And when one perceives his life-threatening disease, internal revolt, the enemy's growth, an ally's calamity, or one's own growth resulting from these — then, under the pretext of a serious illness or a religious duty, one should withdraw.

children.text: KAZ07.2.11/ sva.viṣayastho vā na^upagacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, being in his own territory, one should not approach [the overlord].

children.text: KAZ07.2.12/ āsanno vā^asya cchidreṣu praharet //
children.translated_text: Or, being nearby, one should strike at his vulnerabilities.

children.text: KAZ07.2.13/ balīyasor vā madhya.gatas trāṇa.samartham āśrayeta, yasya vā^antardhiḥ syāt, ubhau vā //
children.translated_text: Or, caught between two powerful [kings], one should seek shelter with one capable of protection, or one who offers concealment — or both.

children.text: KAZ07.2.14/ kapāla.saṃśrayas tiṣṭhet, mūla.haram itarasya^itaram apadiśan //
children.translated_text: One should remain in a state of 'broken-pot' alliance — pointing each toward the other as [mutually] destructive.

children.text: KAZ07.2.15/ bhedam ubhayor vā paraspara.apadeśaṃ prayuñjīta, bhinnayor upāṃśu.daṇḍam //
children.translated_text: Or one should apply the device of mutual accusation to create a breach between the two; when [the breach is made], one should secretly punish [them].

children.text: KAZ07.2.16/ pārśvastho vā balasthayor āsanna.bhayāt pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: Or, positioned alongside, one should act against the threats from the two powerful [kings] nearby.

children.text: KAZ07.2.17/ durga.apāśrayo vā dvaidhī.bhūtas tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, having taken refuge in a fortress, one should remain in a dual policy.

children.text: KAZ07.2.18/ saṃdhi.vigraha.krama.hetubhir vā ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: Or one should act according to the methods prescribed for treaty and hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.2.19/ dūṣya.amitra.āṭavikān ubhayor upagṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: One should win over the corruptible elements, the enemies, and the forest-chiefs of both.

children.text: KAZ07.2.20/ etayor anyataraṃ gacchaṃs tair eva^anyatarasya vyasane praharet //
children.translated_text: Going over to one of the two, one should, through those very [agents], strike at the other's vulnerability.

children.text: KAZ07.2.21/ dvābhyām upahato vā maṇḍala.apāśrayas tiṣṭhet, madhyamam udāsīnaṃ vā saṃśrayeta //
children.translated_text: Or, having been harmed by both, one should remain supported by [one's own] circle [of allies], or seek shelter with the middle [king] or the neutral [king].

children.text: KAZ07.2.22/ tena saha^ekam upagṛhya^itaram ucchindyād, ubhau vā //
children.translated_text: Together with him, having won over one [of the two powerful kings], one should destroy the other — or both.

children.text: KAZ07.2.23/ dvābhyām ucchinno vā madhyama.udāsīnayos tat.pakṣīyāṇāṃ vā rājñāṃ nyāya.vṛttim āśrayeta //
children.translated_text: Or, having been destroyed by both, one should seek shelter with the middle [king], the neutral [king], or kings allied with them, through righteous conduct.

children.text: KAZ07.2.24/ tulyānāṃ vā yasya prakṛtayaḥ sukhyeyur enam, yatrastho vā śaknuyād ātmānam uddhartum, yatra vā pūrva.puruṣa.ucitā gatir āsannaḥ sambandho vā, mitrāṇi bhūyāṃsy atiśaktimanti vā bhaveyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.2.24/ Or, among equals, [he should seek refuge with] one whose subjects would prosper under him, or from where he could raise himself up, or where the traditional refuge of his ancestors lies with close connections, or where his allies are numerous or exceedingly powerful.

children.text:
KAZ07.2.25ab/ priyo yasya bhaved yo vā priyo^asya kataras tayoḥ /
KAZ07.2.25cd/ priyo yasya sa taṃ gacched ity āśraya.gatiḥ parā //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.2.25ab/ One who is dear to another, or one to whom another is dear — between the two,
KAZ07.2.25cd/ he who is dear [to the protector] should go to him — this is the supreme course of seeking refuge.

children.text:
(sama.hīna.jyāyasāṃ guṇa.abhiniveśaḥ - hīna.saṃdhayah)
KAZ07.3.01/ vijigīṣuḥ śakty.apekṣaḥ ṣāḍguṇyam upayuñjīta //
children.translated_text:
(Engagement of qualities among equals, inferiors, and superiors — peace treaties of the weaker)
KAZ07.3.01/ The would-be conqueror (<s>vijigīṣu</s>), with regard to his own power, should employ the sixfold policy.

children.text: KAZ07.3.02/ sama.jyāyobhyāṃ saṃdhīyeta, hīnena vigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.02/ He should make peace with an equal or a superior; he should wage war against an inferior.

children.text: KAZ07.3.03/ vigṛhīto hi jyāyasā hastinā pāda.yuddham iva^abhyupaiti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.03/ For one who wages war against a superior engages in a foot-fight with an elephant, as it were.

children.text: KAZ07.3.04/ samena ca^āmaṃ pātram āmena^ahatam iva^ubhayataḥ kṣayaṃ karoti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.04/ And [war] with an equal, like an unbaked pot struck by an unbaked pot, causes destruction on both sides.

children.text: KAZ07.3.05/ kumbhena^iva^aśmā hīnena^eka.anta.siddhim avāpnoti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.05/ With an inferior, like a stone [against] a pot, he achieves one-sided victory.

children.text: KAZ07.3.06/ jyāyāṃś cen na saṃdhim icched daṇḍa.upanata.vṛttam ābalīyasaṃ vā yogam ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.06/ If a superior does not wish peace, [the weaker king] should adopt the conduct of one submitting to force, or the strategy of the weaker.

children.text: KAZ07.3.07/ samaś cen na saṃdhim icched yāvan.mātram apakuryāt tāvan.mātram asya pratyapakuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.07/ If an equal does not wish peace, [the king] should retaliate to whatever extent the other harms him.

children.text: KAZ07.3.08/ tejo hi saṃdhāna.kāraṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.08/ For energy is the cause of making peace.

children.text: KAZ07.3.09/ na^ataptaṃ lohaṃ lohena saṃdhatta iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.09/ Unheated iron does not join with [another piece of] iron.

children.text: KAZ07.3.10/ hīnaś cet sarvatra^anupraṇatas tiṣṭhet saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.10/ If inferior, he should bow down in every way, stand [submissive], and seek peace.

children.text: KAZ07.3.11/ āraṇyo^agnir iva hi duḥkha.amarṣajaṃ tejo vikramayati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.11/ For, like a forest fire, the energy born of suffering and indignation drives one to exertion.

children.text: KAZ07.3.12/ maṇḍalasya ca^anugrāhyo bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.12/ And he becomes deserving of support from the circle [of kings].

children.text: KAZ07.3.13/ saṃhitaś cet "para.prakṛtayo lubdha.kṣīṇa.apacaritāḥ pratyādāna.bhayād vā na^upagacchanti" iti paśyedd hīno^api vigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.13/ If [the inferior], having made peace, sees that "the enemy's subjects — greedy, impoverished, or maltreated, or fearing confiscation — do not rally [to their king]," then even an inferior should wage war.

children.text: KAZ07.3.14/ vigṛhītaś cet "para.prakṛtayo lubdha.kṣīṇa.apacaritā vigraha.udvignā vā māṃ na^upagacchanti" iti paśyej jyāyān api saṃdhīyeta, vigraha.udvegaṃ vā śamayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.14/ If, having waged war, [the superior] sees that "the enemy's subjects — greedy, impoverished, maltreated, or alarmed by war — do not come over to me," then even a superior should make peace, or should allay the alarm caused by war.

children.text: KAZ07.3.15/ vyasana.yaugapadye^api "guru.vyasano^asmi, laghu.vyasanaḥ paraḥ sukhena pratikṛtya vyasanam ātmano^abhiyuñjyād" iti paśyej jyāyān api saṃdhīyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.15/ Even in the simultaneous occurrence of calamities, if [the superior] sees that "my calamity is grave while the enemy's is light — he could easily remedy his calamity and then attack me" — then even a superior should make peace.

children.text: KAZ07.3.16/ saṃdhi.vigrahayoś cet para.karśanam ātma.upacayaṃ vā na^abhipaśyej jyāyān apy āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.16/ If, through neither peace nor war, he foresees weakening the enemy or strengthening himself — then even a superior should sit quiet.

children.text: KAZ07.3.17/ para.vyasanam apratikāryaṃ cet paśyedd hīno^apy abhiyāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.17/ If he sees the enemy's calamity as irremediable — then even an inferior should march.

children.text: KAZ07.3.18/ apratikārya.āsanna.vyasano vā jyāyān api saṃśrayeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.18/ Or, if [the king himself] has an irremediable and imminent calamity — then even a superior should seek refuge.

children.text: KAZ07.3.19/ saṃdhinā^ekato vigraheṇa^ekataś cet kārya.siddhiṃ paśyej jyāyān api dvaidhī.bhūtas tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.19/ If he sees the accomplishment of his objective through peace on one side and war on the other — then even a superior should adopt the dual policy.

children.text: KAZ07.3.20/ evaṃ samasya ṣāḍguṇya.upayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.20/ Thus the application of the sixfold policy for an equal.

children.text: KAZ07.3.21/ tatra tu prativiśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.3.21/ But here the specific distinction [for the inferior is as follows]:

children.text:
KAZ07.3.22ab/ pravṛtta.cakreṇa^ākrānto rājñā balavatā^abalaḥ /
KAZ07.3.22cd/ saṃdhinā^upanamet tūrṇaṃ kośa.daṇḍa.ātma.bhūmibhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.22ab/ A weak [king] attacked by a powerful king whose wheel [of conquest] is in motion
KAZ07.3.22cd/ should quickly submit through a peace offering his treasury, army, person, or territory.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.23ab/ svayaṃ saṃkhyāta.daṇḍena daṇḍasya vibhavena vā /
KAZ07.3.23cd/ upasthātavyam ity eṣa saṃdhir ātma.āmiṣo mataḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.23ab/ He should personally attend with a specified army or with whatever force he can muster —
KAZ07.3.23cd/ this is the peace called "self-offering" (<s>ātmāmiṣa</s>).

children.text:
KAZ07.3.24ab/ senā.pati.kumārābhyām upasthātavyam ity ayam /
KAZ07.3.24cd/ puruṣa.antara.saṃdhiḥ syān na^ātmanā^ity ātma.rakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.24ab/ That one should attend through the commander-in-chief or the prince —
KAZ07.3.24cd/ this is the "substitute-person peace" (<s>puruṣāntara</s>), self-protecting because not [attending] in person.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.25ab/ ekena^anyatra yātavyaṃ svayaṃ daṇḍena vā^ity ayam /
KAZ07.3.25cd/ adṛṣṭa.puruṣaḥ saṃdhir daṇḍa.mukhya.ātma.rakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.25ab/ That one should march elsewhere with [the specified] army, or [saying] "with my own" —
KAZ07.3.25cd/ this is the "unseen-person peace" (<s>adṛṣṭapuruṣa</s>), self-protecting with the army as the chief [element].

children.text:
KAZ07.3.26ab/ mukhya.strī.bandhanaṃ kuryāt pūrvayoḥ paścime tv arim /
KAZ07.3.26cd/ sādhayed gūḍham ity ete daṇḍa.upanata.saṃdhayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.26ab/ In the first two, he should seize the chiefs' women as hostages; but in the latter,
KAZ07.3.26cd/ he should subdue the enemy secretly — these are the peace treaties under submission to force.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.27ab/ kośa.dānena śeṣāṇāṃ prakṛtīnāṃ vimokṣaṇam /
KAZ07.3.27cd/ parikrayo bhavet saṃdhiḥ sa eva ca yathā.sukham //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.27ab/ Release of the remaining constituent elements through the gift of the treasury
KAZ07.3.27cd/ constitutes the ransom-peace (<s>parikraya</s>); the same [applies] freely [for the rest].

children.text:
KAZ07.3.28ab/ skandha.upaneyo bahudhā jñeyaḥ saṃdhir upagrahaḥ /
KAZ07.3.28cd/ niruddho deśa.kālābhyām atyayaḥ syād upagrahaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.28ab/ The peace involving submission of the army should be understood as variously [applied as] seizure (<s>upagraha</s>);
KAZ07.3.28cd/ [when] blocked by place and time, a transgressive seizure occurs.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.29ab/ viṣahya.dānād āyatyāṃ kṣamaḥ strī.bandhanād api /
KAZ07.3.29cd/ suvarṇa.saṃdhir viśvāsād ekī.bhāva.gato bhavet //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.29ab/ From a bearable gift, effective in the future and even from the seizing of women [as hostages],
KAZ07.3.29cd/ the gold-peace (<s>suvarṇa-saṃdhi</s>), through trust, may become a complete union.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.30ab/ viparītaḥ kapālaḥ syād atyādāna.abhibhāṣitaḥ /
KAZ07.3.30cd/ pūrvayoḥ praṇayet kupyaṃ hasty.aśvaṃ vā gara.anvitam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.30ab/ The reverse — the broken-piece [peace] (<s>kapāla</s>) — is characterized by excessive demands;
KAZ07.3.30cd/ in the first two [cases], he should deliver goods or poisoned elephants and horses.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.31ab/ tṛtīye praṇayed arthaṃ kathayan karmaṇāṃ kṣayam /
KAZ07.3.31cd/ tiṣṭhec caturtha ity ete kośa.upanata.saṃdhayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.31ab/ In the third, he should deliver wealth while speaking of the ruin of his enterprises;
KAZ07.3.31cd/ in the fourth, he should remain still — these are the peace treaties under submission of the treasury.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.32ab/ bhūmy.eka.deśa.tyāgena śeṣa.prakṛti.rakṣaṇam /
KAZ07.3.32cd/ ādiṣṭa.saṃdhis tatra^iṣṭo gūḍha.stena.upaghātinaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.32ab/ Protection of the remaining constituent elements by abandoning a part of the territory
KAZ07.3.32cd/ is the "commanded peace" (<s>ādiṣṭa</s>); therein is preferred [the territory] infested with secret thieves and raiders.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.33ab/ bhūmīnām ātta.sārāṇāṃ mūla.varjaṃ praṇāmanam /
KAZ07.3.33cd/ ucchinna.saṃdhis tatra^iṣṭaḥ para.vyasana.kāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.33ab/ Surrender of territories whose resources have been extracted, except the core,
KAZ07.3.33cd/ is the "severed peace" (<s>ucchinna</s>); therein is preferred [one who] awaits the enemy's calamity.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.34ab/ phala.dānena bhūmīnāṃ mokṣaṇaṃ syād avakrayaḥ /
KAZ07.3.34cd/ phala.atimukto bhūmibhyaḥ saṃdhiḥ sa paridūṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.34ab/ Release of territories through the gift of their revenue is the "lease-peace" (<s>avakraya</s>);
KAZ07.3.34cd/ released from the territories through revenue — that peace is called "contaminating" (<s>paridūṣaṇa</s>).

children.text:
KAZ07.3.35ab/ kuryād avekṣaṇaṃ pūrvau paścimau tv ābalīyasam /
KAZ07.3.35cd/ ādāya phalam ity ete deśa.upanata.saṃdhayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.35ab/ In the first two, he should adopt a watching stance; in the latter two, the strategy of the weaker;
KAZ07.3.35cd/ taking the revenue — these are the peace treaties under submission of territory.

children.text:
KAZ07.3.36ab/ sva.kāryāṇāṃ vaśena^ete deśe kāle ca bhāṣitāḥ /
KAZ07.3.36cd/ ābalīyasikāḥ kāryās trividhā hīna.saṃdhayaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.3.36ab/ These are to be employed according to one's own interests, [considering] place and time;
KAZ07.3.36cd/ the strategies of the weaker are to be applied — [these are] the three types of inferior peace treaties.

children.text:
(vigṛhya.āsanaṃ - saṃdhāya.āsanaṃ - vigṛhya.yānaṃ - saṃdhāya.yānaṃ - sambhūya.prayāṇam)
KAZ07.4.01/ saṃdhi.vigrahayor āsanaṃ yānaṃ ca vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text:
(Sitting quiet after hostility — Sitting quiet after peace — Marching after hostility — Marching after peace — Joint expedition)
KAZ07.4.01/ Sitting quiet and marching, in [the context of] peace and war, have been explained.

children.text: KAZ07.4.02/ sthānam āsanam upekṣaṇaṃ ca^ity āsana.paryāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.02/ Staying, sitting, and disregard — these are synonyms for sitting quiet.

children.text: KAZ07.4.03/ viśeṣas tu - guṇa.ekadeśe sthānam, sva.vṛddhi.prāpty.artham āsanam, upāyānām aprayoga upekṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.03/ But the distinction is: staying is [remaining] at one point of advantage; sitting is [remaining] for the purpose of gaining one's own growth; disregard is the non-employment of strategies.

children.text: KAZ07.4.04/ atisaṃdhāna.kāmayor ari.vijigīṣvor upahantum aśaktayor vigṛhya^āsanaṃ saṃdhāya vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.04/ For two — an enemy and a would-be conqueror — who wish to outwit [each other] and are unable to destroy [each other]: sitting quiet after hostility or after peace.

children.text: KAZ07.4.05/ yadā vā paśyet "sva.daṇḍair mitra.aṭavī.daṇḍair vā samaṃ jyāyāṃsaṃ vā karśayitum utsahe" iti tadā kṛta.bāhya.abhyantara.kṛtyo vigṛhya^āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.05/ Or, when he sees: "With my own forces, or with the forces of allies and forest-tribes, I am able to weaken an equal or even a superior" — then, having accomplished both external and internal tasks, he should sit quiet after hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.4.06/ yadā vā paśyet "utsāha.yuktā me prakṛtayaḥ saṃhatā vivṛddhāḥ sva.karmāṇy avyāhatāś cariṣyanti parasya vā karmāṇy upahaniṣyanti" iti tadā vigṛhya^āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.06/ Or, when he sees: "My subjects, endowed with enterprise, united and prosperous, will carry out their own tasks without hindrance, or will hinder the enemy's tasks" — then he should sit quiet after hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.4.07a/ yadā vā paśyet "parasya^apacaritāḥ kṣīṇā lubdhāḥ sva.cakra.stena.aṭavī.vyathitā vā prakṛtayaḥ svayam upajāpena vā mām eṣyanti, sampannā me vārttā, vipannā parasya, tasya prakṛtayo durbhikṣa.upahatā mām eṣyanti; vipannā me vārttā, sampannā parasya, - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.07a/ Or, when he sees: "The enemy's subjects — maltreated, impoverished, greedy, or harassed by his own circle, thieves, and forest-tribes — will come to me of their own accord or through instigation; my economy is thriving while the enemy's is ruined, and his subjects, afflicted by famine, will come to me; my economy is ruined while the enemy's is thriving —

children.text: KAZ07.4.07b/ taṃ me prakṛtayo na gamiṣyanti, vigṛhya ca^asya dhānya.paśu.hiraṇyāny āhariṣyāmi, sva.paṇya.upaghātīni vā para.paṇyāni nivartayiṣyāmi, - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.07b/ [but] my subjects will not go to him, and by waging war I shall seize his grain, cattle, and gold, or I shall block his trade goods that are harmful to my own trade —

children.text: KAZ07.4.07c/ para.vaṇik.pathād vā saravanti mām eṣyanti vigṛhīte, na^itaram, dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.nigrahaṃ vā vigṛhīto na kariṣyati, tair eva vā vigrahaṃ prāpsyati, - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.07c/ or, through the enemy's trade-route, merchants will come to me if I wage war, but not otherwise; or, [the enemy] when hostile will not be able to suppress his targets, enemies, and forest-tribes, or will come into conflict with them —

children.text: KAZ07.4.07d/ mitraṃ me mitra.bhāvy abhiprayāto bahv.alpa.kālaṃ tanu.kṣaya.vyayam arthaṃ prāpsyati, guṇavatīm ādeyāṃ vā bhūmim, - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.07d/ my ally or potential ally, having marched forth, will obtain much wealth in a short time with little loss and expenditure, or will [acquire] a territory that is rich and worth taking —

children.text: KAZ07.4.07e/ sarva.saṃdohena vā mām anādṛtya prayātu.kāmaḥ kathaṃ na yāyād" iti para.vṛddhi.pratighāta.arthaṃ pratāpa.arthaṃ ca vigṛhya^āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.07e/ or, intending to march forth with all his forces while disregarding me — how could he not march?" — to counter the enemy's growth and to display prowess, he should sit quiet after hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.4.08/ "tam eva hi pratyāvṛtto grasate" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.08/ "For, having turned back, he [the enemy] devours that very [neglected king]" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.4.09/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.09/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.4.10/ karśana.mātram asya kuryād avyasaninaḥ, para.vṛddhyā tu vṛddhaḥ samucchedanam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.10/ He should only weaken [the enemy] if [the enemy is] free from calamity; but one who has grown through the enemy's growth [should be subjected to] total destruction.

children.text: KAZ07.4.11/ evaṃ parasya yātavyo^asmai sāhāyyam avinaṣṭaḥ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.11/ Thus, when the enemy is about to march against [another], [the king], unharmed, should offer him assistance.

children.text: KAZ07.4.12/ tasmāt sarva.saṃdoha.prakṛtaṃ vigṛhya^āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.12/ Therefore, he should sit quiet after hostility directed at the full-scale deployment [of the enemy].

children.text: KAZ07.4.13/ vigṛhya.āsana.hetu.prātilomye saṃdhāya^āsīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.13/ When the reasons for sitting quiet after hostility are reversed, he should sit quiet after peace.

children.text: KAZ07.4.14/ vigṛhya.āsana.hetubhir abhyuccitaḥ sarva.saṃdoha.varjaṃ vigṛhya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.14/ When empowered by the reasons for sitting quiet after hostility, he should march after hostility — excluding a full-scale deployment.

children.text: KAZ07.4.15/ yadā vā paśyet "vyasanī paraḥ, prakṛti.vyasanaṃ vā^asya śeeṣa.prakṛtibhir apratikāryam, sva.cakra.pīḍitā viraktā vā^asya prakṛtayaḥ karśitā nirutsāhāḥ parasparād vā bhinnāḥ śakyā lobhayitum, agny.udaka.vyādhi.maraka.durbhikṣa.nimittaṃ kṣīṇa.yugya.puruṣa.nicaya.rakṣā.vidhānaḥ paraḥ" iti tadā vigṛhya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.15/ Or, when he sees: "The enemy is in calamity; or his calamity of constituent elements is irremediable by the remaining elements; his subjects, oppressed by his own circle, are disaffected, weakened, and without enterprise, or are divided among themselves and can be enticed with greed; or the enemy's store of yoked [animals], manpower, reserves, and defenses is depleted through fire, flood, disease, epidemic, or famine" — then he should march after hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.4.16/ yadā vā paśyet "mitram ākrandaś ca me śūra.vṛddha.anurakta.prakṛtiḥ, viparīta.prakṛtiḥ paraḥ pārṣṇi.grāhaś ca^āsāraś ca, śakṣyāmi mitreṇa^āsāram ākrandena pārṣṇi.grāhaṃ vā vigṛhya yātum" iti tadā vigṛhya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.16/ Or, when he sees: "My ally and the supporter [of my rear] have subjects [who are] brave, mature, and loyal; the enemy and the one who strikes at my rear have adverse subjects and are vulnerable; I shall be able to march after hostility, [using] the ally against the vulnerable one and the supporter against the one who strikes at my rear" — then he should march after hostility.

children.text: KAZ07.4.17/ yadā vā phalam eka.hāryam alpa.kālaṃ paśyet tadā pārṣṇi.grāha.āsārābhyāṃ vigṛhya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.17/ Or, when he sees a prize that can be seized by one [effort], in a short time — then he should march after hostility against [both] the one who strikes at the rear and the vulnerable one.

children.text: KAZ07.4.18/ viparyaye saṃdhāya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.18/ In the reverse situation, he should march after peace.

children.text: KAZ07.4.19/ yadā vā paśyet "na śakyam ekena yātum avaśyaṃ ca yātavyam" iti tadā sama.hīna.jyāyobhiḥ sāmavāyikaiḥ sambhūya yāyād, ekatra nirdiṣṭena^aṃśena, anekatra^anirdiṣṭena^aṃśena //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.19/ Or, when he sees: "It is not possible to march alone, yet marching is absolutely necessary" — then he should march jointly with equals, inferiors, or superiors as confederates, with a specified share if [marching] to one place, with an unspecified share if to many.

children.text: KAZ07.4.20/ teṣām asamavāye daṇḍam anyatamasmān niviṣṭa.aṃśena yāceta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.20/ If they disagree, he should demand a force from any one of them in proportion to their committed share.

children.text: KAZ07.4.21/ sambhūya.abhigamanena vā nirviśyeta, dhruve lābhe nirdiṣṭena^aṃśena, adhruve lābha.aṃśena //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.4.21/ Or, he should invest [the proceeds] through a joint expedition — with a specified share when the gain is certain, with a proportional share of the gain when uncertain.

children.text:
KAZ07.4.22ab/ aṃśo daṇḍa.samaḥ pūrvaḥ prayāsa.sama uttamaḥ /
KAZ07.4.22cd/ vilopo vā yathā.lābhaṃ prakṣepa.sama eva vā //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.4.22ab/ The first share is equal to the army [contributed]; the best is equal to the effort;
KAZ07.4.22cd/ or [there is] plunder according to [actual] gain, or equal to the investment.

children.text:
(yātavya.amitrayor abhigraha.cintāḥ - kṣaya.lobha.virāga.hetavaḥ prakṛtīnāṃ - sāmavāyika.viparimarśah)
KAZ07.5.01/ tulya.sāmanta.vyasane yātavyam amitraṃ vā^ity amitram abhiyāyāt, tat.siddhau yātavyam //
children.translated_text:
(Deliberation on seizing the enemy to be attacked or the one to be attacked — Causes of decline, greed, and disaffection among the constituent elements — Review of confederates)
KAZ07.5.01/ When both the one to be attacked and the enemy have equal neighboring calamities — he should attack the enemy; upon his defeat, [then attack] the one to be attacked.

children.text: KAZ07.5.02/ amitra.siddhau hi yātavyaḥ sāhāyyaṃ dadyān na^amitro yātavya.siddhau //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.02/ For upon defeating the enemy, the one to be attacked would offer assistance; but the enemy would not [offer assistance] upon defeat of the one to be attacked.

children.text: KAZ07.5.03/ guru.vyasanaṃ yātavyaṃ laghu.vyasanam amitraṃ vā^iti "guru.vyasanaṃ saukaryato yāyād" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.03/ [If] the one to be attacked has a grave calamity and the enemy a light one — "He should attack the one with the grave calamity because of the ease" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.5.04/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.04/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.5.05/ laghu.vyasanam amitraṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.05/ He should attack the enemy with the light calamity.

children.text: KAZ07.5.06/ laghv api hi vyasanam abhiyuktasya kṛcchraṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.06/ For even a light calamity becomes severe for one who is attacked.

children.text: KAZ07.5.07/ satyaṃ gurv api gurutaraṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.07/ True, a grave one becomes even graver [when attacked].

children.text: KAZ07.5.08/ anabhiyuktas tu laghu.vyasanaḥ sukhena vyasanaṃ pratikṛtya^amitro yātavyam abhisaret, pārṣṇiṃ vā gṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.08/ But one with a light calamity who is not attacked can easily remedy his calamity and then approach the one to be attacked, or he could strike at the rear.

children.text: KAZ07.5.09/ yātavya.yaugapadye guru.vyasanaṃ nyāya.vṛttiṃ laghu.vyasanam anyāya.vṛttiṃ virakta.prakṛtiṃ vā^iti virakta.prakṛtiṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.09/ When [there is a choice of] two targets to march against simultaneously — one with a grave calamity but righteous conduct, one with a minor calamity but unrighteous conduct, and one with disaffected subjects — he should march against the one with disaffected subjects.

children.text: KAZ07.5.10/ guru.vyasanaṃ nyāya.vṛttim abhiyuktaṃ prakṛtayo^anugṛhṇanti, laghu.vyasanam anyāya.vṛttim upekṣante, viraktā balavantam apy ucchindanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.10/ When one with a grave calamity but righteous conduct is attacked, his subjects support him; one with a minor calamity but unrighteous conduct, they ignore; the disaffected destroy even a powerful one.

children.text: KAZ07.5.11/ tasmād virakta.prakṛtim eva yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.11/ Therefore, he should march against precisely the one with disaffected subjects.

children.text: KAZ07.5.12/ kṣīṇa.lubdha.prakṛtim apacarita.prakṛtiṃ vā^iti kṣīṇa.lubdha.prakṛtiṃ yāyāt, kṣīṇa.lubdhā hi prakṛtayaḥ sukhena^upajāpaṃ pīḍāṃ vā^upagacchanti, na^apacaritāḥ pradhāna.avagraha.sādhyāḥ" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.12/ 'Between one with impoverished and greedy subjects and one with ill-treated subjects — he should march against the one with impoverished and greedy subjects, for impoverished and greedy subjects easily succumb to enticement or oppression, but ill-treated ones can only be won over by seizing their leaders' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.5.13/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.13/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.5.14/ kṣīṇa.lubdhā hi prakṛtayo bhartari snigdhā bhartṛ.hite tiṣṭhanti, upajāpaṃ vā visaṃvādayanti, anurāge sārvaguṇyam iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.14/ For impoverished and greedy subjects, being attached to their master, stand firm in their master's interest, or else they expose the [enemy's] enticement — devotion has all-round virtue.

children.text: KAZ07.5.15/ tasmād apacarita.prakṛtim eva yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.15/ Therefore, he should march against precisely the one with ill-treated subjects.

children.text: KAZ07.5.16/ balavantam anyāya.vṛttiṃ durbalaṃ vā nyāya.vṛttim iti balavantam anyāya.vṛttiṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.16/ Between a powerful one with unrighteous conduct and a weak one with righteous conduct — he should march against the powerful one with unrighteous conduct.

children.text: KAZ07.5.17/ balavantam anyāya.vṛttim abhiyuktaṃ prakṛtayo na^anugṛhṇanti, niṣpātayanti, amitraṃ vā^asya bhajante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.17/ When a powerful one with unrighteous conduct is attacked, his subjects do not support him; they topple him, or go over to his enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.5.18/ durbalaṃ tu nyāya.vṛttim abhiyuktaṃ prakṛtayaḥ parigṛhṇanti, anuniṣpatanti vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.18/ But when a weak one with righteous conduct is attacked, his subjects protect him, or follow him [into exile].

children.text:
KAZ07.5.19ab/ avakṣepeṇa hi satām asatāṃ pragraheṇa ca /
KAZ07.5.19cd/ abhūtānāṃ ca hiṃsānām adharmyāṇāṃ pravartanaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.19ab/ For by disparaging the good and promoting the wicked,
KAZ07.5.19cd/ by initiating acts of harm that are unjust,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.20ab/ ucitānāṃ caritrāṇāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ nivartanaiḥ /
KAZ07.5.20cd/ adharmasya prasaṅgena dharmasya^avagraheṇa ca //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.20ab/ by stopping customary practices that are righteous,
KAZ07.5.20cd/ by promoting <s>adharma</s> and obstructing <s>dharma</s>,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.21ab/ akāryāṇāṃ ca karaṇaiḥ kāryāṇāṃ ca praṇāśanaiḥ /
KAZ07.5.21cd/ apradānaiś ca deyānām adeyānāṃ ca sādhanaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.21ab/ by doing what should not be done and destroying what should be done,
KAZ07.5.21cd/ by not giving what should be given and exacting what should not be taken,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.22ab/ adaṇḍanaiś ca daṇḍyānām adaṇḍyānāṃ ca daṇḍanaiḥ /
KAZ07.5.22cd/ agrāhyāṇām upagrāhair grāhyāṇāṃ ca^anabhigrahaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.22ab/ by not punishing the punishable and punishing the unpunishable,
KAZ07.5.22cd/ by arresting those who should not be arrested and not arresting those who should be,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.23ab/ anarthyānāṃ ca karaṇair arthyānāṃ ca vighātanaiḥ /
KAZ07.5.23cd/ arakṣaṇaiś ca corebhyaḥ svayaṃ ca parimoṣaṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.23ab/ by doing what is unprofitable and thwarting what is profitable,
KAZ07.5.23cd/ by not protecting from thieves and himself plundering,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.24ab/ pātaiḥ puruṣa.kārāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ guṇa.dūṣaṇaiḥ /
KAZ07.5.24cd/ upaghātaiḥ pradhānānāṃ mānyānāṃ ca^avamānanaiḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.24ab/ by ruining the works of meritorious men and corrupting their qualities,
KAZ07.5.24cd/ by injuring the prominent and dishonoring the honorable,

children.text:
KAZ07.5.25ab/ virodhanaiś ca vṛddhānāṃ vaiṣamyeṇa^anṛtena ca /
KAZ07.5.25cd/ kṛtasya^apratikāreṇa sthitasya^akaraṇena ca //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.25ab/ by antagonizing the elders, by unfairness and falsehood,
KAZ07.5.25cd/ by not rewarding the accomplished and not carrying out the established —

children.text:
KAZ07.5.26ab/ rājñaḥ pramāda.ālasyābhyāṃ yoga.kṣema.vadhena vā /
KAZ07.5.26cd/ prakṛtīnāṃ kṣayo lobho vairāgyaṃ ca^upajāyate //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.26ab/ through the king's negligence and laziness, or the destruction of livelihood and security,
KAZ07.5.26cd/ there arise impoverishment, greed, and disaffection among the subjects.

children.text:
KAZ07.5.27ab/ kṣīṇāḥ prakṛtayo lobhaṃ lubdhā yānti virāgatām /
KAZ07.5.27cd/ viraktā yānty amitraṃ vā bhartāraṃ ghnanti vā svayam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.27ab/ Impoverished subjects become greedy; the greedy become disaffected;
KAZ07.5.27cd/ the disaffected go over to the enemy, or they kill their own master.

children.text: KAZ07.5.28/ tasmāt prakṛtīnāṃ kṣaya.lobha.virāga.kāraṇāni na^utpādayet, utpannāni vā sadyaḥ pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.28/ Therefore, he should not give rise to the causes of impoverishment, greed, and disaffection among the subjects; or, once arisen, he should immediately counteract them.

children.text: KAZ07.5.29/ kṣīṇā lubdhā viraktā vā prakṛtaya iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.29/ The subjects are either impoverished, greedy, or disaffected.

children.text: KAZ07.5.30/ kṣīṇāḥ pīḍana.ucchedana.bhayāt sadyaḥ saṃdhiṃ yuddhaṃ niṣpatanaṃ vā rocayante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.30/ The impoverished, from fear of oppression and destruction, quickly favor a peace treaty, war, or emigration.

children.text: KAZ07.5.31/ lubdhā lobhena^asaṃtuṣṭāḥ para.upajāpaṃ lipsante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.31/ The greedy, unsatisfied by their greed, welcome the enemy's enticement.

children.text: KAZ07.5.32/ viraktāḥ para.abhiyogam abhyuttiṣṭhante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.32/ The disaffected rise up to support the enemy's attack.

children.text: KAZ07.5.33/ tāsāṃ hiraṇya.dhānya.kṣayaḥ sarva.upaghātī kṛcchra.pratīkāraś ca, yugya.puruṣa.kṣayo hiraṇya.dhānya.sādhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.33/ Among these, depletion of gold and grain is destructive of all and difficult to remedy; depletion of draft-animals and men can be remedied with gold and grain.

children.text: KAZ07.5.34/ lobha aikadeśiko mukhya.āyattaḥ para.artheṣu śakyaḥ pratihantum ādātuṃ vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.34/ Greed is localized, dependent on leaders, and can be countered or satisfied through the enemy's resources.

children.text: KAZ07.5.35/ virāgaḥ pradhāna.avagraha.sādhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.35/ Disaffection can be remedied by seizing the leaders.

children.text: KAZ07.5.36/ niṣpradhānā hi prakṛtayo bhogyā bhavanty anupajāpyāś ca^anyeṣām, anāpat.sahās tu //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.36/ For subjects without leaders become exploitable and cannot be enticed by others — but they are unable to withstand calamities.

children.text: KAZ07.5.37/ prakṛti.mukhya.pragrahais tu bahudhā bhinnā guptā bhavanty āpat.sahāś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.37/ But subjects, when diversely split by seizure of their leaders, become controllable and able to withstand calamities.

children.text: KAZ07.5.38/ sāmavāyikānām api saṃdhi.vigraha.kāraṇāny avekṣya śakti.śauca.yuktaiḥ sambhūya yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.38/ Even for confederates, having considered the causes of peace and war, he should march together with those who are powerful and trustworthy.

children.text: KAZ07.5.39/ śaktimān hi pārṣṇi.grahaṇe yātrā.sāhāyya.dāne vā śaktaḥ, śuciḥ siddhau ca^asiddhau ca yathā.sthita.kārī^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.39/ For the powerful one is capable of protecting the rear or providing help on the march; the trustworthy one, whether in success or failure, acts as he stands [by his word].

children.text: KAZ07.5.40/ teṣāṃ jyāyasā^ekena dvābhyāṃ samābhyāṃ vā sambhūya yātavyam iti dvābhyāṃ samābhyāṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.40/ Among them, [the choice of] marching with one who is stronger or with two who are equal — two equals are better.

children.text: KAZ07.5.41/ jyāyasā hy avagṛhītaś carati, samābhyām atisaṃdhāna.ādhikye vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.41/ For one controlled by a stronger ally acts under constraint; with two equals, [there is] superiority in mutual outwitting.

children.text: KAZ07.5.42/ tau hi sukhau bhedayitum, duṣṭaś ca^eko dvābhyāṃ niyantuṃ bheda.upagrahaṃ ca^upagantum iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.42/ For two [equals] are easy to divide; and one who becomes treacherous can be controlled by two, [who can also] bring about his division and subjugation.

children.text: KAZ07.5.43/ samena^ekena dvābhyāṃ hīnābhyāṃ vā^iti dvābhyāṃ hīnābhyāṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.43/ [The choice of] one equal or two who are weaker — two weaker ones are better.

children.text: KAZ07.5.44/ tau hi dvi.kārya.sādhakau vaśyau ca bhavataḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.5.44/ For they accomplish the task of two and are manageable.

children.text:
KAZ07.5.45ab/ kārya.siddhau tu - kṛta.arthāj jyāyaso gūḍhaḥ sa.apadeśam apasravet /
KAZ07.5.45cd/ aśuceḥ śuci.vṛttāt tu pratīkṣeta^ā visarjanāt //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.45ab/ Upon the task's completion — from an ally who is stronger and has achieved his aim, one should secretly withdraw with a pretext;
KAZ07.5.45cd/ from one who is untrustworthy but acting virtuously, one should watch until the dismissal.

children.text:
KAZ07.5.46ab/ sattrād apasared yattaḥ kalatram apanīya vā /
KAZ07.5.46cd/ samād api hi labdha.arthād viśvas tasya bhayaṃ bhavet //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.46ab/ He should withdraw carefully from the camp, removing his dependents;
KAZ07.5.46cd/ for even from an equal who has gained his objective, trust [breeds] fear.

children.text:
KAZ07.5.47ab/ jyāyastve ca^api labdha.arthaḥ samo^api parikalpate /
KAZ07.5.47cd/ abhyuccitaś ca^aviśvāsyo vṛddhiś citta.vikāriṇī //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.47ab/ And even one who is superior, having achieved his aim, is regarded as an equal;
KAZ07.5.47cd/ and one who has grown [in power] is untrustworthy — prosperity alters the mind.

children.text:
KAZ07.5.48ab/ viśiṣṭād alpam apy aṃśaṃ labdhvā tuṣṭa.mukho vrajet /
KAZ07.5.48cd/ anaṃśo vā tato^asya^aṅke prahṛtya dvi.guṇaṃ haret //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.48ab/ Having received even a small share from a superior, he should depart with a pleased face;
KAZ07.5.48cd/ or without a share, he should, after striking at his [the superior's] weak point, take twice [as much].

children.text:
KAZ07.5.49ab/ kṛta.arthas tu svayaṃ netā visṛjet sāmavāyikān /
KAZ07.5.49cd/ api jīyeta na jayen maṇḍala.iṣṭas tathā bhavet //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.5.49ab/ But the leader who has accomplished his task should himself dismiss the confederates;
KAZ07.5.49cd/ even if he suffers loss rather than wins — so shall he be esteemed in the circle [of kings].

children.text:
(saṃhita.prayāṇikaṃ - paripaṇita.aparipaṇita.apasṛtāḥ saṃdhayah)
KAZ07.6.01/ vijigīṣur dvitīyāṃ prakṛtim evam atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Joint march — stipulated, unstipulated, and withdrawn treaties)
KAZ07.6.01/ Thus the <s>vijigīṣu</s> (would-be conqueror) should outwit the second constituent element [the ally].

children.text: KAZ07.6.02/ sāmantaṃ saṃhita.prayāṇe yojayet "tvam ito yāhi, aham ito yāsyāmi, samāno lābhaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.02/ He should engage a neighboring king in a joint march: 'You march in this direction; I shall march in that direction. Equal shares [of the spoils].'

children.text: KAZ07.6.03/ lābha.sāmye saṃdhiḥ, vaiṣamye vikramaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.03/ When the shares are equal, it is a treaty; when unequal, [it is occasion for] aggression.

children.text: KAZ07.6.04/ saṃdhiḥ paripaṇitaś ca^aparipaṇitaś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.04/ A treaty is either stipulated or unstipulated.

children.text: KAZ07.6.05/ "tvam etaṃ deśaṃ yāhi, aham imaṃ deśaṃ yāsyāmi" iti paripaṇita.deśaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.05/ 'You attack this region; I shall attack that region' — this is stipulated as to region.

children.text: KAZ07.6.06/ "tvam etāvantaṃ kālaṃ ceṣṭasva, aham etāvantaṃ kālaṃ ceṣṭiṣye" iti paripaṇita.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.06/ 'You operate for this much time; I shall operate for this much time' — this is stipulated as to time.

children.text: KAZ07.6.07/ "tvam etāvat.kāryaṃ sādhaya, aham idaṃ kāryaṃ sādhayiṣyāmi" iti paripaṇita.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.07/ 'You accomplish this task; I shall accomplish that task' — this is stipulated as to objective.

children.text: KAZ07.6.08/ yadi vā manyeta "śaila.vana.nadī.durgam aṭavī.vyavahitaṃ chinna.dhānya.puruṣa.vīvadha.āsāram ayavasa.indhana.udakam avijñātaṃ prakṛṣṭam anya.bhāva.deśīyaṃ vā sainya.vyāyāmānām alabdha.bhaumaṃ vā deśaṃ paro yāsyati, viparītam aham" ity etasmin viśeṣe paripaṇita.deśaṃ saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.08/ Or if he thinks: 'The other will march through terrain that is mountainous, forested, river-cut, fortified, separated by wilderness, stripped of grain, men, and fodder, lacking fuel, forage, and water, unknown, distant, belonging to another [hostile] power, or unfavorable for military maneuvers; while mine is the opposite' — in this advantageous situation, he should enter a treaty stipulated as to region.

children.text: KAZ07.6.09/ yadi vā manyeta "pravarṣa.uṣṇa.śītam ativyādhi.prāyam upakṣīṇa.āhāra.upabhogaṃ sainya.vyāyāmānāṃ ca^auparodhikaṃ kārya.sādhanānām ūnam atiriktaṃ vā kālaṃ paraś ceṣṭiṣyate, viparītam aham" ity etasmin viśeṣe paripaṇita.kālaṃ saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.09/ Or if he thinks: 'The other will operate during a season of excessive rain, heat, or cold, prone to many diseases, with depleted supplies and provisions, obstructive for military maneuvers, and with too little or too much time for accomplishing the task; while mine is the opposite' — in this advantageous situation, he should enter a treaty stipulated as to time.

children.text: KAZ07.6.10/ yadi vā manyeta "pratyādeyaṃ prakṛti.kopakaṃ dīrgha.kālaṃ mahā.kṣaya.vyayam alpam anartha.anubandham akalyam adharmyaṃ madhyama.udāsīna.viruddhaṃ mitra.upaghātakaṃ vā kāryaṃ paraḥ sādhayiṣyati, viparītam aham" ity etasmin viśeṣe paripaṇita.arthaṃ saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.10/ Or if he thinks: 'The other will accomplish a task that is revocable, provoking to the subjects, time-consuming, involving great loss and expenditure, yielding small returns, followed by disadvantage, fraught with danger, unrighteous, opposed by the middle and neutral [kings], or harmful to allies; while mine is the opposite' — in this advantageous situation, he should enter a treaty stipulated as to objective.

children.text: KAZ07.6.11/ evaṃ deśa.kālayoḥ kāla.kāryayor deśa.kāryayor deśa.kāla.kāryāṇāṃ ca^avasthāpanāt sapta.vidhaḥ paripaṇitaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.11/ Thus, through combinations of region and time, time and objective, region and objective, and region, time, and objective — the stipulated [treaty] is sevenfold.

children.text: KAZ07.6.12/ tasmin prāg eva^ārabhya pratiṣṭhāpya ca sva.karmāṇi para.karmasu vikrameta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.12/ In such a [treaty], he should begin and establish his own operations first, and then strike at the enemy's operations.

children.text: KAZ07.6.13/ vyasana.tvara.avamāna.ālasya.yuktam ajñaṃ vā śatrum atisaṃdhātu.kāmo deśa.kāla.kāryāṇām anavasthāpanāt "saṃhitau svaḥ" iti saṃdhi.viśvāsena parac.chidram āsādya prahared ity aparipaṇitaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.13/ Wishing to outwit an enemy who is afflicted by calamity, haste, humiliation, or laziness, or who is ignorant — through the non-stipulation of region, time, or objective, [saying] 'We are united,' he should, through the confidence of the treaty, find the enemy's weakness and strike. This is the unstipulated [treaty].

children.text: KAZ07.6.14/ tatra^etad bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.14/ In this regard, the following applies:

children.text:
KAZ07.6.15ab/ sāmantena^eva sāmantaṃ vidvān āyojya vigrahe /
KAZ07.6.15cd/ tato^anyasya hared bhūmiṃ chittvā pakṣaṃ samantataḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.6.15ab/ The wise one, having pitted a neighboring king against [another] neighboring king in war,
KAZ07.6.15cd/ should then seize the land of the other, having cut down his party on all sides.

children.text: KAZ07.6.16/ saṃdher akṛta.cikīrṣā kṛta.śleṣaṇaṃ kṛta.vidūṣaṇam avaśīrṇa.kriyā ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.16/ [The aspects of] a treaty are: the desire before it is made, the cementing after it is made, the corrupting of [the other party's treaty], and the withdrawal from its operation.

children.text: KAZ07.6.17/ vikramasya prakāśa.yuddhaṃ kūṭa.yuddhaṃ tūṣṇīṃ.yuddham //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.17/ [The aspects of] aggression are: open battle, deceptive battle, and silent [covert] battle.

children.text: KAZ07.6.18/ iti saṃdhi.vikramau //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.18/ Thus treaty and aggression.

children.text: KAZ07.6.19/ apūrvasya saṃdheḥ sa.anubandhaiḥ sāma.ādibhiḥ paryeṣaṇaṃ sama.hīna.jyāyasāṃ ca yathā.balam avasthāpanam akṛta.cikīrṣā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.19/ The desire [for a new treaty]: approaching [potential allies] with conciliation and other means accompanied by [appropriate] inducements, and arranging equal, weaker, and stronger [partners] according to their strength — this is the desire before it is made.

children.text: KAZ07.6.20/ kṛtasya priya.hitābhyām ubhayataḥ paripālanaṃ yathā.sambhāṣitasya ca nibandhanasya^anuvartanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ ca "kathaṃ parasmān na bhidyeta" iti kṛta.śleṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.20/ The cementing [of a treaty]: protecting [it] on both sides through what is dear and beneficial, and following and guarding the stipulated agreement — [thinking:] 'How can the other not break it?' — this is the cementing of what has been made.

children.text: KAZ07.6.21/ parasya^apasaṃdheyatāṃ dūṣya.atisaṃdhānena sthāpayitvā vyatikramaḥ kṛta.vidūṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.21/ Having established the other's [treaty] as violable through an expendable spy's provocation, [one's own] breach [of the other's treaty] — this is the corrupting.

children.text: KAZ07.6.22/ bhṛtyena mitreṇa vā doṣa.apasṛtena pratisaṃdhānam avaśīrṇa.kriyā //
