children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.22/ Making a counter-treaty through a servant or ally who has defected on account of [fabricated] faults — this is the withdrawn operation.

children.text: KAZ07.6.23/ tasyāṃ gata.āgataś catur.vidhaḥ - kāraṇād gata.āgato, viparītaḥ, kāraṇād gato^akāraṇād āgato, viparītaś ca^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.23/ In that [withdrawn operation], the defector is of four kinds: one who went and returned with cause, one who is the opposite, one who went with cause and returned without cause, and one who is the opposite.

children.text: KAZ07.6.24/ svāmino doṣeṇa gato guṇena^āgataḥ parasya guṇena gato doṣeṇa^āgata iti kāraṇād gata.āgataḥ saṃdheyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.24/ One who left due to the master's fault and returned due to [his] virtue, or who went to the other due to [the other's] virtue and returned due to [the other's] fault — [such a one,] who went and returned with cause, should be accepted in a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.6.25/ sva.doṣeṇa gata.āgato guṇam ubhayoḥ parityajya akāraṇād gata.āgataḥ cala.buddhir asaṃdheyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.25/ One who went and returned due to his own faults, or who abandoned the virtues of both and went and returned without cause — [such a one is] of fickle mind and should not be accepted in a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.6.26/ svāmino doṣeṇa gataḥ parasmāt sva.doṣeṇa^āgata iti kāraṇād gato^akāraṇād āgataḥ tarkayitavyaḥ "para.prayuktaḥ svena vā doṣeṇa^apakartu.kāmaḥ, parasya^ucchettāram amitraṃ me jñātvā pratighāta.bhayād āgataḥ, paraṃ vā mām ucchettu.kāmaṃ parityajya^ānṛśaṃsyād āgataḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.26/ One who left due to the master's fault and returned from the other due to his own fault — [one who] went with cause and returned without cause — should be assessed: 'Is he sent by the enemy, or, wishing to do harm from his own fault? Has he come back out of fear of retaliation, knowing the other to be a destroyer-enemy of mine? Or has he come back out of compassion, abandoning the other who wished to destroy me?'

children.text: KAZ07.6.27/ jñātvā kalyāṇa.buddhiṃ pūjayed, anyathā.buddhim apakṛṣṭaṃ vāsayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.27/ If his intention is found to be benign, he should be honored; if otherwise, he should be settled in a remote [location].

children.text: KAZ07.6.28/ sva.doṣeṇa gataḥ para.doṣeṇa^āgata ity akāraṇād gataḥ kāraṇād āgataḥ tarkayitavyaḥ " chidraṃ me pūrayiṣyati, ucito^ayam asya vāsaḥ, paratra^asya jano na ramate, mitrair me saṃhitaḥ, śatrubhir vigṛhītaḥ, lubdha.krūrād āvignaḥ śatru.saṃhitād vā parasmāt" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.6.28/ One who left due to his own fault and returned due to the other's fault — [one who] went without cause and returned with cause — should be assessed: 'He will fill my gap [in resources]; this is his accustomed abode; his people do not enjoy [life] elsewhere; he is allied with my friends; he is at enmity with my enemies; he has fled in alarm from an other who is greedy, cruel, or allied with [my] enemy.'

children.text: KAZ07.6.29/ jñātvā yathā.buddhy avasthāpayitavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained [the nature of the refugee], one should settle him according to one's own judgment.

children.text: KAZ07.6.30/ "kṛta.praṇāśaḥ śakti.hānir vidyā.paṇyatvam āśā.nirvedo deśa.laulyam aviśvāso balavad.vigraho vā parityāga.sthānam" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Destruction of [one's] accomplishments, loss of power, peddling of [one's] learning, weariness of expectations, restlessness in territory, loss of trust, or conflict with a powerful [king] — these are the grounds for abandoning [a refugee]' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.6.31/ bhayam avṛttir amarṣa iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Fear, lack of livelihood, and indignation' — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.6.32/ iha^apakārī tyājyaḥ, para.apakārī saṃdheyaḥ, ubhaya.apakārī tarkayitavya iti samānam //
children.translated_text: 'One who harms here [at home] should be abandoned; one who harms the enemy should be reconciled; one who harms both should be considered' — this is common [to all teachers].

children.text: KAZ07.6.33/ asaṃdheyena tv avaśyaṃ saṃdhātavye yataḥ prabhāvas tataḥ pratividadhyāt //
children.translated_text: But when it is absolutely necessary to make a treaty with one who is not to be treated with, one should take counter-measures from whichever [source provides] advantage.

children.text:
KAZ07.6.34ab/ sa.upakāraṃ vyavahitaṃ guptam āyuḥ.kṣayād iti /
KAZ07.6.34cd/ vāsayed ari.pakṣīyam avaśīrṇa.kriyā.vidhau //
children.translated_text:
With services rendered, secluded, watched, [kept] until the end of life —
thus one should settle one from the enemy's party whose rituals of action have deteriorated.

children.text: KAZ07.6.35ab/ vikramayed bhartari vā siddhaṃ vā daṇḍa.cāriṇam //
children.translated_text: Or one should set him against his [former] master, or [employ] one who is proven as a staff-wielding enforcer.

children.text: KAZ07.6.35cd/ kuryād amitra.aṭavīṣu pratyante vā^anyataḥ kṣipet //
children.translated_text: One should have [such a person] operate in enemy territories or frontiers, or cast him elsewhere.

children.text: KAZ07.6.36ab/ paṇyaṃ kuryād asiddhaṃ vā siddhaṃ vā tena saṃvṛtam //
children.translated_text: One should make him a trader — whether unproven or proven — keeping him under watch.

children.text: KAZ07.6.36cd/ tasya^eva doṣeṇa.adūṣya para.saṃdheya.kāraṇāt //
children.translated_text: Not discrediting him by his own fault, on account of being one who should be reconciled with the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.6.37ab/ atha vā śamayed enam āyaty.artham upāṃśunā //
children.translated_text: Or else, one should pacify him secretly for future purposes.

children.text: KAZ07.6.37cd/ āyatyāṃ ca vadha.prepsuṃ dṛṣṭvā hanyād gata.āgatam //
children.translated_text: And seeing one who seeks to kill in the future, one should slay him when he comes and goes.

children.text: KAZ07.6.38ab/ arito^abhyāgato doṣaḥ śatru.saṃvāsa.kāritaḥ //
children.translated_text: A fault that comes from an enemy is caused by living with a foe;

children.text: KAZ07.6.38cd/ sarpa.saṃvāsa.dharmitvān nitya.udvegena dūṣitaḥ //
children.translated_text: it is like the nature of living with a serpent — tainted by constant anxiety.

children.text: KAZ07.6.39ab/ jāyate plakṣa.bīja.āśāt kapotād iva śālmaleḥ //
children.translated_text: Like a fig-tree seed germinating from a pigeon [dropping on] a silk-cotton tree,

children.text: KAZ07.6.39cd/ udvega.janano nityaṃ paścād api bhaya.āvahaḥ //
children.translated_text: [such a person] constantly generates anxiety and eventually brings danger.

children.text: KAZ07.6.40ab/ prakāśa.yuddhaṃ nirdiṣṭe deśe kāle ca vikramaḥ //
children.translated_text: Open battle is a fight at a designated place and time;

children.text: KAZ07.6.40cd/ vibhīṣaṇam avaskandaḥ pramāda.vyasana.ardanam //
children.translated_text: terrorizing and sudden assault [are employed] to strike at negligence and [exploit] calamity.

children.text: KAZ07.6.41ab/ ekatra tyāga.ghātau ca kūṭa.yuddhasya mātṛkā //
children.translated_text: Abandoning and killing in one stroke — this is the basic form of covert warfare;

children.text: KAZ07.6.41cd/ yoga.gūḍha.upajāpa.arthaṃ tūṣṇīṃ.yuddhasya lakṣaṇam //E
children.translated_text: the mark of silent warfare is [that its purpose is] occult stratagems and secret instigation.

children.text:
(dvaidhī.bhāvikāḥ saṃdhi.vikramāh)
KAZ07.7.01/ vijigīṣur dvitīyāṃ prakṛtim evam upagṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Treaties and attacks under the dual policy)
The conqueror should thus take up a second constituent element.

children.text:
KAZ07.7.02/ sāmantaṃ sāmantena sambhūya yāyāt, yadi vā manyeta "pārṣṇiṃ me na grahīṣyati, pārṣṇi.grāhaṃ vārayiṣyati, yātavyaṃ na^abhisariṣyati, bala.dvaiguṇyaṃ me bhaviṣyati, vīvadha.āsārau me pravartayiṣyati, parasya vārayiṣyati, bahv.ābādhe me pathi kaṇṭakān mardayiṣyati, durga.aṭavy.apasāreṣu daṇḍena cariṣyati, yātavyam aviṣahye doṣe saṃdhau vā sthāpayiṣyati,
labdha.lābha.aṃśo vā śatrūn anyān me viśvāsayiṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text:
He should march together with a feudatory, allied with [another] feudatory, if he considers: 'He will not strike me in the rear; he will ward off my rear-striker; he will not go over to the one to be attacked; my force will be doubled; he will provide me with supplies and reinforcements and will block the enemy's; on my route beset with many obstacles he will clear the thorns; at forts, forest regions, and retreat routes he will deploy his forces; he will keep the one to be attacked in a disadvantageous position in the treaty;
or, having received a share of the gains, he will inspire confidence in my other enemies.'

children.text: KAZ07.7.03/ dvaidhī.bhūto vā kośena daṇḍaṃ daṇḍena kośaṃ sāmantānām anyatamāl lipseta //
children.translated_text: Or, having adopted the dual policy, he should seek from any one of the feudatories — treasury by means of the army, or an army by means of the treasury.

children.text: KAZ07.7.04/ teṣāṃ jyāyaso^adhikena^aṃśena samāt samena hīnādd hīnena^iti sama.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Among them, an equal treaty: with a superior [feudatory], giving a greater share; with an equal, an equal [share]; with an inferior, a lesser [share].

children.text: KAZ07.7.05/ viparyaye viṣama.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: The reverse is an unequal treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.06/ tayor viśeṣa.lābhād atisaṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Gaining a special advantage from either of them is outmaneuvering.

children.text: KAZ07.7.07/ vyasaninam apāya.sthāne saktam anarthinaṃ vā jyāyāṃsaṃ hīno bala.samena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: An inferior should bargain with a superior who is beset with calamity, attached to a dangerous position, or without need — [offering] a gain equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.08/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.09/ evaṃ.bhūto vā hīna.śakti.pratāpa.pūraṇa.arthaṃ sambhāvya.artha.abhisārī mūla.pārṣṇi.trāṇa.arthaṃ vā jyāyāṃsaṃ hīno bala.samād viśiṣṭena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Or, being in such a condition, an inferior — in order to fill up the deficiency in his power and prestige, or pursuing a probable gain, or for the protection of his base and rear — should bargain with a superior [offering] a gain greater than [what is] equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.10/ paṇitaḥ kalyāṇa.buddhim anugṛhṇīyāt, anyathā vikrameta //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, [the superior] should support one of good intentions; otherwise, he should attack.

children.text: KAZ07.7.11/ jāta.vyasana.prakṛti.randhram upasthita.anarthaṃ vā jyāyāṃsaṃ hīno durga.mitra.pratiṣṭabdho vā hrasvam adhvānaṃ yātu.kāmaḥ śatrum ayuddham eka.anta.siddhiṃ vā lābham ādātu.kāmo bala.samādd hīnena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Or, an inferior, when the superior has developed calamities, vulnerabilities in his constituent elements, or is faced with approaching danger — or when [the inferior] is supported by a fort and allies, wishes to march a short distance, seeks to [attack] an enemy without a fight, or to take a gain certain of complete success — should bargain with [a gain] less than equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.12/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.13/ arandhra.vyasano vā jyāyān dur.ārabdha.karmāṇaṃ bhūyaḥ kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ yoktu.kāmo dūṣya.daṇḍaṃ pravāsayitu.kāmo dūṣya.daṇḍam āvāhayitu.kāmo vā pīḍanīyam ucchedanīyaṃ vā hīnena vyathayitu.kāmaḥ saṃdhi.pradhāno vā kalyāṇa.buddhir hīnaṃ lābhaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, a superior without vulnerabilities or calamities — wishing to further involve [the inferior] who has embarked on an ill-conceived enterprise with additional loss and expenditure, wishing to dispatch the disloyal army abroad, wishing to summon the disloyal army [to expose it], wishing to distress with the inferior one who is to be harassed or exterminated, or being one whose chief [policy] is treaty and of good intentions — should accept a lesser gain.

children.text: KAZ07.7.14/ kalyāṇa.buddhinā sambhūya^arthaṃ lipseta, anyathā vikrameta //
children.translated_text: With one of good intentions, he should join in acquiring gain; otherwise, he should attack.

children.text: KAZ07.7.15/ evaṃ samaḥ samam atisaṃdadhyād anugṛhṇīyād vā //
children.translated_text: Thus an equal should outmaneuver an equal, or support [him].

children.text: KAZ07.7.16/ para.anīkasya pratyanīkaṃ mitra.aṭavīnāṃ vā, śatror vibhūmīnāṃ deśikaṃ mūla.pārṣṇi.trāṇa.arthaṃ vā samo bala.samena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: As a counter-force to the enemy's forces, or [to gain] the allies and forest-chiefs, or [to acquire] indigenous guides for [territories of] the enemy lacking [such resources], or for the protection of one's base and rear — an equal should bargain with [a gain] equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.17/ paṇitaḥ kalyāṇa.buddhim anugṛhṇīyāt, anyathā vikrameta //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, [the other equal] should support one of good intentions; otherwise, he should attack.

children.text: KAZ07.7.18/ jāta.vyasana.prakṛti.randhram aneka.viruddham anyato labhamāno vā samo bala.samādd hīnena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: An equal, when the other has developed calamities, vulnerabilities in constituent elements, is opposed by many, or gains from elsewhere — should bargain with [a gain] less than equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.19/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.20/ evaṃ.bhūto vā samaḥ sāmanta.āyatta.kāryaḥ kartavya.balo vā bala.samād viśiṣṭena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Or, an equal in such a condition — dependent on feudatories for his affairs or needing to build up strength — should bargain with [a gain] greater than equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.21/ paṇitaḥ kalyāṇa.buddhim anugṛhṇīyāt anyathā vikrameta //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, [the other] should support one of good intentions; otherwise, he should attack.

children.text: KAZ07.7.22/ jāta.vyasana.prakṛti.randhram abhihantu.kāmaḥ sv.ārabdham eka.anta.siddhiṃ vā^asya karma.upahantu.kāmo mūle yātrāyāṃ vā prahartu.kāmo yātavyād.bhūyo labhamāno vā jyāyāṃsaṃ hīnaṃ samaṃ vā bhūyo yāceta //
children.translated_text: A superior — wishing to strike at one who has developed calamities and vulnerabilities in constituent elements, or wishing to destroy his well-begun enterprise or one certain of complete success, or wishing to strike at his base or campaign, or gaining more from the one to be attacked — should demand more from an inferior, an equal, or a superior.

children.text: KAZ07.7.23/ bhūyo vā yācitaḥ sva.bala.rakṣā.arthaṃ durdharṣam anya.durgam āsāram aṭavīṃ vā para.daṇḍena marditu.kāmaḥ prakṛṣṭe^adhvani kāle vā para.daṇḍaṃ kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ yoktu.kāmaḥ para.daṇḍena vā vivṛddhas tam eva^ucchettu.kāmaḥ para.daṇḍam ādātu.kāmo vā bhūyo dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, when asked for more, one who wishes to protect his own army by having the other's forces crush an invincible rival's fort, an ally, or a forest [tribe]; or one who wishes to exhaust the other's army with loss and expenditure on a long march or [at an unfavorable] time; or one who, having grown [powerful] through the other's army, wishes to destroy that very [ally] — or one who wishes to seize the other's army — should give more.

children.text: KAZ07.7.24/ jyāyān vā hīnaṃ yātavya.apadeśena haste kartu.kāmaḥ param ucchidya vā tam eva^ucchettu.kāmaḥ, tyāgaṃ vā kṛtvā pratyādātu.kāmo bala.samād viśiṣṭena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Or, a superior wishing to get an inferior into his grasp under the pretext of [marching against] the enemy, or wishing to destroy [the inferior] after having destroyed the enemy, or wishing to recover what has been given after making a concession — should bargain with [a gain] greater than equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.25/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.26/ yātavya.saṃhito vā tiṣṭhet, dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.daṇḍaṃ vā^asmai dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Or he should remain allied with the one to be attacked; or he should assign to him the army of the disloyal, the enemy, or the forest [tribes].

children.text: KAZ07.7.27/ jāta.vyasana.prakṛti.randhro vā jyāyān hīnaṃ bala.samena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Or, a superior who has developed calamities and vulnerabilities in constituent elements should bargain with an inferior [offering] a gain equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.28/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.29/ evaṃ.bhūtaṃ hīnaṃ jyāyān bala.samādd hīnena lābhena paṇeta //
children.translated_text: Such an inferior the superior should bargain with [a gain] less than equal in military strength.

children.text: KAZ07.7.30/ paṇitas tasya^apakāra.samartho vikrameta, anyathā saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Having bargained, if capable of harming him, he should attack; otherwise, he should make a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.7.31ab/ ādau budhyeta paṇitaḥ paṇamānaś ca kāraṇam //
children.translated_text: One who has bargained should understand at the outset the purpose of the one bargaining.

children.text: KAZ07.7.31cd/ tato vitarkya.ubhayato yataḥ śreyaś tato vrajet //E
children.translated_text: Then, having deliberated on both sides, he should proceed to what is more advantageous.

children.text:
(yātavya.vṛttiḥ - anugrāhya.mitra.viśeṣāh)
KAZ07.8.01/ yātavyo^abhiyāsyamānaḥ saṃdhi.kāraṇam ādātu.kāmo vihantu.kāmo vā sāmavāyikānām anyatamaṃ lābha.dvaiguṇyena paṇeta //
children.translated_text:
(Conduct toward the enemy to be attacked; Distinctions among allies to be supported)
The enemy to be attacked — one about to be invaded, wishing to obtain the [terms for] a treaty, or wishing to obstruct [the invasion] — should bargain with any one of the confederates, [offering] a gain double [the usual].

children.text: KAZ07.8.02/ paṇamānaḥ kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.pratyavāya.para.upakāra.śarīra.ābādhāṃś ca^asya varṇayet //
children.translated_text: While bargaining, he should describe to him the [potential] losses, expenditures, inconveniences of absence, disadvantages, services rendered to the enemy, and physical dangers.

children.text: KAZ07.8.03/ pratipannam arthena yojayet //
children.translated_text: One who has accepted should be bound with [mutual] interest.

children.text: KAZ07.8.04/ vairaṃ vā parair grāhayitvā visaṃvādayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having created enmity with the others, he should betray [the original ally].

children.text: KAZ07.8.05/ durārabdha.karmāṇaṃ bhūyaḥ kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ yoktu.kāmaḥ sv.ārabdhāṃ vā yātrā.siddhiṃ vighātayitu.kāmo mūle yātrāyāṃ vā prahartu.kāmo yātavya.saṃhitaḥ punar yācitu.kāmaḥ pratyutpanna.artha.kṛcchras tasminn aviśvasto vā tadātve lābham alpam icchet, āyatyāṃ prabhūtam //
children.translated_text: One who wishes to further involve [the enemy] who has embarked on an ill-conceived enterprise with additional loss and expenditure, or wishes to obstruct his own well-begun campaign's success, or wishes to strike at his base or campaign, or is allied with the one to be attacked and wishes to demand [more] again, or is in difficulty regarding his present affairs, or has no trust in him — in the present, should seek a small gain; in the future, a large one.

children.text: KAZ07.8.06/ mitra.upakāram amitra.upaghātam artha.anubandham avekṣamāṇaḥ pūrva.upakārakaṃ kārayitu.kāmo bhūyas tadātve mahāntaṃ lābham utsṛjya^āyatyām alpam icchet //
children.translated_text: One who, looking toward the benefit of an ally, the harm of an enemy, and the continuity of interest, wishes to have a previous benefactor reciprocate — that one, giving up a large present gain, should seek a small one in the future.

children.text: KAZ07.8.07/ dūṣya.amitrābhyāṃ mūla.hareṇa vā jyāyasā vigṛhītaṃ trātu.kāmas tathā.vidham upakāraṃ kārayitu.kāmaḥ sambandha.avekṣī vā tadātve ca^āyatyāṃ ca lābhaṃ na pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: One who wishes to rescue [an ally] who has fallen into conflict with the disloyal, the enemy, or a superior [king] who seizes his base, or who wishes to have such a service reciprocated, or who regards kinship — should accept no gain either in the present or the future.

children.text: KAZ07.8.08/ kṛta.saṃdhir atikramitu.kāmaḥ parasya prakṛti.karśanaṃ mitra.amitra.saṃdhi.viśleṣaṇaṃ vā kartu.kāmaḥ para.abhiyogāt^śaṅkamāno lābham aprāptam adhikaṃ vā yāceta //
children.translated_text: One who, having made a treaty, wishes to violate it, or wishes to exhaust the enemy's constituent elements or to break apart the enemy's alliance with allies — or one who is apprehensive of the enemy's attack — should demand an unattained or excessive gain.

children.text: KAZ07.8.09/ tam itaras tadātve ca^āyatyāṃ ca kramam avekṣeta //
children.translated_text: The other should consider the [long-term] consequence of both the present and the future.

children.text: KAZ07.8.10/ tena pūrve vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the earlier [cases] are explained.

children.text: KAZ07.8.11/ ari.vijigīṣvos tu svaṃ svaṃ mitram anugṛhṇatoḥ śakya.kalya.bhavya.ārambhi.sthira.karma.anurakta.prakṛtibhyo viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: But between the enemy and the conqueror, each supporting his own ally, the distinction [in choosing whom to support] is based on: the ally who is capable, ready, promising, enterprising, firm in action, and with devoted constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ07.8.12/ śakya.ārambhī viṣahyaṃ karma^ārabhate, kalya.ārambhī nirdoṣam, bhavya.ārambhī kalyāṇa.udayam //
children.translated_text: A capable starter undertakes what is feasible; a ready starter undertakes what is faultless; a promising starter undertakes what leads to auspicious results.

children.text: KAZ07.8.13/ sthira.karmā na^asamāpya karma^uparamate //
children.translated_text: One firm in action does not desist before completing [his] undertaking.

children.text: KAZ07.8.14/ anurakta.prakṛtiḥ susahāyatvād alpena^apy anugraheṇa kāryaṃ sādhayati //
children.translated_text: One with devoted constituent elements, being well-supported, accomplishes his task even with a small favor.

children.text: KAZ07.8.15/ ta ete kṛta.arthāḥ sukhena prabhūtaṃ ca^upakurvanti //
children.translated_text: These, when their aims are fulfilled, repay abundantly and with ease.

children.text: KAZ07.8.16/ ataḥ pratilomā na^anugrāhyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those of the opposite character are not to be supported.

children.text: KAZ07.8.17/ tayor eka.puruṣa.anugrahe yo mitraṃ mitra.taraṃ vā^anugṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Of the two [kings], when supporting a single person, the one who supports an ally, or an ally's ally, outmaneuvers [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.8.18/ mitrād ātma.vṛddhiṃ hi prāpnoti, kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.para.upakārān itaraḥ //
children.translated_text: For from an ally, one obtains growth for oneself; the other [gets] losses, expenditures, absence [from home], and services rendered to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.8.19/ kṛta.arthaś ca śatrur vaiguṇyam eti //
children.translated_text: And an enemy whose purpose is accomplished falls into deficiency.

children.text: KAZ07.8.20/ madhyamaṃ tv anugṛhṇator yo madhyamaṃ mitraṃ mitrataraṃ vā^anugṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: But when both are supporting the middle king, the one who supports the middle king's ally, or the ally's ally, outmaneuvers.

children.text: KAZ07.8.21/ mitrād ātma.vṛddhiṃ hi prāpnoti, kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.para.upakārān itaraḥ //
children.translated_text: For from an ally, one obtains growth for oneself; the other [gets] losses, expenditures, absence [from home], and services rendered to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.8.22/ madhyamaś ced anugṛhīto viguṇaḥ syād amitro^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: If the middle king, having been supported, becomes deficient — the enemy outmaneuvers.

children.text: KAZ07.8.23/ kṛta.prayāsaṃ hi madhyama.amitram apasṛtam eka.artha.upagataṃ prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: For he obtains the middle king's enemy — exhausted by effort, withdrawn, and [now] serving a single interest.

children.text: KAZ07.8.24/ tena^udāsīna.anugraho vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, support of the neutral king is explained.

children.text: KAZ07.8.25/ madhyama.udāsīnayor bala.aṃśa.dāne yaḥ śūraṃ kṛta.astraṃ duḥkha.saham anuraktaṃ vā daṇḍaṃ dadāti so^atisaṃdhīyate //
children.translated_text: When giving a portion of military force to the middle or neutral king, the one who gives a brave, well-armed, enduring, and devoted army is outmaneuvered.

children.text: KAZ07.8.26/ viparīto^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: The one who gives the opposite outmaneuvers.

children.text: KAZ07.8.27/ yatra tu daṇḍaḥ prahitas taṃ vā ca^artham anyāṃś ca sādhayati tatra maula.bhṛta.śreṇī.mitra.aṭavī.balānām anyatamam upalabdha.deśa.kālaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt, amitra.aṭavī.balaṃ vā vyavahita.deśa.kālam //
children.translated_text: But where the army that has been dispatched achieves both that objective and others, there one should give the army — whether hereditary, mercenary, guild, allied, or forest forces — having found the right place and time; or the enemy's or forest army, at a displaced place and time.

children.text: KAZ07.8.28/ yaṃ tu manyeta "kṛta.artho me daṇḍaṃ gṛhṇīyād, amitra.aṭavy.abhūmy.anṛtuṣu vā vāsayed, aphalaṃ vā kuryād" iti, daṇḍa.vyāsaṅga.apadeśena na^enam anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: But if one thinks: 'Having accomplished his purpose, he will seize my army; or he will station [me] in [territory infested with] enemies, forest tribes, unfavorable terrain, or at an improper season; or he will render [my efforts] fruitless' — under the pretext of maintaining the army, he should not support him.

children.text: KAZ07.8.29/ evam avaśyaṃ tv anugrahītavye tat.kāla.saham asmai daṇḍaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: But if support is absolutely necessary, he should give him an army capable [only] for the present task.

children.text: KAZ07.8.30/ ā.samāpteś ca^enaṃ vāsayed yodhayec ca bala.vyasanebhyaś ca rakṣet //
children.translated_text: And he should station and employ him until the completion [of the task], and protect him from losses of forces and calamities.

children.text: KAZ07.8.31/ kṛta.arthāc ca sa.apadeśam apasrāvayet //
children.translated_text: And once the objective is accomplished, he should withdraw [the army] under some pretext.

children.text: KAZ07.8.32/ dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.daṇḍaṃ vā^asmai dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Or he should give him an army [composed of] corruptible [elements], enemies, and forest tribes.

children.text: KAZ07.8.33/ yātavyena vā saṃdhāya^enam atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, by making a treaty with the [king] about to be attacked, he should deceive him.

children.text: KAZ07.8.34ab/ same hi lābhe saṃdhiḥ syād viṣame vikramo mataḥ //
children.translated_text: For when the gain is equal, a treaty is [appropriate]; when unequal, aggression is considered [proper].

children.text: KAZ07.8.34cd/ sama.hīna.viśiṣṭānām ity uktāḥ saṃdhi.vikramāḥ //E
children.translated_text: Thus have been stated the [conditions for] treaty and aggression among equals, inferiors, and superiors.

children.text:
(mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.karma.saṃdhayaḥ, tatra mitra.saṃdhiḥ hiraṇya.saṃdhiś ca)
KAZ07.9.01/ saṃhita.prayāṇe mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.lābhānām uttara.uttaro lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text:
(Treaties involving allies, gold, land, and labor; herein the ally-treaty and gold-treaty)
In a joint expedition, among gains of allies, gold, and land, each successive gain is better than the preceding.

children.text: KAZ07.9.02/ mitra.hiraṇye hi bhūmi.lābhād bhavataḥ, mitraṃ hiraṇya.lābhāt //
children.translated_text: For allies and gold result from [the acquisition of] land; an ally results from [the acquisition of] gold.

children.text: KAZ07.9.03/ yo vā lābhaḥ siddhaḥ śeṣayor anyataraṃ sādhayati //
children.translated_text: Or whichever gain is certain [should be pursued first, since it] enables the achievement of either of the remaining two.

children.text: KAZ07.9.04/ "tvaṃ ca^ahaṃ ca mitraṃ labhāvahe" ity evaṃ.ādidh sama.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'You and I shall each gain an ally' — a treaty of this kind is an equal treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.9.05/ "tvaṃ mitram" ity evaṃ.ādir viṣama.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'You [shall gain] an ally' — a treaty of this kind is an unequal treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.9.06/ tayor viśeṣa.lābhād atisaṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Gaining a special advantage [over and above the terms] of either [type of treaty] constitutes over-reaching.

children.text: KAZ07.9.07/ sama.saṃdhau tu yaḥ sampannaṃ mitraṃ mitra.kṛcchre vā mitram avāpnoti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: In an equal treaty, one who obtains a prosperous ally, or an ally in [the other's time of] distress, over-reaches.

children.text: KAZ07.9.08/ āpadd hi sauhṛda.sthairyam utpādayati //
children.translated_text: For adversity produces steadfastness of friendship.

children.text: KAZ07.9.09/ mitra.kṛcchre^api nityam avaśyam anityaṃ vaśyaṃ vā^iti "nityam avaśyaṃ śreyaḥ, tadd hi anupakurvad api na^apakaroti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: Even in the case of an ally in distress — [the question arises]: one who is permanent and uncontrollable, or one who is impermanent and controllable? 'A permanent, uncontrollable [ally] is better, for even without rendering service, he does not cause harm' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.10/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.11/ vaśyam anityaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: A controllable, impermanent [ally] is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.12/ yāvad upakaroti tāvan mitraṃ bhavati, upakāra.lakṣaṇaṃ mitram iti //
children.translated_text: For he is an ally as long as he renders service — alliance is defined by service.

children.text: KAZ07.9.13/ vaśyayor api mahā.bhogam anityam alpa.bhogaṃ vā nityam iti // mahā.bhogam anityaṃ śreyaḥ, mahā.bhogam anityam alpa.kālena mahad.upakurvan mahānti vyaya.sthānāni pratikaroti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: Among controllable [allies] — one of great resources but impermanent, or one of small resources but permanent? 'One of great resources but impermanent is better, for one of great resources, even in a short time, rendering great service, repays great expenditures' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.14/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.15/ nityam alpa.bhogaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: A permanent [ally] of small resources is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.16/ mahā.bhogam anityam upakāra.bhayād apakrāmati, upakṛtya vā pratyādātum īhate //
children.translated_text: One of great resources but impermanent withdraws out of fear of [being obligated to render further] service, or having rendered service, strives to recover [what he gave].

children.text: KAZ07.9.17/ nityam alpa.bhogaṃ sātatyād alpam upakurvan mahatā kālena mahad upakaroti //
children.translated_text: A permanent [ally] of small resources, through continuity, rendering small service over a long time, renders great service.

children.text: KAZ07.9.18/ guru.samutthaṃ mahan mitraṃ laghu.samuttham alpaṃ vā^iti "guru.samutthaṃ mahan mitraṃ pratāpa.karaṃ bhavati, yadā ca^uttiṣṭhate tadā kāryaṃ sādhayati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: An ally of great origin and large [forces], or one of small origin and small [forces]? 'An ally of great origin and large [forces] is better, for he commands awe and, when he rises, accomplishes the task' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.19/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.20/ laghu.samuttham alpaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: One of small origin and small [forces] is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.21/ lagu.samuttham alpaṃ mitraṃ kārya.kālaṃ na^atipātayati daurbalyāc ca yathā.iṣṭa.bhogyaṃ bhavati, na^itarat prakṛṣṭa.bhaumam //
children.translated_text: An ally of small origin and small [forces] does not let the time for action pass by, and due to weakness, can be employed as one wishes — unlike the other, who has extensive territory.

children.text: KAZ07.9.22/ vikṣipta.sainyam avaśya.sainyaṃ vā^iti "vikṣiptaṃ sainyaṃ śakyaṃ pratisaṃhartuṃ vaśyatvād" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: An ally with a scattered army, or one with an uncontrollable army? 'One with a scattered army [is better], for a scattered army can be reassembled since it is controllable' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.23/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.24/ avaśya.sainyaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: One with an uncontrollable army is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.25/ avaśyaṃ hi śakyaṃ sāma.ādibhir vaśyaṃ kartum, na^itarat kārya.vyāsaktaṃ pratisaṃhartum //
children.translated_text: For an uncontrollable [army] can be made controllable through conciliation and other [means]; the other, being engaged in [its own] affairs, cannot be reassembled.

children.text: KAZ07.9.26/ puruṣa.bhogaṃ hiraṇya.bhogaṃ vā mitram iti "puruṣa.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreyaḥ, pruṣa.bhogaṃ mitraṃ pratāpa.karaṃ bhavati, yadā ca^uttiṣṭhate tadā kāryaṃ sādhayati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: An ally who renders service in men, or one who renders service in gold? 'An ally who renders service in men is better, for such an ally commands awe and, when he rises, accomplishes the task' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.27/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.28/ hiraṇya.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: An ally who renders service in gold is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.29/ nityo hi hiraṇyena yogaḥ kadācid daṇḍena //
children.translated_text: For the use of gold is constant, [while] the use of the army is occasional.

children.text: KAZ07.9.30/ daṇḍaś ca hiraṇyena^anye ca kāmāḥ prāpyanta iti //
children.translated_text: And through gold, the army and other desires are obtained.

children.text: KAZ07.9.31/ hiraṇya.bhogaṃ bhūmi.bhogaṃ vā mitram iti "hiraṇya.bhogaṃ gatimattvāt sarva.vyaya.pratīkāra.karam" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: An ally who renders service in gold, or one who renders service in land? 'One who renders service in gold [is better], because, being mobile, it counteracts all expenditures' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.32/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.33/ mitra.hiraṇye hi bhūmi.lābhād bhavata ity uktaṃ purastād //
children.translated_text: For it has been stated earlier that allies and gold result from [the acquisition of] land.

children.text: KAZ07.9.34/ tasmād bhūmi.bhogaṃ mitraṃ śreya iti //
children.translated_text: Therefore, an ally who renders service in land is better.

children.text: KAZ07.9.35/ tulye puruṣa.bhoge vikramaḥ kleśa.sahatvam anurāgaḥ sarva.bala.lābho vā mitra.kulād viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: When service in men is equal, the distinguishing factor is valor, endurance of hardship, devotion, or gaining the full force of the ally's family.

children.text: KAZ07.9.36/ tulye hiraṇya.bhoge prārthita.arthatā prābhūtyam alpa.prayasatā sātatyaṃ ca viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: When service in gold is equal, the distinguishing factor is the [gold] being [already] desired, being abundant, being obtained with little effort, and being constant.

children.text: KAZ07.9.37/ tatra^etad bhavati //
children.translated_text: Herein this [applies]:

children.text:
KAZ07.9.38ab/ nityaṃ vaśyaṃ laghu.utthānaṃ pitṛ.paitāmahaṃ mahat /
KAZ07.9.38cd/ advaidhyaṃ ca^iti sampannaṃ mitraṃ ṣaḍ.guṇam ucyate //
children.translated_text: Permanent, controllable, of quick mobilization, hereditary from father and grandfather, great, and undivided — a prosperous ally is said to have these six qualities.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.39ab/ ṛte yad arthaṃ praṇayād rakṣyate yac ca rakṣati /
KAZ07.9.39cd/ pūrva.upacita.sambandhaṃ tan mitraṃ nityam ucyate //
children.translated_text: One who is protected not for [any] material [gain] but out of affection, and who also protects [in return], with a previously cultivated relationship — that ally is called permanent.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.40ab/ sarva.citra.mahā.bhogaṃ trividhaṃ vaśyam ucyate /
KAZ07.9.40cd/ ekato.bhogy ubhayataḥ sarvato.bhogi ca^aparam //
children.translated_text: All-versatile [and] of great resources — the controllable [ally] is said to be of three kinds: one who can be employed on one front, on both [fronts], or on all [fronts].

children.text:
KAZ07.9.41ab/ ādātṛ vā dātr.api vā jīvaty ariṣu hiṃsayā /
KAZ07.9.41cd/ mitraṃ nityam avaśyaṃ tad.durga.aṭavy.apasāri ca //
children.translated_text: Whether he takes or gives, he lives [on good terms] while harming enemies — such an ally is permanent and uncontrollable, and retreats [only] to forts or forests.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.42ab/ anyato vigṛhītaṃ yal laghu.vyasanam eva vā /
KAZ07.9.42cd/ saṃdhatte ca^upakārāya tan mitraṃ vaśyam adhruvam //
children.translated_text: One who is in conflict with another, or who has only minor vices, and who makes a treaty for the purpose of mutual benefit — that ally is controllable and impermanent.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.43ab/ eka.arthena^atha sambaddham upakārya.vikāri ca /
KAZ07.9.43cd/ mitra.bhāvi bhavaty etan mitram advaidhyam āpadi //
children.translated_text: One bound by a common objective and subject to change through [receiving] favors, who is inclined toward friendship — this ally becomes undivided in adversity.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.44ab/ mitra.bhāvād dhruvaṃ mitraṃ śatru.sādhāraṇāc calam /
KAZ07.9.44cd/ na kasyacid udāsīnaṃ dvayor ubhaya.bhāvi tat //
children.translated_text: From [the quality of] friendship, [an ally may be] firm; from [being] shared with the enemy, unstable. An [ally] who is neutral to neither [side] but inclined toward both — that is [the nature of] such [an ally].

children.text:
KAZ07.9.45ab/ vijigīṣor amitraṃ yan mitram antardhitāṃ gatam /
KAZ07.9.45cd/ upakāre^aniviṣṭaṃ vā^aśaktaṃ vā^anupakāri tat //
children.translated_text: That which is an ally of the would-be conqueror but has gone into obscurity, is not engaged in [rendering] service, or is incapable — that is [an ally that is] unhelpful.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.46ab/ priyaṃ parasya vā rakṣyaṃ pūjyaṃ sambaddham eva vā /
KAZ07.9.46cd/ anugṛhṇāti yan mitraṃ śatru.sādhāraṇaṃ hi tat //
children.translated_text: That which supports what is dear to the enemy, protects [the enemy], honors [the enemy], or is bound [to the enemy] — such an ally is shared with the enemy.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.47ab/ prakṛṣṭa.bhaumaṃ saṃtuṣṭaṃ balavac ca^ālasaṃ ca yat /
KAZ07.9.47cd/ udāsīnaṃ bhavaty etad vyasanād avamānitam //
children.translated_text: One with extensive territory, content, powerful, yet indolent — this becomes neutral, [or] is disregarded due to [its own] calamity.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.48ab/ arer netuś ca yad vṛddhiṃ daurbalyād anuvartate /
KAZ07.9.48cd/ ubhayasya^apy avidviṣṭaṃ vidyād ubhaya.bhāvi tat //
children.translated_text: That which, from weakness, follows the growth of both the enemy and the leader, hated by neither — that should be known as inclined toward both sides.

children.text:
KAZ07.9.49ab/ kāraṇa.akāraṇa.dhvastaṃ kāraṇa.akāraṇa.āgatam /
KAZ07.9.49cd/ yo mitraṃ samupekṣeta sa mṛtyum upagūhati //
children.translated_text: One who disregards an ally that has been destroyed with or without cause, or that has come [to him] with or without cause — he embraces death.

children.text: KAZ07.9.50/ kṣipram alpo lābhaś cirān mahān iti vā "kṣipram alpo lābhaḥ kārya.deśa.kāla.saṃvādakaḥ śreyān" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: A small gain quickly, or a large gain after a long time? 'A small gain quickly [is better, because it is] consistent with the requirements of task, place, and time' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.9.51/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.9.52/ cirād avinipātī bīja.sadharmā mahāml lābhaḥ śreyān, viparyaye pūrvaḥ //
children.translated_text: A large gain, after a long time, not prone to collapse and having the nature of a seed — [that] is better. In the reverse case, the former [is better].

children.text:
KAZ07.9.53ab/ evaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhruve lābhe lābha.aṃśe ca guṇa.udayam /
KAZ07.9.53cd/ sva.artha.siddhi.paro yāyāt saṃhitaḥ sāmavāyikaiḥ //E
children.translated_text: Thus, having considered the prospect of gain and the rise of [favorable] qualities in [each] portion of the gain, one should march forth — intent upon achieving one's own objectives, allied with those in the coalition.

children.text:
(mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.karma.saṃdhayaḥ, tatra bhūmi.saṃdhih)
KAZ07.10.01/ "tvaṃ ca^ahaṃ ca bhūmiṃ labhāvahe" iti bhūmi.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Treaties involving allies, gold, land, and labor; herein the land-treaty)
'You and I shall each gain land' — this is a land-treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.10.02/ tayor yaḥ pratyupasthita.arthaḥ sampannāṃ bhūmim avāpnoti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Of the two, one who obtains prosperous land, or [land that serves] an immediate purpose, over-reaches.

children.text: KAZ07.10.03/ tulye sampanna.alābhe yo balavantam ākramya bhūmim avāpnoti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: When the gain of prosperous [land] is equal, one who obtains land by overpowering a powerful [enemy] over-reaches.

children.text: KAZ07.10.04/ bhūmi.lābhaṃ śatru.karśanaṃ pratāpaṃ ca hi prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: For he obtains land-gain, enemy-weakening, and prestige.

children.text: KAZ07.10.05/ durbalād.bhūmi.lābhe satyaṃ saukaryaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: When the land-gain is from a weak [enemy], there is indeed ease [in obtaining it].

children.text: KAZ07.10.06/ durbala eva ca bhūmi.lābhaḥ, tat.sāmantaś ca mitram amitra.bhāvaṃ gacchati //
children.translated_text: But the land-gain is [only] from a weak [enemy]; and his neighbor, [who was] an ally, turns hostile.

children.text: KAZ07.10.07/ tulye balīyastve yaḥ sthita.śatrum utpāṭya bhūmim avāpnoti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: When the strength [of the enemy] is equal, one who uproots an established enemy and gains land over-reaches.

children.text: KAZ07.10.08/ durga.avāptir hi sva.bhūmi.rakṣaṇam amitra.aṭavī.pratiṣedhaṃ ca karoti //
children.translated_text: For the acquisition of a fort protects one's own territory and repels enemies and forest tribes.

children.text: KAZ07.10.09/ cala.amitrād.bhūmi.lābhe śakya.sāmantato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the land-gain is from a mobile [i.e., nomadic] enemy, the distinguishing factor is [having] a manageable neighbor.

children.text: KAZ07.10.10/ durbala.sāmantā hi kṣipra.āpyāyana.yoga.kṣemā bhavati //
children.translated_text: For a territory with weak neighbors quickly achieves prosperity and security.

children.text: KAZ07.10.11/ viparītā balavat sāmantā kośa.daṇḍa.avacchedanī ca bhūmir bhavati //
children.translated_text: The opposite [holds] for territory with powerful neighbors — [such] land becomes subject to confiscation of its treasury and army.

children.text: KAZ07.10.12/ sampannā nitya.amitrā manda.guṇā vā bhūmir anitya.amitrā^iti "sampannā nitya.amitrā śreyasī bhūmiḥ sampannā hi kośa.daṇḍau sampādayati, tau ca^amitra.pratighātakau ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: Prosperous land with permanent enemies, or land of lesser quality with impermanent enemies? 'Prosperous land with permanent enemies is better, for prosperous land generates treasury and army, and those two repel the enemy' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.10.13/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.10.14/ nitya.amitra.alābhe bhūyān śatru.lābho bhavati //
children.translated_text: Without gaining [respite from] a permanent enemy, the enemy-gain [i.e., harassment] is greater.

children.text: KAZ07.10.15/ nityaś ca śatrur upakṛte ca^apakṛte ca śatrur eva bhavati, anityas tu śatrur upakārād anapakārād vā śāmyati //
children.translated_text: A permanent enemy, whether treated well or ill, remains an enemy; but an impermanent enemy is pacified either by [good] treatment or by [absence of] ill-treatment.

children.text: KAZ07.10.16/ yasyā hi bhūmer bahu.durgāś cora.gaṇair mleccha.aṭavībhir vā nitya.avirahitāḥ pratyantāḥ sā nitya.amitrā, viparyaye tv anitya.amitrā //
children.translated_text: For land whose borderlands are full of fortresses, never free of bands of thieves, and [infested by] <s>Mleccha</s> forest tribes — that is [land] with permanent enemies. In the reverse case, [it has] impermanent enemies.

children.text: KAZ07.10.17/ alpā pratyāsannā mahatī vyavahitā vā bhūmir iti alpā pratyāsannā śreyasī //
children.translated_text: A small [piece of] nearby land, or a large [piece of] distant land? A small nearby [piece] is better.

children.text: KAZ07.10.18/ sukhā hi prāptuṃ pālayitum abhisārayituṃ ca bhavati //
children.translated_text: For it is easy to acquire, protect, and direct [forces toward].

children.text: KAZ07.10.19/ viparītā vyavahitā //
children.translated_text: The opposite [holds for] distant [land].

children.text: KAZ07.10.20/ vyavahitayor api daṇḍa.dhāraṇā^ātma.dhāraṇā vā bhūmir iti ātma.dhāraṇā śreyasī //
children.translated_text: Even among distant [lands] — land that supports an army, or land that supports oneself? Land that supports oneself is better.

children.text: KAZ07.10.21/ sā hi sva.samutthābhyāṃ kośa.daṇḍābhyāṃ dhāryate //
children.translated_text: For it is sustained by its own treasury and army.

children.text: KAZ07.10.22/ viparītā daṇḍa.dhāraṇā daṇḍa.sthānam //
children.translated_text: The opposite [holds for] land that [merely] supports an army — [it is only] a military outpost.

children.text: KAZ07.10.23/ bāliśāt prājñād vā bhūmi.lābha iti bāliśād.bhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: A land-gain from a foolish [king] or from a wise one? A land-gain from a foolish [king] is better.

children.text: KAZ07.10.24/ suprāpyā^anupālyā hi bhavati, apratyādeyā ca //
children.translated_text: For it is easily acquired and, [once acquired,] does not require guarding, and cannot be taken back.

children.text: KAZ07.10.25/ viparītā prājñād anuraktā //
children.translated_text: The opposite [holds for land acquired from] a wise one — [the populace remains] attached [to the former ruler].

children.text: KAZ07.10.26/ pīḍanīya.ucchedanīyayor ucchedanīyād bhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between [gaining land from] one who should be harassed and one who should be uprooted — gaining land from the one to be uprooted is better.

children.text: KAZ07.10.27/ ucchedanīyo hy anapāśrayo durbala.apāśrayo vā^abhiyuktaḥ kośa.daṇḍāv ādāya^apasartu.kāmaḥ prakṛtibhis tyajyate, na pīḍanīyo durga.mitra.pratiṣṭabdhaḥ //
children.translated_text: For one to be uprooted, being without support or with only weak support, when attacked, wishes to flee taking the treasury and army, [but] is abandoned by his subjects — unlike one to be harassed, who is propped up by forts and allies.

children.text: KAZ07.10.28/ durga.pratiṣṭabdhayor api sthala.nadī.durgīyābhyāṃ sthala.durgīyād bhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Even between two propped up by fortresses — from one [propped up by] a land-fortress versus one by a river-fortress — gaining land from one with a land-fortress is better.

children.text: KAZ07.10.29/ sthāleyaṃ hi surodha.avamarda.avaskandam anihśrāvi.śatru ca //
children.translated_text: For a land-fortress is easy to besiege, assault, and surprise, and does not shield the enemy [from observation].

children.text: KAZ07.10.30/ nadī.durgaṃ tu dvi.guṇa.kleśa.karam, udakaṃ ca pātavyaṃ vṛtti.karaṃ ca^amitrasya //
children.translated_text: A river-fort, however, causes double the hardship; and water must be consumed [crossed], and it provides a livelihood for the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.10.31/ nadī.parvata.durgīyābhyāṃ nadī.durgīyād bbhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between [forces defending] river-and-mountain forts, acquiring land from the river-fort [defender] is preferable.

children.text: KAZ07.10.32/ nadī.durgaṃ hi hasti.stambha.saṃkrama.setu.bandha.naubhiḥ sādhyam anitya.gāmbhīryam avasrāvy udakaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: For a river-fort is conquerable by elephants, pillar-bridges, pontoon bridges, and boats; its depth is impermanent and its water drains away.

children.text: KAZ07.10.33/ pārvataṃ tu sv.ārakṣaṃ duruparodhi kṛcchra.ārohaṇam, bhagne ca^ekasmin na sarva.vadhaḥ, śilā.vṛkṣa.pramokṣaś ca mahā.apakāriṇām //
children.translated_text: But a mountain-fort is easily defensible, difficult to besiege, hard to climb; and when one [position] is broken, it does not mean the destruction of all; and the rolling of boulders and trees causes great harm [to the attacker].

children.text: KAZ07.10.34/ nimna.sthala.yodhibhyo nimna.yodhibhyo bhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between [forces with] marsh-ground and ground-fighters, acquiring land from the marsh-fighters is preferable.

children.text: KAZ07.10.35/ nimna.yodhino hy uparuddha.deśa.kālāḥ, sthala.yodhinas tu sarva.deśa.kāla.yodhinaḥ //
children.translated_text: For marsh-fighters are restricted in place and time, whereas ground-fighters fight in all places and at all times.

children.text: KAZ07.10.36/ khanaka.ākāśa.yodhibhyaḥ khanakebhyo bhūmi.lābhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between [forces with] sappers and aerial fighters, acquiring land from the sappers is preferable.

children.text: KAZ07.10.37/ khanakā hi khātena śastreṇa ca^ubhayathā yudhyante, śastreṇa^eva^ākāśa.yodhinaḥ //
children.translated_text: For sappers fight in two ways — with trenches and with weapons — whereas aerial fighters [fight] only with weapons.

children.text:
KAZ07.10.38ab/ evaṃ.vidhyebhyaḥ pṛthivīṃ labhamāno^artha.śāstravit /
KAZ07.10.38cd/ saṃhitebhyaḥ parebhyaś ca viśeṣam adhigacchati //E
children.translated_text:
Thus, one who knows the science of statecraft, acquiring territory from such [combined forces],
obtains a distinction over the allies [of the enemy] and over others.

children.text:
(mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.karma.samdhayah - tatra anavasita.samdhih)
KAZ07.11.01/ "tvaṃ ca^ahaṃ ca śūnyaṃ niveśayāvahe" ity anavasita.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Treaties involving allies, gold, land, and enterprises — therein, the unspecified treaty)
'You and I shall settle a wasteland' — this is an unspecified treaty (<s>anavasitasaṃdhi</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.11.02/ tayor yaḥ pratyupasthita.artho yathā.ukta.guṇāṃ bhūmiṃ niveśayati so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Of the two, whichever one has the resources at hand and settles land with the qualities described [earlier] — he gains the advantage.

children.text: KAZ07.11.03/ tatra^api sthalam audakaṃ vā^iti mahataḥ sthalād alpam audakaṃ śreyaḥ, sātatyād avasthitatvāc ca phalānām //
children.translated_text: In that regard, between dry land and irrigated land — a small [area of] irrigated land is better than a large [area of] dry land, because of the constancy and stability of its produce.

children.text: KAZ07.11.04/ sthalayor api prabhūta.pūrva.apara.sasyam alpa.varṣa.pākam asakta.ārambhaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Between two dry lands, one with abundant early and late harvests, requiring little rain, and allowing uninterrupted cultivation is better.

children.text: KAZ07.11.05/ audakayor api dhānya.vāpam adhānya.vāpāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Between two irrigated lands, one suitable for grain cultivation is better than one not suitable for grain.

children.text: KAZ07.11.06/ tayor alpa.bahutve dhānya.kāntād alpān mahad adhānya.kāntaṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Between the two [lands] differing in size — a large non-grain land is better than a small grain-land.

children.text: KAZ07.11.07/ mahaty avakāśe hi sthālyāś ca^anūpyāś ca^oṣadhayo bhavanti //
children.translated_text: For in a large area, both upland and marshy herbs grow.

children.text: KAZ07.11.08/ durga.ādīni ca karmāṇi prabhūtyena kriyante //
children.translated_text: And enterprises such as fortifications and the like are accomplished through abundance [of resources].

children.text: KAZ07.11.09/ kṛtrimā hi bhūmi.guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: For the qualities of land are [ultimately] man-made.

children.text: KAZ07.11.10/ khani.dhānya.bhogayoḥ khani.bhogaḥ kośa.karaḥ, dhānya.bhogaḥ kośa.koṣṭha.agāra.karaḥ //
children.translated_text: Between lands yielding mines and grain: mine-revenue enriches the treasury; grain-revenue fills both the treasury and the storehouse.

children.text: KAZ07.11.11/ dhānya.mūlā hi durga.ādīnāṃ karmaṇām ārambhāḥ //
children.translated_text: For grain is the foundation for initiating enterprises such as fortification and others.

children.text: KAZ07.11.12/ mahā.viṣaya.vikrayo vā khani.bhogaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Or, mine-revenue is better when it serves as a market for a large territory.

children.text: KAZ07.11.13/ "dravya.hasti.vana.bhogayor dravya.vana.bhogaḥ sarva.karmaṇāṃ yoniḥ prabhūta.nidhāna.kṣamaś ca, viparīto hasti.vana.bhogaḥ" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between lands yielding timber forests and elephant forests: timber-forest revenue is the source of all enterprises and can store abundant [materials]; the opposite is true of elephant-forest revenue" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.11.14/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.11.15/ śakyaṃ dravya.vanam anekam anekasyāṃ bhūmau vāpayitum, na hasti.vanam //
children.translated_text: "It is possible to plant many timber forests on many [types of] land, but not elephant forests.

children.text: KAZ07.11.16/ hasti.pradhāno hi para.anīka.vadha iti //
children.translated_text: For the destruction of the enemy's forces depends primarily on elephants."

children.text: KAZ07.11.17/ vāri.sthala.patha.bhogayor anityo vāri.patha.bhogaḥ, nityaḥ sthala.patha.bhogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Between lands with water-routes and land-routes: water-route revenue is impermanent; land-route revenue is permanent.

children.text: KAZ07.11.18/ bhinna.manuṣyā śreṇī.manuṣyā vā bhūmir iti bhinna.manuṣyā śreyasī //
children.translated_text: Between land populated by [individually] dispersed people and by guild-organized people — land with dispersed people is better.

children.text: KAZ07.11.19/ bhinna.manuṣyā bhogyā bhavati, anupajāpyā ca^anyeṣām, anāpat.sahā tu //
children.translated_text: Land with dispersed people is exploitable and not susceptible to being seduced away by others; but it cannot withstand calamity.

children.text: KAZ07.11.20/ viparītā śreṇī.manuṣyā, kope mahā.doṣā //
children.translated_text: The opposite is true of guild-organized [land]; but it is greatly dangerous when angered.

children.text: KAZ07.11.21/ tasyāṃ cāturvarṇya.niveśe sarva.bhoga.sahatvād avara.varṇa.prāyā śreyasī, bāhulyād dhruvatvāc ca kṛṣyāḥ karṣakavatī, kṛṣyāś ca^anyeṣāṃ ca^ārambhāṇāṃ prayojakatvāt go.rakṣakavatī, paṇya.nicaya.ṛṇa.anugrahād āḍhya.vaṇigvatī //
children.translated_text: In settling the four social classes on that [land]: one predominantly of the lower classes is better, because it tolerates all forms of exploitation; [and] due to the abundance and stability of agriculture, one with farmers [is better]; because it drives agriculture and other enterprises, one with cattle-keepers [is better]; because of the accumulation of merchandise and the benefit of credit, one with wealthy merchants [is better].

children.text: KAZ07.11.22/ bhūmi.guṇānām apāśrayaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Among the qualities of land, the [most important] support is better.

children.text: KAZ07.11.23/ durga.apāśrayā puruṣa.apāśrayā vā bhūmir iti puruṣa.apāśrayā śreyasī //
children.translated_text: Between land supported by fortification and land supported by manpower — land supported by manpower is better.

children.text: KAZ07.11.24/ puruṣavad dhi rājyam //
children.translated_text: For a kingdom depends on its people.

children.text: KAZ07.11.25/ apuruṣā gaur vandhy eva kiṃ duhīta //
children.translated_text: Land without people — like a barren cow, what can it yield?

children.text: KAZ07.11.26/ mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśāṃ tu bhūmim avāptu.kāmaḥ pūrvam eva kretāraṃ paṇeta durbalam arāja.bījinaṃ nirutsāham apakṣam anyāya.vṛttiṃ vyasaninaṃ daiva.pramāṇaṃ yat.kiṃcana.kāriṇaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: But one who wishes to acquire land requiring great loss and expenditure to settle should first arrange the buyer — [selecting one who is] weak, not of royal lineage, lacking in enterprise, without a faction, of unrighteous conduct, addicted to vices, dependent on fate, or one who does whatever comes [his way].

children.text: KAZ07.11.27/ mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśāyāṃ hi bhūmau durbalo rāja.bījī niviṣṭaḥ sagandhābhiḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha kṣaya.vyayena^avasīdati //
children.translated_text: For on land requiring great loss and expenditure to settle, a weak [person] of royal lineage, once installed, sinks together with his constituent elements — who are of the same nature — through the loss and expenditure.

children.text: KAZ07.11.28/ balavān arāja.bījī kṣaya.vyaya.bhayād asagandhābhiḥ prakṛtibhis tyajyate //
children.translated_text: A strong [person] not of royal lineage is abandoned by his constituent elements — who are not of the same nature — out of fear of loss and expenditure.

children.text: KAZ07.11.29/ nirutsāhas tu daṇḍavān api daṇḍasya^apraṇetā sadaṇḍaḥ kṣaya.vyayena^avabhajyate //
children.translated_text: One lacking enterprise, though possessing an army, being unable to deploy the rod of force, is broken apart by loss and expenditure even while armed.

children.text: KAZ07.11.30/ kośavān apy apakṣaḥ kṣaya.vyaya.anugraha.hīnatvān na kutaścit prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: One who has a treasury but no faction, being deficient in the power of conciliation through loss and expenditure, obtains nothing from anywhere.

children.text: KAZ07.11.31/ anyāya.vṛttir niviṣṭam apy utthāpayet //
children.translated_text: One of unrighteous conduct would drive out even those already settled.

children.text: KAZ07.11.32/ sa katham aniviṣṭaṃ niveśayet //
children.translated_text: How then would he settle those not yet settled?

children.text: KAZ07.11.33/ tena vyasanī vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the one addicted to vices is explained.

children.text: KAZ07.11.34/ daiva.pramāṇo mānuṣa.hīno nirārambho vipanna.karma.ārambho vā^avasīdati //
children.translated_text: One dependent on fate, lacking human qualities, without enterprise, or with failed enterprises — sinks.

children.text: KAZ07.11.35/ yat.kiṃcana.kārī na kiṃcid āsādayati //
children.translated_text: One who does whatever comes [his way] achieves nothing.

children.text: KAZ07.11.36/ sa ca^eṣāṃ pāpiṣṭhatamo bhavati //
children.translated_text: And he is the worst of them all.

children.text: KAZ07.11.37/ "yat.kiṃcid.ārabhamāṇo hi vijigīṣoḥ kadācic chidram āsādayed" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "For one who undertakes whatever [comes], might at some time find a vulnerability in the aspiring conqueror" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.11.38/ yathā chidraṃ tathā vināśam apy āsādayed iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Just as he might find a vulnerability, he might also find destruction" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.11.39/ teṣām alābhe yathā pārṣṇi.grāha.upagrahe vakṣyāmas tathā bhūmim avasthāpayet //
children.translated_text: If none of these [persons] are obtainable, [the king] should settle the land as we shall describe in [the section on] the restraint of the rear-enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.11.40/ ity abhihita.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the specified treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.11.41/ guṇavatīm ādeyāṃ vā bhūmiṃ balavatā krayeṇa yācitaḥ saṃdhim avasthāpya dadyāt //
children.translated_text: When asked by a powerful [king] — through purchase — for quality land or land that should be given, one should establish a treaty and give it.

children.text: KAZ07.11.42/ ity anibhṛta.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the restless treaty (<s>anibhṛtasaṃdhi</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.11.43/ samena vā yācitaḥ kāraṇam avekṣya dadyāt "pratyādeyā me bhūmir vaśyā vā, anayā pratibaddhaḥ paro me vaśyo bhaviṣyati^ bhūmi.vikrayād vā mitra.hiraṇya.lābhaḥ kārya.sāmarthya.karo me bhaviṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, when asked by an equal, one should give after considering the reason: 'The land given will be recoverable or controllable by me; or, with the enemy constrained by it, he will become subject to me; or from the sale of the land, the gain of an ally's gold will enhance my capacity for action.'

children.text: KAZ07.11.44/ tena hīnaḥ kretā vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the inferior buyer is explained.

children.text:
KAZ07.11.45ab/ evaṃ mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca sajanām ajanāṃ ca gām /
KAZ07.11.45cd/ labhamāno^atisaṃdhatte śāstravit sāmavāyikān //E
children.translated_text:
Thus, one who knows the treatise, acquiring an ally, gold, and land — both populated and unpopulated —
gains the advantage over fellow-treaty partners.

children.text:
(mitra.hiraṇya.bhūmi.karma.samdhayah, tatra karma.samdhih)
KAZ07.12.01/ "tvaṃ ca^ahaṃ ca durgaṃ kārayāvahe" iti karma.saṃdhiḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Treaties involving allies, gold, land, and enterprises — therein, the enterprise treaty)
'You and I shall build a fort' — this is an enterprise treaty (<s>karmasaṃdhi</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.12.02/ tayor yo daiva.kṛtam aviṣahyam alpa.vyaya.ārambhaṃ durgaṃ kārayati so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Of the two, whichever one builds a fort that is natural, impregnable, and requires little expenditure to construct — he gains the advantage.

children.text: KAZ07.12.03/ tatra^api sthala.nadī.parvata.durgāṇām uttara.uttaraṃ śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: In that regard, among ground, river, and mountain forts — each successive one is better.

children.text: KAZ07.12.04/ setu.bandhayor apy āhārya.udakāt saha.udakaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between two embankments — one with natural water is better than one with brought-in water.

children.text: KAZ07.12.05/ saha.udakayor api prabhūta.vāpa.sthānaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: Between two [embankments] with natural water — one with abundant sowing-ground is better.

children.text: KAZ07.12.06/ dravya.vanayor api yo mahat.sāravad.dravya.aṭavīkaṃ viṣaya.ante nadī.mātṛkaṃ dravya.vanaṃ chedayati so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Between two timber forests — whichever one harvests a timber forest at the boundary of his territory that has great valuable timber, is river-fed, [that one] gains the advantage.

children.text: KAZ07.12.07/ nadī.mātṛkaṃ hi sv.ājīvam apāśrayaś ca^āpadi bhavati //
children.translated_text: For a river-fed [forest] is self-sustaining and serves as a refuge in calamity.

children.text: KAZ07.12.08/ hasti.vanayor api yo bahu.śūra.mṛgaṃ durbala.prativeśaṃ.ananta.avakleśi viṣaya.ante hasti.vanaṃ badhnāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Between two elephant forests — whichever one secures at the boundary of his territory an elephant forest with many fierce [elephants], weak neighbors, causing endless trouble [to others], [that one] gains the advantage.

children.text: KAZ07.12.09/ tatra^api "bahu.kuṇṭha.alpa.śūrayoḥ alpa.śūraṃ śreyaḥ, śūreṣu hi yuddham, alpāḥ śūrā bahūn aśūrān bhañjanti, te bhagnāḥ sva.sainya.avaghātino bhavanti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: In that regard: "Between [a forest with] many tame and few fierce [elephants], one with few fierce [elephants] is better, for fighting is among the fierce; and few fierce [elephants] break many tame ones, and those broken become destructive to their own army" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.12.10/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.12.11/ kuṇṭhā bahavaḥ śreyāṃsaḥ, skandha.viniyogād anekaṃ karma kurvāṇāḥ sveṣām apāśrayo yuddhe, pareṣāṃ durdharṣā vibhīṣaṇāś ca //
children.translated_text: "Many tame [elephants] are better, for being assigned to divisions, they perform many tasks, serve as a support for their own [forces] in battle, and are formidable and terrifying to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.12.12/ bahuṣu hi kuṇṭheṣu vinaya.karmaṇā śakyaṃ śauryam ādhātum, na tv eva^alpeṣu śūreṣu bahutvam iti //
children.translated_text: For among many tame [elephants], it is possible to instill courage through training, but it is not possible to multiply few fierce [elephants]."

children.text: KAZ07.12.13/ khanyor api yaḥ prabhūta.sārām adurga.mārgām alpa.vyaya.ārambhāṃ khaniṃ khānayati, so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Between two mines — whichever one excavates a mine that has abundant valuable [ore], accessible routes, requires little expenditure to develop, [that one] gains the advantage.

children.text: KAZ07.12.14/ tatra^api mahā.sāram alpam alpa.sāraṃ vā prabhūtam iti "mahā.sāram alpaṃ śreyaḥ, vajra.maṇi.muktā.pravāla.hema.rūpya.dhātur hi prabhūtam alpa.sāram atyargheṇa grasate" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: In that regard: between a small [mine with] great [ore] value and an abundant [mine with] small [ore] value — "A small [mine with] great value is better, for diamond, gem, pearl, coral, gold, and silver ores absorb through their high price even an abundant [mine] of little value" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.12.15/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.12.16/ cirād alpo mahā.sārasya kretā vidyate, prabhūtaḥ sātatyād alpa.sārasya //
children.translated_text: "After a long time, a buyer for a small [mine of] great value is [rarely] found; but abundantly for a [mine] of little value, due to constancy [of demand]."

children.text: KAZ07.12.17/ etena vaṇik.patho vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, trade routes are explained.

children.text: KAZ07.12.18/ tatra^api "vāri.sthala.pathayor vāri.pathaḥ śreyān, alpa.vyaya.vyāyāmaḥ prabhūta.paṇya.udayaś ca" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: In that regard: "Between water-routes and land-routes, a water-route is better — it requires little expenditure and effort, and yields abundant merchandise" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.12.19/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.12.20/ samruddha.gatir asārvakālikaḥ prakṛṣṭa.bhaya.yonir niṣpratīkāraś ca vāri.pathaḥ, viparītaḥ sthala.pathaḥ //
children.translated_text: "A water-route has obstructed passage, is not available at all times, is a source of great danger, and is without remedy; the opposite is true of a land-route."

children.text: KAZ07.12.21/ vāri.pathe tu kūla.samyāna.pathayoḥ kūla.pathaḥ paṇya.pattana.bāhulyāt^śreyān, nadī.patho vā, sātatyād viṣahya.ābādhatvāc ca //
children.translated_text: "But among water-routes: between coastal and [open] river routes, a coastal route is better due to the abundance of trading ports; or a river route, due to its constancy and tolerable hazards."

children.text: KAZ07.12.22/ sthala.pathe^api "haimavato dakṣiṇā.pathāt^śreyān, hasty.aśva.gandha.danta.ajina.rūpya.suvarṇa.paṇyāḥ sāravattarāḥ" ity ācāryāḥ" //
children.translated_text: "Among land-routes: 'The Himalayan route is better than the Deccan route — elephants, horses, perfumes, ivory, hides, silver, and gold merchandise are of greater value [there]' — say the teachers."

children.text: KAZ07.12.23/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.12.24/ kambala.ajina.aśva.paṇya.varjāḥ śaṅkha.vajra.maṇi.muktā.suvarṇa.paṇyāś ca prabhūtatarā dakṣiṇā.pathe //
children.translated_text: "Except for blankets, hides, and horse merchandise, conch, diamonds, gems, pearls, and gold merchandise are more abundant on the Deccan route."

children.text: KAZ07.12.25/ dakṣiṇā.pathe^api bahu.khaniḥ sāra.paṇyaḥ prasiddha.gatir alpa.vyaya.vyāyāmo vā vaṇik.pathaḥ śreyān, prabhūta.viṣayo vā phalgu.puṇyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "On the Deccan route, a trade route with many mines, valuable merchandise, well-known passages, and requiring little expenditure and effort is better; or one with a large territory [even if] of small [individual] profit."

children.text: KAZ07.12.26/ tena pūrvaḥ paścimaś ca vaṇik.patho vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the eastern and western trade routes are explained.

children.text: KAZ07.12.27/ tatra^api cakra.pāda.pathayoś cakra.patho vipula.ārambhatvāt^śreyān, deśa.kāla.sambhāvano vā khara.uṣṭra.pathaḥ //
children.translated_text: "In that regard: between cart-routes and foot-routes, a cart-route is better due to the scale of enterprise; or a donkey and camel route, depending on the place and time."

children.text: KAZ07.12.28/ ābhyām aṃsa.patho vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By these two, the shoulder-load route is explained.

children.text: KAZ07.12.29/ para.karma.udayo netuḥ kṣayo vṛddhir viparyaye //
children.translated_text: The rise of the enemy's enterprises means decline for the leader; growth in the reverse case.

children.text: KAZ07.12.30/ tulye karma.pathe sthānaṃ jñeyaṃ svaṃ vijigīṣuṇā //
children.translated_text: When the enterprise-routes are equal, the aspiring conqueror should know this as stability.

children.text: KAZ07.12.31/ alpa.āgama.ativyayatā kṣayo vṛddhir viparyaye //
children.translated_text: Little income and excessive expenditure is decline; growth in the reverse case.

children.text: KAZ07.12.32/ samāya.vyayatā sthānaṃ karmasu jñeyam ātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: Equal income and expenditure should be known as stability in one's enterprises.

children.text: KAZ07.12.33/ tasmād alpa.vyaya.ārambhaṃ durga.ādiṣu mahā.udayam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in fortification and other [enterprises], having obtained one that requires little expenditure but yields great returns —

children.text: KAZ07.12.34/ karma labdhvā viśiṣṭaḥ syād ity uktāḥ karma.saṃdhayaḥ //E
children.translated_text: one becomes distinguished. — Thus are described the enterprise treaties.

children.text:
(pārṣṇi.grāh.cintā)
KAZ07.13.01/ saṃhatya^ari.vijigīṣvor amitrayoḥ para.abhiyoginoḥ pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇator yaḥ śakti.sampannasya pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text:
(Deliberation on striking at the rear)
KAZ07.13.01/ When two enemies — an enemy and a would-be conqueror — both marching to attack [the other], simultaneously seize each other's rear, the one who seizes the rear of the more powerful one outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.02/ śakti.sampanno hy amitram ucchidya pārṣṇi.grāham ucchindyāt, na hīna.śaktir alabdha.lābhaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.02/ For the powerful one, having destroyed his enemy, would destroy the one who struck his rear; but not one of inferior power who has not gained his objective.

children.text: KAZ07.13.03/ śakti.sāmye yo vipula.ārambhasya pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.03/ When they are equal in power, the one who seizes the rear of the one with extensive enterprises outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.04/ vipula.ārambho hy amitram ucchidya pārṣṇi.grāham ucchindyāt, na^alpa.ārambhaḥ sakta.cakraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.04/ For the one with extensive enterprises, having destroyed his enemy, would destroy the one who struck his rear; but not the one with few enterprises whose forces are engaged.

children.text: KAZ07.13.05/ ārambha.sāmye yaḥ sarva.saṃdohena prayātasya pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.05/ When they are equal in enterprises, the one who seizes the rear of the one who has marched with his full forces outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.06/ śūnya.mūlo hy asya sukaro bhavati, naika.deśa.bala.prayātaḥ kṛta.pārṣṇi.pratividhānaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.06/ For one whose base is empty becomes easy [to defeat]; not so one who has marched with only a part of his forces and has made arrangements for the defense of his rear.

children.text: KAZ07.13.07/ bala.upādāna.sāmye yaś cala.amitraṃ prayātasya pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.07/ When they are equal in the [extent of] forces deployed, the one who seizes the rear of the one who has marched against an unstable enemy outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.08/ cala.amitraṃ prayāto hi sukhena^avāpta.siddhiḥ pārṣṇi.grāham ucchindyāt, na sthita.amitraṃ prayātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.08/ For the one who marches against an unstable enemy, having easily achieved his objective, would destroy the one who struck his rear; not so one who marches against a stable enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.13.09/ asau hi durga.pratihataḥ pārṣṇi.grāhe ca pratinivṛttaḥ sthitena^amitreṇa^avagṛhyate //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.09/ For [the latter], repelled by [the enemy's] fort and also having turned back against the one who struck his rear, is seized by the stable enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.13.10/ tena pūrve vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.10/ By this, the preceding [cases] are explained.

children.text: KAZ07.13.11/ śatru.sāmye yo dhārmika.abhiyoginaḥ pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.11/ When the enemies are equal, the one who seizes the rear of the one attacking on just grounds outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.12/ dhārmika.abhiyogī hi sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ ca dveṣyo bhavati, adhārmika.abhiyogī sampriyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.12/ For one who attacks on just grounds becomes odious to both his own and the enemy's [subjects]; one who attacks unjustly becomes popular.

children.text: KAZ07.13.13/ tena mūla.hara.tādātvika.kadarya.abhiyogināṃ pārṣṇi.grahaṇaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.13/ By this, seizing the rear of root-destroyers, present-seizers, and miserly attackers is explained.

children.text: KAZ07.13.14/ mitra.abhiyoginoḥ pārṣṇi.grahaṇe ta eva hetavaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.14/ In seizing the rear of those attacking an ally, the same reasons [apply].

children.text: KAZ07.13.15/ mitram amitraṃ ca^abhiyuñjānayor yo mitra.abhiyoginaḥ pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.15/ When two are attacking — one an ally, the other an enemy — the one who seizes the rear of the ally-attacker outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.16/ mitra.abhiyogī hi sukhena^avāpta.siddhiḥ pārṣṇi.grāham ucchindyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.16/ For the ally-attacker, having easily achieved his objective, would destroy the one who struck his rear.

children.text: KAZ07.13.17/ sukaro hi mitreṇa saṃdhir na^amitreṇa //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.17/ For peace with an ally is easy; not so with an enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.13.18/ mitram amitraṃ ca^uddharator yo^amitra.uddhāriṇaḥ pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇāti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.18/ When two are rescuing — one an ally, the other an enemy — the one who seizes the rear of the enemy-rescuer outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.19/ vṛddha.mitro hy amitra.uddhārī pārṣṇi.grāham ucchindyāt, na^itaraḥ sva.pakṣa.upaghātī //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.19/ For the enemy-rescuer, having strengthened his ally, would destroy the one who struck his rear; not the other, who undermines his own faction.

children.text: KAZ07.13.20/ tayor alabdha.lābha.apagamane yasya.amitro mahato lābhād viyuktaḥ kṣaya.vyaya.adhiko vā sa pārṣṇi.grāho^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.20/ When both fail to gain their objectives and withdraw, the one whose enemy has been deprived of great gains, or has suffered greater losses and expenditure — that rear-striker outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.21/ labdha.lābha.apagamane yasya^amitro lābhena śaktyā hīnaḥ sa pārṣṇi.grāho^atisaṃdhatte, yasya vā yātavyaḥ śatror vigraha.apakāra.samarthaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.21/ When both withdraw having gained their objectives, the one whose enemy has been diminished in gains and power — that rear-striker outwits [the other]; or the one whose target to be attacked is capable of harming the enemy in a conflict.

children.text: KAZ07.13.22/ pārṣṇi.grāhayor api yaḥ śakya.ārambha.bala.upādāna.adhikaḥ sthita.śatruḥ pārśva.sthāyī vā so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.22/ Between two rear-strikers also, the one who is superior in power, enterprises, and forces deployed, who has a stable enemy, or who stands at the flank — he outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.23/ pārśva.sthāyī hi yātavya.abhisāro mūla.ābādhakaś ca bhavati, mūla.ābādhaka eva paścāt.sthāyī //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.23/ For the flank-stander blocks the approach to the target and also threatens the base; whereas the one standing behind merely threatens the base.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.24ab/ pārṣṇi.grāhās trayo jñeyāḥ śatroś ceṣṭā.nirodhakāḥ /
KAZ07.13.24cd/ sāmantaḥ pṛṣṭhato vargaḥ prativeśau ca pārśvayoḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.24ab/ Three types of rear-strikers should be known — those who block the enemy's movements:
KAZ07.13.24cd/ a vassal from behind, a faction, and neighbors at the flanks.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.25ab/ arer netuś ca madhyastho durbalo^antardhir ucyate /
KAZ07.13.25cd/ pratighāto balavato durga.aṭavy.apasāravān //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.25ab/ The middle king [is both the enemy's and the conqueror's] rear-striker; if weak, he is called a 'screened' one;
KAZ07.13.25cd/ if powerful, a 'repeller' — possessing [the advantage of] fort and forest for withdrawal.

children.text: KAZ07.13.26/ madhyamaṃ tvari.vijigīṣvor lipsamānayor madhyamasya pārṣṇiṃ gṛhṇator labdha.lābha.apagamane yo madhyamaṃ mitrād viyojayaty amitraṃ ca mitram āpnoti so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.26/ But when both the enemy and the would-be conqueror are seeking [to win over] the middle king by seizing the middle king's rear — among those withdrawing with their gains, the one who separates the middle king from his ally and himself gains the [middle king's] enemy as an ally — he outwits [the other].
