children.text: KAZ07.13.27/ saṃdheyaś ca śatrur upakurvāṇo, na mitraṃ mitra.bhāvād utkrāntam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.27/ And an enemy who renders service should be made an ally through peace, not an ally who has departed from friendship.

children.text: KAZ07.13.28/ tena^udāsīna.lipsā vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.28/ By this, the [strategy of] winning over the neutral king is explained.

children.text: KAZ07.13.29/ "pārṣṇi.grahaṇa.abhiyānayos tu mantra.yuddhād abhyuccayaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.29/ "In both seizing the rear and marching to attack, however, superiority [comes] from counsel-war [rather than military war].

children.text: Kaś07.13.30/ vyāyāma.yuddhe hi kṣaya.vyayābhyām ubhayor avṛddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.30/ For in a war of exertion, there is no growth for either side, due to losses and expenditures.

children.text: KAZ07.13.31/ jitvā^api hi kṣiṇa.daṇḍa.kośaḥ parājito bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.31/ For even having conquered, one whose army and treasury are depleted becomes as though defeated" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.13.32/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.32/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.13.33/ sumahatā^api kṣaya.vyayena śatru.vināśo^abhyupagantavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.33/ Even with very great losses and expenditure, the destruction of the enemy should be accepted.

children.text: KAZ07.13.34/ tulye kṣaya.vyaye yaḥ purastād dūṣya.balaṃ ghātayitvā nihśalyaḥ paścād vaśya.balo yudhyeta so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.34/ When losses and expenditure are equal, the one who first destroys the disloyal forces and then, free from thorns, fights afterward with obedient forces — he outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.35/ dvayor api purastād dūṣya.bala.ghātinor yo bahulataraṃ śaktimattaram atyanta.dūṣyaṃ ca ghātayet so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.35/ When both first destroy their disloyal forces, the one who destroys [forces that are] more numerous, more powerful, and utterly disloyal — he outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.13.36/ tena^amitra.aṭavī.bala.ghāto vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.13.36/ By this, the destruction of enemy and forest-tribe forces is explained.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.37ab/ pārṣṇi.grāho^abhiyoktā vā yātavyo vā yadā bhavet /
KAZ07.13.37cd/ vijigīṣus tadā tatra netram etat samācaret //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.37ab/ When the rear-striker, the attacker, or the one to be attacked becomes [a threat],
KAZ07.13.37cd/ the would-be conqueror should then apply this strategy there.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.38ab/ pārṣṇi.grāho bhaven netā śatror mitra.abhiyoginaḥ /
KAZ07.13.38cd/ vigrāhya pūrvam ākrandaṃ pārṣṇi.grāha.abhisāriṇā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.38ab/ The rear-striker should become the leader against the enemy who attacks the ally,
KAZ07.13.38cd/ having first engaged the supporter [of the enemy] through the one who approaches the rear-striker.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.39ab/ ākrandena^abhiyuñjānaḥ pārṣṇi.grāhaṃ nivārayet /
KAZ07.13.39cd/ tathā^ākranda.abhisāreṇa pārṣṇi.grāha.abhisāriṇam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.39ab/ One attacking with the supporter should ward off the rear-striker;
KAZ07.13.39cd/ likewise, with the supporter's attacker, [ward off] the one approaching the rear-striker.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.40ab/ ari.mitreṇa mitraṃ ca purastād avaghaṭṭayet /
KAZ07.13.40cd/ mitra.mitram areś ca^api mitra.mitreṇa vārayet //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.40ab/ He should push back the ally's ally with the enemy's ally from the front;
KAZ07.13.40cd/ and he should ward off the enemy's ally's ally with the ally's ally.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.41ab/ mitreṇa grāhayet pārṣṇim abhiyukto^abhiyoginaḥ /
KAZ07.13.41cd/ mitra.mitreṇa ca^ākrandaṃ pārṣṇi.grāhān nivārayet //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.41ab/ When attacked, he should have his ally seize the rear of the attacker;
KAZ07.13.41cd/ and with the ally's ally, he should ward off the rear-strikers from the supporter.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.42ab/ evaṃ maṇḍalam ātma.arthaṃ vijigīṣur niveśayet /
KAZ07.13.42cd/ pṛṣṭhataś ca purastāc ca mitra.prakṛti.sampadā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.42ab/ Thus the would-be conqueror should arrange the circle for his own purpose,
KAZ07.13.42cd/ [securing it] from behind and in front with the excellence of allies and constituent elements.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.43ab/ kṛtsne ca maṇḍale nityaṃ dūtān gūḍhāṃś ca vāsayet /
KAZ07.13.43cd/ mitra.bhūtaḥ sapatnānāṃ hatvā hatvā ca saṃvṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.43ab/ And in the entire circle, he should always station envoys and secret agents,
KAZ07.13.43cd/ appearing as an ally to rivals, destroying them one by one while remaining concealed.

children.text:
KAZ07.13.44ab/ asaṃvṛtasya kāryāṇi prāptāny api viśeṣataḥ /
KAZ07.13.44cd/ nihsaṃśayaṃ vipadyante bhinna.plava iva^udadhau //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.13.44ab/ For the undertakings of one who is unconcealed, even those already achieved, especially,
KAZ07.13.44cd/ assuredly come to ruin, like a vessel with a broken hull upon the ocean.

children.text:
(hīna.śakti.pūraṇam)
KAZ07.14.01/ sāmavāyikair evam abhiyukto vijigīṣur yas teṣāṃ pradhānas taṃ brūyāt "tvayā me saṃdhiḥ, idaṃ hiraṇyam, ahaṃ ca mitram, dvi.guṇā te vṛddhiḥ, na^arhasy ātma.kṣayeṇa mitra.mukhān amitrān vardhayitum, ete hi vṛddhās tvām eva paribhaviṣyanti" iti //
children.translated_text:
(Strengthening a weak force)
KAZ07.14.01/ When the would-be conqueror is attacked thus by confederates, he should address their leader: "Let there be peace between us — here is gold, and I am your ally; your gain will be double. You should not, at the cost of your own destruction, strengthen enemies under the guise of allies, for once they grow strong, they will certainly humiliate you."

children.text: KAZ07.14.02/ bhedaṃ vā brūyāt "anapakāro yathā^aham etaiḥ sambhūya^abhiyuktas tathā tvām apy ete saṃhita.balāḥ svasthā vyasane vā^abhiyokṣyante, balaṃ hi cittaṃ vikaroti, tad eṣāṃ vighātaya" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.02/ Or he should speak of dissension: "Just as these have combined to attack me, an innocent, so too will they, with combined forces, attack you — whether at ease or in difficulty — for power corrupts the mind; therefore destroy their [alliance]."

children.text: KAZ07.14.03/ bhinneṣu pradhānam upagṛhya hīneṣu vikramayet, hīnān anugrāhya vā pradhāne, yathā vā śreyo^abhimanyeta tathā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.03/ When they are divided, having won over the leader, he should act with vigor against the inferiors; or, having conciliated the inferiors, [he should act] against the leader; or however he deems best.

children.text: KAZ07.14.04/ vairaṃ vā parair grāhayitvā visaṃvādayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.04/ Or, having caused them to take up enmity with others, he should break their trust.

children.text: KAZ07.14.05/ phala.bhūyastvena vā pradhānam upajāpya saṃdhiṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.05/ Or, having won over the leader through an abundance of rewards, he should make peace.

children.text: KAZ07.14.06/ atha^ubhaya.vetanāḥ phala.bhūyastvaṃ darśayantaḥ sāmavāyikān "atisaṃhitāḥ stha" ity udddūṣayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.06/ Then, double agents, displaying the abundance of rewards, should corrupt the confederates [saying]: "You are being overly combined."

children.text: KAZ07.14.07/ duṣṭeṣu saṃdhiṃ dūṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.07/ When corrupted, he should [further] spoil [their] peace.

children.text: KAZ07.14.08/ atha^ubhaya.vetanā bhūyo bhedam eṣāṃ kuryuḥ "evaṃ tad yad asmābhir darśitam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.08/ Then the double agents should further divide them [saying]: "See, it is just as we showed you."

children.text: KAZ07.14.09/ bhinneṣv anyatama.upagraheṇa ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.09/ When divided, he should act by winning over any one of them.

KAZ07.14.10/ In the absence of a leader among the confederates, [the king should win over] the one who encourages [them], the one of firm action, the one with loyal subjects, the one who joined the coalition out of greed or fear, the one who fears the would-be conqueror, the one connected by [claim to] a kingdom, an ally, or one with an unstable enemy — the former preferred in the absence of the latter — [he should win over]: the encourager through self-surrender; the one of firm action through conciliation and submission; the one with loyal subjects through the gift of a daughter and maintenance; the greedy one through doubling his share;
the one afraid of them through support of treasury and army; the one afraid of [the conqueror] himself through a guarantee and offering of securities; the one connected by kingdom through union; an ally through things that are agreeable and beneficial to both; or through the surrender of a favor; an unstable enemy, once defeated, through non-hostility and assistance.

children.text: KAZ07.14.11/ yo vā yathā^ayogaṃ bhajeta taṃ tathā sādhayet, sāma.dāna.bheda.daṇḍair vā yathā^āpatsu vyākhyāsyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.11/ Or, whoever submits in whatever manner, he should be won over accordingly — through conciliation, gifts, dissension, or force, as we shall explain [in the chapter] on calamities.

children.text: KAZ07.14.12/ vyasana.upaghāta.tvarito vā kośa.daṇḍābhyāṃ deśe kāle kārye vā^avadhṛtaṃ saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.12/ Or, pressed by calamity or attack, he should seek peace with his treasury and army, [or with one who is] determined regarding place, time, or task.

children.text: KAZ07.14.13/ kṛta.saṃdhir hīnam ātmānaṃ pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.13/ Having made peace, he should remedy his weakness.

children.text: KAZ07.14.14/ pakṣe hīno bandhu.mitra.pakṣaṃ kurvīta, durgam aviṣahyaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.14/ If weak in faction, he should build a faction of kinsmen, friends, and allies, or [build] an impregnable fort.

children.text: KAZ07.14.15/ durga.mitra.pratiṣṭabdho hi sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ ca pūjyo bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.15/ For one who is supported by a fort and friends is honored by both his own and others.

children.text: KAZ07.14.16/ mantra.śakti.hīnaḥ prājña.puruṣa.upacayaṃ vidyā.vṛddha.samyogaṃ vā kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.16/ If weak in the power of counsel, he should acquire men of wisdom, or cultivate the company of the learned and experienced.

children.text: KAZ07.14.17/ tathā hi sadyaḥ śreyaḥ prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.17/ For thereby he quickly attains prosperity.

children.text: KAZ07.14.18/ prabhāva.hīnaḥ prakṛti.yoga.kṣema.siddhau yateta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.18/ If weak in power, he should strive for the success of his subjects' livelihood and security.

children.text: KAZ07.14.19/ jana.padaḥ sarva.karmaṇāṃ yoniḥ, tataḥ prabhāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.19/ The countryside is the source of all enterprises; from it comes power.

children.text: KAZ07.14.20/ tasya sthānam ātmanaś ca^āpadi durgam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.20/ Its refuge, and his own in calamity, is the fort.

children.text: KAZ07.14.21/ setu.bandhaḥ sasyānāṃ yoniḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.21/ Embankments are the source of crops.

children.text: KAZ07.14.22/ nitya.anuṣakto hi varṣa.guṇa.lābhaḥ setu.vāpeṣu //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.22/ For the gain from the rains is always connected with embankments and seed-beds.

children.text: KAZ07.14.23/ vaṇik.pathaḥ para.atisaṃdhānasya yoniḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.23/ Trade-routes are the source of outwitting the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.14.24/ vaṇik.pathena hi daṇḍa.gūḍha.puruṣa.atinayanaṃ śastra.āvaraṇa.yāna.vāhana.krayaś ca kriyate, praveśo nirṇayanaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.24/ For through trade-routes, the secret transport of army and agents, the purchase of weapons, armor, vehicles, and conveyances, and [their] entry and export are accomplished.

children.text: KAZ07.14.25/ khaniḥ saṃgrāma.upakaraṇānāṃ yoniḥ, dravya.vanaṃ durga.karmaṇāṃ yāna.rathayoś ca, hasti.vanaṃ hastinām, gava.aśva.khara.uṣṭrāṇāṃ ca vrajaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.25/ Mines are the source of war materials; the forest of produce for fort construction and for chariots and carts; the elephant forest for elephants; and the cattle-pens for cattle, horses, donkeys, and camels.

children.text: KAZ07.14.26/ teṣām alābhe bandhu.mitra.kulebhyaḥ samārjanam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.26/ When these are unavailable, they should be acquired from kinsmen, friends, and clans.

children.text: KAZ07.14.27/ utsāha.hīnaḥ śreṇī.pravīra.puruṣāṇāṃ cora.gaṇa.āṭavika.mleccha.jātīnāṃ para.apakāriṇāṃ gūḍha.puruṣāṇāṃ ca yathā.lābbham upacayaṃ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.27/ If weak in enterprise, he should build up, as opportunity allows, the guild-warriors, the brave, the bands of thieves, forest-tribes, and barbarian peoples — those harmful to the enemy — and secret agents.

children.text: KAZ07.14.28/ para.miśra.apratīkāram ābalīyasaṃ vā pareṣu prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.14.28/ He should employ against enemies a mixed counter-force or the strategy of the weaker.

children.text:
KAZ07.14.29ab/ evaṃ pakṣeṇa mantreṇa dravyeṇa ca balena ca /
KAZ07.14.29cd/ sampannaḥ pratinirgacchet para.avagraham ātmanaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.14.29ab/ Thus, endowed with faction, counsel, resources, and army,
KAZ07.14.29cd/ he should march out to break the enemy's hold upon him.

children.text:
(vigṛhya.uparodha.hetavah - daṇḍa.upanata.vṛttam)
KAZ07.15.01/ durbalo rājā balavatā^abhiyuktas tad.viśiṣṭa.balam āśrayeta yam itaro mantra.śaktyā na^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Causes of sitting quiet after hostility — Conduct of one submitted to force)
KAZ07.15.01/ A weak king attacked by a powerful one should seek refuge with one of superior forces whom the other cannot outwit through the power of counsel.

children.text: KAZ07.15.02/ tulya.mantra.śaktīnām āyatta.sampado vṛddha.samyogād vā viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.02/ When they are equal in the power of counsel, the distinction comes from the advantage of acquired resources or the company of the experienced.

children.text: KAZ07.15.03/ viśiṣṭa.bala.abhāve sama.balais tulya.bala.saṃghair vā balavataḥ sambhūya tiṣṭhed yān na mantra.prabhāva.śaktibhyām atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.03/ In the absence of a superior force, he should stand firm against a powerful [enemy] by allying with equals — equal in individual strength or combined — whom he could not outwit through counsel, might, or power.

children.text: KAZ07.15.04/ tulya.mantra.prabhāva.śaktīnāṃ vipula.ārambhato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.04/ Among those equal in counsel, might, and power, the distinction lies in the scale of their undertakings.

children.text: KAZ07.15.05/ sama.bala.abhāve hīna.balaiḥ śucibhir utsāhibhiḥ pratyanīka.bhūtair balavataḥ sambhūya tiṣṭhed yān na mantra.prabhāva.utsāha.śaktibhir atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.05/ In the absence of equal forces, he should stand firm against a powerful [enemy] by allying with weaker ones who are trustworthy, energetic, and hostile to the opponent — whom he could not outwit through counsel, might, or energetic power.

children.text: KAZ07.15.06/ tulya.utsāha.śaktīnāṃ sva.yuddha.bhūmi.lābhād viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.06/ Among those equal in energetic power, the distinction lies in obtaining a battlefield favorable to one's own forces.

children.text: KAZ07.15.07/ tulya.bhūmīnāṃ sva.yuddha.kāla.lābhād viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.07/ Among those with equal terrain, the distinction lies in obtaining a time of battle favorable to one's own forces.

children.text: KAZ07.15.08/ tulya.deśa.kālānāṃ yugya.śastra.āvaraṇato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.08/ Among those equal in place and time, the distinction lies in draft-animals, weapons, and armor.

children.text: KAZ07.15.09/ sahāya.abhāve durgam āśrayeta yatra^amitraḥ prabhūta.sainyo^api bhakta.yavasa.indhana.udaka.uparodhaṃ na kuryāt svayaṃ ca kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ yujyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.09/ In the absence of allies, he should take refuge in a fort where the enemy, even with a large army, would be unable to blockade food, fodder, fuel, and water, and would himself suffer attrition and expenditure.

children.text: KAZ07.15.10/ tulya.durgāṇāṃ nicaya.apasārato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.10/ Among forts of equal [strength], the distinction lies in the stores and the [possibility of] withdrawal.

children.text: KAZ07.15.11/ nicaya.apasāra.sampannaṃ hi manuṣya.durgam icched iti kauṭilyaḥ //KAZ07.15.12a/tad ebhiḥ kārṇair āśrayeta - "pārṣṇi.grāham āsāraṃ madhyamam udāsīnaṃ vā pratipādayiṣyāmi, sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhānām anyatamena^asya rājyaṃ hārayiṣyāmi ghātayiṣyāmi vā - //
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.15.11/ He should prefer a fort with ample stores and withdrawal routes that is manned — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.
KAZ07.15.12a/ He should take refuge there for these reasons: 'I shall win over the one who attacks from the rear, the [rear-support] base, the middle [king], or the neutral [king]; I shall have his kingdom taken away or himself killed through one of the neighboring kings, forest chiefs, men of his own lineage, or imprisoned princes —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12b/ kṛtya.pakṣa.upagraheṇa vā^asya durge rāṣṭre skandha.āvāre vā kopaṃ samutthāpayiṣyāmi, śastra.agni.rasa.praṇidhānair aupaniṣadikair vā yathā.iṣṭam āsannaṃ haniṣyāmi - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12b/ or by winning over his faction, I shall stir up rebellion in his fort, countryside, or camp; or with weapons, fire, poison-agents, or esoteric means, I shall kill him at close quarters at will —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12c/ svayaṃ.adhiṣṭhitena vā yoga.praṇidhānena kṣaya.vyayam enam upaneṣyāmi, kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.upatapte vā^asya mitra.varge sainye vā krameṇa^upajāpaṃ prāpsyāmi - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12c/ or through personally directed strategic deployment, I shall wear him down through attrition and expenditure; or when his ally-group or army is worn by attrition, expenditure, and [prolonged] absence, I shall gradually succeed in enticing [them] —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12d/ vīvadha.āsāra.prasāra.vadhena vā^asya skandha.āvāra.avagrahaṃ kariṣyāmi, daṇḍa.upanayena vā^asya randhram utthāpya sarva.saṃdohena prahariṣyāmi, pratihata.utsāhena vā yathā.iṣṭaṃ saṃdhim avāpsyāmi, mayi pratibaddhasya vā sarvataḥ kopāḥ samutthāsyanti - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12d/ or by cutting off his supply lines for fodder, base, and dispersal, I shall pin down his camp; or by bringing up my forces against his weakness, I shall strike with full concentration; or when his élan is broken, I shall obtain a peace treaty on my terms; or while he is tied down against me, revolts will arise against him on all sides —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12e/ nirāsāraṃ vā^asya mūlaṃ mitra.aṭavī.daṇḍair uddhātayiṣyāmi, mahato vā deśasya yoga.kṣemam ihasthaḥ pālayiṣyāmi, sva.vikṣiptaṃ mitra.vikṣiptaṃ vā me sainyam ihasthasya^ekastham aviṣahyaṃ bhaviṣyati, nimna.khāta.rātri.yuddha.viśāradaṃ vā me sainyaṃ pathya.ābādha.muktam āsanne karma kariṣyati - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12e/ or I shall have his base, which is without support, destroyed by allies, forest tribes, and [my own] forces; or, stationed here, I shall protect the livelihood and security of a great territory; or my army — whether scattered by myself or scattered by allies — will become, while I am stationed here, unified and irresistible; or my army, skilled in fighting on low ground, in trenches, and at night, freed from the hardship of the road, will do its work at close quarters —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12f/ viruddha.deśa.kālam iha.āgato vā svayam eva kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ na bhaviṣyati, mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.abhigamyo^ayaṃ deśo durga.aṭavy.apasāra.bāhulyāt - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12f/ or coming here against unfavorable terrain and season, the enemy will himself perish through attrition and expenditure; this region is approachable only at great cost due to the abundance of forts, forests, and withdrawal routes —

children.text: KAZ07.15.12g/ pareṣāṃ vyādhi.prāyaḥ sainya.vyāyāmānām alabdha.bhaumaś ca, tam āpad.gataḥ pravekṣyati, praviṣṭo vā na nirgamiṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.12g/ [this region] is prone to disease for enemy forces, and unfavorable terrain for their maneuvers; in distress, he will enter [the trap], and once entered, he will not get out.'

children.text: KAZ07.15.13/ "kāraṇa.abhāve bala.samucchraye vā parasya durgam unmucya^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.13/ 'In the absence of [any such] advantage, or when the enemy's forces grow, he should abandon the fort and leave.'

children.text: KAZ07.15.14/ agni.pataṅgavad amitre vā praviśet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.14/ 'Or he should rush into the enemy like a moth into a flame.'

children.text: KAZ07.15.15/ anyatara.siddhir hi tyakta.ātmano bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.15/ 'For one who has abandoned [attachment to] life achieves one outcome or the other' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.15.16/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.16/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.15.17/ saṃdheyatām ātmanaḥ parasya ca^upalabhya saṃdadhīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.17/ Having assessed the possibilities of a treaty for himself and the other, he should make peace.

children.text: KAZ07.15.18/ viparyaye vikrameṇa saṃdhim apasāraṃ vā lipseta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.18/ In the contrary case, he should seek a treaty or withdrawal through aggression.

children.text: KAZ07.15.19/ saṃdheyasya vā dūtaṃ preṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.19/ Or he should send an envoy to one amenable to a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.15.20/ tena vā preṣitam artha.mānābhyāṃ satkṛtya brūyāt "idaṃ rājñaḥ paṇya.agāram, idaṃ devī.kumārāṇām, devī.kumāra.vacanāt, idaṃ rājyam ahaṃ ca tvad.arpaṇaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.20/ Or he should honor an envoy sent by the other with wealth and distinction, and say: 'This is the king's store-house; this belongs to the queen and princes. By command of the queen and princes — this kingdom and I myself are at your disposal.'

children.text: KAZ07.15.21/ labdha.saṃśrayaḥ samaya.ācārikavad bhartari varteta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.21/ Having obtained protection, he should conduct himself toward his protector as one bound by a customary agreement.

children.text: KAZ07.15.22/ durga.ādīni ca karmāṇi āvāha.vivāha.putra.abhiṣeka.aśva.paṇya.hasti.grahaṇa.sattra.yātrā.vihāra.gamanāni ca^anujñātaḥ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.22/ He should undertake fort-building and other operations, [as well as] marriage alliances (giving and receiving), coronation of sons, horse-trading, elephant-capture, festivals, processions, pleasure-trips — all with [his protector's] permission.

children.text: KAZ07.15.23/ sva.bhūmy.avasthita.prakṛti.saṃdhim upaghātam apasṛteṣu vā sarvam anujñātaḥ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.23/ [He should undertake] with permission all [activities including] treaties with subjects settled in his own territory, or operations against those who have withdrawn, defected, or caused harm.

children.text: KAZ07.15.24/ duṣṭa.paura.jānapado vā nyāya.vṛttir anyāṃ bhūmiṃ yāceta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.24/ Or [if his subjects are] hostile to him, he should, while maintaining righteous conduct, request another territory.

children.text: KAZ07.15.25/ duṣyavad upāṃśu.daṇḍena vā pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.25/ Or he should act against the marked [enemies] through covert punishment, as [described for] the expendable.

children.text: KAZ07.15.26/ ucitāṃ vā mitrād bhūmiṃ dīyamānāṃ na pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.26/ Or he should not accept territory offered by an ally if it is [too] familiar [and thus would create dependence].

children.text: KAZ07.15.27/ mantri.purohita.senā.pati.yuva.rājānām anyatamam adṛśyamāne bhartari paśyet, yathā.śakti ca^upakuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.27/ When the protector is absent, he should look to one of the minister, chaplain, commander-in-chief, or crown prince, and should assist [the protector] according to his ability.

children.text: KAZ07.15.28/ daivata.svasti.vācaneṣu tat.parā āśiṣo vācayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.28/ At divine benedictions and blessings, he should have prayers recited devoted to [the protector].

children.text: KAZ07.15.29/ sarvatra^ātma.nisargaṃ guṇaṃ brūyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.15.29/ Everywhere, he should speak of his own devotion as a virtue.

children.text:
KAZ07.15.30ab/ samyukta.balavat.sevī viruddhaḥ śaṅkita.ādibhiḥ /
KAZ07.15.30cd/ varteta daṇḍa.upanato bhartary evam avasthitaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.15.30ab/ One who serves a powerful master in alliance, though threatened by suspicious [allies] and others,
KAZ07.15.30cd/ should conduct himself thus, as one who has submitted to [another's] authority.

children.text:
(daṇḍa.upanāyi.vṛttam)
KAZ07.16.01/ anujñāta.saṃdhi.paṇa.udvega.karaṃ balavān vijigīṣamāṇo yataḥ sva.bhūmiḥ sva.ṛtu.vṛttiś ca sva.sainyānām, adurga.apasāraḥ śatrur.apārṣṇir anāsāraś ca, tato yāyāt //
children.translated_text:
(Conduct of one who brings [another] under his authority)
KAZ07.16.01/ The powerful one who wishes to conquer, [having made] a treaty-agreement that causes alarm to the one who has submitted — should march from the direction that is favorable terrain and season for his own forces, and where the enemy is without fort-support, without rear-support, and without a base.

children.text: KAZ07.16.02/ viparyaye kṛta.pratīkāro yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.02/ In the contrary case, he should march after having taken countermeasures.

children.text: KAZ07.16.03/ sāma.dānābhyāṃ durbalān upanamayet, bheda.daṇḍābhyāṃ balavataḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.03/ He should bring the weak to submission through conciliation and gifts, and the powerful through dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ07.16.04/ niyoga.vikalpa.samuccayaiś ca^upāyānām anantara.eka.antarāḥ prakṛtīḥ sādhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.04/ Through application — singly, alternatively, or in combination — of [the four] means, he should subdue the constituent elements one by one, skipping alternate ones.

children.text: KAZ07.16.05/ grāma.araṇya.upajīvi.vraja.vaṇik.patha.anupālanam ujjhita.apasṛta.apakāriṇāṃ ca^arpaṇam iti sāntvam ācaret //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.05/ Protecting villages, forest-dwellers, pastoral camps, and trade routes, and handing over deserters, defectors, and offenders — this constitutes conciliation.

children.text: KAZ07.16.06/ bhūmi.dravya.kanyā.dānam abhayasya ca^iti dānam ācaret //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.06/ Giving land, goods, and maidens, and [granting] immunity — this constitutes gifts.

children.text: KAZ07.16.07/ sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhānām anyatama.upagraheṇa kośa.daṇḍa.bhūmi.dāya.yācanam iti bhedam ācaret //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.07/ Demanding treasury, army, or land-revenue through the leverage of one of the neighboring kings, forest chiefs, men of [the enemy's] lineage, or imprisoned princes — this constitutes dissension.

children.text: KAZ07.16.08/ prakāśa.kūṭa.tūṣṇīṃ.yuddha.durga.lambha.upāyair amitra.pragrahaṇam iti daṇḍam ācaret //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.08/ Seizing the enemy through open warfare, deceptive warfare, silent [covert] warfare, and fort-capture strategies — this constitutes force.

children.text: KAZ07.16.09/ evam utsāhavato daṇḍa.upakāriṇaḥ sthāpayet, sva.prabhāvavataḥ kośa.upakāriṇaḥ, prajñāvato bhūmy.upakāriṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.09/ Thus, he should establish the energetic ones as contributors of military force, the self-reliant ones as contributors to the treasury, and the wise ones as contributors of land.

children.text: KAZ07.16.10/ teṣāṃ paṇya.pattana.grāma.khani.saṃjātena ratna.sāra.phalgu.kupyena dravya.hasti.vana.vraja.samutthena yāna.vāhanena vā yad bahuśa upakaroti tac citra.bhogam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.10/ Among these, the territory from which one receives manifold revenue — through gems, essential commodities, minor goods, and raw materials produced from trade centers, ports, villages, and mines, and through conveyances and mounts produced from forests and cattle camps — that has variegated revenue.

children.text: KAZ07.16.11/ yad daṇḍena kośena vā mahad upakaroti tan mahā.bhogam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.11/ That from which one receives great assistance through military force or treasury — that has great revenue.

children.text: KAZ07.16.12/ yad daṇḍa.kośa.bhūmībhir upakaroti tat sarva.bhogam //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.12/ That from which one receives assistance through military force, treasury, and land — that has complete revenue.

children.text: KAZ07.16.13/ yad amitram ekataḥ pratikaroti tad ekato.bhogi //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.13/ That which counteracts the enemy from one side — that has revenue from one direction.

children.text: KAZ07.16.14/ yad amitram āsāraṃ ca^ubhayataḥ pratikaroti tad ubhayato.bhogi //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.14/ That which counteracts both the enemy and the base [of the rear-attacker] from two sides — that has revenue from two directions.

children.text: KAZ07.16.15/ yad amitra.āsāra.prativeśa.āṭavikān sarvataḥ pratikaroti tat sarvato.bhogi //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.15/ That which counteracts the enemy, the base, the neighbors, and the forest chiefs from all sides — that has revenue from all directions.

children.text: KAZ07.16.16a/ pārṣṇi.grāhaś ca^āṭavikaḥ śatru.mukhyaḥ śatrur vā bhūmi.dāna.sādhyaḥ kaścid āsādyeta, nirguṇayā bhūmyā^enam upagrāhayet, apratisambaddhayā durgastham, nirupajīvyayā^āṭavikaṃ - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.16a/ And if someone — a rear-attacker, a forest chief, the enemy's leader, or the enemy himself — can be won over by a grant of land: he should win over [the rear-attacker] with unprofitable land, [the king] stationed in a fort with unconnected [land], a forest chief with uninhabitable [land] —

children.text: KAZ07.16.16b/ pratyādeyayā tat.kulīnaṃ śatroḥ, apacchinnayā śatror aparuddhaṃ nitya.amitrayā śreṇī.balam, balavat.sāmantayā saṃhata.balam, ubhābhyāṃ yuddhe pratilomam, - //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.16b/ a pretender of the enemy's lineage with revocable [land], the enemy's imprisoned [prince] with land cut off from [the enemy], guild-forces with [land having] a permanent enemy, a confederate force with [land having] a powerful neighbor, one hostile in battle with both [types of land] —

children.text: KAZ07.16.16c/ alabdha.vyāyāmayā^utsāhinam, śūyayā^ari.pakṣīyam, karśitayā^apavāhitam, mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśayā gata.pratyāgatam, anapāśrayayā pratyapasṛtam, pareṇa^anadhivāsyayā svayam eva bhartāram upagrāhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.16c/ an energetic [ally] with land that affords no room for maneuver, one allied with the enemy with desolate [land], a displaced [king] with exhausted [land], one who has come and gone [repeatedly] with land requiring great cost for settlement, one who has retreated with supportless [land], and he should win over the sovereign himself with [land] uninhabitable by others.

children.text: KAZ07.16.17/ teṣāṃ mahā.upakāraṃ nirvikāraṃ ca^anuvartayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.17/ Among these, he should uphold the one who renders great service and is trustworthy.

children.text: KAZ07.16.18/ pratilomam upāṃśunā sādhayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.18/ The hostile [one] he should subdue through covert means.

children.text: KAZ07.16.19/ upakāriṇam upakāra.śaktyā toṣayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.19/ The helpful one he should satisfy according to the measure of his help.

children.text: KAZ07.16.20/ prayāsataś ca^artha.mānau kuryād, vyasaneṣu ca^anugraham //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.20/ He should confer wealth and honor on those who exert themselves, and grant relief in calamities.

children.text: KAZ07.16.21/ svayaṃ.āgatānāṃ yathā.iṣṭa.darśanaṃ pratividhānaṃ ca kuryāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.21/ He should grant audience and make provision as desired for those who come of their own accord.

children.text: KAZ07.16.22/ paribhava.upaghāta.kutsa.ativādāṃś ca^eṣu na prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.22/ And he should not subject them to insult, injury, reproach, or harsh words.

children.text: KAZ07.16.23/ dattvā ca^abhayaṃ pitā^iva^anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.23/ Having granted immunity, he should protect [them] like a father.

children.text: KAZ07.16.24/ yaś ca^asya^apakuryāt tad doṣam abhivikhyāpya prakāśam enaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.24/ And whoever acts against him — having publicized his offenses, he should execute him publicly.

children.text: KAZ07.16.25/ para.udvega.kāraṇād vā dāṇḍakarmikavac ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.25/ Or, to cause alarm to others, he should act like an enforcer of punishments.

children.text: KAZ07.16.26/ na ca hatasya bhūmi.dravya.putra.dārān abhimanyeta //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.26/ But he should not covet the land, goods, sons, or wives of the slain.

children.text: KAZ07.16.27/ kulyān apy asya sveṣu pātreṣu sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.27/ He should also install [the slain's] kinsmen in their proper positions.

children.text: KAZ07.16.28/ karmaṇi mṛtasya putraṃ rājye sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.28/ He should install the son of one who has died in action on his throne.

children.text: KAZ07.16.29/ evam asya daṇḍa.upanatāḥ putra.pautrān anuvartante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.29/ Thus, those who have submitted to his authority follow him through sons and grandsons.

children.text: KAZ07.16.30/ yas tu^upanatān hatvā baddhvā vā bhūmi.dravya.putra.dārān abhimanyeta tasya^udvignaṃ maṇḍalam abhāvāya^uttiṣṭhate //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.30/ But one who, after killing or imprisoning those who have submitted, covets their land, goods, sons, and wives — against him the alarmed circle [of kings] rises up for his destruction.

children.text: KAZ07.16.31/ ye ca^asya^amātyāḥ sva.bhūmiṣv āyattās te ca^asya^udvignā maṇḍalam āśrayante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.31/ And those ministers of his who are established in their own territories, being alarmed by him, take refuge in the circle [of kings].

children.text: KAZ07.16.32/ svayaṃ vā rājyaṃ prāṇān vā^asya^abhimanyante //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.16.32/ Or they themselves covet his kingdom or his life.

children.text:
KAZ07.16.33ab/ sva.bhūmiṣu ca rājānas tasmāt sāmnā^anupālitāḥ /
KAZ07.16.33cd/ bhavanty anuguṇā rājñaḥ putra.pautra.anuvartinaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ07.16.33ab/ Therefore, kings who have been protected with conciliation in their own territories
KAZ07.16.33cd/ become favorable to the king, following him through sons and grandsons.

children.text:
(samdhi.karma -samādhi.mokṣah)
KAZ07.17.01/ śamaḥ saṃdhiḥ samādhir ity eko^arthaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Treaty operations — peace and its release)
KAZ07.17.01/ <s>Śama</s> (pacification), <s>saṃdhi</s> (treaty), and <s>samādhi</s> (settlement) — [these are] synonymous.

children.text: KAZ07.17.02/ rājñāṃ viśvāsa.upagamaḥ śamaḥ saṃdhiḥ samādhir iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.02/ The approach of mutual trust between kings is pacification, treaty, settlement.

children.text: KAZ07.17.03/ "satyaṃ śapatho vā calaḥ saṃdhiḥ, pratibhūḥ pratigraho vā sthāvaraḥ" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.03/ 'A treaty [sealed with] truth or an oath is unstable; one [guaranteed by] hostages or pledges is stable' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ07.17.04/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.04/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ07.17.05/ satyaṃ śapatho vā paratra^iha ca sthāvaraḥ saṃdhiḥ, iha.artha eva pratibhūḥ pratigraho vā bala.apekṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.05/ A treaty [sealed with] truth or an oath is stable both in this world and the next; one [guaranteed by] hostages or pledges concerns only this-worldly matters and depends on [relative] strength.

children.text: KAZ07.17.06/ "saṃhitāḥ smaḥ" iti satya.saṃdhāḥ pūrve rājānaḥ satyena saṃdadhire //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.06/ 'We are united' — thus the righteous ancient kings made treaties through truth.

children.text: KAZ07.17.07/ tasya^atikrame śapathena agny.udaka.sītā.prākāra.loṣṭa.hasti.skandha.aśva.pṛṣṭa.ratha.upastha.śastra.ratna.bīja.gandha.rasa.suvarṇa.hiraṇyāny ālebhire "hanyur etāni tyajeyuś ca^enaṃ yaḥ śapatham atikrāmet" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.07/ In case of its violation, they swore oaths touching fire, water, furrow, rampart, clod, elephant's shoulder, horse's back, chariot's seat, weapons, gems, seeds, perfumes, liquids, gold, and silver: 'May these destroy and abandon the one who violates the oath.'

children.text: KAZ07.17.08/ śapatha.atikrame mahatāṃ tapasvināṃ mukhyānāṃ vā prātibhāvya.bandhaḥ pratibhūḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.08/ In case of oath-violation, the guarantee by the suretyship of great ascetics or leading men — that is the hostage [guarantee].

children.text: KAZ07.17.09/ tasmin yaḥ para.avagraha.samarthān pratibhuvo gṛhṇāti, so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.09/ In that, the one who obtains hostages capable of seizing the other's [assets] outwits [the other].

children.text: KAZ07.17.10/ viparīto^atisaṃdhīyate //
children.translated_text: KAZ07.17.10/ The one who does the opposite is outwitted.

children.text: KAZ07.17.11/ bandhu.mukhya.pragrahaḥ pratigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: The seizing of kinsmen and chiefs is a hostage treaty (<s>pratigraha</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.17.12/ tasmin yo dūṣya.amātyaṃ dūṣya.apatyaṃ vā dadāti, so^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Therein, the one who gives a disloyal minister or disloyal offspring outmaneuvers.

children.text:
KAZ07.17.13/ viparīto^atisaṃdhīyate
KAZ07.17.14/ pratigraha.grahaṇa.viśvastasya hi paraś chidreṣu nirapekṣaḥ praharati //
children.translated_text:
The opposite is outmaneuvered.
For the enemy, having gained the trust [of the hostage-giver] through accepting the hostage, strikes at his vulnerabilities without hesitation.

children.text: KAZ07.17.15/ apatya.samādhau tu kanyā.putra.dāne dadat tu kanyām atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: But in an offspring-reconciliation treaty, between the giving of a daughter and a son, one who gives a daughter outmaneuvers.

children.text: KAZ07.17.16/ kanyā hy adāyādā pareṣām eva^arthāya^ākleśyā(?) ca //
children.translated_text: For a daughter is not an heir, exists for others' benefit, and is free from trouble.

children.text: KAZ07.17.17/ viparītaḥ putraḥ //
children.translated_text: A son is the opposite.

children.text: KAZ07.17.18/ putrayor api yo jātyaṃ prājñaṃ śūraṃ kṛta.astram eka.putraṃ vā dadāti so^atisaṃdhīyate //
children.translated_text: Even between two sons, the one who gives one who is of noble birth, intelligent, brave, skilled in arms, or an only son — is outmaneuvered.

children.text: KAZ07.17.19/ viparīto^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: The one who gives the opposite outmaneuvers.

children.text: KAZ07.17.20/ jātyād ajātyo hi lupta.dāyāda.saṃtānatvād ādhātuṃ śreyān, prājñād aprājño mantra.śakti.lopāt, śūrād aśūra utsāha.śakti.lopāt, kṛta.astrād akṛta.astraḥ prahartavya.sampal.lopāt, eka.putrād aneka.putro nirapekṣatvāt //
children.translated_text: For one of ignoble birth is better to pledge than one of noble birth — because [the ignoble one's] line of heirs is cut off; one who is unintelligent rather than intelligent — because of the loss of the power of counsel; one who is cowardly rather than brave — because of the loss of the power of enterprise; one unskilled in arms rather than skilled — because of the loss of the ability to strike; one with many sons rather than an only son — because of the absence of attachment.

children.text: KAZ07.17.21/ jātya.prājñayor jātyam aprājñam aiśvarya.prakṛtir anuvartate, prājñam ajātyaṃ mantra.adhikāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Between one of noble birth and one who is intelligent — one of ignoble birth who is intelligent [is preferred] for the authority of counsel; the sovereignty of nature follows the noble [but] unintelligent one.

children.text: KAZ07.17.22/ mantra.adhikāre^api vṛddha.samyogāj jātyaḥ prājñam atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Even in the authority of counsel, through association with elders, one of noble birth outmaneuvers the intelligent one.

children.text: KAZ07.17.23/ prājña.śūrayoḥ prājñam aśūraṃ mati.karmaṇāṃ yogo^anuvartate, śūram aprājñaṃ vikrama.adhikāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Between one who is intelligent and one who is brave — one who is intelligent but cowardly commands the combination of wisdom and action; the brave but unintelligent one [has] the authority of valor.

children.text: KAZ07.17.24/ vikrama.adhikāre^api hastinam iva lubdhakaḥ prājñaḥ śūram atisaṃdhatteś //
children.translated_text: Even in the authority of valor, the intelligent one outmaneuvers the brave — like a hunter [outmaneuvers] an elephant.

children.text: KAZ07.17.25/ śūra.kṛta.astrayoḥ śūram akṛta.astraṃ vikrama.vyavasāyo^anuvartate, kṛta.astram aśūraṃ lakṣya.lambha.adhikāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Between one who is brave and one skilled in arms — the brave but unskilled commands the determination of valor; the skilled but cowardly one [has] the authority of hitting the mark.

children.text: KAZ07.17.26/ lakṣya.lambha.adhikāre^api sthairya.pratipatty.asammoṣaiḥ śūraḥ kṛta.astram atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: Even in the authority of hitting the mark, the brave one outmaneuvers the skilled through steadfastness, resourcefulness, and presence of mind.

children.text: KAZ07.17.27/ bahv.eka.putrayor bahu.putra ekaṃ dattvā śeṣa.pratiṣṭabdhaḥ saṃdhim atikrāmati, na^itaraḥ //
children.translated_text: Between one with many sons and one with one son — the one with many, having given one, is supported by the remainder and may violate the treaty; the other cannot.

children.text: KAZ07.17.28/ putra.sarva.sva.dāne saṃdhiś cet putra.phalato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: If the treaty involves the giving of a son and all one's property — the distinction is based on the [quality of] the son's offspring.

children.text: KAZ07.17.29/ sama.phalayoḥ śakta.prajananato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the offspring are equal — the distinction is based on the ability to produce [more] children.

children.text: KAZ07.17.30/ śakta.prajananayor apy upasthita.prajananato viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even when both are capable of producing children — the distinction is based on one who has a child imminent.

children.text: KAZ07.17.31/ śaktimaty eka.putre tu lupta.putra.utpattir ātmānam ādadhyāt, na ca^eka.putram iti //
children.translated_text: But when one capable [of producing children] has an only son, [the king] whose line of offspring has been cut should offer himself, but not his only son.

children.text: KAZ07.17.32/ abhyuccīyamānaḥ samādhi.mokṣaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: When being overwhelmed, he should arrange his release from the reconciliation.

children.text: KAZ07.17.33/ kumāra.āsannāḥ sattriṇaḥ kāru.śilpi.vyañjanāḥ karmāṇi kurvāṇāḥ suruṅgayā rātrāv upakhānayitvā kumāram apahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Secret agents near the prince, disguised as artisans and craftsmen, while performing their work, should dig a tunnel at night and abduct the prince.

children.text: KAZ07.17.34/ naṭanartaka.gāyana.vādaka.vāg.jīvana.kuśīlava.plavaka.saubhikā vā pūrva.praṇihitāḥ param upatiṣṭheran //
children.translated_text: Or actors, dancers, singers, musicians, elocutionists, entertainers, acrobats, and magicians — previously planted — should attend upon the enemy.

children.text: KAZ07.17.35/ te kumāraṃ paraṃ.parayā^upatiṣṭheran //
children.translated_text: They should attend upon the prince with utmost care.

children.text: KAZ07.17.36/ teṣām aniyata.kāla.praveśa.sthāna.nirgamanāni sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should establish for them unrestricted times of entry, residence, and departure.

children.text: KAZ07.17.37/ tatas tad.vyañjano vā rātrau pratiṣṭheta //
children.translated_text: Then, one disguised as one of them should escape at night.

children.text: KAZ07.17.38/ tena rūpa.ājīvā bhāryā.vyañjanāś ca vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, [escapes by] those who live by their appearance and those disguised as wives are explained.

children.text: KAZ07.17.39/ teṣāṃ vā tūrya.bhāṇḍa.phelāṃ gṛhītvā nirgacchet //
children.translated_text: Or he should escape having taken [a place among] the hollow instruments, vessels, and containers of those [performers].

children.text: KAZ07.17.40/ sūda.ārālika.snāpaka.saṃvāhaka.āstaraka.kalpaka.prasādhaka.udaka.paricārakair vā dravya.vastra.bhāṇḍa.phelā.śayana.āsana.sambhogair nirhriyeta //
children.translated_text: Or he should be carried out by cooks, kitchen servants, bath attendants, masseurs, bed-makers, barbers, dressers, and water attendants — among the materials, clothes, vessels, containers, bedding, seats, and furnishings.

children.text: KAZ07.17.41/ paricārakac.chadmanā vā kiṃcid arūpa.velāyām ādāya nirgacchet, suruṅgā.mukhena vā niśā.upahāreṇa //
children.translated_text: Or, in the disguise of an attendant, he should take something at an unusual hour and leave; or through a tunnel opening, with a nighttime offering [as pretext].

children.text: KAZ07.17.42/ toya.āśaye vā vāruṇaṃ yogam ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, at a water reservoir, he should employ the aquatic method (<s>vāruṇayoga</s>).

children.text: KAZ07.17.43/ vaidehaka.vyañjanā vā pakva.anna.phala.vyavahāreṇa^ārakṣiṣu rasam upacārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as traders, through dealings in cooked food and fruits, should administer poison to the guards.

children.text: KAZ07.17.44/ daivata.upahāra.śrāddha.prahavaṇa.nimittam ārakṣiṣu madana.yoga.yuktam anna.pānaṃ rasaṃ vā prayujya^apagacchet, ārakṣaka.protsāhanena vā //
children.translated_text: Under the pretext of offerings to deities, funeral feasts, or banquets, having administered food, drink, or seasoning mixed with a narcotic preparation (<s>madanayoga</s>) to the guards, he should escape — or through the incitement of the guards [themselves].

children.text: KAZ07.17.45/ nāgaraka.kuśīlava.cikitsaka.āpūpika.vyañjanā vā rātrau samṛddha.gṛhāṇy ādīpayeyuḥ ārakṣiṇāṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as townsmen, entertainers, physicians, or pastry-makers should set fire to prosperous houses at night — or to the guards' [quarters].

children.text: KAZ07.17.46/ vaidehaka.vyañjanā vā paṇya.saṃsthām ādīpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as traders should set fire to the marketplace.

children.text: KAZ07.17.47/ anyad vā śarīraṃ nikṣipya sva.gṛham ādīpayed anupāta.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having placed another body [as a decoy] and set fire to his own quarters, he should [escape] out of fear of pursuit.

children.text: KAZ07.17.48/ tataḥ saṃdhic.cheda.khāta.suruṅgābhir apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Then he should escape through breaches in walls, ditches, or tunnels.

children.text: KAZ07.17.49/ kāca.kumbha.bhāṇḍa.bhāra.vyañjano vā rātrau pratiṣṭheta //
children.translated_text: Or, disguised as a porter of glass, pots, vessels, and bundles, he should depart at night.

children.text: KAZ07.17.50/ muṇḍa.jaṭilānāṃ pravāsanāny anupraviṣṭo vā rātrau tad.vyañjanaḥ pratiṣṭheta, virūpa.vyādhi.karaṇa.araṇya.carac.chadmanām anyatamena vā //KAZ07.17.51/ preta.vyañjano vā gūḍhair nirhriyeta //
children.translated_text:
Or, having entered among the departing groups of shaven [monks] and matted-hair [ascetics], disguised as one of them, he should depart at night — or in any one of the disguises of a deformed person, a sick person, or a forest-dweller.
Or, disguised as a corpse, he should be carried out by hidden [agents].

children.text: KAZ07.17.52/ pretaṃ vā strī.veṣeṇa^anugacchet //
children.translated_text: Or he should follow a funeral procession in the guise of a woman.

children.text: KAZ07.17.53/ vana.cara.vyañjanāś ca^enam anyato yāntam anyato^apadiśeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And forest-dweller agents should direct those pursuing him in one direction while he goes in another.

children.text: KAZ07.17.54/ tato^anyato gacchet //
children.translated_text: Then he should go in yet another direction.

children.text: KAZ07.17.55/ cakra.carāṇāṃ vā śakaṭa.vāṭair apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Or he should escape in the wagon trains of itinerant traders.

children.text: KAZ07.17.56/ āsanne ca^anupāte sattraṃ vā gṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: And when pursuit is close, he should take up a sacrificial session [as refuge].

children.text: KAZ07.17.57/ sattra.abhāve hiraṇyaṃ rasa.viddhaṃ vā bhakṣya.jātam ubhayataḥ.panthānam utsṛjet //
children.translated_text: In the absence of a sacrificial session, he should scatter gold or mercury-treated edible substances on both sides of the road.

children.text: KAZ07.17.58/ tato^anyato^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Then he should escape in another direction.

children.text: KAZ07.17.59/ gṛhīto vā sāma.ādibhir anupātam atisaṃdadhyāt, rasa.viddhena vā pathy.adanena //
children.translated_text: Or, if caught, he should outmaneuver his pursuers through conciliation and other means, or with mercury-treated food along the path.

children.text: KAZ07.17.60/ vāruṇa.yoga.agni.dāheṣu vā śarīram anyad ādhāya śatrum abhiyuñjīta "putro me tvayā hataḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, in [the confusion of] water-magic, fire, and arson, having placed another body [as evidence], he should confront the enemy [saying]: 'My son has been killed by you.'

children.text: KAZ07.17.61a/ upāttac.channa.śastro vā rātrau vikramya rakṣiṣu //
children.translated_text: Or, having taken up concealed weapons, attacking the guards by force at night,

children.text: KAZ07.17.61b/ śīghra.pātair apasared gūḍha.praṇihitaiḥ saha //E
children.translated_text: he should escape swiftly with his secretly deployed [agents].

children.text:
(madhyama.caritam - udāsīna.caritam - maṇḍala.caritam)
KAZ07.18.01/ madhyamasya^ātmā tṛtīyā pañcamī ca prakṛtī prakṛtayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Conduct of the middle king; Conduct of the neutral king; Conduct in the circle [of kings])
The constituent elements of the middle king are: himself, the third, and the fifth [positions]; [these are] his natural [allies].

children.text: KAZ07.18.02/ dvitīyā caturthī ṣaṣṭhī ca vikṛtayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The second, fourth, and sixth are his adversaries.

children.text: KAZ07.18.03/ tac ced ubhayaṃ madhyamo^anugṛhṇīyāt, vijigīṣur madhyama.anulomaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: If the middle king should support both [the conqueror and the enemy], the conqueror should be favorable to the middle king.

children.text: KAZ07.18.04/ na ced anugṛhṇīyāt, prakṛty.anulomaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: If he does not support [both], [the conqueror] should be favorable to the [middle king's] constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ07.18.05/ madyamaś ced vijigīṣor mitraṃ mitra.bhāvi lipseta, mitrasya^ātmanaś ca mitrāṇy utthāpya madhyamāc ca mitrāṇi bhedayitvā mitraṃ trāyeta //
children.translated_text: If the middle king seeks [to take] the conqueror's ally or one becoming an ally, [the conqueror] should rally the allies of his ally and of himself, and having broken away the allies from the middle king, should protect his ally.

children.text: KAZ07.18.06/ maṇḍalaṃ vā protsāhayet "atipravṛddho^ayaṃ madhyamaḥ sarveṣāṃ no vināśāya^abhyutthitaḥ, sambhūya^asya yātrāṃ vihanāma" iti //
children.translated_text: Or he should rouse the circle [of kings]: 'This middle king has grown excessively and has risen for the destruction of us all; let us unite and obstruct his campaign.'

children.text: KAZ07.18.07/ tac cen maṇḍalam anugṛhṇīyāt, madhyama.avagraheṇa^ātmānam upabṛṃhayet //
children.translated_text: If the circle supports [this plan], he should strengthen himself by [contributing to] the restraint of the middle king.

children.text: KAZ07.18.08/ na ced anugṛhṇīyāt, kośa.daṇḍābhyāṃ mitram anugṛhya ye madhyama.dveṣiṇo rājānaḥ paraspara.anugṛhītā vā bahavas tiṣṭheyuḥ, eka.siddhau vā bahavaḥ sidhyeyuḥ, parasparād vā śaṅkitā na^uttiṣṭheran, teṣāṃ pradhānam ekam āsannaṃ vā sāma.dānābhyāṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: If [the circle] does not support [it], having aided his ally with treasury and army, he should obtain — by conciliation and gifts — the chief among those kings who are hostile to the middle king, or who are mutually supportive and numerous, or those through whom the success of one [entails] the success of many, or those who are mutually suspicious and would not rise [against him].

children.text: KAZ07.18.09/ dvi.guṇo dvitīyaṃ tri.gunas tṛtīyam //
children.translated_text: With double [effort] the second, with triple the third.

children.text: KAZ07.18.10/ evam abhyuccito madhyamam avagṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Thus having grown, he should restrain the middle king.

children.text: KAZ07.18.11/ deśa.kāla.atipattau vā saṃdhāya madhyamena mitrasya sācivyaṃ kuryāt, dūṣyeṣu vā karma.saṃdhim //
children.translated_text: Or, when place and time have passed, having made a treaty with the middle king, he should assist his ally; or he should make an operational alliance with the disloyal [elements of the middle king].

children.text: KAZ07.18.12/ karśanīyaṃ vā^asya mitraṃ madhyamo lipseta, pratistambhayed enaṃ "ahaṃ tvā trāyeya" iti ā karśanāt //
children.translated_text: Or, the middle king may seek an ally of his who should be worn down — [in that case, the conqueror] should obstruct him [saying] 'I shall protect you,' until [the ally has been] worn down.

children.text: KAZ07.18.13/ karśitam enaṃ trāyeta //
children.translated_text: Having been worn down, he should then rescue him.

children.text: KAZ07.18.14/ ucchedanīyaṃ vā^asya mitraṃ madhyamo lipseta, karśitam enaṃ trāyeta madhyama.vṛddhi.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: Or, the middle king may seek an ally of his who should be exterminated — [in that case, the conqueror] should rescue the ally after he has been worn down, out of fear of the middle king's growth.

children.text: KAZ07.18.15/ ucchinnaṃ vā bhūmy.anugraheṇa haste kuryād anyatra^apasāra.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: Or, when [the ally] has been exterminated, he should get him into his hands through a grant of territory — except when there is fear of [the ally's] defection.

children.text: KAZ07.18.16/ karśanīya.ucchedanīyayoś cen mitrāṇi madhyamasya sācivya.karāṇi syuḥ, puruṣa.antareṇa saṃdhīyeta //
children.translated_text: If the allies of those to be worn down or exterminated should assist the middle king, [the conqueror] should make a treaty through an intermediary.

children.text: KAZ07.18.17/ vijigīṣor vā tayor mitrāṇy avagraha.samarthāni syuḥ, saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, if the allies of those two are capable of restraining [them] on behalf of the conqueror, he should enter into a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.18.18/ amitraṃ vā^asya madhyamo lipseta, saṃdhim upeyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, if the middle king seeks his enemy — he should enter into a treaty.

children.text: KAZ07.18.19/ evaṃ sva.arthaś ca kṛto bhavati madhyamasya priyaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Thus his own objective is also accomplished, and it pleases the middle king.

children.text: KAZ07.18.20/ madhyamaś cet sva.mitraṃ mitra.bhāvi lipseta, puruṣa.antareṇa saṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: If the middle king seeks his own ally or one becoming an ally, [the conqueror] should make a treaty through an intermediary.

children.text: KAZ07.18.21/ sa.apekṣaṃ vā "na^arhasi mitram ucchettum" iti vārayet //
children.translated_text: Or, with due regard, he should prevent [it saying]: 'You should not destroy my ally.'

children.text: KAZ07.18.22/ upekṣeta vā "maṇḍalam asya kupyatu sva.pakṣa.vadhāt" iti //
children.translated_text: Or he should disregard [it, thinking]: 'Let the circle become angry at him for destroying one of its own party.'

children.text: KAZ07.18.23/ amitram ātmano vā madhyamo lipseta, kośa.daṇḍābhyām enam adṛśyamāno^anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, if the middle king seeks his own enemy, [the conqueror] should secretly support him with treasury and army without being seen.

children.text: KAZ07.18.24/ udāsīnaṃ vā madhyamo lipseta, asmai sāhāyyaṃ dadyād "udāsīnād bhidyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, if the middle king seeks the neutral king, he should give assistance to [the neutral king thinking]: 'Let him break away from the middle king.'

children.text: KAZ07.18.25/ madhyama.udāsīnayor yo maṇḍalasya^abhipretas tam āśrayeta //
children.translated_text: Between the middle and the neutral king, whichever one is preferred by the circle [of kings] — [the conqueror] should take refuge with him.

children.text: KAZ07.18.26/ madhyama.caritena^udāsīna.caritaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: The conduct toward the neutral king is explained by the conduct toward the middle king.

children.text: KAZ07.18.27/ udāsīnaś cen madhyamaṃ lipseta, yataḥ śatrum atisaṃdadhyān mitrasya^upakāraṃ kuryād udāsīnaṃ vā daṇḍa.upakāriṇaṃ labheta tataḥ pariṇameta //
children.translated_text: If the neutral king seeks the middle king, [the conqueror] should align himself with whichever [course] would: outmaneuver the enemy, render service to an ally, or gain the neutral king as one who assists with armed force.

children.text: KAZ07.18.28/ evam upabṛhya^ātmānam ari.prakṛtiṃ karśayen mitra.prakṛtiṃ ca^upagṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Thus, having strengthened himself, he should wear down the enemy's constituent elements and take up the ally's constituent elements.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.29a/ saty apy amitra.bhāve tasya^anātmavān nitya.apakārī śatruḥ śatru.saṃhitaḥ pārṣṇi.grāho vā vyasanī yātavyo vyasane vā netur abhiyoktā ity ari.bhāvinaḥ, eka.artha.abhiprayātaḥ pṛthag.artha.abhiprayātaḥ sambhūya.yātrikaḥ saṃhita.prayāṇikaḥ sva.artha.abhiprayātaḥ sāmutthāyikaḥ kośa.daṇḍayor anyatarasya kretā vikretā vā dvaidhī.bhāvika iti mitra.bhāvinaḥ,
- //
children.translated_text:
Even when enmity exists, [the following are] those who tend toward enmity: one who is without self-control, who constantly causes harm, a [declared] enemy, one allied with the enemy, a rear-striker, one beset with calamity who is one to be marched against, or one who attacks when the leader is in calamity. Those who tend toward alliance: one who has set out for the same objective, one who has set out for a different objective, a joint campaigner, an allied marcher, one who has set out for his own objective, a co-riser, one who buys or sells either the treasury or the army, one of the dual policy.
Those who tend to become feudatory vassals:

children.text: KAZ07.18.29b/ sāmanto balavataḥ pratighāto^antardhiḥ prativeśo vā balavataḥ pārṣṇi.grāho vā svayam upanataḥ pratāpa.upanato vā daṇḍa.upanata iti bhṛtya.bhāvinaḥ sāmantāḥ //
children.translated_text: a feudatory [who provides] a check against a powerful [king], a buffer, or a neighbor of a powerful [king]; or a rear-striker [who has come] of his own accord, or one brought by [displays of] power, or one brought by force.

children.text: KAZ07.18.30/ tair bhūmy.eka.antarā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By these, those one territory removed are explained.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.31ab/ teṣāṃ śatru.virodhe yan mitram eka.arthatāṃ vrajet /
KAZ07.18.31cd/ śaktyā tad.anugṛhṇīyād viṣaheta yayā param //
children.translated_text:
Among them, an ally who, in opposing the enemy, would unite for a common cause —
him one should support with such strength as would enable one to withstand the enemy.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.32ab/ prasādhya śatruṃ yan mitraṃ vṛddhaṃ gacched avaśyatām /
KAZ07.18.32cd/ sāmanta.eka.antarābhyāṃ tat.prakṛtibhyāṃ virodhayet //
children.translated_text:
An ally who, having vanquished the enemy, would grow [powerful and become] uncontrollable —
him one should set in conflict with the feudatories and their constituent elements on both sides.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.33ab/ tat.kulīna.aparuddhābhyāṃ bhūmiṃ vā tasya hārayet /
KAZ07.18.33cd/ yathā vā^anugraha.apekṣaṃ vaśyaṃ tiṣṭhet tathā caret //
children.translated_text:
Or one should have his territory taken away through members of his own family or those excluded [from succession];
or one should conduct affairs in such a way that [the ally] remains dependent, looking for continued support.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.34ab/ na^upakuryād amitraṃ vā gacched yad atikarśitam /
KAZ07.18.34cd/ tad ahīnam avṛddhaṃ ca sthāpayen mitram arthavit //
children.translated_text:
One should not assist, or should go to, an enemy that has been excessively weakened;
but one should keep it neither too diminished nor too grown — this is the policy of one who knows statecraft.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.35ab/ artha.yuktyā calaṃ mitraṃ saṃdhiṃ yad upagacchati /
KAZ07.18.35cd/ tasya^apagamane hetuṃ vihanyān na caled yathā //
children.translated_text:
A fickle ally that enters into a treaty through [mere] material inducement —
one should destroy the cause of its departure, so that it does not waver.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.36ab/ ari.sādhāraṇaṃ yad vā tiṣṭhet tad aritaḥ śaṭham /
KAZ07.18.36cd/ bhedayed bhinnam ucchindyāt tataḥ śatrum anantaram //
children.translated_text:
An [ally] that is shared with the enemy — towards it, one should act deceitfully from the enemy's side;
one should break it away, and once broken, destroy the enemy next.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.37ab/ udāsīnaṃ ca yat tiṣṭhet sāmantais tad virodhayet /
KAZ07.18.37cd/ tato vigraha.saṃtaptam upakāre niveśayet //
children.translated_text:
An [ally] that remains neutral — one should set it at odds with its neighbors;
then, exhausted by hostility, employ it in one's own service.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.38ab/ amitraṃ vijigīṣuṃ ca yat saṃcarati durbalam /
KAZ07.18.38cd/ tad balena^anugṛhṇīyād yathā syān na parān.mukham //
children.translated_text:
An [ally] that is weak and associates with the enemy and the aspiring conqueror —
one should support it with force, so that it does not turn away.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.39ab/ apanīya tato^anyasyāṃ bhūmau vā samniveśayet /
KAZ07.18.39cd/ niveśya pūrvaṃ tatra^anyad daṇḍa.anugraha.hetunā //
children.translated_text:
Or, having removed [it from there], one should settle it in another territory,
having first settled another [in its place] through the rod of force and conciliation.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.40ab/ apakuryāt samarthaṃ vā na^upakuryād yad āpadi /
KAZ07.18.40cd/ ucchindyād eva tan.mitraṃ viśvasya^aṅkam upasthitam //
children.translated_text:
An [ally] that is capable of causing harm but does not assist in calamity —
one should destroy that ally who has come into one's lap trusting [in friendship].

children.text:
KAZ07.18.41ab/ mitra.vyasanato vā^arir uttiṣṭhed yo^anavagrahaḥ /
KAZ07.18.41cd/ mitreṇa^eva bhavet sādhyaś chādita.vyasanena saḥ //
children.translated_text:
Or, an enemy who arises from an ally's calamity and is unrestrained —
should be dealt with by that very ally whose calamity has been concealed.

children.text:
KAZ07.18.41ab/ amitra.vyasanān mitram utthitaṃ yad virajyati /
KAZ07.18.41cd/ ari.vyasana.siddhyā tat.śatruṇā^eva prasidhyati //
children.translated_text:
An ally that, risen from the enemy's calamity, becomes estranged —
that ally is to be subdued by the enemy's own enemy through the success [gained from] the enemy's calamity.

children.text: KAZ07.18.42ab/ vṛddhiṃ kṣayaṃ ca sthānaṃ ca karśana.ucchedanaṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: Growth, decline, stability, attrition, and destruction —

children.text:
KAZ07.18.42cd/ sarva.upāyān samādadhyād etān yaś ca^artha.śāstravit /
KAZ07.18.43ab/ evam anyonya.saṃcāraṃ ṣāḍguṇyaṃ yo^anupaśyati //
children.translated_text:
all these expedients should be employed by one who knows statecraft;
and one who perceives the mutual interplay of the sixfold policy in this manner —

children.text: KAZ07.18.43cd/ sa buddhi.nigalair baddhair iṣṭaṃ krīḍati pārthivaiḥ //E
children.translated_text: he plays at will with kings bound by the fetters of intellect.

children.text:
(prakṛti.vyasana.vargah)
KAZ08.1.01/ vyasana.yaugapadye saukaryato yātavyaṃ rakṣitavyaṃ vā^iti vyasana.cintā //
children.translated_text:
(Category of calamities of the constituent elements)
When calamities occur simultaneously, the deliberation on calamities [determines] which one should be attacked or defended against, based on ease [of dealing with it].

children.text: KAZ08.1.02/ daivaṃ mānuṣaṃ vā prakṛti.vyasanam anaya.apanayābhyāṃ sambhavati //
children.translated_text: A calamity of the constituent elements — whether natural or man-made — arises from misfortune or misgovernment.

children.text: KAZ08.1.03/ guṇa.prātilomyam abhāvaḥ pradoṣaḥ prasaṅgaḥ pīḍā vā vyasanam //
children.translated_text: A calamity is: the reversal of qualities, their absence, corruption, involvement [in vice], or oppression.

children.text: KAZ08.1.04/ vyasyaty enaṃ śreyasa iti vyasanam //
children.translated_text: It is called a calamity (<s>vyasana</s>) because it causes one to fall from prosperity.

children.text: KAZ08.1.05/ "svāmy.amātya.jana.pada.durga.kośa.daṇḍa.mitra.vyasanānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ garīyaḥ" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Among calamities of the king, ministers, countryside, fortification, treasury, army, and ally — each preceding one is more serious" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.1.06/ na^iti bharadvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.07/ "svāmy.amātya.vyasanayor amātya.vyasanaṃ garīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the king and the ministers — the ministers' calamity is more serious.

children.text: KAZ08.1.08/ mantro mantra.phala.avāptiḥ karma.anuṣṭhānam āya.vyaya.karma daṇḍa.praṇayanam amitra.aṭavī.pratiṣedho rājya.rakṣaṇaṃ vyasana.pratīkāraḥ kumāra.rakṣaṇam abhiṣekaś ca kumārāṇām āyattam amātyeṣu //
children.translated_text: Counsel, the attainment of the fruits of counsel, the execution of undertakings, the business of income and expenditure, the administration of punishment, the suppression of enemies and forest-chiefs, the protection of the kingdom, the remedy for calamities, the protection of princes, and the consecration of princes — all depend on the ministers.

children.text: KAZ08.1.09/ teṣām abhāve tad.abhāvaḥ, chinna.pakṣasya^iva rājñaś ceṣṭā.nāśaś ca //
children.translated_text: In their absence, all these cease; and the king, like one with clipped wings, loses the capacity for action.

children.text: KAZ08.1.10/ vyasaneṣu ca^āsannaḥ para.upajāpaḥ //
children.translated_text: And in [times of] calamity, the [danger of] subversion by the enemy is near at hand.

children.text: KAZ08.1.11/ vaiguṇye ca prāṇa.ābādhaḥ prāṇa.antika.caratvād rājñaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And in [the ministers'] deficiency, there is danger to life, because the king lives in close proximity [to them]" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.12/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.13/ mantri.purohita.ādi.bhṛtya.vargam adhyakṣa.pracāraṃ puruṣa.dravya.prakṛti.vyasana.pratīkāram edhanaṃ ca rājā^eva karoti //
children.translated_text: "The king himself appoints the corps of servants headed by the counselors and the chaplain, [establishes] the operations of the superintendents, [arranges] the remedy for calamities of persons and material constituent elements, and [provides for] their augmentation.

children.text: KAZ08.1.14/ vyasaniṣu vā^amātyeṣv anyān avyasaninaḥ karoti //
children.translated_text: Or, when ministers are afflicted by calamity, he appoints other, unafflicted ones.

children.text: KAZ08.1.15/ pūjya.pūjane dūṣya.avagrahe ca nitya.yuktas tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: And he stands constantly engaged in honoring those who are to be honored and in restraining those who are to be restrained.

children.text: KAZ08.1.16/ svāmī ca sampannaḥ sva.sampadbhiḥ prakṛtīḥ sampādayati //
children.translated_text: Moreover, a king who is well-endowed, through his own excellences, brings the constituent elements to excellence.

children.text: KAZ08.1.17/ sa yat.śīlas tat.śīlāḥ prakṛtayo bhavanti, utthāne pramāde ca tad.āyattatvāt //
children.translated_text: The constituent elements become of the same character as the king — whether in enterprise or in negligence — because they depend on him.

children.text: KAZ08.1.18/ tat.kūṭa.sthānīyo hi svāmī^iti //
children.translated_text: For the king is the foundation of all" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.19/ "amātya.jana.pada.vyasanayor jana.pada.vyasanaṃ garīyaḥ" iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the ministers and the countryside — the countryside's calamity is more serious" — says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.20/ "kośo daṇḍaḥ kupyaṃ viṣṭir vāhanaṃ nicayāś ca jana.padād uttiṣṭhante //
children.translated_text: "The treasury, the army, raw materials, labor, transport, and provisions — all arise from the countryside.

children.text: KAZ08.1.21/ teṣām abhāvo jana.pada.abhāve, svāmy.amātyayoś ca^anantaraḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: In the absence of the countryside, all these cease; and it is next [in importance] to the king and the ministers" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.22/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.23/ amātya.mūlāḥ sarva.ārambhāḥ - jana.padasya karma.siddhayaḥ svataḥ parataś ca yoga.kṣema.sādhanaṃ vyasana.pratīkāraḥ śūnya.niveśa.upacayau daṇḍa.kara.anugrahaś ca^iti //
children.translated_text: "All undertakings are rooted in the ministers — the accomplishment of the countryside's works both by itself and from external [sources], the securing of welfare and livelihood, the remedy for calamities, the settling and development of wastelands, and the administration of punishment, taxation, and concessions."

children.text: KAZ08.1.24/ "jana.pada.durga.vyasanayor durga.vyasanam" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the countryside and the fortification — the fortification's [calamity is more serious]" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.25/ "durge hi kośa.daṇḍa.utpattir āpadi sthānaṃ ca jana.padasya //
children.translated_text: "For in a fortification arise the treasury and the army; and it is the place of refuge for the countryside in calamity.

children.text: KAZ08.1.26/ śaktimattarāś ca paurā jānapadebhyo nityāś ca^āpadi sahāyā rājñaḥ //
children.translated_text: And the city-dwellers are more powerful than the country-folk, and are the king's constant helpers in calamity.

children.text: KAZ08.1.27/ jānapadās tv amitra.sādhāraṇāḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: The country-folk, however, are shared with the enemy" — they say.

children.text: KAZ08.1.28/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.29/ jana.pada.mūlā durga.kośa.daṇḍa.setu.vārttā.ārambhāḥ //
children.translated_text: "The countryside is the root of fortifications, the treasury, the army, embankments, and economic enterprises.

children.text: KAZ08.1.30/ śauryaṃ sthairyaṃ dākṣyaṃ bāhulyaṃ ca jānapadeṣu //
children.translated_text: Valor, steadfastness, skill, and abundance [of manpower] are [found] among the country-folk.

children.text: KAZ08.1.31/ parvata.antar.dvīpāś ca durgā na^adhyuṣyante jana.pada.abhāvāt //
children.translated_text: And mountain and island fortifications are uninhabitable in the absence of country-folk.

children.text: KAZ08.1.32/ karṣaka.prāye tu durga.vyasanam, āyudhīya.prāye tu jana.pade jana.pada.vyasanam iti //
children.translated_text: But when the countryside is predominantly agricultural, the fortification's calamity [is more serious]; when the countryside is predominantly military, the countryside's calamity [is more serious]."

children.text: KAZ08.1.33/ "durga.kośa.vyasanayoḥ kośa.vyasanam" iti piśunaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the fortification and the treasury — the treasury's [calamity is more serious]" — says <s>Piśuna</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.34/ "kośa.mūlo hi durga.saṃskāro durga.rakṣaṇaṃ jana.pada.mitra.amitra.nigraho deśa.antaritānām utsāhanaṃ daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāraś ca //
children.translated_text: "For the treasury is the root of the repair of fortifications, the defense of fortifications, the control of the countryside and allies, the suppression of enemies, the encouragement of those in remote regions, and the operations of the army and its forces.

children.text: KAZ08.1.35/ durgaḥ kośād upajāpyaḥ pareṣām //
children.translated_text: The fortification, [more easily than the treasury], can be subverted by the enemy's wealth.

children.text: KAZ08.1.36/ kośam ādāya ca vyasane śakyam apayātum, na durgam" iti //
children.translated_text: And it is possible to flee with the treasury in a calamity, but not with the fortification" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.37/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.38/ durga.arpaṇaḥ kośo daṇḍas tūṣṇīṃ.yuddhaṃ sva.pakṣa.nigraho daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāra āsāra.pratigrahaḥ para.cakra.aṭavī.pratiṣedhaś ca //
children.translated_text: "The fortification is the shelter of the treasury; and the army fights a silent war [from within it]; the control of one's own faction, the operations of the army and its forces, the reception of reinforcements, and the repelling of enemy forces and forest-chiefs [all depend on the fortification].

children.text: KAZ08.1.39/ durga.abhāve ca kośaḥ pareṣām //
children.translated_text: And in the absence of fortification, the treasury [belongs] to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ08.1.40/ dṛśyate hi durgavatām anucchittir iti //
children.translated_text: For it is seen that those who possess fortifications are not destroyed" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.41/ "kośa.daṇḍavyasanayor daṇḍa.vyasanam" iti kauṇapadantaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the treasury and the army — the army's [calamity is more serious]" — says <s>Kauṇapadanta</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.42/ "daṇḍa.mūlo hi mitra.amitra.nigrahaḥ para.daṇḍa.utsāhanaṃ sva.daṇḍa.pratigrahaś ca //
children.translated_text: "For the army is the root of the suppression of friends and enemies, the encouragement of the enemy's army, the deployment of one's own army, [and the conduct of military operations].

children.text: KAZ08.1.43/ daṇḍa.abhāve ca dhruvaḥ kośa.vināśaḥ //
children.translated_text: And in the absence of an army, the destruction of the treasury is certain.

children.text: KAZ08.1.44/ kośa.abhāve ca śakyaḥ kupyena bhūmyā para.bhūmi.svayaṃ.grāheṇa vā daṇḍaḥ piṇḍayitum, daṇḍavatā ca kośaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the absence of the treasury, it is [still] possible to gather an army through raw materials, land, or the seizure of foreign territory; and with an army, [one can acquire] a treasury.

children.text: KAZ08.1.45/ svāminaś ca^āsanna.vṛttitvād amātya.sadharmā daṇḍaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And because the army lives in close proximity to the king, it shares the nature of the ministers" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.46/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.47/ kośa.mūlo hi daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: "For the army is rooted in the treasury.

children.text: KAZ08.1.48/ kośa.abhāve daṇḍaḥ paraṃ gacchati, svāminaṃ vā hanti //
children.translated_text: In the absence of the treasury, the army goes over to the enemy or kills the king himself.

children.text: KAZ08.1.49/ sarva.abhiyoga.karaś ca kośo dharma.kāma.hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: And the treasury, which accomplishes all objectives, is the means of <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.50/ deśa.kāla.kārya.vaśena tu kośa.daṇḍayor anyataraḥ pramāṇī.bhavati //
children.translated_text: But depending on the place, time, and task — either the treasury or the army may be the more decisive.

children.text: KAZ08.1.51/ lambha.pālano hi daṇḍaḥ kośasya, kośaḥ kośasya daṇḍasya ca bhavati //
children.translated_text: For the army serves to acquire and protect the treasury; the treasury serves [to maintain] both the treasury and the army.

children.text: KAZ08.1.52/ sarva.dravya.prayojakatvāt kośa.vyasanaṃ garīya iti //
children.translated_text: Because the treasury is the instrument of all material resources, the treasury's calamity is more serious" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.53/ "daṇḍa.mitra.vyasanayor mitra.vyasanam" iti vātavyādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between calamities of the army and the ally — the ally's [calamity is more serious]" — says <s>Vātavyādhi</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.54/ "mitram abhṛtaṃ vyavahitaṃ ca karma karoti, pārṣṇi.grāham āsāram amitram āṭavikaṃ ca pratikaroti, kośa.daṇḍa.bhūmibhiś ca^upakaroti vyasana.avasthā.yogam" iti //
children.translated_text: "For the ally performs tasks without wages and at a distance; he counteracts the rear-enemy, the reinforcing [ally of the enemy], the hostile [neighbor], and the forest-chief; and he assists with treasury, army, and land in times of calamity" — he says.

children.text: KAZ08.1.55/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.1.56/ daṇḍavato mitraṃ mitra.bhāve tiṣṭhati, amitro vā mitra.bhāve //
children.translated_text: "For one who has an army — the ally remains in the state of friendship; or the enemy [assumes] the state of friendship.

children.text: KAZ08.1.57/ daṇḍa.mitrayos tu sādhāraṇe kārye sārataḥ sva.yuddha.deśa.kāla.lābhād viśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: But between the army and the ally, in a joint enterprise — the distinction [in value] depends on the essential character [of each], one's own battle, place, time, and opportunity.

children.text: KAZ08.1.58/ śīghra.abhiyāne tv amitra.āṭavika.anabhyantara.kope ca na mitraṃ vidyate //
children.translated_text: In a swift attack, however, or in the revolt of the enemy, forest-chiefs, or internal [factions] — the ally is of no use.

children.text: KAZ08.1.59/ vyasana.yaugapadye para.vṛddhau ca mitram artha.yuktau tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text: When calamities are simultaneous and the enemy is growing — the ally remains [useful] in [matters of] material resources and policy."

children.text: KAZ08.1.60/ iti prakṛti.vyasana.sampradhāraṇam uktam //
children.translated_text: Thus the deliberation on calamities of the constituent elements has been stated.

children.text:
KAZ08.1.61ab/ prakṛty.avayavānāṃ tu vyasanasya viśeṣataḥ /
KAZ08.1.61cd/ bahu.bhāvo^anurāgo vā sāro vā kārya.sādhakaḥ //
