children.translated_text:
Of the subdivisions of the constituent elements, in particular calamities,
what is decisive is either their multitude, their loyalty, or their essential quality.

children.text:
KAZ08.1.62ab/ dvayos tu vyasane tulye viśeṣo guṇataḥ kṣayāt /
KAZ08.1.62cd/ śeṣa.prakṛti.sādguṇyaṃ yadi syān na^avidheyakam //
children.translated_text:
But when two calamities are equal, the distinction [is drawn] from quality and loss;
if the remaining constituent elements are of good quality, [the calamity] is not unmanageable.

children.text:
KAZ08.1.63ab/ śeṣa.prakṛti.nāśas tu yatra^eka.vyasanād bhavet /
KAZ08.1.63cd/ vyasanaṃ tad garīyaḥ syāt pradhānasya^itarasya vā //E
children.translated_text:
But where the destruction of the remaining constituent elements
results from a single calamity — that calamity is more serious, whether of the principal [element] or of the other.

children.text:
(rāja.rājyayor vyasana.cintā)
KAZ08.2.01/ rājā rājyam iti prakṛti.saṃkṣepaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Deliberation on calamities of the king and kingdom)
The king and the kingdom — this is the summary of the constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ08.2.02/ rājño^abhyantaro bāhyo vā kopa iti //
children.translated_text: The king's danger is internal or external.

children.text: KAZ08.2.03/ ahi.bhayād abhyantaraḥ kopo bāhya.kopāt pāpīyān, antar.amātya.kopaś ca^antaḥ.kopāt //
children.translated_text: Internal danger, like [the danger from] a snake, is worse than external danger; and the danger from a minister's revolt is worse than internal [popular] revolt.

children.text: KAZ08.2.04/ tasmāt kośa.daṇḍa.śaktim ātma.saṃsthāṃ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should establish the power of treasury and army firmly under one's own control.

children.text: KAZ08.2.05/ "dvairājya.vairājyayor dvairājyam anyonya.pakṣa.dveṣa.anurāgābhyāṃ paraspara.saṃgharṣeṇa vā vinaśyati, vairājyaṃ tu prakṛti.citta.grahaṇa.apekṣi yathā.sthitam anyair bhujyate" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Between dual kingship and absence of a king — dual kingship, [being worse,] perishes through mutual faction-hatred and -attachment, or through mutual friction; whereas the absence of a king, which depends on winning the hearts of the people, is simply enjoyed as it is by others" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.2.06/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.2.07/ pitā.putrayor bhrātror vā dvairājyaṃ tulya.yoga.kṣemam amātya.avagrahaṃ vartayati //
children.translated_text: "Dual kingship of father and son, or of brothers, ensures equal welfare and security and operates under the restraint of ministers.

children.text: KAZ08.2.08/ vairājyaṃ tu jīvataḥ parasya^ācchidya "na^etan mama" iti manyamānaḥ karśayati, apavāhayati, paṇyaṃ vā karoti, viraktaṃ vā parityajya^apagacchati^iti //
children.translated_text: But the absence of a king — when one seizes [the kingdom] of a living [predecessor] thinking 'this is not mine' — he exploits it, drives away [the people], or treats it as merchandise, or abandons the disaffected [kingdom] and departs."

children.text: KAZ08.2.09/ andhaś calita.śāstro vā rājā^iti "aśāstra.cakṣur andho yat.kiṃcana.kārī dṛḍha.abhiniveśī para.praṇeyo vā rājyam anyāyena^upahanti, calita.śāstras tu yatra śāstrāc calita.matir bhavati śakya.anunayo bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "A blind king or one who has deviated from the treatise — 'A king blind to the treatise, doing whatever he pleases, rigidly stubborn, or led by others, ruins the kingdom unjustly; but one who has deviated from the treatise, where his mind has [merely] strayed from the treatise, can be persuaded back' — say the teachers."

children.text: KAZ08.2.10/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.2.11/ andho rājā śakyate sahāya.sampadā yatra tatra vā paryavasthāpayitum //
children.translated_text: "A blind king can, through the excellence of his helpers, be restrained anywhere.

children.text: KAZ08.2.12/ calita.śāstras tu śāstrād anyathā.abhiniviṣṭa.buddhir anyāyena rājyam ātmānaṃ ca^upahanti^iti //
children.translated_text: But one who has deviated from the treatise, whose intellect is fixed on what is contrary to the treatise, ruins the kingdom and himself."

children.text: KAZ08.2.13/ vyādhito navo vā rājā^iti "vyādhito rājā rājya.upaghātam amātya.mūlaṃ prāṇa.ābādhaṃ vā rājya.mūlam avāpnoti, navas tu rājā sva.dharma.anugraha.parihāra.dāna.māna.karmabhiḥ prakṛti.rañjana.upakāraiś carati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "A diseased or a new king — 'A diseased king incurs either the ruin of the kingdom, which is rooted in the ministers, or danger to life, which is rooted in the kingdom; but a new king, through proper duty, concessions, exemptions, gifts, and honors, and through works that please and benefit the subjects, conducts himself [properly]' — say the teachers."

children.text: KAZ08.2.14/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so" — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.2.15/ vyādhito rājā yathā.pravṛttaṃ rāja.praṇidhim anuvartayati //
children.translated_text: "A diseased king continues the established system of royal governance [as it is]."

children.text: KAZ08.2.16/ navas tu rājā bala.āvarjitaṃ "mama^idaṃ rājyam" iti yathā.iṣṭam anavagrahaś carati //
children.translated_text: But a new king, having won over the army, acts as he pleases without restraint, [thinking] 'This kingdom is mine.'

children.text: KAZ08.2.17/ sāmutthāyikair avagṛhīto vā rājya.upaghātaṃ marṣayati //
children.translated_text: Or, restrained by the existing [officials], he tolerates damage to the kingdom.

children.text: KAZ08.2.18/ prakṛtiṣv arūḍhaḥ sukham ucchettuṃ bhavati^iti //
children.translated_text: Not being established among the subjects, he is easy to uproot.

children.text: KAZ08.2.19/ vyādhite viśeṣaḥ pāpa.rogya.pāpa.rogī ca //
children.translated_text: In the case of an ailing [king], the distinction is [between] an evil disease and an evil-diseased [king].

children.text: KAZ08.2.20/ nave^apy abhijāto^anabhijāta iti //
children.translated_text: Even among new [kings], [the distinction is] between one of noble birth and one not of noble birth.

children.text: KAZ08.2.21/ durbalo^abhijāto balavān anabhijāto rājā^iti "durbalasya^abhijātasya^upajāpaṃ daurbalya.apekṣāḥ prakṛtayaḥ kṛcchreṇa^upagacchanti, balavataś ca^anabhijātasya bala.apekṣāḥ sukhena" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: A weak king of noble birth versus a powerful king not of noble birth — 'For the subversion of a weak [king] of noble birth, the subjects approach with difficulty, being wary of his weakness; but for a powerful [king] not of noble birth, being attracted by his power, they approach easily' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.2.22/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.2.23/ durbalam abhijātaṃ prakṛtayaḥ svayam upanamanti, jātyam aiśvarya.prakṛtir anuvartata iti //
children.translated_text: The subjects voluntarily submit to a weak [king] of noble birth, for the nature of sovereignty follows lineage.

children.text: KAZ08.2.24/ balavataś ca^anabhijātasya^upajāpaṃ visaṃvādayanti, anurāge sārvaguṇyam iti //
children.translated_text: But they resist the subversion of a powerful [king] not of noble birth; in affection lies the sum of all virtues.

children.text: KAZ08.2.25/ prayāsa.vadhāt sasya.vadho muṣṭi.vadhāt pāpīyān, nirājīvatvād avṛṣṭir ativṛṣṭitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Destruction of crops is worse than destruction of effort, [and] destruction [by] drought is worse than destruction by excessive rain, because it leaves no livelihood.

children.text:
KAZ08.2.26ab/ dvayor dvayor vyasanayoḥ prakṛtīnāṃ bala.abalam /
KAZ08.2.26cd/ pāramparya.krameṇa^uktaṃ yāne sthāne ca kāraṇam //E
children.translated_text: The relative strength and weakness of the constituent elements in each pair of calamities has been stated in progressive order — [this determines] the reason for marching or staying.

children.text:
(puruṣa.vyasana.vargah)
KAZ08.3.01/ avidyā.vinayaḥ puruṣa.vyasana.hetuḥ //
children.translated_text:
(The category of personal vices)
Lack of training in learning is the cause of personal vices.

children.text: KAZ08.3.02/ avinīto hi vyasana.doṣān na paśyati //
children.translated_text: For an untrained person does not see the faults of vices.

children.text: KAZ08.3.03/ tān upadekṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: We shall describe them.

children.text: KAZ08.3.04/ kopajas tri.vargaḥ, kāmajaś catur.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: The triad born of anger, and the tetrad born of desire.

children.text: KAZ08.3.05/ tayoḥ kopo garīyān //
children.translated_text: Of the two, anger is the more serious.

children.text: KAZ08.3.06/ sarvatra hi kopaś carati //
children.translated_text: For anger operates everywhere.

children.text: KAZ08.3.07/ prāyaśaś ca kopa.vaśā rājānaḥ prakṛti.kopair hatāḥ śrūyante, kāma.vaśāḥ kṣaya.nimittam ari.vyādhibhir iti //
children.translated_text: And generally, kings overcome by anger are heard to have been destroyed by the fury of their subjects; those overcome by desire, [are destroyed] through wasting diseases brought on by enemies.

children.text: KAZ08.3.08/ na^iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.09/ "sat.puruṣa.ācāraḥ kopo vaira.yātanam avajñā.vadho bhīta.manuṣyatā ca //
children.translated_text: "Anger is the conduct of a noble person — it is the instrument of retribution against enemies, of contemptuous punishment, and of establishing fear among men.

children.text: KAZ08.3.10/ nityaś ca kopena sambandhaḥ pāpa.pratiṣedha.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: And there is a constant connection with anger for the purpose of preventing evil.

children.text: KAZ08.3.11/ kāmaḥ siddhi.lābhaḥ sāntvaṃ tyāga.śīlatā sampriya.bhāvaś ca //
children.translated_text: Desire is the reward of success, [a means of] conciliation, a disposition to generosity, the state of mutual affection.

children.text: KAZ08.3.12/ nityaś ca kāmena sambandhaḥ kṛta.karmaṇaḥ phala.upabhoga.arthaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And there is a constant connection with desire for the purpose of enjoying the fruits of accomplished work."

children.text: KAZ08.3.13/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.14/ dveṣyatā śatru.vedanaṃ duḥkha.āsaṅgaś ca kopaḥ //
children.translated_text: Anger is [the source of] being hated, enmity with enemies, and the attachment to misery.

children.text: KAZ08.3.15/ paribhavo dravya.nāśaḥ pāṭaccara.dyūtakāra.lubdhaka.gāyana.vādakaiś ca^anarthyaiḥ samyogaḥ kāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: Desire is [the source of] humiliation, loss of property, and association with the unworthy — cheats, gamblers, hunters, singers, and musicians.

children.text: KAZ08.3.16/ tayoḥ paribhavād dveṣyatā garīyasī //
children.translated_text: Of the two, being hated [from anger] is worse than humiliation [from desire].

children.text: KAZ08.3.17/ paribhūtaḥ svaiḥ paraiś ca^avagṛhyate, dveṣyaḥ samucchidyata iti //KAZ08.3.18/ dravya.nāśāt^śatru.vedanaṃ garīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who is humiliated is restrained by his own and by others; one who is hated is utterly destroyed. Loss of property is less [serious] than enmity with enemies.

children.text: KAZ08.3.19/ dravya.nāśaḥ kośa.ābādhakaḥ, śatru.vedanaṃ prāṇa.ābādhakam iti //
children.translated_text: Loss of property harms the treasury; enmity with enemies harms life itself.

children.text: KAZ08.3.20/ anarthya.samyogād duḥkha.samyogo garīyān //
children.translated_text: The attachment to misery is worse than association with the unworthy.

children.text: KAZ08.3.21/ anarthya.samyogo muhūrta.pratīkāro, dīrgha.kleśa.karo duḥkhānām āsaṅga iti //
children.translated_text: Association with the unworthy is remedied in a moment; attachment to miseries causes prolonged affliction.

children.text: KAZ08.3.22/ tasmāt kopo garīyān //
children.translated_text: Therefore anger is more serious.

children.text: KAZ08.3.23/ vāk.pāruṣyam artha.dūṣaṇaṃ daṇḍa.pāruṣyam iti //
children.translated_text: Harshness of speech, corruption of wealth, and harshness of punishment — [these are the subdivisions of anger].

children.text: KAZ08.3.24/ "vāk.pāruṣya.artha.dūṣaṇayor vāk.pāruṣyaṃ garīyaḥ" iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of harshness of speech and corruption of wealth, harshness of speech is more serious" — says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.25/ "paruṣa.mukto hi tejasvī tejasā pratyārohati //
children.translated_text: "For a spirited person, when abused, rises in fury.

children.text: KAZ08.3.26/ durukta.śalyaṃ hṛdi nikhātaṃ tejaḥ.saṃdīpanam indriya.upatāpi ca" iti //
children.translated_text: The thorn of harsh words, lodged in the heart, inflames one's spirit and torments the senses."

children.text: KAZ08.3.27/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.28/ artha.pūjā vāk.śalyam apahanti, vṛtti.vilopas tv artha.dūṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: Material honor removes the thorn of words, but corruption of wealth is the destruction of livelihood.

children.text: KAZ08.3.29/ adānam ādānaṃ vināśaḥ parityāgo vā^arthasya^ity artha.dūṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: Non-giving, [unjust] confiscation, destruction, or abandonment of wealth — this is corruption of wealth.

children.text: KAZ08.3.30/ "artha.dūṣaṇa.daṇḍa.pāruṣyayor artha.dūṣaṇaṃ garīyaḥ" iti pārāśarāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of corruption of wealth and harshness of punishment, corruption of wealth is more serious" — say the followers of <s>Parāśara</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.31/ "artha.mūlau dharma.kāmau //
children.translated_text: "<s>Dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> are rooted in <s>artha</s> (wealth).

children.text: KAZ08.3.32/ artha.pratibaddhaś ca loko vartate //
children.translated_text: And the world functions [only when] supported by wealth.

children.text: KAZ08.3.33/ tasya.upaghāto garīyān" iti //
children.translated_text: Its destruction is more serious."

children.text: KAZ08.3.34/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.35/ sumahatā^apy arthena na kaścana śarīra.vināśam icchet //
children.translated_text: For no one would wish the destruction of the body even for an immense amount of wealth.

children.text: KAZ08.3.36/ daṇḍa.pāruṣyāc ca tam eva doṣam anyebhyaḥ prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: And from harshness of punishment, one incurs that very fault from others [i.e., retaliation].

children.text: KAZ08.3.37/ iti kopajas tri.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the triad born of anger.

children.text: KAZ08.3.38/ kāmajas tu mṛgayā dyūtaṃ striyaḥ pānam iti catur.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: The tetrad born of desire is: hunting, gambling, women, and drinking.

children.text: KAZ08.3.39/ tasya "mṛgayā.dyūtayor mṛgayā garīyasī" iti piśunaḥ //
children.translated_text: Of these, 'of hunting and gambling, hunting is more serious' — says <s>Piśuna</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.40/ "stena.amitra.vyāla.dāva.praskhalana.bhaya.din.mohāḥ kṣut.pipāse ca prāṇa.ābādhas tasyām //
children.translated_text: "In hunting, there are dangers to life from thieves, enemies, wild animals, forest fires, stumbling, daytime [attacks], and confusion; and hunger and thirst.

children.text: KAZ08.3.41/ dyūte tu jitam eva^akṣa.viduṣā yathā jayat.sena.duryodhanābhyām" iti //
children.translated_text: But in gambling, one who is skilled at dice always wins — as with <s>Jayatsena</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s>."

children.text: KAZ08.3.42/ na^ity kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.43/ tayor apy anyatara.parājayo^asti^iti nala.yudhiṣṭhirābhyāṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: Even in that [gambling], defeat of one or the other is [possible] — as illustrated by <s>Nala</s> and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.44/ tad eva vijita.dravyam āmiṣaṃ vaira.anubandhaś ca //
children.translated_text: The very wealth won [by the other] becomes a lure and a source of prolonged enmity.

children.text: KAZ08.3.45/ sato^arthasya vipratipattir asataś ca^arjanam apratibhukta.nāśo mūtra.purīṣa.dhāraṇa.bubhukṣā.ādibhiś ca vyādhi.lābha iti dyūta.doṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: Loss of existing wealth and acquisition of non-existent [debts], destruction without enjoyment, and disease from holding urine, feces, and hunger — these are the faults of gambling.

children.text: KAZ08.3.46/ mṛgayāyāṃ tu vyāyāmaḥ śleṣma.pitta.medaḥ.sveda.nāśaś cale sthite ca kāye lakṣa.paricayaḥ kopa.bhaya.sthāneṣu ca mṛgāṇāṃ citta.jñānam anitya.yānaṃ ca^iti //
children.translated_text: But in hunting, there is physical exercise, destruction of phlegm, bile, fat, and sweat, skill in [hitting] targets both moving and stationary, knowledge of the temperament of wild animals in [situations of] anger and fear, and occasional travel.

children.text: KAZ08.3.47/ "dyūta.strī.vyasanayoḥ kaitava.vyasanam" iti kauṇapadantaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of the vices of gambling and women, the vice of gambling [is worse]" — says <s>Kauṇapadanta</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.48/ "sātatyena hi niśi pradīpe mātari ca mṛtāyāṃ dīvyaty eva kitavaḥ //
children.translated_text: "For, continuously, even at night by lamplight and even when his mother has died, the gambler goes on playing.

children.text: KAZ08.3.49/ kṛcchre ca pratipṛṣṭaḥ kupyati //
children.translated_text: And when questioned in difficulty, he grows angry.

children.text: KAZ08.3.50/ strī.vyasane tu snāna.pratikarma.bhojana.bhūmiṣu bhavaty eva dharma.artha.paripraśnaḥ //
children.translated_text: But in the vice of women, there are opportunities for inquiry into <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> during bathing, grooming, and dining.

children.text: KAZ08.3.51/ śakyā ca strī rājahite.niyoktum, upāṃśu.daṇḍena vyādhinā vā vyāvartayitum avasrāvayituṃ vā" iti //
children.translated_text: And a woman can be employed in the king's interest, or turned away through secret punishment or disease, or dismissed."

children.text: KAZ08.3.52/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.53/ sapratyādeyaṃ dyūtaṃ niṣpratyādeyaṃ strī.vyasanam //
children.translated_text: Gambling losses are recoverable; the vice of women is irrecoverable.

children.text: KAZ08.3.54/ adarśanaṃ kārya.nirvedaḥ kāla.atipātanād anartho dharma.lopaś ca tantra.daurbalyaṃ pāna.anubandhaś ca^iti //
children.translated_text: [The vice of women produces:] non-visibility [to the public], neglect of duties, harm through missing the [right] time, loss of <s>dharma</s>, weakness of governance, association with drinking.

children.text: KAZ08.3.55/ "strī.pāna.vyasanayoḥ strī.vyasanam" iti vātavyādhiḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of the vices of women and drinking, the vice of women [is worse]" — says <s>Vātavyādhi</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.56/ "strīṣu hi bāliśyam aneka.vidhaṃ niśānta.praṇidhau vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: "For there is many a kind of foolishness in [the case of] women, as has been explained in [the section on] surveillance of the inner quarters.

children.text: KAZ08.3.57/ pāne tu śabda.ādīnām indriya.arthānām upabhogaḥ prīti.dānaṃ parijana.pūjanaṃ karma.śrama.vadhaś ca" iti //
children.translated_text: But in drinking, there is enjoyment of the sense-objects — sound and the rest — [and] the giving of pleasure, the honoring of attendants, and the removal of work-fatigue."

children.text: KAZ08.3.58/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.3.59/ strī.vyasane bhavaty apatya.utpattir ātma.rakṣaṇaṃ ca^antar.dāreṣu, viparyayo vā bāhyeṣu, agamyeṣu sarva.ucchittiḥ //
children.translated_text: In the vice of women, there is [at least] the production of offspring and self-protection [when it is] among one's own wives; the opposite [results from] outside [women]; and from [relations with] those who are forbidden, total ruin.

children.text: KAZ08.3.60/ tad ubhayaṃ pāna.vyasane //
children.translated_text: Both [sets of evils] [result] from the vice of drinking.

children.text: KAZ08.3.61/ pāna.sampat - saṃjñā.nāśo^anunmattasya^unmattatvam apretasya pretatvaṃ kaupīna.darśanaṃ śruta.prajñā.prāṇa.vitta.mitra.hāniḥ sadbhir viyogo^anarthya.samyogas tantrī.gīta.naipuṇyeṣu ca^arthaghneṣu prasaṅga iti //
children.translated_text: The full effects of drinking: destruction of awareness for one who is not insane, [yet behaves as if] insane; [appearing] dead though not dead; exposure of [one's] private parts; loss of learning, wisdom, life, wealth, and friends; separation from the good; association with the unworthy; and engagement in the arts of strings and song — which are destructive of wealth.

children.text: KAZ08.3.62/ dyūta.madyayor dyūtam //
children.translated_text: Of gambling and drinking, gambling [is worse].

children.text: KAZ08.3.63/ ekeṣāṃ paṇa.nimitto jayaḥ parājayo vā prāṇiṣu niścetaneṣu vā pakṣa.dvaidhena prakṛti.kopaṃ karoti //
children.translated_text: For some, victory or defeat wagered on living or non-living [objects], by the division into two factions, produces fury among the subjects.

children.text: KAZ08.3.64/ viśeṣataś ca saṃghānāṃ saṃgha.dharmiṇāṃ ca rāja.kulānāṃ dyūta.nimitto bhedas tan.nimitto vināśa ity asat.pragrahaḥ pāpiṣṭhatamo vyasanānāṃ tantra.daurbalyād iti //
children.translated_text: And especially for republics and for royal families that follow republican principles, factional splits caused by gambling lead to destruction — [this is] the most wicked form of indulgence in vice, because of the weakness of the state [it causes].

children.text:
KAZ08.3.65ab/ asatāṃ pragrahaḥ kāmaḥ kopaś ca^avagrahaḥ satām /
KAZ08.3.65cd/ vyasanaṃ doṣa.bāhulyād atyantam ubhayaṃ matam //
children.translated_text: Desire is the indulgence of the wicked; anger is the restraint of the good. Both, through the abundance of their faults, are considered extreme vices.

children.text:
KAZ08.3.66ab/ tasmāt kopaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca vyasana.ārambham ātmavān /
KAZ08.3.66cd/ parityajen mūla.haraṃ vṛddha.sevī jita.indriyaḥ //E
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who is self-controlled, having conquered the senses, serving the elders, should abandon anger, desire, and the onset of vices — which destroy the very root.

children.text:
(pīḍana.vargah - stambha.vargah - kośa.sanga.vargah)
KAZ08.4.01/ daiva.pīḍanaṃ - agnir udakaṃ vyādhir durbhikṣaṃ maraka iti //
children.translated_text:
(The category of afflictions — the category of obstructions — the category of treasury losses)
Divine afflictions are: fire, flood, disease, famine, and pestilence.

children.text: KAZ08.4.02/ "agny.udakayor agni.pīḍanam apratikāryaṃ sarva.dāhi ca, śakya.apagamanaṃ tārya.ābādham udaka.pīḍanam" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of fire and flood, fire-affliction is irremediable and consumes everything; flood-affliction is escapable and [causes] harm [only] to what must be crossed" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.03/ na^it kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.04/ agnir grāmam ardha.grāmaṃ vā dahati, udaka.vegas tu grāma.śata.pravāhī^iti //
children.translated_text: Fire burns a village or half a village; but a flood's current carries away hundreds of villages.

children.text: KAZ08.4.05/ "vyādhi.durbhikṣayor vyādhiḥ preta.vyādhita.upasṛṣṭa.paricāraka.vyāyāma.uparodhena karmāṇy upahanti, durbhikṣaṃ punar akarma.upaghāti hiraṇya.paśu.kara.dāyi ca" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of disease and famine, disease impairs work through [the need to attend to] the dead, the sick, and the afflicted, and through obstruction of [attendants'] activities; but famine is not destructive of work and is productive of gold, cattle, and taxes" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.06/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.07/ eka.deśa.pīḍano vyādhiḥ śakya.pratīkāraś ca, sarva.deśa.pīḍanaṃ durbhikṣaṃ prāṇinām ajīvanāya^iti //
children.translated_text: Disease afflicts [only] one region and is remediable; famine afflicts all regions and leads to the destruction of living beings.

children.text: KAZ08.4.08/ tena marako vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, pestilence is explained [as worst].

children.text: KAZ08.4.09/ "kṣudraka.mukhya.kṣayayoḥ kṣudraka.kṣayaḥ karmaṇām ayoga.kṣemaṃ karoti, mukhya.kṣayaḥ karma.anuṣṭhāna.uparodha.dharmā" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of the destruction of the petty and the prominent — the destruction of the petty causes insecurity of work; the destruction of the prominent obstructs the execution of work" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.10/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.11/ śakyaḥ kṣudraka.kṣayaḥ pratisaṃdhātuṃ bāhulyāt kṣudrakāṇām, na mukhya.kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The destruction of the petty is remediable because of the abundance of petty [people]; not so the destruction of the prominent.

children.text: KAZ08.4.12/ sahasreṣu hi mukhyo bhavaty eko na vā sattva.prajñā.ādhikyāt tad.āśrayatvāt kṣudrakāṇām iti //
children.translated_text: For among thousands, [only] one or none may be prominent — due to [their] superiority in courage and wisdom; and the petty depend on them.

children.text: KAZ08.4.13/ "sva.cakra.para.cakrayoḥ sva.cakram atimātrābhyāṃ daṇḍa.karābhyāṃ pīḍayaty aśakyaṃ ca vārayitum, para.cakraṃ tu śakyaṃ praiyoddhum upasāreṇa saṃdhinā vā mokṣayitum" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of one's own forces and the enemy's forces [causing distress] — one's own forces oppress with excessive punishments and taxes, and it is impossible to prevent this; but the enemy's forces can be fought off or freed from through a march or a treaty" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.14/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.15/ sva.cakra.pīḍanaṃ prakṛti.puruṣa.mukhya.upagraha.vighātābhyāṃ śakyate vārayitum eka.deśaṃ vā pīḍayati, sarva.deśa.pīḍanaṃ tu para.cakraṃ vilopa.ghāta.dāha.vidhvaṃsana.apavāhanaiḥ pīḍayati^iti //
children.translated_text: The distress caused by one's own forces can be prevented by winning over or removing the leaders of the subjects and constituents, and it afflicts [only] one region; but the enemy's forces, afflicting all regions, oppress through plunder, slaughter, burning, destruction, and deportation.

children.text: KAZ08.4.16/ "prakṛti.rāja.vivādayoḥ prakṛiti.vivādaḥ prakṛtīnāṃ bhedakaḥ para.abhiyogān āvahati, rāja.vivādas tu prakṛtīnāṃ dvi.guṇa.bhakta.vetana.parihāra.karo bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: "Of a quarrel among the subjects and a quarrel with the king — a quarrel among the subjects, by splitting the subjects, invites [the enemy's] attack; but a quarrel with the king results in doubled food-rations, wages, and exemptions for the subjects" — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.17/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.18/ śakyaḥ prakṛti.vivādaḥ prakṛti.mukhya.upagraheṇa kalaha.sthāna.apanayanena vā vārayitum //
children.translated_text: A quarrel among the subjects can be prevented by winning over the leaders of the subjects or by removing the cause of the quarrel.

children.text: KAZ08.4.19/ vivadamānās tu prakṛtayaḥ paraspara.saṃgharṣeṇa^upakurvanti //
children.translated_text: And subjects in quarrel, through mutual friction, actually help [each other by strengthening the ruler's position].

children.text: KAZ08.4.20/ rāja.vivādas tu pīḍana.ucchedanāya prakṛtīnāṃ dvi.guṇa.vyāyāma.sādhya iti //
children.translated_text: But a quarrel with the king, aimed at the oppression and uprooting of the subjects, requires double the effort to resolve.

children.text: KAZ08.4.21/ "deśa.rāja.vihārayor deśa.vihāras traikālyena karma.phala.upaghātaṃ karoti, rāja.vihāras tu kāru.śilpi.kuśīlava.vāg.jīvana.rūpa.ājīvā.vaidehaka.upakāraṃ karoti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.21/ "Between calamities of the country and the king's recreation: country-recreation harms the fruit of work over all three seasons, whereas the king's recreation benefits artisans, craftsmen, performers, orators, courtesans, and traders" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.22/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.22/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.23/ deśa.vihāraḥ karma.śramam avadhā.artham alpaṃ bhakṣayati bhakṣayitvā ca bhūyaḥ karmasu yogaṃ gacchati, rāja.vihāras tu svayaṃ vallabhaiś ca svayaṃ.grāha.praṇaya.paṇya.agāra.kārya.upagrahaiḥ pīḍayati^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.23/ Country-recreation consumes little in order to relieve the fatigue of work and, having consumed, returns to productive labor; but the king's recreation oppresses through his own [demands] and those of his favorites — through confiscation, forced gifts, and harassment of markets and businesses.

children.text: KAZ08.4.24/ "subhagā.kumārayoḥ kumāraḥ svayaṃ vallabhaiś ca svayaṃ.grāha.praṇaya.paṇya.agāra.kārya.upagrahaiḥ pīḍayati, subhagā vilāsa.upabhogena" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.24/ "Between [the calamities of] a favorite woman and a prince: the prince oppresses through his own [demands] and those of his favorites — through confiscation, forced gifts, and harassment of markets and businesses; the favorite woman, through indulgence and luxury" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.25/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.25/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.26/ śakyaḥ kumāro mantri.purohitābhyāṃ vārayitum, na subhagā bāliśyād anarthya.jana.samyogāc ca^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.26/ A prince can be restrained by the minister and the chaplain, but not a favorite woman — because of her foolishness and her association with worthless people.

children.text: KAZ08.4.27/ "śreṇī.mukhyayoḥ śreṇī bāhulyād anavagrahā steya.sāhasābhyāṃ pīḍayati, mukhyaḥ kārya.anugraha.vighātābhyām" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.27/ "Between [the calamities of] a guild and a chief: the guild, being numerous and uncontrollable, oppresses through theft and violence; the chief, through obstruction and hindrance of business" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.28/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.28/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.29/ suvyāvartyā śreṇī samāna.śīla.vyasanatvāt, śreṇī.mukhya.eka.deśa.upagraheṇa vā //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.29/ A guild is easily turned around because its members share the same disposition and vices, or by winning over one part of the guild-chief [system].

children.text: KAZ08.4.30/ stambha.yukto mukhyaḥ para.prāṇa.dravya.upaghātābhyāṃ pīḍayati^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.30/ A chief, supported by [his own] power, oppresses through harm to life and property.

children.text: KAZ08.4.31/ "samnidhātṛ.samāhartroḥ samnidhātā kṛta.vidūṣaṇa.atyayābhyāṃ pīḍayati, samāhartā karaṇa.adhiṣṭhitaḥ pradiṣṭa.phala.upabhogī bhavati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.31/ "Between [the calamities of] the treasurer and the collector: the treasurer oppresses through corruption and penalties on accomplished [revenue]; the collector, established in the mechanism [of collection], enjoys the designated fruits" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.32/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.32/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.33/ samnidhātā kṛta.avastham anyaiḥ kośa.praveśyaṃ pratigṛhṇāti, samāhartā tu pūrvam artham ātmanaḥ kṛtvā paścād rāja.arthaṃ karoti praṇāśayati vā, para.sva.ādāne ca sva.pratyayaś carati^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.33/ The treasurer receives what is already in a fixed state, [deposited] by others into the treasury; but the collector first makes the revenue his own and then makes it the king's or destroys it, and in seizing others' property, acts on his own authority.

children.text: KAZ08.4.34/ "anta.pāla.vaidehakayor anta.pālaś cora.prasarga.deya.atyādānābhyāṃ vaṇik.pathaṃ pīḍayati, vaidehakās tu paṇya..pratipaṇya.anugrahaiḥ prasādhayanti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.34/ "Between [the calamities of] the frontier guard and the trader: the frontier guard oppresses the trade-route through releasing thieves, collecting undue taxes, and excessive levies; but the traders develop [the route] through concessions on goods and counter-goods" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.35/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.35/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.36/ anta.pālaḥ paṇya.sampāta.anugraheṇa vartayati, vaidehakās tu sambhūya paṇyānām utkarṣa.apakarṣaṃ kurvāṇāḥ paṇe paṇa.śataṃ kumbhe kumbha.śatam ity ājīvanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.36/ The frontier guard subsists by facilitating the flow of merchandise; but traders, combining together, create artificial scarcity and abundance of goods, profiting one hundred [<s>paṇas</s>] on a [single] <s>paṇa</s>, a hundred pots on one pot.

children.text: KAZ08.4.37/ abhijāta.uparuddhā bhūmiḥ paśu.vraja.uparuddhā vā^iti "abhijāta.uparuddhā bhūmiḥ mahā.phalā^apy āyudhīya.upakāriṇī na kṣamā mokṣayituṃ vyasana.ābādha.bhayāt, paśu.vraja.uparuddhā tu kṛṣi.yogyā kṣamā mokṣayitum //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.37/ "Between land occupied by noblemen and land occupied by cattle-herds: land occupied by noblemen, though of great yield and useful for the military, cannot be freed because of the fear of calamity and distress; but land occupied by cattle-herds, being suitable for cultivation, can be freed.

children.text: KAZ08.4.38/ vivītaṃ hi kṣetreṇa bādhyate" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.38/ For a commons is encroached upon by cultivated fields" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.39/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.39/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.40/ abhijāta.uparuddhā bhūmir atyanta.mahā.upakārā^api kṣamā mokṣayituṃ vyasana.ābādha.bhayāt, paśu.vraja.uparuddhā tu kośa.vāhana.upakāriṇī na kṣamā mokṣayitum, anyatra sasya.vāpa.uparodhād iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.40/ Land occupied by noblemen, though of exceedingly great benefit, can be freed because of the fear of calamity and distress; but land occupied by cattle-herds, being useful for the treasury and transport, cannot be freed — except when it obstructs crop-sowing.

children.text: KAZ08.4.41/ "pratirodhaka.āṭavikayoḥ pratirodhakā rātri.sattra.carāḥ śarīra.ākramiṇo nityāḥ śata.sahasra.ahapāriṇaḥ pradhāna.kopakāś ca vyavahitāḥ pratyantara.araṇya.carāś ca^āṭavikāḥ prakāśā dṛsyāś caranti, eka.deśa.ghātakāś ca" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.41/ "Between interceptors and forest-tribesmen: interceptors operate at night by stealth, are bodily assailants, are permanent, can destroy hundreds of thousands in a day, provoke the chiefs, and operate in the gaps [of law]; forest-tribesmen roam in near-frontier forests, operate openly and visibly, and destroy [only] one area at a time" — so [say] the teachers.

children.text: KAZ08.4.42/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.42/ Not so — [says] <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ08.4.43/ pratirodhakāḥ pramattasya^aparahanti, alpāḥ kuṇṭhāḥ sukhā jñātuṃ grahītuṃ ca, sva.deśasthāḥ prabhūtā vikrāntāś ca^āṭavikāḥ prakāśa.yodino^apahartāro hantāraś ca deśānāṃ rāja.sadharmāṇa iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.43/ Interceptors plunder [only] those who are off-guard, are few, dull, and easy to identify and capture; but forest-tribesmen, established in their own territory, are numerous, fierce, open fighters, plunderers and destroyers of entire regions, and share the nature of kings.

children.text: KAZ08.4.44/ mṛga.hasti.vanayoḥ mṛgāḥ prabhūtāḥ prabhūta.māṃsa.carma.upakāriṇo manda.grāsa.avakleśinaḥ suniyamyāś ca //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.44/ Between [the calamities of] wild game and elephants: wild game are numerous, useful for abundant meat and hides, consume little fodder, and cause little distress, and are easy to control.

children.text: KAZ08.4.45/ viparītā hastino gṛhyamāṇā duṣṭāś ca deśa.vināśāya^iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.45/ Elephants are the opposite — and when being captured, [if] they become aggressive, [they bring] destruction of the region.

children.text: KAZ08.4.46/ sva.para.sthānīya.upakārayoḥ sva.sthānīya.upakāro dhānya.paśu.hiraṇya.kupya.upakāro jānapadānām āpady ātma.dhāraṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.46/ Between [calamities] beneficial to one's own and another's headquarters: what is beneficial to one's own headquarters — beneficial in grain, cattle, gold, and raw materials — sustains the people in calamity.

children.text: KAZ08.4.47/ viparītaḥ para.sthānīya.upakāraḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.4.47/ The opposite is what benefits another's headquarters.

children.text:
KAZ08.4.48/ iti pīḍanāni - ābhyantaro mukhya.stambho bāhyo^amitra.aṭavī.stambhaḥ // [iti stambha.vargah]
KAZ08.4.49/ tābhyāṃ pīḍanair yathā.uktaiś ca pīḍitaḥ, sakto mukhyeṣu, parihāra.upahataḥ, prakīrṇo, mithyā.saṃhṛtaḥ, sāmanta.aṭavī.hṛta iti kośa.saṅga.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.4.48/ Thus the afflictions: internal obstruction is that of chiefs within; external obstruction is that of enemies and forest-tribes. [Thus ends the category of obstruction.]
KAZ08.4.49/ One afflicted by these obstructions and by the afflictions described — caught among chiefs, damaged by exemptions, dispersed, falsely reconciled, seized by vassals and forest-tribes — this is the category of treasury-loss.

children.text:
KAZ08.4.50ab/ pīḍanānām anutpattāv utpannānāṃ ca vāraṇe /
KAZ08.4.50cd/ yateta deśa.vṛddhy.arthaṃ nāśe ca stambha.saṅgayoḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.4.50ab/ He should strive for the non-arising of afflictions and the prevention of those that have arisen,
KAZ08.4.50cd/ for the growth of the territory and for the destruction of obstruction and loss.

children.text:
(bala.vyasana.vargah - mitra.vyasana.vargah)
KAZ08.5.01/ bala.vyasanāni - amānitam, vimānitam, abhṛtam, vyādhitam, nava.āgatam, dūra.āyātam, pariśrāntam, parikṣīṇam, pratihatam, hata.agra.vegam, anṛtu.prāptam, abhūmi.prāptam, āśā.nirvedi, parisṛptam, kalatra.garbhi, antaḥ.śalyam, kupita.mūlam, bhinna.garbham, apasṛtam, atikṣiptam, upaniviṣṭam, samāptam, uparuddham, parikṣiptam, chinna.dhānya.puruṣa.vīvadham,
sva.vikṣiptam, mitra.vikṣiptam, dūṣya.yuktam, duṣṭa.pārṣṇi.grāham, śūnya.mūlam, asvāmi.saṃhatam, bhinna.kūṭam, andham iti //
children.translated_text:
(Category of army calamities — Category of ally calamities)
KAZ08.5.01/ Army calamities: dishonored, humiliated, unpaid, diseased, newly arrived, come from afar, exhausted, depleted, repelled, with broken front-momentum, arrived out of season, arrived in wrong terrain, despairing, surrounded, encumbered with camp-followers, harboring internal thorns, with an angry base, with a broken core, withdrawn, overextended, encamped, completed, besieged, encircled, with grain-and-manpower supply cut,
scattered by one's own, scattered by an ally, yoked with disloyal [elements], with a hostile rear-striker, with an empty base, united without a master, with a broken formation, and blind.

children.text: KAZ08.5.02/ teṣām amānita.vimānita.aniyatayor amānitaṃ kṛta.artha.mānaṃ yudhyeta, na vimānitam antaḥ.kopam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.02/ Between the dishonored and the humiliated — which are both unsettled: the dishonored, honored for its achievements, would fight; not the humiliated, harboring internal anger.

children.text: KAZ08.5.03/ abhṛta.vyādhitayor abhṛtaṃ tadātva.kṛta.vetanaṃ yudhyeta, na vyādhitam akarmaṇyam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.03/ Between the unpaid and the diseased: the unpaid, given immediate wages, would fight; not the diseased, being unfit for work.

children.text: KAZ08.5.04/ nava.āgata.dūra.āyātayor nava.āgatam anyata upalabdha.deśam anava.miśraṃ yudhyeta, na dūra.āyatam āyata.gata.parikleśam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.04/ Between the newly arrived and the come-from-afar: the newly arrived, having found terrain elsewhere and not yet intermixed, would fight; not the come-from-afar, exhausted from the long journey.

children.text: KAZ08.5.05/ pariśrānta.parikṣīṇayoḥ pariśrāntaṃ snāna.bhojana.svapna.labdha.viśrāmaṃ yudhyeta, na parikṣīṇam anyatra^āhave kṣīṇayugya.puruṣam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.05/ Between the exhausted and the depleted: the exhausted, having recovered through bathing, food, and sleep, would fight; not the depleted, whose yoked animals and men are wasted from a previous battle.

children.text: KAZ08.5.06/ pratihata.hata.agra.vegayoḥ pratihatam agra.pāta.bhagnaṃ pravīra.puruṣa.saṃhataṃ yudhyeta, na hata.agra.vegam agra.pāta.hata.vīram //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.06/ Between the repelled and the one with broken front-momentum: the repelled, broken in the initial charge but having its brave warriors still united, would fight; not the one with broken front-momentum, whose warriors are killed in the initial charge.

children.text: KAZ08.5.07/ anṛtv.abhūmi.prāptayor anṛtu.prāptaṃ yatha.ṛtu.yugya.śastra.āvaraṇaṃ yudhyeta, na^abhūmi.prāptam avaruddha.prasāra.vyāyāmam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.07/ Between the arrived-out-of-season and the arrived-in-wrong-terrain: the arrived-out-of-season, having yoked animals, weapons, and armor suited to the season, would fight; not the arrived-in-wrong-terrain, whose movement and exercise are restricted.

children.text: KAZ08.5.08/ āśā.nirvedi.parisṛptayor āśā.nirvedi labdha.abhiprāyaṃ yudhyeta, na parisṛptam apasṛta.mukhyam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.08/ Between the despairing and the surrounded: the despairing, having gained its purpose, would fight; not the surrounded, whose chiefs have deserted.

children.text: KAZ08.5.09/ kalatra.garbhy.antaḥ.śalyayoḥ kalatra.garbhi unmucya kalatraṃ yudhyeta, na^antaḥ.śalyam antara.mitram //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.09/ Between the encumbered-with-camp-followers and the harboring-internal-thorns: the encumbered, having released its camp-followers, would fight; not the one harboring internal thorns, having secret enemies within.

children.text: KAZ08.5.10/ kupita.mūla.bhinna.garbhayoḥ kupita.mūlaṃ praśamita.kopaṃ sāma.ādibhir yudhyeta, na bhinna.garbham anyonyasmād bhinnam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.10/ Between the angry-base and the broken-core: the angry-base, its anger pacified through conciliation and other [means], would fight; not the broken-core, whose [units] are divided from one another.

children.text: KAZ08.5.11/ apasṛta.atikṣiptayor apasṛtam eka.rājya.atikrāntaṃ mantra.vyāyāmābhyāṃ sattra.mitra.apāśrayaṃ yudhyeta, na^atikṣiptam aneka.rājya.atikrāntaṃ bahv.ābādhatvāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.11/ Between the withdrawn and the overextended: the withdrawn, having crossed one kingdom, [being maintainable] through counsel, exertion, and support of agents and allies, would fight; not the overextended, having crossed many kingdoms, because of being beset by many [threats].

children.text: KAZ08.5.12/ upaniviṣṭa.samāptayor upaniviṣṭaṃ pṛthag.yāna.sthānam atisaṃdhāya^ariṃ yudhyeta, na samāptam ariṇā^eka.sthāna.yānam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.12/ Between the encamped and the completed [formation]: the encamped, having outwitted the enemy by [choosing] separate routes and positions of march, would fight; not the completed, whose route and position of march coincide with the enemy's.

children.text: KAZ08.5.13/ uparuddha.parikṣiptayor uparuddham anyato niṣkramya^uparoddhāraṃ pratiyudhyeta, na parikṣiptaṃ sarvataḥ pratiruddham //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.13/ Between the besieged and the encircled: the besieged, sallying forth from another [direction], could fight back against the besieger; not the encircled, blocked from all sides.

children.text: KAZ08.5.14/ chinna.dhānya.puruṣa.vīvadhayoḥ chinna.dhānyam anyato dhānyam ānīya jaṅgama.sthāvara.āhāraṃ vā yudhyeta, na chinna.puruṣa.vīvadham anabhisāram //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.14/ Between the grain-cut and the manpower-cut: the grain-cut, having brought grain from elsewhere or subsisting on mobile and stationary food [sources], would fight; not the manpower-cut, which cannot advance.

children.text: KAZ08.5.15/ sva.vikṣipta.mitra.vikṣiptayoḥ sva.vikṣiptaṃ sva.bhūmau vikṣiptaṃ sainyam āpadi śakyam āvāhayitum, na mitra.vikṣiptaṃ viprakṛṣṭa.deśa.kālatvāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.15/ Between the self-scattered and the ally-scattered: the self-scattered, being an army scattered in one's own territory, can be recalled in a crisis; not the ally-scattered, being in a distant place and time.

children.text: KAZ08.5.16/ dūṣya.yukta.duṣṭa.pārṣṇi.grāhayor dūṣya.yuktam āpta.puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitam asaṃhataṃ yudhyeta, na duṣṭa.pārṣṇi.grāhaṃ pṛṣṭha.abhighāta.trastam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.16/ Between the yoked-with-disloyal and the hostile-rear-striker: the yoked-with-disloyal, placed under trusted commanders and kept unconcentrated, would fight; not the one with a hostile rear-striker, terrified of being struck from behind.

children.text: KAZ08.5.17/ śūnya.mūla.asvāmi.saṃhatayoḥ śūnya.mūlaṃ kṛta.paura.jānapada.ārakṣaṃ sarva.saṃdohena yudhyeta, na^asvāmi.saṃhataṃ rāja.senā.pati.hīnam //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.17/ Between the empty-base and the united-without-master: the empty-base, having ensured the protection of townspeople and countryfolk, would fight with its full forces; not the united-without-master, lacking both king and commander.

children.text: KAZ08.5.18/ bhinna.kūṭa.andhayor bhinna.kūṭam anya.adhiṣṭhitaṃ yudhyeta, na^andham adeśikaṃ - iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ08.5.18/ Between the broken-formation and the blind: the broken-formation, placed under other [commanders], would fight; not the blind, without guides.

children.text:
KAZ08.5.19ab/ doṣa.śuddhir bala.āvāpaḥ sattra.sthāna.atisaṃhitam /
KAZ08.5.19cd/ saṃdhiś ca^uttara.pakṣasya bala.vyasana.sādhanam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.19ab/ Purging the defect, reinforcing the army, deploying agents, strategic positioning,
KAZ08.5.19cd/ and peace with the opposing side — these are the remedies for army calamities.

children.text:
KAZ08.5.20ab/ rakṣet sva.daṇḍaṃ vyasane śatrubhyo nityam utthitaḥ /
KAZ08.5.20cd/ prahared daṇḍa.randhreṣu śatrūṇāṃ nityam utthitaḥ //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.20ab/ He should protect his own army in calamity from enemies, ever vigilant;
KAZ08.5.20cd/ he should strike at the vulnerable points of the enemies' armies, ever vigilant.

children.text:
KAZ08.5.21ab/ yato nimittaṃ vyasanaṃ prakṛtīnām avāpnuyāt /
KAZ08.5.21cd/ prāg eva pratikurvīta tan nimittam atandritaḥ /
KAZ08.5.22ab/ abhiyātaṃ svayaṃ mitraṃ sambhūya^anya.vaśena vā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.21ab/ Whatever the cause from which calamity of the constituent elements might arise,
KAZ08.5.21cd/ he should preemptively counteract that cause without delay.
KAZ08.5.22ab/ An ally who is attacked — personally, jointly, or under another's control —

children.text:
KAZ08.5.22cd/ parityaktam aśaktyā vā lobhena praṇayena vā /
KAZ08.5.23ab/ vikrītam abhiyuñjāne saṃgrāme vā^apavartinā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.22cd/ or abandoned through inability, or through greed, or through attachment;
KAZ08.5.23ab/ or sold out when attacked, or by one who retreats in battle;

children.text:
KAZ08.5.23cd/ dvaidhī.bhāvena vā^amitraṃ yāsyatā vā^anyam anyataḥ /
KAZ08.5.24ab/ pṛthag vā saha.yāne vā viśvāsena^atisaṃhitam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.23cd/ or by one who adopts a dual policy, or by one about to march against another enemy;
KAZ08.5.24ab/ or outwitted through trust, whether marching separately or jointly;

children.text:
KAZ08.5.24cd/ bhaya.avamāna.ālasyair vā vyasanān na pramokṣitam /
KAZ08.5.25ab/ avaruddhaṃ sva.bhūmibhyaḥ samīpād vā bhayād gatam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.24cd/ or not freed from calamity through fear, contempt, or laziness;
KAZ08.5.25ab/ or cut off from his own territories, or driven away from proximity out of fear;

children.text:
KAZ08.5.25cd/ ācchedanād adānād vā dattvā vā^apy avamānitam /
KAZ08.5.26ab/ atyāhāritam arthaṃ vā svayaṃ para.mukhena vā //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.25cd/ or humiliated through confiscation, non-giving, or giving [and then slighting];
KAZ08.5.26ab/ or whose property is excessively taken — by oneself or through another;

children.text:
KAZ08.5.26cd/ atibhāre niyuktaṃ vā bhaṅktvā param upasthitam /
KAZ08.5.27ab/ upekṣitam aśaktyā vā prārthayitvā virodhitam //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.26cd/ or subjected to an excessive burden, or one who, having been broken, has submitted to the enemy;
KAZ08.5.27ab/ or neglected through inability, or opposed after being solicited —

children.text:
KAZ08.5.27cd/ kṛcchreṇa sādhyate mitraṃ siddhaṃ ca^āśu virajyati /
KAZ08.5.28ab/ kṛta.prayāsaṃ mānyaṃ vā mohān mitram amānitam /
KAZ08.5.28cd/ mānitaṃ vā na sadṛśaṃ śaktito vā nivāritam //

KAZ08.5.29ab/ mitra.upaghāta.trastaṃ vā śaṅkitaṃ vā^ari.saṃhitāt /
KAZ08.5.29cd/ dūṣyair vā bhedituṃ mitraṃ sādhyaṃ siddhaṃ ca tiṣṭhati //
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.29ab/ or frightened by the ally's ill-treatment, or suspicious of [the king's] alliance with the enemy;
KAZ08.5.29cd/ an ally to be split by disloyal [agents] — whether being cultivated or already won — remains [vulnerable].

children.text:
KAZ08.5.30ab/ tasmān na^utpādayed enān doṣān mitra.upaghātakān /
KAZ08.5.30cd/ utpannān vā praśamayed guṇair doṣa.upaghātibhiḥ //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ08.5.30ab/ Therefore, one should not give rise to these faults that damage alliances;
KAZ08.5.30cd/ or, once arisen, should pacify them with virtues that counteract the faults.

children.text:
(śakti.deśa.kāla.bala.abala.jnānam - yātrā.kālāh)
KAZ09.1.01/ vijigīṣur ātmanaḥ parasya ca bala.abalaṃ śakti.deśa.kāla.yātrā.kāla.bala.samuddāna.kāla.paścāt.kopa.kṣaya.vyaya.lābha.āpadāṃ jñātvā viśiṣṭa.balo yāyāt, anyathā^āsīta //
children.translated_text:
(Knowledge of power, place, time, strength and weakness — times for military campaigns)
KAZ09.1.01/ The <s>vijigīṣu</s> (would-be conqueror), having assessed his own and the enemy's strength and weakness in terms of power, place, time, campaign timing, force mobilization timing, rear-attacks, attrition, expenditure, gains, and calamities, should march when he has superior strength; otherwise, he should remain still.

children.text: KAZ09.1.02/ "utsāha.prabhāvayor utsāhaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.02/ 'Between energy and resources, energy is better.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.03/ svayaṃ hi rājā śūro balavān arogaḥ kṛta.astro daṇḍa.dvitīyo^api śaktaḥ prabhāvavantaṃ rājānaṃ jetum //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.03/ 'For a king who is himself brave, strong, healthy, and skilled in arms is capable — even with force alone as his second — of conquering a king possessed of resources.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.04/ alpo^api ca^asya daṇḍas tejasā kṛtya.karo bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.04/ 'And even a small force of his, by its élan, becomes effective.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.05/ nirutsāhas tu prabhāvavān rājā vikrama.abhipanno naśyati" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.05/ 'But a king who has resources but no energy perishes when attacked by force' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ09.1.06/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.06/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.1.07/ prabhāvavān utsāhavantaṃ rājānaṃ prabhāvena^atisaṃdhatte tad.viśiṣṭam anyaṃ rājānam āvāhya bhṛtvā krītvā pravīra.puruṣān //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.07/ A king with resources outwits an energetic king through his resources — by summoning another king superior to him, by hiring or purchasing outstanding warriors.

children.text: KAZ09.1.08/ prabhūta.prabhāva.haya.hasti.ratha.upakaraṇa.sampannaś ca^asya daṇḍaḥ sarvatra^apratihataś carati //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.08/ And his force, abundantly supplied with resources, horses, elephants, chariots, and equipment, moves unopposed everywhere.

children.text: KAZ09.1.09/ utsāhavataś ca prabhāvavanto jitvā krītvā ca striyo bālāḥ paṅgavo^andhāś ca pṛthivīṃ jigyur iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.09/ And [it is known that] the resourceful — having conquered and bought women, children, the lame, and the blind — conquered the earth.

children.text: KAZ09.1.10/ "prabhāva.mantrayoḥ prabhāvaḥ śreyān //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.10/ 'Between resources and counsel, resources are better.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.11/ mantra.śakti.sampanno hi vandhya.buddhir aprabhāvo bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.11/ 'For one endowed with the power of counsel but barren of purpose is resourceless.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.12/ mantra.karma ca^asya niścitam aprabhāvo garbha.dhānyam avṛṣṭir iva^upahanti" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.12/ 'And his well-deliberated plan, being resourceless, destroys [everything] like a drought [destroys] embryonic grain' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ09.1.13/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.13/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.1.14/ mantra.śaktiḥ śreyasī //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.14/ The power of counsel is superior.

children.text: KAZ09.1.15/ prajñā.śāstra.cakṣur hi rājā^alpena^api prayatnena mantram ādhātuṃ śaktaḥ parān utsāha.prabhāvavataś ca sāma.ādibhir yoga.upaniṣadbhyāṃ ca^atisaṃdhātum //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.15/ For a king whose eyes are wisdom and the treatises (<s>śāstra</s>) is capable, with even little effort, of devising counsel, and of outwitting enemies possessed of both energy and resources through conciliation and other [means], as well as through strategic and esoteric [devices].

children.text: KAZ09.1.16/ evam utsāha.prabhāva.mantra.śaktīnām uttara.uttara.adhiko^atisaṃdhatte //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.16/ Thus, among the powers of energy, resources, and counsel, each succeeding one outwits [the one before].

children.text: KAZ09.1.17/ deśaḥ pṛthivī //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.17/ Place means the earth.

children.text: KAZ09.1.18/ tasyāṃ himavat.samudra.antaram udīcīnaṃ yojana.sahasra.parimāṇaṃ tiryak cakra.varti.kṣetram //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.18/ On it, the northern [region] between the <s>Himālayas</s> and the ocean, a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in breadth across — that is the field of the universal sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>).

children.text: KAZ09.1.19/ tatra^araṇyo grāmyaḥ parvata audako bhaumaḥ samo viṣama iti viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.19/ In it, [there are] the following distinctions: forested, agricultural, mountainous, aquatic, terrestrial, level, and rough [terrain].

children.text: KAZ09.1.20/ teṣu yathā.sva.bala.vṛddhi.karaṃ karma prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.20/ On these, he should employ operations that augment his own forces accordingly.

children.text: KAZ09.1.21/ yatra.ātmanaḥ sainya.vyāyāmānāṃ bhūmiḥ, abhūmiḥ parasya, sa uttamo deśaḥ, viparīto^adhamaḥ, sādhāraṇo madhyamaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.21/ Where the terrain is favorable for one's own army's maneuvers and unfavorable for the enemy — that is the best terrain; the opposite, the worst; terrain [favorable to] both, the middling.

children.text: KAZ09.1.22/ kālaḥ śīta.uṣṇa.varṣa.ātmā //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.22/ Time is characterized by cold, heat, and rain.

children.text: KAZ09.1.23/ tasya rātrir ahaḥ pakṣo māsa ṛtur ayanaṃ saṃvatsaro yugam iti viśeṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.23/ Its subdivisions are: night, day, fortnight, month, season, solstice, year, and age (<s>yuga</s>).

children.text: KAZ09.1.24/ teṣu yathā.sva.bala.vṛddhi.karaṃ karma.prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.24/ On these, he should employ operations that augment his own forces accordingly.

children.text: KAZ09.1.25/ yatra.ātmanaḥ sainya.vyāyāmānām ṛtuḥ anṛtuḥ parasya, sa uttamaḥ kālaḥ, viparīto^adhamaḥ, sādhāraṇo madhyamaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.25/ Where the season is favorable for one's own army's maneuvers and unfavorable for the enemy — that is the best time; the opposite, the worst; [time favorable to] both, the middling.

children.text: KAZ09.1.26/ "śakti.deśa.kālānāṃ tu śaktiḥ śreyasī" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.26/ 'Among power, place, and time, power is the best' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ09.1.27/ śaktimān hi nimna.sthalavato deśasya śīta.uṣṇa.varṣavataś ca kālasya śaktaḥ pratīkāre bhavati //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.27/ For one who is powerful is able to counter [the effects of] terrain — whether low or high — and of season — whether cold, hot, or rainy.

children.text: KAZ09.1.28/ "deśaḥ śreyān" ity eke //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.28/ 'Place is best' — say some.

children.text: KAZ09.1.29/ "sthala.gato hi śvā nakraṃ vikarṣati, nimna.gato nakraḥ śvānam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.29/ 'For a dog on dry land drags a crocodile; a crocodile in the water [drags] a dog.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.30/ "kālaḥ śreyān" ity eke //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.30/ 'Time is best' — say others.

children.text: KAZ09.1.31/ "divā kākaḥ kauśikaṃ hanti, rātrau kauśikaḥ kākam" iti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.31/ 'By day, a crow kills an owl; by night, an owl kills a crow.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.32/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.32/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.1.33/ paraspara.sādhakā hi śakti.deśa.kālāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.33/ For power, place, and time are mutually reinforcing.

children.text: KAZ09.1.34/ tair abhyuccitas tṛtīyaṃ caturthaṃ vā daṇḍasya^aṃśaṃ mūle pārṣṇyāṃ pratyanta.aṭavīṣu ca rakṣā vidhāya kārya.sādhana.sahaṃ kośa.daṇḍaṃ ca^ādāya kṣīṇa.purāṇa.bhaktam agṛhīta.nava.bhaktam asaṃskṛta.durgama.mitraṃ vārṣikaṃ ca^asya sasyaṃ haimanaṃ ca muṣṭim upahantuṃ mārgaśīrṣīṃ yātrāṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.34/ Enhanced by these [factors], having set aside a third or fourth of the army for protection of the base, the rear, and the frontier and forest [regions], and taking with him a treasury and army sufficient for the task — he should march in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> [November-December] to destroy [the enemy's] autumn crop and winter grain-reserves, when [the enemy's] old provisions are depleted and new provisions not yet secured, and whose forts and alliances are unprepared.

children.text: KAZ09.1.35/ haimānaṃ ca^asya sasyaṃ vāsantikaṃ ca muṣṭim upahantuṃ caitrīṃ yātrāṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.35/ He should march in <s>Caitra</s> [March-April] to destroy the enemy's winter crop and spring grain-reserves.

children.text: KAZ09.1.36/ kṣīṇa.kṛṇa.kāṣṭha.udakam asaṃskṛta.durgama.mitraṃ vāsantikaṃ ca^asya sasyaṃ vārṣikīṃ ca muṣṭim upahantuṃ jyeṣṭhāmūlīyāṃ yātrāṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.36/ He should march in <s>Jyeṣṭhāmūlīya</s> [May-June] to destroy the enemy's spring crop and monsoon grain-reserves, when his fuel, timber, and water are depleted and his forts and alliances unprepared.

children.text: KAZ09.1.37/ atyuṣṇam alpa.yavasa.indhana.udakaṃ vā deśaṃ hemante yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.37/ Or he should march in winter to a territory that is extremely hot and poor in fodder, fuel, and water.

children.text: KAZ09.1.38/ tuṣāra.durdinam agādha.nimna.prāyaṃ gahana.tṛṇa.vṛkṣaṃ vā deśaṃ grīṣme yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.38/ Or he should march in summer to a territory that is snowy, stormy, with deep marshy lowlands, and dense grass and trees.

children.text: KAZ09.1.39/ sva.sainya.vyāyāma.yogyaṃ parasya^ayogyaṃ varṣati yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.39/ During the rains he should march to a terrain suitable for his own army's maneuvers and unsuitable for the enemy's.

children.text: KAZ09.1.40/ mārgaśīrṣīṃ taiṣīṃ ca^antareṇa dīrgha.kālāṃ yātrāṃ yāyāt, caitrīṃ vaiśākhīṃ ca^antareṇa madhyama.kālām, jyeṣṭhāmūlīyām āṣāḍhīṃ ca^antareṇa hrasva.kālām, upoṣiṣyan vyasane caturthīm //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.40/ Between <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Taiṣa</s> [Pauṣa], he should undertake a long-duration campaign; between <s>Caitra</s> and <s>Vaiśākha</s>, a medium-duration one; between <s>Jyeṣṭhāmūlīya</s> and <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, a short-duration one; and in famine conditions, a fourth [very short] one.

children.text: KAZ09.1.41/ vyasana.abhiyānaṃ vigṛhya.yāne vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.41/ Attacking during the enemy's calamity is explained under 'marching after hostilities.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.42/ prāyaśaś ca^ācāryāḥ "para.vyasane yātavyam" ity upadiśanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.42/ And the teachers generally advise: 'One should march when the enemy has a calamity.'

children.text: KAZ09.1.43/ śakty.udaye yātavyam anaikānntikatvād vyasanānām iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.43/ One should march when one's own power has risen — because calamities are not permanent — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.1.44/ yadā vā prayātaḥ karśayitum ucchetuṃ vā śaknuyād amitraṃ tadā yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.44/ Or he should march whenever he can weaken or destroy the enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.1.45/ atyuṣṇa.upakṣīṇe kāle hasti.bala.prāyo yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.45/ When the season is extremely hot and supplies are depleted, he should march with a predominantly elephant force.

children.text: KAZ09.1.46/ hastino hy antaḥ.svedāḥ kuṣṭhino bhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.46/ For elephants that [retain] internal moisture suffer skin disease [otherwise].

children.text: KAZ09.1.47/ anavagāhamānās toyam apibantaś ca^antar.avakṣārāc ca^andhī.bhavanti //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.47/ Not wading into water, not drinking, and due to internal desiccation, they become blind.

children.text: KAZ09.1.48/ tasmāt prabhūta.udake deśe varṣati ca hasti.bala.prāyo yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.48/ Therefore, in a region with abundant water and during the rains, he should march with a predominantly elephant force.

children.text: KAZ09.1.49/ viparyaye khara.uṣṭra.aśva.bala.prāyo deśam alpa.varṣa.paṅkam //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.49/ In the opposite [dry] conditions, [he should march] with predominantly donkey, camel, and horse forces, to terrain with little rain and mud.

children.text: KAZ09.1.50/ varṣati maru.prāyaṃ catur.aṅga.balo yāyāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.50/ During the rains, to predominantly desert [terrain], with a four-division army.

children.text: KAZ09.1.51/ sama.viṣama.nimna.sthala.hrasva.dīrgha.vaśena vā^adhvano yātrāṃ vibhajet //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.1.51/ Or he should divide the march according to whether the road is level, rough, low, high, short, or long.

children.text:
KAZ09.1.52ab/ sarvā vā hrasva.kālāḥ syur yātavyāḥ kārya.lāghavāt /
KAZ09.1.52cd/ dīrghāḥ kārya.gurutvād vā varṣā.vāsaḥ paratra ca //E
children.translated_text:
KAZ09.1.52ab/ Or all [campaigns] should be short-duration due to the simplicity of the task;
KAZ09.1.52cd/ or long-duration due to the gravity of the task — with the rainy-season encampment in the [enemy's] territory.

children.text:
(bala.upādāna.kālāh -samnāha.guṇāh -pratibala.karma)
KAZ09.2.01/ maula.bhṛtaka.śreṇī.mitra.amitra.aṭavī.balānāṃ samuddāna.kālāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Times for raising forces — qualities of armor — counter-force operations)
KAZ09.2.01/ [These are] the appropriate times for raising hereditary, hired, guild, allied, enemy, and forest tribal forces.

children.text:
KAZ09.2.02/ mūla.rakṣaṇād atiriktaṃ maula.balam, atyāvāpa.yuktā vā maulā mūle vikurvīran, bahula.anurakta.maula.balaḥ sāra.balo vā pratiyoddhā, vyāyāmena yoddhavyam, prakṛṣṭe^adhvani kāle vā kṣaya.vyaya.sahatvān maulānām, bahula.anurakta.sampāte ca yātavyasya^upajāpa.bhayād anya.sainyānāṃ bhṛta.ādīnām aviśvāse, bala.kṣaye vā sarva.sainyānāṃ - iti maula.bala.kālaḥ
//
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.02/ [The time for] hereditary forces: the hereditary army [should be raised] in excess of [what is needed for] base-protection — or if the hereditary troops under excessive deployment might rebel at the base; when the opposing force is predominantly hereditary, loyal, and of quality; when warfare requires training; when the road and the time are long, because hereditary troops can endure attrition and expenditure; when there is danger of enticement of other forces (hired, etc.) in a march against a foe who encounters massive loyal [forces]; and in case of depletion of all forces — this is the time for hereditary forces.

children.text: KAZ09.2.03/ "prabhūtaṃ me bhṛta.balam alpaṃ ca maula.balamṇ" "parasya^alpaṃ viraktaṃ vā maula.balam, phalgu.prāyam asāraṃ vā bhṛta.sainyamṇ" "mantreṇa yoddhavyam alpa.vyāyāmenaṇ" "hrasvo deśaḥ kālo vā tanu.kṣaya.vyayahṇ" "alpa.āvāpaṃ śānta.upajāpaṃ viśvastaṃ vā me sainyamṇ" "parasya^alpaḥ prasāro hantavyahṇ" - iti bhṛta.bala.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.03/ 'I have an abundance of hired forces and a small hereditary army'; 'The enemy has a small or disaffected hereditary army, or his hired forces are mostly inferior and lacking in quality'; 'Warfare must be [conducted] through counsel with little training'; 'The terrain or time is short, with minimal attrition and expenditure'; 'My army has few deployments, quelled enticement, or is trusted'; 'The enemy's dispersal is small and must be attacked' — this is the time for hired forces.

children.text: KAZ09.2.04/ "prabhūtaṃ me śreṇī.balam, śakyaṃ mūle yātrāyāṃ ca^ādhātumṇ" hrasvaḥ pravāsaḥ, śreṇī.bala.prāyaḥ pratiyoddhā mantra.vyāyāmābhyāṃ pratiyoddhu.kāmaḥ, daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāraḥ - iti śreṇī.bala.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.04/ 'I have abundant guild-forces that can be deployed at the base and on campaign'; [or] the journey is short, the opposing army is predominantly guild-based, wishing to fight with counsel and training, [and] a military-style engagement — this is the time for guild-forces.

children.text:
KAZ09.2.05/ "prabhūtaṃ me mitra.balaṃ śakyaṃ mūle yātrāyāṃ ca^ādhātumṇ" "alpaḥ pravāso mantra.yuddhāc ca bhūyo vyāyāma.yuddhamṇ" "mitra.balena vā pūrvam aṭavīṃ nagara.sthānam āsāraṃ vā yodhayitvā paścāt sva.balena yoddhayiṣyāmiṇ" "mitra.sādhāraṇaṃ vā me kāryamṇ" "mitra.āyattā vā me kārya.siddhihṇ" "āsannam anugrāhyaṃ vā me mitramṇ" "atyāvāpaṃ vā^asya sādayiṣyāmi"
- iti mitra.bala.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.05/ 'I have abundant allied forces that can be deployed at the base and on campaign'; 'The journey is short, and warfare through training is more [important] than warfare through counsel'; 'Or I shall first fight the forest and frontier regions or the base with allied forces, then fight with my own forces afterward'; 'Or my task is shared with the ally'; 'Or my success depends on the ally'; 'Or my ally who should be supported is nearby'; 'Or I shall use it as an excessive deployment' — this is the time for allied forces.

children.text:
KAZ09.2.06/ "prabhūtaṃ me śatru.balam, śatru.balena yodhayiṣyāmi nagara.sthānam aṭavīṃ vā, tatra me śva.varāhayoḥ kalahe caṇḍālasya^iva^anyatara.siddhir bhaviṣyatiṇ" "āsārāṇām aṭavīnāṃ vā kaṇṭaka.mardanam etat kariṣyāmiṇ" - atyupacitaṃ vā kopa.bhayān nityam āsannam ari.balaṃ vāsayed, anyatra.abhyantara.kopa.śaṅkāyāḥ - śatru.yuddha.avara.yuddha.kālaś ca
- ity amitra.bala.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.06/ 'I have abundant enemy forces; I shall fight the frontier or the forest with enemy forces — in this, like a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> in a fight between dog and boar, one outcome or the other will result for me'; 'This will serve as elimination of thorns — of the [enemy's own] bases and forests' — or an excessively accumulated [enemy] force, due to fear of rebellion, should always be stationed near [the enemy]; otherwise [one might] suspect an internal revolt — [this together with] the lesser battle-time is the time for enemy forces.

children.text: KAZ09.2.07/ tena^aṭavī.bala.kālo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.07/ By this, the time for forest tribal forces is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.2.08/ mārga.ādeśikam, para.bhūmi.yogyam, ari.yuddha.pratilomam, aṭavī.bala.prāyaḥ śatrur vā, "bilvaṃ bilvena hanyatāmṇ" alpaḥ prasāro hantavyaḥ - ity aṭavī.bala.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.08/ [They serve as] guides for the route, suited to the enemy's terrain, hostile to the enemy in battle, [useful when] the enemy army is predominantly tribal — 'let thorn be struck by thorn' — and [when] their small dispersal must be struck — this is the time for forest tribal forces.

children.text:
KAZ09.2.09/ sainyam anekam anekastham uktam anuktaṃ vā vilopa.arthaṃ yad uttiṣṭhati tad autsāhikaṃ - abhakta.vetanaṃ vilopa.viṣṭi.pratāpa.karaṃ bhedyaṃ pareṣām, abhedyaṃ tulya.deśa.jāti.śilpa.prāyaṃ saṃhataṃ mahat // [iti bala.upādāna.kālāh]
KAZ09.2.10/ teṣāṃ kupya.bhṛtam amitra.aṭavī.balaṃ vilopa.bhṛtaṃ vā kuryāt //
children.translated_text:
KAZ09.2.09/ An army [that is] manifold, stationed in many places, raised — whether commissioned or not — for the purpose of plunder, is called the enthusiastic force — [which] receives no food or wages [but] is sustained by plunder, forced labor, and terror. It is divisible by enemies, but indivisible when [composed of] people predominantly from the same region, caste, and craft, and when it is large and united.
KAZ09.2.10/ Among these, the one [sustained by] raw materials should be made into an enemy or forest tribal force, or one sustained by plunder.

children.text: KAZ09.2.11/ amitrasya vā bala.kāle pratyutpanne śatru.balam avagṛhṇīyāt, anyatra vā preṣayet, aphalaṃ vā kuryāt, vikṣiptaṃ vā vāsayet, kāle vā^atikrānte visṛjet //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.11/ Or, when the enemy's force-mobilization time has arrived, he should seize the enemy's forces, or send them elsewhere, or render them fruitless, or station them scattered, or dismiss them when the [opportune] time has passed.

children.text: KAZ09.2.12/ parasya ca^etad bala.samuddānaṃ vighātayet, ātmanaḥ sampādayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.12/ And he should thwart the enemy's force-mobilization while facilitating his own.

children.text: KAZ09.2.13/ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca^eṣāṃ śreyaḥ samnāhayitum //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.13/ And among these, it is better to armor the first [in order].

children.text: KAZ09.2.14/ tad.bhāva.bhāvitvān nitya.satkāra.anugamāc ca maula.balaṃ bhṛta.balāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.14/ Because of its inherent nature [loyalty] and because of constant honor and attendance, the hereditary force is better than the hired force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.15/ nitya.anantaraṃ kṣipra.utthāyi vaśyaṃ va bhṛta.balaṃ śreṇī.balāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.15/ [The hired force,] being always at hand, quickly mobilized, and controllable, is better than the guild force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.16/ jānapadam eka.artha.upagataṃ tulya.saṃgharṣa.amarṣa.siddhi.lābhaṃ ca śreṇī.balaṃ mitra.balāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.16/ [The guild force,] being from the countryside, unified in purpose, and sharing equally in the hardships, resentment, success, and gains [of war], is better than the allied force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.17/ aparimita.deśa.kālam eka.artha.upagamāc ca mitra.balam amitra.balāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.17/ [The allied force,] available for unlimited place and time and unified in purpose, is better than the enemy force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.18/ ārya.adhiṣṭhitam amitra.balam aṭavī.balāt^śreyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.18/ [The enemy force,] when commanded by a noble-born [officer], is better than the forest tribal force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.19/ tad ubhayaṃ vilopa.artham //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.19/ Both of those [enemy and tribal forces] are [useful] for plundering.

children.text: KAZ09.2.20/ avilope vyasane ca tābhyām ahi.bhayaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.20/ When there is no plunder or [in case of] calamity, there is danger from them as from a snake.

children.text: KAZ09.2.21/ "brāhmaṇa.kṣatriya.vaiśya.śūdra.sainyānāṃ tejaḥ.prādhānyāt pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ śreyaḥ samnāhayitum" ity ācāryāḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.21/ 'Among armies of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>, it is better to armor the earlier ones first, due to the primacy of their élan' — say the teachers.

children.text: KAZ09.2.22/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.22/ Not so, says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.2.23/ praṇipātena brāhmaṇa.balaṃ paro^abhihārayet //
children.translated_text: KAZ09.2.23/ The enemy would cause a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> army to bow down through prostration.

children.text: KAZ09.2.24/ praharaṇa.vidyā.vinītaṃ tu kṣatriya.balaṃ śreyaḥ, bahula.sāraṃ vā vaiśya.śūdra.balam iti //
children.translated_text: But a <s>Kṣatriya</s> force trained in weapons and military science is better; or a <s>Vaiśya</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> force that is numerous and strong.

children.text: KAZ09.2.25/ tasmād evaṃ.balaḥ paraḥ, tasya^etat pratibalam iti bala.samuddānaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, [one should think:] 'The enemy has such-and-such a force; this is the counter-force for it' — and should arrange the mobilization of forces accordingly.

children.text: KAZ09.2.26/ hasti.yantra.śakaṭa.garbha.kunta.prāsa.hāṭaka.veṇu.śalyavad hasti.balasya pratibalam //
children.translated_text: Against an elephant force — [the counter-force consists of] elephants equipped with machines, carts, belly-coverings, spears, barbed javelins, iron darts, and bamboo stakes.

children.text: KAZ09.2.27/ tad eva pāṣāṇa.laguḍa.āvaraṇa.aṅkuśa.kaca.grahaṇī.prāyaṃ ratha.balasya pratibalam //
children.translated_text: That same [counter-force], predominantly equipped with stones, clubs, shields, goads, and hair-grappling devices, serves as the counter-force against a chariot force.

children.text: KAZ09.2.28/ tad eva^aśvānāṃ pratibalam, varmiṇo vā hastino^aśvā vā varmiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: That same serves as the counter-force against horses; or armored elephants [against] horses, or armored horses [against elephants].

children.text: KAZ09.2.29/ kavacino rathā āvaraṇinaḥ pattayaś ca catur.aṅga.balasya pratibalam //
children.translated_text: Armored chariots, shielded infantry — these constitute the counter-force against a combined four-division army.

children.text:
KAZ09.2.30ab/ evaṃ bala.samuddānaṃ para.sainya.nivāraṇam /
KAZ09.2.30cd/ vibhavena sva.sainyānāṃ kuryād aṅga.vikalpaśaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
Thus, the mobilization of forces and the countering of the enemy's army
should be done by the [king's] resources, varying the composition of divisions.

children.text:
(paścāt.kopa.cintā - bāhya.abhyantara.prakṛti.kopa.pratīkārah)
KAZ09.3.01/ alpaḥ paścāt.kopo mahān purastāl.lābha iti alpaḥ paścāt.kopo garīyān //
children.translated_text:
(Deliberation on revolt in the rear — Remedies for revolt of internal and external constituent elements)
'A small revolt in the rear but a great gain in the front' — [even so,] the small revolt in the rear is more serious.

children.text: KAZ09.3.02/ alpaṃ paścāt.kopaṃ prayātassya dūṣya.amitra.āṭavikā hi sarvataḥ samedhayanti, prakṛti.kopo vā //
children.translated_text: For when one has marched out with even a small revolt in the rear, the corruptible elements, enemies, and forest-chiefs intensify it from all sides; or the constituent elements revolt.

children.text: KAZ09.3.03/ labdham api ca mahāntaṃ purastāl.lāham evaṃ.bhūte bhṛtya.mitra.kṣaya.vyayā grasante //
children.translated_text: And even a great gain in the front, in such a situation, is consumed by the loss and expenditure [incurred through] servants and allies.

children.text: KAZ09.3.04/ tasmāt sahasra.ekīyaḥ purastāl.lābhasya^ayogaḥ śata.ekīyo vā paścāt.kopa iti na yāyāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, if the gain in the front is [achievable only] at the cost of a thousand and the revolt in the rear at the cost of even a hundred — one should not march.

children.text: KAZ09.3.05/ sūcī.mukhā hy anarthā iti loka.pravādaḥ //
children.translated_text: For 'misfortunes are like needles in their point of entry' — as the popular saying goes.

children.text: KAZ09.3.06/ paścāt.kope sāma.dāna.bheda.daṇḍān prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: In a revolt in the rear, one should apply conciliation, gifts, sowing dissension, and force.

children.text: KAZ09.3.07/ purastāl.lābhe senā.patiṃ kumāraṃ vā daṇḍa.cāriṇaṃ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: For the gain in the front, one should appoint the general or a prince as the leader of the force.

children.text: KAZ09.3.08/ balavān vā rājā paścāt.kopa.avagraha.samarthaḥ purastāl.lābham ādātuṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, a powerful king who is capable of suppressing the revolt in the rear should march to seize the gain in the front.

children.text: KAZ09.3.09/ abhyantara.kopa.śaṅkāyāṃ śaṅkitān ādāya yāyāt, bāhya.kopa.śaṅkāyāṃ vā putra.dāram eṣām //
children.translated_text: When there is suspicion of internal revolt — one should march taking the suspects along; or, when there is suspicion of external revolt — [taking along] their wives and children.

children.text: KAZ09.3.10/ abhyantara.avagrahaṃ kṛtvā śūnya.pālam aneka.bala.vargam aneka.mukhyaṃ ca sthāpayitvā yāyāt, na vā yāyāt //
children.translated_text: Having suppressed the internal [revolt] and having stationed a guardian of the [home] territory with multiple divisions of troops and multiple chiefs — he should march; or he should not march.

children.text: KAZ09.3.11/ abhyantara.kopo bāhya.kopāt pāpīyān ity uktaṃ purastāt //
children.translated_text: That internal revolt is worse than external revolt has been stated previously.

children.text: KAZ09.3.12/ mantra.purohita.senā.pati.yuva.rājānām anyatama.kopo^abhyantara.kopaḥ //
children.translated_text: The revolt of any one of the counselors, chaplain, general, or heir-apparent constitutes internal revolt.

children.text: KAZ09.3.13/ tam ātma.doṣa.tyāgena para.śakty.aparādha.vaśena vā sādhayet //
children.translated_text: This should be remedied either by abandoning one's own faults or by [exploiting] the failings of the opponent's power.

children.text: KAZ09.3.14/ mahā.aparādhe^api purohite samrodhanam avasrāvaṇaṃ vā siddhiḥ, yuva.rāje samrodhanaṃ nigraho vā guṇavaty anyasmin sati putre //
children.translated_text: Even in a great offense — for the chaplain, the remedy is imprisonment or banishment; for the heir-apparent — imprisonment or restraint, if there is another son of merit.

children.text: KAZ09.3.15/ putraṃ bhrātaram anyaṃ vā kulyaṃ rāja.grāhiṇam utsāhena sādhayet, utsāha.abbhāve gṛhīta.anuvartana.saṃdhi.karmabhyām ari.saṃdhāna.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: A son, brother, or other member of the royal family who has seized [power] should be subdued through enterprise; in the absence of enterprise — through submission, compliance, and treaty-making, out of fear of his allying with the enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.3.16/ anyebhyas tad.vidhebhyo vā bhūmi.dānair viśvāsayed enam //
children.translated_text: Or one should win his confidence through grants of land to others of his kind.
