children.text: KAZ09.3.17/ tad.viśiṣṭaṃ svayaṃ.grāhaṃ daṇḍaṃ vā preṣayet, sāmanta.āṭavikān vā, tair vigṛhītam atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or one should dispatch against him a force superior [to his own], or one's own seizure-force, or neighboring and forest-chiefs; having engaged him in conflict with them, one should outmaneuver him.

children.text: KAZ09.3.18/ aparuddha.ādānaṃ pāragrāmikaṃ vā yogam ātiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text: Or, one should adopt the expedient of seizing what is not [yet] blocked, or the expedition across villages.

children.text: KAZ09.3.19/ etena mantra.senā.patī vyākhyātau //
children.translated_text: By this, the counselors and the general are explained.

children.text: KAZ09.3.20/ mantry.ādi.varjānām antar.amātyānām anyatama.kopo^antar.amātya.kopaḥ //
children.translated_text: The revolt of any one of the inner ministers — excluding the counselors and others — constitutes the internal-minister revolt.

children.text: KAZ09.3.21/ tatra^api yathā.arham upāyān prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: In that case too, one should apply the appropriate expedients.

children.text: KAZ09.3.22/ rāṣṭra.mukhya.anta.pāla.āṭavika.daṇḍa.upanatānām anyatama.kopo bāhya.kopaḥ //
children.translated_text: The revolt of any one of the district chiefs, border-guards, forest-chiefs, or those brought under the rod [of force] constitutes external revolt.

children.text: KAZ09.3.23/ tam anyonyena^avagrāhayet //
children.translated_text: This one should suppress through [setting] one against the other.

children.text: KAZ09.3.24/ atidurga.pratiṣṭabdhaṃ vā sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhānām anyatamena^avagrāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or, one strongly entrenched in a difficult fortress should be suppressed by any one of the neighboring chiefs, forest-chiefs, their kinsmen, or the captured [agents].

children.text: KAZ09.3.25/ mitreṇa^upagrāhayed vā yathā na^amitraṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, one should have him seized by an ally, so that he does not go over to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.3.26/ amitrād vā sattrī bhedayed enaṃ - "ayaṃ tvā yoga.puruṣaṃ manyamāno bhartary eva vikramayiṣyati, avāpta.artho daṇḍa.cāriṇam amitra.āṭavikeṣu kṛcchre vā prayāse yokṣyati, viputra.dāram ante vā vāsayiṣyati //
children.translated_text: Or, a secret agent from the enemy's side should create a split in him [saying]: 'This [enemy king] considers you a tool; once he has achieved his purpose, he will turn you against your own master; having gained his objective, he will assign you as leader of the force to campaign against forest-chiefs in difficult terrain;

children.text: KAZ09.3.27/ pratihata.vikramaṃ tvāṃ bhartary paṇyaṃ kariṣyati, tvayā vā saṃdhiṃ kṛtvā bhartāram eva prasādayiṣyati //
children.translated_text: or he will station you at the frontier, separated from wife and children; or, with your valor frustrated against the master, he will make merchandise of you; or, having made a treaty with you, he will go and conciliate your own master.

children.text: KAZ09.3.28/ mitram upakṛṣṭaṃ vā^asya gaccha" iti //
children.translated_text: Or — go to a well-disposed ally of his.'

children.text: KAZ09.3.29/ pratipannam iṣṭa.abhiprāyaiḥ pūjayet //
children.translated_text: One who accepts should be honored with fulfillment of his wishes.

children.text: KAZ09.3.30/ apratipannasya saṃśrayaṃ bhedayed "asau te yoga.puruṣaḥ praṇihitaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: For one who does not accept, his refuge should be broken: 'That man of yours is a planted secret agent.'

children.text: KAZ09.3.31/ sattrī ca^enam abhityakta.śāsanair ghātayet, gūḍha.puruṣair vā //
children.translated_text: And the secret agent, through those who have defected from his authority, should have him killed; or through covert agents.

children.text: KAZ09.3.32/ saha.prasthāyino vā^asya pravīra.puruṣān yathā.abhiprāya.karaṇena^āvāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or, [the king] should win over his best men among his followers through fulfillment of their desires.

children.text: KAZ09.3.33/ tena praṇihitān sattrī brūyāt //
children.translated_text: The secret agent should [then] report the [names of those] planted by him.

children.text: KAZ09.3.34/ iti siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the [method of] success.

children.text: KAZ09.3.35/ parasya ca^enān kopān utthāpayet, ātmanaś ca śamayet //
children.translated_text: And one should incite these revolts in the enemy, and pacify them in one's own [domain].

children.text: KAZ09.3.36/ yaḥ kopaṃ kartuṃ śamayituṃ vā śaktas tatra^upajāpaḥ kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text: Where [an enemy agent] is capable of inciting or pacifying a revolt — there, counter-subversion should be employed.

children.text: KAZ09.3.37/ yaḥ satya.saṃdhaḥ śaktaḥ karmaṇi phala.avāptau ca^anugrahītuṃ vinipāte ca trātuṃ tatra pratijāpaḥ kāryaḥ, tarkayitavyaś ca kalyāṇa.buddhir uta^aho śaṭha iti //
children.translated_text: Where one is true to his word, capable of supporting [others] in action and in the acquisition of rewards, and of protecting in downfall — there, counter-subversion should be employed; and one should ascertain whether he is of benevolent intent or deceitful.

children.text:
KAZ09.3.38/ śaṭho hi bāhyo^abhyantaram evam upajapati - "bhartāraṃ cedd hatvā māṃ pratipādayiṣyati śatru.vadho bhūmi.lābhaś ca me dvividho lābho bhaviṣyati, atha vā śatrur enam āhaniṣyati^iti hata.bandhu.pakṣas tulya.doṣa.daṇḍena^udvignaś ca me bhūyān akṛtya.pakṣo bhaviṣyati, tad.vidhe vā^anyasminn api śaṅkito bhaviṣyati, anyam anyaṃ ca^asya mukhyam
abhityakta.śāsanena ghātayiṣyāmi" iti //
children.translated_text:
For a deceitful external [agent] subverts an internal [official] thus: 'If he kills his master and delivers [the kingdom] to me, I gain twofold: the destruction of the enemy and the acquisition of land. Or, if the enemy [master] kills him, then with his kinsmen and faction killed, terrified by the punishment for the shared offense, a greater faction of his will become opposed [to the master]; or [the master] will become suspicious of any other similar [official],
and I shall have each successive chief of his killed through agents who defect from his authority.'

children.text:
KAZ09.3.39/ abhyantaro vā śaṭho bāhyam evam upajapati - "kośam asya hariṣyāmi, daṇḍaṃ vā^asya haniṣyāmi, duṣṭaṃ vā bhartāram anena ghātayiṣyāmi, pratipannaṃ bāhyam amitra.āṭavikeṣu vikramayiṣyāmi "cakram asya sajyatām, vairam asya prasajyatām, tataḥ sva.adhīno me bhaviṣyati, tato bhartāram eva prasādayiṣyāmi, svayaṃ vā rājyaṃ grahīṣyāmiṇ" baddhvā vā bāhya.bhūmiṃ
bhartṛ.bhūmiṃ ca^ubhayam avāpsyāmi, viruddhaṃ vā^āvāhayitvā bāhyaṃ viśvastaṃ ghātayiṣyāmi, śūnyaṃ vā^asya mūlaṃ hariṣyāmi" iti //
children.translated_text:
Or, a deceitful internal [official] subverts an external [rebel] thus: 'I shall steal his treasury, or I shall destroy his army, or I shall have his corrupt master killed by him. Having committed the external [rebel], I shall deploy him against the enemy and forest-chiefs: "Let his resources be exhausted, let his hostility be prolonged — then he will become subject to me; and then I shall conciliate my own master, or I shall seize the kingdom myself."
Or, having bound [the rebel], I shall obtain both the external territory and my master's territory; or, having lured back the defector and gained [his] trust, I shall have the external [rebel] killed; or I shall plunder his unguarded base.'

children.text: KAZ09.3.40/ kalyāṇa.buddhis tu saha.jīvy artham upajapati //
children.translated_text: But one of benevolent intent subverts [the rebel] for the purpose of living together [in peace].

children.text: KAZ09.3.41/ kalyāṇa.buddhinā saṃdadhīta, śaṭhaṃ "tathā" iti pratigṛhya^atisaṃdadhyāt - iti //
children.translated_text: With one of benevolent intent, one should make a treaty; with the deceitful one, saying 'Yes,' one should outmaneuver him.

children.text:
KAZ09.3.42ab/ evam upalabhya - pare parebhyaḥ sve svebhyaḥ sve parebhyaḥ svataḥ pare /
KAZ09.3.42cd/ rakṣyāḥ svebhyaḥ parebhyaś ca nityam ātmā vipaścitā //E
children.translated_text:
Thus, having ascertained — the enemy's [agents subverting] the enemy's [people], one's own [agents subverting] one's own, one's own [subverting] the enemy's, and the enemy's [subverting] one's own —
the wise [king] should always protect himself from his own and from others.

children.text:
(kṣaya.vyaya.lābha.viparimarśah)
KAZ09.4.01/ yugya.puruṣa.apacayaḥ kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Deliberation on loss, expenditure, and gain)
The diminution of draft animals and men is loss.

children.text: KAZ09.4.02/ hiraṇya.dhānya.apacayo vyayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The diminution of gold and grain is expenditure.

children.text: KAZ09.4.03/ tābhyāṃ bahu.guṇa.viśiṣṭe lābhe yāyāt //
children.translated_text: One should march when the gain is many times greater than both of these.

children.text: KAZ09.4.04/ ādeyaḥ pratyādeyaḥ prasādakaḥ prakopako hrasva.kālas tanu.kṣayo^alpa.vyayo mahān vṛddhy.udayaḥ kalyo dharmyaḥ purogaś ca^iti lābha.sampat //
children.translated_text: Seizable, recoverable, conciliatory, provocative, of short duration, involving small loss, involving little expenditure, great, productive of growth, healthy, righteous, and leading [to more gains] — these are the excellences of gain.

children.text: KAZ09.4.05/ suprāpya.anupālyaḥ pareṣām apratyādeya ity ādeyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Easily attainable, not needing [constant] protection, and not recoverable by others — this is 'seizable.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.06/ viparyaye pratyādeyaḥ //
children.translated_text: The opposite is 'recoverable' [by the enemy].

children.text: KAZ09.4.07/ tam ādadānas tatrastho vā vināśaṃ prāpnoti //
children.translated_text: One who seizes it [i.e., a recoverable gain], whether stationed there or not, meets destruction.

children.text:
KAZ09.4.08/ yadi vā paśyet "pratyādeyam ādāya kośa.daṇḍa.nicaya.rakṣā.vidhānāny avasrāvayiṣyāmi, khani.dravya.hasti.vana.setu.bandha.vaṇik.pathān uddhṛta.sārān kariṣyāmi, prakṛtīr asya karśayiṣyāmi, apavāhayiṣyāmi, āyogena^ārādhayiṣyāmi vā, tāḥ paraṃ pratiyogena kopayiṣyati, pratipakṣe vā^asya paṇyam enaṃ kariṣyāmi, mitram aparuddhaṃ vā^asya pratipādayiṣyāmi,
mitrasya svasya vā deśasya pīḍām atrasthas taskarebhyaḥ parebhyaś ca pratikariṣyāmi, mitram āśrayaṃ vā^asya vaiguṇyaṃ grāhayiṣyāmi, tad amitra.viraktaṃ tat.kulīnaṃ pratipatsyate, satkṛtya vā^asmai bhūmiṃ dāsyāmi iti
saṃhita.samutthitaṃ mitraṃ me cirāya bhaviṣyati" iti pratyādeyam api lābham ādadīta //
KAZ09.4.09/ ity ādeya.pratyādeyau vyākhyātau //
children.translated_text: Thus the seizable and the recoverable are explained.

children.text: KAZ09.4.10/ adhārmikād dhārmikasya lābho labhyamānaḥ sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ ca prasādako bhavati //
children.translated_text: A gain obtained from an unrighteous [source] by a righteous [king] — when obtained — becomes pleasing to both one's own [people] and others.

children.text: KAZ09.4.11/ viparītaḥ prakopaka iti //
children.translated_text: The opposite is provocative.

children.text: KAZ09.4.12/ mantriṇām upadeśāl lābho^alabhyamānaḥ kopako bhavati "ayam asmābhiḥ kṣaya.vyayau grāhitaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: A gain that is not obtained despite the counsel of ministers becomes provocative [of their discontent]: 'We have been subjected to loss and expenditure by him.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.13/ dūṣya.mantriṇām anādarāl lābho labhyamānaḥ kopako bhavati "siddha.artho^ayam asmān vināśayiṣyati" iti //
children.translated_text: A gain that is obtained despite the disregard of corrupt ministers becomes provocative: 'Having achieved his purpose, he will destroy us.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.14/ viparītaḥ prasādakaḥ //
children.translated_text: The opposite is conciliatory.

children.text:
KAZ09.4.15/ iti prasādaka.kopakau vyākhyātau
KAZ09.4.16/ gamana.mātra.sādhyatvād hrasva.kālah
KAZ09.4.17/ mantra.sādhyatvāt tanu.kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
Thus the conciliatory and the provocative are explained.
One achievable merely by marching is 'of short duration.'
One achievable by counsel [alone] involves 'small loss.'

children.text:
KAZ09.4.18/ bhakta.mātra.vyayatvād alpa.vyayah
KAZ09.4.19/ tadātva.vaipulyān mahān //
children.translated_text:
One requiring only the expenditure of provisions involves 'little expenditure.'
One that is immediate and abundant is 'great.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.20/ artha.anubandhakatvād vṛddhy.udayaḥ //
children.translated_text: One that leads to further material gain is 'productive of growth.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.21/ nirābādhakatvāt kalyaḥ //
children.translated_text: One that causes no harassment is 'healthy.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.22/ praśasta.upādānād dharmyaḥ //
children.translated_text: One obtained from praiseworthy means is 'righteous.'

children.text: KAZ09.4.23/ sāmavāyikānām anirbandha.gāmitvāt purogaḥ - iti //
children.translated_text: One that does not lead to binding obligations toward allies is 'leading [to more gains].'

children.text: KAZ09.4.24/ tulye lābhe deśa.kālau śakty.upāyau priya.apriyau java.ajavau sāmīpya.viprakarṣau tadātva.anubandhau sāratva.sātatye bāhulya.bāhu.guṇye ca vimṛśya bahu.guṇa.yuktaṃ lābham ādadīta //
children.translated_text: When gains are equal, one should consider: place and time, power and means, the pleasant and the unpleasant, speed and slowness, proximity and distance, immediacy and future consequence, essential quality and constancy, number and multiplicity — and should seize the gain endowed with the most advantages.

children.text: KAZ09.4.25/ lābha.vighnāḥ - kāmaḥ kopaḥ sādhvasaṃ kāruṇyaṃ hrīr anārya.bhāvo mānaḥ sānukrośatā para.loka.apekṣā dhārmikatvam atyāgitvaṃ dainyam asūyā hasta.gata.avamāno daurātmyam aviśvāso bhayam apratīkāraḥ śīta.uṣṇa.varṣāṇām ākṣamyaṃ maṅgala.tithi.nakṣatra.iṣṭitvam iti //
children.translated_text: Obstacles to gain: desire, anger, timidity, compassion, modesty, ignoble disposition, pride, sentimentality, preoccupation with the next world, excessive righteousness, unwillingness to give up [what one has], dejection, envy, contempt for what is at hand, wickedness, distrust, fear, failure to counteract, intolerance of cold, heat, and rain, and devotion to auspicious days, lunar dates, and asterisms.

children.text:
KAZ09.4.26ab/ nakṣatram ati pṛcchantaṃ bālam artho^ativartate /
KAZ09.4.26cd/ artho hy arthasya nakṣatraṃ kiṃ kariṣyanti tārakāḥ //
children.translated_text:
Fortune passes by the child who keeps asking about asterisms;
for wealth itself is the asterism of wealth — what will the stars do?

children.text:
KAZ09.4.27ab/ na^adhanāḥ prāpnuvanty arthān narā yatna.śatair api /
KAZ09.4.27cd/ arthair arthā prabadhyante gajāḥ prajigajair iva //E
children.translated_text:
Men who have no resources do not obtain wealth even with a hundred efforts;
riches are attracted by riches, as elephants are [attracted] by decoy elephants.

children.text:
(bāhya.abhyantarāś ca^āpadah)
KAZ09.5.01/ saṃdhy.ādīnām ayathā.uddeśa.avasthāpanam apanayaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(External and internal calamities)
The misapplication of treaties and the like, contrary to the prescribed guidelines, is misgovernment (<s>apanaya</s>).

children.text: KAZ09.5.02/ tasmād āpadaḥ sambhavanti //
children.translated_text: From that, calamities arise.

children.text: KAZ09.5.03/ bāhya.utpattir abhyantara.pratijāpā, abhyantara.utpattir bāhya.pratijāpā, bāhya.utpattir bāhya.pratijāpā, abhyantara.utpattir abhyantara.pratijāpā - ity āpadaḥ //
children.translated_text: An external uprising with internal instigation, an internal uprising with external instigation, an external uprising with external instigation, an internal uprising with internal instigation — these are the [four types of] calamity.

children.text: KAZ09.5.04/ yatra bāhyā abhyantara.anupajapanti, abhyantarā vā bāhyān, tatra.ubhaya.yoge pratijapataḥ siddhir viśeṣavatī //
children.translated_text: Where externals instigate internals, or internals instigate externals — there, through the combined method, the counter-instigator achieves a distinctly superior result.

children.text: KAZ09.5.05/ suvyājā hi pratijapitāro bhavanti, na^upajapitāraḥ //
children.translated_text: For counter-instigators have plausible pretexts, while instigators do not.

children.text: KAZ09.5.06/ teṣu praśānteṣu na^anyān^śaknuyur upajapitum upajapitāraḥ //
children.translated_text: When these [original instigators] have been pacified, the instigators cannot instigate others.

children.text: KAZ09.5.07/ kṛcchra.upajāpā hi bāhyānām abhyantarās teṣām itare vā //
children.translated_text: For the instigators of externals among internals, and vice versa, are difficult to instigate.

children.text: KAZ09.5.08/ mahataś ca prayatnasya vadhaḥ pareṣām, artha.anubandhaś ca^ātmana iti //
children.translated_text: And a great effort [results in] the death of the enemies and the continuation of interest for oneself.

children.text: KAZ09.5.09/ abhyantareṣu pratijapatsu sāma.dāne prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: When internals are counter-instigating, one should employ conciliation and gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.5.10/ sthāna.māna.karma sāntvam //
children.translated_text: Position, honor, and assignment of duties constitute conciliation.

children.text: KAZ09.5.11/ anugraha.parihārau karmasv āyogo vā dānam //
children.translated_text: Granting favors and exemptions in affairs, or [direct material] provision, constitutes gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.5.12/ bāhyeṣu pratijapatsu bheda.daṇḍau prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: When externals are counter-instigating, one should employ dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ09.5.13/ sattriṇo mitra.vyañjanā vā bāhyānāṃ cāram eṣāṃ brūyuḥ "ayaṃ vo rājā dūṣya.vyañjanair atisaṃdhātu.kāmaḥ, budhyadhvam" iti //
children.translated_text: Secret agents or those disguised as friends should tell the externals about their [leader's] espionage activities: 'Your king intends to outmaneuver you through agents disguised as corruptibles; be aware.'

children.text: KAZ09.5.14/ dūṣyeṣu vā dūṣya.vyañjanāḥ praṇihitā dūṣyān bāhyair bhedayeyuḥ, bāhyān vā dūṣyaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, among the disloyal, agents disguised as the disloyal should sow dissension between the disloyal and the externals, or between the externals and the disloyal.

children.text: KAZ09.5.15/ dūṣyān anupraviṣṭā vā tīkṣṇāḥ śastra.rasābhyāṃ hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, ruthless agents who have infiltrated the disloyal should kill them with weapons and poison.

children.text: KAZ09.5.16/ āhūya vā bāhyān ghātayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, having summoned the externals, they should have them killed.

children.text: KAZ09.5.17/ yatra bāhyā bāhyān upajapanti, abhyantarān abhyantarā vā, tatra^ekānta.yoga upajapituḥ siddhir viśeṣavatī //
children.translated_text: Where externals instigate externals, or internals instigate internals — there, through the one-sided method, the instigator achieves a distinctly superior result.

children.text: KAZ09.5.18/ doṣa.śuddhau hi dūṣyā na vidyante //
children.translated_text: For when the source of corruption is purified, the corruptible elements do not exist.

children.text: KAZ09.5.19/ dūṣya.śuddhau hi doṣaḥ punar anyān dūṣayati //
children.translated_text: When the corruptible elements are purified, the source of corruption corrupts others again.

children.text: KAZ09.5.20/ tasmād bāhyeṣu^upajapatsu bheda.daṇḍau prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Therefore, when externals are instigating, one should employ dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ09.5.21/ sattriṇo mitra.vyañjanā vā brūyuḥ "ayaṃ vo rājā svayam ādātu.kāmaḥ, vigṛhītāḥ sthānena rājñā, budhyadhvam" iti //
children.translated_text: Secret agents or those disguised as friends should say: 'Your king himself wishes to seize [your possessions]; you are at odds with the king over your positions; be aware.'

children.text: KAZ09.5.22/ pratijapitur vā dūta.daṇḍān anupraviṣṭās tīkṣṇāḥ śastra.rasa.ādibhir eṣāṃ chidreṣu prahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, ruthless agents who have infiltrated the counter-instigator's envoy-forces should strike at their vulnerabilities with weapons, poison, and the like.

children.text: KAZ09.5.23/ tataḥ sattriṇaḥ pratijapitāram abhiśaṃseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the secret agents should accuse the counter-instigator.

children.text: KAZ09.5.24/ abhyantarān abhyantareṣu^upajapatsu yathā.arham upāyaṃ prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: When internals instigate internals, one should employ the appropriate method.

children.text: KAZ09.5.25/ tuṣṭa.liṅgam atuṣṭaṃ viparītaṃ vā sāma prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: One who shows signs of contentment but is discontented, or the reverse — one should apply conciliation.

children.text: KAZ09.5.26/ śauca.sāmarthya.apadeśena vyasana.abhyudaya.avekṣaṇena vā pratipūjanam iti dānam //
children.translated_text: Honoring [them] on the pretext of their integrity and ability, or by attending to their misfortunes and successes — this constitutes gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.5.27/ mitra.vyañjano vā brūyād etān "citta.jñāna.artham upadhāsyati vo rājā, tad asya^ākhyātavyam iti //
children.translated_text: Or one disguised as a friend should tell them: 'The king will test you through trials of loyalty; you must report this [to him].'

children.text: KAZ09.5.28/ parasparād vā bhedayed enān "asau ca^asau ca vo rājany evam upajapati" - iti bhedaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or one should sow dissension among them mutually: 'So-and-so instigates your king thus' — this is dissension.

children.text: KAZ09.5.29/ dāṇḍakarmikavac ca daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: And force is [applied] as with the staff-wielding enforcer.

children.text: KAZ09.5.30/ etāsāṃ catasṛṇām āpadām abhyantarām eva pūrvaṃ sādhayet //
children.translated_text: Of these four types of calamity, one should first resolve the internal one.

children.text: KAZ09.5.31/ ahi.bhayād abhyantara.kopo bāhya.kopāt pāpīyān ity uktaṃ purastād //
children.translated_text: For it has been said earlier that internal revolt, like the fear of a snake [within the household], is worse than external revolt.

children.text:
KAZ09.5.32ab/ pūrvāṃ pūrvāṃ vijānīyāl laghvīm āpadam āpadām /
KAZ09.5.32cd/ utthitāṃ balavadbhyo vā gurvīṃ laghvīṃ viparyaye //E
children.translated_text:
One should recognize among calamities that each earlier one is lighter;
but one arising from powerful [enemies] is grave, and in the reverse case, light.

children.text:
(dūṣya.śatru.samyuktāh <āpadah>)
KAZ09.6.01/ dūṣyebhyaḥ śatrubhyaś ca dvividhā śuddhā //
children.translated_text:
(Calamities connected with the disloyal and enemies)
From the disloyal and from enemies, the purification is twofold.

children.text: KAZ09.6.02/ dūṣya.śuddhāyāṃ paureṣu jānapadeṣu vā daṇḍa.varjān upāyān prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: In the purification from the disloyal — among townspeople and countryfolk — one should employ the methods other than force.

children.text: KAZ09.6.03/ daṇḍo hi mahā.jane kṣeptum aśakyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For force cannot be cast upon a multitude.

children.text: KAZ09.6.04/ kṣipto vā taṃ ca^arthaṃ na kuryāt, anyaṃ ca^anartham utpādayet //
children.translated_text: If cast, it would not achieve that purpose and would generate other harm.

children.text: KAZ09.6.05/ mukhyeṣu tv eṣāṃ dāṇḍa.karmikavac ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: But against their leaders, one should proceed as with the staff-wielding enforcer.

children.text: KAZ09.6.06/ śatru.śuddhāyāṃ yataḥ śatruḥ pradhānaḥ kāryo vā tataḥ sāma.ādibhiḥ siddhiṃ lipseta //
children.translated_text: In the purification from enemies — from whichever direction the enemy is chief or should be made chief — from that [direction] one should seek success through conciliation and the other [methods].

children.text: KAZ09.6.07/ svāminy āyattā pradhāna.siddhiḥ, mantriṣv āyattā^āyatta.siddhiḥ, ubhaya.āyattā pradhāna.āyatta.siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Success dependent on the king is primary success; success dependent on the ministers is dependent success; success dependent on both is success dependent on the primary.

children.text: KAZ09.6.08/ dūṣya.adūṣyāṇām āmiśritatvād āmiśrā //
children.translated_text: Because of the mixture of the disloyal and the non-disloyal — it is mixed.

children.text: KAZ09.6.09/ āmiśrāyām adūṣyataḥ siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: In a mixed [situation], success [comes] from the non-disloyal.

children.text: KAZ09.6.10/ ālambana.abhāve hy ālambitā na vidyante //
children.translated_text: For in the absence of a support, those who take support do not exist.

children.text: KAZ09.6.11/ mitra.amitrāṇām ekī.bhāvāt para.miśrā //
children.translated_text: Because of the merging into one of allies and enemies — it is a mixed-with-the-enemy [situation].

children.text: KAZ09.6.12/ para.miśrāyāṃ mitrataḥ siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: In a situation mixed with the enemy, success [comes] from the ally.

children.text: KAZ09.6.13/ sukaro hi mitreṇa saṃdhiḥ, na^amitreṇa^iti //
children.translated_text: For a treaty with an ally is easy, not with an enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.6.14/ mitraṃ cen na saṃdhim icched abhīkṣṇam upajapet //
children.translated_text: If the ally does not desire a treaty, one should instigate him repeatedly.

children.text: KAZ09.6.15/ tataḥ sattribhir amitrād bhedayitvā mitraṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: Then, having detached [him] from the enemy through secret agents, one should gain the ally.

children.text: KAZ09.6.16/ mitra.saṃghasya vā yo^anta.sthāyī taṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: Or, of the ally-group, one should gain whoever is on the fringe.

children.text: KAZ09.6.17/ anta.sthāyini labdhe madhya.sthāyino bhidyante //
children.translated_text: When the fringe-member has been gained, the core members are divided.

children.text: KAZ09.6.18/ madhya.sthāyinaṃ vā labheta //
children.translated_text: Or one should gain the core member.

children.text: KAZ09.6.19/ madhya.sthāyini labdhe na^anta.sthāyinaḥ saṃhanyante //
children.translated_text: When the core member has been gained, the fringe members do not unite.

children.text: KAZ09.6.20/ yathā ca^eṣām āśraya.bhedas tān upāyān prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: And whatever methods [would lead to] the breaking of their [mutual] support — those methods one should employ.

children.text: KAZ09.6.21/ dhārmikaṃ jāti.kula.śruta.vṛtta.stavena sambandhena pūrveṣāṃ traikālya.upakārān apakārābhyāṃ vā sāntvayet //
children.translated_text: One should conciliate the righteous one through praise of his caste, family, learning, and conduct, through kinship, and by recounting the past services of ancestors over three generations — or through [pointing out] the two [consequences of] harm.

children.text: KAZ09.6.22/ nivṛtta.utsāhaṃ vigraha.śrāntaṃ pratihata.upāyaṃ kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ pravāsena ca^upataptaṃ śaucena^anyaṃ lipsamānam anyasmād vā śaṅkamānaṃ maitrī.pradhānaṃ vā kalyāṇa.buddhiṃ sāmnā sādhayet //
children.translated_text: One whose enterprise has ceased, who is weary of conflict, whose stratagems have failed, who is afflicted by losses, expenditures, and absence [from home], one seeking another [alliance] out of integrity, or one apprehensive of another, one whose chief [disposition] is friendship, one of good intentions — one should win over through conciliation.

children.text: KAZ09.6.23/ lubdhaṃ kṣīṇaṃ vā tapasvi.mukhya.avasthāpanā.pūrvaṃ dānena sādhayet //
children.translated_text: The greedy or the impoverished — having first established ascetics and chiefs — one should win over through gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.6.24/ tat pañca.vidhaṃ - deya.visargo gṛhīta.anuvartanam ātta.pratidānaṃ sva.dravya.dānam apūrvaṃ para.sveṣu svayaṃ.grāha.dānaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: That [gift] is of five kinds: release of what is to be given; continuation of what has been received; return of what has been taken; giving of one's own resources without precedent; and self-help granting of rights over others' properties.

children.text: KAZ09.6.25/ iti dāna.karma //
children.translated_text: This is the operation of gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.6.26/ paraspara.dveṣa.vaira.bhūmi.haraṇa.śaṅkitam ato^anyatamena bhedayet //
children.translated_text: One who is apprehensive through mutual hatred, enmity, or land-seizure — one should divide by any one of these [causes].

children.text: KAZ09.6.27/ bhīruṃ vā pratighātena "kṛta.saṃdhir eṣa tvayi karma.kariṣyati, mitram asya nisṛṣṭam, saṃdhau vā na^abhyantaraḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or one who is timid, through counter-threats: 'This one has made a treaty and will act against you; his ally has been empowered; or you are not part of the treaty.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.28/ yasya vā sva.deśād anya.deśād vā paṇyāni paṇya.agāratayā^āgaccheyuḥ tāni asya "yātavyāl labdhāni" iti sattriṇaś cārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, to one whose merchandise comes from his own or another country to warehouses — the secret agents should circulate [the rumor]: 'This was obtained from the enemy to be attacked.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.29/ bahulī.bhūte śāsanam abhityaktena preṣayet "etat te paṇyaṃ paṇya.agāraṃ vā mayā te preṣitam, sāmavāyikeṣu vikramasva, apagaccha vā, tataḥ paṇa.śeṣam avāpsyasi" iti //
children.translated_text: When [the merchandise] has accumulated, one should send a message through a [seemingly] runaway: 'This merchandise or warehouse has been sent to you by me; attack among the confederates, or depart; afterwards you will receive the balance [payment].'

children.text: KAZ09.6.30/ tataḥ sattriṇaḥ pareṣu grāhayeyuḥ "etad ari.pradattam" iti //
children.translated_text: Then the secret agents should have the others seize [it, saying]: 'This was given by the enemy.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.31/ śatru.prakhyātaṃ vā paṇyam avijñātaṃ vijigīṣuṃ gacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, merchandise known to be from the enemy [but] not identified [as such] should reach the conqueror.

children.text: KAZ09.6.32/ tad asya vaidehaka.vyañjanāḥ śatru.mukhyeṣu vikrīṇīran //
children.translated_text: Those disguised as traders should sell it among the chiefs of the enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.6.33/ tataḥ sattriṇaḥ pareṣu grāhayeyuḥ "etat paṇyam ari.pradattam" iti //
children.translated_text: Then the secret agents should have the others seize [it, saying]: 'This merchandise was given by the enemy.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.34/ mahā.aparādhān artha.mānābhyām upagṛhya vā śastra.rasa.agnibhir amitre praṇidadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having won over great criminals with wealth and honors, one should deploy them among the enemy with weapons, poison, and fire.

children.text: KAZ09.6.35/ atha^ekam amātyaṃ niṣpātayet //
children.translated_text: Then one should let one minister escape.

children.text: KAZ09.6.36/ tasya putra.dāram upagṛhya rātrau hatam iti khyāpayet //
children.translated_text: Having seized his son and wife, one should announce that he was killed at night.

children.text: KAZ09.6.37/ atha^amātyaḥ śatros tān eka.ekaśaḥ prarūpayet //
children.translated_text: Then the minister should identify the enemy's [chiefs] one by one [to the conqueror].

children.text: KAZ09.6.38/ te ced yathā.uktaṃ kuryur na ca^enān grāhayet //
children.translated_text: If they act as described, one should not seize them [yet].

children.text: KAZ09.6.39/ aśaktimato vā grāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should seize [only] those who lack power.

children.text: KAZ09.6.40/ āpta.bhāva.upagato mukhyād asya^ātmānaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ kathayet //
children.translated_text: One who has gained the trust [of a chief], in a position of confidence, should tell the chief that the [king] himself needs to be protected [from a plot].

children.text: KAZ09.6.41/ atha^amitra.śāsanaṃ mukhya.upaghātāya preṣitam ubhaya.vetano grāhayet //
children.translated_text: Then one should have a double agent seize a message from the enemy sent for the destruction of the chief.

children.text: KAZ09.6.42/ utsāha.śaktimato vā preṣayet "amuṣya rājyaṃ gṛhāṇa, yathā.asthito naḥ saṃdhiḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or one should send [a message] to one who has the power and enterprise: 'Seize the kingdom of so-and-so; our treaty stands as established.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.43/ tataḥ sattriṇaḥ pareṣu grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the secret agents should have the others seize [the message].

children.text: KAZ09.6.44/ ekasya skandha.āvāraṃ vīvadham āsāraṃ vā ghātayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should destroy the camp, the supplies, or the reinforcements of one [chief].

children.text: KAZ09.6.45/ itareṣu maitrīṃ bruvāṇāḥ "tvam eteṣāṃ ghātayitavyaḥ" ity upajapeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: To the others, declaring friendship, they should instigate: 'You are to be killed by these [men].'

children.text: KAZ09.6.46/ yasya vā pravīra.puruṣo hastī hayo vā mriyeta gūḍha.puruṣair hanyeta hriyeta vā sattriṇaḥ paraspara.upahataṃ brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, when the champion warrior, elephant, or horse of any one [chief] dies, is secretly killed, or is stolen by hidden agents — the secret agents should say it was done mutually [by the other chiefs].

children.text: KAZ09.6.47/ tataḥ śāsanam abhiśastasya preṣayet "bhūyaḥ kuru tataḥ paṇa.śeeṣam avāpsyasi" iti //
children.translated_text: Then one should send a message to the accused: 'Do more; afterwards you will receive the balance [payment].'

children.text: KAZ09.6.48/ tad ubhaya.vetanā grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Double agents should have [this message] seized.

children.text: KAZ09.6.49/ bhinneṣv anyatamaṃ labheta //
children.translated_text: When they are divided, one should gain any one of them.

children.text: KAZ09.6.50/ tena senā.pati.kumāra.daṇḍa.cāriṇo vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, generals, princes, and military commanders are explained.

children.text: KAZ09.6.51/ sāṃdhikaṃ ca bhedaṃ prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: And one should employ dissension arising from treaties.

children.text: KAZ09.6.52/ iti bheda.karma //
children.translated_text: This is the operation of dissension.

children.text: KAZ09.6.53/ tīkṣṇam utsāhinaṃ vyasaninaṃ sthita.śatruṃ vā gūḍha.puruṣāḥ śastra.agni.rasa.ādibhiḥ sādhayeyuḥ, saukaryato vā teṣām anyatamaḥ //
children.translated_text: One who is fierce, enterprising, addicted to vices, or one who has a standing enemy — hidden agents should dispatch with weapons, fire, poison, and the like; or any one of those [agents], according to ease.

children.text: KAZ09.6.54/ tīkṣṇo hy ekaḥ śastra.rasa.agnibhiḥ sādhayet //
children.translated_text: For a single ruthless agent can accomplish [the task] with weapons, poison, or fire.

children.text: KAZ09.6.55/ ayaṃ sarva.saṃdoha.karma viśiṣṭaṃ vā karoti //
children.translated_text: This one performs the task of the entire collective, or a special [task].

children.text: KAZ09.6.56/ ity upāya.catur.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the fourfold set of methods.

children.text: KAZ09.6.57/ pūrvaḥ pūrvaś ca^asya laghiṣṭhaḥ //
children.translated_text: And each earlier one is the lightest.

children.text: KAZ09.6.58/ sāntvam eka.guṇam //
children.translated_text: Conciliation is single-fold.

children.text: KAZ09.6.59/ dānaṃ dvi.guṇaṃ sāntva.pūrvam //
children.translated_text: Gifts are twofold, preceded by conciliation.

children.text: KAZ09.6.60/ bhedas tri.guṇaḥ sāntva.dāna.pūrvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Dissension is threefold, preceded by conciliation and gifts.

children.text: KAZ09.6.61/ daṇḍaś catur.guṇaḥ sāntva.dāna.bheda.pūrvaḥ //
children.translated_text: Force is fourfold, preceded by conciliation, gifts, and dissension.

children.text: KAZ09.6.62/ ity abhiyuñjāneṣu^uktam //
children.translated_text: This has been stated for [those who are] attacking.

children.text: KAZ09.6.63/ sva.bhūmiṣṭheṣu tu ta eva^upāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: But for those [enemies] stationed on one's own soil, the same methods [apply].

children.text: KAZ09.6.64/ viśeṣas tu //
children.translated_text: But there is a distinction.

children.text: KAZ09.6.65/ sva.bhūmiṣṭhānām anyatamasya paṇya.agārair abhijñātān dūta.mukhyān abhīkṣṇaṃ preṣayet //
children.translated_text: To any one of those stationed on one's own soil, one should repeatedly send well-known envoy-chiefs through warehouses.

children.text: KAZ09.6.66/ ta enaṃ saṃdhau para.hiṃsāyāṃ vā yojayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should engage him in a treaty or in harming the enemy.

children.text: KAZ09.6.67/ apratipadyamānaṃ "kṛto naḥ saṃdhiḥ" ity āvedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If he does not accept, they should report: 'Our treaty is made.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.68/ tam itareṣām ubhaya.vetanāḥ saṃkrāmayeyuḥ "ayaṃ vo rājā duṣṭaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Double agents should then convey to the others: 'Your king is corrupt.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.69/ yasya vā yasmād bhayaṃ vairaṃ dveṣo vā taṃ tasmād bhedayeyuḥ "ayaṃ te śatruṇā saṃdhatte, purā tvām atisaṃdhatte, kṣiprataraṃ saṃdhīyasva, nigrahe ca^asya prayatasva" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, whichever one has fear, enmity, or hatred toward whomever — [agents] should divide him from that one [saying]: 'This one is making a treaty with your enemy; before he outmaneuvers you, make a treaty quickly and strive for his suppression.'

children.text: KAZ09.6.70/ āvāha.vivāhābhyāṃ vā kṛtvā samyogam asamyuktān bhedayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having created an alliance through marriage ties, one should divide those who are not [so] united.

children.text: KAZ09.6.71/ sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhaiś ca^eṣāṃ rājyāni ghātayet, sārtha.vraja.aṭavīr vā, daṇḍaṃ vā^abhisṛtam //
children.translated_text: And through feudatories, forest chiefs, members of their own families, and those excluded [from succession], one should attack their kingdoms — or their caravans, herds, and forest areas — or their marching army.

children.text: KAZ09.6.72/ paraspara.apāśrayāś ca^eṣāṃ jāti.saṃghāś chidreṣu prahareyuḥ, gūḍhāś ca^agni.rasa.śastreṇa //
children.translated_text: And their caste-guilds, mutually supportive, should strike at their vulnerabilities; and hidden agents with fire, poison, and weapons.

children.text:
KAZ09.6.73ab/ vītaṃsa.gilavac ca^arīn yogair ācaritaiḥ śaṭhaḥ /
KAZ09.6.73cd/ ghātayet para.miśrāyāṃ viśvāsena^āmiṣeṇa ca //E
children.translated_text:
And like the fowler and the fish-swallower, the cunning one should destroy enemies through practiced stratagems
in a situation mixed with the enemy — through trust and bait.

children.text:
(artha.anartha.samśaya.yuktāh <āpadah> - tāsām upāya.vikalpajāh siddhayah)
KAZ09.7.01/ kāma.ādir utsekaḥ svāḥ prakṛtīḥ kopayati, apanayo bāhyāḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Calamities involving gain, loss, and doubt — successes arising from varieties of expedients)
Excitement born of desire and the like angers one's own subjects; misgovernment angers external [parties].

children.text: KAZ09.7.02/ tad ubhayam āsurī vṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: Both together constitute the demonic mode of conduct.

children.text: KAZ09.7.03/ sva.jana.vikāraḥ kopaḥ //
children.translated_text: Fury among one's own people constitutes sedition.

children.text: KAZ09.7.04/ para.vṛddhi.hetuṣu āpad.artho^anarthaḥ saṃśaya iti //
children.translated_text: With respect to the causes of the enemy's growth — [what appears to be] gain is [in fact] loss, and [what seems] doubtful [is likewise problematic].

children.text: KAZ09.7.05/ yo^arthaḥ śatru.vṛddhim aprāptaḥ karoti, prāptaḥ pratyādeyaḥ pareṣāṃ bhavati, prāpyamāṇo vā kṣaya.vyaya.udayo bhavati, sa bhavaty āpad.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: A gain which, when not obtained, promotes the enemy's growth; which, when obtained, becomes recoverable by the enemy; or which, in the process of being obtained, results in decline, expenditure, and [counter-]rise — that is a calamitous gain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.06/ yathā sāmantānām āmiṣa.bhūtaḥ sāmanta.vyasanajo lābhaḥ, śatru.prārthito vā sva.bhāva.adhigamyo lābhaḥ, paścāt kopena pārṣṇi.grāheṇa vā vigṛhītaḥ purastāl.lābhaḥ, mitra.ucchedena saṃdhi.vyatikrameṇa vā maṇḍala.viruddho lābhaḥ ity āpad.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: For example: a gain arising from a neighbor's calamity that becomes a lure for [other] neighbors; or a gain that is sought by the enemy and obtainable by its own nature; or a gain [secured] in front while being attacked from the rear by sedition; or a gain that violates [the order of] the circle through the destruction of an ally or violation of a treaty — these are calamitous gains.

children.text: KAZ09.7.07/ svataḥ parato vā bhaya.utpattir ity anarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The arising of danger from oneself or from the enemy — that is loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.08/ tayoḥ artho na vā^iti, anartho na vā^iti, artho^anartha iti, anartho^artha iti saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Of the two: 'Will there be gain or not?' 'Will there be loss or not?' 'Will there be gain but also loss?' 'Will there be loss but also gain?' — these are doubts.

children.text: KAZ09.7.09/ śatru.mitram utsāhayitum artho na vā^iti saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'To incite the enemy's ally — will there be gain or not?' — this is a doubt.

children.text: KAZ09.7.10/ śatru.balam artha.mānābhyām āvāhayitum anartho na vā^iti saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'To win over the enemy's forces through wealth and honor — will there be loss or not?' — this is a doubt.

children.text: KAZ09.7.11/ balavat.sāmantāṃ bhūmim ādātum artho^anartha iti saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'To seize territory from a powerful neighbor — will there be gain that is also loss?' — this is a doubt.

children.text: KAZ09.7.12/ jāyasā sambhūyayānam anartho^artha iti saṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'To march jointly with a more powerful [king] — will there be loss that is also gain?' — this is a doubt.

children.text: KAZ09.7.13/ teṣām artha.saṃśayam upagacchet //
children.translated_text: Of these, one should pursue the doubt that tends toward gain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.14/ artho^artha.anubandhaḥ, artho niranubandhaḥ, artho^anartha.anubandhaḥ, anartho^artha.anubandhaḥ, anartho niranubandhaḥ, anartho^anartha.anubandhaḥ ity anubandha.ṣaḍ.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: Gain followed by gain; gain without consequences; gain followed by loss; loss followed by gain; loss without consequences; loss followed by loss — this is the sixfold classification of consequences.

children.text: KAZ09.7.15/ śatrum utpāṭya pārṣṇi.grāha.ādānam artho^anartha.anubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Uprooting the enemy and then seizing [territory from] the rear-enemy — this is gain followed by loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.16/ udāsīnasya daṇḍa.anugrahaḥ phalena artho niranubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Supporting the neutral [king] with the army, resulting in [immediate] benefit — this is gain without consequences.

children.text: KAZ09.7.17/ parasya^antar.ucchedanam artho^anartha.anubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Internal destruction of the enemy [that destabilizes one's own position] — this is gain followed by loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.18/ śatru.prativeśasya^anugrahaḥ kośa.daṇḍābhyām anartho^anartha.anubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Supporting a neighbor of the enemy with treasury and army [that strengthens the enemy's circle] — this is loss followed by loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.19/ hīna.śaktim utsāhya nivṛttir anartho niranubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Inciting one of lesser power and then withdrawing — this is loss without consequences.

children.text: KAZ09.7.20/ jyāyāṃsam utthāpya nivṛttir anartho^anartha.anubandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Inciting one of greater [power] and then withdrawing — this is loss followed by loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.21/ teṣāṃ pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ śreyān upasamprāptum //
children.translated_text: Of these, each preceding [outcome] is better to obtain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.22/ iti kārya.avasthāpanam //
children.translated_text: This is the assessment of the situation.

children.text: KAZ09.7.23/ samantato yugapad.artha.utpattiḥ samantato^artha.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: When gains arise simultaneously from all sides, that constitutes a calamity of gain from all sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.24/ sā^eva pārṣṇi.grāha.vigṛhītā samantato^artha.saṃśaya.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: The same, when the rear-enemy is hostile, becomes a calamity of doubtful gain from all sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.25/ tayor mitra.ākranda.upagrahāt siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Success in both [situations] comes from winning over the ally and the one who cries for help.

children.text: KAZ09.7.26/ samantataḥ śatrubhyo bhaya.utpattiḥ samantto^anartha.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: When dangers arise from enemies on all sides, that constitutes a calamity of loss from all sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.27/ sā^eva mitra.vigṛhītā samantato^anartha.saṃśaya.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: The same, when allies are hostile, becomes a calamity of doubtful loss from all sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.28/ tayoś cala.amitra.ākranda.upagrahāt siddhiḥ, para.miśra.apratīkāro vā //
children.translated_text: Success in both [situations] comes from winning over the unstable [enemy's] ally and the one who cries for help, or from the absence of a remedy when [the enemy's forces are] mixed with the other's.

children.text: KAZ09.7.29/ ito lābha itarato lābha ity ubhayato^artha.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'From this side a gain, from that side a gain' — this constitutes a calamity of gain from both sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.30/ tasyāṃ samantato^arthāyāṃ ca lābha.guṇa.yuktam artham ādātuṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: In that [situation], and in a calamity of gain from all sides, one should march to seize the gain that has the most [favorable] qualities.

children.text: KAZ09.7.31/ tulye lābha.guṇe pradhānam āsannam anatipātinam ūno vā yena bhavet tam ādātuṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: When the qualities of gain are equal, one should march to seize that which is principal, nearby, not likely to pass away, or that which would make up for one's deficiency.

children.text: KAZ09.7.32/ ito^anartha itarato^anartha ity ubhayato^anartha.āpat //
children.translated_text: 'From this side a loss, from that side a loss' — this constitutes a calamity of loss from both sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.33/ tasyāṃ samantato^anarthāyāṃ ca mitrebhyaḥ siddhiṃ lipseta //
children.translated_text: In that [situation], and in a calamity of loss from all sides, one should seek success through allies.

children.text: KAZ09.7.34/ mitra.abhāve prakṛtīnāṃ laghīyasya^ekato^anarthāṃ sādhayet, ubhayato^anarthāṃ jyāyasyā, samantato^anarthāṃ mūlena pratikuryāt //
children.translated_text: In the absence of allies, one should remedy the loss on one side through the subjects' lighter [burden]; the loss on both sides through the more powerful [subjects]; the loss from all sides through the root [capital].

children.text: KAZ09.7.35/ aśakye sarvam utsṛjya^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: When it is impossible, one should abandon everything and depart.

children.text: KAZ09.7.36/ dṛṣṭā hi jīvataḥ punar.āvṛttir yathā suyātrā.udayanābhyām //
children.translated_text: For, as long as one lives, return is possible — as [illustrated] by <s>Suyātra</s> and <s>Udayana</s>.

children.text: KAZ09.7.37/ ito lābha itarato rājya.abhimarśa ity ubhayato^artha.anartha.āpad bhavati //
children.translated_text: 'From this side a gain, from that side a threat to the kingdom' — this constitutes a calamity of gain-and-loss from both sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.38/ tasyām anartha.sādhako yo^arthas tam ādātuṃ yāyāt //
children.translated_text: In that [situation], one should march to seize the gain that neutralizes the loss.

children.text: KAZ09.7.39/ anyathā hi rājya.abhimarśaṃ vārayet //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, one should ward off the threat to the kingdom.

children.text: KAZ09.7.40/ etayā samantato^artha.anartha.āpad vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the calamity of gain-and-loss from all sides is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.7.41/ ito^anartha itarato^artha.saṃśaya ity ubhayato^anartha.artha.saṃśayā //
children.translated_text: 'From this side a loss, from that side a doubtful gain' — this constitutes a [calamity of] loss and doubtful gain from both sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.42/ tasyāṃ pūrvam anarthaṃ sādhayet, tat.siddhāv artha.saṃśayam //
children.translated_text: In that [situation], one should first remedy the loss; upon its resolution, [pursue] the doubtful gain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.43/ etayā samantato^anartha.artha.saṃśayā vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the [calamity of] loss and doubtful gain from all sides is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.7.44/ ito^artha itarato^anartha.saṃśaya ity ubhayato^artha.anartha.saṃśaya.āpad //
children.translated_text: 'From this side a gain, from that side a doubtful loss' — this constitutes a calamity of gain and doubtful loss from both sides.

children.text: KAZ09.7.45/ etayā samantato^artha.anartha.saṃśayā vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the [calamity of] gain and doubtful loss from all sides is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.7.46/ tasyāṃ pūrvāṃ pūrvāṃ prakṛtīnām anartha.saṃśayān mokṣayituṃ yateta //
children.translated_text: In that [situation], one should strive to free the constituent elements from the earlier [more pressing] doubtful losses first.

children.text: KAZ09.7.47/ śreyo hi mitram anartha.saṃśaye tiṣṭhan na daṇḍaḥ, daṇḍo vā na kośa iti //
children.translated_text: For it is better that an ally should remain in [a state of] doubtful loss rather than the army; and the army rather than the treasury.

children.text: KAZ09.7.48/ samagra.mokṣaṇa.abhāve prakṛtīnām avayavān mokṣayituṃ yateta //
children.translated_text: When complete liberation [of all constituents] is not possible, one should strive to liberate portions of the constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ09.7.49/ tatra puruṣa.prakṛtīnāṃ bahulam anuraktaṃ vā tīkṣṇa.lubdha.varjam, dravya.prakṛtīnāṃ sāraṃ mahā.upakāraṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Of these, for human constituents — [one should save] the majority or the devoted, excluding the fierce and the greedy; for material constituents — the essential or the most useful.

children.text: KAZ09.7.50/ saṃdhinā^āsanena dvaidhī.bhāvena vā laghūni, viparyayair gurūṇi //
children.translated_text: Through treaty, sitting quiet, or the dual policy, [one should resolve] the lighter [calamities]; through the opposite [means], the heavier ones.

children.text: KAZ09.7.51/ kṣaya.sthāna.vṛddhīnāṃ ca^uttara.uttaraṃ lipseta //
children.translated_text: Among decline, stability, and growth, one should seek each successive [higher] state.

children.text: KAZ09.7.52/ prātilomyena vā kṣaya.ādīnām āyatyāṃ viśeṣaṃ paśyet //
children.translated_text: Or, one should look for the distinguishing advantage in the future, in the reverse order of decline and the rest.

children.text: KAZ09.7.53/ iti deśa.avasthāpanam //
children.translated_text: This is the assessment of the situation.

children.text: KAZ09.7.54/ etena yātrā.ādi.madhya.anteṣv artha.anartha.saṃśayānām upasamprāptir vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the occurrence of gain, loss, and doubt at the beginning, middle, and end of a campaign is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.7.55/ nirantara.yogitvāc ca^artha.anartha.saṃśayānāṃ yātrā.ādāv arthaḥ śreyān upasamprāptuṃ pārṣṇi.grāha.āsāra.pratighāte kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.pratyādeye mūla.rakṣaṇeṣu ca bhavati //
children.translated_text: Because gain, loss, and doubt are inseparably connected, gain at the beginning of a campaign is better to obtain — for it [enables] the repelling of the rear-enemy and the vanguard-attack, [compensates for] decline, expenditure, and exile, [establishes] recoverability, and [ensures] the protection of the base.

children.text: KAZ09.7.56/ tathā^anarthaḥ saṃśayo vā sva.bhūmiṣṭhasya viṣahyo bhavati //
children.translated_text: Likewise, loss or doubt is more endurable for one who is on his own territory.

children.text: KAZ09.7.57/ etena yātrā.madhye^artha.anartha.saṃśayānām upasamprāptir vyākhyātā //
children.translated_text: By this, the occurrence of gain, loss, and doubt in the middle of a campaign is explained.

children.text: KAZ09.7.58/ yātrā.ante tu karśanīyam ucchedanīyaṃ vā karśayitvā^ucchidya vā^arthaḥ śreyān upasamprāptuṃ na^anarthaḥ saṃśayo vā para.ābādha.bhayāt //
children.translated_text: At the end of a campaign, however — having weakened or uprooted one who is to be weakened or uprooted — gain is better to obtain, not loss or doubt, because of the danger from the enemy's attack.

children.text: KAZ09.7.59/ sāmavāyikānām apurogasya tu yātrā.madhya.antago^anarthaḥ saṃśayo vā śreyān upasamprāptum anirbandha.gāmitvāt //
children.translated_text: But for one who is not the leader among coalition partners, loss or doubt in the middle or at the end of a campaign is better to obtain, because it does not lead to [excessive] commitment.

children.text: KAZ09.7.60/ artho dharmaḥ kāma ity artha.tri.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: Gain is <s>artha</s> (material wealth), <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) — this is the triad of gains.

children.text: KAZ09.7.61/ tasya pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ śreyān upasamprāptum //
children.translated_text: Of these, each preceding one is better to obtain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.62/ anartho^adharmaḥ śoka ity anartha.tri.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: Loss is <s>anartha</s> (material loss), <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), and <s>śoka</s> (grief) — this is the triad of losses.

children.text: KAZ09.7.63/ tasya pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ śreyān pratikartum //
children.translated_text: Of these, each preceding one is better to counteract.

children.text: KAZ09.7.64/ artho^anartha iti, dharmo^adharma iti, kāmaḥ śoka iti saṃśaya.tri.vargaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Gain or loss?', '<s>Dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>?', '<s>Kāma</s> or grief?' — this is the triad of doubts.

children.text: KAZ09.7.65/ tasya^uttara.pakṣa.siddhau pūrva.pakṣaḥ śreyān upasamprāptum //
children.translated_text: Of these, when the latter alternative succeeds, the former alternative is better to obtain.

children.text: KAZ09.7.66/ iti kāla.avasthāpanam //
children.translated_text: This is the assessment of timing.

children.text: KAZ09.7.67/ ity āpadaḥ - tāsāṃ siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the calamities — and their resolution.

children.text: KAZ09.7.68/ putra.bhrātṛ.bandhuṣu sāma.dānābhyāṃ siddhir anurūpā, paura.jānapada.daṇḍa.mukhyeṣu dāna.bhedābhyām, sāmanta.āṭavikeṣu bheda.daṇḍābhyām //
children.translated_text: With sons, brothers, and kinsmen, success is appropriate through conciliation and gifts; with townspeople, countryfolk, army chiefs, and prominent persons — through gifts and dissension; with neighboring kings and forest chieftains — through dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ09.7.69/ eṣā^anulomā, viparyaye pratilomā //
children.translated_text: This is the natural order; in the reverse case, the reverse order.

children.text: KAZ09.7.70/ mitra.amitreṣu vyāmiśrā siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: With friends and enemies, success [is achieved through] a mixed [application of expedients].

children.text: KAZ09.7.71/ paraspara.sādhakā hy upāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: For the expedients are mutually supportive.

children.text: KAZ09.7.72/ śatroḥ śaṅkita.amātyeṣu sāntvaṃ prayuktaṃ śeṣa.prayogaṃ nivartayati, dūṣya.amātyeṣu dānam, saṃghāteṣu bhedaḥ, śaktimatsu daṇḍa iti //
children.translated_text: Against the enemy's suspected ministers, conciliation, once applied, halts further [hostile] deployment; against corruptible ministers, gifts; against factions, dissension; against the powerful, force.

children.text: KAZ09.7.73/ guru.lāghava.yogāc ca^āpadāṃ niyoga.vikalpa.samuccayā bhavanti //
children.translated_text: According to the gravity and levity of calamities, the expedients are applied as prescription, alternative, or combination.

children.text: KAZ09.7.74/ "anena^eva^upāyena na^anyena" iti niyogaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'By this very expedient and no other' — this is a prescription.

children.text: KAZ09.7.75/ "anena vā^anyena vā" iti vikalpaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'By this or by another' — this is an alternative.

children.text: KAZ09.7.76/ "anena^anyena ca" iti samuccayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'By this and by another' — this is a combination.

children.text: KAZ09.7.77/ teṣām eka.yogāś catvāras tri.yogāś ca, dvi.yogāḥ ṣaṭ, ekaś catur.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Of these, there are four single-expedient [applications], four triple-expedient, six double-expedient, and one quadruple-expedient.

children.text: KAZ09.7.78/ iti pañca.daśa.upāyāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus there are fifteen expedients.

children.text: KAZ09.7.79/ tāvantaḥ pratilomāḥ //
children.translated_text: The same in reverse order [makes] an equal number.

children.text: KAZ09.7.80/ teṣām ekena^upāyena siddhir eka.siddhiḥ, dvābhyāṃ dvi.siddhiḥ, tribhis tri.siddhiḥ, caturbhiś catuḥ.siddhir iti //
children.translated_text: Of these, success through one expedient is single-success; through two, double-success; through three, triple-success; through four, quadruple-success.

children.text:
KAZ09.7.81/ dharma.mūlatvāt kāma.phalatvāc ca^arthasya dharma.artha.kāma.anubandhā yā^arthasya siddhiḥ sā sarva.artha.siddhiḥ // <iti siddhayah>
KAZ09.7.82/ daivād agnir udakaṃ vyādhiḥ pramāro vidravo durbhikṣam āsurī sṛṣṭir ity āpadaḥ //
children.translated_text:
Since <s>artha</s> is rooted in <s>dharma</s> and has <s>kāma</s> as its fruit, that success of <s>artha</s> which is accompanied by <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> is the complete success. These are the successes.
Divine [calamities are]: fire, flood, disease, pestilence, panic-flight, famine, and demonic affliction.

children.text: KAZ09.7.83/ tāsāṃ daivata.brāhmaṇa.rpaṇipātataḥ siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Success against them [comes] from supplication to deities and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

children.text:
KAZ09.7.84ab/ ativṛṣṭir avṛṣṭir vā sṛṣṭir vā yā^āsurī bhavet /
KAZ09.7.84cd/ tasyām ātharvaṇaṃ karma siddha.ārambhāś ca siddhayaḥ //E
children.translated_text: Whether there is excessive rain, drought, or a demonic affliction — for these, <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (Atharva Vedic) rites and undertakings by accomplished [practitioners] are the remedies.

children.text:
(skandha.āvāra.niveśah)
KAZ10.1.01/ vāstuka.praśaste vāstuni nāyaka.vardhaki mauhūrtikāḥ skandha.āvāram, vṛttaṃ dīrghaṃ catur.aśraṃ vā bhūmi.vaśena vā, catur.dvāraṃ ṣaṭ.pathaṃ nava.saṃsthānaṃ māpayeyuḥ khāta.vapra.sāla.dvāra.aṭṭālaka.sampannaṃ bhaye sthāne ca //
children.translated_text:
(Setting up the military camp)
Architects, master builders, and astrologers should lay out the military camp on ground approved as auspicious — circular, oblong, or square according to the terrain — with four gates, six [main] roads, and nine sections, furnished with ditches, ramparts, halls, gates, and watchtowers, both for danger and for stationing [troops].

children.text: KAZ10.1.02/ madhyamasya^uttare nava.bhāge rāja.vāstukaṃ dhanuḥ.śata.āyāmam ardha.vistāram, paścima.ardhe tasya^antaḥ.puram //
children.translated_text: In the northern ninth of the middle [section], the royal quarters — one hundred bow-lengths long and half as wide — with the inner apartments in its western half.

children.text: KAZ10.1.03/ antar.vaṃśika.sainyaṃ ca^ante niviśeta //
children.translated_text: The palace guard should be stationed at the end [of the royal quarters].

children.text: KAZ10.1.04/ purastād upasthānam, dakṣiṇataḥ kośa.śāsana.kārya.karaṇāni, vāmato rāja.aupavāhyānāṃ hasty.aśva.rathānāṃ sthānam //
children.translated_text: In front, the audience hall; to the south, the treasury and the secretariat offices; to the left, the stations for the king's elephants, horses, and chariots.

children.text: KAZ10.1.05/ ato dhanuḥ.śata.antarāś catvāraḥ śakaṭa.methī.pratati.stambha.sāla.parikṣepāḥ //
children.translated_text: Beyond this, at intervals of one hundred bow-lengths, [there are] four enclosures of cart-barriers, post-enclosures, and palisade-halls.

children.text: KAZ10.1.06/ prathame purastān mantri.purohitau, daṇṣiṇataḥ koṣṭha.agāraṃ mahānasaṃ ca, vāmataḥ kupya.āyudha.agāram //
children.translated_text: In the first [enclosure] — the ministers and chaplain in front; to the south, the granary and kitchen; to the left, the storehouse for commodities and the armory.

children.text: KAZ10.1.07/ dvitīye maula.bhṛtānāṃ sthānam aśva.rathānāṃ senā.pateś ca //
children.translated_text: In the second, the quarters of the hereditary and hired troops, [with] horses, chariots, and the commander-in-chief.

children.text: KAZ10.1.08/ tṛtīye hastinaḥ śreṇyaḥ praśāstā ca //
children.translated_text: In the third, the elephants, the guilds, and the superintendent.

children.text: KAZ10.1.09/ caturthe viṣṭir nāyako mitra.amitra.aṭavī.balaṃ sva.puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitam //
children.translated_text: In the fourth, the levied troops, the leader, and the forces of allies, enemies, and forest tribes — supervised by [the king's] own men.

children.text: KAZ10.1.10/ vaṇijo rūpa.ājīvāś ca^anu.mahā.patham //
children.translated_text: Merchants and courtesans [should be stationed] along the main road.

children.text: KAZ10.1.11/ bāhyato lubdhaka.śva.gaṇinaḥ satūrya.agnayaḥ, gūḍhāś ca^ārakṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: On the outside, hunters and dog-keepers with torches and fires, and concealed guards.

children.text: KAZ10.1.12/ śatrūṇām āpāte kūpa.kūṭa.avapāta.kaṇṭakinīś ca sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: Against enemy attacks, he should set up wells, spike-traps, pitfalls, and thorn-barriers.

children.text: KAZ10.1.13/ aṣṭādaśa.vargāṇām ārakṣa.viparyāsaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: He should arrange alternating guard-duty for the eighteen divisions.

children.text: KAZ10.1.14/ diva.āyāmaṃ ca kārayed apasarpa.jñāna.artham //
KAZ10.1.15/ vivāda.saurika.samāja.dyūta.vāraṇaṃ ca kārayet, mudrā.rakṣaṇaṃ ca //
KAZ10.1.16/ senā.nivṛttam āyudhīyam aśāsanaṃ śūnya.pālo badhnīyāt //

KAZ10.1.17ab/ purastād adhvanaḥ samyak.praśāstā rakṣaṇāni ca /
KAZ10.1.17cd/ yāyād vardhaki.viṣṭibhyām udakāni ca kārayet //E

(skandha.āvāra.prayāṇam - bala.vyasana.avaskanda.kāla.rakṣaṇam)
KAZ10.2.01/ grāma.araṇyānām adhvani niveśān yavasa.indhana.udaka.vaśena parisaṃkhyāya sthāna.āsana.gamana.kālaṃ ca yātrāṃ yāyāt //
KAZ10.2.02/ tat.pratīkāra.dvi.guṇaṃ bhakta.upakaraṇaṃ vāhayet //
KAZ10.2.03/ aśakto vā sainyeṣv āyojayet, antareṣu vā nicinuyāt //
KAZ10.2.04/ purastān nāyakaḥ, madhye kalatraṃ svāmī ca, pārśvayor aśvā bāhu.utsāraḥ, cakra.anteṣu hastinaḥ prasāra.vṛddhir vā, paścāt senā.patir yāyāt niviśeta //
KAZ10.2.05/ sarvato vana.ājīvaḥ prasāraḥ //
KAZ10.2.06/ sva.deśād anvāyatir vīvadhaḥ //
KAZ10.2.07/ mitra.balam āsāraḥ //
KAZ10.2.08/ kalatra.sthānam apasāraḥ //
KAZ10.2.09/ purastād adhyāghāte makareṇa yāyāt, paścāt^śakaṭena, pārśvayor vajreṇa, samantataḥ sarvato.bhadreṇa, eka.ayane sūcyā //
KAZ10.2.10/ pathi.dvaidhī.bhāve svabhūmito yāyāt //
KAZ10.2.11/ abhūmiṣṭhānāṃ hi sva.bhūmiṣṭhā yuddhe pratilomā bhavanti //
KAZ10.2.12/ yojanam adhamā, adhyardhaṃ madhyamā, dvi.yojanam uttamā, sambhāvyā vā gatiḥ //

KAZ10.2.13/ āśraya.kārī sampanna.ghātī pārṣṇir āsāro madhyama udāsīno vā pratikartavyaḥ, saṃkaṭo mārgaḥ śodhayitavyaḥ, kośo daṇḍo mitra.amitra.aṭavī.balaṃ viṣṭi.ṛtur vā pratīkṣyāḥ, kṛta.durga.karma.nicaya.rakṣā.kṣayaḥ krīta.bala.nirvedo mitra.bala.nirvedaś ca^āgamiṣyati, upajapitāro vā na^atitvarayanti, śatrur abhiprāyaṃ vā pūrayiṣyati, iti śanair yāyāt,
viparyaye śīghram //
KAZ10.2.14/ hasti.stambha.saṃkrama.setu.bandha.nau.kāṣṭha.veṇu.saṃghātair alābu.carma.karaṇḍa.dṛti.plava.gaṇḍikā.veṇikābhiś ca^udakāni tārayet //
KAZ10.2.15/ tīrtha.abhigrahe hasty.aśvair anyato rātrāv uttārya sattraṃ gṛhṇīyāt //
KAZ10.2.16/ anudake cakri.catuṣpadaṃ ca^adhva.pramāṇena śaktyā^udakaṃ vāhayet //

KAZ10.2.17/ dīrgha.kāntāram anudakaṃ yavasa.indhana.udaka.hīnaṃ vā kṛcchra.adhvānam abhiyoga.praskannaṃ kṣut.pipāsā.adhva.klāntaṃ paṅka.toya.gambhīrāṇāṃ vā nadī.darī.śailānām udyāna.apayāne vyāsaktam eka.ayana.mārge śaila.viṣame saṃkaṭe vā bahulī.bhūtaṃ niveśe prasthite visamnāhaṃ bhojana.vyāsaktam āyata.gata.pariśrāntam avasuptaṃ vyādhi.maraka.durbhikṣa.pīḍitaṃ
vyādhita.patty.aśva.dvipam abhūmiṣṭhaṃ vā bala.vyasaneṣu vā sva.sainyaṃ rakṣet, para.sainyaṃ ca^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.2.18/ eka.ayana.mārga.prayātasya senā.niścāra.grāsa.āhāra.śayyā.prastāra.agni.nidhāna.dhvaja.āyudha.saṃkhyānena para.bala.jñānam //
KAZ10.2.19/ tadā^ātmāno gūhayet //

KAZ10.2.20ab/ pārvataṃ vana.durgaṃ vā sāpasāra.pratigraham /
KAZ10.2.20cd/ sva.bhumau pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yudhyeta niviśeta ca //E

(kūṭa.yuddha.vikalpāh - sva.sainya.utsāhanam - sva.balāny abala.vyāyogah)
KAZ10.3.01/ bala.viśiṣṭaḥ kṛta.upajāpaḥ prativihita.ṛtuḥ sva.bhūmyāṃ prakāśa.yuddham upeyāt //
KAZ10.3.02/ viparyaye kūṭa.yuddham //
KAZ10.3.03/ bala.vyasana.avaskanda.kāleṣu param abhihanyāt, abhūmiṣṭhaṃ vā sva.bhūmiṣṭhaḥ, prakṛti.pragraho vā sva.bhūmiṣṭham //
KAZ10.3.04/ dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.balair vā bhaṅgaṃ dattvā vibhūmi.prāptaṃ hanyāt //
KAZ10.3.05/ saṃhata.anīkaṃ hastibhir bhedayet //
KAZ10.3.06/ pūrvaṃ bhaṅga.pradānena^anupralīnaṃ bhinnam abhinnaḥ pratinivṛtya hanyāt //
KAZ10.3.07/ purastād abhihatya pracalaṃ vimukhaṃ vā pṛṣṭhato hasty.aśvena^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.08/ pṛṣṭhato^abhihatyā pracalaṃ vimukhaṃ vā purastāt sāra.balena^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.09/ tābhyāṃ pārśva.abhigātau vyākhyātau //
KAZ10.3.10/ yato vā dūṣya.phalgu.balaṃ tato^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.11/ purastād viṣamāyāṃ pṛṣṭhato^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.12/ pṛṣṭhato viṣamāyāṃ purastād abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.13/ pārśvato viṣamāyām itarato^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.14/ dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.balair vā pūrvaṃ yodhayitvā śrāntam aśrāntaḥ param abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.15/ dūṣya.balena vā svayaṃ bhaṅgaṃ dattvā "jitam" iti viśvastam aviśvastaḥ sattra.apāśrayo^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.16/ sārtha.vraja.skandha.āvāra.saṃvāha.vilopa.pramattam apramatto^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.17/ phalgu.bala.avacchanna.sāra.balo vā para.vīrān anupraviśya hanyāt //
KAZ10.3.18/ go.grahaṇena śvā.pada.vadhena vā para.vīrān ākṛṣya sattrac.channo^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.19/ rātrāv avaskandena jāgarayitvā nidrā.klāntān avasuptān vā divā hanyāt //
KAZ10.3.20/ sapāda.carma.kośair vā hastibhiḥ sauptikaṃ dadyāt //
KAZ10.3.21/ ahaḥ.samnāha.pariśrāntān apara.ahne^abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.22/ śuṣka.carma.vṛtta.śarkara.ākośakair go.mahiṣa.uṣṭra.yūthair vā trasnubhir akṛta.hasty.aśvaṃ bhinnam abhinnaḥ pratinivṛttaṃ hanyāt //
KAZ10.3.23/ pratisūrya.vātaṃ vā sarvam abhihanyāt //
KAZ10.3.24/ dhānvana.vana.saṃkaṭa.paṅka.śaila.nimna.viṣama.nāvo gāvaḥ śakaṭavyūho nīhāro rātrir iti sattrāṇi //
KAZ10.3.25/ pūrve ca praharaṇa.kālāḥ kūṭa.yuddha.hetavaḥ //
KAZ10.3.26/ saṃgrāmas tu nirdiṣṭa.deśa.kālo dharmiṣṭhaḥ //
KAZ10.3.27/ saṃhatya daṇḍaṃ brūyāt "tulya.vetano^asmi, bhavadbhiḥ saha bhogyam idaṃ rājyam, mayā^abhihitaiḥ paro^abhihantavyaḥ" iti //
KAZ10.3.28/ vedeṣv apy anuśrūyate samāpta.dakṣiṇānāṃ yajñānām avabhṛtheṣu "sā te gatir yā śūrāṇām" iti //
KAZ10.3.29/ api^iha ślokau bhavataḥ //

KAZ10.3.30ab/ "yān yajña.saṃghais tapasā ca viprāḥ svarga.eṣiṇaḥ pātra.cayaiś ca yānti /
KAZ10.3.30cd/ kṣaṇena tān apy atiyānti śūrāḥ prāṇān suyuddheṣu parityajantaḥ //

KAZ10.3.31ab/ "navaṃ śarāvaṃ salilasya pūrṇaṃ susaṃskṛtaṃ darbha.kṛta.uttarīyam /
KAZ10.3.31cd/ tat tasya mā bhūn narakaṃ ca gacched yo bhartṛ.piṇḍasya kṛte na yudhyet - iti //
KAZ10.3.32/ mantri.purohitābhyām utsāhayed yodhān vyūha.sampadā //
KAZ10.3.33/ kārtāntika.ādiś ca^asya vargaḥ sarvajña.daivata.samyoga.khyāpanābhyāṃ sva.pakṣam uddharṣayet, para.pakṣaṃ ca^udvejayet //
KAZ10.3.34/ "śvo yuddham" iti kṛta.upavāsaḥ śastra.vāhanaṃ ca^anuśayīta //
KAZ10.3.35/ atharvabhiś ca juhuyāt //
KAZ10.3.36/ vijaya.yuktāḥ svargīyāś ca^āśiṣo vācayet //
KAZ10.3.37/ brāhmaṇebhyaś ca^ātmānam atisṛjet //
KAZ10.3.38/ śaurya.śilpa.abhijana.anurāga.yuktam artha.mānābhyām avisaṃvāditam anīka.garbhaṃ kurvīta //
KAZ10.3.39/ pitṛ.putra.bhrātṛkāṇām āyudhīyānām adhvajaṃ muṇḍa.anīkaṃ rāja.sthānam //
KAZ10.3.40/ hastī ratho vā rāja.vāhanam aśva.anubandhaḥ //
KAZ10.3.41/ yat prāya.sainyo yatra vā vinītaḥ syāt t(ad) adhirohayet //
KAZ10.3.42/ rāja.vyañjano vyūha.adhiṣṭhānam āyojyaḥ //
KAZ10.3.43/ sūta.māgadhāḥ śūrāṇāṃ svargam asvargaṃ bhīrūṇāṃ jāti.saṃgha.kula.karma.vṛtta.stavaṃ ca yodhānāṃ varṇayeyuḥ //
KAZ10.3.44/ purohita.puruṣāḥ kṛtya.abhicāraṃ brūyuḥ, yantrika.vardhaki.mauhūrtikāḥ sva.karma.siddhim asiddhiṃ pareṣām //

KAZ10.3.45/ senā.patir artha.mānābhyām abhisaṃskṛtam anīkam ābhāṣeta - "śata.sāhasro rāja.vadhaḥ, pañcāśat.sāhasraḥ senā.pati.kumāra.vadhaḥ, daśa.sāhasraḥ pravīra.mukhya.vadhaḥ, pañca.sāhasro hasti.ratha.vadhaḥ, sāhasro^aśva.vadhaḥ, śatyaḥ patti.mukhya.vadhaḥ, śiro viṃśatikaṃ bhoga.dvaiguṇyaṃ svayaṃ.grāhaś ca" iti //
KAZ10.3.46/ tad eṣāṃ daśa.varga.adhipatayo vidyuḥ //
KAZ10.3.47/ cikitsakāḥ śastra.yantra.agada.sneha.vastra.hastāḥ striyaś ca^anna.pāna.rakṣiṇyaḥ puruṣāṇām uddharṣaṇīyāḥ pṛṣṭhatas tiṣṭheyuḥ //
KAZ10.3.48/ adakṣiṇā.mukhaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ.sūryam anuloma.vātam anīkaṃ sva.bhūmau vyūheta //
KAZ10.3.49/ para.bhūmi.vyūhe ca^aśvāṃś cārayeyuḥ //
KAZ10.3.50/ yatra sthānaṃ prajavaś ca^abhūmir vyūhasya tatra sthitaḥ prajavitaś ca^ubhayathā jīyeta // viparyaye jayati, ubhayathā sthāne prajave ca //
KAZ10.3.52/ samā viṣamā vyāmiśrā vā bhūmir iti purastāt pārśvābhyāṃ paścāc ca jñeyā //
KAZ10.3.53/ samāyāṃ daṇḍa.maṇḍala.vyūhāḥ, viṣamāyāṃ bhoga.asaṃhata.vyūhāḥ, vyāmiśrāyāṃ viṣama.vyūhāḥ //
KAZ10.3.54/ viśiṣṭa.balaṃ bhaṅktvā saṃdhiṃ yāceta //
KAZ10.3.55/ sama.balena yācitaḥ saṃdadhīta //
KAZ10.3.56/ hīnam anuhanyāt, na tv eva sva.bhūmi.prāptaṃ tyakta.ātmānaṃ vā //

KAZ10.3.57ab/ punar.āvartamānasya nirāśasya ca jīvite /
KAZ10.3.57cd/ adhāryo jāyate vegas tasmād bhagnaṃ na pīḍayet //E

(yuddha.bhūmayah - patty.aśva.ratha.hasti.karmāṇi)
KAZ10.4.01/ sva.bhūmiḥ patty.aśva.ratha.dvipānām iṣṭā yuddhe niveśe ca //
KAZ10.4.02/ dhānvana.vana.nimna.sthala.yodhināṃ khanaka.ākāśa.divā.rātri.yodhināṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ nādeya.pārvata.ānūpa.sārasānāṃ ca hastinām aśvānāṃ ca yathā.svam iṣṭā yuddha.bhūmayaḥ kālāś ca //
children.translated_text: The preferred battlegrounds and seasons for warriors of arid, forest, lowland, and highland terrain, for sappers, aerial fighters, and day and night fighters, and for elephants and horses suited to riverine, mountainous, marshy, and lake regions are [determined] according to their respective [strengths].

children.text: KAZ10.4.03/ samā sthirā^abhikāśā nirutkhātinya.cakra.khurā^anakṣa.grāhiṇya.vṛkṣa.gulma.vratatī.stambha.kedāra.śvabhra.valmīka.sikatā.paṅka.bhaṅgurā daraṇa.hīnā ca ratha.bhūmiḥ, hasty.aśvayor manuṣyāṇāṃ ca same viṣame hitā yuddhe niveśe ca //
children.translated_text: Level, firm, open ground — free from pits, impediments to wheels and hooves, not entangling axles, devoid of trees, shrubs, creepers, stumps, embankments, ditches, anthills, sandy and muddy patches, and soft spots — is chariot terrain; terrain both level and uneven is beneficial for elephants, horses, and men in battle and in encampment.

children.text: KAZ10.4.04/ aṇv.aśma.vṛkṣā hrasva.laṅghanīya.śvabhrā manda.daraṇa.doṣā ca^aśva.bhūmiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ground with small stones and trees, with shallow and easily jumpable ditches, and with mild soft-ground defects is horse terrain.

children.text: KAZ10.4.05/ sthūla.sthāṇv aśma.vṛkṣa.vratatī.valmīka.gulmā padāti.bhūmiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ground with large stumps, stones, trees, creepers, anthills, and shrubs is infantry terrain.

children.text: KAZ10.4.06/ gamya.śaila.nimna.viṣamā mardanīya.vṛkṣā chedanīya.vratatī paṅka.bhaṅgurā daraṇa.hīnā ca hasti.bhūmiḥ //
children.translated_text: Ground with passable hills, depressions, and uneven [features], with trees that can be trampled, with creepers that can be cut, with muddy but not soft patches, and without sinkholes is elephant terrain.

children.text: KAZ10.4.07/ akaṇṭakiny abahu.viṣamā pratyāsāravatī^iti padātīnām atiśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Terrain free of thorns, not excessively uneven, and with [nearby] cover for retreat — that is the advantage of infantry.

children.text: KAZ10.4.08/ dvi.guṇa.pratyāsārā kardama.udaka.khañjana.hīnā nihśarkarā^iti vājinām atiśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Terrain with double the retreat cover, free of mud, water, and mire, and without gravel — that is the advantage of cavalry.

children.text: KAZ10.4.09/ pāṃsu.kardama.udaka.nala.śara.ādhānavatī śva.daṇṣṭra.hīnā mahā.vṛkṣa.śākhā.ghāta.viyuktā^iti hastinām atiśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Terrain with dust, mud, water, and reed-and-rush beds, free of caltrops, and not obstructed by the striking of large tree branches — that is the advantage of elephants.

children.text: KAZ10.4.10/ toya.āśaya.apāśrayavatī nirutkhātinī kedāra.hīnā vyāvartana.samarthā^iti rathānām atiśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Terrain with water reservoirs and shelters nearby, without pits, free of embankments, and capable of turning [maneuvers] — that is the advantage of chariots.

children.text: KAZ10.4.11/ uktā sarveṣāṃ bhūmiḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the terrain for all [arms] has been described.

children.text: KAZ10.4.12/ etayā sarva.bala.niveśā yuddhāni ca vyākhyātāni bhavanti //
children.translated_text: By this, the encampments and battles of all forces are explained.

children.text: KAZ10.4.13/ bhūmi.vāsa.vana.vicayo^aviṣama.toya.tīrtha.vāta.raśmi.grahaṇaṃ vīvadha.āsārayor ghāto rakṣā vā viśuddhiḥ sthāpanā ca balasya prasāra.vṛddhir bāhu.utsāraḥ pūrva.prahāro vyāveśanaṃ vyāvedhanam āśvāso grahaṇaṃ mokṣaṇaṃ mārga.anusāra.vinimayaḥ kośa.kumāra.abhiharaṇaṃ jaghana.koṭy.abhighāto hīna.anusāraṇam anuyānaṃ samāja.karma^ity aśva.karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: Reconnaissance of terrain, habitation, and forest; seizing favorable conditions of uneven ground, water-fords, wind, and sunlight; striking or defending against storm-showers and rain; purification, stationing, and expanding the force; extending the flank; delivering the first blow; engaging; piercing through; giving respite; capturing; releasing; exchanging and pursuing routes; seizing the treasury and princes; striking the rear and flanks; pursuing the weakened; following up; and tournament action — these are the functions of cavalry.

children.text: KAZ10.4.14/ puro.yānam akṛta.mārga.vāsa.tīrtha.karma bāhu.utsāras toya.taraṇa.avataraṇe sthāna.gamana.avataraṇaṃ viṣama.sambādha.praveśo^agni.dāna.śamanam eka.aṅga.vijayo bhinna.saṃdhānam abhinna.bhedanaṃ vyasane trāṇam abhighāto vibhīṣikā trāsanaṃ.audāryaṃ grahaṇaṃ mokṣaṇaṃ sāla.dvāra.aṭṭālaka.bhañjanaṃ kośa.vāhana.apavāhanam iti hasti.karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: Advancing in the van; making roads, habitations, and fords where none exist; extending the flanks; crossing and descending into water; stationing, moving, and descending [from heights]; penetrating narrow and difficult passes; extinguishing fires; single-arm victory; repairing what is broken; breaking what is unbroken; rescue in calamity; striking; creating terror and panic; display of might; capturing; releasing; smashing gates, ramparts, and watchtowers; and carrying away treasuries and vehicles — these are the functions of elephants.

children.text: KAZ10.4.15/ sva.bala.rakṣā catur.aṅga.bala.pratiṣedhaḥ saṃgrāme grahaṇaṃ mokṣaṇaṃ bhinna.saṃdhānam abhinna.bhedanaṃ trāsanam audāryaṃ bhīma.ghoṣaś ca^iti ratha.karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: Protecting one's own force; repelling the four-division army; capturing and releasing in battle; repairing what is broken; breaking what is unbroken; creating panic; display of might; and making terrifying sounds — these are the functions of chariots.

children.text: KAZ10.4.16/ sarva.deśa.kāla.śastra.vahanaṃ vyāyāmaś ca^iti padāti.karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: Bearing arms and exercising in all terrains and seasons — these are the functions of infantry.

children.text: KAZ10.4.17/ śibira.mārga.setu.kūpa.tīrtha.śodhana.karma yantra.āyudha.āvaraṇa.upakaraṇa.grāsa.vahanam āyodhanāc ca praharaṇa.āvaraṇa.pratividdha.apanayanam iti viṣṭi.karmāṇi //
children.translated_text: Clearing of camp, roads, bridges, wells, and fords; carrying engines, weapons, armor, equipment, and provisions; and removing weapons, armor, and the wounded from the battlefield — these are the functions of forced laborers.

children.text:
KAZ10.4.18ab/ kuryād gava.aśva.vyāyogaṃ ratheṣv alpa.hayo nṛpaḥ /
KAZ10.4.18cd/ khara.uṣṭra.śakaṭānāṃ vā garbham alpa.gajas tathā //E
children.translated_text: A king deficient in horses should employ oxen and horses yoked together in chariots, or similarly use donkeys, camels, and carts [as substitutes]; likewise one deficient in elephants [should make substitutions].

children.text:
(pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānām bala.agrato vyūha.vibhāgah - sāra.phalgu.bala.vibhāgah - patty.aśva.ratha.hasti.yuddhāni)
KAZ10.5.01/ pañca.dhanuḥ.śata.apakṛṣṭaṃ durgam avasthāpya yuddham upeyāt, bhūmi.vaśena vā //
children.translated_text:
(Division of the array into wings, flanks, and breast for the force-front — distribution of elite and weak troops — infantry, cavalry, chariot, and elephant combats)
Having stationed the baggage train five hundred bow-lengths to the rear, one should engage in battle — or according to the terrain.

children.text: KAZ10.5.02/ vibhakta.mukhyām acakṣur.viṣaye mokṣayitvā senāṃ senā.pati.nāyakau vyūheyātām //
children.translated_text: Having divided the chiefs [among units] and released the army beyond the enemy's sight, the commander-in-chief and the generals should form the array.

children.text: KAZ10.5.03/ śama.antaraṃ pattiṃ sthāpayet, tri.śama.antaram aśvam, pañca.śama.antaraṃ rathaṃ hastinaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: He should station infantry at one <s>śama</s>-interval [one bow-length apart], cavalry at three <s>śama</s>-intervals, and chariots or elephants at five <s>śama</s>-intervals.

children.text: KAZ10.5.04/ dvi.guṇa.antaraṃ tri.guṇa.antaraṃ vā vyūheta //
children.translated_text: Or he may form the array at double or triple intervals.

children.text: KAZ10.5.05/ evaṃ yathā.sukham asambādhaṃ yudhyeta //
children.translated_text: Thus one should fight comfortably and without crowding.

children.text: KAZ10.5.06/ pañca.aratni dhanuḥ //
children.translated_text: A <s>dhanus</s> (bow-length) equals five <s>aratni</s>s (cubits).

children.text: KAZ10.5.07/ tasmin dhanvinaṃ sthāpayet, tri.dhanuṣy aśvam, pañca.dhanuṣi rathaṃ hastinaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: In [each] one he should station an archer; in three <s>dhanus</s>-lengths a horseman; in five <s>dhanus</s>-lengths a chariot or an elephant.

children.text: KAZ10.5.08/ pañca.dhanur anīka.saṃdhiḥ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānām //
children.translated_text: The junction of units for the wings, flanks, and breast is five <s>dhanus</s>-lengths.

children.text: KAZ10.5.09/ aśvasya trayaḥ puruṣāḥ pratiyoddhāraḥ //
children.translated_text: Three men are the counter-fighters for [each] horse.

children.text: KAZ10.5.10/ pañca.daśa rathasya hastino vā, pañca ca^aśvāḥ //
children.translated_text: Fifteen [men] are the counter-fighters for [each] chariot or elephant, and five horses.

children.text: KAZ10.5.11/ tāvantaḥ pāda.gopā vāji.ratha.dvipānāṃ vidheyāḥ //
children.translated_text: An equal number of foot-guards should be assigned to horses, chariots, and elephants.

children.text: KAZ10.5.12/ trīṇi trikāṇy anīkaṃ rathānām urasyaṃ sthāpayet, tāvat kakṣaṃ pakṣaṃ ca^ubhayataḥ //
children.translated_text: He should station three triads of chariots as the breast unit, and the same [number] on both sides as flanks and wings.
