children.text: KAZ10.5.13/ pañca.catvāriṃśad evaṃ rathā ratha.vyūhe bhavanti, dve śate pañca.viṃśatiś ca^aśvāḥ, ṣaṭ.śatāni pañca.saptatiś ca puruṣāḥ pratiyodhāraḥ, tāvantaḥ pāda.gopāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus in a chariot array there are forty-five chariots, two hundred and twenty-five horses, six hundred and seventy-five counter-fighting men, and an equal number of foot-guards.

children.text: KAZ10.5.14/ eṣa sama.vyūhaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the balanced array.

children.text: KAZ10.5.15/ tasya dvi.ratha.uttarā vṛddhir ā.eka.viṃśati.rathād iti //
children.translated_text: Its increment is by two chariots up to twenty-one chariots.

children.text: KAZ10.5.16/ evam ojā daśa sama.vyūha.prakṛtayo bhavanti //
children.translated_text: Thus there are ten types of balanced arrays in odd [numbers].

children.text: KAZ10.5.17/ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānāṃ mitho viṣama.saṃkhyāne viṣama.vyūhaḥ //
children.translated_text: When wings, flanks, and breast have mutually unequal numbers, it is an unbalanced array.

children.text: KAZ10.5.18/ tasya^api dvi.ratha^uttarā vṛddhir ā.eka.viṃśati.rathād iti //
children.translated_text: Its increment too is by two chariots up to twenty-one chariots.

children.text: KAZ10.5.19/ evam ojā daśa viṣama.vyūha.prakṛtayo bhavanti //
children.translated_text: Thus there are ten types of unbalanced arrays in odd [numbers].

children.text: KAZ10.5.20/ ataḥ sainyānāṃ vyūha.śeṣam āvāpaḥ kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text: From this, the remaining troops should be distributed as supplements to the arrays.

children.text: KAZ10.5.21/ rathānāṃ dvau tri.bhāgāv aṅgeṣv āvāpayet, śeṣam urasyaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: Two-thirds of the chariots should be distributed to the wings, and the remainder stationed as the breast.

children.text: KAZ10.5.22/ evaṃ tri.bhāga.ūno rathānām āvāpaḥ kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the chariot supplement should be made with [only] one-third less.

children.text: KAZ10.5.23/ tena hastinām aśvānām āvāpo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the supplementation of elephants and horses is explained.

children.text: KAZ10.5.24/ yāvad.aśva.ratha.dvipānāṃ yuddha.sambādhanm na kuryāt tāvad āvāpaḥ kāryaḥ //
children.translated_text: The supplementation should be made so long as it does not cause crowding in the combat of horses, chariots, and elephants.

children.text: KAZ10.5.25/ daṇḍa.bāhulyam āvāpaḥ //
children.translated_text: An increase in the corps is a supplement (<s>āvāpa</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.5.26/ patti.bāhulyaṃ pratyāpāvaḥ //
children.translated_text: An increase in infantry is a withdrawal-supplement (<s>pratyāpāva</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.5.27/ eka.aṅga.bāhulyam anvāvāpaḥ //
children.translated_text: An increase in a single arm is an after-supplement (<s>anvāvāpa</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.5.28/ dūṣya.bāhulyam atyāvāpaḥ //
children.translated_text: An increase in irregular troops is an over-supplement (<s>atyāvāpa</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.5.29/ para.āvāpāt pratyāvāpāc ca catur.guṇād ā.aṣṭa.guṇād iti vā vibhavataḥ sainyānām āvāpaḥ //
children.translated_text: The supplementation of armies is from four-fold up to eight-fold the enemy's supplement or withdrawal-supplement, according to one's capacity.

children.text: KAZ10.5.30/ ratha.vyūhena hasti.vyūho vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: The elephant array is explained by the chariot array.

children.text: KAZ10.5.31/ vyāmiśro vā hasti.ratha.aśvānāṃ - cakra.anteṣu hastinaḥ pārśvayor aśvā rathā urasye //
children.translated_text: Or a mixed [array] of elephants, chariots, and horses — elephants at the extremities of the flanks, horses on the sides, chariots at the breast.

children.text: KAZ10.5.32/ hastinām urasyaṃ rathānāṃ kakṣāv aśvānāṃ pakṣāv iti madhya.bhedī //
children.translated_text: The breast of elephants, flanks of chariots, wings of horses — this is the center-breaking [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.5.33/ viparīto^anta.bhedī //
children.translated_text: The reverse is the end-breaking [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.5.34/ hastinām eva tu śuddhaḥ - sāmnāhyānām urasyam aupavāhyānāṃ jaghanaṃ vyālānāṃ koṭyāv iti //
children.translated_text: A pure elephant [array]: armored [elephants] at the breast, transport elephants at the rear, and wild elephants at the flanks.

children.text: KAZ10.5.35/ aśva.vyūho - varmiṇām urasyaṃ śuddhānāṃ kakṣa.pakṣāv iti //
children.translated_text: A horse array: armored [horses] at the breast, unarmored at the flanks and wings.

children.text: KAZ10.5.36/ patti.vyūhaḥ - purastād āvaraṇinaḥ pṛṣṭhato dhanvinaḥ //
children.translated_text: An infantry array: shield-bearers in front, archers behind.

children.text: KAZ10.5.37/ iti śuddhāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the pure [arrays].

children.text: KAZ10.5.38/ pattayaḥ pakṣayor aśvāḥ pārśvayoḥ hastinaḥ pṛṣṭhato rathāḥ purastāt, para.vyūha.vaśena vā viparyāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Infantry on the wings, horses on the sides, elephants behind, chariots in front — or the reverse according to the enemy's array.

children.text: KAZ10.5.39/ iti dvy.aṅga.bala.vibhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the two-arm force-division.

children.text: KAZ10.5.40/ tena tr.aṅga.bala.vibhāgo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the three-arm force-division is explained.

children.text:
KAZ10.5.41/ daṇḍa.sampat sāra.balaṃ puṃsāṃ
KAZ10.5.42/ hasty.aśvayor viśeṣaḥ kulaṃ jātiḥ sattvaṃ vayaḥ.sthatā prāṇo varṣma javas tejaḥ śilpaṃ stairyam udagratā vidheyatvaṃ suvyañjana.ācāratā^iti //
children.translated_text:
The excellence of a corps constitutes its elite troops among men.
For elephants and horses, the distinction [of excellence consists of]: lineage, breed, spirit, maturity of age, vitality, stature, speed, energy, skill, steadiness, tallness, obedience, and good markings and behavior.

children.text: KAZ10.5.43/ patty.aśva.ratha.dvipānāṃ sāra.tri.bhāgam urasyaṃ sthāpayet, dvau tri.bhāgau kakṣaṃ pakṣaṃ ca^ubhayataḥ, anulomam anusāram, pratilomaṃ tṛtīya.sāram, phalgu pratilomam //
children.translated_text: He should station the elite one-third of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants at the breast, and the [remaining] two-thirds at the flanks and wings on both sides; with the grain [of strength] as the pursuit [force]; with one-third elite as a counter-current [reserve]; and the weak against the counter-current.

children.text: KAZ10.5.44/ evaṃ sarvam upayogaṃ gamayet //
children.translated_text: Thus he should deploy all for maximum effectiveness.

children.text: KAZ10.5.45/ phalgu.balam anteṣv avadhāya vega.abhihūliko bhavati //
children.translated_text: If weak troops are placed at the ends, one becomes overwhelmed by the [enemy's] charge.

children.text: KAZ10.5.46/ sāra.balam agrataḥ kṛtvā koṭīṣv anusāraṃ kuryāt, jaghane tṛtiyiya.sāram, madhye phalgu.balam //
children.translated_text: Placing elite troops in front, station the pursuit [force] at the flanks, one-third elite at the rear, and weak troops in the center.

children.text: KAZ10.5.47/ evam etat sahiṣṇu bhavati //
children.translated_text: Thus this [formation] becomes resilient.

children.text: KAZ10.5.48/ vyūhaṃ tu sthāpayitvā pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānām ekena dvābhyāṃ vā praharet, śeṣaiḥ pratigṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Having arranged the array, one should strike with one or two of the wings, flanks, or breast, and hold [the rest] in reserve with the remainder.

children.text: KAZ10.5.49/ yat parasya durbalaṃ vīta.hasty.aśvaṃ dūṣya.amātyaṃ kṛta.upajāpaṃ vā tat.prabhūta.sāreṇa^abhihanyāt //
children.translated_text: Whatever [section] of the enemy is weak, devoid of elephants and horses, with disloyal ministers, or where subversion has been effected — that should be struck with a superior elite force.

children.text: KAZ10.5.50/ yad vā parasya sāriṣṭhaṃ tad.dvi.guṇa.sāreṇa^abhihanyāt //
children.translated_text: Or whatever [section] of the enemy is strongest in elite [troops] — that should be struck with a force of double the elite strength.

children.text: KAZ10.5.51/ yad aṅgam alpa.sāram ātmanas tad bahunā^upacinuyāt //
children.translated_text: Whatever arm of one's own is deficient in elite [troops], that should be reinforced with large numbers.

children.text: KAZ10.5.52/ yataḥ parasya^apacayas tato^abhyāśe vyūheta, yatot vā bhayaṃ syāt //
children.translated_text: One should form the array near the point from which the enemy's decline [can be effected], or from where danger may threaten.

children.text: KAZ10.5.53/ abhisṛtaṃ parisṛtam atisṛtam apasṛtam unmathya.avadhānaṃ valayo go.mūtrikā maṇḍalaṃ prakīrṇikā vyāvṛtta.pṛṣṭham anuvaṃśam agrataḥ pārśvābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhato bhagna.rakṣā bhagna.anupāta ity aśva.yuddhāni //
children.translated_text: Frontal charge, encirclement, outflanking, retreat, crushing and holding, enveloping loops, serpentine advance, wheeling, scattered engagement, turning the rear, following the line, [attack] from front, from flanks, from behind, broken-rank defense, and broken-rank pursuit — these are cavalry combats.

children.text: KAZ10.5.54/ prakīrṇika.āvarjāny etāny eva caturṇām aṅgānāṃ vyasta.samastānāṃ vā ghātaḥ, pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānāṃ ca prabhañjanam avaskandaḥ sauptikaṃ ca^iti hasit.yuddhāni //
children.translated_text: These same [maneuvers] — with the addition of scattered-and-overturning, the striking of the four arms singly or in combination, the shattering of wings, flanks, and breast, the surprise attack, and the night attack — are elephant combats.

children.text: KAZ10.5.55/ unmathya.avadhāna.varjāny etāny eva sva.bhūmāv abhiyāna.apayāna.sthita.yuddhāni^iti ratha.yuddhāni //
children.translated_text: These same — except crushing-and-holding — with advancing, retreating, and stationary combat on one's own ground, are chariot combats.

children.text: KAZ10.5.56/ sarva.deśa.kāla.praharaṇam upāṃśu.daṇḍaś ca^iti patti.yuddhāni //
children.translated_text: Fighting with all weapons in all terrains and seasons, and covert operations — these are infantry combats.

children.text:
KAZ10.5.57ab/ etena vidhinā vyūhān ojān yugmāṃś ca kārayet /
KAZ10.5.57cd/ vibhavo yāvad aṅgānāṃ caturṇāṃ sadṛśo bhavet //
children.translated_text: By this method, one should construct arrays both odd and even, until the forces of the four arms are equal [in deployment].

children.text:
KAZ10.5.58ab/ dve śate dhanuṣāṃ gatvā rājā tiṣṭhet pratigrahe /
KAZ10.5.58cd/ bhinna.saṃghātanaṃ tasmān na yudhyeta^apratigrahaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
Having advanced two hundred bow-lengths, the king should remain with the reserve.
Without a reserve, one should not fight — for that would mean failure to restore a broken formation.

children.text:
(daṇḍa.bhoga.maṇḍala.asamhata.vyūha.vyūhanam - tasya prativyūha.sthānam)
KAZ10.6.01/ pakṣāv urasyaṃ pratigraha ity auśanaso vyūha.vibhāgaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Arraying the staff, serpent, circle, and dispersed formations — their counter-formations)
Wings, breast, and reserve — this is the division of the array according to <s>Uśanas</s>.

children.text: KAZ10.6.02/ pakṣau kakṣāv urasym pratigraha iti bārhasptyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Wings, flanks, breast, and reserve — [this is the division] according to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: KAZ10.6.03/ prapakṣa.kakṣa.urasyā ubhayoḥ daṇḍa.bhoga.maṇḍala.asaṃhatāḥ prakṛti.vyūhāḥ //
children.translated_text: With sub-wings, flanks, and breast on both sides, the fundamental arrays are the staff, serpent, circle, and dispersed.

children.text: KAZ10.6.04/ tatra tiryag.vṛttir daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: There, a lateral movement is the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.6.05/ samastānām anvāvṛttir bhogaḥ //
children.translated_text: A sequential movement of all [units] is the serpent (<s>bhoga</s>) [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.6.06/ saratāṃ sarvato.vṛttir maṇḍalaḥ //
children.translated_text: An all-directional movement of those in motion is the circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>) [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.6.07/ sthitānāṃ pṛthag.anīka.vṛttir asaṃhataḥ //
children.translated_text: An independent unit-movement of those stationed is the dispersed (<s>asaṃhata</s>) [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.6.08/ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyaiḥ samaṃ vartamāno daṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: When advancing uniformly with wings, flanks, and breast, it is a [simple] staff.

children.text: KAZ10.6.09/ sa kakṣa.atikrāntaḥ pradaraḥ //
children.translated_text: When the flanks extend beyond [the breast], it is a piercing staff (<s>pradara</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.10/ sa eva pakṣa.kakṣābhyāṃ pratikrānto dṛḍhakaḥ //
children.translated_text: When drawn back with both flanks and wings [ahead], it is a firm staff (<s>dṛḍhaka</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.11/ sa eva^atikrāntaḥ pakṣābhyām asahyaḥ //
children.translated_text: When extended by both wings [further out], it is the irresistible [staff] (<s>asahya</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.12/ pakṣāv avasthāpya^urasya.atikrāntaḥ śyenaḥ //
children.translated_text: When the wings are held back and the breast extends forward, it is the hawk (<s>śyena</s>) [formation].

children.text: KAZ10.6.13/ viparyaye cāpaṃ cāpa.kukuṣiḥ pratiṣṭhaḥ supratiṣṭhaś ca //
children.translated_text: In the reverse, the bow [formation], bow-shoulder, <s>pratiṣṭha</s> (firm), and <s>supratiṣṭha</s> (very firm).

children.text: KAZ10.6.14/ cāpa.pakṣaḥ saṃjayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The bow-winged is <s>saṃjaya</s> (complete victory).

children.text: KAZ10.6.15/ sa eva^urasya.atikrānto vijayaḥ //
children.translated_text: The same, extending beyond the breast, is <s>vijaya</s> (victory).

children.text: KAZ10.6.16/ sthūla.karṇa.pakṣaḥ sthūṇa.akarṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: The thick-eared wing is <s>sthūṇākarṇa</s> (pillar-eared).

children.text: KAZ10.6.17/ dvi.guṇa.pakṣa.sthūṇo viśāla.vijayaḥ //
children.translated_text: With wings double the pillar is <s>viśālavijaya</s> (broad victory).

children.text: KAZ10.6.18/ try.abhikrānta.pakṣaś camū.mukhaḥ //
children.translated_text: With wings advanced in three [steps] is <s>camūmukha</s> (army-face).

children.text: KAZ10.6.19/ viparyaye jhaṣa.āsyaḥ //
children.translated_text: In the reverse, [it is] <s>jhaṣāsya</s> (fish-mouth).

children.text: KAZ10.6.20/ ūrdhva.rājir daṇḍaḥ sūcī //
children.translated_text: A vertical line is the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) or needle (<s>sūcī</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.21/ dvau daṇḍau valayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Two staffs [form] a circle (<s>valaya</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.22/ catvāro durjayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Four [form] the <s>durjaya</s> (invincible).

children.text: KAZ10.6.23/ iti daṇḍa.vyūhāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the staff-formations.

children.text: KAZ10.6.24/ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyair viṣamaṃ vartamāno bhogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Moving unevenly with wing, flank, and breast is the serpent (<s>bhoga</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.25/ sa sarpa.sārī go.mūtrikā vā //
children.translated_text: It is the snake-gliding (<s>sarpasārī</s>) or cow-urine [pattern] (<s>gomūtrikā</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.26/ sa yugma.urasyo daṇḍa.pakṣaḥ śakaṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: With paired breast and staff-wing, [it is] the cart (<s>śakaṭa</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.27/ viparyaye makaraḥ //
children.translated_text: In the reverse, [it is] the crocodile (<s>makara</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.28/ hasty.aśva.rathair vyatikīrṇaḥ śakaṭaḥ pāripatantakaḥ //
children.translated_text: The cart interspersed with elephants, horses, and chariots is the <s>pāripatantaka</s> (flying-around).

children.text: KAZ10.6.29/ iti bhoga.vyūhāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the serpent-formations.

children.text: KAZ10.6.30/ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānām ekī.bhāve maṇḍalaḥ //
children.translated_text: When wing, flank, and breast are merged into one, [it is] the circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.31/ sa sarvato.mukhaḥ sarvato.bhadraḥ //
children.translated_text: It is the all-facing (<s>sarvatomukha</s>) or all-auspicious (<s>sarvatobhadra</s>).

children.text: KAZ10.6.32/ aṣṭa.anīko durjayaḥ //
children.translated_text: With eight divisions, [it is] the <s>durjaya</s> (invincible).

children.text: KAZ10.6.33/ iti maṇḍala.vyūhāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the circle-formations.

children.text: KAZ10.6.34/ pakṣa.kakṣa.urasyānām asaṃhatād asaṃhataḥ //
children.translated_text: From the dispersed [elements of] wing, flank, and breast, [the formation is] dispersed.

children.text: KAZ10.6.35/ sa pañca.anīkānām ākṛti.sthāpanād vajro godhā vā //
children.translated_text: It is the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) or <s>godhā</s> (iguana), from the arrangement of five divisions.

children.text: KAZ10.6.36/ caturṇām uddhānakaḥ kākapadī vā //
children.translated_text: With four [divisions], the <s>uddhānaka</s> (uplifter) or <s>kākapadī</s> (crow's-foot).

children.text: KAZ10.6.37/ trayāṇām ardha.candrakaḥ karkaṭaka.śṛṅgī vā //
children.translated_text: With three, the <s>ardhacandrakā</s> (half-moon) or <s>karkaṭaśṛṅgī</s> (crab's-horn).

children.text: KAZ10.6.38/ ity asaṃhata.vyūhāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the dispersed formations.

children.text: KAZ10.6.39/ ratha.urasyo hasti.kakṣo^aśva.pṛṣṭho^ariṣṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: With chariots in the breast, elephants on the flanks, and cavalry at the rear — [this is] <s>ariṣṭa</s> (invulnerable).

children.text: KAZ10.6.40/ pattayo^aśvā rathā hastinaś ca^anupṛṣṭham acalaḥ //
children.translated_text: Infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants in successive ranks — [this is] <s>acala</s> (immovable).

children.text: KAZ10.6.41/ hastino^aśvā rathāḥ pattayaś ca^anupṛṣṭham apratihataḥ //
children.translated_text: Elephants, cavalry, chariots, and infantry in successive ranks — [this is] <s>apratihata</s> (irresistible).

children.text: KAZ10.6.42/ teṣāṃ pradaraṃ dṛḍhakena ghātayet, dṛḍhakam asahyena, śyenaṃ cāpena, pratiṣṭhaṃ supratiṣṭhena, saṃjayaṃ vijayena, sthūṇa.ākarṇaṃ viśāla.vijayena, pāripatantakaṃ sarvato.bhadreṇa //
children.translated_text: Of these, one should strike the <s>pradara</s> (breach) with the <s>dṛḍhaka</s> (solid); the <s>dṛḍhaka</s> with the <s>asahya</s> (unbearable); the hawk with the bow; the <s>pratiṣṭha</s> with the <s>supratiṣṭha</s>; the <s>saṃjaya</s> with the <s>vijaya</s>; the <s>sthūṇākarṇa</s> with the <s>viśālavijaya</s>; the <s>pāripatantaka</s> with the <s>sarvatobhadra</s>.

children.text: KAZ10.6.43/ durjayena sarvān prativyūheta //
children.translated_text: With the <s>durjaya</s>, one should counter all [formations].

children.text: KAZ10.6.44/ patty.aśva.ratha.dvipānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvam uttareṇa ghātayet, hīna.aṅgam adhika.aṅgena ca^iti //
children.translated_text: Among infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants, each earlier [type] should be struck by each later one, and one with fewer [components] by one with more.

children.text: KAZ10.6.45/ aṅga.daśakasya^ekaḥ patiḥ patikaḥ, patika.daśakasya^ekaḥ senā.patiḥ, tad.daśakasya^eko nāyaka iti //
children.translated_text: The commander of a unit of ten is a <s>patika</s>; of ten <s>patikas</s>, a <s>senāpati</s> (army-captain); of ten of those, a <s>nāyaka</s> (leader).

children.text: KAZ10.6.46/ sa tūrya.ghoṣa.dhvaja.patākābhir vyūha.aṅgānāṃ saṃjñāḥ sthāpayed aṅga.vibhāge saṃghāte sthāne gamane vyāvartane praharaṇe ca //
children.translated_text: He should establish signals for the units of the formation through drum-sounds, flags, and banners — for dividing the units, assembling, stationing, marching, wheeling, and striking.

children.text: KAZ10.6.47/ same vyūhe deśa.kāla.sāra.yogāt siddhiḥ //
children.translated_text: When formations are equal, success [comes] from the [right] combination of terrain, time, and elite [troops].

children.text:
KAZ10.6.48ab/ yantrair upaniṣad.yogais tīkṣṇair vyāsakta.ghātibhiḥ /
KAZ10.6.48cd/ māyābhir deva.samyogaiḥ śakaṭair hasti.bhīṣaṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Through machines, secret devices, poisons, far-reaching weapons, illusions, connections with [what appear to be] divine [forces], carts terrifying to elephants,

children.text:
KAZ10.6.49ab/ dūṣya.prakopair go.yūthaiḥ skandha.āvāra.pradīpanaiḥ /
KAZ10.6.49cd/ koṭī.jaghana.ghātair vā dūta.vyañjana.bhedanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: through inciting corruptible [elements], cattle-herds, setting fire to the camp, strikes at the flank and rear, or breaking [the enemy's resolve] through messages from agents [saying]:

children.text:
KAZ10.6.50ab/ "durgaṃ dagdhaṃ hṛtaṃ vā te kopaḥ kulyaḥ samutthitaḥ /
KAZ10.6.50cd/ śatrur āṭaviko vā" iti parasya^udvegam ācaret //
children.translated_text: 'Your fort has been burned or captured; a revolt of your clan has arisen; or an enemy or a forest chieftain [has attacked]' — thus one should create panic in the enemy.

children.text:
KAZ10.6.51ab/ ekaṃ hanyān na vā hanyād iṣuḥ kṣipto dhanuṣmatā /
KAZ10.6.51cd/ prajñānena tu matiḥ kṣiptā hanyād garbha.gatān api //E
children.translated_text: An arrow shot by an archer may kill one or may not; but a stratagem deployed by intelligence can kill even those [yet] in the womb.

children.text:
(bheda.upādānāni - upāmśu.daṇḍāh)
KAZ11.1.01/ saṃgha.lābho daṇḍa.mitra.lābhānām uttamaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Means of sowing dissension — covert punishments)
The acquisition of a republic (<s>saṃgha</s>) is the greatest of gains through force or allies.

children.text: KAZ11.1.02/ saṃghā hi saṃhatatvād adhṛṣyāḥ pareṣām //
children.translated_text: For republics, being united, are invincible to enemies.

children.text: KAZ11.1.03/ tān anuguṇān bhuñjīta sāma.dānābhyām, viguṇān bheda.daṇḍābhyām //
children.translated_text: Those that are favorable, one should enjoy through conciliation and gifts; those that are hostile, through dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ11.1.04/ kāmboja.surāṣṭra.kṣatriya.śreṇy.ādayo vārtta.śastra.upajīvinaḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāmbojas</s>, <s>Surāṣṭras</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>-guilds, and the like subsist on both trade and arms.

children.text: KAZ11.1.05/ licchivika.vṛjika.mallaka.madraka.kukura.kuru.pāñcāla.ādayo rāja.śabda.upajīvinaḥ //
children.translated_text: The <s>Licchavikas</s>, <s>Vṛjikas</s>, <s>Mallakas</s>, <s>Madrakas</s>, <s>Kukuras</s>, <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Pāñcālas</s>, and the like subsist on the title of king.

children.text: KAZ11.1.06/ sarveṣām āsannāḥ sattriṇaḥ saṃghānāṃ paraspara.nyaṅga.dveṣa.vaira.kalaha.sthānāny upalabhya krama.abhinītaṃ bhedam upacārayeyuḥ "asau tvā vijalpati" iti //
children.translated_text: Stationary spies close to them all should discover grounds for mutual disparagement, hatred, enmity, and quarrel among the republican leaders, and should systematically introduce dissension — [saying] 'So-and-so speaks ill of you.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.07/ evam ubhayato.baddha.roṣāṇāṃ vidyā.śilpa.dyūta.vaihārikeṣv ācārya.vyañjanā bāla.kalahān utpādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, having bound [them] in mutual anger, agents disguised as teachers should stir up quarrels among the youth in schools of learning, crafts, and gambling halls.

children.text: KAZ11.1.08/ veśa.śauṇḍikeṣu vā pratiloma.praśaṃsābhiḥ saṃgha.mukhya.manuṣyāṇāṃ tīkṣṇāḥ kalahān utpādayeyuḥ, kṛtya.pakṣa.upagraheṇa vā //
children.translated_text: Or, in taverns and drinking halls, firebrand agents should stir up quarrels among the republican leaders through backhanded praise, or by winning over the seducible faction.

children.text: KAZ11.1.09/ kumārakān viśiṣṭac.chindikayā hīnac.chindikān utsāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should incite the [aristocratic] young men by showing that those with distinguished emblems are [no better than] those with inferior emblems.

children.text: KAZ11.1.10/ viśiṣṭānāṃ ca^eka.pātraṃ vivāhaṃ vā hīnebhyo vārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And they should prevent the distinguished from sharing a common table or intermarrying with the inferior.

children.text: KAZ11.1.11/ hīnān vā viśiṣṭair eka.pātre vivāhe vā yojayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should compel the inferior to share a table or intermarry with the distinguished.

children.text: KAZ11.1.12/ avahīnān vā tulya.bhāva.upagamane kulataḥ pauruṣataḥ sthāna.viparyāsato vā //
children.translated_text: Or [they should humiliate] those who have been slighted, [suggesting] that they are being treated as equals — [whether the slight is] based on lineage, personal merit, or position.

children.text: KAZ11.1.13/ vyavahāram avasthitaṃ vā pratiloma.sthāpanena niśāmayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should provoke [them] by reversing an established custom or practice.

children.text: KAZ11.1.14/ vivāda.padeṣu vā dravya.paśu.manuṣya.abhighātena rātrau tīkṣṇāḥ kalahān utpādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, on grounds of dispute, firebrand agents should stir up quarrels at night through attacks on property, cattle, or persons.

children.text: KAZ11.1.15/ sarveṣu ca kalaha.sthāneṣu hīna.pakṣaṃ rājā kośa.daṇḍābhyām upagṛhya pratipakṣa.vadhe yojayet //
children.translated_text: In all situations of quarrel, the king, having supported the weaker faction with treasury and army, should employ [it] to destroy the opposing faction.

children.text: KAZ11.1.16/ bhinnān apavāhayed vā //
children.translated_text: Or he should draw away the defeated [faction].

children.text: KAZ11.1.17/ bhūmau ca^eṣāṃ pañca.kulīṃ daśa.kulīṃ vā kṛṣyāyāṃ niveśayet //
children.translated_text: And in [their] territory, he should settle them in groups of five or ten families on agricultural land.

children.text: KAZ11.1.18/ ekasthā hi śastra.grahaṇa.samarthāḥ syuḥ //
children.translated_text: For when they are together [in one place], they would be capable of taking up arms.

children.text: KAZ11.1.19/ samavāye ca^eṣām atyayaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: And he should impose penalties for [their] assembling.

children.text: KAZ11.1.20/ rāja.śabdibhir avaruddham avakṣiptaṃ vā kulyam abhijātaṃ rāja.putratve sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: A clan member who has been imprisoned or humiliated by those [republics] bearing the title of king, [if he is] of noble birth, should be installed in princely rank.

children.text: KAZ11.1.21/ kārtāntika.ādiś ca^asya vargo rāja.lakṣaṇyatāṃ saṃgheṣu prakāśayet //
children.translated_text: And a group of astrologers and the like should publicize his royal marks among the republics.

children.text: KAZ11.1.22/ saṃgha.mukhyāṃś ca dharmiṣṭhān upajapet "sva.dharmam amuṣya rājñaḥ putre bhrātari vā pratipadyadhvam" iti //
children.translated_text: And they should subvert the righteous leaders of the republics [saying]: 'Establish your proper duty through the son or brother of such-and-such a king.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.23/ pratipanneṣu kṛtya.pakṣa.upagraha.artham arthaṃ daṇḍaṃ ca preṣayet //
children.translated_text: When they have agreed, he should send wealth and forces for the purpose of winning over the seducible faction.

children.text: KAZ11.1.24/ vikrama.kāle śauṇḍika.vyañjanāḥ putra.dāra.preta.apadeśena "naiṣecanikam" iti madana.rasa.yuktān madya.kumbhān^śataśaḥ prayaccheyuḥ //
children.translated_text: At the time of attack, agents disguised as tavern-keepers should distribute hundreds of pots of liquor mixed with an intoxicating drug, under the pretext of a son's, wife's, or [relative's] death — [calling it] a 'funeral libation.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.25/ caitya.daivata.dvāra.rakṣā.sthāneṣu ca sattriṇaḥ samaya.karma.nikṣepaṃ sahiraṇya.abhijñāna.mudrāṇi hiraṇya.bhājanāni ca prarūpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And at shrines, deity-temples, gates, and guard-posts, stationary spies should expose [planted] guild-deposits with identifying marks — gold coins and gold vessels bearing [royal] seals.

children.text: KAZ11.1.26/ dṛśyamāneṣu ca saṃgheṣu "rājakīyāḥ" ity āvedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And when the republics see [these items], they should announce: 'These are the king's [property].'

children.text: KAZ11.1.27/ atha^avaskandaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Then he should launch a surprise attack.

children.text: KAZ11.1.28/ saṃghānāṃ vā vāhana.hiraṇye kālike gṛhītvā saṃgha.mukhyāya prakhyātaṃ dravyaṃ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, having seized the transport and gold of the republics at a [vulnerable] time, he should give the well-known property to the republic's leader.

children.text: KAZ11.1.29/ tad eṣāṃ yācite "dattam amuṣmai mukhyāya" iti brūyāt //
children.translated_text: When they come asking for it, he should say: 'It was given to such-and-such a leader.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.30/ etena skandha.āvāra.aṭavī.bhedo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the splitting of a military camp or a forest tribe is explained.

children.text: KAZ11.1.31/ saṃgha.mukhya.putram ātma.sambhāvitaṃ vā sattrī grāhayet "amuṣya rājñaḥ putras tvam, śatru.bhayād iha nyasto^asi" iti //
children.translated_text: Or a stationary spy should convince the son of a republican leader, or one who overestimates himself: 'You are the son of such-and-such a king, deposited here out of fear of enemies.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.32/ pratipannaṃ rājā kośa.daṇḍābhyām upagṛhya saṃgheṣu vikramayet //
children.translated_text: Once [he has] accepted [this identity], the king, having supported him with treasury and army, should use him to attack the hostile [republics].

children.text: KAZ11.1.33/ avāpta.arthas tam api pravāsayet //
children.translated_text: Having achieved the objective, he should exile even him.

children.text: KAZ11.1.34/ bandhakī.poṣakāḥ plavaka.naṭa.nartaka.saubhikā vā praṇihitāḥ strībhiḥ parama.rūpa.yauvanābhiḥ saṃgha.mukhyān unmādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Pimps, divers, actors, dancers, or magicians, [all] planted [as agents], should drive the republican leaders mad with women of supreme beauty and youth.

children.text: KAZ11.1.35/ jāta.kāmānām anyatamasya pratyayaṃ kṛtvā^anyatra gamanena prasabha.haraṇena vā kalahān utpādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When desire has arisen [in several leaders] for one [of these women], by establishing intimacy with one and then departing to another, or by forcibly seizing [her], they should stir up quarrels.

children.text: KAZ11.1.36/ kalahe tīkṣṇāḥ karma kuryuḥ "hato^ayam itthaṃ kāmukaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: In the quarrel, firebrand agents should act: 'This lustful one has been killed in this way.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.37/ visaṃvāditaṃ vā marṣayamāṇam abhisṛtya strī brūyāt "asau māṃ mukhyas tvayi jāta.kāmāṃ bādhate, tasmin^jīvati na^iha sthāsyāmi" iti ghātam asya prayojayet //
children.translated_text: Or a woman, approaching a [leader] who has been deceived and is silently enduring [the slight], should say: 'That leader, while I was in love with you, harasses me. As long as he lives, I will not stay here' — thus she should incite his murder.

children.text: KAZ11.1.38/ prasahya.apahṛtā vā vana.ante kriḍā.gṛhe vā^apahartāraṃ rātrau tīkṣṇena ghātayet, svayaṃ vā rasena //
children.translated_text: Or a [woman] who has been forcibly abducted — in a forest-edge or a pleasure-house — should have the abductor killed at night by a firebrand agent, or [should kill him] herself with poison.

children.text: KAZ11.1.39/ tataḥ prakāśayet "amunā me priyo hataḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Then she should proclaim: 'He killed my beloved.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.40/ jāta.kāmaṃ vā siddha.vyañjanaḥ sāṃvadanikībhir auṣadhībhiḥ saṃvāsya rasena^atisaṃdhāya^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Or an agent disguised as a <s>siddha</s> (accomplished ascetic), having caused [a leader] smitten with desire to cohabit [with a woman] using seductive herbs, should deceive him with poison and depart.

children.text: KAZ11.1.41/ tasminn apakrānte sattriṇaḥ para.prayogam abhiśaṃseyuḥ //
children.translated_text: After his departure, stationary spies should accuse [the dead leader's associates of] an enemy's machination.

children.text: KAZ11.1.42/ āḍhya.vidhavā gūḍha.ājīvā yoga.striyo vā dāya.nikṣepa.arthaṃ vivadamānāḥ saṃgha.mukhyān unmādayeyuḥ, aditi.kauśika.striyo nartakī.gāyanā vā //
children.translated_text: Or wealthy widows, women living by secret means, or female ascetics, disputing over inheritance or deposits, should drive republican leaders mad; or women [known as] <s>Aditi-Kauśika</s>-women, or dancing girls and singers.

children.text: KAZ11.1.43/ pratipannān gūḍha.veśmasu rātri.samāgama.praviṣṭāṃs tīkṣṇā hanyur baddhvā hareyur vā //
children.translated_text: Those who have responded [to the seduction] and entered secret houses for nighttime meetings — firebrand agents should kill them, or bind and carry them off.

children.text: KAZ11.1.44/ sattrī vā strī.lolupaṃ saṃgha.mukhyaṃ prarūpayet "amuṣmin grāme daridra.kullam apasṛtam, tasya strī rāja.arhā, gṛhāṇa^enām" iti //
children.translated_text: Or a stationary spy should inform a republican leader who is lustful: 'In such-and-such a village, a poor family has withdrawn; their woman is worthy of a king — take her.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.45/ gṛhītāyām ardha.māsa.anantaraṃ siddha.vyañjano dūṣya.saṃgha.mukhya.madhye prakrośet "asau me mukhyo bhāryāṃ snuṣāṃ bhaginīṃ duhitaraṃ vā^adhicarati" iti //
children.translated_text: After she has been taken, within a fortnight, an agent disguised as a [member of the] corruptible leader's circle should cry out publicly: 'That leader violates my wife, my daughter-in-law, my sister, or my daughter.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.46/ taṃ cet saṃgho nigṛhṇīyāt, rājā^enam upagṛhya viguṇeṣu vikramayet //
children.translated_text: If the republic restrains him, the king, having taken him under his wing with treasury and army, should use him to attack the hostile [elements].

children.text: KAZ11.1.47/ anigṛhīte siddha.vyañjanaṃ rātrau tīkṣṇāḥ pravāsayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: If [the republic does] not restrain [the leader], firebrand agents should banish the agent [posing as complainant] at night.

children.text: KAZ11.1.48/ tatas tad.vyañjanāḥ prakrośeyuḥ "asau brahmahā brāhmaṇī.jāraś ca" iti //
children.translated_text: Then agents disguised as [his supporters] should cry out: 'He is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-murderer and a seducer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman!'

children.text: KAZ11.1.49/ kārtāntika.vyañjano vā kanyām anyena vṛtām anyasya prarūpayet "amuṣya kanyā rāja.patnī rāja.prasavinī ca bhaviṣyati, sarva.svena prasahya vā^enāṃ labhasva" iti //
children.translated_text: Or an agent disguised as an astrologer should recommend a maiden already betrothed to one man, to another: 'This maiden will be a queen and mother of a king. Obtain her at any cost, even by force.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.50/ alabhyamānāyāṃ para.pakṣam uddharṣayet //
children.translated_text: If she is not obtained, he should incite the opposing faction.

children.text: KAZ11.1.51/ labdhāyāṃ siddhaḥ kalahaḥ //
children.translated_text: If she is obtained, the quarrel is established.

children.text: KAZ11.1.52/ bhikṣukī vā priya.bhāryaṃ mukhyaṃ brūyāt "asau te mukhyo yauvana.utsikto bhāryāyāṃ māṃ prāhiṇot, tasya^ahaṃ bhayāl lekhyam ābharaṇaṃ gṛhītvā^āgatā^asmi, nirdoṣā te bhāryā, gūḍham asmin pratikartavyam, aham api tāvat pratipatsyāmi" iti //
children.translated_text: Or a mendicant woman should tell a leader who is devoted to his wife: 'That leader, intoxicated with youth, has sent me to your wife. Out of fear of him, I came carrying a letter and an ornament [from him]. Your wife is innocent. This must be dealt with secretly. I too shall act accordingly.'

children.text: KAZ11.1.53/ evaṃ.ādiṣu kalaha.sthāneṣu svayam utpanne vā kalahe tīkṣṇair utpādite vā hīna.pakṣaṃ rājā kośa.daṇḍābhyām upagṛhya viguṇeṣu vikramayed apavāhayed vā //
children.translated_text: In such and similar grounds for quarrel — whether a quarrel arises spontaneously or is instigated by firebrand agents — the king, having supported the weaker faction with treasury and army, should attack the hostile [elements] or draw them away.

children.text: KAZ11.1.54/ saṃgheṣv evam eka.rājo varteta //
children.translated_text: Thus should a sole monarch conduct himself toward republics.

children.text: KAZ11.1.55/ saṃghāś ca^apy evam eka.rājād etebhyo^atisaṃghān ebhyo rakṣayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And republics should likewise protect themselves from a sole monarch using these very [methods], and from other more powerful republics.

children.text:
KAZ11.1.56ab/ saṃgha.mukhyaś ca saṃgheṣu nyāya.vṛttir hitaḥ priyaḥ /
KAZ11.1.56cd/ dānto yukta.janas tiṣṭhet sarva.citta.anuvartakaḥ //E
children.translated_text: A republican leader should dwell among the republics — righteous in conduct, beneficial, beloved, self-controlled, with devoted followers, and conforming to the mind of all.

children.text:
(dūta.karma)
KAZ12.1.01/ "balīyasā^abhiyukto durbalaḥ sarvatra^anupraṇato vetasa.dharmā tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text:
(<s>Dūta-karma</s> — The duties of envoys)
A weak king, when attacked by a stronger one, should stand yielding everywhere like a reed — this is the law of the reed.

children.text: KAZ12.1.02/ indrasya hi sa praṇamati yo balīyaso namati" iti bhāradvājaḥ //
children.translated_text: "For he who bows before the stronger bows before <s>Indra</s> himself" — thus says <s>Bhāradvāja</s>.

children.text: KAZ12.1.03/ "sarva.saṃdohena balānāṃ yudhyeta //
children.translated_text: "He should fight with all his collected forces" —

children.text: KAZ12.1.04/ parākramo hi vyasanam apahanti //
children.translated_text: "For valor removes calamity;

children.text: KAZ12.1.05/ sva.dharmaś ca^eṣa kṣatriyasya, yuddhe jayaḥ parājayo vā" iti viśāla.akṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: and this is the <s>svadharma</s> (own duty) of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> — victory or defeat in battle" — thus says <s>Viśālākṣa</s>.

children.text: KAZ12.1.06/ na^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: "Not so," says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ12.1.07/ sarvatra^anupraṇataḥ kulaiḍaka iva nirāśo jīvite vasati //
children.translated_text: One who yields everywhere lives without hope of life, like a castrated ram.

children.text: KAZ12.1.08/ yudhyamānaś ca^alpa.sainyaḥ samudram iva^aplavo^avagāhamānaḥ sīdati //
children.translated_text: And one who fights with a small army perishes, like one plunging into the ocean without a raft.

children.text: KAZ12.1.09/ tad.viśiṣṭaṃ tu rājānam āśrito durgam aviṣahyaṃ vā ceṣṭeta //
children.translated_text: Rather, he should take refuge with a distinguished king or resort to an impregnable fortress and act [from there].

children.text: KAZ12.1.10/ trayo^abhiyoktāro dharma.lobha.asura.vijayina iti //
children.translated_text: There are three types of aggressors — conquerors by <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), by <s>lobha</s> (greed), and by <s>asura</s> (demonic) victory.

children.text: KAZ12.1.11/ teṣām abhyavapattyā dharma.vijayī tuṣyati //
children.translated_text: Of these, the <s>dharma-vijayī</s> (righteous conqueror) is satisfied by submission.

children.text: KAZ12.1.12/ tam abhyavapadyeta, pareṣām api bhayāt //
children.translated_text: One should submit to him, even out of fear of the others.

children.text: KAZ12.1.13/ bhūmi.dravya.haraṇena lobha.vijayī tuṣyati //
children.translated_text: The <s>lobha-vijayī</s> (greedy conqueror) is satisfied by the seizure of land and wealth.

children.text: KAZ12.1.14/ tam arthena^abhyavapadyeta //
children.translated_text: One should submit to him by [offering] wealth.

children.text: KAZ12.1.15/ bhūmi.dravya.putra.dāra.prāṇa.haraṇena^asura.vijayī //
children.translated_text: The <s>asura-vijayī</s> (demonic conqueror) [is satisfied] by the seizure of land, wealth, sons, wives, and lives.

children.text: KAZ12.1.16/ taṃ bhūmi.dravyābhyām upagṛhya^agrāhyaḥ pratikurvīta //
children.translated_text: Against him, having propitiated him with land and wealth, one should make oneself unassailable and retaliate.

children.text: KAZ12.1.17/ teṣām anyatamam uttiṣṭhamānaṃ saṃdhinā mantra.yuddhena kūṭa.yuddhena vā prativyūheta //
children.translated_text: Against any one of these who rises up, one should counter with a treaty, diplomatic warfare, or covert warfare.

children.text: KAZ12.1.18/ śatru.pakṣam asya sāma.dānābhyām, sva.pakṣaṃ bheda.daṇḍābhyām //
children.translated_text: His enemy's faction — [one should win over] through conciliation and gifts; his own faction — through dissension and force.

children.text: KAZ12.1.19/ durgaṃ rāṣṭraṃ skandha.āvāraṃ vā^asya gūḍhāḥ śastra.rasa.agnibhiḥ sādhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Secret agents should destroy his fortress, territory, or military camp by weapons, poison, and fire.

children.text: KAZ12.1.20/ sarvataḥ pārṣṇim asya grāhayet //
children.translated_text: One should cause his rear to be seized from all sides.

children.text: KAZ12.1.21/ aṭavībhir vā rājyaṃ ghātayet, tat.kulīna.aparuddhābhyāṃ vā hārayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should have his kingdom ravaged by forest tribes, or have it seized through a claimant of his dynasty or a besieged [pretender].

children.text: KAZ12.1.22/ apakāra.anteṣu ca^asya dūṭaṃ preṣayet //
children.translated_text: And one should send an envoy to him at the conclusion of hostile acts.

children.text: KAZ12.1.23/ anapakṛtya vā saṃdhānam //
children.translated_text: Or, peace without having inflicted harm.

children.text: KAZ12.1.24/ tathā^apy abhiprayāntaṃ kośa.daṇḍayoḥ pāda.uttaram aho.rātra.uttaraṃ vā saṃdhiṃ yāceta //
children.translated_text: Even so, against one who continues to advance, one should sue for a treaty [by offering] a quarter or more of the treasury and army, or a day-and-night's march worth more.

children.text: KAZ12.1.25/ sa ced daṇḍa.saṃdhiṃ yāceta, kuṇṭham asmai hasty.aśvaṃ dadyād, utsāhitaṃ vā gara.yuktam //
children.translated_text: If he demands a treaty [guaranteed by] army [hostages], one should give him lame elephants and horses, or spirited ones mixed with poison.

children.text: KAZ12.1.26/ puruṣa.saṃdhiṃ yāceta, dūṣya.amitra.aṭavī.balam asmai dadyād yoga.puruṣa.adhiṣṭhitam //
children.translated_text: If he demands a treaty [guaranteed by] men, one should give him corruptible, hostile, or forest-tribal troops supervised by secret agents.

children.text: KAZ12.1.27/ tathā kuryād yathā^ubhaya.vināśaḥ syāt //
children.translated_text: One should arrange it so that the destruction of both [the hostages and the enemy] occurs.

children.text: KAZ12.1.28/ tīkṣṇa.balaṃ vā^asmai dadyād yad avamānitaṃ vikurvīta, maulam anuraktaṃ vā yad asya vyasane^apakuryāt //
children.translated_text: Or one should give him fierce troops who, when insulted, would revolt; or loyal hereditary troops who would harm him in [times of] his calamity.

children.text: KAZ12.1.29/ kośa.saṃdhiṃ yāceta, sāram asmai dadyād yasya kretāraṃ na^adhigacchet, kupyam ayuddha.yogyaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: If he demands a treaty [guaranteed by] treasury, one should give him goods for which no buyer can be found, or raw materials unfit for war.

children.text: KAZ12.1.30/ bhūmi.saṃdhiṃ yāceta, pratyādeyāṃ nitya.amitrām anapāśrayāṃ mahā.kṣaya.vyaya.niveśāṃ vā^asmai bhūmiṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: If he demands a treaty [guaranteed by] territory, one should give him land that is recoverable, perpetually hostile [to the enemy], without refuge, or requiring great expenditure of loss and cost to maintain.

children.text: KAZ12.1.31/ sarva.svena vā rāja.dhānī.varjena saṃdhiṃ yāceta balīyasaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or one should sue for peace from the stronger [king by offering] everything except the capital.

children.text:
KAZ12.1.32ab/ yat prasahya hared anyas tat prayacced upāyataḥ /
KAZ12.1.32cd/ rakṣet sva.dehaṃ na dhanaṃ kā hy anitye dhane dayā //E
children.translated_text:
What another would seize by force, that one should give up by policy;
one should protect one's own body, not wealth — for what compassion is there for transient wealth?

children.text:
(mantra.yuddha)
KAZ12.2.01/ sa cet saṃdhau na^avatiṣṭheta, brūyād enaṃ - "ime śatru.ṣaḍ.varga.vaśagā rājāno vinaṣṭāḥ, teṣām anātmavatāṃ na^arhasi mārgam anugantum //
children.translated_text:
(<s>Mantra-yuddha</s> — Diplomatic warfare)
If he does not abide by a treaty, one should say to him: "These kings, having fallen under the control of the enemy's six-fold circle, have perished. You should not follow the path of those who lacked self-control.

children.text: KAZ12.2.02/ dharmam arthaṃ ca^avekṣasva //
children.translated_text: Consider <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and <s>artha</s> (material gain).

children.text: KAZ12.2.03/ mitra.mukhā hy amitrās te ye tvā sāhasam adharmam artha.atikramaṃ ca grāhayanti //
children.translated_text: For those enemies of yours who appear as friends are the ones who lead you into recklessness, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), and transgression of <s>artha</s>.

children.text: KAZ12.2.04/ śūrais tyakta.ātmabhiḥ saha yoddhuṃ sāhasam, jana.kṣayam ubhayataḥ kartum adharmaḥ, dṛṣṭam arthaṃ mitram aduṣṭaṃ ca tyaktum artha.atikramaḥ //
children.translated_text: To fight alongside heroes who have abandoned their lives is recklessness; to cause destruction of people on both sides is <s>adharma</s>; to abandon visible wealth and an unoffending friend is transgression of <s>artha</s>.

children.text: KAZ12.2.05/ mitravāṃś ca sa rājā, bhūyaś ca^etena^arthena mitrāṇy udyojayiṣyati yāni tvā sarvato^abhiyāsyanti //
children.translated_text: And that king has allies, and with these resources he will mobilize more allies who will attack you from all sides.

children.text: KAZ12.2.06/ na ca madhyama.udāsīnayor maṇḍalasya vā parityaktaḥ, bhavāṃs tu parityaktaḥ yattvā samudyuktam upaprekṣante "bhūyaḥ kṣaya.vyayābhyāṃ yujyatām, mitrāc ca bhidyatām, atha^enaṃ parityakta.mūlaṃ sukhena^ucchetsyāmaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: He has not been abandoned by the <s>madhyama</s> (middle king), the <s>udāsīna</s> (neutral king), or the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle of kings); but you have been abandoned. They watch you, having exerted yourself, [thinking]: 'Let him be further burdened with losses and expenditures, and let him be separated from his ally — then we shall easily destroy him, stripped of his base.'

children.text: KAZ12.2.07/ sa bhavān na^arhati mitra.mukhānām amitrāṇāṃ śrotum, mitrāṇy udvejayitum amitrāṃś ca śreyasā yoktum, prāṇa.saṃśayam anarthaṃ ca^upagantum" iti yacchet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should not listen to those enemies who appear as friends, nor should you alienate [your] allies and join [your] enemies to [your] advantage, nor should you court danger to life and calamity" — thus one should restrain [him].

children.text: KAZ12.2.08/ tathā^api pratiṣṭhamānasya prakṛti.kopam asya kārayed yathā saṃgha.vṛtte vyākhyātaṃ yoga.vāmane ca //
children.translated_text: If he still persists, one should cause sedition among his subjects, as described in the section on the conduct of corporations and on secret instigation.

children.text: KAZ12.2.09/ tīkṣṇa.rasada.prayogaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: And the employment of secret agents with poison.

children.text: KAZ12.2.10/ yad uktam ātma.rakṣitake rakṣyaṃ tatra tīkṣṇān rasadāṃś ca prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: What has been stated in the chapter on self-protection as requiring guarding — there, [against the enemy,] one should employ sharp [agents] and poisoners.

children.text: KAZ12.2.11/ bandhakī.poṣakāḥ parama.rūpa.yauvanābhiḥ strībhiḥ senā.mukhyān unmādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Keepers of courtesans, with women of supreme beauty and youth, should infatuate the enemy's army chiefs.

children.text: KAZ12.2.12/ bahūnām ekasyāṃ dvayor vā mukhyayoḥ kāme jāte tīkṣṇāḥ kalahān utpādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When desire for a single woman arises among many, or between two chiefs, sharp agents should instigate quarrels.

children.text: KAZ12.2.13/ kalahe parājita.pakṣaṃ paratra.apagamane yātrā.sāhāyya.dāne vā bhartur yojayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: In the quarrel, the defeated party should be induced by his master to defect to the other side, or to provide assistance for a military campaign.

children.text: KAZ12.2.14/ kāma.vaśān vā siddha.vyañjanāḥ sāṃvadanikībhir oṣadhībhir atisaṃdhānāya mukhyeṣu rasaṃ dāpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, through the power of lust, agents disguised as accomplished [women] should administer poison to the chiefs through aphrodisiac herbs, for the purpose of entrapment.

children.text: KAZ12.2.15/ vaidehaka.vyañjane vā rāja.mahiṣyāḥ subhagāyāḥ preṣyām āsannāṃ kāma.nimittam arthena^abhivṛṣya parityajet //
children.translated_text: Or, in the guise of a merchant, having lavished wealth on an intimate maid of the queen-consort on account of love, one should then abandon her.

children.text: KAZ12.2.16/ tasya^eva paricāraka.vyañjana.upadiṣṭaḥ siddha.vyañjanaḥ sāṃvadanikīm oṣadhīṃ dadyāt "vaidehaka.śarīre^avaghātavyā" iti //
children.translated_text: An agent, disguised as the same [merchant's] attendant and directed [by him], should give [the maid] an aphrodisiac herb [saying]: "It is to be applied on the merchant's body."

children.text: KAZ12.2.17/ siddhe subhagāyā apy enaṃ yogam upadiśet "rāja.śarīre^avadhātavyā" iti //
children.translated_text: When it works, he should also prescribe the same formula for the queen-consort [saying]: "It is to be applied on the king's body."

children.text: KAZ12.2.18/ tato rasena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Thereby, one should entrap [the king] through poison.

children.text: KAZ12.2.19/ kārtāntika.vyañjano vā mahā.mātraṃ "rāja.lakṣaṇa.sampannam" krama.abhinītaṃ brūyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, an agent disguised as an astrologer should tell a minister that he "possesses the marks of a king," [having been] gradually cultivated.

children.text: KAZ12.2.20/ bhāryām asya bhikṣukī "rāja.patnī rāja.prasavinī vā bhaviṣyasi" iti //
children.translated_text: A female mendicant should tell his wife: "You will become a queen or the mother of a king."

children.text: KAZ12.2.21/ bhāryā.vyañjanā vā mahā.mātraṃ brūyāt "rājā kila mām avarodhayiṣyati, tava^antikāya pattra.lekhyam ābharaṇaṃ ca^idaṃ parivrājikayā^āhṛtam" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, a woman disguised as the [minister's] wife should tell the minister: "The king, it seems, intends to abduct me. This letter and this ornament have been brought to your quarters by a wandering ascetic."

children.text: KAZ12.2.22/ sūda.ārālika.vyañjano vā rasa.prayoga.arthaṃ rāja.vacanam arthaṃ ca^asya lobhanīyam abhinayet //
children.translated_text: Or, an agent disguised as a cook or chef should present a royal command and enticing wealth to him, for the purpose of administering poison.

children.text: KAZ12.2.23/ tad asya vaidehaka.vyañjanaḥ pratisaṃdadhyāt, kārya.siddhiṃ ca brūyāt //
children.translated_text: An agent disguised as a merchant should confirm this to him and speak of the success of the plan.

children.text: KAZ12.2.24/ evam ekena dvābhyāṃ tribhir ity upāyair eka.ekam asya mahā.mātraṃ vikramāya^apagamanāya vā yojayet - iti //
children.translated_text: Thus, by one, two, or three expedients, one should incite each of his ministers individually — either to revolt or to defect.

children.text: KAZ12.2.25/ durgeṣu ca^asya śūnya.pāla.āsannāḥ sattriṇaḥ paura.jānapadeṣu maitrī.nimittam āvedayeyuḥ - "śūnya.pālena^uktā yodhāś ca^adhikaraṇasthāś ca "kṛcchra.gato rājā jīvann āgamiṣyati, na vā, prasahya vittam ārjayadhvam, amitrāṃś ca hata" iti //
children.translated_text: And in his fortresses, spies positioned near the garrison commander should report to the townspeople and countryfolk under the pretext of friendship: "The garrison commander has told the soldiers and magistrates: 'The king is in distress; he may return alive or not. Seize wealth by force and slay the enemies.'"

children.text: KAZ12.2.26/ bahulī.bhūte tīkṣṇāḥ paurān niśāsv āhārayeyuḥ, mukhyāṃś ca^abhihanyuḥ "evaṃ kriyante ye śūnya.pālasya na śuśrūṣante" iti //
children.translated_text: When [the rumor] has spread widely, sharp agents should rob the townspeople at night and kill prominent persons, [saying]: "Thus are treated those who do not obey the garrison commander."

children.text: KAZ12.2.27/ śūnya.pāla.sthāneṣu ca saśoṇitāni śastra.vitta.bandhanāny utsṛjeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And at the stations of the garrison commander, they should leave behind bloodstained weapons, money, and bonds.

children.text: KAZ12.2.28/ tataḥ sattriṇaḥ "śūnya.pālo ghātayati vilopayati ca" ity āvedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then the spies should report: "The garrison commander is having [people] killed and plundered."

children.text: KAZ12.2.29/ evaṃ jānapadān samāhartur bhedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus they should turn the countryfolk against the revenue collector.

children.text: KAZ12.2.30/ samāhartṛ.puruṣāṃs tu grāma.madhyeṣu rātrau tīkṣṇā hatvā brūyuḥ "evaṃ kriyante ye jana.padam adharmeṇa bādhante" iti //
children.translated_text: The sharp agents should kill the revenue collector's men in the midst of villages at night and say: "Thus are treated those who oppress the people with <s>adharma</s> (injustice)."

children.text: KAZ12.2.31/ samutpanne doṣe śūnya.pālaṃ samāhartāraṃ vā prakṛti.kopena ghātayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When trouble has arisen, they should have the garrison commander or revenue collector killed through popular uprising.

children.text: KAZ12.2.32/ tat.kulīnam aparuddhaṃ vā pratipādayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should install a claimant of that dynasty or a besieged [pretender].

children.text:
KAZ12.2.33ab/ antaḥ.pura.pura.dvāraṃ dravya.dhānya.parigrahān /
KAZ12.2.33cd/ daheyus tāṃś ca hanyur vā brūyur asya^ārta.vādinaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
They should burn the inner palace, city gates, and stores of goods and grain;
and kill those [loyal to the enemy], or his agents should proclaim distress.

children.text:
(senā.mukhya.vadhah<dvitīyo bhāgah> - maṇḍala.protsāhanam)
KAZ12.3.01/ rājño rāja.vallabhānāṃ ca^āsannāḥ sattriṇaḥ patty.aśva.ratha.dvipa.mukhyānāṃ "rājā kruddhaḥ" iti suhṛd.viśvāsena mitra.sthānīyeṣu kathayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Slaying of army chiefs — <second part> — Instigation through the circle [of kings])
Spies positioned near the king and the king's favorites should tell the chiefs of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants, in confidential friendship, that "the king is angry [with them]."

children.text: KAZ12.3.02/ bahulī.bhūte tīkṣṇāḥ kṛta.rātri.cāra.pratīkārā gṛheṣu "svāmi.vacanena^āgamyatām" iti brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When [the rumor] has spread, sharp agents, having prepared countermeasures against night patrols, should go to their houses [and say]: "Come, by the master's command."

children.text: KAZ12.3.03/ tānnirgacchata eva^abhihanyuḥ, "svāmi.saṃdeśaḥ" iti ca^āsannān brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should strike them down as they come out, and tell those nearby: "[This is] the master's order."

children.text: KAZ12.3.04/ ye ca^apravāsitās tān sattriṇo brūyuḥ "etat tad yad asmābhiḥ kathitam, jīvitu.kāmena^apakrāntavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: And those who have not [yet] fled — spies should tell them: "This is what we had warned of. One who wishes to live must flee."

children.text: KAZ12.3.05/ yebhyaś ca rājā yācito na dadāti tān sattriṇo brūyuḥ - "uktaḥ śūnya.pālo rājñā "ayācyam artham asau ca^asau ca mā yācate, mayā pratyākhyātāḥ śatru.saṃhitāḥ, teṣām uddharaṇe prayatasva" iti //
children.translated_text: And those from whom the king has refused requests — spies should tell them: "The garrison commander has been told by the king: 'So-and-so keeps asking for things that should not be requested. They have been rejected by me as being in league with the enemy. Endeavor to eliminate them.'"

children.text: KAZ12.3.06/ tataḥ pūrvavad ācaret //
children.translated_text: Then one should proceed as before.

children.text: KAZ12.3.07/ yebhyaś ca rājā yācito dadāti tān sattriṇo brūyuḥ - "uktaḥ śūnya.pālo rājñā "ayācyam artham asau ca^asau ca mā yācate, tebhyo mayā so^artho viśvāsa.arthaṃ dattaḥ, śatru.saṃhitāḥ, teṣām uddharaṇe prayatasva" iti //
children.translated_text: And those from whom the king grants requests — spies should tell them: "The garrison commander has been told by the king: 'So-and-so keeps asking for things that should not be requested. I have given them what they asked for to win their trust. They are in league with the enemy. Endeavor to eliminate them.'"

children.text: KAZ12.3.08/ tataḥ pūrvavad ācaret //
children.translated_text: Then one should proceed as before.

children.text: KAZ12.3.09/ ye ca^enaṃ yācyam arthaṃ na yācante tān sattriṇo brūyuḥ - "uktaḥ śūnya.pālo rājñā "yācyam artham asau ca^asau ca mā na yācate, kim anyat sva.doṣa.śaṅkitatvāt, teṣām uddharaṇe prayatasva" iti //
children.translated_text: And those who do not request what is rightfully requestable — spies should tell them: "The garrison commander has been told by the king: 'So-and-so does not request what may be requested. What else [can this mean] except that they suspect their own guilt? Endeavor to eliminate them.'"

children.text: KAZ12.3.10/ tataḥ pūrvavad ācaret //
children.translated_text: Then one should proceed as before.

children.text: KAZ12.3.11/ etena sarvaḥ kṛtya.pakṣo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, the entire category of subvertible persons is explained.

children.text: KAZ12.3.12/ pratyāsanno vā rājānaṃ sattrī grāhayet "asau ca^asau ca te mahā.mātraḥ śatru.puruṣaiḥ sambhāṣate" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, a spy positioned near the king should cause him to seize [certain ministers, saying]: "Such-and-such minister of yours is in communication with enemy agents."

children.text: KAZ12.3.13/ pratipanne dūṣyān asya śāsana.harān darśayet "etat tat" iti //
children.translated_text: When [the king] is convinced, one should show him corruptible agents carrying [forged] orders, [saying]: "This is the proof."

children.text: KAZ12.3.14/ senā.mukhya.prakṛti.puruṣān vā bhūmyā hiraṇyena vā lobhayitvā sveṣu vikramayed apavāhayed vā //
children.translated_text: Or, having tempted the enemy's army chiefs and chief subjects with land or gold, one should cause them to revolt [and join one's own side] or to desert.

children.text: KAZ12.3.15/ yo^asya putraḥ samīpe durge vā prativasati taṃ sattriṇā^upajāpayet "ātma.sampannataras tvaṃ putraḥ, tathā^apy antar.hitaḥ, tat.kim upekṣase vikramya gṛhāṇa, purā tvā yuva.rājo vināśayati" iti //
children.translated_text: Whichever son of his resides near him or in a fortress — a spy should instigate him: "You are a worthier son, yet you are kept hidden. Why do you tolerate this? Seize [power] by force before the crown prince destroys you."

children.text: KAZ12.3.16/ tat.kulīnam aparuddhaṃ vā hiraṇyena pratilobhya brūyāt "antar.balaṃ pratyanta.skandham antaṃ vā^asya pramṛdnīhi" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, having tempted a claimant of that dynasty or a besieged [pretender] with gold, one should say: "Crush his interior forces, frontier garrisons, or bring about his end."

children.text: KAZ12.3.17/ āṭavikān artha.mānābhyām upagṛhya rājyam asya ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Having won over the forest chieftains with wealth and honors, he should have [the enemy's] kingdom destroyed.

children.text: KAZ12.3.18/ pārṣṇi.grāhaṃ vā^asya brūyāt "eṣa khalu rājā mām ucchidya tvām ucchetsyati, pārṣṇim asya gṛhāṇa, tvayi nivṛttasya^ahaṃ pārṣṇiṃ grahīṣyāmi" iti //
children.translated_text: Or he should tell [the enemy's] rear-attacker: 'This king will surely destroy you after uprooting me. Attack his rear; when he turns back against you, I will seize his rear.'

children.text: KAZ12.3.19/ mitrāṇi vā^asya brūyāt "ahaṃ vaḥ setuḥ, mayi vibhinne sarvān eṣa vo rājā plāvayiṣyati, sambhūya vā^asya yātrāṃ vihanāma" iti //
children.translated_text: Or he should tell [the enemy's] allies: 'I am your bridge; if I am broken, this king will overwhelm all of you. Or let us jointly obstruct his campaign.'

children.text: KAZ12.3.20/ tat.saṃhatānām asaṃhatānāṃ ca preṣayet "eṣa khalu rājā mām utpāṭya bhavatsu karma kariṣyati, budhyadhvam, ahaṃ vaḥ śreyān abhyupapattum" iti //
children.translated_text: To those who are united and those who are not, he should send [the message]: 'This king, after uprooting me, will act against you. Be aware — I am better able to come to your aid.'

children.text:
KAZ12.3.21ab/ madhyamasya prahiṇuyād udāsīnasya vā punaḥ /
KAZ12.3.21cd/ yathā^āsannasya mokṣa.arthaṃ sarva.svena tad.arpaṇam //E
children.translated_text: He should send [a message] to the <s>madhyama</s> (neutral king) or again to the <s>udāsīna</s> (indifferent king), offering everything to the nearest one for the sake of liberation.

children.text:
(śastra.agni.rasa.praṇidhayah - vīvadhā.sāra.prrasāra.vadhah)
KAZ12.4.01/ ye ca^asya durgeṣu vaidehakavyañjanāḥ, grāmesu gṛhapatika.vyañjanāḥ, jana.pada.saṃdhiṣu go.rakṣaka.tāpasa.vyañjanāḥ, te sāmanta.āṭavika.tat.kulīna.aparuddhānāṃ paṇya.āgāra.pūrvaṃ preṣayeyuḥ "ayaṃ deśo hāryaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text:
(Agents using weapons, fire, and poison — destruction through supply-train raids)
Those of his [agents] who are disguised as traders in the forts, as householders in the villages, and as cowherds and ascetics at the borders of the countryside — they should send [word] to the frontier lords, forest chieftains, kinsmen, and disaffected persons, first [establishing] trading posts, [saying]: 'This territory is to be seized.'

children.text: KAZ12.4.02/ āgatāṃś ca^eṣāṃ durge gūḍha.puruṣān artha.mānābhyām abhisatkṛtya prakṛtic.chidrāṇi pradarśayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And when those [allies] arrive, the secret agents in the fort should honor them with wealth and honors and reveal the vulnerabilities of the [enemy's] constituent elements.

children.text: KAZ12.4.03/ teṣu taiḥ saha prahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Among those, they should strike together with them.

children.text: KAZ12.4.04/ skandha.āvāre vā^asya śauṇḍika.vyañjanaḥ putram abhityaktaṃ sthāpayitvā^avaskanda.kāle rasena pravāsayitvā "naiṣecanikam" iti madana.rasa.yuktān madyakumbhān^śataśaḥ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, in his military camp, [an agent] disguised as a liquor-seller, having placed an ostensibly banished son, at the time of assault, having intoxicated [the enemy troops] with poison, saying 'It is a ceremonial offering,' should distribute hundreds of liquor pots mixed with <s>madana</s> (intoxicating) poison.

children.text: KAZ12.4.05/ śuddhaṃ vā madyaṃ pādyaṃ vā madyaṃ dadyād ekam ahaḥ, uttaraṃ ras.siddhaṃ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Or he should give pure liquor or watered-down liquor on one day, and on the next provide [liquor] mixed with poison.

children.text: KAZ12.4.06/ śuddhaṃ vā madyaṃ daṇḍa.mukhyebhyaḥ pradāya mada.kāle rasa.siddhaṃ prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Or having given pure liquor to the army commanders, at the time of intoxication, he should provide poison-mixed [liquor].

children.text: KAZ12.4.07/ daṇḍa.mukhya.vyañjano vā putram abhityaktam iti samānam //
children.translated_text: Or [an agent] disguised as an army commander with an ostensibly banished son — the same [procedure applies].

children.text: KAZ12.4.08/ pākva.māṃsika.audanika.auṇḍika.āpūpika.vyañjanā vā paṇya.viśeṣam avaghoṣayitvā paraspara.saṃgharṣeṇa kālikaṃ samarghataram iti vā parān āhūya rasena sva.paṇyāny apacārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as sellers of cooked meat, porridge, spirits, and cakes, having announced a special sale, through mutual competition [saying] 'the seasonal [goods] are cheaper,' or having invited others, should spoil their own wares with poison.

children.text: KAZ12.4.09/ surā.kṣīra.dadhi.sarpis.tailāni vā tad.vyavahartṛ.hasteṣu gṛhītā striyo bālāś ca rasa.yukteṣu sva.bhājaneṣu parikireyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should distribute liquor, milk, curds, ghee, and oils in their own poison-laced vessels through women and children obtained by those who deal in such commodities.

children.text: KAZ12.4.10/ "anena^argheṇa, viśiṣṭaṃ vā bhūyo dīyatām" iti tatra^eva^avākireyuḥ //
children.translated_text: 'At this price, or let even more of the superior [quality] be given' — thus they should scatter [the poisoned goods] right there.

children.text: KAZ12.4.11/ etāny eva vaidehaka.vyañjanāḥ, paṇya.vireyeṇa^āhartāro vā //
children.translated_text: These same [methods apply to agents] disguised as traders, or importers who bring goods for resale.

children.text: KAZ12.4.12/ hasty.aśvānāṃ vidhā.yavaseṣu rasam āsannā dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Those stationed nearby should administer poison in the grass and fodder for elephants and horses.

children.text: KAZ12.4.13/ karma.kara.vyañjanā vā rasa.aktaṃ yavasam udakaṃ vā vikrīṇīran //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as laborers should sell poison-smeared fodder or water.

children.text: KAZ12.4.14/ cira.saṃsṛṣṭā vā go.vāṇijakā gavām aja.avīnāṃ vā yūthāny avaskanda.kāleṣu pareṣāṃ moha.sthāneṣu pramuñceyuḥ, aśva.khara.uṣṭramahiṣa.ādīnāṃ duṣṭāṃś ca //
children.translated_text: Or cattle-traders who have long been associated [with the enemy camp] should release herds of cattle, goats, and sheep at the time of assault into the enemy's vulnerable positions, along with maddened horses, donkeys, camels, and buffaloes.

children.text: KAZ12.4.15/ tad.vyañjanā vā cucchundarī.śoṇita.akta.akṣān //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as those [cattle-traders should release animals] with eyes smeared with musk-shrew blood.

children.text: KAZ12.4.16/ lubdhaka.vyañjanā vā vyāla.mṛgān pañjarebhyaḥ pramuñceyuḥ, sarpa.grāhā vā sarpān ugra.viṣān, hasti.jīvino vā hastinaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as hunters should release wild beasts from cages; snake-catchers should release highly venomous serpents; elephant-keepers should release elephants.

children.text: KAZ12.4.17/ agni.jīvino vā^agnim avasṛjeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or fire-workers should let loose fire.

children.text: KAZ12.4.18/ gūḍha.puruṣā vā vimukhān patty.aśva.ratha.dvipa.mukhyān abhihanyuḥ, ādīpayeyur vā mukhya.āvāsān //
children.translated_text: Or secret agents should strike down the leaders of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants when they are routed, or set fire to the quarters of the chief officers.

children.text: KAZ12.4.19/ dūṣya.amitra.āṭavika.vyañjanāḥ praṇihitāḥ pṛṣṭha.abhighātam avaskanda.pratigrahaṃ vā kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Agents deployed as <s>dūṣyas</s> (corruptible persons), enemy agents, or forest-tribe agents should deliver attacks from the rear or receive the assault [as fifth-columnists].

children.text: KAZ12.4.20/ vana.gūḍhā vā pratyanta.skandham upaniṣkṛṣya^abhihanyuḥ, eka.ayane vīvadha.āsāra.prasārān vā //
children.translated_text: Or those hidden in the forest, having drawn out a flank column, should strike it down, or [strike down] supply-train raids and outposts on a single route.

children.text: KAZ12.4.21/ sasaṃketaṃ vā rātri.yuddhe bhūri.tūryam āhatya brūyuḥ "anupraviṣṭāḥ smo, labdhaṃ rājyam" iti //
children.translated_text: Or in night battle, with a pre-arranged signal, having sounded many war-drums, they should proclaim: 'We have entered! The kingdom is won!'

children.text: KAZ12.4.22/ rāja.āvāsam anupraviṣṭā vā saṃkuleṣu rājānaṃ hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or having entered the royal quarters, they should kill the king in the confusion.

children.text: KAZ12.4.23/ sarvato vā prayātam ena(?eva?) mleccha.āṭavika.daṇṭa.cāriṇaḥ sattra.apāśrayāḥ stambha.vāṭa.apāśrayā vā hanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, when [the enemy] has marched out in all directions, <s>Mleccha</s> and forest-tribe soldiers serving as roving patrols, sheltered in sacrificial halls or post-enclosures, should slay [him].

children.text: KAZ12.4.24/ lubdhaka.vyañjanā vā^avaskanda.saṃkuleṣu gūḍha.yuddha.hetubhir abhihanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or [agents] disguised as hunters should strike [the enemy] during the confusion of an assault, using concealed weapons.

children.text: KAZ12.4.25/ eka.ayane vā śaila.stambha.vāṭa.khañjana.antar.udake vā sva.bhūmi.balena^abhihanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or on a single route — at rocky defiles, post-enclosures, marshy ground, or underwater [crossings] — they should strike with forces familiar with the terrain.

children.text: KAZ12.4.26/ nadī.saras.taṭāka.setu.bandha.bheda.vegena vā plāvayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should flood [the enemy] by breaking the embankments of rivers, lakes, reservoirs, and dams.

children.text: KAZ12.4.27/ dhānvana.vana.durga.nimna.durgasthaṃ vā yoga.agni.dhūmābhyāṃ nāśayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should destroy [the enemy] trapped in desert-forts, forest-forts, or low-lying forts with magical fire and smoke.

children.text: KAZ12.4.28/ saṃkaṭa.gatam agninā, dhānvana.gataṃ dhūmena, nidhāna.gataṃ rasena, toya.avagāḍhaṃ duṣṭa.grāhair udaka.caraṇair vā tīkṣṇāḥ sādhayeyuḥ, ādīpta.āvāsān niṣpatantaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Or the fierce [agents] should dispatch — one trapped in a narrow pass with fire, one in a desert with smoke, one in a hiding place with poison, one submerged in water with vicious crocodiles or aquatic [creatures], or one fleeing from a burning dwelling.

children.text:
KAZ12.4.29ab/ yoga.vāmana.yogābhyāṃ yogena^anyatamena vā /
KAZ12.4.29cd/ amitram atisaṃdadhyāt saktam uktāsu bhūmiṣu //E
children.translated_text: By the combination of stratagem and ruse, by stratagem alone, or by some other [means], one should outwit the enemy entangled in the aforementioned terrains.

children.text:
(yoga.atisamdhānam - daṇḍa.atisamdhānam - eka.vijayah)
KAZ12.5.01/ daiva.tejyāyām(devatā.ijyāyām?) yātrāyām amitrasya bahūni pūjā.āgama.sthānāni bhaktitaḥ //
children.translated_text:
(Outwitting through stratagem — outwitting through force — sole victory)
During the enemy's campaign for worship of deities, [he has] many places of worship and pilgrimage approached with devotion.

children.text: KAZ12.5.02/ tatra^asya yogam ubjayet //
children.translated_text: There one should set a trap for him through stratagem.

children.text: KAZ12.5.03/ devatā.gṛha.praviṣṭasya^upari yantra.mokṣaṇena gūḍha.bhittiṃ śilāṃ vā pātayet //
children.translated_text: When [the enemy] has entered a temple, one should drop upon him a concealed stone or a wall-slab by releasing a mechanism from above.

children.text: KAZ12.5.04/ śilā.śastra.varṣam uttama.āgārāt, kapāṭam avapātitaṃ vā, bhitti.praṇihitam eka.deśa.baddhaṃ vā parighaṃ mokṣayet //
children.translated_text: A shower of stones and weapons from an upper story, or a dropped gate-panel, or a bar set in the wall and fastened at one end — one should release [it].

children.text: KAZ12.5.05/ devatā.deha.dhvaja.praharaṇāni vā^asya^upariṣṭāt pātayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should cause the body [images], banners, and weapons of the deity to fall upon him from above.

children.text: KAZ12.5.06/ sthāna.āsana.gamana.bhūmiṣu vā^asya go.maya.pradehena gandha.udaka.prasekena vā rasam aticārayet, puṣpa.cūrṇa.upahāreṇa vā //
children.translated_text: Or on the ground where he stands, sits, or walks, one should apply poison through cow-dung plaster, sprinkling of scented water, or offering of flowers and powders.

children.text: KAZ12.5.07/ gandha.praticchannaṃ vā^asya tīkṣṇaṃ dhūmam atinayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should convey to him pungent smoke concealed by incense.

children.text: KAZ12.5.08/ śūlakūpam avapātanaṃ vā śayana.āsanasya^adhastād yantra.baddha.talam enaṃ kīla.mokṣaṇena praveśayet //
children.translated_text: A spiked pit or a trapdoor — a mechanism-fastened floor beneath his bed or seat — one should make him fall through by releasing the bolt.

children.text: KAZ12.5.09/ pratyāsanne vā^amitre jana.padāj janam avarodha.kṣamam atinayet //
children.translated_text: Or when the enemy is near, one should evacuate the people capable of withstanding siege from the countryside.

children.text: KAZ12.5.10/ durgāc ca^anavarodha.kṣamam apanayet, pratyādeyam ari.viṣayaṃ vā preṣayet //
children.translated_text: And those incapable of withstanding siege should be removed from the fort, or sent to enemy territory as returnable [agents].

children.text: KAZ12.5.11/ jana.padaṃ ca^ekasthaṃ śaila.vana.nadī.durgeṣv aṭavī.vyavahiteṣu vā putra.bhrātṛ.parigṛhītaṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: And the population should be settled in one place — in hill-forts, forest-forts, or river-forts, or [places] separated by wilderness — under the charge of sons and brothers.

children.text: KAZ12.5.12/ uparodha.hetavo daṇḍa.upanata.vṛtte vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: The causes of besiegement are explained in the section on conduct toward a power-submitting [king].

children.text: KAZ12.5.13/ tṛṇa.kāṣṭham ā.yojanād dāhayet //
children.translated_text: One should burn grass and firewood up to a <s>yojana</s> [around].

children.text: KAZ12.5.14/ udakāni ca dūṣayet, avasrāvayec ca //
children.translated_text: And one should poison the water supplies and drain them off.

children.text: KAZ12.5.15/ kūpa.kūṭa.avapāta.kaṇṭakinīś ca bahir ubjayet //
children.translated_text: And outside, one should set up wells, camouflaged pits, pitfalls, and thorn-barriers.

children.text: KAZ12.5.16/ suruṅgām amitra.sthāne bahu.mukhīṃ kṛtvā nicaya.mukhyān abhihārayet, amitraṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Having made a multi-entrance tunnel to the enemy's position, one should bring in the chief warriors of the garrison, or [bring out] the enemy [for capture].

children.text: KAZ12.5.17/ para.prayuktāyāṃ vā suruṅgāyāṃ parikhām udaka.antikīṃ khānayet, kūpa.śālām anusālaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Or in a tunnel dug by the enemy, one should dig a ditch reaching the water, or a well-chamber or a row of wells.

children.text: KAZ12.5.18/ toya.kumbhān kāṃsya.bhāṇḍāni vā śaṅkā.sthāneṣu sthāpayet khāta.abhijñāna.artham //
children.translated_text: One should place water-jars or bronze vessels at suspected spots for the purpose of detecting excavation.

children.text: KAZ12.5.19/ jñāte suruṅgā.pathe pratisuruṅgāṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: When the tunnel path is discovered, one should have a counter-tunnel dug.

children.text: KAZ12.5.20/ madhye bhittvā dhūmam udakaṃ vā prayacchet //
children.translated_text: Having broken through in the middle, one should send in smoke or water.

children.text:
KAZ12.5.21/ prativihita.durgo vā mūle dāyād<am> kṛtvā pratilomām asya diśaṃ gacchet, yato vā mitrair bandhubhir āṭavikair vā saṃsṛjyeta parasya^amitrair dūṣyair vā mahadbhiḥ, yato vā gato^asya mitrair viyogaṃ kuryāt pārṣṇiṃ vā gṛhṇīyāt rājyaṃ vā^asya hārayet vīvadha.āsāra.prasārān vā vārayet, yato vā śaknuyād ākṣikavad apakṣepeṇa^asya prahartum, yato vā
svaṃ rājyaṃ trāyeta mūlasya^upacayaṃ vā kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having secured his fort against counter-measures, having placed an heir at the capital, he should march in the direction opposite to the enemy — to where he can unite with allies, kinsmen, or forest chiefs who are enemies of the other, or with great <s>dūṣyas</s> (disaffected elements); or going from where he can cause the enemy's separation from allies, or seize his rear, or capture his kingdom, or block supply-train raids and outposts; or from where he can strike the enemy glancingly like a dice-player; or from where he can protect his own kingdom or augment the base.

children.text: KAZ12.5.22/ yataḥ saṃdhim abhipretaṃ labheta tato vā gacchet //
children.translated_text: Or he should go in the direction from which he may obtain a desired treaty.

children.text: KAZ12.5.23/ saha.prasthāyino vā^asya preṣayeyuḥ "ayaṃ te śatrur asmākaṃ hasta.gataḥ, paṇyaṃ viprakāraṃ vā^apadiśya hiraṇyam antaḥ.sāra.balaṃ ca preṣaya yasya^enam arpayema baddhaṃ pravāsitaṃ vā" iti //
children.translated_text: Or his marching companions should send [a message]: 'This enemy of yours has fallen into our hands. On the pretext of trade or tribute, send gold and a core force, so that we may deliver him to you, bound or exiled.'

children.text: KAZ12.5.24/ pratipanne hiraṇyaṃ sāra.balaṃ ca^ādadīta //
children.translated_text: When [the enemy] has complied, one should seize the gold and the core force.

children.text: KAZ12.5.25/ anta.pālo vā durga.sampradāne bala.eka.deśam atinīya viśvastaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or a border-guard, having led away a portion of the force on the pretext of surrendering the fort, should slay [the enemy] when he is trusting.

children.text: KAZ12.5.26/ jana.padam ekasthaṃ vā ghātayitum amitra.anīkam āvāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or to destroy the concentrated population, one should draw in the enemy's army.

children.text: KAZ12.5.27/ tad avaruddha.deśam atinīya viśvastaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Having led [the enemy] away to the occupied territory, one should slay him when he is trusting.

children.text: KAZ12.5.28/ mitra.vyañjano vā bāhyasya preṣayet "kṣīṇam asmin durge dhānyaṃ snehāḥ kṣāro lavaṇaṃ vā, tad amuṣmin deśe kāle ca pravekṣyati, tad upagṛhāṇa" iti //
children.translated_text: Or [an agent] disguised as a friend of the external [enemy] should send [word]: 'In this fort, the grain, oils, alkali, or salt are exhausted. He will enter at such a place and time — so seize him.'

children.text: KAZ12.5.29/ tato rasa.viddhaṃ dhānyaṃ snehaṃ kṣāraṃ lavaṇaṃ vā dūṣya.amitra.āṭavikāḥ praveśayeyuḥ, anye vā^abhityaktāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then <s>dūṣyas</s> (corruptible agents), enemy agents, and forest-tribe agents should introduce poison-tainted grain, oil, alkali, or salt — or others ostensibly banished.

children.text: KAZ12.5.30/ tena sarva.bhāṇḍa.vīvadha.grahaṇaṃ vyākhyātam //
children.translated_text: By this, the seizure of all goods and supply-trains is explained.

children.text: KAZ12.5.31/ saṃdhiṃ vā kṛtvā hiraṇya.eka.deśam asmai dadyāt, vilambamānaḥ śeṣam //
children.translated_text: Or having made a treaty, one should give him a portion of the gold, delaying the remainder.

children.text: KAZ12.5.32/ tato rakṣā.vidhānāny avasrāvayet //
children.translated_text: Then one should undermine [the enemy's] security arrangements.

children.text: KAZ12.5.33/ agni.rasa.śastrair vā praharet //
children.translated_text: Or one should strike with fire, poison, and weapons.

children.text: KAZ12.5.34/ hiraṇya.pratigrāhiṇo vā^asya vallabhān anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or one should win over the enemy's favorites who accept gold.

children.text: KAZ12.5.35/ parikṣīṇo vā^asmai durgaṃ dattvā nirgacchet //
children.translated_text: Or, when exhausted, one should surrender the fort to him and depart.

children.text: KAZ12.5.36/ suruṅgayā kukṣi.pradareṇa vā prākāra.bhedena nirgacchet //
children.translated_text: One should escape through a tunnel, by breaching a side-wall, or by breaking through the rampart.

children.text: KAZ12.5.37/ rātrāv avaskandaṃ dattvā siddhas tiṣṭhet, asiddhaḥ pārśvena^apagacchet //
children.translated_text: Having launched a night assault, if successful one should stand firm; if unsuccessful, one should retreat by a side route.

children.text: KAZ12.5.38/ pāṣaṇḍac.chadmanā manda.parivāro nirgacchet //
children.translated_text: Disguised as an ascetic with a small retinue, one should escape.

children.text: KAZ12.5.39/ preta.vyañjano vā gūḍhair nihriyeta //
children.translated_text: Or disguised as a corpse, one should be secretly carried out by hidden [agents].

children.text: KAZ12.5.40/ strī.veṣa.dhārī vā pretam anugacchet //
children.translated_text: Or wearing women's garments, one should follow a funeral procession.

children.text: KAZ12.5.41/ daivata.upahāra.śrāddha.prahavaṇeṣu vā rasa.viddham anna.pānam avasṛjya //
children.translated_text: Or at divine offerings, <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral) ceremonies, and oblations, having released poison-laced food and drink,
