children.text: KAZ12.5.42/ kṛta.upajāpo dūṣya.vyañjanair niṣpatya gūḍha.sainyo^abhihanyāt //
children.translated_text: having subverted [the enemy's men] and escaped with agents disguised as <s>dūṣyas</s>, with a concealed army, one should strike.

children.text: KAZ12.5.43/ evaṃ gṛhīta.durgo vā prāśya.prāśaṃ caityam upasthāpya daivata.pratimāc.chidraṃ praviśya^āsīta, gūḍha.bhittiṃ vā, daivata.pratimā.yuktaṃ vā bhūmi.gṛham //
children.translated_text: Or, if the fort is thus captured, gradually consuming [remaining supplies], having set up a shrine, one should enter through a hollow in the deity's image and remain there — or in a concealed wall-chamber, or in an underground room fitted with a deity's image.

children.text: KAZ12.5.44/ vismṛte suruṅgayā rātrau rāja.āvāsam anupraviśya suptam amitraṃ hanyāt //
children.translated_text: When [the enemy] is off guard, one should enter the royal quarters at night through a tunnel and slay the sleeping enemy.

children.text: KAZ12.5.45/ yantra.viśleṣaṇaṃ vā viśleṣya^adhastād avapātayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having loosened a mechanism, one should cause [the enemy] to fall through [a trap] below.

children.text: KAZ12.5.46/ rasa.agni.yogena^avaliptaṃ gṛhaṃ jatu.gṛhaṃ vā^adhiśayānam amitram ādīpayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should set ablaze a dwelling smeared with fire-poison mixture, or a lac-house, while the enemy sleeps within.

children.text: KAZ12.5.47/ pramada.vana.vihārāṇām anyatame vā vihāra.sthāne pramattaṃ bhūmi.gṛha.suruṅgā.gūḍha.bhitti.praviṣṭās tīkṣṇā hanyuḥ, gūḍha.praṇihitā vā rasena //
children.translated_text: Or, at one of the pleasure-garden promenades or other recreational spots, assassins (<s>tīkṣṇāḥ</s>) who have entered through underground chambers, tunnels, or concealed walls should kill him when off guard; or agents secretly deployed [should kill him] with poison.

children.text: KAZ12.5.48/ svapato vā niruddhe deśe gūḍhāḥ striyaḥ sarpa.rasa.agni.dhūmān upari muñceyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, while he sleeps in a secured area, concealed women should release snakes, poison, fire, or smoke from above.

children.text: KAZ12.5.49/ pratyutpanne vā kāraṇe yad yad upapadyeta tat tad amitre^antaḥ.pura.gate gūḍha.saṃcāraḥ prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Or, when an occasion arises, whatever is feasible — that the secret operative should employ against the enemy who has entered the inner apartments.

children.text: KAZ12.5.50/ tato gūḍham eva^apagacchet, svajana.saṃjñāṃ ca prarūpayet //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, he should depart secretly and give the pre-arranged signal to his own people.

children.text:
KAZ12.4.51ab/ dvāhsthān varṣadharāṃś ca^anyān nigūḍha.upahitān pare /
KAZ12.4.51cd/tūrya.saṃjñābhir āhūya dviṣat.śeṣāṇi ghātayet //E
children.translated_text: Having summoned the gate-guards and other sentinels who have been secretly planted by the enemy, using musical signals, one should slay the remaining [forces] of the enemy.

children.text:
(upajāpah)
KAZ13.1.01/ vijigīṣuḥ para.grāmam avāptu.kāmaḥ sarvajña.daivata.samyoga.khyāpanābhyāṃ sva.pakṣam uddharṣayet, para.pakṣaṃ ca^udvejayet //
children.translated_text:
(<s>Upajāpa</s> — Instigation)
The <s>vijigīṣu</s> (would-be conqueror), desiring to gain the enemy's territory, should inspire his own side and alarm the enemy's side through displays of omniscience and divine connections.

children.text: KAZ13.1.02/ sarvajña.khyāpanaṃ tu - gṛha.guhya.pravṛtti.jñānena pratyādeśo mukhyānām, kaṇṭaka.śodhana.apasarpa.avagamena prakāśanaṃ rāja.dviṣṭa.kāriṇām, vijñāpya.upāyana.khyāpanam adṛṣṭa.saṃsarga.vidyā.saṃjñā.ādibhiḥ, videśa.pravṛtti.jñānaṃ tad ahar eva gṛha.kapotena mudrā.samyuktena //
children.translated_text: The display of omniscience [consists of]: impressing the chiefs through knowledge of household secrets and private affairs; exposing those who act against the king through intelligence from <s>kaṇṭaka-śodhana</s> (anti-criminal operations) and secret agents; displaying acknowledged offerings and gifts through unseen contacts, secret sciences, and signals; and knowing events in foreign lands that very day through a homing pigeon bearing a sealed message.

children.text:
KAZ13.1.03/ daivata.samyoga.khyāpanaṃ tu - suruṅgā.mukhena^agni.caitya.daivata.pratimāc.chidrān anupraviṣṭair agni.caitya.daivata.vyañjanaiḥ sambhāṣaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ ca, udakād utthitair vā nāga.varuṇa.vyañjanaiḥ sambhāṣaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ ca, rātrāv antar.udake samudra.vālukā.kośaṃ praṇidhāya^agni.mālā.darśanam, śilā.śikya.avagṛhīte plavake sthānam, udaka.bastinā
jarāyuṇā vā śiro^avagūḍha.nāsaḥ pṛṣata.antra.kulīra.nakra.śiṃśumāra.udravasābhir vā śata.pākyaṃ tailaṃ nastaḥ prayogaḥ //
children.translated_text: The display of divine connection [consists of]: conversation and worship with figures bearing the marks of <s>Agni</s>, sacred shrines, and deities — who have entered through openings in fire-shrines, sacred trees, and deity images via tunnel mouths; or conversation and worship with figures bearing the marks of <s>Nāga</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> who have risen from water; at night, placing a luminous ocean-sand gem under water to create the appearance of a garland of fire; standing on a float suspended from a stone sling; and the application of oil boiled a hundred times through the nostrils, with the head submerged using a water-bladder or a membrane, breathing through the intestines of a deer, crab, crocodile, porpoise, or otter.

children.text: KAZ13.1.04/ tena rātri.gaṇaś carati //
children.translated_text: By this [method], one can move about at night [under water].

children.text: KAZ13.1.05/ ity udaka.caraṇāni //
children.translated_text: These are the techniques of moving in water.

children.text: KAZ13.1.06/ tair varuṇa.nāga.kanyā.vākya.kriyā sambhāṣaṇaṃ ca, kopa.sthāneṣu mukhād agni.dhūma.utsargaḥ //
children.translated_text: Through these, one performs the speech and actions [attributed to] <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Nāga</s>-maidens, and conducts conversations [with them]; at places of discontent, one releases fire and smoke from the mouth.

children.text: KAZ13.1.07/ tad asya sva.viṣaye kārtāntika.naimittika.mauhūrtika.paurāṇika.ikṣaṇika.gūḍha.puruṣāḥ sācivya.karās tad.darśinaś ca prakāśayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: His secret agents disguised as astrologers, interpreters of omens, horoscopists, <s>Purāṇa</s>-reciters, and palmists should publicize these [divine displays] in his own territory, and act as ministers witnessing them.

children.text: KAZ13.1.08/ parasya viṣaye daivata.darśanaṃ divya.kośa.daṇḍa.utpattiṃ ca^asya brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: In the enemy's territory, they should proclaim the [king's] divine visions and the appearance of celestial treasures and armies.

children.text: KAZ13.1.09/ daivata.praśna.nimitta.vāyasa.aṅga.vidyā.svapna.mṛga.pakṣi.vyāhāreṣu ca^asya vijayaṃ brūyuḥ, viparītam amitrasya //
children.translated_text: In divination queries, omens, crow-augury, dream-interpretation, and animal and bird utterances, they should proclaim his victory — and the opposite for the enemy.

children.text: KAZ13.1.10/ sadundubhim ulkāṃ ca parasya nakṣatre darśayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should display a meteor with drumbeat directed at the enemy's constellation.

children.text: KAZ13.1.11/ parasya mukhyān mitratvena^upadiśanto dūta.vyañjanāḥ svāmi.satkāraṃ brūyuḥ, sva.pakṣa.bala.ādhānaṃ para.pakṣa.pratighātaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Those disguised as envoys, presenting themselves as friends to the enemy's chiefs, should speak of the master's honor, the strengthening of his own faction, and the undermining of the enemy's faction.

children.text: KAZ13.1.12/ tulya.yoga.kṣemam amātyānām āyudhīyānāṃ ca kathayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should tell the [enemy's] ministers and military officers of the equal prosperity and security [available on the conqueror's side].

children.text: KAZ13.1.13/ teṣu vyasana.abhyudaya.avekṣaṇam apatya.pūjanaṃ ca prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Toward them, he should employ attentiveness to their misfortunes and successes, and honor to their offspring.

children.text: KAZ13.1.14/ tena para.pakṣam utsāhayed yathā.uktaṃ purastāt //
children.translated_text: By this, he should incite the enemy's faction, as previously described.

children.text: KAZ13.1.15/ bhūyaś ca vakṣyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: And we shall explain further.

children.text:
KAZ13.1.16/ sādhāraṇa.gardabhena dakṣān, lakuṭa.śākhā.hananābhyāṃ daṇḍa.cāriṇaḥ, kula.eḍakena ca^udvignān, aśani.varṣeṇa vimānitān, vidulena^avakeśinā vāyasa.piṇḍena kaitavaja.meghena^iti vihata.āśān durbhaga.alaṃkāreṇa dveṣiṇā^iti pūjā.phalān, vyāghra.carmaṇā mṛtyu.kūṭena ca^upahitān, pīlu.vikhādanena karaka.yoṣṭrayā gardabhī.kṣīrā.abhimanthanena^iti
dhruva.upakāriṇa iti //
children.translated_text: Through the 'shared donkey' [trick, one wins over] the capable; through beating with clubs and branches, the wandering ascetics; through the 'clan ram' [trick], the anxious; through thunderbolt and rain, the humiliated; through the reed-screen, the shaven-headed, the crow-offering, and the sham-cloud — those whose hopes are shattered; through the ornament-of-misfortune, the hateful — thus [winning over] those who [seek] fruits of honor; through the tiger-skin and death-contrivance, those who are endangered; through the <s>pīlu</s>-fruit gnawing, the hail-brick, and the churning of donkey's milk — those who are permanent allies.

children.text:
KAZ13.1.17/ pratipannān artha.mānābhyāṃ yojayet
KAZ13.1.18/ dravya.bhaktac.chidreṣu ca^enān dravya.bhakta.dānair anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text:
Those who have come over should be employed with wealth and honor.
And he should reward them with gifts of money and provisions when there are gaps in their supplies and rations.

children.text: KAZ13.1.19/ apratigṛhṇatāṃ strī.kumāra.alaṃkārān abhihareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: For those who do not accept, [agents] should send ornaments for their women and children.

children.text: KAZ13.1.20/ durbhikṣa.stena.aṭavy.upaghāteṣu ca paura.jānapadān utsāhayantaḥ sattriṇo brūyuḥ "rājānam anugrahaṃ yācāmahe^ niranugrahāḥ paratra gacchāmaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And in times of famine, robbery, and forest-tribe attacks, charitable agents, inciting the townspeople and countryfolk, should say: 'Let us petition the king for assistance — if we receive no aid, we shall depart elsewhere.'

children.text:
KAZ13.1.21ab/ tathā^iti pratipanneṣu dravya.dhānyāny aparigrahaiḥ /
KAZ13.1.21cd/ sācivyaṃ kāryam ity etad upajāpād bhūtaṃ mahat //E
children.translated_text: When they agree, [agents] with no possessions should provide money and grain, and [declare] that assistance should be rendered — this great [result] is accomplished through instigation.

children.text:
(yoga.vāmanam)
KAZ13.2.01/ muṇḍo jaṭilo vā parvata.guha.āvāsī catur.varṣa.śata.āyur bruvāṇaḥ prabhūta.jaṭila.ante.vāsī nagara.abhyāśe tiṣṭhet //
children.translated_text:
(<s>Yoga-vāmana</s> — Deceptive stratagems)
A shaven or matted-haired [ascetic], dwelling in a mountain cave, claiming to be four hundred years old, with many matted-haired disciples, should station himself near the city.

children.text: KAZ13.2.02/ śiṣyāś ca^asya mūla.phala.upagamanair amātyān rājānaṃ ca bhagavad.darśanāya yojayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: His disciples, through offerings of roots and fruits, should arrange for the ministers and the king to come for an audience with the holy one.

children.text: KAZ13.2.03/ samāgatāś ca rājñā pūrva.rāja.deśa.abhijñānāni kathayet, "śate śate ca varṣāṇāṃ pūrṇe^aham agniṃ praviśya punar bālo bhavāmi, tad iha bhavat samīpe caturtham agniṃ pravekṣyāmi, avaśyaṃ me bhavān mānayitavyaḥ, trīn varān vṛṇīṣṇa(vṛṣīṣva)" iti //
children.translated_text: When they have assembled, he should tell the king about identifying marks of previous kings and lands, [saying]: 'Every hundred years, I enter the fire and become young again. Now I shall enter the fire for the fourth time in your presence. You must honor me. Choose three boons.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.04/ pratipannaṃ brūyāt "sapta.rātram iha saputra.dāreṇa prekṣā.prahavaṇa.pūrvaṃ vastavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: To the one who agrees, he should say: 'You must stay here for seven nights with your wife and children, preceded by festivities and spectacles.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.05/ vasantam avaskandeta //
children.translated_text: While he stays, one should attack him.

children.text: KAZ13.2.06/ muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā sthānika.vyañjanaḥ prabhūta.jaṭila.ante.vāsī vasta.śoṇita.digdhāṃ veṇu.śalākāṃ suvarṇa.cūrṇena^avalipya valmīke nidadhyād upajihvika.anusaraṇa.artham, svarṇa.nālikāṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Or, a shaven or matted-haired [agent] bearing the marks of a local [deity], with many matted-haired disciples, should place in an anthill a bamboo stick smeared with goat's blood, coated with gold dust, for the purpose of attracting followers — or a golden tube.

children.text: KAZ13.2.07/ tataḥ sattrī rājñaḥ kathayet "asau siddhaḥ puṣpitaṃ nidhiṃ jānāti" iti //
children.translated_text: Then an operative should tell the king: 'That accomplished one knows of a blossoming treasure.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.08/ sa rājñā pṛṣṭhaḥ "tathā" iti brūyāt, tac ca^abhijñānaṃ darśayet, bhūyo vā hiraṇyam antar.ādhāya //
children.translated_text: When questioned by the king, he should say 'Indeed so,' and show the proof — or again, after secretly placing gold inside.

children.text: KAZ13.2.09/ brūyāc ca^enaṃ "nāga.rakṣito^ayaṃ nidhiḥ praṇipāta.sādhyaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: And he should tell him: 'This treasure is guarded by <s>Nāgas</s> and can be obtained only through prostration.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.10/ pratipannaṃ brūyāt "sapta.rātram" iti samānam //
children.translated_text: To the one who agrees, he should say 'seven nights' — the same [procedure as before].

children.text: KAZ13.2.11/ sthānika.vyañjanaṃ vā rātrau tejana.agni.yuktam ekānte tiṣṭhantaṃ sattriṇaḥ krama.abhīnītaṃ rājñaḥ kathayeyuḥ "asau siddhaḥ sāmedhikaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, [an agent] bearing the marks of a local [deity], standing alone at night with a fire-tipped shaft — operatives, having gradually brought [the king's attention to him], should tell the king: 'That accomplished one possesses magical prosperity.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.12/ taṃ rājā yam arthaṃ yāceta tam asya kariṣyamāṇaḥ "sapta.rātram" iti samānam //
children.translated_text: Whatever the king should ask of him, [the agent] promising to accomplish it — 'seven nights' — the same [as before].

children.text: KAZ13.2.13/ siddha.vyañjano vā rājānaṃ jambhaka.vidyābhiḥ pralobhayet //
children.translated_text: Or, one disguised as an adept should entice the king with spellbinding arts.

children.text: KAZ13.2.14/ taṃ rājā^iti samānam //
children.translated_text: The king, to him — the same [procedure as before].

children.text: KAZ13.2.15/ siddha.vyañjano vā deśa.devatām abhyarhitām āśritya prahavaṇair abhīkṣṇaṃ prakṛti.mukhyān abhisaṃvāsya krameṇa rājānam atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, one disguised as an adept, relying on a revered regional deity, through spectacles should gradually cultivate the prominent subjects and then deceive the king.

children.text: KAZ13.2.16/ jaṭila.vyañjanam antar.udaka.vāsinaṃ vā sarva.śvetaṃ taṭa.suruṅgā.bhūmi.gṛha.apasaraṇaṃ varuṇaṃ nāga.rājaṃ vā sattriṇaḥ krama.abhinītaṃ rājñaḥ kathayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, operatives should tell the king about one bearing the mark of a matted-haired [ascetic], or one dwelling under water, all white, with an escape route through a bank-tunnel or underground chamber — [describing him as] <s>Varuṇa</s> or <s>Nāga-rāja</s>, having gradually introduced [the sighting].

children.text: KAZ13.2.17/ taṃ rājā^iti samānam //
children.translated_text: The king, to him — the same [procedure as before].

children.text: KAZ13.2.18/ jana.pada.ante.vāsī siddha.vyañjano vā rājānaṃ śatru.darśanāya yojayet //
children.translated_text: Or, an adept-looking [agent] dwelling at the border of the countryside should arrange for the king to come to see the enemy.

children.text: KAZ13.2.19/ pratipannaṃ bimbaṃ kṛtvā śatrum āvāhayitvā niruddhe deśe ghātayet //
children.translated_text: When he agrees, [the agent] should make an image, invoke the enemy [into it], and in a secured area, slay [the king].

children.text: KAZ13.2.20/ aśva.paṇya.upayātā vaidehaka.vyañjanāḥ paṇya.upāyana.nimittam āhūya rājānaṃ paṇya.parīkṣāyām āsaktam aśva.vyatikīrṇaṃ vā hanyuḥ, aśvaiś ca prahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, those disguised as merchants who have arrived with horse-merchandise, having summoned the king on the pretext of examining the goods and presenting gifts, should kill him while he is engrossed in inspecting the merchandise or mingled among the horses — and they should attack with the horses.

children.text: KAZ13.2.21/ nagara.abhyāśe vā caityam āruhya rātrau tīkṣṇāḥ kumbheṣu nālīn vā vidulāni dhamantaḥ "svāmino mukhyānāṃ vā māṃsāni bhakṣayiṣyāmaḥ, pūjā no vartatām" ity avyaktaṃ brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, near the city, assassins who have climbed a sacred tree should, at night, blowing through pipes or reed-screens into pots, say indistinctly: 'We shall devour the flesh of the lord and the chiefs — let worship be performed for us.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.22/ tad eṣāṃ naimittika.mauhūrtika.vyañjanāḥ khyāpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: That [proclamation], those disguised as astrologers and horoscopists should make widely known.

children.text: KAZ13.2.23/ maṅgalye vā hrade taṭāka.madhye vā rātrau tejana.taila.abhyaktā nāga.rūpiṇaḥ śakti.musalāny ayomayāni niṣpeṣayantas tathaiva brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, at night, in a sacred tank or in the middle of a reservoir, [agents] in the form of <s>Nāgas</s>, anointed with luminous oil, striking iron maces and pestles, should proclaim the same.

children.text: KAZ13.2.24/ ṛkṣa.carma.kañcukino vā^agni.dhūma.utsarga.yuktā rakṣo.rūpaṃ vahantas trir apasavyaṃ nagaraṃ kurvāṇāḥ śva.sṛgāla.vāśita.antareṣu tathaiva brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, those wearing bear-skin jackets, equipped with fire-and-smoke devices, assuming the form of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, circling the city thrice counter-clockwise, should proclaim the same between the howlings of dogs and jackals.

children.text: KAZ13.2.25/ caitya.daivata.pratimāṃ vā tejana.tailena^abhra.paṭalac.channena^agninā vā rātrau prajvālya tathaiva brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, at night, having set ablaze a sacred-tree shrine or deity image with fire concealed by a cloud-like covering and luminous oil, they should proclaim the same.

children.text: KAZ13.2.26/ tad anye khyāpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Others should publicize that.

children.text: KAZ13.2.27/ daivata.pratimānām abhyarhitānāṃ vā śoṇitena prasrāvam atimātraṃ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, they should cause excessive bleeding from revered deity images with blood.

children.text: KAZ13.2.28/ tad anye deva.rudhira.saṃsrāve saṃgrāme parājayaṃ brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Others should then proclaim that the divine blood-flow portends defeat in battle.

children.text: KAZ13.2.29/ saṃdhi.rātriṣu śmaśāna.pramukhe vā caityam ūrdhva.bhakṣitair manuṣyaiḥ prarūpayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: On conjunction-nights or before cremation grounds, they should display a sacred tree with humans [appearing to be] eaten from above.

children.text: KAZ13.2.30/ tato rakṣo.rūpī manuṣyakaṃ yāceta //
children.translated_text: Then one in <s>Rākṣasa</s> form should demand a human [sacrifice].

children.text: KAZ13.2.31/ yaś ca^atra śūra.vādiko^anyatamo vā draṣṭum āgacchet tam anye loha.musalair hanyuḥ, yathā rakṣobhir hata iti jñāyeta //
children.translated_text: And whoever — some boastful hero or another — comes to see, others should strike him down with iron pestles, so that it is understood he was killed by <s>Rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: KAZ13.2.32/ tad adbhutaṃ rājñas tad.darśinaḥ sattriṇaś ca kathayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: That marvel, witnesses and operatives should report to the king.

children.text: KAZ13.2.33/ tato naimititka.mauhūrtika.vyañjanāḥ śāntiṃ prāyaś.cittaṃ brūyuḥ "anyathā mahad akuśalaṃ rājño deśasya ca" iti //
children.translated_text: Then those disguised as omen-readers and horoscopists should prescribe pacificatory rites and expiations, [saying]: 'Otherwise, great misfortune [will befall] the king and the realm.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.34/ pratipannaṃ "eteṣu sapta.rātram eka.eka.mantra.bali.homaṃ svayaṃ rājñā kartavyam" iti brūyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When he agrees, they should say: 'For seven nights, the king himself must perform the invocation, offering, and fire-oblation for each of these, one by one.'

children.text: KAZ13.2.35/ tataḥ samānam //
children.translated_text: Then — the same [procedure as before].

children.text: KAZ13.2.36/ etān vā yogān ātmani darśayitvā pratikurvīta pareṣām upadeśa.artham //
children.translated_text: Or, having displayed these very stratagems against oneself, one should counter them — for the purpose of instructing the enemy's [people].

children.text: KAZ13.2.37/ tataḥ prayojayed yogān //
children.translated_text: Then one should employ the [actual] stratagems.

children.text: KAZ13.2.38/ yoga.darśana.pratīkāreṇa vā kośa.abhisaṃharaṇaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: Or, through displaying and countering stratagems, one should gather treasure.

children.text: KAZ13.2.39/ hasti.kāmaṃ vā nāga.vana.pālā hastinā lakṣaṇyena pralobhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, elephant-forest-keepers should entice one who desires elephants with a fine specimen.

children.text: KAZ13.2.40/ pratipannaṃ gahanam eka.ayanaṃ vā^atinīya ghātayeyuḥ, baddhvā vā^apahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When he agrees, they should lead him into a dense or single-path [forest] and have him killed — or capture him bound.

children.text: KAZ13.2.41/ tena mṛgayā.kāmo vyākhyātaḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, [the stratagem for] one who desires hunting is also explained.

children.text: KAZ13.2.42/ dravya.strī.lolupam āḍhya.vidhavābhir vā parama.rūpa.yauvanābhiḥ strībhir dāya.nikṣepa.artham upanītābhiḥ sattriṇaḥ pralobhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, operatives should entice one who is greedy for wealth and women with rich widows or women of supreme beauty and youth, brought on the pretext of depositing or entrusting property.

children.text: KAZ13.2.43/ pratipannaṃ rātrau sattrac.channāḥ samāgame śastra.rasābhyāṃ ghātayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: When he agrees, [agents] concealed within the venue should kill him at the rendezvous with weapons and poison, at night.

children.text: KAZ13.2.44/ siddha.pravrajita.caitya.stūpa.daivata.pratimānām abhīkṣṇa.abhigamaneṣu vā bhūmi.gṛha.suruṅga.ārūḍha.bhitti.praviṣṭās tīkṣṇāḥ param abhihanyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, during frequent visits to [images of] accomplished ascetics, wandering monks, sacred trees, <s>stūpas</s>, and deity images, assassins who have entered through underground chambers, tunnels, or scaled walls should strike the enemy.

children.text:
KAZ13.2.45ab/ yeṣu deśeṣu yāḥ prekṣāḥ prekṣate pārthivaḥ svayam /
KAK13.2.45cd/ yātrā.vihāre ramate yatra krīḍati vā^ambhasi //
children.translated_text: Whatever spectacles the king himself watches in which places, and whatever pilgrimages or excursions he enjoys, and wherever he sports in water —

children.text:
KAZ13.2.46ab/ dhig.ukty.ādiṣu sarveṣu yajña.prahavaṇeṣu vā /
KAZ13.2.46cd/ sūtikā.preta.rogeṣu prīti.śoka.bhayeṣu vā /
KAZ13.2.47ab/ pramādaṃ yāti yasmin vā viśvāsāt sva.jana.utsave //
children.translated_text: In all [occasions involving] verbal abuse and the like, sacrificial ceremonies, childbirth, death, illness, joy, grief, or fear, or when he becomes careless due to trust at a celebration of his own people —

children.text:
KAZ13.2.47cd/ yatra^asya^ārakṣi.saṃcāro durdine saṃkuleṣu vā /
KAZ13.2.48ab/ vipra.sthāne pradīpte vā praviṣṭe nirjane^api vā /
KAZ13.2.48cd/ vastra.ābharaṇa.mālyānāṃ phelābhiḥ śayana.āsanaiḥ //
children.translated_text: where his movements are unguarded, in bad weather or tumultuous occasions, when his dwelling is ablaze or when he has entered a deserted [place] — with discarded garments, ornaments, and garlands, with beds and seats,

children.text:
KAZ13.2.49ab/ madya.bhojana.phelābhis tūryair vā^abhigatāḥ saha /
KAZ13.2.49cd/ prahareyur ariṃ tīkṣṇāḥ pūrva.praṇihitaiḥ saha //E
KAZ13.2.50ab/ yathaiva praviśeyuś ca dviṣataḥ sattra.hetubhiḥ /
KAZ13.2.50cd/ tathaiva ca^apagaccheyur ity uktaṃ yoga.vāmanam //
children.translated_text:
with discarded liquor and food, or with musical instruments — fierce agents, together with those previously planted, should strike the enemy.
Just as they enter the enemy's [quarters] under pretexts of religious sessions, so too should they withdraw — this is called the stratagem of 'emetic' [<s>yoga-vāmana</s>].

children.text:
(apasarpa.praṇidhih)
KAZ13.3.01/ śreṇī.mukhyam āptaṃ niṣpātayet //
children.translated_text:
(Deployment of secret agents)
He should cause a trusted guild-chief to defect [to the enemy].

children.text: KAZ13.3.02/ sa param āśrtya pakṣa.apadeśena sva.viṣayāt sācivya.kara.sahāya.upādānaṃ kurvīta //
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge with the enemy under the pretext of faction, he should obtain from his [the enemy's] territory the position of minister, tax-collector, or military aide.

children.text: KAZ13.3.03/ kṛta.apasarpa.upacayo vā param anumānya svāmino dūṣya.grāmaṃ vīta.hasty.aśvaṃ dūṣya.amātyaṃ daṇḍam ākrandaṃ vā hatvā parasya preṣayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having accumulated a force of secret agents and gained the enemy's confidence, he should slay the master's disloyal troops, those without elephants and horses, or the disloyal minister's corps or the frontier force, and deliver [them] to the enemy.

children.text: KAZ13.3.04/ jana.pada.eka.deśaṃ śreṇīm aṭavīṃ vā sahāya.upādāna.arthaṃ saṃśrayeta //
children.translated_text: He should take shelter in a section of the countryside, a guild, or a forest tribe for the purpose of gathering allies.

children.text: KAZ13.3.05/ viśvāsam upagataḥ svāminaḥ preṣayet //
children.translated_text: Having gained [the enemy's] trust, he should send [intelligence] to his master.

children.text: KAZ13.3.06/ tataḥ svāmī hasti.bandhanam aṭavī.ghātaṃ vā^apadiśya gūḍham eva praharet //
children.translated_text: Then the master, under the pretext of capturing elephants or raiding the forest, should strike covertly.

children.text: KAZ13.3.07/ etena^amātya.aṭavikā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, [the deployment of] ministers and forest chiefs [as secret agents] is explained.

children.text: KAZ13.3.08/ śatruṇā maitrīṃ kṛtvā^amātyān avakṣipet //
children.translated_text: Having made friendship with the enemy, he should cause [his own] ministers to be dismissed.

children.text: KAZ13.3.09/ te tat.śatroḥ preṣayeyuḥ "bhartāraṃ naḥ prasādaya" iti //
children.translated_text: They should send [word] to that enemy: 'Reconcile us with our master.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.10/ sa yaṃ dūtaṃ preṣayet, tam upālabheta "bhartā te mām amātyair bhedayati, na ca punar iha^āgantavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: He should reproach whatever envoy [the enemy] sends: 'Your master is trying to divide me from my ministers — do not come here again.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.11/ atha^ekam amātyaṃ niṣpātayet //
children.translated_text: Then he should cause one minister to defect [to the enemy].

children.text: KAZ13.3.12/ sa param āśritya yoga.apasarpa.aparakta.dūṣyān aśaktimataḥ stena^āṭavikān ubhaya.upaghātakān vā parasya^upaharet //
children.translated_text: Having taken refuge with the enemy, he should deliver to the enemy [people who are] agents provocateurs, disaffected persons, disloyal elements, weaklings, thieves, forest brigands, or those who harm both sides.

children.text: KAZ13.3.13/ āpta.bhāva.upagataḥ pravīra.puruṣa.upaghātam asya^upahared anta.pālam āṭavikaṃ daṇḍa.cāriṇaṃ vā "dṛḍham asau ca^asau ca te śatruṇā saṃdhatte" iti //
children.translated_text: Having gained trusted status, he should arrange the assassination of the enemy's valiant men, or [undermine] the frontier governor, the forest chief, or the army commander, [telling them]: 'So-and-so and so-and-so are firmly allied with your enemy.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.14/ atha paścād abhityakta.śāsanair enān ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Then afterward, he should have them slain by those who have [seemingly] renounced their allegiance.

children.text: KAZ13.3.15/ daṇḍa.bala.vyavahāreṇa vā śatrum udyojya ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or, by provoking the enemy through a display of military force, he should have him destroyed.

children.text: KAZ13.3.16/ kṛtya.pakṣa.upagraheṇa vā parasya.amitraṃ rājānam ātmany apakārayitvā^abhiyuñjīta //
children.translated_text: Or, by winning over the enemy's faction through cultivated partisans, having instigated a hostile king against the enemy, he should attack.

children.text: KAZ13.3.17/ tataḥ parasya preṣayet "asau te vairī mama^apakaroti, tam ehi sambhūya haniṣyāvaḥ, bhūmau hiraṇye vā te parigrahaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Then he should send [word] to the enemy: 'That adversary of yours is harming me — come, let us join forces and destroy him; you shall have the territory or the gold.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.18/ pratipannam abhisatkṛtya^āgatam avaskandena prakāśayuddhena vā śatruṇā ghātayet //
children.translated_text: When [the enemy king] has agreed and arrived, he should have [him] destroyed by the [hostile] king through a surprise attack or open battle.

children.text: KAZ13.3.19/ abhiviśvāsana.arthaṃ bhūmi.dāna.putra.abhiṣeka.rakṣā.apadeśena vā grāhayet //
children.translated_text: Or, for the purpose of winning trust, he should seize [the enemy] under the pretext of granting territory, anointing his son, or providing protection.

children.text: KAZ13.3.20/ aviṣahyam upāṃśu.daṇḍena vā ghātayet //
children.translated_text: If [the enemy is] irresistible, he should have [him] destroyed through covert punishment.

children.text: KAZ13.3.21/ sa ced daṇḍaṃ dadyān na svayam āgacchet tam asya vairiṇā ghātayet //
children.translated_text: If [the enemy] would send [only] an army but not come himself, [the agent] should have him slain by his [own] adversary.

children.text: KAZ13.3.22/ daṇḍena vā prayātum icchen na vijigīṣuṇā tathā^apy enam ubhayataḥ.sampīḍanena ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or if [the enemy] wishes to march with an army but not with the would-be conqueror, even so he should have him destroyed by squeezing from both sides.

children.text: KAZ13.3.23/ aviśvasto vā pratyekaśo yātum icched rājya.eka.deśaṃ vā yātavyasya^ādātu.kāmaḥ, tathā^apy enaṃ vairiṇā sarva.saṃdohena vā ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or if [the enemy], being distrustful, wishes to march separately, or wishes to take a portion of the kingdom of the one to be attacked — even so, he should have him destroyed by the adversary or by a general mobilization.

children.text: KAZ13.3.24/ vairiṇā vā saktasya daṇḍa.upanayena mūlam anyato hārayet //
children.translated_text: Or while [the enemy] is engaged with the adversary, he should seize his base through an advancing force.

children.text: KAZ13.3.25/ śatru.bhūmyā vā mitraṃ paṇeta, mitra.bhūmyā vā śatrum //
children.translated_text: Or he should barter the enemy's territory for [the support of] an ally, or the ally's territory for [neutralizing] the enemy.

children.text: KAZ13.3.26/ tataḥ śatru.bhūmi.lipsāyāṃ mitreṇa^ātmany apakārayitvā^abhiyuñjīta - iti samānāḥ pūrveṇa sarva eva yogāḥ //
children.translated_text: Then, when desiring the enemy's territory, having instigated the ally to harm [the enemy] and attacked — all these stratagems are similar to the foregoing.

children.text: KAZ13.3.27/ śatruṃ vā mitra.bhūmi.lipsāyāṃ pratipannaṃ daṇḍena^anugṛhṇīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or he should support with [his] army the enemy who has agreed to seek the ally's territory.

children.text: KAZ13.3.28/ tato mitra.gatam atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Then he should double-cross [the enemy] who has gone to the ally.

children.text: KAZ13.3.29/ kṛta.pratividhāno vā vyasanam ātmano darśayitvā mitreṇa^amitram utsāhayitvā^ātmānam abhiyojayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having made counter-preparations and displaying his own calamity, having induced the ally to incite the enemy, he should get [the enemy] to attack himself.

children.text: KAZ13.3.30/ tataḥ sampīḍanena ghātayet, jīva.grāheṇa vā rājya.vinimayaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: Then he should destroy [the enemy] by squeezing, or through live capture compel an exchange of kingdoms.

children.text: KAZ13.3.31/ mitreṇa^āśritaś cet^śatrur agrāhye sthātum icchet sāmanta.ādibhir mūlam asya hārayet //
children.translated_text: If the enemy, having taken refuge with the ally, wishes to remain in an unassailable [position], he should seize his base through neighboring kings and others.

children.text: KAZ13.3.32/ daṇḍena vā trātum ichet tam asya ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or if [the ally] wishes to rescue [the enemy] with military force, he should have that [ally] destroyed.

children.text: KAZ13.3.33/ tau cen na bhidyeyātāṃ prakāśam eva^anyonya.bhūmyā paṇeta //
children.translated_text: If those two cannot be divided, he should openly barter with each other's territory.

children.text: KAZ13.3.34/ tataḥ parasparaṃ mitra.vyañjanā vā ubhaya.vetanā vā dūtān preṣayeyuḥ "ayaṃ te rājā bhūmiṃ lipsate śatru.saṃhitaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Then they should send emissaries to each other, disguised as friends or as agents receiving wages from both, [saying]: 'This king, allied with [your] enemy, seeks your territory.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.35/ tayor anyataro jāta.āśaṅka.āroṣaḥ, pūrvavac ceṣteta //
children.translated_text: Whichever of the two becomes suspicious and angry, he should act as before.

children.text: KAZ13.3.36/ durga.rāṣṭra.daṇḍa.mukhyān vā kṛtya.pakṣa.hetubhir abhivikhyāpya pravrājayet //
children.translated_text: Or he should publicly denounce and exile the chiefs of the fort, the countryside, and the army through cultivated partisan motives.

children.text: KAZ13.3.37/ te yuddha.avaskanda.avarodha.vyasaneṣu śatrum atisaṃdadhyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should then double-cross the enemy during battles, surprise attacks, sieges, and calamities.

children.text: KAZ13.3.38/ bhedaṃ vā^asya sva.vargebhyaḥ kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or they should create dissension among [the enemy's] own faction.

children.text: KAZ13.3.39/ abhityakta.śāsanaiḥ pratisamānayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who have [seemingly] renounced their allegiance should bring them back [under control].

children.text: KAZ13.3.40/ lubdhaka.vyañjanā vā māṃsa.vikrayeṇa dvāhsthā dauvārika.apāśrayāś cora.abhyāgamaṃ parasya dvis trir iti nivedya labdha.pratyayā bhartur anīkaṃ dvidhā niveśya grāma.vadhe^avaskande ca dviṣato brūyuḥ "āsannaś cora.gaṇaḥ, mahāṃś ca^ākrandaḥ, prabhūtaṃ sainyam āgacchatu" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, disguised as hunters and selling meat, gate-guards under the protection of the chief doorkeeper, having reported the approach of thieves to the enemy two or three times and gained his trust, should divide the master's army in two and, during a village raid and surprise attack, tell the enemy: 'The bandit gang is nearby and the alarm is great — send a large force.'

children.text: KAZ13.3.41/ tad arpayitvā grāma.ghāta.daṇḍasya sainyam itarad ādāya rātrau durga.dvāreṣu brūyuḥ "hataś cora.gaṇaḥ, siddha.yātram idaṃ sainyam āgatam, dvāram apāvriyatām" iti //
children.translated_text: Having dispatched that [force] against the village-raiding army, they should take the other [remaining] force and at night announce at the fort gates: 'The bandit gang has been destroyed — this victorious army has returned — open the gates!'

children.text: KAZ13.3.42/ pūrva.praṇihitā vā dvārāṇi dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or agents previously planted should open the gates.

children.text: KAZ13.3.43/ taiḥ saha prahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Together with them, they should attack.

children.text: KAZ13.3.44/ kāru.śilpi.pāṣaṇḍa.kuśīlava.vaidehaka.vyañjanān āyudhīyān vvā para.durge praṇidadhyāt //
children.translated_text: He should plant armed agents in the enemy's fort disguised as artisans, craftsmen, ascetics, performers, and traders.

children.text: KAZ13.3.45/ teṣāṃ gṛha.patika.vyañjanāḥ kāṣṭha.tṛṇa.dhānya.paṇya.śakaṭaiḥ praharaṇa.āvaraṇāny abhihareyuḥ, deva.dhvaja.pratimābhir vā //
children.translated_text: Those disguised as householders should smuggle in weapons and armor in carts [loaded with] timber, grass, grain, and merchandise — or in images and banners of deities.

children.text: KAZ13.3.46/ tatas tad.vyañjanāḥ pramatta.vadham avaskanda.pratigraham abhipraharaṇaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ śaṅkha.dundubhi.śabdena vā "praviṣṭam" ity āvedayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then those bearing [such] disguises should announce the slaying of the unwary, the capture of the surprised, and the striking from behind — or [announce] 'It has been breached!' with the sound of conches and drums.

children.text: KAZ13.3.47/ prākāra.dvāra.aṭṭālaka.dānam anīka.bhedaṃ ghātaṃ vā kuryuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should effect the surrender of ramparts, gates, and watchtowers, or the breaking of the [enemy's] forces, or their destruction.

children.text: KAZ13.3.48/ sārtha.gaṇa.vāsibhir ātivāhikaiḥ kanyā.vāhikair aśva.paṇya.vyavahāribhir upakaraṇa.hārakair dhānya.kretṛ.vikretṛbhir vā pravrajita.liṅgibhir dūtaiś ca daṇaḍ.atinayanam, saṃdhi.karma.viśvāsana.artham //
children.translated_text: Through caravan members, camp-followers, bridal escorts, horse-traders, equipment-carriers, grain buyers and sellers, or those disguised as wandering ascetics and envoys — the army should be smuggled in, for the purpose of creating trust through a peace treaty.

children.text: KAZ13.3.49/ iti rāja.apasarpāḥ //
children.translated_text: These are the royal secret-agent operations.

children.text: KAZ13.3.50/ eta eva^aṭavīnām apasarpāḥ kaṇṭaka.śodhana.uktāś ca //
children.translated_text: These same are the secret-agent operations for forest tribes, and [the methods] described under 'removal of thorns' [also apply].

children.text: KAZ13.3.51/ vrajam aṭavy.āsannam apasarpāḥ sārthaṃ vā corair ghātayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Secret agents should have thieves attack a nomadic camp or caravan near a forest.

children.text: KAZ13.3.52/ kṛta.saṃketam anna.pānaṃ ca^atra madana.rasa.viddhaṃ vā kṛtvā^apagaccheyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Having arranged a signal and either poisoned the food and drink with stupefying substances, they should withdraw.

children.text: KAZ13.3.53/ go.pālaka.vaidehakāś ca tataś corān gṛhīta.loptra.bhārān madana.rasa.vikāra.kāle^avaskandayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Then cowherd and trader [agents] should assault the thieves — who have seized their loads of plunder — at the time the stupefying substance takes effect.

children.text: KAZ13.3.54/ saṃkarṣaṇa.daivatīyo vā muṇḍa.jaṭila.vyañjanaḥ prahavaṇa.karmaṇā madana.rasa.yogena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or one [disguised as a devotee] of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> (deity), with the appearance of a shaven-headed or matted-hair [ascetic], should deceive [the forest tribes] through a sacrificial ceremony and the application of stupefying substances.

children.text: KAZ13.3.55/ atha^avaskandaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Then he should deliver the surprise attack.

children.text: KAZ13.3.56/ śauṇḍika.vyañjano vā daivata.preta.kārya.utsava.samājeṣv āṭavikān surā.vikraya.upāyana.nimittaṃ madana.rasa.yogena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or one disguised as a liquor-seller, during divine rites, funerary ceremonies, festivals, and assemblies, should deceive the forest tribesmen through the sale and offering of liquor mixed with stupefying substances.

children.text: KAZ13.3.57/ atha^avaskandaṃ dadyāt //
children.translated_text: Then he should deliver the surprise attack.

children.text:
KAZ13.3.58ab/ grāma.ghāta.praviṣṭāṃ vā vikṣipya bahudhā^aṭavīm /
KAZ13.3.58cd/ ghātayed iti corāṇām apasarpāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //E
children.translated_text: Or, having scattered and divided the forest [tribe] that has entered for village-raiding, he should destroy [them] — thus are the secret-agent operations against thieves proclaimed.

children.text:
(paryupāsana.karma - avamardah)
KAZ13.4.01/ karśana.pūrvaṃ paryupāsana.karma //
children.translated_text:
(Operations of siege — the assault)
Siege operations [should be preceded] by attrition.

children.text: KAZ13.4.02/ jana.padaṃ yathā.niviṣṭam abhaye sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: He should secure the countryside's inhabitants in safety as they are settled.

children.text: KAZ13.4.03/ utthitam anugraha.parihārābhyāṃ niveṣayet, anyatra^apasarataḥ //
children.translated_text: Those who have risen [in revolt] he should resettle through conciliation and exemptions — except those who flee.

children.text: KAZ13.4.04/ saṃgrāmād anyasyāṃ bhūmau niveśayet, ekasyāṃ vā vāsayet //
children.translated_text: He should settle [the population] on land other than the battlefield, or confine them to a single [location].

children.text: KAZ13.4.05/ na hy ajano jana.pado rājyam ajana.padaṃ vā bhavati^iti kauṭilyaḥ //
children.translated_text: For a country without people is no kingdom, nor is a kingdom without a country — says <s>Kauṭilya</s>.

children.text: KAZ13.4.06/ viṣamasthasya muṣṭiṃ sasyaṃ vā hanyād, vīvadha.prasārau ca //
children.translated_text: He should destroy the crops or grain stores of one stationed in a difficult position, and [cut off] his supply trains and foraging.

children.text:
KAZ13.4.07ab/ prasāra.vīvadhac.chedān muṣṭi.sasya.vadhād api /
KAZ13.4.07cd/ vamanād gūḍha.ghātāc ca jāyate prakṛti.kṣayaḥ //
children.translated_text: Through cutting off of foraging and supply trains, through destruction of grain stores and crops, through 'emetic' [stratagem], and through covert assassination — the destruction of the [enemy's] subjects is effected.

children.text: KAZ13.4.08/ "prabhūta.guṇa.baddha(vaddha).anya.kupya.yantra.śastra.āvaraṇa.viṣṭir aśmi.samagraṃ me sainyam, ṛtuś ca purastāt, apartuḥ parasya, vyādhi.durbhikṣa.nicaya.rakṣā.kṣayaḥ krīta.bala.nirvedo mitra.bala.nirvedaś ca" iti paryupāsīta //
children.translated_text: 'My army is complete with abundant provisions, stockpiled supplies, machines, weapons, armor, and forced laborers; the season favors me but is adverse for the enemy; there is attrition of his [resources through] disease, famine, stores, garrison, and expenditure; and demoralization of his hired forces and allied forces' — [under such conditions] he should undertake a siege.

children.text: KAZ13.4.09/ kṛtvā skandha.āvārasya rakṣāṃ vīvadha.āsārayoḥ pathaś ca, parikṣipya durgaṃ khāta.sālābhyām, dūṣayitvā^udakam, avasrāvya parikhāḥ sampūrayitvā vā, suruṅgā.bala.kuṭikābhyāṃ vapra.prākārau hārayet, dāraṃ ca guḍena //
children.translated_text: Having secured the protection of the base-camp and the paths for supply trains and reinforcements, having encircled the fort with a moat and stockade, having contaminated the water, and having drained or filled the moats, he should breach the rampart and wall through tunnel-forces and siege-sheds, and the gate through battering rams.

children.text: KAZ13.4.10/ nimnaṃ vā pāṃsu.mālayā^ācchādayet //
children.translated_text: Or he should cover a low [section of the wall] with an earthen ramp.

children.text: KAZ13.4.11/ bahula.ārakṣaṃ yantrair ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Where the garrison is numerous, he should strike with siege engines.

children.text: KAZ13.4.12/ niṣkirād upaniṣkṛṣya^aśvaiś ca prahareyuḥ //
children.translated_text: They should draw [the enemy] out from sorties with cavalry and attack.

children.text: KAZ13.4.13/ vikrama.antareṣu ca niyoga.vikalpa.samuccayaiś ca^upāyānāṃ siddhiṃ lipseta //
children.translated_text: And in the intervals between assaults, he should seek success of [his] strategies through [their] individual, alternative, or combined application.

children.text: KAZ13.4.14/ durga.vāsinaḥ śyena.kāka.naptṛ.bhāsa.śuka.sārika.ulūka.kapotān grāhayitvā puccheṣv agni.yoga.yuktān para.durge visṛjet //
children.translated_text: He should have the fort's inhabitants capture hawks, crows, <s>naptṛ</s>-birds, vultures, parrots, <s>sārikā</s>s (mynas), owls, and pigeons, attach fire-compounds to their tails, and release them into the enemy's fort.

children.text: KAZ13.4.15/ apakṛṣṭa.skandha.āvārād ucchrita.dhvaja.dhanva.ārakṣo vā mānuṣeṇa^agninā para.durgam ādīpayet //
children.translated_text: Or, from a distance beyond the base-camp, with elevated banners and armed guards, he should set fire to the enemy's fort with man-made fire.

children.text: KAZ13.4.16/ gūḍha.purṣāś ca^antar.durga.pālakā nakula.vānara.biḍāla.śunāṃ puccheṣv agni.yogam ādhāya kāṇḍa.nicaya.rakṣā.vidhāna.veśmasu visṛjeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And covert agents inside the fort, acting as inner-fort guards, should attach fire-compounds to the tails of mongooses, monkeys, cats, and dogs and release them in the armories, store-houses, and guard-quarters.

children.text: KAZ13.4.17/ śuṣka.matsyānām udareṣv agnim ādhāya vallūre vā vāyasa.upahāreṇa vayobhir hārayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Placing fire inside the bellies of dried fish or in leather bags, they should have birds carry [them] as offerings to crows [i.e., food for birds].

children.text: KAZ13.4.18/ sarala.deva.dāru.pūti.tṛṇa.guggulu.śrī.veṣṭakasarjarasalākṣāgulikāḥ khara.uṣṭra.ajāvīnāṃ leṇḍaṃ ca^agni.dhāraṇam //
children.translated_text: Pine, <s>devadāru</s> (Himalayan cedar), rotten grass, <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>śrīveṣṭaka</s> (pine resin), <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin), and lac pellets, together with the dung of donkeys, camels, sheep, and goats — [these are] fire-carrying [agents].

children.text: KAZ13.4.19/ priyāla.cūrṇam avalgu.jamaṣī.madhu.ucchiṣṭam aśva.khara.uṣṭra.go.leṇḍam ity eṣa kṣepyo^agni.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Powder of <s>priyāla</s>, lac, iron-filings, beeswax, and dung of horses, donkeys, camels, and cattle — this is the fire-compound to be hurled.

children.text: KAZ13.4.20/ sarva.loha.cūrṇam agni.varṇaṃ vā kumbhī.sīsa.trapu.cūrṇaṃ vā pāribhadraka.palāśa.puṣpa.keśa.maṣī.taila.madhu.ucchiṣṭaka.śrī.veṣṭaka.yukto^agni.yogo viśvāsa.ghātī vā //
children.translated_text: Powder of all metals, or powder of iron-colored lead, tin, and copper, combined with <s>pāribhadraka</s> flower, <s>palāśa</s> flower, hair, soot, oil, beeswax, and resin — this is the fire-compound, or the 'trust-destroyer.'

children.text: KAZ13.4.21/ tena^avaliptaḥ śaṇa.trapusa.valka.veṣṭito bāṇa ity agni.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: An arrow smeared with this and wrapped in hemp or gourd-bark — this is the fire-arrow compound.

children.text: KAZ13.4.22/ na tv eva vidyamāne parākrame^agnim avasṛjet //
children.translated_text: But one should never resort to fire when valor [alone] can accomplish the task.

children.text: KAZ13.4.23/ aviśvāsyo hy agnir daiva.pīḍanaṃ ca, apratisaṃkhyāta.prāṇi.dhānya.paśu.hiraṇya.kupya.dravya.kṣaya.karaḥ //
children.translated_text: For fire is unreliable and causes divine affliction, and it destroys lives, grain, cattle, gold, raw materials, and goods beyond reckoning.

children.text:
KAZ13.4.24/ kṣīṇa.nicayaṃ ca^avāptam api rājyaṃ kṣayāya^eva bhavati // (iti paryupāsana.karma)
KAZ13.4.25/ "sarva.ārambha.upakaraṇa.viṣṭi.sampanno^asmi, vyādhitaḥ para upadhā.viruddha.prakṛtir akṛta.durga.karma.nicayo vā, nirāsāraḥ sāsāro vā purā mitraiḥ saṃdhatte" ity avamarda.kālaḥ //
children.translated_text:
And a kingdom obtained with depleted stores only leads to ruin. (Thus ends the section on siege operations.)
"I am equipped with all resources, instruments, and labor; the enemy is afflicted, his subjects are hostile to [his] policies, and he has not prepared his fort, works, or stores — whether he is without reserves or with reserves — before he forms an alliance with his allies" — this is the time for assault.

children.text: KAZ13.4.26/ svayam agnau jāte samutthāpite vā prahavaṇe prekṣā.anīka.darśana.saṅga.saurika.kalaheṣu nitya.yuddha.śrānta.bale bahula.yuddha.pratividdha.preta.puruṣe jāgaraṇa.klānta.supta.jane durdine nadī.vege vā nīhāra.samplave vā^avamṛdnīyāt //
children.translated_text: When fire has broken out by itself or has been set, during festivities, parades, elephant displays, engagements, or <s>saurika</s> (marketplace) disturbances — when the defending force is exhausted by constant fighting, when many soldiers are wounded or dead from frequent battles, when the people are fatigued from keeping watch and are asleep — in bad weather, during river floods, or in a fog — one should crush [the enemy].

children.text: KAZ13.4.27/ skandha.āvāram utsṛjya vā vana.gūḍhaḥ śatruṃ niṣkrāntaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having abandoned the military camp and hidden in the forest, one should ambush the enemy when he comes out.

children.text: KAZ13.4.28/ mitra.āsāra.mukhya.vyañjano vā samruddhena maitrīṃ kṛtvā dūtam abhityaktaṃ preṣayet - "idaṃ te chidram, ime dūṣyāḥ" "samroddhur vā chidram, ayaṃ te kṛtya.pakṣaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, [an agent] disguised as a chief of an allied reinforcement, having formed a friendship with the besieged, should send an envoy to the besieger [saying]: "Here is your weak point; these are [your] corruptible men" — or, "Here is a weak point of the besieger; here is a faction you can exploit."

children.text: KAZ13.4.29/ taṃ pratidūtam ādāya nirgacchantaṃ vijigīṣur gṛhītvā doṣam abhivikhyāpya pravāsya apagacchet //
children.translated_text: When [the besieger] comes out taking the counter-envoy, the aspiring conqueror should seize him, publicly proclaim his fault, banish him, and withdraw.

children.text: KAZ13.4.30/ tato mitra.āsāra.vyañjano vā samruddhaṃ brūyāt "māṃ trātum upanirgaccha, mayā vā saha samroddhāraṃ jahi" iti //
children.translated_text: Then an agent disguised as an allied reinforcement should tell the besieged: "Come out to rescue me, or join me in attacking the besieger."

children.text: KAZ13.4.31/ pratipannam ubhayataḥ.sampīḍanena ghātayet, jīva.grāheṇa vā rājya.vinimayaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: When he complies, one should destroy him by squeezing from both sides; or by capturing him alive, one should force an exchange of kingdoms.

children.text: KAZ13.4.32/ nagaraṃ vā^asya pramṛdnīyāt //
children.translated_text: Or one should crush his capital city.

children.text: KAZ13.4.33/ sāra.balaṃ vā^asya vamayitvā^abhihanyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having drawn out his best troops, one should strike them down.

children.text: KAZ13.4.34/ tena daṇḍa.upanata.āṭavikā vyākhyātāḥ //
children.translated_text: By this, [the treatment of] forest chieftains subdued by force is explained.

children.text: KAZ13.4.35/ daṇḍa.upanata.āṭavikayor anyataro vā samruddhasya preṣayet - "ayaṃ samroddhā vyādhitaḥ, pārṣṇi.grāheṇa^abhiyuktaḥ, chidram anyad utthitam, anyasyāṃ bhūmāv apayātu.kāmaḥ" iti //
children.translated_text: Or one should send either a force-subdued [chieftain] or a forest tribesman to the besieged [saying]: "The besieger is ill, attacked by a rear-enemy, another vulnerability has arisen, [or] he intends to march to another territory."

children.text: KAZ13.4.36/ pratipanne samroddhā skandha.āvāram ādīpya^apayāyāt //
children.translated_text: When [the besieged] complies, the besieger should set fire to the military camp and withdraw.

children.text: KAZ13.4.37/ tataḥ pūrvavad ācaret //
children.translated_text: Then one should proceed as before.

children.text: KAZ13.4.38/ paṇya.sampātaṃ vā kṛtvā paṇyena^enaṃ rasa.viddhena^atisaṃdadhyāt //
children.translated_text: Or, having arranged a market exchange, one should entrap him with goods laced with poison.

children.text: KAZ13.4.39/ āsāra.vyañjano vā samruddhasya dūtaṃ preṣayet - "mayā bāhyam abhihatam upanirgaccha^abhihantum" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, an agent disguised as a reinforcement should send an envoy to the besieged: "I have defeated the outer [forces]; come out to attack."

children.text: KAZ13.4.40/ pratipannaṃ pūrvavad ācaret //
children.translated_text: When he complies, one should proceed as before.

children.text: KAZ13.4.41/ mitraṃ bandhuṃ vā^apadiśya yoga.puruṣāḥ śāsana.mudrā.hastāḥ praviśya durgaṃ grāhayeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, pretending to be a friend or kinsman, secret agents bearing royal seals and letters should enter and seize the fortress.

children.text: KAZ13.4.42/ āsāra.vyañjñano vā samruddhasya preṣayet - "amuṣmin deśe kāle ca skandha.āvāram abhihaniṣyāmi, yuṣmābhir api yoddhavyam" iti //
children.translated_text: Or, an agent disguised as a reinforcement should send word to the besieged: "At such-and-such place and time I will attack the military camp; you too should fight."

children.text: KAZ13.4.43/ pratipannaṃ yathā.uktam abhyāghāta.saṃkulaṃ darśayitvā rātrau durgān niṣkrāntaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: When he complies, having shown him a scene of confused fighting as described, one should ambush him at night when he comes out of the fortress.

children.text: KAZ13.4.44/ yad vā mitram āvāhayed āṭavvikaṃ vā, tam utsāhayet "vikramya samruddhe bhūmim asya pratipadyasva" iti //
children.translated_text: Or one should invite an ally or a forest chieftain and urge him: "Attack the besieged and seize his territory by force."

children.text: KAZ13.4.45/ vikrāntaṃ prakṛtibhir dūṣya.mukhya.upagraheṇa vā ghātayet, svayaṃ vā rasena "mitra.ghātako^ayam" ity avāpta.arthaḥ //
children.translated_text: When he has attacked, one should have him destroyed through his own subjects, or through the capture of corruptible chiefs; or [one should destroy him] oneself by poison [saying]: "He is a friend-killer" — having achieved one's objective.

children.text: KAZ13.4.46/ vikramitu.kāmaṃ vā mitra.vyañjanaḥ parasya^abhiśaṃset //
children.translated_text: Or, an agent disguised as a friend should denounce to the other [king] one who intends to attack.

children.text: KAZ13.4.47/ āpta.bhāva.upagataḥ pravīra.puruṣānasya^upaghātayet //
children.translated_text: Having gained his trust, one should have his chief warriors assassinated.

children.text: KAZ13.4.48/ saṃdhiṃ vā kṛtvā jana.padam enaṃ niveśayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having made a treaty, one should settle him in the countryside.

children.text: KAZ13.4.49/ niviṣṭam asya jana.padam avijñāto hanyāt //
children.translated_text: Once settled, one should have his people destroyed without detection.

children.text: KAZ13.4.50/ apakārayitvā dūṣya.āṭavikeṣu vā bala.eka.deśam atinīya durgam avaskandena hārayet //
children.translated_text: Or, having caused provocations through corruptible agents and forest tribes, and having drawn away a portion of his forces, one should seize the fortress by a sudden assault.

children.text: KAZ13.4.51/ dūṣya.amitra.āṭavika.dveṣya.pratyapasṛtāś ca kṛta.artha.māna.saṃjñā.cihnāḥ para.durgam avaskandeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: And corruptible agents, enemy [defectors], forest tribesmen, hostile persons, and those who have fallen back — bearing signs, signals, and insignia of accomplished [allies] — should storm the enemy's fortress.

children.text: KAZ13.4.52/ para.durgam avaskandya skandha.āvāraṃ vā patita.parān.mukha.abhipannam ukta.keśa.śastra.bhaya.virūpebhyaś ca^abhayam ayudhyamānebhyaś ca dadyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Having stormed the enemy's fortress or military camp, one should grant safety to those who have fallen, turned back, or surrendered, and to those with disheveled hair, bearing [only] weapons [in submission], disfigured by fear, and to those who do not fight.

children.text: KAZ13.4.53/ para.durgam avāpya viśuddha.śatru.pakṣaṃ kṛta.upāṃśu.daṇḍa.pratīkāram antar.bahiś ca praviśet //
children.translated_text: Having seized the enemy's fortress, having purged the enemy's faction and having set up secret counter-measures, one should enter [the fortress] both from within and without.

children.text: KAZ13.4.54/ evaṃ vijigīṣur amitra.bhūmiṃ labdhvā madhyamaṃ lipseta, tat.siddhāv udāsīnam //
children.translated_text: Thus the aspiring conqueror, having obtained the enemy's territory, should seek [to win] the <s>madhyama</s> (middle king); upon success there, the <s>udāsīna</s> (neutral king).

children.text: KAZ13.4.55/ eṣa prathamo mārgaḥ pṛthivīṃ jetum //
children.translated_text: This is the first path to conquer the earth.

children.text: KAZ13.4.56/ madhyama.udāsīnayor abhāve guṇa.atiśayena^ari.prakṛtīḥ sādhayet, tata uttarāḥ prakṛtīḥ //
children.translated_text: In the absence of the <s>madhyama</s> and <s>udāsīna</s>, one should win over the enemy's subjects through superior qualities, and then the subjects beyond them.

children.text: KAZ13.4.57/ eṣa dvitīyo mārgaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the second path.

children.text: KAZ13.4.58/ maṇḍalasya^abhāve śatruṇā mitraṃ mitreṇa vā śatrum ubhayataḥ.sampīḍanena sādhayet //
children.translated_text: In the absence of a [complete] circle [of kings], one should subdue the enemy through an ally, or an ally through the enemy, by squeezing from both sides.

children.text: KAZ13.4.59/ eṣa.tṛtīyo mārgaḥ //
children.translated_text: This is the third path.

children.text: KAZ13.4.60/ śakyam ekaṃ vā sāmantaṃ sādhayet, tena dvi.guṇo dvitīyam, tri.guṇas tṛtīyam //
children.translated_text: Or one should subdue a single capable neighbor; with him, being twice as strong, a second; being thrice as strong, a third.

children.text: KAZ13.4.61/ eṣa caturtho mārgaḥ pṛthivīṃ jetum //
children.translated_text: This is the fourth path to conquer the earth.

children.text: KAZ13.4.62/ jitvā ca pṛthivīṃ vibhakta.varṇa.āśramāṃ sva.dharmeṇa bhuñjīta //
children.translated_text: And having conquered the earth, one should enjoy it with [its] <s>varṇas</s> (social orders) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) properly divided, according to one's own <s>dharma</s>.

children.text:
KAZ13.4.63ab/ upajāpo^apasarpaś ca vāmanaṃ paryupāsanam /
KAZ13.4.63cd/ avamardaś ca pañca^ete durga.lambhasya hetavaḥ //E
children.translated_text:
Instigation, infiltration, secret subversion, siege,
and assault — these five are the means of capturing a fortress.

children.text:
(labdha.praśamanam)
KAZ13.5.01/ dvividhaṃ vijigīṣoḥ samutthānaṃ - aṭavy.ādikam eka.grāma.ādikaṃ ca //
children.translated_text:
(Pacification of the conquered)
The aspiring conqueror's campaigns are of two kinds — those beginning with forest [regions] and those beginning with a single village.

children.text: KAZ13.5.02/ trividhaś ca^asya lambhaḥ - navo, bhūta.pūrvaḥ, pitrya iti //
children.translated_text: And his acquisitions are of three kinds — new, formerly held, and ancestral.

children.text: KAZ13.5.03/ navam avāpya lābhaṃ para.doṣān sva.guṇaiś chādayet, guṇān guṇa.dvaiguṇyena //
children.translated_text: Having obtained a new acquisition, one should conceal the [previous ruler's] faults with one's own virtues, and surpass his virtues with double the virtues.

children.text: KAZ13.5.04/ sva.dharma.karma.anugraha.parihāra.dāna.māna.karmabhiś ca prakṛti.priya.hitāny anuvarteta //
children.translated_text: And through acts of [upholding] one's own <s>dharma</s>, [granting] favors, exemptions, gifts, and honors, one should pursue what is dear and beneficial to the subjects.

children.text: KAZ13.5.05/ yathā.sambhāṣitaṃ ca kṛtya.pakṣam upagrāhayet, bhūyaś ca kṛta.prayāsam //
children.translated_text: And one should win over the subvertible faction as promised, and even more so those who have exerted themselves [on one's behalf].

children.text: KAZ13.5.06/ aviśvāso hi visaṃvādakaḥ sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ ca bhavati, prakṛti.viruddha.ācāraś ca //
children.translated_text: For breaking faith causes distrust among both one's own and others' [subjects], as does conduct contrary to [established] customs.

children.text: KAZ13.5.07/ tasmāt samāna.śīla.veṣa.bhāṣā.ācāratām upagachet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should adopt the same character, dress, language, and customs [as the conquered people].

children.text: KAZ13.5.08/ deśa.daivata.smāja.utsava.vihāreṣu ca bhaktim anuvarteta //
children.translated_text: And one should show devotion to the local deities, festivals, assemblies, and places of recreation.

children.text: KAZ13.5.09/ deśa.grāma.jāti.saṃgha.mukhyeṣu ca^abhīkṣṇaṃ sattriṇaḥ parasya^apacāraṃ darśayeyuḥ, māhābhāgyaṃ bhaktiṃ ca teṣu svāminaḥ, svāmi.satkāraṃ ca vidyamānam //
children.translated_text: And among the chiefs of the region, village, caste, and guild, spies should constantly point out the previous [ruler's] misconduct, the master's great fortune and devotion toward them, and the honor that the master currently bestows.

children.text: KAZ13.5.10/ ucitaiś ca^enān bhoga.parihāra.rakṣā.avekṣaṇair bhuñjīta //
children.translated_text: And one should enjoy [the territory] with the customary provisions, exemptions, and protective supervision.

children.text: KAZ13.5.11/ sarva.devatā.āśrama.pūjanaṃ ca vidyā.vākya.dharma.śūra.puruṣāṇāṃ ca bhūmi.dravya.dāna.parihārān kārayet, sarva.bandhana.mokṣaṇam anugrahaṃ dīna.anātha.vyādhitānāṃ ca //
children.translated_text: And one should arrange worship of all deities and <s>āśramas</s> (hermitages), and grants of land, wealth, and exemptions to men of learning, eloquence, <s>dharma</s>, and valor; the release of all prisoners; and benevolence toward the poor, the helpless, and the sick.

children.text: KAZ13.5.12/ cāturmāsyeṣv ardha.māsikam aghātam, paurṇamāsīṣu ca cātūrātrikaṃ rāja.deśa.nakṣatreṣv aikarātrikam //
children.translated_text: During the <s>cāturmāsya</s> (four-month seasonal) periods, a half-month prohibition on animal slaughter; on full-moon days, a four-night prohibition; and on the royal, regional, and natal asterisms, a one-night prohibition.

children.text: KAZ13.5.13/ yoni.bāla.vadhaṃ puṃstva.upaghātaṃ ca pratiṣedhayet //
children.translated_text: One should prohibit the killing of pregnant [animals] and young ones, and the mutilation of [animals'] reproductive organs.

children.text: KAZ13.5.14/ yac ca kośa.daṇḍa.upaghātakam adharmiṣṭhaṃ vā caritraṃ manyeta tad apanīya dharmya.vyavahāraṃ sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: And whatever practice one considers harmful to the treasury and army, or unrighteous — that one should abolish and establish a righteous administration.

children.text: KAZ13.5.15/ cora.prakṛtīnāṃ mleccha.jātīnāṃ ca sthāna.viparyāsam anekasthaṃ kārayet, durga.rāṣṭra.daṇḍa.mukhyānāṃ ca //
children.translated_text: One should cause the displacement of tribes of thieves and <s>mleccha</s> (barbarian) peoples to multiple [separate] locations, as well as of the chiefs of fortresses, territories, and armies.

children.text: KAZ13.5.16/ parā.upagṛhītānāṃ ca mantri.purohitānāṃ parasya pratyanteṣv anekasthaṃ vāsaṃ kārayet //
children.translated_text: And the ministers and chaplains who were employed by the previous [ruler] should be settled in multiple locations along the frontiers.

children.text: KAZ13.5.17/ apakāra.samarthān anukṣiyato vā bhartṛ.vināśam upāṃśu.daṇḍena praśamayet //
children.translated_text: Those capable of causing harm or those who are wasting away [in resentment] — one should suppress through the death of the master [i.e., the former ruler's loyalists] by secret punishment.

children.text: KAZ13.5.18/ sva.deśīyān vā pareṇa vā^aparuddhān apavāhita.sthāneṣu sthāpayet //
children.translated_text: Or one should install [people] from one's own country, or those besieged by the enemy, in the vacated positions.

children.text: KAZ13.5.19/ yaś ca tat.kulīnaḥ pratyādeyam ādātuṃ śaktaḥ, pratyanta.aṭavīstho vā prabādhitum abhijātaḥ, tasmai viguṇāṃ bhūmiṃ prayacchet, guṇavatyāś catur.bhāgaṃ vā kośa.daṇḍa.dānam avasthāpya, yad upakurvāṇaḥ paura.jānapadān kopayet //
children.translated_text: And whoever is of that dynasty and capable of reclaiming [the territory], or who is stationed on the frontier or in the forest and is of noble birth with the power to cause trouble — to him one should give inferior land, or a quarter [of the revenue] of productive land, having imposed a levy of treasury and army, so that [while serving] he would anger the townspeople and countryfolk.

children.text: KAZ13.5.20/ kupitais tair enaṃ ghātayet //
children.translated_text: Then one should have him killed by the angered [people].

children.text: KAZ13.5.21/ prakṛtibhir upakruṣṭam apanayet, aupaghātike vā deśe niveśayet - iti //
children.translated_text: One who is denounced by the subjects should be removed, or should be settled in a hazardous region.

children.text: KAZ13.5.22/ bhūta.pūrve yena doṣeṇa^apavṛttas taṃ prakṛti.doṣaṃ chādayet, yena ca guṇena^upāvṛttas taṃ tīvrī.kuryāt - iti //
children.translated_text: In [territory] formerly held — whatever fault caused one's expulsion, that defect in the subjects one should conceal; and whatever virtue caused one's return, that one should intensify.

children.text: KAZ13.5.23/ pitrye pitur doṣāṃś chādayet, guṇāṃś ca prakāśayet - iti //
children.translated_text: In ancestral [territory] — one should conceal the father's faults and publicize his virtues.

children.text:
KAZ13.5.24ab/ caritram akṛtaṃ dharmyaṃ kṛtaṃ ca^anyaiḥ pravartayet /
KAZ13.5.24cd/ pravartayen na ca^adharmyaṃ kṛtaṃ ca^anyair nivartayet //E
children.translated_text:
One should introduce righteous practices not [previously] established, and continue those established by others;
one should not introduce unrighteous [practices], and should abolish those established by others.

children.text:
para.bala.ghāta.prayogah)
KAZ14.1.01/ cāturvarṇya.rakṣā.artham aupaniṣadikam adharmiṣṭheṣu prayuñjīta //
children.translated_text:
(Methods for destroying the enemy's forces)
For the protection of the four <s>varṇas</s> (social orders), one should employ <s>aupaniṣadika</s> (esoteric/occult) methods against the unrighteous.

children.text: KAZ14.1.02/ kāla.kūṭa.ādir viṣa.vargaḥ śraddheya.deśa.veṣa.śilpa.bhāṣā.abhijana.apadeśaiḥ kubja.vāmana.kirāta.mūka.badhira.jaḍa.andhac.chadmabhir mleccha.jātīyair abhipretaiḥ strībhiḥ pumbhiś ca para.śarīra.upabhogeṣv avadhātavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Kālakūṭa</s> and other poisons should be administered through persons of trustworthy appearance, region, dress, craft, language, and lineage — disguised as hunchbacks, dwarves, <s>Kirātas</s> (hill tribesmen), mutes, deaf, idiots, or blind persons — through <s>mleccha</s> (barbarian) tribesmen, suitable women and men, in [items for] the enemy's bodily enjoyment.

children.text: KAZ14.1.03/ rāja.krīḍā.bhāṇḍa.nidhāna.dravya.upabbhogeṣu gūḍhāḥ śastra.nidhānaṃ kuryuḥ, sattra.ājīvinaś ca rātri.cāriṇo^agni.jīvinaś ca^agni.nidhānam //
children.translated_text: Secret agents should plant weapons in the king's playthings, stores, and articles of enjoyment; and those who live by espionage, night-prowlers, and fire-keepers should plant fire [devices].

children.text: KAZ14.1.04/ citra.bheka.kauṇḍinyaka.kṛkaṇa.pañca.kuṣṭha.śata.padī.cūrṇam ucci.diṇga.kambalī.śata.kanda(kardama?).idhma.kṛkalāsa.cūrṇaṃ gṛha.golika.andha.ahi.kakra.kaṇṭaka.pūti.kīṭa.gomārikā.cūrṇaṃ bhallātaka.avalgu.jara.samyuktaṃ sadyaḥ.prāṇa.haram, eteṣāṃ vā dhūmaḥ //
children.translated_text: Powder of spotted frog, <s>kauṇḍinyaka</s>, <s>kṛkaṇa</s> (partridge), five [types of] <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin-disease insects), and centipede; powder of <s>ucciḍiṅga</s>, <s>kambalī</s>, <s>śatakanda</s>, tinder, and chameleon; powder of house-lizard, blind snake, <s>kakra</s>, thorn-insect, stink-bug, and <s>gomārikā</s> — combined with <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), <s>avalgu</s>, and <s>jara</s> — is instantly lethal; or the smoke of these.

children.text:
KAZ14.1.05ab/ kīṭo vā^anyatamas taptaḥ kṛṣṇa.sarpa.priyaṅgubhiḥ /
KAZ14.1.05cd/ śoṣayed eṣa samyogaḥ sadyaḥ.prāṇa.haro mataḥ //
children.translated_text:
Or any one of these insects, heated with black serpent [venom] and <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry),
causes withering — this combination is considered instantly lethal.

children.text: KAZ14.1.06/ dhāma.argava.yātu.dhāna.mūlaṃ bhallātaka.puṣpa.cūrṇa.yuktam ārdhamāsikaḥ //
children.translated_text: The root of <s>dhāmārgava</s> and <s>yātudhāna</s>, combined with powder of <s>bhallātaka</s> flowers, [is lethal] within a fortnight.

children.text: KAZ14.1.07/ vyāghātaka.mūlaṃ bhallātaka.puṣpa.cūrṇa.yuktaṃ kīṭa.yogo māsikaḥ //
children.translated_text: The root of <s>vyāghātaka</s>, combined with powder of <s>bhallātaka</s> flowers, [in] the insect-compound, [is lethal] within a month.

children.text: KAZ14.1.08/ kalā.mātraṃ puruṣāṇām, dvi.guṇaṃ khara.aśvānām, catur.guṇaṃ hasty.uṣṭrāṇām //
children.translated_text: A <s>kalā</s>-measure [is the dose] for humans; double for donkeys and horses; quadruple for elephants and camels.

children.text: KAZ14.1.09/ śata.kardama.uccidiṅga.kara.vīra.kaṭu.tumbī.matsya.dhūmo madana.kodrava.palālena hasti.karṇa.palāśa.palālena vā pravāta.anuvāte praṇīto yāvac carati tāvan mārayati //
children.translated_text: Smoke produced from <s>śata-kardama</s>, <s>uccidiṅga</s>, <s>kara-vīra</s> (oleander), bitter gourd, and fish — with <s>madana-kodrava</s> (narcotic millet) chaff, or with <s>hasti-karṇa-palāśa</s> (Butea leaf) chaff — directed with the wind, kills as far as it travels.

children.text: KAZ14.1.10/ pūki.kīṭa.mastya.kaṭu.tumbī.śata.kardama.idhma.indra.gopa.cūrṇaṃ pūti.kīṭa.kṣudra.ārālā.hema.vidārī.cūrṇaṃ vā basta.śṛṅga.khura.cūrṇa.yuktam andhī.karo dhūmaḥ //
children.translated_text: A powder of stinkbugs, insects, fish, bitter gourd, <s>śata-kardama</s> fuel, and fireflies — or a powder of putrid insects, small <s>ārālā</s>, golden <s>vidārī</s> — combined with goat-horn and hoof powder, produces a blinding smoke.

children.text: KAZ14.1.11/ pūti.karañja.pattra.hari.tāla.manaḥ.śilā.guñja.ārakta.kārpāsa.palāla.anya.āsphoṭa.kāca.go.śakṛd.rasa.piṣṭam andhī.karo dhūmaḥ //
children.translated_text: A paste of <s>pūti-karañja</s> leaves, orpiment, realgar, <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea), red cotton-chaff, <s>āsphoṭa</s>, glass, and cow-dung juice produces a blinding smoke.

children.text: KAZ14.1.12/ sarpa.nirmokaṃ go.aśva.purīṣam andha.ahika.śiraś ca^andhī.karo dhūmaḥ //
children.translated_text: A snake's sloughed skin, cow and horse dung, and the head of a blind snake produce a blinding smoke.

children.text:
KAZ14.1.13/ pārāvata.plavaka.kravya.adānāṃ hasti.nara.varāhāṇāṃ ca mūtra.purīṣaṃ kāsīsa.hiṅgu.yava.tuṣa.kaṇa.taṇḍulāḥ kārpāsa.kuṭaja.kośa.atakīnāṃ ca bījāni go.mūtrikā.bhāṇḍī.mūlaṃ nimba.śigru.phaṇirja.kākṣīva.pīluka.bhaṅgaḥ sarpa.śapharī.carma hasti.nakha.śṛṅga.cūrṇam ity eṣa dhūmo madana.kodrava.palālena hasti.karṇa.palāśa.palālena vā praṇītaḥ pratyekaśo
yāvac carati tāvan mārayati //
children.translated_text: The urine and dung of pigeons, ducks, and carrion-eating [birds], as well as of elephants, humans, and boars; iron vitriol, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), barley husks, rice grains, and broken rice; seeds of cotton, <s>kuṭaja</s>, and <s>kośa-atakī</s>; roots of <s>go-mūtrikā</s> and <s>bhāṇḍī</s>; <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree), <s>phaṇirja</s>, <s>kākṣīva</s>, <s>pīluka</s>, and hemp; skin of snakes and <s>śapharī</s> fish; powder of elephant nails and horns — this smoke, produced with <s>madana-kodrava</s> chaff or <s>hasti-karṇa-palāśa</s> chaff, each individually, kills as far as it travels.

children.text: KAZ14.1.14/ kālī.kuṣṭha.naḍa.śatāvalī.mūlaṃ sarpa.pracalāka.kṛkaṇa.pañca.kuṣṭha.cūrṇaṃ vā dhūmaḥ pūrva.kalpena^ārdra.śuṣka.palālena vā praṇītaḥ saṃgrāma.avataraṇa.avaskandana.saṃkuleṣu kṛta.nejana.udaka.akṣi.pratīkāraiḥ praṇītaḥ sarva.prāṇināṃ netraghnaḥ //
children.translated_text: The root of <s>kālī</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, reed, and <s>śatāvalī</s> — or powder of snakes, chameleons, <s>kṛkaṇa</s> [lizards], and <s>pañca-kuṣṭha</s> — this smoke, produced with the above method using wet or dry chaff, deployed in the confusion of battle-engagement, assault, and skirmishes, by those who have protected their own eyes with eye-wash solution, destroys the eyes of all living beings.

children.text: KAZ14.1.15/ śārikā.kapota.baka.balākā.leṇḍam arka.akṣi.pīluka.snuhi.kṣīra.piṣṭam andhī.karaṇam añjanam udaka.dūṣaṇaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: Droppings of <s>śārikā</s> (myna bird), pigeon, crane, and flamingo — ground with the milk of <s>arka</s>, <s>akṣi-pīluka</s>, and <s>snuhi</s> (cactus-spurge) — is a blinding collyrium and also a water-pollutant.

children.text: KAZ14.1.16/ yavaka.śāli.mūla.madana.phala.jātī.pattra.nara.mūtra.yogaḥ plakṣa.vidārī.mūla.yukto mūka.udumbara.madana.kodrava.kvātha.yukto hasti.karṇa.palāśa.kvātha.yukto vā madana.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of <s>yavaka</s>, <s>śāli</s> (rice) root, <s>madana</s> fruit, jasmine leaves, and human urine — combined with <s>plakṣa</s> and <s>vidārī</s> root, or with a decoction of <s>mūka-udumbara</s> and <s>madana-kodrava</s>, or with a decoction of <s>hasti-karṇa-palāśa</s> — is a <s>madana</s>-compound (intoxicant).

children.text: KAZ14.1.17/ śṛṅgi.gautama.vṛka.kaṇṭaka.ara.mayūra.padī.yogo guñjā.lāṅgalī.viṣa.mūlika.iṅgudī.yogaḥ kara.vīra.akṣi.pīluka.arka.mṛga.māraṇī.yogo madna.kodrava.kvātha.yukto hasti.karṇa.palāśa.kvātha.yukto vā madana.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of <s>śṛṅgi</s>, <s>gautama</s>, <s>vṛka-kaṇṭaka</s>, <s>ara</s>, and peacock's foot — or a compound of <s>guñjā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, poison-root, and <s>iṅgudī</s> — or a compound of oleander, <s>akṣi-pīluka</s>, <s>arka</s>, and deer-slaying [plant] — combined with a decoction of <s>madana-kodrava</s> or <s>hasti-karṇa-palāśa</s>, is a <s>madana</s>-compound.

children.text: KAZ14.1.18/ samastā vā yavasa.indhana.udaka.dūṣaṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, all [of the above] combined are pollutants of fodder, fuel, and water.

children.text: KAZ14.1.19/ kṛta.kaṇḍala.kṛkalāsa.gṛha.golika.andha.ahika.dhūmo netra.vadham unmādaṃ ca karoti //
children.translated_text: Smoke from <s>kṛta-kaṇḍala</s> [insect], chameleon, house-lizard, and blind snake causes eye-destruction and madness.

children.text: KAZ14.1.20/ kṛkalāsa.gṛha.golikā.yogaḥ kuṣṭha.karaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of chameleon and house-lizard causes leprosy.

children.text: KAZ14.1.21/ sa eva citram eka.antra.madhu.yuktaḥ prameham āpādayati, manuṣya.lohita.yuktaḥ śoṣam //
children.translated_text: The same, mixed with honey and a single intestine, produces urinary disease; mixed with human blood, it produces wasting disease.

children.text: KAZ14.1.22/ dūṣī.viṣaṃ madana.kodrava.cūrṇam apajihvikā.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: Slow-acting poison is powder of <s>madana-kodrava</s>; the <s>apajihvikā</s> compound [is another form].

children.text: KAZ14.1.23/ mātṛ.vāhaka.añjali.kāra.pracalāka.bheka.akṣi.pīluka.yogo viṣūcikā.karaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of <s>mātṛ-vāhaka</s>, <s>añjali-kāra</s>, chameleon, frog, <s>akṣi-pīluka</s> causes cholera.

children.text: KAZ14.1.24/ pañca.kuṣṭhaka.kauṇḍinya.karāja.vṛkṣa.puṣpa.madhu.yogo jvara.karaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of <s>pañca-kuṣṭhaka</s>, <s>kauṇḍinya</s>, and <s>karāja</s> tree flowers with honey causes fever.

children.text: KAZ14.1.25/ bhāsana.kula.jihvā.granthikā.yogaḥ kharī.kṣīra.piṣṭo mūka.badhira..karo māsa.ardha.māsikaḥ //
children.translated_text: A compound of <s>bhāsana</s>, <s>kula-jihvā</s>, and <s>granthikā</s>, ground with donkey's milk, causes dumbness and deafness for a half-month to a month.

children.text: KAZ14.1.26/ kalā.mātraṃ puruṣāṇām it samānaṃ pūrveṇa //
children.translated_text: The dose for humans is one <s>kalā</s>-measure — the same as above.

children.text: KAZ14.1.27/ bhaṅga.kvātha.upanayanam auṣadhānām, cūrṇaṃ prāṇa.bhṛtām, sarveṣāṃ vā kvātha.upanayanam, evaṃ vīryavattaraṃ bhavti //
children.translated_text: Preparation with a decoction of hemp is [the method] for medicines; powder [is the form] for living beings; or a decoction-based preparation for all — thus it becomes more potent.

children.text: KAZ14.1.28/ iti yoga.sampat //
children.translated_text: This is the perfection of compounds.

children.text: KAZ14.1.29/ śālmalī vidārī.dhānya.siddho mūla.vatsa.nābha.samyuktaś cucchundarī.śoṇita.pralepena digdho bāṇo yaṃ vidhyati sa viddho^anyān daśa.puruṣān daśati, te daṣṭā daśa^anyān daśanti puruṣān //
children.translated_text: An arrow made from <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree) and <s>vidārī</s> grain, combined with <s>vatsa-nābha</s> root, smeared with a coating of musk-shrew's blood — whomever it strikes, that stricken one bites ten other men, and they, bitten, bite ten more men.

children.text: KAZ14.1.30/ ballātaka.yātu.dhānāva.anudhā.mārgava.bāṇānāṃ puṣpair elaka.akṣi.guggulu.hālāhalānāṃ ca kaṣāyaṃ basta.nara.śoṇita.yuktaṃ daṃśa.yogaḥ //
children.translated_text: A decoction of the flowers of <s>ballātaka</s> (marking nut), <s>yātu-dhānava</s>, <s>anudhā</s>, <s>mārgava</s> arrows, and of <s>elaka</s>, <s>akṣi-guggulu</s>, and <s>hālāhala</s> — combined with goat and human blood — is a biting-compound.

children.text: KAZ14.1.31/ tato^ardha.dharaṇiko yogaḥ saktu.piṇyākābhyām udake praṇīto dhanuḥ.śata.āyāmam udaka.āśayaṃ dūṣayati //
children.translated_text: From this, a half-<s>dharaṇa</s> dose of the compound, introduced into water with roasted barley-flour and oil-cake, poisons a reservoir up to a hundred bow-lengths in extent.

children.text: KAZ14.1.32/ matsya.paramparā hy etena daṣṭā^abhimṛṣṭā vā viṣī.bhavati, yaś ca^etad udakaṃ pibati spṛśati vā //
children.translated_text: For fish in succession, having been bitten or touched by this, become poisonous — and whoever drinks or touches that water [is also poisoned].

children.text: KAZ14.1.33/ rakta.śveta.sarṣapair godhā tri.pakṣam uṣṭrikāyāṃ bhūmau nikhātāyāṃ nihitā vadhyena^uddhṛtā yāvat paśyati tāvan mārayati, kṛṣṇa.sarpo vā //
children.translated_text: A monitor lizard, fed for three fortnights on red and white mustard seeds, placed in a buried camel [carcass], when extracted by the victim — kills as far as it can see; likewise a black snake.

children.text: KAZ14.1.34/ vidyut.pradagdho^aṅgāro jvālo vā vidyut.pradagdhaiḥ kāṣṭhair gṛhītaś ca^anuvāsitaḥ kṛttikāsu bharaṇīṣu vā raudreṇa karmaṇā^abhihuto^agniḥ praṇītaś ca nispratīkāro dahati //
children.translated_text: A charcoal or flame from a lightning-struck [tree], seized with lightning-struck wood and fumigated, offered with a <s>Raudra</s> rite on the <s>Kṛttikā</s> or <s>Bharaṇī</s> asterisms and then deployed — is a fire without remedy that burns [everything].

children.text:
KAZ14.1.35ab/ karmārād agnim āhṛtya kṣaudreṇa juhuyāt pṛthak /
KAZ14.1.35cd/ surayā śauṇḍikād agniṃ mārgato^agniṃ ghṛtena ca //
children.translated_text: Having brought fire from a blacksmith, one should offer separately with honey; fire from a distiller, with liquor; fire from the road, with ghee;

children.text:
KAZ14.1.36ab/ mālyena ca^eka.patny.agniṃ puṃścaly.agniṃ ca sarṣapaiḥ /
KAZ14.1.36cd/ dadhnā ca sūtikāsv agnim āhita.agniṃ ca taṇḍulaiḥ //
children.translated_text: fire from a faithful wife, with garlands; fire from a promiscuous woman, with mustard seeds; fire from a woman in confinement, with curds; fire from one who maintains the sacred fire, with rice grains;

children.text: KAZ14.1.37ab/ caṇḍāla.agniṃ ca māṃsena cita.agniṃ mānuṣeṇa ca //
children.translated_text: fire from a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, with [animal] flesh; fire from a funeral pyre, with human [flesh];

children.text: KAZ14.1.37cd/ samastān basta.vasayā mānuṣeṇa dhruveṇa ca //
